article_ideas.angle: Economics and architecture of agent orchestration, with a practical Pareto decision rule.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent architects, and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Simple harnesses with robust tooling (like Prime Agent or basic REPLs) can be more competitive and cost-effective than overly complex multi-agent architectures.
article_ideas.thesis: Scaling agent count imposes measurable token, latency, and signal-density costs; teams should default to a simple tool-rich harness and only add multi-agent complexity when it wins on an explicit cost-to-performance frontier.
article_ideas.title: The Harness Tax: Why More Agents Is Not More Capability
article_ideas.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD

article_ideas.angle: Diagnostic playbook for agent failures using the Mismanaged Geniuses hypothesis.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, ML platform teams, and applied AI researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Current frontier LLMs are 'geniuses' in capability but 'mismanaged' by poor task decomposition and harness design.
article_ideas.thesis: Many multi-step agent failures are orchestration defects, not intelligence limits, so ablation of harness and task decomposition should precede model upgrades.
article_ideas.title: Mismanaged Geniuses: Fix the Decomposition Before Buying a Bigger Model
article_ideas.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD

article_ideas.angle: Research systems argument for separating model capability from execution-structure capability.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers and senior agent-system builders
article_ideas.based_on: Language model harnesses act as compositional generalizers.
article_ideas.thesis: Because harness scaffolding can induce length and domain generalization without changing the base transformer, harness design deserves its own benchmarks, ablations, and engineering ownership.
article_ideas.title: Harnesses as Compositional Generalizers: The Execution Layer Is a First-Class Artifact
article_ideas.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD

article_ideas.angle: Systems verification and reliability critique of kernel-generation benchmarks.
article_ideas.audience: ML systems, compiler, and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Kernel writing has a severe verification and reward-hacking problem.
article_ideas.thesis: AI-generated GPU kernels can dominate benchmarks while suffering severe reward hacking, so rank must be replaced or supplemented by adversarial correctness and generality verification.
article_ideas.title: Leaderboard Kernels Are Not Production Kernels
article_ideas.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD

article_ideas.angle: Architectural argument backed by the failure modes of end-to-end S2S models and the control requirements of enterprise deployments.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, product leaders, and enterprise architects building agentic systems.
article_ideas.based_on: Enterprise differentiation shifts from model weights to the harness layer
article_ideas.thesis: Raw speech-to-speech models are demo-ready but enterprise-deployable only when wrapped in a harness that provides retrieval, tool calling, grounding, and citations; therefore differentiation shifts from model weights to the control layer.
article_ideas.title: The Harness Is the Product: Why Enterprise Voice Agents Are Won at the Control Layer
article_ideas.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen

article_ideas.angle: Mechanism deep dive contrasting cascaded VAD heuristics with learned endpointing and its latency-accuracy claims.
article_ideas.audience: Voice AI engineers and real-time systems developers.
article_ideas.based_on: Turn boundaries and endpointing are learned/predicted by the model rather than derived from VAD silence thresholds
article_ideas.thesis: VAD silence thresholds are brittle and create a false tradeoff between premature interruption and frustrating pauses; model-driven endpointing resolves this by predicting turn boundaries from audio context and achieving sub-300ms p50 latency without weakening reasoning.
article_ideas.title: Stop Tuning VAD: Learned Turn-Taking as the End of Threshold Engineering
article_ideas.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen

article_ideas.angle: Design constraint framing, using the 3–5s panic threshold and sub-300ms p50 claim as the bounds of acceptable silence.
article_ideas.audience: Voice UX designers, product managers, and reliability engineers.
article_ideas.based_on: Latency in voice agents is framed as a trust/psychological-safety variable
article_ideas.thesis: Latency in voice agents is a trust variable with a concrete abandonment threshold, so endpointing and inference latency must be engineered to a silence budget rather than merely minimized.
article_ideas.title: The 300ms Trust Budget: Designing Voice Agents Around Psychological Safety
article_ideas.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen

article_ideas.angle: Architecture pattern article comparing full S2S, cascaded, and audio-in/text-out designs.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and multimodal agent developers.
article_ideas.based_on: Dialog-RSN-1 splits the modality at a deliberate boundary
article_ideas.thesis: Splitting modality at the understanding-control boundary—consuming audio natively but emitting text—lets multimodal agents preserve tone, emotion, and timing while retaining governance, tooling, and deterministic search.
article_ideas.title: Audio In, Text Out: The Control Seam for Auditable Multimodal Agents
article_ideas.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the AI-coding debate away from code quality and toward target selection and objective specification, using the archery/homing-arrow framing and the observation that customers don't care about the tech stack.
article_ideas.audience: Staff and principal engineers, engineering managers, and agent-platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Accuracy is decoupled from value, so automated execution equally amplifies effort spent on the wrong target
article_ideas.thesis: Once agents can hit any target, execution accuracy is decoupled from value, which means automated execution equally amplifies effort spent on the wrong problem — the failure mode of the agent era is not bad code but efficient pursuit of unimportant work, and that failure is invisible to every existing engineering metric.
article_ideas.title: The Homing Arrow Problem: When Execution Accuracy Stops Being the Bottleneck
article_ideas.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds

article_ideas.angle: Argue for treating API/primitive design as the primary agent-reliability lever, the way tool schemas and guardrails function in agent harnesses, rather than treating model choice or prompt craft as the lever.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework and platform engineers, tool-schema designers
article_ideas.based_on: Agent task success is bounded by the shape of the primitives and interfaces exposed to it
article_ideas.thesis: Agent task success is bounded by the shape of the primitives and interfaces exposed to it, so narrow, explicit, well-typed primitives are the real quality-control mechanism for machine execution — tighter primitives trade flexibility for reliable execution, and that trade should be made deliberately at the interface layer rather than absorbed by prompts or review.
article_ideas.title: Good Primitives Are a Reliability Feature, Not a Design Preference
article_ideas.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds

article_ideas.angle: Translate the ATMs/autopilot accountability argument into a concrete placement rule for approval gates, and state the throughput caveat the analogy conveniently omits.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and infrastructure engineers, risk and compliance leads for AI systems
article_ideas.based_on: the retained human role is not the execution skill but accountability for consequences
article_ideas.thesis: The durable human role under automation is accountability for outcomes rather than execution skill, so human-in-the-loop gates should sit at irreversible-consequence boundaries instead of being spread uniformly across the workflow — but this is only defensible if gate throughput does not become the new bottleneck, which the automation precedents do not establish.
article_ideas.title: Put the Human Where the Consequence Is Irreversible
article_ideas.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds

article_ideas.angle: Reinterpret Instagram/WhatsApp-style tiny-team restraint as a failure-domain reduction mechanism for automated execution rather than an aesthetic choice, including the boundary condition the talk leaves open.
article_ideas.audience: Product engineers, startup founders, platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Minimizing feature and interface surface area reduces both coordination cost and the error surface of automated execution
article_ideas.thesis: Minimizing feature and interface surface area is usually framed as UX taste or product strategy, but for agent-built and agent-operated products it is a reliability lever: fewer primitives shrink both human coordination cost and the error domain available to an automated executor, and restraint therefore has a measurable failure-rate payoff.
article_ideas.title: Product Restraint Is an Operational Reliability Property
article_ideas.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds

article_ideas.angle: Engineering management and process design
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and automation practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: perform the task manually about five times first
article_ideas.thesis: The five-time heuristic is useful for triggering automation, but teams should replace it with a measurement-driven approach that identifies the task-specific threshold where agent success rate plateaus.
article_ideas.title: The Five-Time Rule Is a Starting Point, Not a Law
article_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg Brockman

article_ideas.angle: Software architecture
article_ideas.audience: Backend and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: running against cloud apps independently of the user's device
article_ideas.thesis: Proactive agents require a persistent cloud runtime with their own identity, credentials, and durable state; designing for this decoupled execution model is essential for reliable background automation.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Should Outlive Your Laptop
article_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg Brockman

article_ideas.angle: AI-assisted software development
article_ideas.audience: Software engineers and engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: AI handles the mechanics of coding and execution while humans provide vision and judgment.
article_ideas.thesis: As AI absorbs execution, the limiting factor in agentic development becomes human review and specification; investing in review interfaces and acceptance criteria is the new high-leverage engineering work.
article_ideas.title: The Real Bottleneck Is Review, Not Coding
article_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg Brockman

article_ideas.angle: Business strategy for AI-native startups
article_ideas.audience: Founders and product strategists
article_ideas.based_on: The line between enterprise and consumer is blurring as software becomes commoditized.
article_ideas.thesis: When AI commoditizes software production, defensibility shifts from execution capacity to distribution, proprietary data, and domain-specific evaluation assets.
article_ideas.title: What's Left When Software Is Free?
article_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg Brockman

article_ideas.angle: Apply Theory of Constraints to SDLC agent portfolios: instrument the value stream, rank stages, then fund agents in ranked order — with a counterexample set from review, incident, and legacy refactoring work where non-coding agents produced large documented ROI.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, platform/DevEx teams, and agent product owners allocating AI budgets
article_ideas.based_on: Code generation is not the bottleneck; code gen represents only 14-16% of the overall value stream.
article_ideas.thesis: Coding assistance sits on a small share of the delivery value stream, so agent investment should be ranked by cycle-time contribution per stage; the visible artifact (code) is not the limiting constraint, and portfolios built around the IDE will keep producing sublinear system-level returns.
article_ideas.title: Your Coding Copilot Is Optimizing 14% of the Value Stream
article_ideas.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX

article_ideas.angle: Argue that quality proxies must be split into separate instruments for generation ease and reviewer verifiability, and show what a size-aware AI review policy would have to enforce.
article_ideas.audience: Staff+ engineers, code review tooling teams, and quality/eval owners
article_ideas.based_on: Code maintainability perceived score went up ~4%, but change confidence went down ~6%.
article_ideas.thesis: Perceived maintainability and reviewer change confidence have decoupled under AI-assisted delivery, and because PR size grew alongside them, any evaluation harness that reports maintainability alone will pass code that reviewers will not stand behind; review capacity, not generation capacity, is the constraint to engineer against.
article_ideas.title: Easier to Modify, Harder to Trust: The Two Quality Signals AI Decoupled
article_ideas.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX

article_ideas.angle: Show the gap between task-level speedup evidence and org-level effect size, then specify the matched-cohort and interrupted time-series designs required before attributing any of the gain to AI.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leads, platform teams, and technical due-diligence audiences
article_ideas.based_on: median PR throughput increased by 7.76% and average by 13.1% in longitudinal studies
article_ideas.thesis: Longitudinal org-level data showing median PR throughput up 7.76% with no organization reaching 2x is the correct prior for coding-agent ROI; individual-task benchmarks are not projections of organizational throughput, and any 5x or 10x claim is making a claim about measurement, not about delivery.
article_ideas.title: The 7.76% Reality Check: Why Task-Level Speedups Do Not Survive Aggregation
article_ideas.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX

article_ideas.angle: Reframe flaky-test and CI-latency work as agent-platform dependencies, and separate 'what is happening' AI metrics (utilization, impact, cost) from 'whether it is working' DevEx/DevProd metrics when defining the gate.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and infrastructure engineers, DevEx leads, and QA/test infrastructure owners
article_ideas.based_on: AI readiness depends on clear documentation, data structures, manageable code, fast local CI, and non-flaky test suites.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent effectiveness is bounded by documentation clarity, codebase manageability, local CI latency, and test determinism; flaky tests are therefore a blocker to agent adoption with an owner and a deadline, and readiness tiers should gate rollout rather than sit beside it.
article_ideas.title: AI Readiness Is an Infrastructure Problem, Not a Model Problem
article_ideas.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX

article_ideas.angle: Dismantle the assumption that 'tests pass' equals 'safe to merge' by contrasting test-execution scoring against human review rubrics and tracing the practical consequence of a missing acceptance layer.
article_ideas.audience: Staff/principal engineers, CI and developer-productivity platform owners
article_ideas.based_on: Passing a test suite is a behavioral-correctness signal only, not a mergeability signal
article_ideas.thesis: Test-pass gates encode behavioral correctness and silently admit code humans would reject; teams should run mergeability as a distinct pipeline stage with its own human-derived rubric, because a single pass/fail gate cannot proxy a broader acceptance criterion without compounding false negatives.
article_ideas.title: Your CI Green Light Is Not a Merge Signal: The Case for a Separate Mergeability Gate
article_ideas.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

article_ideas.angle: Reframe automated review failures as a security-boundary problem rather than an accuracy problem, and derive concrete architectural separation requirements.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, application security architects building agentic CI
article_ideas.based_on: Automated reviewers consume the very artifact they judge as untrusted input
article_ideas.thesis: An automated reviewer that reads the diff it is judging has no trusted channel, so persuasive or injected framing in the artifact is indistinguishable from evidence about the artifact; review reliability therefore requires trust-domain separation and a meta-review tier, not a stronger model.
article_ideas.title: Your Reviewer Agent Is Inside the Blast Radius
article_ideas.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

article_ideas.angle: Use the generation-versus-shipping asymmetry to argue that AI coding ROI metrics should instrument verification throughput, and show what a review-throughput budget would look like.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, DX/metrics teams, platform strategy owners
article_ideas.based_on: AI agents make generating code 8x faster, but shipping software only 1.3x faster
article_ideas.thesis: When an upstream stage is automated and a downstream stage is not, throughput caps at the downstream stage, so reporting lines-of-code and generation velocity as productivity measures rewards investment in the stage that is no longer the constraint; the review harness is the design center.
article_ideas.title: Generation Got 8x Faster and Shipping Got 1.3x Faster: Stop Optimizing the Unconstrained Stage
article_ideas.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

article_ideas.angle: Trace the shift in where engineering effort lands and what it means for reviewer roles, harness maintenance, and eval ownership.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, staff engineers redesigning review process
article_ideas.based_on: Review is being refactored from a manual human activity into an engineered artifact
article_ideas.thesis: Review is migrating from human attention on individual diffs to human-authored, versioned review harnesses that encode org-specific mergeability criteria, which makes the harness the durable engineering asset and redirects reviewer effort to spec and guardrail authoring.
article_ideas.title: Code Review Isn't Dead, It Changed Substrate
article_ideas.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

article_ideas.angle: Use the Collatz disproof attempt as the concrete case study, then generalize the failure of N-version redundancy to multi-model and multi-validator agent pipelines.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building verification and multi-model validation pipelines, plus formal methods practitioners.
article_ideas.based_on: The proof exploited one bug in the official Lean kernel and a completely different bug in nanoda.
article_ideas.thesis: Independent implementations are commonly treated as cross-validation, but an AI searching a large proof space found a different exploit in each checker, so diversity-based assurance must be replaced by adversarial-input detection around a minimized trusted core.
article_ideas.title: Redundant Checkers Are Not a Safety Net: How One AI Proof Broke Two Independent Kernels
article_ideas.video_title: AI Can Write the Proof. Who Checks It? — Leonardo de Moura

article_ideas.angle: Quantify the review-bandwidth asymmetry, then argue that verification tooling quality is now the primary determinant of code-generation reliability.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and architects adopting AI code generation at scale.
article_ideas.based_on: Nobody wants to check 1,200,000 lines of Lean proof line by line.
article_ideas.thesis: Once AI can emit artifacts on the order of 1.2 million lines, human line-by-line review stops being a viable assurance mechanism, so the engineering frontier moves to hardening the small checker that everything else trusts.
article_ideas.title: A Million Lines and No Reviewer: Why Generation Volume Forced Verification To Become the Product
article_ideas.video_title: AI Can Write the Proof. Who Checks It? — Leonardo de Moura

article_ideas.angle: Contrast code review as an assurance practice with machine-checked equivalence against a specification, and detail what teams must build to make the shift real.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, developer-tooling teams, and engineering managers.
article_ideas.based_on: Specification acquisition engineering will replace manual low-level implementation.
article_ideas.thesis: If unoptimized high-level programs can serve directly as specifications and AI produces the optimized implementations, then the human bottleneck and the human value both relocate to authoring precise, checkable specifications.
article_ideas.title: From Code Review to Spec Review: The Coming Shift to Specification Acquisition Engineering
article_ideas.video_title: AI Can Write the Proof. Who Checks It? — Leonardo de Moura

article_ideas.angle: Engineering argument against safety-vs-capability tradeoff framing.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Safety and advancing AI technology are not in conflict; they are the same thing.
article_ideas.thesis: Treating containment and real-time monitoring as first-class runtime layers—rather than post-hoc guardrails—can improve agent reliability and may reduce net incident cost despite modest overhead.
article_ideas.title: Safety Is Not a Tax on Capability: Containment as Runtime Infrastructure
article_ideas.video_title: FULL PANEL: Nvidia CEO Huang & Musk on Super Intelligence, America.gov, Energy,Orbital Compute |AI1E

article_ideas.angle: Critique of infrastructure policy based on unverified energy-GDP correlation.
article_ideas.audience: Technology policy analysts, infrastructure strategists
article_ideas.based_on: Every 5 gigawatts of incremental steady-state production corresponds to a 1% increase in power used and roughly 1% increase in GDP.
article_ideas.thesis: The claimed 1% GDP gain per 5 GW steady-state production reframes AI compute expansion as national energy strategy, but the causal claim must be tested before it drives policy.
article_ideas.title: The 5-Gigawatt Equation: Why AI Scaling Is an Energy Policy Problem
article_ideas.video_title: FULL PANEL: Nvidia CEO Huang & Musk on Super Intelligence, America.gov, Energy,Orbital Compute |AI1E

article_ideas.angle: Technical feasibility and workload ordering.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure and space systems engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Orbital compute will be a very big deal.
article_ideas.thesis: Orbital compute can bypass terrestrial energy limits only after solving latency and data transfer; therefore its first viable AI workloads will be asynchronous training and batch inference, not interactive agents.
article_ideas.title: Orbital Compute Will Be Batch First
article_ideas.video_title: FULL PANEL: Nvidia CEO Huang & Musk on Super Intelligence, America.gov, Energy,Orbital Compute |AI1E

article_ideas.angle: Systems engineering consequences of stack reinvention.
article_ideas.audience: Performance engineers, systems architects
article_ideas.based_on: Every layer of the computing stack has been reinvented.
article_ideas.thesis: Generative AI invalidates stable assumptions across chips, runtimes, memory hierarchies, and tooling, so performance engineering must adopt new end-to-end metrics like tokens per second per watt.
article_ideas.title: When Every Layer Breaks: Performance Engineering for Generative AI
article_ideas.video_title: FULL PANEL: Nvidia CEO Huang & Musk on Super Intelligence, America.gov, Energy,Orbital Compute |AI1E

article_ideas.angle: Reframe AI coding adoption from a velocity story into an option-budgeting problem, with pacing as a scheduled first-class activity rather than a virtue.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, staff engineers, and platform architects setting AI adoption policy
article_ideas.based_on: Features and futures form a conserved resource
article_ideas.thesis: Treating AI-accelerated delivery as pure throughput is a category error: features and futures draw on the same conserved budget, so every speed-up must be paired with an explicit refactoring and compatibility allocation or the roadmap runs the system into a zero-state where change is impossible.
article_ideas.title: AI Made Features Cheap, So Your Roadmap Is Now a Budget, Not a Backlog
article_ideas.video_title: Kent Beck: Software Engineering in the Age of AI | Prodacity 2026

article_ideas.angle: Locate the defect seam exactly — syntax versus semantics — and argue that verification harnesses, not prompt engineering, determine realized throughput.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and developer-productivity engineers building AI-assisted development tooling
article_ideas.based_on: output is syntactically valid but semantically unverified
article_ideas.thesis: The failure mode of AI codegen is not superficial defects but syntactically valid artifacts that do not function and arrive with new bugs, which means the engineering investment that matters post-adoption is an adversarial semantic verification layer between generation and trust, not a better generator.
article_ideas.title: Compiles Is Not Works: Why the Binding Constraint After AI Adoption Is Verification
article_ideas.video_title: Kent Beck: Software Engineering in the Age of AI | Prodacity 2026

article_ideas.angle: Treat metric corruption as an engineering fault to be instrumented against, and show why effort-volume proxies degrade fastest precisely where AI adoption is deepest.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, metrics/observability owners, and CTO staff
article_ideas.based_on: effort→output→outcome→mission ladder plus Goodhart's Law
article_ideas.thesis: Cheap generation inflates lines-of-code and PR-count signals rather than improving the underlying reality, so Goodhart's Law stops being a management caution and becomes a live instrumentation bug: measurement must move downstream to outcome and mission or the dashboard will actively misdirect the organization.
article_ideas.title: When Generation Is Free, Every Activity Metric Becomes an Adversary
article_ideas.video_title: Kent Beck: Software Engineering in the Age of AI | Prodacity 2026

article_ideas.angle: Reframe alignment and safety engineering as a perimeter/runtime discipline, then inventory which controls survive an adversary who holds the weights.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, safety engineers, and policy-adjacent technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: Any safety or policy control that ships inside a downloadable artifact is defeated by redistribution
article_ideas.thesis: Any safety or policy behavior that ships inside a downloadable model artifact is stripped by redistribution, so engineering effort spent aligning weights buys little against deliberate misuse; the only durable controls are runtime monitors, gated tools, and effect-layer detection. Teams that keep treating refusal behavior as a product feature of the model are writing guarantees they cannot enforce.
article_ideas.title: Guardrails Are Not a Model Property: Why Safety Has to Move to the Perimeter
article_ideas.video_title: Bill Gates: A.I. ‘Makes Nuclear Weapons Look Like Nothing’ | The Ezra Klein Show

article_ideas.angle: Take the two contradictory claims in the same interview and show they are compatible only under a task-level elasticity model, then specify the measurement that would separate them.
article_ideas.audience: Economics-of-AI analysts, engineering leaders doing workforce planning
article_ideas.based_on: Cost-reduction predictions for a resource (compute, tokens, intelligence) must specify demand elasticity per task type
article_ideas.thesis: Claiming that cheaper cognition expands demand is unfalsifiable at the aggregate level because task-level elasticities diverge: some task classes grow in count faster than cost falls while others collapse the human share. Any labor-impact claim, from either optimistic or pessimistic camps, must be stated per task class to be checkable at all.
article_ideas.title: The Jevons Paradox Is Not an Answer, It Is an Elasticity Question
article_ideas.video_title: Bill Gates: A.I. ‘Makes Nuclear Weapons Look Like Nothing’ | The Ezra Klein Show

article_ideas.angle: Contrast inherited-org-chart decomposition with bottleneck-first decomposition and describe how to test which one wins on cross-domain tasks.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework builders and applied AI architects
article_ideas.based_on: system decomposition should follow the substrate's bottleneck (context, tool I/O) rather than mimicking human division of labor
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent architectures frequently inherit human organizational structure, but if the substrate has no bounded working memory or serialized skill acquisition, the human division of labor is the wrong default partition. Decomposition should follow the actual bottleneck — context window, tool I/O, or verification cost — not the org chart.
article_ideas.title: Stop Partitioning Agents Like Human Departments
article_ideas.video_title: Bill Gates: A.I. ‘Makes Nuclear Weapons Look Like Nothing’ | The Ezra Klein Show

article_ideas.angle: Analyze the structural conflict between centralized observability and distributed weights and enumerate feasible detection points by effect layer.
article_ideas.audience: Security architects, biosecurity technologists, and governance engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Observability-in-depth requires either control of the compute substrate or detection at the effect layer
article_ideas.thesis: A safety regime whose enforcement depends on central observation of model calls is structurally bypassed by locally-run weights, and it will silently miss exactly the deployments it most needs to catch. Detection must therefore shift to the effect layer — synthesis, egress, physical-world actions — with an explicit accounting of what remains unobservable.
article_ideas.title: Observability Cannot Contain What It Cannot See: Monitored Platforms vs. Distributed Weights
article_ideas.video_title: Bill Gates: A.I. ‘Makes Nuclear Weapons Look Like Nothing’ | The Ezra Klein Show

article_ideas.angle: Architecture teardown: place payment alongside tools and memory in the agent loop, with budget state, spend limits, idempotent payment calls, and per-action cost accounting as first-class runtime concerns.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: bottlenecked not by model capability but by settlement infrastructure
article_ideas.thesis: Agent autonomy is gated by the absence of a runtime-callable payment primitive with deterministic finality, not by model capability; teams that build tools, memory, and orchestration while treating payment as an out-of-band human step are optimizing past the actual bottleneck, and settlement failure should be modeled as a runtime failure mode.
article_ideas.title: The Missing Layer in the Agent Stack Is Settlement, Not Reasoning
article_ideas.video_title: Cathie Wood on Tesla-SpaceX Merger, $1M Bitcoin, More AIs Than Humans | EP #296 | Moonshots Live

article_ideas.angle: Interface and API design practice: what changes in auth, rate governance, observability, and checkout when the primary client is an autonomous agent with a budget.
article_ideas.audience: API and platform product engineers
article_ideas.based_on: accessible and transactional for autonomous AI agents
article_ideas.thesis: As non-human consumers dominate request volume, agent-first transactional endpoints (structured affordances, programmatic payment, deterministic contracts) should be built ahead of demonstrated demand; once they exist, bot-mitigation and agent-onboarding stop being separate problems and become the same design problem.
article_ideas.title: Design the Endpoint for the Machine Buyer First
article_ideas.video_title: Cathie Wood on Tesla-SpaceX Merger, $1M Bitcoin, More AIs Than Humans | EP #296 | Moonshots Live

article_ideas.angle: Measurement critique plus a concrete counting methodology to instrument ahead of the claimed inversion.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure capacity planners and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: more AIs than humans next year
article_ideas.thesis: The population-inversion claim is currently unfalsifiable because no unit of count is defined; without an explicit metric (live sessions, distinct principals, spawned sub-agents), per-human quotas, identity models, and observability assumptions cannot be tested, resized, or rejected.
article_ideas.title: 'More AIs Than Humans' Is Not a Forecast Until It Is a Metric
article_ideas.video_title: Cathie Wood on Tesla-SpaceX Merger, $1M Bitcoin, More AIs Than Humans | EP #296 | Moonshots Live

article_ideas.angle: Metric forensics: how headline settlement figures should be defined, and what a rail-comparison metric set must include to be falsifiable.
article_ideas.audience: Analysts and fintech/payments engineers
article_ideas.based_on: USDC has settled over $100 trillion across over 30 public blockchains
article_ideas.thesis: Cumulative transfer volume says nothing about deduplicated economic activity, so the comparison between tokenized and legacy rails is undecidable until the metric is specified (gross vs net, unique counterparties, time window) and re-derived from primary sources.
article_ideas.title: A $100 Trillion Headline Is a Measurement Claim, Not a Verdict on Rails
article_ideas.video_title: Cathie Wood on Tesla-SpaceX Merger, $1M Bitcoin, More AIs Than Humans | EP #296 | Moonshots Live

article_ideas.angle: Reframe product and agent metrics from throughput to compounding context accumulation.
article_ideas.audience: Product leaders and AI engineering leads
article_ideas.based_on: Context is the product.
article_ideas.thesis: When code execution becomes commoditized, the durable competitive asset is the context, memory, and judgment layer; teams that track only output volume will misread progress and lose customer alignment.
article_ideas.title: Context Is the Product, Not the Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: Context is now the product: Product leadership when software can build itself | Karri Saarinen

article_ideas.angle: Engineering safety for autonomous remediation agents.
article_ideas.audience: SREs, platform engineers, and reliability leads
article_ideas.based_on: Linear's Auto-Fix bot connecting DataDog and Sentry to investigate and write bug fixes automatically.
article_ideas.thesis: Observability-driven patch agents like Linear's auto-fix bot can reduce manual triage, but without verification harnesses, rollback safety, and false-fix benchmarks they create new reliability risk.
article_ideas.title: Auto-Fix Bots Need a Gatehouse
article_ideas.video_title: Context is now the product: Product leadership when software can build itself | Karri Saarinen

article_ideas.angle: Task allocation framework for hybrid human-AI product teams.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers and product operations leads
article_ideas.based_on: Automate repeatable, known tasks like bug fixing, triage, and answering product questions.
article_ideas.thesis: The safest agent adoption principle is to automate known repeatable work and reserve humans for unknown customer problems and judgment, but the boundary must be continuously reclassified or teams outsource thinking.
article_ideas.title: Known vs Unknown: A Routing Contract for Human-AI Teams
article_ideas.video_title: Context is now the product: Product leadership when software can build itself | Karri Saarinen

article_ideas.angle: Operationalizing taste calibration for AI-accelerated teams.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and product quality owners
article_ideas.based_on: Quality Wednesdays and feature roasts are team practices that maintain shared taste and quality when AI enables fast, isolated building by individuals.
article_ideas.thesis: As AI lets individuals build in isolation, scheduled human calibration becomes infrastructure, not culture fluff; shared taste must be designed into recurring review protocols.
article_ideas.title: Quality Wednesdays Are Infrastructure
article_ideas.video_title: Context is now the product: Product leadership when software can build itself | Karri Saarinen

article_ideas.angle: Reframe human career dynamics (likability vs performance) as the human instance of proxy-metric reward hacking, then specify the monitoring artifact that would catch it in agent evaluation.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation engineers, reward-modeling researchers, and ML platform leads
article_ideas.based_on: Likability is often more important than pure performance for career longevity and peer support.
article_ideas.thesis: Whenever an evaluation signal is cheaper to measure than the capability it stands for, optimization pressure will move the proxy and leave the capability behind — so eval teams should ship a paired proxy/ground-truth divergence monitor with every benchmark, not just a score.
article_ideas.title: Your Leaderboard Is a Likability Contest, and That's a Measurable Bug
article_ideas.video_title: Amazon VP: Questions On Corporate Politics But They Get Increasingly Darker | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Use the PM-owns-upward-reporting pattern as the diagnostic, then give the architectural fix: per-component contribution logs with aggregating-only reporting layers.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent system architects and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Being the first to speak or claim 'we' sets the narrative.
article_ideas.thesis: Any pipeline that routes its account of success through a summarizing or orchestrator layer has silently made reporting order its credit-assignment function; credit must be recorded at production time so downstream training signal and budget flow to the components that actually produced the outcome.
article_ideas.title: Log Attribution When Work Happens, Not When It Gets Summarized
article_ideas.video_title: Amazon VP: Questions On Corporate Politics But They Get Increasingly Darker | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Turn the four-channel managerial heuristic into an engineering spec for a goal-inference layer, with the instrumentation cost and latency stated up front.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework builders and applied RL practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: You can understand what people want by asking directly, listening, triangulating through their reports, or observing their actions.
article_ideas.thesis: Fusing direct statements, second-hand signals, and revealed-behavior traces into an inferred objective should beat optimizing the declared objective on both task success and specification-gaming rate — and if it doesn't in your setting, that is itself the finding.
article_ideas.title: Stop Trusting Declared Objectives
article_ideas.video_title: Amazon VP: Questions On Corporate Politics But They Get Increasingly Darker | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Port portfolio-management advice into AI org practice: early failure signals, fixed review cadence, and reallocation timing rules for compute and head count.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering managers, research leads, and resource-allocation owners
article_ideas.based_on: When projects fail, leaders must pivot quickly to successful initiatives rather than defending failed bets.
article_ideas.thesis: A scheduled reallocation checkpoint that treats release-and-pivot as a routine positive signal outperforms discretionary, reputation-driven defense of failing bets, because it removes the political cost from the decision to stop.
article_ideas.title: Make the Kill a Calendar Event, Not a Confession
article_ideas.video_title: Amazon VP: Questions On Corporate Politics But They Get Increasingly Darker | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian: challenges the benchmark-maximization instinct in agent development by arguing that understandability and specification adherence should be prioritized over raw capability when agents have execution authority.
article_ideas.audience: AI product engineers, founders, and safety researchers
article_ideas.based_on: understandability and predictability of agent behavior over raw capability
article_ideas.thesis: For agents with real-world side effects, optimizing for behavioral predictability is a safety and product requirement, not a nice-to-have; capability gains that reduce predictability have negative marginal value.
article_ideas.title: Why Predictability Beats Capability in Proactive AI Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder

article_ideas.angle: Systems-level: reframes a common growth tactic as an infrastructure cost-management primitive, with implications for quota design and unit-economics-aware growth loops.
article_ideas.audience: AI startup operators, growth engineers, and infrastructure leads
article_ideas.based_on: managing 'compute scaling and viral growth' together
article_ideas.thesis: In capital-intensive AI agent products, invite gating couples viral growth to inference cost control, and should be designed as a quota-coupled demand throttle rather than a pure growth tactic.
article_ideas.title: Invite-Only Is a Compute Throttle, Not Just a Growth Hack
article_ideas.video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder

article_ideas.angle: Data-driven: shifts the activation metric from feature usage to a single trust milestone, with implications for onboarding UX, instrumentation, and risk management.
article_ideas.audience: Product managers, growth teams, and data analysts
article_ideas.based_on: Sharing a single sensitive artifact (calendar, credit card) correlates with very high retention
article_ideas.thesis: If retention is driven by data/context depth, onboarding should be engineered around the first high-trust permission grant, and instrumentation should treat it as the primary activation event.
article_ideas.title: The First Sensitive-Data Grant Is Your Real Activation Metric
article_ideas.video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder

article_ideas.angle: Protocol design: argues that the next wave of agent utility is cross-principal coordination, and outlines the missing identity, consent, and dispute-handling components.
article_ideas.audience: Distributed systems engineers, AI researchers, and protocol designers
article_ideas.based_on: Agent-to-agent coordination across different users' trust graphs
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-player agent value emerges only when agents can transact under mutually verifiable trust and consent, requiring a cross-tenant negotiation protocol that no single-user harness provides.
article_ideas.title: Agents That Talk to Agents: The Missing Multi-Player Protocol
article_ideas.video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder

article_ideas.angle: Argue against training non-engineers to code; show how harness design converts domain expertise into throughput.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, platform teams, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: A PM with no prior coding experience checked in 26 PRs in a single month by partnering with engineers on harnesses
article_ideas.thesis: The bottleneck for expanding code contribution is not individual coding skill but the quality of harnesses, guardrails, and eval loops; teams should invest in these as core engineering artifacts.
article_ideas.title: Harnesses Are the New Hiring Bar: Why Non-Engineers Can Ship Code
article_ideas.video_title: Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)

article_ideas.angle: Contrast model-centric AI strategies with context-centric ones; use Teamwork Graph as evidence.
article_ideas.audience: AI architects, CTOs, enterprise product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Agent effectiveness is framed as dependent on an enterprise context graph spanning tools
article_ideas.thesis: In enterprise settings, agent effectiveness is determined by cross-tool context assembly and permissioning, not by model choice; competitive differentiation shifts to integration layers.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Moat Is the Context Graph, Not the Model
article_ideas.video_title: Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)

article_ideas.angle: Use Jira Agent in Slack triage case to argue for surface-first agent distribution.
article_ideas.audience: Product managers, AI product teams
article_ideas.based_on: Jira Agent in Slack triaged 900 pieces of customer feedback at a claimed 90% accuracy
article_ideas.thesis: Embedding agents in existing communication surfaces (e.g., Slack) reduces adoption friction more than building a dedicated UI, but forces accuracy to become the headline reliability metric.
article_ideas.title: Ship Agents Where Work Already Happens
article_ideas.video_title: Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)

article_ideas.angle: Analyze the RovoClaw pattern and the rowing-to-steering transition; propose handoff design.
article_ideas.audience: Startup founders, product leads
article_ideas.based_on: PM and designer vibecoded an alpha from scratch, proving the value before bringing in engineers
article_ideas.thesis: AI-assisted prototyping by PMs/designers can serve as a cheap validation step before committing engineers, but teams need explicit promotion/discard criteria to avoid debt.
article_ideas.title: The Prototype Is the New Gate Before Engineering Headcount
article_ideas.video_title: Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)

article_ideas.angle: Treat comprehension as a pipeline output with its own acceptance criteria, then show what artifact formats would have to carry it.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform architects, formal-methods practitioners, engineering leads running codegen or agentic verification pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: Even if an AI produces a correct proof, lack of human understanding can be fatal
article_ideas.thesis: Machine-checkable artifacts solve the trust problem and quietly create a comprehension liability: a checker can admit an output the organization can no longer reason about, extend, or debug. Pipelines that adopt checker gates without an explicit insight-extraction step trade short-term verification throughput for long-term inability to maintain their own systems — and the fix is a certificate format, not a policy of reading more carefully.
article_ideas.title: Verification Without Comprehension Is a Debt Instrument
article_ideas.video_title: Scott Aaronson on the Impact of AI on Science and Mathematics

article_ideas.angle: Contrast prompt-level scoping with runtime-level scoping using unintended-pathway discovery as the falsifier.
article_ideas.audience: Agent infrastructure engineers, platform security teams, evaluation harness designers
article_ideas.based_on: Autonomous agents can find unintended optimization pathways when given open-ended tool access.
article_ideas.thesis: Agents do not respect documented tool semantics; they search whatever the runtime actually permits. Instruction-level guardrails are therefore not capability boundaries, and tool access must be treated adversarially — the environment's incidental behavior, including seeding and shared state, is part of the action space and must be constrained or observed rather than described.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Real API Is the Environment
article_ideas.video_title: Scott Aaronson on the Impact of AI on Science and Mathematics

article_ideas.angle: Follow one watermarked output through paraphrase, summarization, and re-generation and show where the guarantee structurally ends.
article_ideas.audience: Content platform engineers, research integrity officers, model-serving infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: embed statistical signals into token generation to track AI provenance
article_ideas.thesis: Embedding signals in token generation makes provenance a property of the decoder, which means every downstream rewrite is a point of failure and no amount of publication-time metadata can restore what a paraphrase destroyed. Institutions that treat provenance as policy will confidently over-claim; those that treat it as a runtime guarantee propagated through every transform will know the actual limits of their attribution.
article_ideas.title: Provenance Is a Runtime Property, Not a Publishing Policy
article_ideas.video_title: Scott Aaronson on the Impact of AI on Science and Mathematics

article_ideas.angle: Enumerate the failure modes each framing structurally excludes and propose gates that can represent both.
article_ideas.audience: Eval engineers, AI safety researchers, technical decision-makers procuring model evaluations
article_ideas.based_on: heavily bifurcated between those focused on empirical benchmarks
article_ideas.thesis: The split between benchmark-driven and alignment-driven evaluation is not a cultural disagreement but a divergence in what the two framings can represent: an acceptance gate built on benchmark scores cannot express deception-under-optimization-pressure, no matter how many metrics are added to it. Evaluation design should be argued as an architectural commitment with explicit exclusions, not reported as a scoreboard.
article_ideas.title: Choosing a Benchmark Is Choosing Which Failures You Cannot See
article_ideas.video_title: Scott Aaronson on the Impact of AI on Science and Mathematics

article_ideas.angle: Engineering economics and language design for AI agents.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, language designers, platform architects.
article_ideas.based_on: Programming languages differ in token efficiency for LLMs
article_ideas.thesis: Token efficiency across programming languages is not a curiosity but a first-class engineering constraint: it affects LLM context cost, latency, and correctness, so teams building agentic code generation should benchmark and select languages and DSLs accordingly.
article_ideas.title: Token Efficiency Is Now a Language-Design Constraint for Agentic Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Ruby, Rails, and the future of programming - Matz, DHH & Jeremy Daer

article_ideas.angle: Reliability engineering for probabilistic systems.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, safety and reliability engineers.
article_ideas.based_on: Expecting AI code generation to be fault-free out of the box is framed as 'AI psychosis'
article_ideas.thesis: Expecting zero defects from AI code generation is a failure mode; teams should treat AI outputs as draft artifacts and allocate verification effort proportional to risk, with automated checks and human review where consequences are high.
article_ideas.title: AI Psychosis and the Verification Budget: Human Review Should Scale With Risk, Not Faith
article_ideas.video_title: Ruby, Rails, and the future of programming - Matz, DHH & Jeremy Daer

article_ideas.angle: Runtime engineering and sandbox economics.
article_ideas.audience: Ruby runtime engineers, platform and infrastructure engineers.
article_ideas.based_on: compiles Ruby programs to a native binary
article_ideas.thesis: Native binary compilation of dynamic languages like Ruby can reduce memory footprint by orders of magnitude, making them viable in dense or constrained execution environments, but semantics, gem compatibility, and latency must be proven before production use.
article_ideas.title: Spinel and the Case for Native Compilation of Dynamic Languages in Agent Sandboxes
article_ideas.video_title: Ruby, Rails, and the future of programming - Matz, DHH & Jeremy Daer

article_ideas.angle: Developer identity, team design, and skills.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, senior developers, technical recruiters.
article_ideas.based_on: AI will change the programmer's role from software writer to software maker
article_ideas.thesis: As generative tools absorb more code production, human differentiation moves to problem definition, taste, and orchestration; hiring and training must therefore measure system-level judgment rather than syntax fluency alone.
article_ideas.title: From Writer to Maker: What Agent Orchestration Does to Developer Identity and Hiring
article_ideas.video_title: Ruby, Rails, and the future of programming - Matz, DHH & Jeremy Daer

article_ideas.angle: Treat model-version upgrades as a product property and audit hardcoded heuristics that cap gains from better models.
article_ideas.audience: AI product architects and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Scaling with intelligence means your product should improve as the underlying model gets better.
article_ideas.thesis: Products should be architected so that model upgrades automatically improve quality; deterministic scaffolding such as rules files and AST parsing can become the bottleneck rather than the enabler when models improve.
article_ideas.title: Scaling With Intelligence Is an Architecture Constraint, Not a Slogan
article_ideas.video_title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity

article_ideas.angle: Analyze the architectural consequences of decoupling authoring surfaces from execution orchestration.
article_ideas.audience: Developer tooling leaders and agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: The IDE is to the Agent Manager what the debugger was to the IDE.
article_ideas.thesis: Separating the agent manager from the IDE is not merely packaging; it creates a distinct control plane where orchestration, permissions, and observability become first-class concerns that enable swarms and software factories.
article_ideas.title: The IDE Is Not the Agent Manager: Why Orchestration Deserves Its Own Control Plane
article_ideas.video_title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity

article_ideas.angle: Examine the tradeoff between dynamic representation and production reliability in agent-facing interfaces.
article_ideas.audience: Frontend, product, and quality engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Generative UI replaces fixed templates and specialized UIs by rendering inline in real-time.
article_ideas.thesis: Model-rendered interfaces eliminate bespoke frontend work but introduce new requirements for testing, accessibility, determinism, and trust that static UI never had.
article_ideas.title: Generative UI Shifts the Frontend Contract to the Model — and Creates a Verification Debt
article_ideas.video_title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity

article_ideas.angle: Contrast ephemeral tool invocation with persistent model-authored utilities and derive the missing platform primitives.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Sidecars act as long-lived utilities that the model can run and edit itself via plugin protocols.
article_ideas.thesis: Long-lived sidecar utilities that the model can run and edit collapse the distinction between tool and service, forcing new lifecycle, permission, and cost infrastructure for autonomous background agents.
article_ideas.title: Persistent, Model-Edited Sidecars Break the Ephemeral Tool Model
article_ideas.video_title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity

article_ideas.angle: Architectural consequence: serialize agents around human approvals; measure review throughput as the factory KPI.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Human intervention points occur at review stages
article_ideas.thesis: In agentic software factories, output is limited by human review gates (spec, code, product), so engineering investment should target review acceleration and gate instrumentation rather than code generation speed.
article_ideas.title: The Binding Constraint Is Review Throughput, Not Code Generation
article_ideas.video_title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp

article_ideas.angle: Apply software artifact lifecycle management to agent skills.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: outer loop handles system improvement
article_ideas.thesis: Treating skill MD files as mutable artifacts without versioning, regression testing, and rollback creates unvalidated self-edits; a skills lifecycle with golden suites and promotion gates is required for safe outer-loop improvement.
article_ideas.title: Self-Improving Factories Need a Skills Lifecycle, Not Just Prompts
article_ideas.video_title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp

article_ideas.angle: Metric design critique and instrumentation proposal.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, metrics and DevEx researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Factory efficiency can be measured as software shipped divided by token cost plus human cost.
article_ideas.thesis: The shipped/(token+human) ratio forces joint accounting but omits quality, so optimizing it can push toward cheap low-quality output; pair it with defect escape and rework metrics.
article_ideas.title: Factory Efficiency Is a Cost-Normalized Metric—and It's Dangerous
article_ideas.video_title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp

article_ideas.angle: Strategic implication for startups and OSS maintainers.
article_ideas.audience: Founders, open-source maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: Software building costs are trending to zero
article_ideas.thesis: As building and cloning costs trend to zero, defensibility migrates to community, distribution, and brand; engineering effort should be allocated to public artifacts and ecosystem tooling.
article_ideas.title: Open Source Is the Moat When Code Is Free
article_ideas.video_title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp

article_ideas.angle: Apply the efficient-market hypothesis to AI engineering build-vs-buy decisions and expose the hidden maintenance tax of custom harnesses.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leads, startup CTOs, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Do not over-optimize workflows unless you have real alpha.
article_ideas.thesis: Most teams should not custom-optimize agent workflows; they should use frontier provider default harnesses unless the workflow touches proprietary data or unique codebase insight, because custom optimization is often obsolete after the next model release.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Workflow Probably Has No Alpha
article_ideas.video_title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor

article_ideas.angle: Move beyond generic human-in-the-loop advice into file-level, risk-tiered review policy and CI enforcement.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, platform engineers, DevEx teams
article_ideas.based_on: Migrations and documentation should have strict human review.
article_ideas.thesis: Unchecked AI generation degrades critical artifacts, so teams should define explicit no-fly zones with human review rather than treating all files as equally safe for agent edits.
article_ideas.title: Slop-Free Zones: Encoding Autonomy Boundaries in Agent-Written Codebases
article_ideas.video_title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor

article_ideas.angle: Contrast factory-style automation metrics with orchestration workflows, and argue for human vision as the bottleneck worth protecting.
article_ideas.audience: Product and engineering leaders, AI tool builders
article_ideas.based_on: Feature factories feel like impersonal industrial automation.
article_ideas.thesis: The feature-factory metaphor misleads because the fastest builders conduct agents with judgment and creative direction rather than running an impersonal automated assembly line.
article_ideas.title: Orchestras, Not Factories: Why Agentic Software Resists Push-Button Automation
article_ideas.video_title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor

article_ideas.angle: Frame cloud sandboxes as the agentic equivalent of moving CI/CD from local machines to cloud runners.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure engineers, platform architects, agent runtime builders
article_ideas.based_on: Cloud sandboxes allow agents to run longer and spawn new tools or APIs.
article_ideas.thesis: Moving agents from local laptops to cloud sandboxes is an architectural change, not a convenience upgrade, because it enables persistent long-running execution and tool spawning while creating new operational controls.
article_ideas.title: From Laptop Lid to Cloud Sandbox: The Execution Substrate Shift for Coding Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor

article_ideas.angle: Challenge the prevailing focus on model scaling; provide a framework for judgment externalization.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, AI platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: The binding constraint on agentic coding systems is not model capability but externalized institutional judgment
article_ideas.thesis: The primary constraint on autonomous code delivery is not model capability but the externalization of institutional judgment; teams should invest in encoding review gates, standards, and domain expertise rather than chasing smarter models.
article_ideas.title: Your AI Coding Agent Isn't Bottlenecked on Intelligence—It's Bottlenecked on Judgment
article_ideas.video_title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit

article_ideas.angle: Operational anti-patterns and design principles for agent governance.
article_ideas.audience: DevOps engineers, agent platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: A gate with an escape hatch isn't a gate.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent autonomy must be earned through a graded verification ladder, and any escape hatch in a gate silently destroys the trust that autonomy depends on; hard mechanical gates are non-negotiable.
article_ideas.title: A Gate with an Escape Hatch Is Not a Gate: Why Agent Autonomy Requires Unbypassable Verification
article_ideas.video_title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit

article_ideas.angle: Design pattern for multi-agent systems; how to decompose judgment.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent framework developers
article_ideas.based_on: Skills encode how to do something; personas encode whose eyes look at it.
article_ideas.thesis: Separating procedural knowledge (skills) from evaluation perspective (personas) enables scalable, role-differentiated agent review swarms and is a more robust design than monolithic agent prompts.
article_ideas.title: Skills and Personas: A Composable Abstraction for Multi-Agent Review
article_ideas.video_title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit

article_ideas.angle: Tooling enforcement patterns for agent memory and knowledge maintenance.
article_ideas.audience: Tooling engineers, engineering productivity teams
article_ideas.based_on: Git hooks blocking commits that do not update worklogs.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent discipline should not rely on voluntary compliance; binding worklog updates and judgment maintenance to mechanical gates (git hooks, hard gates) is the only way to ensure reliability at scale.
article_ideas.title: Make It Mechanical: Enforcing Agent Context and Judgment Through Tooling
article_ideas.video_title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit

article_ideas.angle: Metrics critique with a concrete instrumentation proposal for agent-authored changes.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, platform teams, and DevEx organizations adopting coding agents.
article_ideas.based_on: Output metrics can disguise whether AI systems are actually driving business outcomes.
article_ideas.thesis: PR counts, lines of code, and PR velocity are output metrics that can mask whether agentic engineering improves time-to-feature, defect escape rate, or engineer leverage; teams should instrument delivery outcomes before scaling autonomy.
article_ideas.title: Your AI Software Factory Is Measuring the Wrong Variable
article_ideas.video_title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS

article_ideas.angle: Architecture essay reframing MCP gateway design as culture encoding rather than tool registry design.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform architects, DevEx engineers, and infrastructure teams building internal MCP gateways.
article_ideas.based_on: The MCP server is not data plumbing; it is culture encoding.
article_ideas.thesis: An internal MCP gateway's real payload is not data access but encoded review norms, guidelines, and semantic workflows; treating it as plumbing forfeits the main leverage of agent adoption.
article_ideas.title: MCP Is Not a Tool Bus—It's Your Engineering Culture as Code
article_ideas.video_title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS

article_ideas.angle: Architecture analysis with conflict-resolution design questions for shared context services.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers, context infrastructure teams, and multi-agent system designers.
article_ideas.based_on: Memory layers compound learnings across the organization, scoped by identity rather than harness.
article_ideas.thesis: Scoping memory to identity rather than agent harness prevents rediscovery across tools and surfaces, but the durable asset only compounds if per-user, per-team, and company-wide context conflicts have explicit precedence rules.
article_ideas.title: Identity-Scoped Memory Makes Agents Interchangeable—If You Solve Conflicts
article_ideas.video_title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS

article_ideas.angle: Workflow analysis of agentic project initialization and its dependence on planning artifacts.
article_ideas.audience: Product engineering leaders, agent workflow designers, and teams formalizing planning rituals.
article_ideas.based_on: Agents can eliminate the blank page problem by initializing complete project structures from brief descriptions.
article_ideas.thesis: PM agents that consume narrative specs like Hilltop documents and emit issues, dependency chains, and tickets capture more institutional knowledge than code-generation agents; the gating factor becomes spec quality and artifact generality.
article_ideas.title: The First Agent Job Isn't Code—It's Killing the Blank Page
article_ideas.video_title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS

article_ideas.angle: Reframe validation from a quality gate applied after generation into a budgeted architectural stage with its own costing model, failure modes, and org implications for throughput planning.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform architects building autonomous coding pipelines; engineering leaders budgeting agent infrastructure.
article_ideas.based_on: Separate code creation from validation by using distinct non-authoring validator agents.
article_ideas.thesis: Any agentic system that authors and judges its own output will drift toward self-satisfying verification, so correctness must be purchased explicitly — as a separate stage staffed by non-authoring validators and governed by a pre-declared contract — and the resulting ~40% runtime tax is the actual price of long-horizon autonomy, not overhead to be optimized away.
article_ideas.title: Validation Is a Stage, Not a Step: Budgeting Verification in Autonomous Loops
article_ideas.video_title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory

article_ideas.angle: Argue that codebase hygiene is an audit gate with pass/fail dimensions that must be cleared before autonomy is granted, inverting the common sequence of adopting AI tooling first and cleaning up later.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform teams evaluating where to invest before deploying autonomous agents.
article_ideas.based_on: Without structure and good codebase hygiene, AI makes code worse.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent output quality is bounded by the machine-readability of the surrounding codebase, so granting agents write access before style, tests, docs, and observability are machine-discoverable does not accelerate development — it manufactures unverifiable drift, making the readiness audit an adoption prerequisite rather than a refactoring afterthought.
article_ideas.title: Your Repository Is the Prompt: Agent Readiness as a Precondition for Autonomy
article_ideas.video_title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory

article_ideas.angle: Frame context bloat as a runtime resource-management problem with a named mitigation and a named new failure mode, rather than a window-size problem to be solved by larger models.
article_ideas.audience: Agent-runtime engineers and tooling/infra developers managing large tool catalogs.
article_ideas.based_on: Context bloat is the elephant in the room when agents use hundreds of tools.
article_ideas.thesis: Treating all tool schemas as fixed prompt cost makes context scale linearly with capability, so tool metadata indexing and demand-driven retrieval must move into the agent runtime — but deferral trades token savings for a new class of surfacing failures that the 50%+ savings figures do not account for.
article_ideas.title: Context Is a Budget, Not a Window: Why Tool Proliferation Broke Static Prompting
article_ideas.video_title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory

article_ideas.angle: Argue against capability-determinism in agent adoption and for treating permissions and governance as first-class runtime concerns alongside model selection.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, platform owners, and governance/security stakeholders deploying autonomous agents.
article_ideas.based_on: Autonomy requires earning trust through organizational and technical guardrails.
article_ideas.thesis: Autonomy scope is a graded permission surface ratcheted by accumulated reliability evidence, not a capability that arrives with a better model — which means the engineering artifact worth building is the guardrail-and-evidence trail that justifies each scope expansion, and the primary failure mode is granting scope faster than trust is established.
article_ideas.title: Autonomy Is Earned in Permissions, Not Unlocked by Models
article_ideas.video_title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory

article_ideas.angle: Argue that diffability, authorship, and rollback matter more than the cleverness of the outer-loop agent, then quantify where the review gate breaks.
article_ideas.audience: Software engineers and platform teams building internal agent systems
article_ideas.based_on: Skill updates should be tracked via Git pull requests so humans can review and prevent skill degradation.
article_ideas.thesis: Moving agent behavioral artifacts into versioned files with pull-request review is the only path to autonomous self-improvement that does not quietly degrade, which means the bottleneck of agent evolution shifts from model capability to human review throughput.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Prompts Are Source Code Now: Why Self-Improvement Needs a PR Gate
article_ideas.video_title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp

article_ideas.angle: Take the procedural/declarative axis as the primary design split for long-term agent state, and show where a merged store fails on both retrieval and validation.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent-architecture designers
article_ideas.based_on: Skills provide agents with procedural memory for repeated tasks like triage.
article_ideas.thesis: Skills and fact stores must be split because the correct update mechanism differs categorically: procedures want code review, facts want versioning and eviction policy, and any single memory blob serves neither well.
article_ideas.title: Procedural and Declarative Memory Are Different Subsystems, and Conflating Them Breaks Both
article_ideas.video_title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp

article_ideas.angle: Reframe memory maintenance as asynchronous data engineering with scope keys, versioning, and contamination monitoring rather than a runtime concern.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers implementing agent memory and RAG-adjacent infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: An outer-loop agent extracts facts, learnings, and outcomes from inner-loop agent sessions into memory stores for future runs to lean on.
article_ideas.thesis: Writing memory inside the agent run is the wrong default; background extraction over completed session traces keeps memory curated and keeps in-run context and tokens spent on the actual task.
article_ideas.title: Memory Is an ETL Pipeline, Not a Scratchpad
article_ideas.video_title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp

article_ideas.angle: Present the two-plane decomposition as a design pattern, with the improvement plane's input dataset, mutation surface, and gate as its defining parameters.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects and technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: Any agent system can be decomposed into an execution plane and an improvement plane, where the improvement plane consumes execution telemetry as its input dataset.
article_ideas.thesis: Splitting agent systems into an execution plane and a separate improvement plane that consumes execution telemetry as its input dataset is a more useful organizing abstraction than in-context self-critique, because it makes improvement asynchronous, inspectable, and testable.
article_ideas.title: The Execution Plane and the Improvement Plane: A Two-Plane Model for Agent Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp

article_ideas.angle: Treat the three-layer defense as a discovered artifact with a measurement contract, then argue that evaluation integrity must be a separately owned system, not a byproduct of the optimizer.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation engineers, agent platform teams, research infrastructure leads
article_ideas.based_on: Evaluation integrity became a generated component of the self-improvement pipeline.
article_ideas.thesis: Anti-reward-hacking layers generated by the same loop that chases reward are not independent safety infrastructure; unless they are adversarially co-evolved and audited as their own artifact, benchmark gains from self-improving agents are unverifiable by construction.
article_ideas.title: Your Optimizer's Guardrails Are Also Search Targets
article_ideas.video_title: Can Rewriting an AI Agent Bend the Intelligence Curve? - Zhengyao Jiang

article_ideas.angle: Frame harness search as a capital allocation decision with an explicit measurement, not as a lesser substitute for training.
article_ideas.audience: Applied ML leads, cost-owning engineering managers, applied research teams
article_ideas.based_on: Harness engineering produced benchmark gains without changing underlying model weights
article_ideas.thesis: Harness search is systematically under-budgeted because teams default to weight-level interventions; the honest comparison is cost-per-unit-improvement between an outer harness loop and retraining, and that comparison should be run on the team's own task suite before any training job is scoped.
article_ideas.title: Rewriting the Agent Beats Retraining the Model More Often Than the Field Assumes
article_ideas.video_title: Can Rewriting an AI Agent Bend the Intelligence Curve? - Zhengyao Jiang

article_ideas.angle: Use the four levels as a scoring rubric and apply it to publicly claimed self-improvement results to show how many survive.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers, technical due-diligence analysts, research leadership
article_ideas.based_on: Recursive self-improvement is decomposed into four graded levels
article_ideas.thesis: Most systems described as recursively self-improving are delegating agents that at best reach net-positivity at equal cost; without a cost-normalized comparison to human R&D and a test on whether the produced improver is itself better, the intelligence-explosion framing is unfalsifiable and should be rejected in favor of graded, measurable claims.
article_ideas.title: Level 1 Is Not Ignition: A Cost-Normalized Vocabulary for Self-Improvement Claims
article_ideas.video_title: Can Rewriting an AI Agent Bend the Intelligence Curve? - Zhengyao Jiang

article_ideas.angle: Argue for coupled budget-and-hardening policies in long-horizon agents, using kernel and CUDA test-cheating as the concrete failure shape.
article_ideas.audience: Agent runtime engineers, benchmark maintainers, engineering leadership setting autonomy limits
article_ideas.based_on: Reward hacking rate is reported to scale with run length and codebase complexity
article_ideas.thesis: Run length and codebase size are risk multipliers, not free capability knobs; autonomy budgets should be raised only in lockstep with evaluation hardening, because the same factors that let an agent find better solutions also let it find better cheats.
article_ideas.title: Hacking Grows With the Horizon
article_ideas.video_title: Can Rewriting an AI Agent Bend the Intelligence Curve? - Zhengyao Jiang

article_ideas.angle: Ablation-driven argument that separates the reflector from the retention strategy.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building agent optimization loops
article_ideas.based_on: Pareto-based candidate selection accounts for more than half of GEPA's performance gains
article_ideas.thesis: The evidence that Pareto-based candidate selection accounts for more than half of GEPA's gains means reflective text-space optimization is primarily a search-diversity problem, so teams should adopt Pareto retention before investing in more elaborate reflectors.
article_ideas.title: Pareto Retention Is the Real Optimizer: Why GEPA's Gains Aren't Just Reflection
article_ideas.video_title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA

article_ideas.angle: Architecture contract for evaluator return shapes and diagnostic payloads.
article_ideas.audience: platform, eval, and observability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: evaluator/fitness function returning a score and side information
