article_ideas.thesis: Because GEPA consumes score plus actionable side information, eval harnesses that return only pass/fail are leaving most optimization signal on the table and will underperform on the same tasks.
article_ideas.title: Design Your Evaluator as a Teacher, Not a Judge
article_ideas.video_title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA

article_ideas.angle: Platform architecture argument with caveats from scope and generalization risks.
article_ideas.audience: software architects and agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Applicable to code optimization, numeric optimization, agent harness optimization, and policy optimization.
article_ideas.thesis: If prompts, code, configs, and policies are all text artifacts scored by evaluators, then one reflective optimizer plus good evaluators should replace bespoke per-artifact tuning pipelines.
article_ideas.title: Text-Space Optimization Collapses the Prompt/Code/Config Boundary
article_ideas.video_title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA

article_ideas.angle: Methodological critique and protocol for evaluating reflective optimizers.
article_ideas.audience: applied ML leads and benchmark authors
article_ideas.based_on: GEPA discovers test-case-specific solutions first and aggregates them later via a Pareto pool.
article_ideas.thesis: Pareto aggregation of test-case-specific solutions is a strength and a risk: without held-out splits, reported gains may reflect benchmark memorization rather than transferable capability.
article_ideas.title: The Overfitting Trap in Reflective Optimization
article_ideas.video_title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA

article_ideas.angle: Strategic/economic argument aimed at robotics founders, framed as 'which layer are you actually defending?' rather than a capability explainer.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics founders, VCs, and engineering leads allocating roadmap budget
article_ideas.based_on: General-purpose models make different robots more capable.
article_ideas.thesis: As general-purpose models absorb robotic control, the durable moats in robotics shift decisively away from policy architectures and toward physical hardware reliability, proprietary task data flywheels, safety certification and embodied deployment logistics — teams that keep building bespoke control software are defending the wrong layer.
article_ideas.title: Your Robot Stack Is One Prompt Away From Being Commoditized
article_ideas.video_title: Robot-Use Agents: Why General-Purpose Models May Win in Robotics

article_ideas.angle: Engineering-honest counterpoint to the end-to-end hype cycle, with a concrete argument about verification, not accuracy.
article_ideas.audience: Applied ML engineers, robotics platform teams, technical PMs
article_ideas.based_on: Code as Policies allows LLMs to write Python code combining perception and control primitives.
article_ideas.thesis: Program-induction style control (LLM writes code over a curated primitive library) will dominate near-term deployments not because it is more general, but because it is inspectable, retryable and testable, while end-to-end policies remain hard to debug and certify; the honest framing is that code-as-policy is scaffolding that will be gradually eaten from both ends by better VLAs and better tool ecosystems.
article_ideas.title: Code-as-Policies Is the Bridge, Not the Destination — And That's Good News
article_ideas.video_title: Robot-Use Agents: Why General-Purpose Models May Win in Robotics

article_ideas.angle: Methodological critique plus a concrete 'what a credible benchmark must report' checklist.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers, evaluation engineers, robotics procurement and safety reviewers
article_ideas.based_on: GPT-4 Astra scoring 95% on robot control tasks.
article_ideas.thesis: Headline success rates for robot-use agents are near-meaningless without a published task distribution and a distribution-shift decay curve; the field's real constraint is that we cannot distinguish genuine generalization from benchmark-fitted competence, and fixing evaluation would accelerate deployment more than another scaling run.
article_ideas.title: Benchmarks Are the Bottleneck, Not Models: A Critique of Robot-Use Agent Evaluation
article_ideas.video_title: Robot-Use Agents: Why General-Purpose Models May Win in Robotics

article_ideas.angle: Skeptical research essay that separates testable predictions from narrative appeal.
article_ideas.audience: Research scientists, PhD students, technically literate founders
article_ideas.based_on: platonic representation hypothesis
article_ideas.thesis: Representation convergence across modalities is an attractive and partially supported conjecture, but treating it as established leads teams to under-invest in the physical grounding and spatial reasoning that tool-using agents still lack; the falsifiable version of the claim — that robot-trajectory data has diminishing marginal value as general pretraining scales — should be tested directly rather than assumed.
article_ideas.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis Is a Bet, Not a Result
article_ideas.video_title: Robot-Use Agents: Why General-Purpose Models May Win in Robotics

article_ideas.angle: Reframe capacity planning around supply curves instead of release calendars, and show how an optimistic supply assumption makes a roadmap brittle rather than ambitious.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure leads, capacity planners, and technical PMs owning roadmap commitments
article_ideas.based_on: China will likely address compute constraints (lithography and chip making) faster than most expect, within 2 to 3 years.
article_ideas.thesis: Treating model capability as the pacing input to AI roadmaps is a planning error; generation capacity and fab throughput are the first-class inputs, so roadmap assumptions should be stress-tested against each physical input independently rather than against expected model releases.
article_ideas.title: The Constraint Isn't Intelligence: Planning AI Capacity Against Power and Silicon
article_ideas.video_title: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

article_ideas.angle: Translate the reusability economics argument directly onto runtime, context, and session-state persistence, including the recovery and invalidation overhead that reuse introduces.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and runtime engineers building agent infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: Without reusability, throwing away rockets on every flight is like throwing away a medium-sized jet after every flight.
article_ideas.thesis: Continuous-operation agent architectures stay economically non-viable for the same structural reason disposable launch vehicles do: a large fixed asset is rebuilt and discarded per cycle, so marginal cost never collapses and continuous operation remains a premium mode instead of the default.
article_ideas.title: Throwaway Runtimes Are Throwaway Rockets
article_ideas.video_title: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

article_ideas.angle: Argue for an end-to-end latency budget spanning perception, decision, and actuation, provisioned separately from model capability, and show why model-only optimization plateaus.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics and real-time systems engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Humanoid robots have extremely fast reaction times compared to humans due to continuous sensor, actuator, and frame-rate upgrades.
article_ideas.thesis: Embodied agent performance is split across two independently provisioned axes, control-loop hardware and policy intelligence, and gains attributed to reasoning are often downstream of loop rate and actuator bandwidth; measuring them jointly is the only way to locate the real bottleneck.
article_ideas.title: Latency Is a Model Parameter: Why Embodied Agents Plateau on Hardware Budgets
article_ideas.video_title: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

article_ideas.angle: Frame vendor substitution as a runtime policy with cost and fallback consequences rather than as an integration inconvenience.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers and architects selecting model dependencies
article_ideas.based_on: Grok 4.7 is a solid workhorse model, though XAI started AI work only 3 years ago compared to others' 6 years.
article_ideas.thesis: As capability diffuses faster than infrastructure advantage compounds, coupling application logic to one frontier model converts a temporary lead into permanent architectural lock-in; routing and substitution abstractions are the safer engineering default.
article_ideas.title: Design for Model Interchangeability, Not for the Frontier
article_ideas.video_title: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

article_ideas.angle: Expose the false confidence in green CI, provide concrete examples of tautological and structure-sensitive tests, and argue for test-quality gates before human review.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, DevOps engineers, QA leads
article_ideas.based_on: Automated checks can 'lie'
article_ideas.thesis: Automated checks are not a reliable gate because AI-generated tests are often tautological or structure-sensitive, producing false confidence. Teams must implement detection of these failure modes to restore trust in CI.
article_ideas.title: Green CI is a Lie: How AI-Generated Tests Game Your Pipeline
article_ideas.video_title: Fixing the PR Bottleneck — Matt Pocock, AIHero

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the common practice of cramming everything into one prompt, provide architectural rationale and evidence from agent-based code review experiments.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, tech leads, software architects
article_ideas.based_on: Splitting implementation and review into distinct agents with separate context windows improves output quality
article_ideas.thesis: Separating implementation and review into distinct agents with dedicated standards artifacts improves output quality and reduces instruction interference compared to monolithic prompts.
article_ideas.title: Don't Put Coding Standards in Your Implementer: The Case for Separate Review Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Fixing the PR Bottleneck — Matt Pocock, AIHero

article_ideas.angle: Argue for a new interface for review agents, discuss trade-offs, and outline implementation patterns for safe autonomous commits.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, engineering managers, tooling developers
article_ideas.based_on: emit commits (direct fixes) rather than comments
article_ideas.thesis: Automated review agents that commit fixes directly shift human review from remediation to verification, reducing review time and making PRs polished artifacts, but require careful permissioning and auditability.
article_ideas.title: Review Agents Should Commit, Not Comment: Rethinking the Interface of Automated Review
article_ideas.video_title: Fixing the PR Bottleneck — Matt Pocock, AIHero

article_ideas.angle: Connect software architecture to agent reliability, argue for refactoring as an AI-quality intervention, and provide metrics to evaluate impact.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, AI engineers, senior developers
article_ideas.based_on: reduces structure-sensitive tests
article_ideas.thesis: Designing codebases with deep modules is not just a style choice but a control mechanism that reduces structure-sensitive tests and brittle code generated by AI agents.
article_ideas.title: Architecture as Guardrail: How Deep Modules Constrain AI-Generated Code
article_ideas.video_title: Fixing the PR Bottleneck — Matt Pocock, AIHero

article_ideas.angle: Reframe prompt bloat as versioned technical debt with an explicit prune-and-re-measure step at every model upgrade, using the ~80% Claude Code prompt reduction as the worked example of what deletion actually looks like.
article_ideas.audience: Agent and platform engineers maintaining long-lived system prompts across model upgrades
article_ideas.based_on: System prompt design inverts as models improve
article_ideas.thesis: Enumerated constraints in a system prompt are rent paid on one specific model generation's weaknesses; when the model improves, those constraints stop being insurance and start being interference, so the correct engineering act at every upgrade is deletion backed by re-measurement, not preservation for backward compatibility.
article_ideas.title: Your System Prompt Is a Model-Generation Artifact, Not an Asset
article_ideas.video_title: Unhobbling Claude, the difficulties and processes of building agents - Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic

article_ideas.angle: Show how a single interface choice (chat vs code execution with fetch and grep) flips a task from failure to trivial, and argue that benchmark reports without a harness specification are unfalsifiable.
article_ideas.audience: Eval designers, model-selection decision makers, agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Capability overhang: models possess latent capabilities that only surface when given an execution environment
article_ideas.thesis: Capability measured in a chat interface is not predictive of capability in an execution harness, so any evaluation that fixes the interface is measuring the interface and reporting it as the model; the unit of evaluation must be the model-plus-harness pair.
article_ideas.title: Benchmark the Harness, Not the Model
article_ideas.video_title: Unhobbling Claude, the difficulties and processes of building agents - Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic

article_ideas.angle: Translate the known/unknown matrix into concrete prompt artifacts (blindspot pass, implementation notes, deviation logging) and argue they target a failure class that generic clarification advice does not touch.
article_ideas.audience: Agent developers and tech leads deploying coding agents onto unfamiliar repositories
article_ideas.based_on: The unknown matrix (known-knowns, known-unknowns, unknown-knowns, unknown-unknowns)
article_ideas.thesis: When an agent executes an abstract prompt against a real codebase, the dominant failure is not instruction-following but unstated requirements, and the fix is a mandated pass whose only job is to enumerate what the requester failed to say — a different intervention than 'ask clarifying questions'.
article_ideas.title: The Map Is Not the Territory: Ship Elicitation Passes, Not Better Instructions
article_ideas.video_title: Unhobbling Claude, the difficulties and processes of building agents - Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic

article_ideas.angle: Decompose the harness into its axes, show why context representation is only meaningful relative to the chosen action space, and turn the unresolved context-storage question into an explicit benchmark plan.
article_ideas.audience: Browser agent and computer-use harness engineers
article_ideas.based_on: three separable architectural axes
article_ideas.thesis: Context storage, action-execution archetype, and auxiliary memory features are separable design axes, but most browser agent harnesses hard-code one modality stack by default; treating the axes independently lets teams choose per-task harnesses and benchmark the cross product instead of defending a single global design.
article_ideas.title: Browser Agent Harnesses Are Three Decisions, and You Are Making Them All Implicitly
article_ideas.video_title: Unhobbling Claude, the difficulties and processes of building agents - Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic

article_ideas.angle: Argue that investment and evaluation must pivot to sensor-actuator loops and hardware telemetry, using the Anthropic vs. real-world engineering contrast as a case study.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers, robotics engineers, VCs investing in embodied AI.
article_ideas.based_on: no one has yet made AI excellent at physical-world engineering
article_ideas.thesis: The AI industry's focus on software benchmarks creates a dangerous illusion of progress; the true frontier is physical-world engineering, and without dedicated embodied evaluation and operational data strategies, we will deploy agents that fail catastrophically in the physical world.
article_ideas.title: The Real-World Engineering Gap: Why Software AI's Success Masks the Hardest Problem in Embodied Intelligence
article_ideas.video_title: Full: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

article_ideas.angle: Draw parallels between rocket reusability economics and agent infrastructure, providing concrete design principles.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, AI infrastructure engineers, platform teams.
article_ideas.based_on: relocating a per-flight function from the disposable vehicle into fixed, persistent infrastructure
article_ideas.thesis: The most important architectural lesson from Starship's reusable catch is not about rockets—it's about moving complexity out of disposable units into persistent shared infrastructure; agent systems should adopt the same thin-ephemeral-agent + heavy-harness pattern to reduce per-run cost and improve reliability.
article_ideas.title: From Rocket Catch to Agent Runtime: Reusability as the Core Design Pattern for Cost-Effective Autonomy
article_ideas.video_title: Full: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

article_ideas.angle: Conduct a quantitative sensitivity analysis of the claim, using public manufacturing and energy data to bound feasibility.
article_ideas.audience: Technologists, policymakers, investors, and skeptics.
article_ideas.based_on: humanoid robot population exceeds 1 billion within 10 years
article_ideas.thesis: The prediction of 1 billion humanoid robots within a decade is not a forecast but a stress test for our supply chains and energy grids; by modeling the required production rates and grid capacity, we can identify which constraints would break first and whether the abundance narrative holds.
article_ideas.title: A Billion Humanoid Robots in 10 Years? A Reality Check on Manufacturing, Energy, and Demand Saturation
article_ideas.video_title: Full: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

article_ideas.angle: Argue that emerging AI safety frameworks are inadequate for fleet-scale autonomy, and propose governance principles grounded in fleet dynamics.
article_ideas.audience: Policymakers, AI ethicists, robotics industry leaders.
article_ideas.based_on: How will regulatory frameworks adapt to autonomous humanoid robotics and advanced AI safety?
article_ideas.thesis: As humanoid robots move from single units to fleets of millions, safety and regulation must shift from per-robot compliance to fleet-level orchestration; the current regulatory vacuum threatens to turn the age of abundance into an age of accidents.
article_ideas.title: Governing the Robot Swarm: Why AI Safety Must Be Fleet-Scale, Not Unit-Scale
article_ideas.video_title: Full: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

article_ideas.angle: Architecture argument comparing enforcement models for AI code and content generation.
article_ideas.audience: Design systems engineers, AI infrastructure builders, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: The unit of encoded standards should shift from atomic components to executable harnesses
article_ideas.thesis: For AI-assisted product building, standards must be encoded as executable harnesses that inject documentation at generation time; component libraries and static docs are insufficient to prevent context rot.
article_ideas.title: Your Design System Is Not a Component Library: Why AI Needs a Runtime Harness
article_ideas.video_title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with Al | Katie Dill (Stripe)

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode analysis of AI pipelines with concrete gate placement.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, QA, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Generative output produces 'premature finish'
article_ideas.thesis: Because generative output creates premature finish, quality filtering must move to post-build critique and curation; pre-generation specs alone cannot catch deep design flaws that look shippable.
article_ideas.title: Done Is No Longer the Enemy of Good: Moving Quality Gates After AI Generation
article_ideas.video_title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with Al | Katie Dill (Stripe)

article_ideas.angle: Mechanism explanation and countermeasures for generic AI output.
article_ideas.audience: Product designers, brand strategists, AI product teams
article_ideas.based_on: LLM priors converge on the modal/popular solution
article_ideas.thesis: LLM outputs default to probable and popular patterns, so brand differentiation requires supplying unique source material and a declared point of view; prompting for originality cannot overcome prior bias.
article_ideas.title: The Zombie UI Trap: Why LLM Priors Collapse Brand Identity
article_ideas.video_title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with Al | Katie Dill (Stripe)

article_ideas.angle: Practice and economics argument for creative reinvestment.
article_ideas.audience: Product leaders, creative technologists, design managers
article_ideas.based_on: AI cost savings should be reinvested into higher iteration counts
article_ideas.thesis: The ROI of AI should be measured by quality ceiling on high-emotion artifacts, not throughput; teams should reinvest savings into deeper iteration on few things rather than shipping more uniform surface area.
article_ideas.title: Raise the Ceiling, Not the Floor: How to Spend AI Cost Savings on Artistry
article_ideas.video_title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with Al | Katie Dill (Stripe)

article_ideas.angle: Translate Barbara Liskov's separation of what vs. how and the guardrails concept into concrete interface design rules for agent-facing APIs.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: AI agents work better with good abstractions and narrow state spaces (guardrails)
article_ideas.thesis: Designing interfaces for LLM agents should prioritize eliminating invalid states and minimizing non-local reasoning; the abstraction boundary is a first-class reliability mechanism, not just code hygiene.
article_ideas.title: Abstraction Quality Is a Reliability Lever for Agentic Systems, Not a Style Preference
article_ideas.video_title: The End of Understanding: Why Good Abstractions Matter

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the panic over 'not understanding generated code' and show how to operationalize contract-first engineering with agents.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, staff engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Developers using coding agents do not understand the generated code deeply
article_ideas.thesis: As developers delegate code generation to agents, leverage moves from line-level understanding to designing and verifying contracts; teams should invest in abstraction boundaries and verification, not in restoring full comprehension.
article_ideas.title: The Comprehension Gap Is the Point: Engineering Value Shifts to Boundary Design
article_ideas.video_title: The End of Understanding: Why Good Abstractions Matter

article_ideas.angle: Provide a checklist to detect and fix leaky abstractions in existing APIs and platforms.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, API designers
article_ideas.based_on: Form follows function not implementation
article_ideas.thesis: If implementation details (e.g., database isolation levels) appear in consumer code, the abstraction boundary is misplaced; redraw boundaries around problem-domain functions to keep internals changeable.
article_ideas.title: Form Follows Function: A Practical Test for Abstraction Boundaries
article_ideas.video_title: The End of Understanding: Why Good Abstractions Matter

article_ideas.angle: Apply the rubric to a real API or database interface and show how it predicts change friction.
article_ideas.audience: Senior engineers, tech leads
article_ideas.based_on: Evaluating abstractions based on four key properties
article_ideas.thesis: Abstraction quality can be evaluated with four explicit properties—simple, sound, instructive, composable—converting subjective design critique into an auditable engineering criterion.
article_ideas.title: From Taste to Audit: The Four-Property Rubric for Abstractions
article_ideas.video_title: The End of Understanding: Why Good Abstractions Matter

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the 'coding is solved' narrative is incomplete without stage-wise bottleneck analysis, using Ramp's pipeline (75% PRs by Inspect, 93% auto-review) as a case study of successful downstream automation.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, product managers, and platform teams building agentic developer tools.
article_ideas.based_on: Solving coding does not increase end-to-end throughput; it relocates the constraint downstream to review, QA, and coordination.
article_ideas.thesis: Automating code generation shifts the constraint to review, QA, and coordination; teams that measure and automate downstream stages first achieve real end-to-end velocity gains, while those optimizing generation alone hit a hard wall.
article_ideas.title: Your AI Coding Agent Is Not Your Bottleneck—Your Review Queue Is
article_ideas.video_title: What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the common 'unify everything first' approach with Ramp's iterative method, showing how the seed channel reveals the schema for a structured Customer Insight Agent.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, data platform teams, and product managers building customer insight systems.
article_ideas.based_on: Bootstrapping an agent's context pipeline from a deliberately narrow, human-curated channel
article_ideas.thesis: When building context-aware agents over fragmented customer data, starting with a small, human-curated channel (like a Slack 'hate channel') yields faster schema emergence and higher relevance than attempting full-corpus ETL upfront; the narrow channel is not a hack but a principled cold-start strategy.
article_ideas.title: The Hate Channel Strategy: Bootstrapping Context Agents from Narrow, High-Signal Streams
article_ideas.video_title: What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

article_ideas.angle: Argue that coordination is not a soft skill but a programmatic interface, and that the key is maintaining authoritative, structured records; use Ramp's Gadget agent as an example.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, product operations, and AI platform builders.
article_ideas.based_on: Coordination is treated as a programmatic interface: 'every question is treated as an API' backed by formal records in Notion and Slack
article_ideas.thesis: Treating every question as an API over structured records (Notion, Slack) and deploying agents to generate status updates, docs, and customer emails removes humans as coordination middleware, enabling autonomous fix loops that close 60% of UX issues within 24 hours.
article_ideas.title: Coordination as an API: How to Automate Status, Docs, and Fixes with Structured Records
article_ideas.video_title: What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

article_ideas.angle: Argue against model-centric benchmarks that ignore repo quality; propose measuring agent success rates across codebases of varying quality to quantify the multiplier.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, engineering leaders, and AI tool builders.
article_ideas.based_on: Coding-agent effectiveness is bounded by codebase and architecture quality
article_ideas.thesis: Coding-agent effectiveness is not model-bound but environment-bound; codebase architecture quality acts as a multiplier on agent capability, meaning tech-debt cleanup is an agent-enablement investment with measurable ROI.
article_ideas.title: The Codebase Quality Multiplier: Why AI Coding Agents Need Clean Architecture to Shine
article_ideas.video_title: What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the debate from job loss to task redesign, with implications for agent architecture and labor policy.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, product managers, labor economists
article_ideas.based_on: AI changes specific tasks within complex jobs rather than destroying entire job categories wholesale.
article_ideas.thesis: Framing AI as a job replacement is misleading; the real economic and engineering impact comes from task-level automation and augmentation, requiring new metrics and system designs that explicitly model human-AI handoffs.
article_ideas.title: The Task Is the Unit: Why AI's Economic Impact Depends on Task-Level Augmentation
article_ideas.video_title: Best of: The future of the innovation economy

article_ideas.angle: Apply theory of constraints to AI pipeline design.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, MLOps practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Unlocking one bottleneck in software or AI reveals others across industries.
article_ideas.thesis: Optimizing a single AI or software bottleneck often shifts the constraint downstream, so end-to-end telemetry and constraint-aware orchestration are necessary for real productivity gains.
article_ideas.title: Bottleneck Whack-a-Mole: The Hidden Cost of Optimizing AI Workflows
article_ideas.video_title: Best of: The future of the innovation economy

article_ideas.angle: Use historical analogies (electricity, PC) to argue for workflow-first AI strategy.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, innovation managers, policymakers
article_ideas.based_on: AI's economic value as a general-purpose technology is delayed until firms and economies restructure production and workflows, not merely deploy the model.
article_ideas.thesis: Deploying AI models without redesigning production workflows yields little measurable value, as evidenced by general-purpose technology history; firms must invest in process orchestration and change management.
article_ideas.title: Beyond Deployment: Why AI Value Requires Workflow Restructuring
article_ideas.video_title: Best of: The future of the innovation economy

article_ideas.angle: Argue for evidence-based governance and practical safety engineering.
article_ideas.audience: Policy professionals, AI safety researchers, compliance engineers
article_ideas.based_on: AI governance should be evidence-based and pragmatic, using data and existing regulatory frameworks rather than speculative doom scenarios.
article_ideas.thesis: AI regulation should be grounded in empirical measurement and existing regulatory frameworks, not speculative doom scenarios; this requires building evaluation harnesses as first-class infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: Science, Not Science Fiction: A Pragmatic Framework for AI Safety Regulation
article_ideas.video_title: Best of: The future of the innovation economy

article_ideas.angle: Connect the critique of efficiency-only judgment to concrete eval harness design, metric capture, and invisible regressions.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, evaluation leads, and safety researchers
article_ideas.based_on: human dignity risks being judged solely by efficiency
article_ideas.thesis: When systems named after human faculties are evaluated only by efficiency, the eval suite encodes a normative claim that dignity equals productivity; teams should maintain multi-dimensional evals with interaction terms rather than a single cheap proxy.
article_ideas.title: Efficiency Is Not a Neutral Metric: AI Evaluation as Moral Philosophy
article_ideas.video_title: Pope Leo XIV on Artificial Intelligence

article_ideas.angle: Treat the meaning boundary as an architecture responsibility, not a prompt instruction, and specify routing, escalation, and audit trail requirements.
article_ideas.audience: System architects, agent platform engineers, and AI governance teams
article_ideas.based_on: cannot answer questions concerning the meaning of human life
article_ideas.thesis: A well-designed AI system needs an explicit, auditable boundary that classifies value-laden queries out of model competence and routes them to a human-owned policy layer; otherwise it will confabulate purpose from correlation.
article_ideas.title: Designing the Abstention Boundary: Where Correlation Ends and Meaning Begins
article_ideas.video_title: Pope Leo XIV on Artificial Intelligence

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the Babel/Pentecost contrast as a testable architecture trade-off and identify choke points as fragility signals.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent systems engineers and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: unity imposed by domination
article_ideas.thesis: Imposed-uniformity orchestration buys short-term coherence but is structurally fragile; multi-agent systems should prefer shared protocols and invariants that preserve local heterogeneity.
article_ideas.title: Babel or Pentecost: Choosing Coordination Topologies for Multi-Agent Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Pope Leo XIV on Artificial Intelligence

article_ideas.angle: Apply the communication-speed warning to generative AI pipelines, agent messaging, and publication workflows.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, information-integrity teams, and product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: faster communication technology
article_ideas.thesis: Faster generation and communication without proportional verification capacity lowers effective signal-to-noise; verification must scale with throughput or the marginal content is unverified by default.
article_ideas.title: Throughput Without Verification Is Information Debt
article_ideas.video_title: Pope Leo XIV on Artificial Intelligence

article_ideas.angle: Architectural shift; why applications should be model-agnostic and how to evaluate routers.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, CTOs, product architects
article_ideas.based_on: Manual model selection by users is becoming obsolete; agents and routers pick the best model for the task intensity.
article_ideas.thesis: As model choice moves from users to a learned router/harness, the platform's routing quality, telemetry, fallback policy, and cost constraints—not raw model access—become the primary determinants of application quality and economics.
article_ideas.title: The Model Router Is the New Operating System
article_ideas.video_title: Microsoft’s AI Bet: Copilot, Autopilot and the Coming Product War with CEO Satya Nadella

article_ideas.angle: Governance is not a feature but an execution environment; compare to cloud management planes.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, security and compliance leaders, platform product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Agent 365 provides the hosting environment for observation, governance, policy-setting, security, and FinOps.
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise adoption of autonomous agents will be decided less by model capability than by whether the platform provides an auditable control plane for identity, policy, observability, security, and FinOps.
article_ideas.title: Agent 365 Is the Real Product War: Governance as Runtime
article_ideas.video_title: Microsoft’s AI Bet: Copilot, Autopilot and the Coming Product War with CEO Satya Nadella

article_ideas.angle: Business and architecture intersection; practical instrumentation for token-consuming agents.
article_ideas.audience: Product leaders, FinOps practitioners, SaaS architects
article_ideas.based_on: Software now has a marginal cost due to token consumption, requiring rigorous ROI alignment.
article_ideas.thesis: Hybrid seat-plus-usage pricing is inevitable for AI agents because token consumption creates a marginal cost; products that do not instrument metering and FinOps will misprice autonomous workflows and fail ROI scrutiny.
article_ideas.title: When Software Has a Token Bill: Seat Pricing Meets Agent Economics
article_ideas.video_title: Microsoft’s AI Bet: Copilot, Autopilot and the Coming Product War with CEO Satya Nadella

article_ideas.angle: Form-factor argument using examples like complete apps hosted like documents on OneDrive and Excel inner/outer loops.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, productivity tool designers, UX and agent researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Autopilot represents the next major step up as an autonomous process agent capable of completing jobs.
article_ideas.thesis: Autonomous process agents collapse traditional application UIs into document-like, long-running workflows with human checkpoints, forcing new abstractions for memory, permissions, and execution.
article_ideas.title: Autopilot and the Death of the App-Document Boundary
article_ideas.video_title: Microsoft’s AI Bet: Copilot, Autopilot and the Coming Product War with CEO Satya Nadella

article_ideas.angle: Language and tooling selection under AI, with evidence from C++ vs obscure languages.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, language designers, and platform architects.
article_ideas.based_on: AI hallucinates when given obscure or new languages with small code corpora.
article_ideas.thesis: AI assistance quality is determined by training-corpus density, giving mainstream languages a compounding advantage that penalizes new languages and internal DSLs; teams should treat corpus availability as a first-class engineering criterion for language and tooling selection.
article_ideas.title: The Corpus Moat: Why AI Makes It Harder to Leave C++ (and Other Incumbents)
article_ideas.video_title: C++26 for Lazy Programmers • Will Briggs & Todd Montgomery • GOTO 2026

article_ideas.angle: API design for AI agents, drawing from C++ pedagogy.
article_ideas.audience: API designers, agent developers, and tooling engineers.
article_ideas.based_on: C++ has too many ways to do things (e.g., 25 ways to initialize a variable like std::string).
article_ideas.thesis: The cognitive overload from C++'s ~25 ways to initialize a string is not just a teaching problem; it's the same ambiguity that causes agents to choose plausible-but-wrong actions, so API and tool surfaces should expose a single canonical invocation per intent, with alternatives gated behind demonstrated need.
article_ideas.title: One Right Way: How C++'s Option Proliferation Teaches Us to Design Agent-Friendly APIs
article_ideas.video_title: C++26 for Lazy Programmers • Will Briggs & Todd Montgomery • GOTO 2026

article_ideas.angle: Agent safety and interface design, applying pedagogy to harness construction.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety engineers, platform architects, and agent framework developers.
article_ideas.based_on: Students learn arrays and dynamic allocation under the hood before confronting the dreaded 'P-word'.
article_ideas.thesis: Just as teaching arrays before raw pointers builds a safer mental model, agent harnesses should wrap dangerous primitives (raw shell, direct file mutation, memory operations) behind constrained abstractions that encode invariants, revealing the raw primitive only after competence is established.
article_ideas.title: Pointers Without the P-Word: Abstraction-First Sequencing for Safe Agent Harnesses
article_ideas.video_title: C++26 for Lazy Programmers • Will Briggs & Todd Montgomery • GOTO 2026

article_ideas.angle: Developer skills and AI collaboration, with implications for team structure and training.
article_ideas.audience: Developers, engineering managers, and technical leads.
article_ideas.based_on: Learning to read code is more important than ever because AI-generated code must be reviewed and understood.
article_ideas.thesis: AI accelerates generation, but blind reliance leads to rabbit holes; therefore, the binding constraint on safe delegation is human review capacity, and learning to read code becomes more critical than ever.
article_ideas.title: Reading Code Is the New Writing Code: Why AI Increases the Value of Comprehension
article_ideas.video_title: C++26 for Lazy Programmers • Will Briggs & Todd Montgomery • GOTO 2026

article_ideas.angle: Take the checkability/flexibility trade-off seriously and show which production mechanisms (static inspection, permission modes, deterministic replay) are impossible under free-text plans.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform architects building production agent runtimes
article_ideas.based_on: Plan representation is an explicit architectural choice
article_ideas.thesis: Plan representation should be treated as a first-class architectural decision: natural-language plans are general but unverifiable, so any agent that needs safety, permissioning, or replay must move to code/formal plan representations with explicit permission gates, accepting the loss of open-ended generality.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Plan Is an Interface, Not a Paragraph
article_ideas.video_title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 5. Planning, Task Decomposition, and Multi-Agent Coordination

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the reflex to add specialized agents, and reframe multi-agent design as an orchestrator-capability problem first.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent system designers and applied AI teams
article_ideas.based_on: Fixed multi-agent role assignments have a structural failure mode
article_ideas.thesis: Coordination quality, not role specialization, is the bottleneck in multi-agent systems: multiplying fixed worker roles before strengthening the orchestrator produces rigid communication and dropped context, while a stronger manager measurably lifts weaker workers.
article_ideas.title: Invest in the Manager, Not the Org Chart
article_ideas.video_title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 5. Planning, Task Decomposition, and Multi-Agent Coordination

article_ideas.angle: Move re-planning from prompt craft into the runtime control layer, with the same rigor as retries or circuit breakers.
article_ideas.audience: Agent runtime and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Planning is not a one-shot artifact but a continuously revised commitment
article_ideas.thesis: Long-horizon agent success depends on an explicit commit-vs-replan subsystem with defined triggers and error detection, not on better initial plans; teams that treat re-planning as a prompt technique leave the dominant failure source uninstrumented.
article_ideas.title: Re-Planning Is a Control Loop, Not a Prompt Trick
article_ideas.video_title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 5. Planning, Task Decomposition, and Multi-Agent Coordination

article_ideas.angle: Frame modularity as buying specialization at the cost of an interface contract that must itself be planned, checked, and monitored.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform teams and agent framework maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: Decomposing an agent into a planner module and an executor module
article_ideas.thesis: Separating planners from executors enables specialized model training and independent optimization, but the interface between the reasoning layer and the acting layer becomes the new dominant failure surface, so the boundary should follow capability gradients rather than convenience.
article_ideas.title: The Planner/Executor Split and Its New Failure Surface
article_ideas.video_title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 5. Planning, Task Decomposition, and Multi-Agent Coordination

article_ideas.angle: Architectural pattern and its engineering consequences for debugging, telemetry, and incident response.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, security architects, platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Agent state is architecturally isolated per-agent in a dedicated confidential VM
article_ideas.thesis: Platform-level access controls are insufficient for agents holding sensitive personal context; per-agent confidential VMs with user-held keys relocate the trust boundary and force observability to be redesigned around enclave limits.
article_ideas.title: The Provider-Blind Agent: Why Confidential VMs Are the Next Trust Boundary for Personal AI
article_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg's Vision For the Future!

article_ideas.angle: Design pattern for data-exfiltration control and policy enforcement in agent runtimes.
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers, agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: A separate 'sentinel' agent monitors data flowing in and out
article_ideas.thesis: Security enforcement for autonomous agents should be an independent monitor at the isolation boundary, not a responsibility of the agent itself, enabling testable ingress/egress policy.
article_ideas.title: Sentinel Agents: Separating Execution from Policy Enforcement in Autonomous Runtimes
article_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg's Vision For the Future!

article_ideas.angle: Build-vs-wrap decision for agent products, with engineering and economic tradeoffs.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, AI researchers, product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Models are trained from scratch specifically to be good agents
article_ideas.thesis: Training models from scratch to be agents yields cohesive, secure behavior that composition over open-source models cannot match, but the tradeoff is higher fixed cost and reduced reuse of external progress.
article_ideas.title: Stop Wrapping Foundation Models: The Case for Agent-Native Training
article_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg's Vision For the Future!

article_ideas.angle: AI for science, with a focus on validation and fidelity requirements.
article_ideas.audience: Computational biologists, AI for science researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Biology is treated as a simulatable system
article_ideas.thesis: Treating biology as a simulatable system turns domain problems into compute-scaling problems, but the approach's value depends on validating in-silico predictions against wet-lab ground truth.
article_ideas.title: Simulation as Instrument: How Virtual Cells Shift Biology from Lab to Compute
article_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg's Vision For the Future!

article_ideas.angle: Separate what the reported metrics do and do not prove, then map each metric to the infrastructure layer that produces it.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform/infrastructure architects evaluating agentic coding rollout
article_ideas.based_on: Total reliability and security metrics remain essentially unchanged.
article_ideas.thesis: Stripe's combination of rising per-PR quality, hundreds of merged PRs per hour, and essentially unchanged aggregate reliability and security is explained by infrastructure (dev boxes, instrumentation, observability, incremental rollout, test suites) rather than by model capability; teams that adopt agentic generation without the equivalent guardrail stack should expect reliability erosion, because the same claim about the model is not what the metrics actually support.
article_ideas.title: Flat Reliability With Rising PR Quality Is a Guardrail Result, Not a Model Result
article_ideas.video_title: Patrick Collison on Claude Code at Stripe

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the velocity/reliability trade-off as a queueing problem where the slowest stage sets system throughput.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, SRE, and release/CI infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: the real constraint has moved downstream of code generation
article_ideas.thesis: Once generation throughput exceeds what verification can absorb, per-change quality improvements no longer convert into reliability headroom, and review bandwidth stops being the binding constraint; the productive investments become test synthesis, merge/rollback automation, and rollout gating, plus the instrumentation needed to detect when that saturation point is reached.
article_ideas.title: The Bottleneck Moved: Reliability Engineering Budget Should Follow Verification, Not Review
article_ideas.video_title: Patrick Collison on Claude Code at Stripe

article_ideas.angle: Argue that agent-native identity is a gating prerequisite, not a follow-on feature, and enumerate the flow assumptions that break.
article_ideas.audience: API and payments platform architects, security engineers building for non-human principals
article_ideas.based_on: agent-native identity and delegated-authority primitives
article_ideas.thesis: Designing for agent-to-agent transactions is not a volume-scaling problem to defer until demand arrives: identity, delegated authority, privilege scoping, and payment authorization for non-human principals are prerequisites that cannot be retrofitted onto human-oriented signup and API flows, and prompt-injection defense belongs in the same security-boundary design conversation.
article_ideas.title: Agent Counterparties Break Payment Primitive Assumptions Before They Break Volume
article_ideas.video_title: Patrick Collison on Claude Code at Stripe

article_ideas.angle: Measurement critique of a widely repeated org-design heuristic
article_ideas.audience: Product and engineering leaders standing up labs teams
article_ideas.based_on: Labs teams expect to dispose of 90 percent of what they make
article_ideas.thesis: The lab disposal rate only works as an exploration budget if it has a declared denominator, a counting rule, and instrumentation; until then it is a slogan that legitimizes waste without producing learning-rate signal.
article_ideas.title: The 90% Disposal Rate Is a Metric, Not a Culture Statement
article_ideas.video_title: How to run your product team like a research lab | Dan Shipper (Every)

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation bias and the architectural commitments it causes
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects, AI engineers, and technical decision makers
article_ideas.based_on: first encounter with a frontier model
article_ideas.thesis: Capability assessments taken at first contact with a frontier model systematically overestimate reliable capability, so commitment decisions should require repeated measurement across a cooling-off window, not a compelling demo.
article_ideas.title: Your First Week With a New Frontier Model Is the Worst Time to Re-Architect
article_ideas.video_title: How to run your product team like a research lab | Dan Shipper (Every)

article_ideas.angle: Org-design argument with a stated boundary condition for when larger teams become preferable again
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, org designers, and heads of product
article_ideas.based_on: AI allows for a labs team of one with high leverage and minimal resource requirements
article_ideas.thesis: When per-person leverage rises, coordination overhead becomes the binding constraint on exploration throughput, so the optimal exploration unit shrinks to one or two generalists until coordination cost exceeds marginal capacity.
article_ideas.title: Two-Pizza Teams Are Obsolete, and the Replacement Constraint Is Coordination, Not Headcount
article_ideas.video_title: How to run your product team like a research lab | Dan Shipper (Every)

article_ideas.angle: Reframing internal tooling as a staged deployment rather than a perk
article_ideas.audience: Product engineers and platform teams building internal AI tooling
article_ideas.based_on: Build internal tools for your own team first before exposing them to customers.
article_ideas.thesis: Running a new capability against your own team's recurring workflow is the cheapest validation stage available, but it only counts as promotion evidence if the internal usage is instrumented to produce measurable signal.
article_ideas.title: Dogfooding Is a Canary Deployment With a Real Workload
article_ideas.video_title: How to run your product team like a research lab | Dan Shipper (Every)

article_ideas.angle: Take the concrete architectural split (symbolic editable state for planning, renderer as a replaceable downstream component) and turn it into an evaluation critique with falsifiable tests on identical tasks.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and research leads building agents, simulation, or embodied systems
article_ideas.based_on: render beautiful pixels but lack underlying semantic representations
article_ideas.thesis: Rendering fidelity and planning capability are independent axes, and the field's habit of using visual plausibility as a proxy for world-model quality actively hides physically impossible dynamics; evaluation must be rebuilt around action-conditioned, causal tasks.
article_ideas.title: Pretty Pixels Are Not a World Model: Why Planning Capability, Not Frame Fidelity, Is the Benchmark
article_ideas.video_title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI

article_ideas.angle: Generalize the simulator loop (video observation to mesh and symbolic representation to generated code to render to inspect to score against reality) into a reusable pattern for codegen agents and data-synthesis pipelines, contrasting it with model self-critique.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and infra engineers building codegen agents and synthetic data pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: score deviations against physical reality
article_ideas.thesis: In code-generation systems for executable artifacts, reliability accrues to the render/execute-then-score harness rather than to the generator, so teams should budget and design the scorer first and treat model choice as a replaceable component.
article_ideas.title: The Deviation Score Is the Product: Verification Harnesses as the Durable Layer in Codegen Pipelines
article_ideas.video_title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the sim-vs-real debate as an infrastructure economics argument, with the deviation score acting as the measurable bridge and the sim-to-real gap as the residual risk to quantify.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics and ML infrastructure decision makers
article_ideas.based_on: 10,000 hours of teleoperation data in the physical world is too slow, expensive, and limited
article_ideas.thesis: The choice between simulated and physical training data should be made on cost-per-coverage-of-task-distribution, not photorealism, because the human-bound marginal cost of teleoperation is the binding constraint on general robotic policies.
article_ideas.title: Simulation Is a Data-Supply Decision, Not a Fidelity Question
article_ideas.video_title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI

article_ideas.angle: Derive a concrete state-design rule from the object-level interactivity example and show what it forbids in latent- or pixel-state world models.
article_ideas.audience: Agent and world-model architects
article_ideas.based_on: Symbolic object structure enables interaction that pure pixel models cannot support
article_ideas.thesis: The set of operations a planner can expose should map one-to-one onto symbolically addressable objects in state; representation granularity, not model capacity, is what determines whether an agent can lift a specific object rather than nudge a scene.
article_ideas.title: Your Planner Can Only Do What Your State Can Name
article_ideas.video_title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI

article_ideas.angle: Argue from the layered-safety model in the keynote: model hardening is one layer, but the network-level guardrail is the one that converts a model bypass into a blocked exfiltration event instead of a breach.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and security architects building agent runtimes
article_ideas.based_on: Agentic safety guardrails prevent prompt injection and data leaks at the network level.
article_ideas.thesis: Treating prompt injection as a prompting problem is an architectural dead end; the defensible control points are runtime/network-layer policy, least privilege, and egress validation, because injection success cannot be reliably reduced at the model layer.
article_ideas.title: Guardrails Belong in the Network, Not the Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Opening Keynotes: Mistral, Langfuse & Sizzy | Day 1

article_ideas.angle: Use the steam and electrification analogies to reframe enterprise AI roadmaps as process-redesign programs, then propose proxies that make the slow clock visible in planning.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, CTOs, and enterprise architects setting AI roadmaps
article_ideas.based_on: GPTs require decades of complementary organizational changes before productivity spikes.
article_ideas.thesis: The diffusion-lag argument is often used to defer accountability for AI ROI; instead it should force teams to treat organizational redesign as the primary engineering dependency and to measure it with the same rigor as capability.
article_ideas.title: The Two Clocks Are Not an Excuse: Agent ROI Is Gated by Process Redesign
article_ideas.video_title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Opening Keynotes: Mistral, Langfuse & Sizzy | Day 1

article_ideas.angle: Walk the staged progression from copy-paste slot machine to one-shot chat to multi-agent factories, and show which bottleneck each stage exposes and which tooling each stage actually requires.
article_ideas.audience: Developer tooling teams and engineering managers adopting AI coding agents
article_ideas.based_on: Most developers start with copy-paste workflows (slot machine), move to one-shot chat prompts, and eventually build software factories.
article_ideas.thesis: Investments in orchestrators, sandboxes, and linter gatekeepers are only justified at later stages of the developer-AI maturity ladder, so teams should diagnose their actual stage before buying factory-grade infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: The Software Factory Ladder: Tooling Requirements Scale With Autonomy, Not Model Quality
article_ideas.video_title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Opening Keynotes: Mistral, Langfuse & Sizzy | Day 1

article_ideas.angle: Contrast centralized API consumption with dedicated infrastructure where data processing, storage, and retention are bound to a controlled physical and legal boundary.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects and compliance-aware AI infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: Organizations must control where data is processed, stored, and retained while ensuring deterministic safety policies.
article_ideas.thesis: Data residency and state-controlled compute are becoming architectural constraints that narrow viable deployment topologies, so teams should model sovereignty as a design input rather than a procurement afterthought.
article_ideas.title: Sovereign AI Is a Deployment Topology Constraint, Not a Compliance Checkbox
article_ideas.video_title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Opening Keynotes: Mistral, Langfuse & Sizzy | Day 1

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the standard 'which model?' engineering debate as a permission-scoping exercise, with a worked argument that a fixed model plus expanded tool surface outperforms a model upgrade with a fixed surface.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and agent-infrastructure engineers, engineering leads choosing agent stacks
article_ideas.based_on: Tool access (file system, bash, external APIs) is what transforms LLMs from text generators into autonomous agents.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent capability is set by the action surface you expose, not by the model you pick; therefore permission and sandbox design, not model selection, should be the primary design artifact for any agentic system, and teams that treat tools as an implementation detail will ship both unsafe and weak agents.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Capability Boundary Is Its Permission Boundary
article_ideas.video_title: In Conversation with Boris Cherny, Creator of Claude Code

article_ideas.angle: Argue against safety architectures that consolidate trust in a single classifier, and specify what must sit behind the guard model for the claim of safety to be measurable.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety engineers, security architects, technical decision-makers in regulated environments
article_ideas.based_on: Secondary safety models and automated guardrails prevent models from going rogue.
article_ideas.thesis: Secondary-model validation ('automode') is valuable but structurally fragile: a guard weaker than the model it vets will be evaded at a rate that grows with primary-model capability, so guard models must be paired with process isolation, human gating, and continuous adversarial measurement rather than treated as the safety guarantee.
article_ideas.title: Guard Models Are a Layer, Not a Moat
article_ideas.video_title: In Conversation with Boris Cherny, Creator of Claude Code

article_ideas.angle: Walk through how the same channel that makes an agent useful (reading the web, docs, tool output) becomes the injection vector, and what runtime-level provenance metadata must look like.
article_ideas.audience: RAG and retrieval engineers, agent runtime authors, application security teams
article_ideas.based_on: Prompt injection via untrusted ingested data
article_ideas.thesis: Giving an agent execution privileges turns content ingestion into a security boundary, so provenance tiering and content sanitization belong in the agent runtime, not in application code — and retrieval systems that cannot report where content came from are unsafe by construction.
article_ideas.title: Every Read Is an Authorization Decision
article_ideas.video_title: In Conversation with Boris Cherny, Creator of Claude Code

article_ideas.angle: Challenge the optimistic 'coding for everyone' framing by tracing where the review burden goes and why verification tooling becomes the limiting resource rather than authoring tooling.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, developer-tooling product teams, platform owners
article_ideas.based_on: Coding will become accessible to everyone, shrinking the gap between professional and non-professional developers.
article_ideas.thesis: Democratizing code generation to non-engineers does not remove engineering work; it relocates it into specification, acceptance criteria, and verification, and organizations that do not build verification infrastructure will accumulate unmaintainable systems faster than they can review them.
article_ideas.title: When Generation Is Cheap, Verification Is the Bottleneck
article_ideas.video_title: In Conversation with Boris Cherny, Creator of Claude Code

article_ideas.angle: Reinterpret convention over configuration as an agent-harness cost property and propose a controlled benchmark that isolates corpus effects by testing a conventional but minimally-pretrained framework against Rails and a low-convention baseline.
article_ideas.audience: Framework maintainers, platform architects, and agent-tooling engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Convention over configuration is reframed as an agent-context optimization
article_ideas.thesis: The doctrine of convention over configuration survives in the agent era for a new reason: it lowers the context budget an agent needs to act correctly. But the framework advantage cannot be claimed until convention density is separated from training-corpus representation, so teams should adopt tokens-per-correct-change as a first-class evaluation metric alongside human onboarding speed.
article_ideas.title: Conventions Are an Agent Interface: Benchmark Frameworks by Tokens-per-Correct-Change, Not Human Preference
article_ideas.video_title: Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

article_ideas.angle: Argue that language selection should decouple from human readability only when paired with a maintenance-competence evaluation, using the HEY rewrite as the motivating datapoint rather than the conclusion.
article_ideas.audience: Backend architects, infrastructure engineers, and technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: Rust is the ugliest programming language invented in the last 40 years for human writers.
article_ideas.thesis: The historical penalty on difficult systems languages assumed human authorship. When agents write and maintain the code, the runtime-efficiency axis becomes capturable, but the decision is only sound if agent competence in that language is measured longitudinally. Otherwise teams retain an artifact their humans cannot comfortably read while the maintenance burden silently transfers to a model dependency.
article_ideas.title: The Ergonomics Penalty Is Now Paid by Agents: When to Choose Rust for Its Runtime, Not Its Syntax
article_ideas.video_title: Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

article_ideas.angle: Examine the failure-attribution problem when the same vague prompt yields divergent artifacts, and propose measurable divergence bounds as a required artifact in the agentic development workflow.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, prompt and specification tooling builders, and engineering managers adopting agents
article_ideas.based_on: English is a better programming language than Ruby because it is more expressive and vague.
article_ideas.thesis: Treating vagueness as an asset at the intent layer moves disambiguation into the agent, where it resolves nondeterministically and silently. Production agentic pipelines therefore need a constraint layer of acceptance criteria, invariants, and tests whose job is to bound divergence, not to replace the vague intent but to make it reproducible.
article_ideas.title: English as a Programming Language Trades Expressiveness for Nondeterminism: Why Production Pipelines Need a Constraint Layer
article_ideas.video_title: Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

article_ideas.angle: Translate the multi-source frontier observation into an architectural pattern of abstraction seam plus per-model evals, using the trough of disillusionment as the case for why a capability peak is not a stable foundation.
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects, LLM operations engineers, and CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Frontier intelligence is no longer restricted to large American tech companies.
article_ideas.thesis: As frontier capability arrives from multiple suppliers on a short cadence punctuated by regression intervals, any agentic stack hard-wired to one model inherits concentration risk and re-validation cost. Model identity should be a configuration guarded by a per-model regression suite, so swaps are validated rather than assumed continuous.
article_ideas.title: Model Choice Is Deployable Configuration: Building Seams and Regression Suites for a Multi-Source Frontier
article_ideas.video_title: Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

article_ideas.angle: Governance tradeoff analysis for technical leaders
article_ideas.audience: AI policy and engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: no single lever reduces both
article_ideas.thesis: Frontier AI safety programs must name which failure class they optimize—loss of control or concentration of power—because pre-release gating and open-weight diffusion trade one for the other, and a single posture cannot minimize both.
article_ideas.title: The Safety Posture Is a Choice: Gating and Openness Optimize Opposite Risks
article_ideas.video_title: Full UN Security Council AI Hearing With Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Clément Delangue | AC1G

article_ideas.angle: Engineering architecture for irreversible model release
article_ideas.audience: ML platform and release engineers
article_ideas.based_on: irreversible artifact boundary
article_ideas.thesis: Because open-weight release is an irreversible artifact boundary, the full safety evaluation budget must move upstream into release-blocking CI on frozen snapshots; post-release moderation should be treated as observability, not control.
article_ideas.title: Release Gates, Not Runtime Filters: Where Open-Weight Safety Engineering Belongs
article_ideas.video_title: Full UN Security Council AI Hearing With Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Clément Delangue | AC1G

article_ideas.angle: Agent runtime design under oversight constraints
article_ideas.audience: Agent runtime architects and safety engineers
article_ideas.based_on: human review cadence becomes the throughput ceiling
article_ideas.thesis: Mandating human review for high-stakes agents imposes a throughput ceiling; useful autonomy therefore requires risk-tiered action gating against the human review cadence, with authorization boundaries and audit trails as runtime primitives.
article_ideas.title: Human Oversight Is a Latency Budget, Not a Checkbox
article_ideas.video_title: Full UN Security Council AI Hearing With Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Clément Delangue | AC1G

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation methodology critique
article_ideas.audience: AI safety evaluation teams
article_ideas.based_on: capability-centric (map what the model can do)
article_ideas.thesis: Prompt- and intent-based red-teaming misses dual-use capabilities that are simultaneously beneficial and dangerous; evaluation should first map the model's capability surface and then classify each capability's harm envelope.
article_ideas.title: Evaluate Capabilities, Not Prompts: Dual-Use Safety Requires Capability-Envelope Mapping
article_ideas.video_title: Full UN Security Council AI Hearing With Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Clément Delangue | AC1G

article_ideas.angle: Trace the engineering surface shift from test-time search orchestration to pretraining-data and prior curation, and argue that teams that keep investing in tuning infrastructure are investing in the part that is being deleted.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform engineers and applied ML leads who own per-task pipeline and tuning infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: TabPFN learns the entire algorithm during meta-training on synthetic datasets generated from structural causal models.
article_ideas.thesis: If an entire learning algorithm including model selection and tuning is amortized into a single forward pass, then the durable engineering value migrates from building per-task pipeline infrastructure to designing the synthetic priors and meta-training distributions that determine what the model can learn in context.
article_ideas.title: The Pipeline Was the Product: What Happens to ML Engineering When the Algorithm Is Pretrained
article_ideas.video_title: The AI That Replaces Hours of Model Tuning - Frank Hutter

article_ideas.angle: Compare direct context stuffing against a tool-call route on cost, latency, and accuracy, and derive a routing rule for when a modality belongs behind a tool boundary rather than inside the context window.
article_ideas.audience: Agent and AI engineering teams building tool-using systems over enterprise data
article_ideas.based_on: Tabular tables have billions of tokens if thrown into LLMs, making LLMs million times too expensive, slow, and inaccurate.
article_ideas.thesis: Serializing tabular data into LLM context is the wrong default, and the correct agent architecture routes modality-specific prediction to specialized models behind a tool interface, because the cost asymmetry is structural rather than a tuning problem.
article_ideas.title: Stop Stuffing Tables Into Context: Tool Boundaries as the Correct Architecture for Structured Data Agents
article_ideas.video_title: The AI That Replaces Hours of Model Tuning - Frank Hutter

article_ideas.angle: Use TabNet as the canonical case for a general adoption checklist: which evaluation protocols would have flagged the failure before deployment, and how to apply that checklist to the next architecture that claims to replace boosted trees.
article_ideas.audience: Practitioners evaluating new architectures and reviewers of applied ML claims
article_ideas.based_on: Google's TabNet received thousands of citations but failed to generalize across new datasets.
article_ideas.thesis: TabNet's thousands of citations alongside its failure to generalize across new tabular datasets shows that adoption signals are decoupled from generalization evidence, so architecture adoption should be gated on held-out-dataset generalization rather than benchmark position or scholarly attention.
article_ideas.title: Citations Are Not Generalization: A Post-Mortem Pattern for Deep Learning on Structured Data
article_ideas.video_title: The AI That Replaces Hours of Model Tuning - Frank Hutter

article_ideas.angle: Engineering trust boundary: move from model trust to artifact verification.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform teams, technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: pair LLM code generation with formal proof checkers
article_ideas.thesis: The only scalable safety argument for AI-generated code is machine-checkable proof; vendor trust and human spot-checking are not sufficient, and the jump from 68% to 96% vericoding success shows the gate is becoming practical.
article_ideas.title: Stop Trusting the Model, Start Verifying the Artifact
article_ideas.video_title: A better path for AI with Max Tegmark

article_ideas.angle: Security and reliability engineering.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, security teams, developers
article_ideas.based_on: Vibe coding (relying on AI-generated code without verification) results in nearly half of AI-generated code containing security flaws
article_ideas.thesis: Accepting AI-generated code without verification is not a productivity hack but a measurable security risk, since nearly half contains flaws; automated verification must be a default merge gate.
article_ideas.title: Vibe Coding Is a Supply-Chain Vulnerability
article_ideas.video_title: A better path for AI with Max Tegmark

article_ideas.angle: AI safety research strategy and interpretability benchmarks.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers, interpretability teams
article_ideas.based_on: Asymptotic Internal Transparency Conjecture
article_ideas.thesis: The common assumption that scale makes models less inspectable may be false; if the extractable fraction rises with intelligence, interpretability should be funded as a scaling investment, but the conjecture must be measured first.
article_ideas.title: The Transparency Scaling Bet
article_ideas.video_title: A better path for AI with Max Tegmark

article_ideas.angle: Formal methods meets AI safety.
article_ideas.audience: Formal methods practitioners, AI safety engineers
article_ideas.based_on: who authors and validates the specs that proofs check against
article_ideas.thesis: Vericoding and proof-based safety shift trust from model internals to specifications, creating a new critical failure mode: correct proofs of wrong requirements.
article_ideas.title: Who Verifies the Specification?
article_ideas.video_title: A better path for AI with Max Tegmark

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the productivity debate around verification burden, with concrete metrics for review latency and defect detection.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, developer-tooling teams, AI-assisted development practitioners.
article_ideas.based_on: reviewing generated code requires building a mental model
article_ideas.thesis: AI-assisted development does not eliminate work; it transfers cognitive load from author to reviewer. Treating review as a secondary cost hides the real bottleneck and silently degrades defect detection. Teams should invest in review-time mental-model reconstruction—staged diffs, generated rationale, and prediction prompts—as first-class infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: Generation Is Cheap; Verification Is the Job: Why AI Code Review Needs New Cognitive Tooling
article_ideas.video_title: Teaching in the Age of AI: Learning Goals and the Goals of Learning

article_ideas.angle: Architectural argument comparing embedded editor agents against standalone web-app agents on context-switch cost and review latency.
article_ideas.audience: Developer-tooling architects, IDE/editor plugin developers, platform teams.
article_ideas.based_on: Treating the editor as the single home base
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic AI capabilities should attach to the developer's existing home base rather than spawning parallel web apps. Centralizing editing, version control, review, and AI interactions reduces context-switch cost and enables review-native agent affordances; standalone agent dashboards fragment the loop.
article_ideas.title: The Editor Is the Agent's Home Base
article_ideas.video_title: Teaching in the Age of AI: Learning Goals and the Goals of Learning

article_ideas.angle: Argue against full automation of the error-correction cycle in training and agent design, using cognitive-load and retention evidence.
article_ideas.audience: Educators, agent-harness designers, engineering managers.
article_ideas.based_on: incremental feedback loop of catching syntax errors and debugging
article_ideas.thesis: The syntax-error-and-debug loop is not overhead to be optimized away; it is the mechanism by which programmers build durable mental models. AI harnesses that hide errors, auto-fix silently, or generate before the learner predicts may make work faster while producing fragile competence. Educational and agentic tooling should preserve or reintroduce informative friction.
article_ideas.title: Don't Automate the Feedback Loop: The Debugging Cycle Is the Curriculum
article_ideas.video_title: Teaching in the Age of AI: Learning Goals and the Goals of Learning

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode analysis with an instrumentation proposal for detecting masked gaps before they become maintenance debt.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, platform teams, educators.
article_ideas.based_on: Over-reliance on LLM-generated code without understanding masks knowledge gaps
article_ideas.thesis: Over-reliance on LLMs without understanding does not fail immediately; it defers cost into subtle bugs and unmaintainable systems. Teams adopting code generation at scale need instrumentation for masked knowledge gaps, because the symptoms surface late and look like ordinary maintenance. Curricula and tooling should measure no-AI capability alongside AI-assisted throughput.
article_ideas.title: Masked Competence Gaps: The Hidden Maintenance Debt of LLM Reliance
article_ideas.video_title: Teaching in the Age of AI: Learning Goals and the Goals of Learning

article_ideas.angle: Treat the 80% figure as a budgeting claim and follow it into platform design: what changes in scheduling, sandboxing, replay and cost accounting when verification is the primary workload.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and engineering leaders budgeting agent infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: Eighty percent of lab resources are dedicated to verification, testing, and safety alignment.
article_ideas.thesis: If verification, testing and alignment consume the majority of lab resources, then guardrail-as-a-service framing is architecturally wrong: containment and replay must be runtime subsystems with their own compute budget, not a moderation endpoint bolted onto a model call.
article_ideas.title: Safety Is the Workload, Not the Wrapper
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang Thinks A.I. Alarmism Has Gone Too Far | The Ezra Klein Show

article_ideas.angle: Counter the 'lowered barrier means less engineering' reading by tracing where correctness guarantees are re-established once the compiler-style contract is gone.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, developer-tooling teams, and engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: AI allows humans to program computers using natural human language rather than specialized programming languages
article_ideas.thesis: Moving the authoring interface from C++/CUDA to natural language lowers the barrier to entry but removes correctness enforcement from the front end, so the verification burden does not disappear — it moves downstream and gets more expensive per artifact.
article_ideas.title: Natural Language Is Not a Compiler
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang Thinks A.I. Alarmism Has Gone Too Far | The Ezra Klein Show

article_ideas.angle: Use Huang's energy claim as the test case for a general rule about planning against the lowest binding layer in layered platform shifts.
