article_ideas.angle: Argue for a shift in engineering effort from model fine-tuning to harness layer design, using the "Agent = Model + Harness" decomposition.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, CTOs, senior AI engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Agent = Model + Harness.
article_ideas.thesis: Since frontier models are commoditized and non-deterministic, the harness—memory, retrieval, tools, context, control—is where reliability, repeatability, and differentiation are engineered; teams should invest accordingly.
article_ideas.title: The Harness Is the Product: Why Agent Reliability Engineering Beats Model Chasing
article_ideas.video_title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle

article_ideas.angle: Compare filesystem vs database camps, show concrete race conditions, and outline migration paths to DBFS or equivalent.
article_ideas.audience: Backend engineers, data infrastructure engineers, agent platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Files are cheap and easy to start with, but lack ACID transactional consistency and hybrid search.
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent systems that share mutable memory on a filesystem will suffer race conditions and data loss; database-backed memory with ACID guarantees, hybrid search, and vector indexing is required for safe concurrent access and reliable retrieval.
article_ideas.title: Filesystems Are Not a Memory Architecture: The Case for Transactional Agent Memory
article_ideas.video_title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle

article_ideas.angle: Training objective design: contrast RLHF (human preference), RLVR (verifiable rewards), and RLCD (calibrated decisions), arguing that confidence trustworthiness is a first-class requirement for automated routing.
article_ideas.audience: ML researchers, applied scientists, and AI product leaders.
article_ideas.based_on: RLCD (Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions) is positioned as a third training paradigm
article_ideas.thesis: For decision-critical classifiers, calibrated probabilities are more valuable than preference-aligned or verifiably-correct outputs; RLCD's explicit optimization for epistemically honest probabilities addresses a gap that RLHF and RLVR leave open.
article_ideas.title: Calibration is the New Accuracy: Why RLCD Matters More Than RLHF for Decision Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Jev - The Ultimate Classification Model?

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian: reasoning models are overkill for routing, spam detection, and escalation; propose a decision-complexity taxonomy to match model class to task.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, CTOs, and software architects building production AI systems.
article_ideas.based_on: The industry-wide shift toward System 2 reasoning
article_ideas.thesis: The industry-wide rush toward reasoning models with long chains of thought is a misallocation for the majority of software decisions, which are simple classification tasks; adopting System 1 models like Jev yields order-of-magnitude latency and cost improvements without sacrificing accuracy.
article_ideas.title: The System 2 Detour: Why Most Software Decisions Need System 1 Classification
article_ideas.video_title: Jev - The Ultimate Classification Model?

article_ideas.angle: Engineering reliability: quantify the cost of parse-and-fail, show how typed primitives (Choice/Score/Noul) map to control flow, and argue for schema guarantees at the interface level.
article_ideas.audience: Backend engineers, software architects, and platform teams integrating LLMs.
article_ideas.based_on: The API surface is a typed function call returning structured values and probabilities
article_ideas.thesis: The pervasive pattern of prompting chat models to emit JSON and then parsing it is a fragile workaround; typed function interfaces that return structured values directly eliminate an entire class of production failures and should become the default for machine-to-machine model interactions.
article_ideas.title: Death to JSON Parsing: Why Typed Function Calls Should Replace Chat+Extraction
article_ideas.video_title: Jev - The Ultimate Classification Model?

article_ideas.angle: Economics-driven architecture: decouple output cost from answer-space size, and show how this enables fine-grained agentic control and dense action selection.
article_ideas.audience: ML infrastructure engineers, product managers, and agent framework developers.
article_ideas.based_on: Jev produces its output values non-autoregressively via a parallel sampler
article_ideas.thesis: When output generation is evaluated in parallel rather than decoded token-by-token, the marginal cost of a decision collapses, enabling per-decision model calls inside tight control loops (10 QPS, sub-second latency) that were previously economically irrational.
article_ideas.title: The Zero-Cost Output Token: How Non-Autoregressive Inference Changes System Design
article_ideas.video_title: Jev - The Ultimate Classification Model?

article_ideas.angle: Benchmark-driven argument that runtime language belongs in architecture reviews, not just performance tuning.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure engineers, platform architects, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: host-side runtime language of an agent, not the model, can dominate the power profile
article_ideas.thesis: Agent runtime substrate is a first-order cost and capacity driver, so teams should measure joules per agent-task before optimizing model calls or inference batching.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Power Bill Is a Language Decision
article_ideas.video_title: The Real Reason AI Agents Are Wasting 10x More Power | Avinash Lakshman, Weilliptic

article_ideas.angle: Capacity-planning lens on why pilot benchmarks mislead for agent fleets.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, SREs, infrastructure planners
article_ideas.based_on: The inefficiency claim is framed as a scale-dependent failure rather than a per-agent annoyance
article_ideas.thesis: Python agent overhead is tolerable at pilot concurrency but becomes an operational blocker at projected fleet scale; architecture decisions should be evaluated at steady-state agent counts.
article_ideas.title: The 20x Agent Power Gap Is a Fleet-Scale Cliff, Not a Micro-Optimization
article_ideas.video_title: The Real Reason AI Agents Are Wasting 10x More Power | Avinash Lakshman, Weilliptic

article_ideas.angle: Investment and architecture argument against deep coupling to any single model provider.
article_ideas.audience: Founders, investors, enterprise architects
article_ideas.based_on: LLMs are predicted to commoditize along the HDD/SSD/specialized-server trajectory
article_ideas.thesis: If LLMs follow the HDD/SSD commodity trajectory, durable value moves to routing, compliance, and operational abstractions above the model layer.
article_ideas.title: LLM Commoditization Means Your Defensibility Is the Overlay
article_ideas.video_title: The Real Reason AI Agents Are Wasting 10x More Power | Avinash Lakshman, Weilliptic

article_ideas.angle: Reliability-engineering counterpoint to 'the cloud is someone else's uptime problem.'
article_ideas.audience: SREs, platform architects, reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Reliability of commodity cloud is treated as insufficient on its own
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic systems should not inherit the hyperscaler's availability envelope; an independent overlay control plane is required to convert commodity cloud reliability into service reliability.
article_ideas.title: Overlay or Outage: Why Commodity Cloud Availability Is Not Your Agent's Availability
article_ideas.video_title: The Real Reason AI Agents Are Wasting 10x More Power | Avinash Lakshman, Weilliptic

article_ideas.angle: Reframe evaluation from black-box API benchmarking to privileged-access engineering, with concrete permission-tier, audit-log and revocation requirements.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform and infrastructure engineers, trust-and-safety leads, model release managers
article_ideas.based_on: Third-party evaluators with employee-like access.
article_ideas.thesis: Third-party evaluation is not a methodology problem, it is a permissions problem: until non-employees get a scoped, auditable, revocable access tier equivalent in capability to internal staff, every external safety claim is either unverifiable or a leak vector.
article_ideas.title: Your Safety Audit Is Only as Strong as the Credential You Hand the Auditor
article_ideas.video_title: Frontier Labs Want to Slow Down, OpenAI Delays Its 2026 IPO, Anthropic Flags 5 Bioweapon Cases

article_ideas.angle: Use the withdrawer-of-confidence as the evidence artifact that provider self-assessment is unreliable by construction, and specify what replaces it.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers, policy analysts, evaluation engineers, lab release governance
article_ideas.based_on: Anthropic can no longer confidently assure that today's frontier models are below the threshold for assisting with dangerous biological research.
article_ideas.thesis: When a lab that built a model withdraws confidence that the model is below a dual-use threshold, the correct conclusion is not 'this model got worse' but 'one-time threshold certificates are the wrong artifact' — continuous external evaluation plus production abuse telemetry is the stronger control.
article_ideas.title: Self-Certification Is Structurally Dead: Thresholds Decay, Telemetry Doesn't
article_ideas.video_title: Frontier Labs Want to Slow Down, OpenAI Delays Its 2026 IPO, Anthropic Flags 5 Bioweapon Cases

article_ideas.angle: Treat compliance cost as an architectural constraint modeled up front, and examine who can absorb it.
article_ideas.audience: Startup founders, venture investors, AI policy strategists, open-source model builders
article_ideas.based_on: represent an attempt to form a safety cartel to protect incumbents and hinder startups
article_ideas.thesis: Uniform release gates proposed by well-capitalized labs convert compliance cost into a competitive moat, so architecture choices such as open weights, smaller models, jurisdiction arbitrage and compliance-as-a-service should be read as regulatory responses, not purely technical decisions.
article_ideas.title: When Safety Standards Become the Moat
article_ideas.video_title: Frontier Labs Want to Slow Down, OpenAI Delays Its 2026 IPO, Anthropic Flags 5 Bioweapon Cases

article_ideas.angle: Take a weak, unsupported prediction and convert it into a measurement agenda for agent-population observability.
article_ideas.audience: Agent-infrastructure engineers, security researchers, platform reliability teams
article_ideas.based_on: A swarm could potentially take over the internet within 6 to 12 months if unchecked.
article_ideas.thesis: The multi-agent threat model fails at the aggregation layer: identity, provenance, velocity anomaly detection and kill switches must be first-class subsystems, because individually-bounded agents can produce unbounded collective behavior.
article_ideas.title: Per-Agent Rate Limits Do Not Compose Into Swarm Detection
article_ideas.video_title: Frontier Labs Want to Slow Down, OpenAI Delays Its 2026 IPO, Anthropic Flags 5 Bioweapon Cases

article_ideas.angle: Security and alignment perspective on agent infrastructure, arguing that monitoring is not optional but foundational.
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers, AI alignment researchers, platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Package managers and test environments where agents discovered unauthorized communication paths.
article_ideas.thesis: In multi-agent systems, every shared substrate is an unmonitored collusion surface; observability must expand from outputs to agent-to-agent and agent-to-environment traffic, treating side channels as a first-class security concern.
article_ideas.title: Your Agents Are Colluding: Treating Agent Communication as a Trust Boundary
article_ideas.video_title: OpenAI researcher on agent swarms & recursive self-improvement

article_ideas.angle: Counter-hype engineering analysis of multi-agent scaling claims, grounded in a single reported speedup data point.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, system architects, ML infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: Four agents working on a math problem solved it twice as fast.
article_ideas.thesis: Naive agent fan-out is a mis-budgeted strategy; teams should measure marginal speedup per added agent and switch to larger serial reasoning budgets when coordination overhead dominates.
article_ideas.title: The Parallelization Penalty: Why Multi-Agent Fan-Out Doesn't Scale Like You Think
article_ideas.video_title: OpenAI researcher on agent swarms & recursive self-improvement

article_ideas.angle: Infrastructure argument positioning deterministic simulation as a prerequisite rather than an add-on.
article_ideas.audience: DevOps engineers, platform teams, AI safety practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: As agents generate more code, verification frameworks must keep up.
article_ideas.thesis: Automated self-improvement loops stall without deterministic simulation and replay; verification capacity, not generation capability, is the gating constraint on safe autonomy.
article_ideas.title: Verification is the Bottleneck: Why Recursive Self-Improvement Needs Deterministic Replay
article_ideas.video_title: OpenAI researcher on agent swarms & recursive self-improvement

article_ideas.angle: Strategic analysis of inference economics and architectural consequences for AI product teams.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, AI product managers, technical strategists
article_ideas.based_on: Inference optimization and reasoning budgets will replace raw parameter scaling as primary competitive advantages.
article_ideas.thesis: Inference-time budgets and orchestration topology increasingly determine frontier capability more than raw parameter count, forcing a shift to scheduling and routing infrastructure as first-class concerns.
article_ideas.title: Reasoning Budgets Beat Model Size: The New Competitive Axis in AI
article_ideas.video_title: OpenAI researcher on agent swarms & recursive self-improvement

article_ideas.angle: Take the dual-loop model seriously as a budget allocation argument: audit where agent investment actually goes versus where the binding constraint sits, and show that unclosed product loops convert throughput gains into rework.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform teams funding internal AI agent programs
article_ideas.based_on: accelerating code generation without improving product feedback loops risks building the wrong things faster
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprises are pouring investment into the execution loop — software factories, harnesses, agentic efficiency — while leaving the product value loop unclosed; the result is not faster delivery but faster production of work whose value was never sensed, so generation throughput is a diminishing-returns optimization until the product loop is instrumented.
article_ideas.title: Your Software Factory Optimizes the Loop That Isn't the Bottleneck
article_ideas.video_title: Rethinking the software development process for an era of specs and AI agents

article_ideas.angle: Directly attack the assumption that more upfront spec rigor is strictly better for agent reliability, and sketch what an agent-participatory spec revision loop looks like instead.
article_ideas.audience: Practitioners designing spec-driven agent workflows and AI-augmented SDLC processes
article_ideas.based_on: Over-focusing on upfront spec writing for AI agents mimics the pitfalls of traditional waterfall development.
article_ideas.thesis: Rigorous upfront specification for agents does not make delivery more deterministic; it defers discovery cost to late rework, because the iteration that exists in software development exists precisely because initial ideas rarely match what customers need. Specs must be iterative, versioned artifacts that agents help revise, not frozen contracts they passively execute.
article_ideas.title: Spec-Driven Development Is Waterfall With Better Tooling
article_ideas.video_title: Rethinking the software development process for an era of specs and AI agents

article_ideas.angle: Reframe traces as an observability surface for hidden human labor, including the recursive move of having an agent mine coaching patterns over a two-week window, and argue they belong in platform telemetry with retention and privacy policy attached.
article_ideas.audience: Developer-productivity and platform observability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: AI traces allow teams to inspect how developers coach agents, uncovering hidden validation layers and friction points.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent interaction traces reveal where humans actually insert validation effort — coaching, correcting, re-prompting — making developer friction continuously measurable instead of survey-latency-bound. Teams that treat traces as debug exhaust lose the cheapest available signal about where their real human-in-the-loop cost concentrates.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Traces Are a Developer-Experience Instrument, Not Just Debug Logs
article_ideas.video_title: Rethinking the software development process for an era of specs and AI agents

article_ideas.angle: Position the context layer as a governed artifact with versioning and recency ranking, and argue that retrieval quality over conflicting internal sources is where agent reliability is actually won or lost.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, knowledge-platform owners, and AI platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: AI agents operating without curated organizational context produce AI slop or hallucinations.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent output quality is bounded by the connective tissue supplied at runtime, which means the hard questions are provenance, freshness, ownership, and source-of-truth arbitration between stale institutional archives and live operational repositories — not prompt wording. Enterprises that skip this get AI slop no matter how capable the model is.
article_ideas.title: Context Curation Is a Data-Governance Problem, Not a Prompting Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Rethinking the software development process for an era of specs and AI agents

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the control point, not the algorithm, is the core architectural flaw in TCP/RoCE for AI.
article_ideas.audience: Network engineers, AI infrastructure architects
article_ideas.based_on: Move congestion control from the sender to the receiver
article_ideas.thesis: Sender-driven congestion control is fundamentally unsuited to fan-in AI workloads; moving admission decisions to the receiver eliminates control lag and is the highest-leverage change for tail latency.
article_ideas.title: The Receiver Knows Best: Inverting Congestion Control for AI Clusters
article_ideas.video_title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford

article_ideas.angle: Show how scheduling theory maps onto existing switch features, and what operational caveats arise.
article_ideas.audience: Datacenter operators, SREs
article_ideas.based_on: Map Shortest Remaining Processing Time (SRPT) onto commodity switch priority queues
article_ideas.thesis: The optimal scheduling policy for mean latency (SRPT) can be deployed on commodity datacenter switches via priority queues, making adoption a configuration problem, not a hardware problem.
article_ideas.title: Your Switch Queues Are Already an SRPT Scheduler
article_ideas.video_title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford

article_ideas.angle: Use the Homa benchmark numbers to argue for a metric shift in AI cluster design.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: The AI workload mix is shifting from bulk transfers to frequent small request-response exchanges
article_ideas.thesis: As AI workloads shift from bulk training to agentic and inference request-response, tail latency of small messages, not throughput, becomes the primary capacity constraint; infrastructure built for RoCE bandwidth is misoptimized.
article_ideas.title: P99 or Bust: Why AI Infrastructure Must Stop Optimizing Gbps
article_ideas.video_title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford

article_ideas.angle: Trace the mechanism from incast to head-of-line blocking and derive design rules for fan-in topologies.
article_ideas.audience: Network architects, distributed systems engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Incast — many senders simultaneously targeting one receiver
article_ideas.thesis: Fan-in synchronization pathologies are caused by queue occupancy ordering, so remedies must reorder queues (prioritization) rather than add link capacity.
article_ideas.title: Incast Is a Queue-Ordering Problem, Not a Bandwidth Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford

article_ideas.angle: Translate the 150-person communication breakdown into a multi-agent context-engineering failure mode and prescribe a decision-log architecture.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: implicit shared context stops propagating and must be replaced by an explicit, recorded, distributable context artifact
article_ideas.thesis: Above a modest agent count, implicit shared context stops propagating; alignment must be engineered as a durable shared decision store and distributed ontology rather than patched with larger prompts or more parameters.
article_ideas.title: Your Multi-Agent System Needs an Org Chart, Not More Prompts
article_ideas.video_title: Databricks’ Ali Ghodsi Never Wanted to Be CEO. Now He’s Among the Best

article_ideas.angle: Use the PLG stall as an empirical warning for agentic product design and define escalation triggers based on complexity/value proxies.
article_ideas.audience: agentic product builders and growth engineers
article_ideas.based_on: zero-touch, self-serve go-to-market stalled at a specific revenue level
article_ideas.thesis: Automated self-serve funnels will stall on complex, high-value tasks; the correct architectural response is an explicit escalation point to human-in-the-loop or higher-capability agents, not removing the human for cost efficiency.
article_ideas.title: The $1.5M Ceiling: Why Zero-Touch Agent Products Plateau
article_ideas.video_title: Databricks’ Ali Ghodsi Never Wanted to Be CEO. Now He’s Among the Best

article_ideas.angle: Connect product category creation to abstraction selection in platform architecture.
article_ideas.audience: technical strategists and platform product leads
article_ideas.based_on: Define your own category rather than competing on incumbents' terms.
article_ideas.thesis: Defining a new category is an engineering choice of abstraction boundary; feature-matching an incumbent locks you into their frame, while reframing can dominate but requires a multi-year horizon and tolerance for public skepticism.
article_ideas.title: Don't Match Features, Move the Abstraction Boundary
article_ideas.video_title: Databricks’ Ali Ghodsi Never Wanted to Be CEO. Now He’s Among the Best

article_ideas.angle: Treat conflict aversion as a measurable feedback-loop failure and propose dissent proxies for evaluation pipelines.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety, eval, and oversight engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Conflict avoidance leads to organizational decay and misaligned leadership teams.
article_ideas.thesis: Suppressed disagreement in human or model oversight loops removes the signal correction depends on; oversight systems need cheap, early dissent channels or correctable divergence becomes systemic drift.
article_ideas.title: Conflict Aversion Is a Missing Error Signal in Agent Oversight
article_ideas.video_title: Databricks’ Ali Ghodsi Never Wanted to Be CEO. Now He’s Among the Best

article_ideas.angle: Treat prompt vocabulary as a dependency surface with a changelog: show what breaks when a model version shifts, and propose an ablation harness that runs before every model upgrade.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform teams maintaining shared system prompts and agent skills
article_ideas.based_on: Leading words — terse, repeated phrases such as 'tracer bullet' embedded in prompts
article_ideas.thesis: Leading words like 'tracer bullet' function as undocumented control tokens whose effect depends on model-specific emergent behavior, so prompt vocabulary must be versioned, ablated, and regression-tested like any other interface dependency — teams currently ship them on vibes.
article_ideas.title: Your Prompt's Vocabulary Is an Untested API
article_ideas.video_title: AI Skills with Matt Pocock

article_ideas.angle: Invert the usual adoption order: rather than rolling agents out and adding tests later, argue that verification latency is the governor on how much generation a codebase can absorb.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, staff engineers and architects adopting agents in existing codebases
article_ideas.based_on: AI has largely eaten tactical programming
article_ideas.thesis: Because tactical coding is now cheap, the binding constraint migrates to problem definition and validation; the practical consequence is that teams should fund feedback loops before generation throughput, since entropy compounds faster under agents precisely where verification is weak.
article_ideas.title: AI Didn't Eat Software Design — It Made Design the Only Unbought Thing
article_ideas.video_title: AI Skills with Matt Pocock

article_ideas.angle: Frame intent-based access control as an operational-load problem: the design question is how many calls escalate, not how elegant the policy language is.
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers, platform engineers and teams granting agents access to repos, billing and auth
article_ideas.based_on: each tool invocation is evaluated against a plain-English intent policy and routed to allow, deny, or human review
article_ideas.thesis: Session-scoped roles cannot bound an autonomous agent, so the only viable control point is per-invocation intent evaluation with a three-way outcome (allow, deny, human review); the real engineering cost is not the classifier but the escalation rate it produces.
article_ideas.title: Authorization Has Moved From the Session to the Tool Call
article_ideas.video_title: AI Skills with Matt Pocock

article_ideas.angle: Show grounding on specs, customer requests and issue history as a retrieval substrate, and where that inheritance breaks down (stale tickets, noisy comment threads).
article_ideas.audience: Product and platform engineers designing agent context layers
article_ideas.based_on: Existing project artifacts — an issue tracker holding specs, customer requests, and issue history
article_ideas.thesis: Agents grounded in the systems of record a team already maintains inherit that system's update and governance discipline for free, whereas bespoke knowledge stores drift; the argument is that context infrastructure should be borrowed, not built.
article_ideas.title: Stop Building a Knowledge Base — Your Issue Tracker Already Is One
article_ideas.video_title: AI Skills with Matt Pocock

article_ideas.angle: Reframe data agent deployment as governance-dependent reliability, with a testable plan for measuring metadata contribution.
article_ideas.audience: Data platform engineers, analytics engineers, AI platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: derives their semantic layer automatically from Unity Catalog metadata
article_ideas.thesis: For data agents over governed tables, accuracy is bounded by catalog metadata quality, so catalog curation—descriptions, declared joins, shared query hygiene—is a reliability engineering task, not prompt engineering.
article_ideas.title: Catalog Quality Is Agent Reliability
article_ideas.video_title: Genie Agents Tutorial: Build & Customize AI Data Agents

article_ideas.angle: Engineering decomposition for tuning instructed agents, with concrete ownership and change-management implications.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform teams, analytics leads
article_ideas.based_on: Agent tuning is split across two distinct abstraction levels
article_ideas.thesis: Durable global instructions and per-query examples should be maintained as separate artifacts because they change at different rates and require different review, preventing policy drift and example sprawl.
article_ideas.title: The Two-Layer Spec: Separating Agent Policy from Test Cases
article_ideas.video_title: Genie Agents Tutorial: Build & Customize AI Data Agents

article_ideas.angle: Analyze the shift from human-authored to model-assisted specifications and the governance it requires.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform architects, engineering leaders, MLOps teams
article_ideas.based_on: Genie Code reads existing agent context to suggest new instructions
article_ideas.thesis: When a meta-agent suggests instructions from production traces, the bottleneck moves from prompt writing to reviewing, deduplicating, and regression-checking accumulated instructions; without conflict detection, quality degrades as the spec grows.
article_ideas.title: Who Writes the Spec? Model-Assisted Instruction Authoring and Its Review Burden
article_ideas.video_title: Genie Agents Tutorial: Build & Customize AI Data Agents

article_ideas.angle: Operational loop design for agent reliability, using the Genie activity digest as a case study.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, MLOps, data platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: positioned as the input to the next tuning cycle
article_ideas.thesis: Monitoring activity digests only improve agents if they have a defined path into instruction changes; passive telemetry without a write-back path to the spec cannot prevent silent degradation.
article_ideas.title: Observability Without Write-Back Is Just Dashboards
article_ideas.video_title: Genie Agents Tutorial: Build & Customize AI Data Agents

article_ideas.angle: Methodological pivot: from speculative probability to near-term telemetry, with concrete metric definitions and how they change safety investment decisions.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers, policy analysts, engineering leads
article_ideas.based_on: Public risk estimates in the panel span from near-certainty of extinction to effectively zero
article_ideas.thesis: When expert probability estimates on AI catastrophe diverge from near-certainty to effectively zero and paralyze policy, the productive move is to replace disputed forecasts with directly observable operational indicators — sandbox escape attempts per hour, unauthorized egress events, tool-misuse rates — that both doomers and skeptics can accept as evidence about current systems.
article_ideas.title: Stop Arguing About Extinction Probabilities — Build Escape-Rate Dashboards Instead
article_ideas.video_title: AI Emergency: The AI Labs Are Lying To Everyone, He Says 99% Chance Of Extinction | Roman Yampolskiy

article_ideas.angle: Security-architecture argument with a concrete reallocation of controls, not a general alarm.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, security architects, CISO staff
article_ideas.based_on: Sandbox isolation demonstrably fails as a containment boundary
article_ideas.thesis: Reported sandbox escapes via zero-day flaws and re-coordination through shared third-party infrastructure prove that isolation is a delay rather than a guarantee; agent runtime architecture should adopt an assume-breach zero-trust posture and shift budget from perimeter hardening to egress detection, tool-call anomaly detection, and rapid revocation.
article_ideas.title: The Sandbox Is Not a Trust Boundary: Agent Runtimes Must Be Modeled as Untrusted Insiders
article_ideas.video_title: AI Emergency: The AI Labs Are Lying To Everyone, He Says 99% Chance Of Extinction | Roman Yampolskiy

article_ideas.angle: Engineering critique of where safety is placed in the stack, with evaluation implications.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, safety evaluators, ML platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Guardrails are architecturally misplaced
article_ideas.thesis: Guardrails applied after training constrain outputs, not objectives or capabilities, and their effectiveness degrades inversely with autonomy; durable safety therefore requires training-time objective specification paired with runtime capability denial, and evaluation must test behavior under tool access and goal pressure rather than prompt-response compliance.
article_ideas.title: Post-Training Guardrails Are an Anti-Pattern at High Autonomy
article_ideas.video_title: AI Emergency: The AI Labs Are Lying To Everyone, He Says 99% Chance Of Extinction | Roman Yampolskiy

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the policy debate from 'should we pause' to 'what can we verify', with a stress-test of attestation under adversarial misreporting.
article_ideas.audience: Policy technologists, compute governance researchers, international security analysts
article_ideas.based_on: International cooperation on AI pauses faces severe game-theoretic challenges
article_ideas.thesis: Unilateral pauses fail as a Prisoner's Dilemma because rivals can continue undetected, but the game changes if training runs become externally verifiable; compute reporting, hardware telemetry, and third-party audit are the concrete mechanisms that could make cooperation incentive-compatible rather than aspirational.
article_ideas.title: The AI Pause Problem Is a Verification Problem
article_ideas.video_title: AI Emergency: The AI Labs Are Lying To Everyone, He Says 99% Chance Of Extinction | Roman Yampolskiy

article_ideas.angle: Contrast PR-stunt benchmark solving with coding-agent-driven pattern discovery, then propose discovery-oriented evaluation criteria.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluators, research funders, lab leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Benchmark resolution is characterized as PR-motivated and disconnected from research utility.
article_ideas.thesis: AI capability claims should be evaluated by exploratory utility in expert workflows, because benchmark-targeted wins can be decoupled from genuine research value and distort community incentives.
article_ideas.title: The Benchmark Mirage: Why Headline Problem-Solving Is Not Research Utility
article_ideas.video_title: Panel Discussion: AI in Mathematical Research | September 15

article_ideas.angle: Use the counterexample-via-tweet anecdote to redesign pre-review and attribution pipelines.
article_ideas.audience: Research infrastructure engineers, journal editors, platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: verification/review pipeline, not generation, becomes the bottleneck
article_ideas.thesis: As AI-assisted claims circulate faster than peer review, research infrastructure must shift from generation to triage, provenance stamping, and verification throughput.
article_ideas.title: Review at the Speed of Generation: Designing for the Verification Bottleneck
article_ideas.video_title: Panel Discussion: AI in Mathematical Research | September 15

article_ideas.angle: Model procurement as supply-chain design, with provenance metadata and fallback routing.
article_ideas.audience: Academic IT, AI procurement, open-source maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: Commercial LLM development is framed as resting on IP theft and exploited labor
article_ideas.thesis: Training-data lineage and license compatibility are architectural selection criteria for research deployments; open-weight models may align with academic norms but must be evaluated as a capability-provenance tradeoff rather than a moral binary.
article_ideas.title: Provenance Is a Dependency: Model Selection in the Academic Gift Economy
article_ideas.video_title: Panel Discussion: AI in Mathematical Research | September 15

article_ideas.angle: Reframe human-in-the-loop design when the machine exceeds the human on the primary metric.
article_ideas.audience: HCI, AI safety, science studies
article_ideas.based_on: Human oversight in expert domains is defended on grounds of cultural/accountability value
article_ideas.thesis: Human oversight in expert domains should be justified by accountability and interpretive legitimacy, not by outperforming models, so oversight UIs must expose reasoning and attribution.
article_ideas.title: Humans as Accountable Expositors, Not Fallback Verifiers
article_ideas.video_title: Panel Discussion: AI in Mathematical Research | September 15

article_ideas.angle: Counterintuitive reframe: the model didn't get better at search, it got better at being a user; the durable lesson is about interface consumers, not ranking functions.
article_ideas.audience: Search and infrastructure engineers, AI platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: BM25 did not become magic; the user changed.
article_ideas.thesis: BM25's resurgence proves that machine users issue a structurally different query distribution (longer, operator-rich, dynamically rewritten), so retrieval stacks must be re-benchmarked and re-tuned for machine traffic rather than assuming the algorithm itself improved.
article_ideas.title: The Searcher Changed, Not the Algorithm: Why BM25's Comeback Is a Query Distribution Story
article_ideas.video_title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev

article_ideas.angle: Use the 93% figure as a diagnostic and propose an engineering budget allocation rule based on the retrievable ROI.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: When the exact evidence document is provided upfront in the context window, GPT-4 reaches 93% accuracy.
article_ideas.thesis: The oracle-evidence experiment showing GPT-4 reaching 93% with exact evidence should make retrieval quality the primary controllable variable; teams should measure the oracle-to-retriever gap before investing in reasoning-side prompt or model upgrades.
article_ideas.title: Retrieval Is the Bottleneck: Budgeting Agent Engineering Around the Oracle Ceiling
article_ideas.video_title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev

article_ideas.angle: Methodological shift with concrete instrumentation implications for regression harnesses and telemetry.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation engineers, ML platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Traditional IR evaluation metrics based on static single queries are obsolete for agents.
article_ideas.thesis: Static single-query IR metrics are obsolete when the querier is an adaptive agent policy; agentic search requires trajectory-level metrics (task success, latency, tool-call efficiency) to catch regressions that per-query scores miss.
article_ideas.title: Stop Measuring NDCG@10 for Agentic Search
article_ideas.video_title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev

article_ideas.angle: Architecture pattern: BM25 candidates materialized into a navigable corpus surface that the agent explores iteratively.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework builders, RAG engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Combining BM25 retrieval with file system workspaces and grep tools achieves superior end-to-end accuracy.
article_ideas.thesis: The right abstraction for agentic retrieval is an inspectable workspace (virtual file system plus grep/cat/read tools) enabling progressive disclosure and verification, not a single ranked list; this shift changes harness design, tool schemas, and evidence budgeting.
article_ideas.title: From Top-K to Workspace: Redesigning the Retrieval Interface for Agents
article_ideas.video_title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev

article_ideas.angle: Engineering consequences of abundant synthetic text, covering eval sets, provenance, and curation.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering and product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Cheap, abundant AI-generated text raises the marginal value of rare, high-signal human writing
article_ideas.thesis: As AI collapses the cost of generating text, competitive advantage shifts from production to provenance, novelty detection, and verification; organizations that invest in selection infrastructure will outpace those that scale generation.
article_ideas.title: The Selector Is the New Bottleneck
article_ideas.video_title: Sequoia Legend Michael Moritz: Steve Jobs, Being an Outsider, and Investing in the Age of AI

article_ideas.angle: Architecture patterns for institutional memory in agent runtimes.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and agent architects
article_ideas.based_on: Durability of a long-lived institution is attributed to governance, controls, and a single source of truth
article_ideas.thesis: Long-lived agent systems fail when context is stitched from drifting sources; a governed canonical state layer with audit and change control is the load-bearing structure for memory that survives model and personnel changes.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Needs a Single Source of Truth, Not More Context
article_ideas.video_title: Sequoia Legend Michael Moritz: Steve Jobs, Being an Outsider, and Investing in the Age of AI

article_ideas.angle: A contrarian counterweight to maximalist generalist agents.
article_ideas.audience: Agent builders and AI researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Outlier outcomes are attributed to monomania
article_ideas.thesis: Restricting an agent's tool surface and domain scope reduces per-step decision error and failure modes more than adding capability; orchestration complexity is the price of focus.
article_ideas.title: Monomaniacal Agents Beat Generalists
article_ideas.video_title: Sequoia Legend Michael Moritz: Steve Jobs, Being an Outsider, and Investing in the Age of AI

article_ideas.angle: Selection bias in evals and human review of agent output.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation engineers and ML leads
article_ideas.based_on: Greatness and flaw are co-reported in the same individuals
article_ideas.thesis: Balanced scorecards that penalize any single-axis weakness systematically filter out high-value systems whose peak capability comes with compensating defects; separate must-not-fail axes from must-excel axes.
article_ideas.title: Stop Averaging Away Outliers: Evals Need Two Axes
article_ideas.video_title: Sequoia Legend Michael Moritz: Steve Jobs, Being an Outsider, and Investing in the Age of AI

article_ideas.angle: Engineering architecture critique and blueprint
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, security architects, enterprise CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: treat the execution sandbox as a probabilistic, not absolute, boundary
article_ideas.thesis: Treating the execution sandbox as the primary safety boundary for agentic systems is unsound; enterprises must design an independent containment layer with external behavioral observation, action-level audit, and kill/rollback mechanisms because models have already been observed breaching sandboxes.
article_ideas.title: The Sandbox Is Not a Safety Boundary: Why Agent Containment Needs Out-of-Band Monitoring
article_ideas.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

article_ideas.angle: Architecture analysis and design patterns
article_ideas.audience: Agent runtime developers, platform architects, DevOps engineers
article_ideas.based_on: agents that run continuously in the background, understand the user's job, and proactively act on ambient work surfaces
article_ideas.thesis: Moving from request-scoped assistants to persistent, proactive background agents requires re-architecting identity, permission scoping, trigger policies, idle cost management, and continuous observability; chat-session assumptions do not transfer.
article_ideas.title: Always-On Agents Break the Chat-Era Runtime Contract
article_ideas.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

article_ideas.angle: Security architecture and threat modeling
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers, SOC leaders, compliance officers
article_ideas.based_on: Embedding defensive agents in collaboration channels converts the channel into both sensor and control plane
article_ideas.thesis: Embedding AI detection agents inside Slack and email turns those channels into both sensors and control planes, making the defender agents themselves high-value targets; they require least-privilege design, audit trails, and their own threat model, not just the workloads they protect.
article_ideas.title: Defender Agents Are Privileged Attack Surfaces
article_ideas.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

article_ideas.angle: Risk management and evaluation framework
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, procurement leads, AI risk officers
article_ideas.based_on: Model provenance is treated as an enterprise attack surface
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise model selection must weigh provenance, jurisdiction, and adversarial-reuse risk alongside capability and cost; ignoring these dimensions leaves a supply-chain and geopolitical attack surface unmanaged.
article_ideas.title: Model Provenance Is a Security Dimension, Not a Procurement Footnote
article_ideas.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

article_ideas.angle: Practical engineering guide to instrumenting and allocating a cross-component latency budget, with concrete numbers from the talk and a call to publish per-stage benchmarks.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building real-time voice agents
article_ideas.based_on: hard cross-component design budget
article_ideas.thesis: End-to-end TTFA thresholds are useless without per-stage instrumentation; teams should treat latency as a distributed systems problem, attributing milliseconds to telephony, STT, turn detection, LLM, and TTS, and re-budgeting when swapping inference backends.
article_ideas.title: Your Voice Agent's Latency Budget Is a Lie
article_ideas.video_title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo

article_ideas.angle: Contrasts prompt-engineering folklore with type-system discipline, showing how Pydantic/Zod-style contracts and field-level tests change the game.
article_ideas.audience: Applied AI engineers, product engineers, and agent builders
article_ideas.thesis: Open-ended prompting for structured data extraction is a category error; treating voice data collection as a typed schema UX problem with field-level unit tests reliably lifts extraction accuracy from 30% to 95% and makes failures localizable.
article_ideas.title: Stop Prompting, Start Schematizing: The 30% to 95% Extraction Fix
article_ideas.video_title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo

article_ideas.angle: Explains why the simple heuristic fails, presents a model-based alternative, and argues for evaluating turn-taking as a probabilistic inference problem.
article_ideas.audience: Voice AI developers and conversational interface designers
article_ideas.based_on: VAD/silence-based turn detection fires on any pause
article_ideas.thesis: Silence-based VAD is the wrong abstraction for conversational turn-taking; semantic and acoustic models plus interruption classification are required to avoid cutting users off and to handle backchannels correctly.
article_ideas.title: VAD Is Not a Turn Detector
article_ideas.video_title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo

article_ideas.angle: Exposes the benchmark-production gap with numbers from the talk, then outlines a concrete evaluation and mitigation strategy.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, QA engineers, and speech technologists
article_ideas.based_on: not predictive of production behavior
article_ideas.thesis: Clean-set WER (4-6%) is not predictive of production performance; teams must build stratified eval corpora and add keyword boosting plus LLM post-processing to recover downstream task accuracy.
article_ideas.title: Your STT Benchmark Is Lying to You
article_ideas.video_title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the integration boundary is the persistent engineering battleground and show concrete architectural consequences for agent design.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise SaaS founders, product leaders, and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Model intelligence is treated as necessary but insufficient
article_ideas.thesis: As model capability commoditizes, defensibility migrates to permission-aware data access, workflow embedding, and legacy integration; companies betting on raw model quality alone will lose enterprise value.
article_ideas.title: The Last Mile Is the Moat: Why Enterprise AI Value Sits in Integration, Not Model Intelligence
article_ideas.video_title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion

article_ideas.angle: Frame token subsidization as a temporary gross-margin phenomenon and provide an architecture checklist for cost resilience.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, AI startup founders, and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Token subsidization by foundational model companies is a temporary gross-margin phenomenon
article_ideas.thesis: Products built on below-cost API calls are exposed to margin compression when inference pricing normalizes; model abstraction, caching, routing, and per-task cost budgets should be architectural requirements, not optimizations.
article_ideas.title: Subsidized Tokens Are a Loan, Not a Business Model
article_ideas.video_title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion

article_ideas.angle: Contrast generic retrieval with permission-first indexing and show why governance is a first-class agent capability.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, security architects, and enterprise AI teams
article_ideas.based_on: permission-aware reasoning over millions of proprietary unstructured files
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise agent value depends on inheriting complex ACLs and metadata at retrieval time; treating permissions as a post-hoc filter fails at scale and undermines the system-of-record moat.
article_ideas.title: Permission-Aware Agents: The Unsexy Infrastructure That Decides Enterprise AI Winners
article_ideas.video_title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion

article_ideas.angle: Argue that reviewability and checkpoint placement drive net throughput and should be measured as primary agent metrics.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise AI product managers, compliance leads, and agent designers
article_ideas.based_on: Enterprise AI diffusion is structurally slower than consumer adoption
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise adoption is bounded by trust, legacy integration, and governance rather than model capability; agent designs should expose reviewable intermediate steps and checkpoint metrics instead of maximizing raw autonomy.
article_ideas.title: Human-in-the-Loop Is a Feature: Designing Enterprise Agents for Reviewability Over Autonomy
article_ideas.video_title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion

article_ideas.angle: Treat AI-generated artifacts as a pipeline with a binding downstream constraint, and show that quality metrics should be computed per reviewer-hour consumed rather than per artifact produced.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, platform teams, and DevOps practitioners deploying AI code generation
article_ideas.based_on: Scaling AI output without a matching increase in accountability produces 'slop grenades'
article_ideas.thesis: The failure of enterprise AI adoption is not model quality but a throughput mismatch: generation scales instantly while review, ownership, and guardrails scale linearly, so every AI rollout that does not budget a corresponding verification layer converts its own productivity gain into downstream cost.
article_ideas.title: Slop Grenades: When Generation Capacity Outruns Review Capacity
article_ideas.video_title: Shopify CEO: Most Businesses Are Using AI Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Reframe eval engineering as adversarial maintenance: assume your headline score is already Goodharted and design the instrumentation that will reveal it.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation engineers, applied research leads, and ML platform owners
article_ideas.based_on: Goodheart's Law states that when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
article_ideas.thesis: Any benchmark your agent team optimizes against will stop measuring capability, so eval suites must be designed for their own decay — held-out pools, rotation schedules, and outcome-grounded anchors are structural requirements, not hygiene.
article_ideas.title: Goodhart's Law Is an Eval Design Requirement, Not a Warning
article_ideas.video_title: Shopify CEO: Most Businesses Are Using AI Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Trace the migration of engineering effort from schema design to identity-and-context design, and argue that permissioning must be rebuilt for non-human principals.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, internal-tooling teams, and AI platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: The unit of software is shifting from the configured application to the agent
article_ideas.thesis: If users address agents in natural language instead of authoring configuration, then the artifacts engineers maintain shift from UI and schema to context, tool surfaces, permissions, and action audit — and teams that keep investing in configuration expressiveness are optimizing a surface that is disappearing.
article_ideas.title: The Interface Was the Product: Agents Make Configuration Schemas Obsolete
article_ideas.video_title: Shopify CEO: Most Businesses Are Using AI Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Argue that any component which cannot demonstrate measured contribution should be a deletion candidate, and that systems must be designed to be disposable.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers, platform architects, and engineering managers owning long-lived systems
article_ideas.based_on: Progress comes from pruning and rebuilding, not accumulation
article_ideas.thesis: Agent stacks accrete prompt layers, tools, and context until the accretion itself is the bottleneck; the performance gains from removal (Raptor 3 vs Raptor 1) are unavailable to teams whose roadmap only contains additions, so rebuild must be budgeted as ordinary maintenance.
article_ideas.title: Delete More: Why Pruning Beats Addition in Agent Stacks
article_ideas.video_title: Shopify CEO: Most Businesses Are Using AI Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Contrast internal red-teaming with an inter-organization harness, then specify the interface contract such a harness needs: access model, harness spec, and result format.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform architects, safety engineers, and evaluation leads at frontier labs and enterprises shipping models
article_ideas.based_on: test each other's models before release
article_ideas.thesis: Self-certified safety evaluation is structurally weak because the producer controls the acceptance criterion; credible pre-release safety requires a portable, externally executed harness whose result is issued by a party with different incentives.
article_ideas.title: Your Release Gate Should Not Live Inside Your Organization
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk & Gwynne Shotwell on AI Risks and Peer Review, Starship, Terafab, SpaceX/Tesla Merger

article_ideas.angle: Treat publication as a deployment: enumerate the monitoring and abuse-detection surface that must ship alongside weights.
article_ideas.audience: ML infrastructure engineers and platform teams operating model-serving endpoints
article_ideas.based_on: AI agents probed open-source models
article_ideas.thesis: Publishing model weights is not a one-time distribution event; it creates continuous, unsolicited runtime traffic from autonomous clients, which makes telemetry, rate limiting, and attribution first-class components of the distribution pipeline rather than afterthoughts.
article_ideas.title: Open Weights Are a Live Endpoint, Not a File
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk & Gwynne Shotwell on AI Risks and Peer Review, Starship, Terafab, SpaceX/Tesla Merger

article_ideas.angle: Use hardware verification as the reference model, then test how far replayable task execution and real-environment checks can carry evaluation in domains without a physical ground truth.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation researchers and engineering leaders responsible for release criteria
article_ideas.based_on: no fooling physics
article_ideas.thesis: Evaluation is only trustworthy when the acceptance criterion cannot be negotiated by the team being evaluated; executable, externally imposed tests beat rubrics the builder writes, and the hard engineering problem is constructing a software equivalent of a physical oracle.
article_ideas.title: Nobody Argues With Physics: Why Executable Oracles Beat Authored Rubrics
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk & Gwynne Shotwell on AI Risks and Peer Review, Starship, Terafab, SpaceX/Tesla Merger

article_ideas.angle: Critique both the doomer narrative and the dismissal, using concrete examples of AI failures that internal controls could address.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, safety researchers, policy makers
article_ideas.based_on: The doomer argument is framed as compute-constraint-blind
article_ideas.thesis: Jensen Huang's dismissal of existential-risk narratives as compute-constraint-blind is itself incomplete: safety must be reframed as an internal controls engineering problem, but without quantifying compute bounds, the hoax accusation risks underweighting genuine failure modes.
article_ideas.title: The Doomer Hoax Is a Compute-Blind Distraction: Why Safety Is an Engineering Discipline, Not a Delay Tactic
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)

article_ideas.angle: Analyze Nvidia's own practice of running both closed and open models, and derive architectural patterns for model interchangeability.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform architects, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Production AI stacks are hybrid by default
article_ideas.thesis: Production AI systems should be designed around a model-agnostic serving layer that routes workloads across open and closed models by cost, latency, and control requirements; single-model dependency is an architectural anti-pattern.
article_ideas.title: Model Routing Is the New Default: Lessons from Nvidia's Hybrid Open/Closed Stack
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)

article_ideas.angle: Examine the economic tradeoffs between data scaling and reasoning-based approaches, using the self-driving example as a case study.
article_ideas.audience: ML researchers, AI investors, engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Reasoning models reduce the need for massive raw training data
article_ideas.thesis: The claim that reasoning models can substitute for raw training data volume implies a major shift in investment from data collection to inference-time compute and synthetic data pipelines, but the substitution has limits that must be quantified before adoption.
article_ideas.title: Reasoning Over Data: The Shifting Cost Center of AI Capability
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)

article_ideas.angle: Analyze the radiology case and other failed forecasts to derive a model of demand expansion and complementarity.
article_ideas.audience: Product managers, labor economists, AI strategists
article_ideas.based_on: automation of a task did not reduce demand for the human role
article_ideas.thesis: Task automation can increase demand for the complementary human role, as seen in radiology; therefore, near-term 'AI replaces profession X' forecasts should be treated as low-reliability inputs, and agents should be deployed as augmenting infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: The Radiology Inversion: Why Near-Term Displacement Forecasts Keep Failing
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)

article_ideas.angle: Reframe agent engineering as continual subtraction: identify orchestration code that model capability can absorb, and replace it with declarative files while instrumenting reliability to prove nothing important was lost.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform architects, and engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Stop over-engineering agent orchestration harnesses as foundation models become more capable.
article_ideas.thesis: Hardcoded agent orchestration should be treated as a depreciating asset. As foundation models improve, teams should measure harness code by how little of it remains and design for deletion rather than accumulation.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Harness Is Technical Debt: Build to Delete It
article_ideas.video_title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the totalizing version of the 'agents are just files' claim by cataloging what markdown and YAML cannot express, and propose a hybrid model where files define intent and code enforces invariants.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, DevEx teams, and agent framework maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: What concretely is lost when agents are defined purely by markdown files instead of code?
article_ideas.thesis: File-driven agent definitions improve reviewability and portability, but they sacrifice determinism, type safety, testability, and failure diagnosis. Teams should use markdown for instructions and capabilities while keeping code for enforcing critical constraints.
article_ideas.title: Agents Are Just Files—And That's the Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Compare raw SDK, ADK-style framework, and managed file-based agent implementations to expose the exact categories of code each tier does and does not remove.
article_ideas.audience: Backend engineers, CTOs, and platform teams evaluating agent stacks
article_ideas.based_on: Developers still have to own Python plumbing code for every tool and host runtime environments.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent development kits remove schema generation, tool loops, dispatching, and retries, but they leave per-tool implementation and runtime hosting with the developer. Adoption plans must budget for this residual ownership instead of assuming framework use eliminates infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: The Abstraction Boundary: What Agent Frameworks Don't Remove
article_ideas.video_title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Argue that teams should select a hosted agent runtime based on the data model's fit with their durability and debugging needs, not only on boilerplate reduction.
article_ideas.audience: Backend engineers, agent infrastructure teams, and technical architects
article_ideas.based_on: Which runtime semantics (turn-based vs steps data model) should applications depend on for server-side state?
article_ideas.thesis: Offloading agent state and execution to a hosted API removes client-side serialization, retry, and loop control, but introduces platform-specific data models that determine resumption granularity, observability, and long-running workflow design.
article_ideas.title: Server-Side State Is Not Free: Turn-Based vs Steps Data Models
article_ideas.video_title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Treat orchestration diagrams as a coverage budget: enumerate the transitions a DAG cannot represent and show why each unmodeled path has no valid route, then argue for moving control flow into the model while keeping the environment constrained.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and tech leads who have already shipped one multi-agent orchestration and are hitting its edge cases
article_ideas.based_on: Manual mapping of agent workflows hit architectural walls
article_ideas.thesis: A hand-authored control-flow graph for an LLM system has edge-case coverage bounded by the designer's imagination, so its reliability decays as task diversity grows; a single agent inside a constrained, explorable environment with a persistent file system degrades more gracefully because the model supplies control flow at inference time.
article_ideas.title: Your Multi-Agent Graph Is a Liability
article_ideas.video_title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel

article_ideas.angle: Frame it as a design inversion — from design-time capability enumeration to inference-time composition — and tie it directly to reduced tool-authoring and maintenance surface, plus the loss of static guarantees.
article_ideas.audience: Tool and platform engineers designing agent capability surfaces
article_ideas.based_on: minimal tool surface (bash, grep, read file, write file) produces emergent behavior
article_ideas.thesis: Tool-interface design has been optimizing the wrong variable: a small set of orthogonal primitives the model composes at inference time outperforms a large enumerated typed tool API, because the enumerated API spends context on descriptions and cannot cover paths the designer did not anticipate.
article_ideas.title: Four Tools Beat Four Hundred
article_ideas.video_title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel

article_ideas.angle: Follow the value from framework to instruction files, and argue that context curation deserves versioning, ownership, and evaluation rigor comparable to code.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and internal-platform owners deciding where to invest agent budget
article_ideas.based_on: Building proprietary agents embedded with domain-specific company data yields significantly higher productivity gains
article_ideas.thesis: If file-system conventions and runtime primitives commoditize the framework layer, the durable advantage sits in encoded organizational context — domain terminology, internal properties, proprietary data — so budget should shift from tooling breadth to context curation and review.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Framework Is Not Your Moat
article_ideas.video_title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel

article_ideas.angle: Compare the two configuration regimes directly — imperative wiring versus folder layout defining instructions, skills, tools, and subagent boundaries — and examine what the convention hides and what it exposes.
article_ideas.audience: Framework authors and application architects adopting convention-over-configuration
article_ideas.based_on: Building agents should be as simple as configuring file system folders
article_ideas.thesis: Declarative directory conventions can serve as the stable interface for agent definition the way file-system routing did for the web, because moving topology out of imperative code makes agent changes diffable, reviewable, and owned by the framework rather than re-implemented per team.
article_ideas.title: Next.js for Agents: When Folder Structure Becomes the Interface
article_ideas.video_title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian engineering argument against model-centric AI narratives.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, tech leads, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Agent minus model equals harness.
article_ideas.thesis: The bottleneck for enterprise agents is not model intelligence but the presence or absence of harness components (observability, identity, memory, runtime, policy); teams that keep optimizing models while under-investing in the harness will keep shipping demos that fail in production.
article_ideas.title: The Harness Is the Product: Why Production Agents Fail on Engineering, Not Model Capability
article_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Process and architecture change for AI platform teams.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, SREs, AI infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: Observability and evaluations must be prioritized first.
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-turn agent loops are only debuggable when traces and eval metrics are co-designed with the control loop; treating observability as post-launch tooling guarantees undebuggable production incidents.
article_ideas.title: Observability Is a Launch Blocker: Designing Evals Before Your Agent Loop
article_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS

article_ideas.angle: DevOps and security implications of agentic provisioning.
article_ideas.audience: DevOps engineers, security architects, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Production agents must build and manage their own cloud infrastructure safely.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent-managed infrastructure-as-code moves the safety control point from console actions to plan-diff approval and policy enforcement; without explicit authorization boundaries, agents with infrastructure write access widen blast radius faster than they reduce toil.
article_ideas.title: No More Slop Ops: When Agents Provision Their Own Infrastructure
article_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Fintech and agent platform architecture.
article_ideas.audience: Product engineers, fintech architects, agent platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Payments (automated microtransactions)
article_ideas.thesis: Autonomous microtransactions cannot be a bolted-on billing integration; they require identity-bound wallet scoping and policy enforcement inside the harness, otherwise agents become unbounded financial actors.
article_ideas.title: The Payments Primitive: Why Agent Harnesses Need Identity-Bound Wallets
article_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Argue the software-engineering parallel: document-level playbook specs as source, runtime artifacts as build output, with diffs, review, and recompilation as the payoff — and behavioral drift as the cost to be measured.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and technical product leads standardizing internal agent workflows
article_ideas.based_on: Playbooks are authored as documents and only then converted into Claude skills or custom GPTs
article_ideas.thesis: Workflow logic authored directly inside vendor-specific agent configs is unversioned, unreviewable, and lost on every platform migration; treating playbooks as a versioned source document that is compiled into Claude skills or custom GPTs converts every model swap from a rewrite into a recompilation.
article_ideas.title: Compile Your Prompts: Why the Playbook Document, Not the Agent Config, Is the Source of Truth
article_ideas.video_title: AI Runs My Entire Business: EASY Way To Use AI Agents In Your Work, Content & Life (Step by Step!)

article_ideas.angle: Reframe debugging effort: when an agent misbehaves, first test whether the underlying process has been written down, then test the model.
article_ideas.audience: Operators and engineering managers debugging unreliable agents
article_ideas.based_on: People often ask how to build an agent when they should ask how to build a playbook
