article_ideas.audience: Agent framework architects, developer tooling teams, engineering leaders designing multi-agent workflows
article_ideas.based_on: When AI agents build software iteratively from scratch without seeing prior agent evolution
article_ideas.thesis: What one agent passes to the next is not plumbing but design: code-only handoff optimizes for reproducibility and context hygiene while discarding design intent, and that trade has a measurable downstream cost. Treating the handoff artifact — code, code plus history, or code plus design contracts — as a first-class architectural component is the precondition for making per-feature defect rates roughly constant instead of compounding.
article_ideas.title: The Handoff Artifact Is an Architecture Decision
article_ideas.video_title: The Data Structure Problem AI Coding Agents Can't See

article_ideas.angle: Take the ecological psychiatry critique and apply it to machine learning evaluation design, arguing that evaluation is an epistemic frame, not a passive ruler.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluators, alignment researchers, benchmark designers
article_ideas.based_on: The frame in which a system reasons determines which states look pathological
article_ideas.thesis: Benchmarks are not neutral measuring instruments; they encode an implicit answer to which world the agent is supposed to live in, and that ontology determines whether disconnection from the environment is registered as failure or silently discarded as irrelevant.
article_ideas.title: Every benchmark hides a model of the agent's world
article_ideas.video_title: The Levels of Consciousness Psychiatry Denies | Brian Stafford

article_ideas.angle: Translate rites-of-passage and underworld soul work into an engineering pattern of backups, isolated transformation sandboxes, and re-entry protocols.
article_ideas.audience: AI systems engineers, agentic architecture designers, long-lived agent maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: requires a destructive release of the current structure inside a temporary ceremonial container
article_ideas.thesis: Continuous optimization in production cannot change a system's core direction because it cannot tolerate the needed period of disorganization; safe deep change requires deliberately scheduled, bounded exceptions where the old objective is allowed to die first.
article_ideas.title: AI needs an underworld: engineering destructive, schedule-contained cycles of self-change
article_ideas.video_title: The Levels of Consciousness Psychiatry Denies | Brian Stafford

article_ideas.angle: Use the claim about childhood eco-centric consciousness loss to fault monotonic-evaluation approaches and argue for longitudinal checkpoints that preserve early 'wild' snapshots.
article_ideas.audience: ML researchers, pretraining teams, alignment evaluators
article_ideas.based_on: Capability collapse during training can be invisible to final evaluation
article_ideas.thesis: SOTA final evaluation can be consistent with losing almost all of an initially dominant creative/environmental ability if that ability lived only in the early distribution and was never made part of the measurement baseline.
article_ideas.title: The 95% solution: why endpoint benchmarks stay flat while most early capability disappears
article_ideas.video_title: The Levels of Consciousness Psychiatry Denies | Brian Stafford

article_ideas.angle: Critique the industry's focus on maximizing catalyst power and argue that durable value is created in the post-catalyst consolidation protocol.
article_ideas.audience: Agent developers, applied AI product teams, capability expansion engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Separate the insight-generation phase from the integration phase; optimize the integration contract as much as the catalyst.
article_ideas.thesis: Any capability-expanding event that relies on a catalyst or sudden injection, whether a psychedelic-like insight, a new tool, or an amplitude of new context, is useless unless the surrounding system has a deliberate integration phase that rebuilds identity around the new state.
article_ideas.title: After the blast: why integration is the underdesigned half of every frontier systems expansion
article_ideas.video_title: The Levels of Consciousness Psychiatry Denies | Brian Stafford

article_ideas.angle: An architecture anti-pattern article focused on the structural guarantees lost when text-to-text stitching replaces programmatic joins.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and data platform teams building agentic data systems
article_ideas.based_on: Do not implement joins by asking an LLM to generate text over relational content.
article_ideas.thesis: LLMs should not be used as relational join engines; production AI systems should let deterministic relational engines execute joins and use LLMs only for translation, planning, and explanation.
article_ideas.title: Your AI Agents Can't Join Tables by Reading Text
article_ideas.video_title: Do Databases Have a Future? | Conversations in Action

article_ideas.angle: An evaluation-critique article connecting schema rot to misleading benchmark deltas.
article_ideas.audience: Data engineering leaders, AI evaluation teams, and enterprise data platform buyers
article_ideas.based_on: The gap between benchmark performance and enterprise performance of data agents is caused by schema rot.
article_ideas.thesis: Clean public text-to-SQL benchmark scores are poor predictors of enterprise data-agent performance because they omit schema rot; evaluation suites must encode production warehouse messiness before deployment claims are credible.
article_ideas.title: The Spider/Bird Performance Mirage
article_ideas.video_title: Do Databases Have a Future? | Conversations in Action

article_ideas.angle: An engineering-decision article challenging the default addition of graph stores to AI/data stacks.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Graph databases model data as edge tables and node tables, which are fundamentally relational.
article_ideas.thesis: Most graph database use cases are just node tables and edge tables, so the burden of proof for adopting a graph database is measured query performance on your actual workload, not a belief that graph semantics require a new engine.
article_ideas.title: Graph Databases Are Beautiful Relations Until You Benchmark Them
article_ideas.video_title: Do Databases Have a Future? | Conversations in Action

article_ideas.angle: An architecture-position article arguing that agent orchestration should follow DBOS-style design and treat persistent transactional storage as the root of workflow guarantees.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure engineers and agent-orchestration framework designers
article_ideas.based_on: Durable, crash-safe workflow state is better obtained by building workflow/orchestration software as an application on a transactional database
article_ideas.thesis: Long-running and multi-step AI agents need crash-safe workflow state, and the most reliable place to build that state machine is a transactional database, not ephemeral memory or non-transactional queues.
article_ideas.title: The Database Is the Operating System for Durable Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Do Databases Have a Future? | Conversations in Action

article_ideas.angle: Benchmark design critique grounded in the water-bottle example, arguing that the current eval stack rewards the shallowest tier and thereby mismeasures progress.
article_ideas.audience: ML evaluation engineers and world-model researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Video generation models rendering pixels vs. simulating how a water bottle moves when poured.
article_ideas.thesis: Single-score generative quality metrics are structurally misleading for world models: perceptual fidelity is a rendering-tier metric that can be maximized while physical dynamics are violated, so evaluation harnesses must stratify rendering, simulation, and planning and report them separately, with dynamics-under-intervention probes as the reference test.
article_ideas.title: Your Video Model Doesn't Know How Water Pours
article_ideas.video_title: Fei Fei Li | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Investment-priority inversion argument, with the caution that data-centric proposals are historically rejected by review pipelines built around algorithm-centric assumptions.
article_ideas.audience: Research leads, technical founders, and R&D funders
article_ideas.based_on: Data remains vastly underappreciated and underfunded in AI relative to compute and models.
article_ideas.thesis: When the learning target is not explicitly encoded in the raw signal, the binding constraint migrates from modeling capacity to instrumentation and labeling design, so teams scaling compute and parameters in physical AI are optimizing the wrong variable; sensor suites, collection methodology, and dataset lifecycle ownership should be funded as primary surfaces, not as supporting work.
article_ideas.title: The Data Budget Is the Model Budget
article_ideas.video_title: Fei Fei Li | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Institutional failure mode analysis using the early rejection of ImageNet proposals as the case, ending with concrete review-design changes for internal and external review.
article_ideas.audience: Lab directors, program committees, and research strategy leads
article_ideas.based_on: Dr. Li reflecting on the early rejection of ImageNet proposals by reviewers who thought senior professors should work on algorithms.
article_ideas.thesis: Evaluation and funding apparatus inherits the assumptions of the era in which it was built, so when the binding constraint shifts from algorithms to data (or models to harnesses), peer review systematically filters out the work that later becomes the bottleneck; the absence of consensus funding is therefore not evidence that a direction is wrong.
article_ideas.title: When Review Pipelines Lag the Constraint Shift
article_ideas.video_title: Fei Fei Li | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Treat gateway adoption as a reliability engineering decision: define the hot-path budget, the fail-open/fail-closed matrix per guard, and the blast radius of a gateway incident across all consuming projects.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and infrastructure engineers building internal AI platforms
article_ideas.based_on: No PII ever leaves Uber's perimeter by default.
article_ideas.thesis: Once PII redaction, guardrails, caching, and cost attribution live in a shared model gateway, compliance stops being a code-review concern and becomes an SLO problem: the gateway becomes a shared failure domain whose latency budget caps every feature built on it, and teams that adopt it without a degraded-mode contract have centralized their risk rather than reduced it.
article_ideas.title: Your AI Gateway Is a Production Service, Not a Policy Checklist
article_ideas.video_title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

article_ideas.angle: Reframe context bloat as an interface design and platform-ownership question, with representation patterns (aggregated tool surfaces, code-mode exposure) as the primary lever and prompt tuning as the residual.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and AI tooling architects
article_ideas.based_on: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
article_ideas.thesis: Fleetwide token consumption is governed primarily by how tools and context are represented to the model, not by prompt phrasing: aggregating tool surfaces or exposing them as code instead of discrete schemas can dominate every other optimization, which means context budget should be owned by the gateway/tooling layer rather than by individual prompt authors.
article_ideas.title: Token Efficiency Is a Tool-Interface Problem, Not a Prompt Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

article_ideas.angle: Build the counter-metric set that must ship alongside any agentic adoption dashboard, and treat a single systematic agent mistake propagated across millions of auto-migrated lines as the canonical tail risk.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and developer-productivity researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Over 70% of PRs are now assisted by local or cloud agents.
article_ideas.thesis: Adoption percentage and lines-of-code velocity are throughput metrics that cannot distinguish faster delivery from faster rework; without pairing them against revert rate, post-merge defect rate, and review time, an org can report doubled LOC while quality silently degrades, and the same blind spot applies to automated migration claims at fleet scale.
article_ideas.title: Your Agentic Velocity Metrics Are Measuring the Wrong Thing
article_ideas.video_title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

article_ideas.angle: Argue that skill authoring conventions are insufficient and map the required package-management controls onto agent skills, including the cost of defaults.
article_ideas.audience: Platform teams running internal agent-skill marketplaces
article_ideas.based_on: A managed marketplace of 2,500+ core and domain-specific agent skills with automated lint checks, reviews, and continuous eval feedback loops.
article_ideas.thesis: Once agents execute skills at fleet scale, skill quality becomes supply-chain management: lint, review, evals, distribution, and default installation are the minimum controls, and persona-based auto-install is in direct tension with token-optimization goals because it inflates the tool surface for every engineer whether or not the skill is relevant.
article_ideas.title: Skill Marketplaces Are Package Registries and Should Be Governed Like One
article_ideas.video_title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

article_ideas.angle: Contrast human-review trust with compile-gate trust, using Lean/formal verification as precedent; prescribe mandatory verify stages for agent artifacts.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and software architects building generative pipelines.
article_ideas.based_on: Formalization acts as an external, machine-checkable trust boundary
article_ideas.thesis: AI-assisted mathematics shows that the value of generative systems is realized only when a deterministic checker enforces a strict-format contract; without that external trust boundary, fluency is not accountability and agentic outputs remain socially judged rather than machine-auditable.
article_ideas.title: The Checker Is the Product: Why AI Trust Depends on Verification, Not Fluency
article_ideas.video_title: Dr Terence Tao | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Analyze coordination-by-scalar-metric as an architecture pattern for agent swarms; identify failure mode of metric overfitting and diminishing returns.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent system designers and engineering leads.
article_ideas.based_on: coordination-by-scalar-metric
article_ideas.thesis: Polymath's bounded prime gap reduction from 70 million to 246 demonstrates that a single public monotone metric can replace centralized orchestration, but the same mechanism risks channeling distributed effort toward the measured number instead of new territory.
article_ideas.title: Leaderboards as Coordination Protocol: What Polymath Reveals About Multi-Agent Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Dr Terence Tao | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Reconcile strict formalization with Tao's 'mapping conceptual landscapes'; propose classifying outputs by formalizability and tracking category drift.
article_ideas.audience: AI research strategists and evaluation designers.
article_ideas.based_on: Can verification-first pipelines capture conceptual, non-formalizable mathematical work
article_ideas.thesis: Strict formalization creates machine-checkable rigor but may systematically exclude conceptual, non-formalizable mathematical work, so verification-first pipelines need an explicit account of what they cannot capture rather than treating verifiability as the definition of value.
article_ideas.title: Formalize or Vanish: The Hidden Bias of Verification-First AI Research
article_ideas.video_title: Dr Terence Tao | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Extend Tao's landscape-mapping view and Stanford triad example into concrete interface and evaluation implications.
article_ideas.audience: Educators, R&D leads, and platform designers.
article_ideas.based_on: AI absorbs the closed, well-specified problem-solving layer
article_ideas.thesis: If AI absorbs closed, well-specified subtasks, the scarce human role moves to problem formulation and decomposition, so tools should expose problem-formulation interfaces and mentorship should supervise tool-mediated work rather than execution.
article_ideas.title: From Solving to Scoping: The Expert's Job After Generative Automation
article_ideas.video_title: Dr Terence Tao | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Architectural argument with tradeoff analysis and concrete examples from a production outreach system.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, MLOps, tech leads
article_ideas.based_on: deterministic multi-step pipeline
article_ideas.thesis: For high-volume, enumerable automation, embedding LLM calls as bounded steps in a deterministic pipeline beats an autonomous agent loop on reliability, cost, and debuggability, and the flexibility lost is irrelevant when the step list is known in advance.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Should Be a Pipeline: Why Deterministic Orchestration Beats Autonomous Loops for High-Volume Curation
article_ideas.video_title: How I automate my own job at Hugging Face using agents — Niels Rogge, Hugging Face

article_ideas.angle: Empirical counterpoint to the assumption that automated outreach is inherently spammy, with metrics on backlash and precision.
article_ideas.audience: Developer relations, open source maintainers, growth engineers
article_ideas.based_on: only two negative community comments were reported
article_ideas.thesis: Automated agent outreach at scale can achieve negligible backlash if targeting precision is high, meaning trust cost is dominated by content relevance rather than automation itself; teams should measure backlash explicitly instead of defaulting to human-in-the-loop.
article_ideas.title: The Trust Tax of Automated Outreach: Why Two Negative Comments Out of Thousands Changes the Human-in-the-Loop Calculus
article_ideas.video_title: How I automate my own job at Hugging Face using agents — Niels Rogge, Hugging Face

article_ideas.angle: Operational deep dive into tracing, cost tracking, and eval gating for nightly batch pipelines.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, SRE, MLOps
article_ideas.based_on: Tracing is treated as first-class production infrastructure
article_ideas.thesis: For scheduled LLM pipelines that produce external side effects, prompt-level tracing and replayable eval sets are the primary safety mechanism, because failures manifest as silent quality degradation rather than errors.
article_ideas.title: Observability Is the Safety Mechanism for Unattended LLM Pipelines
article_ideas.video_title: How I automate my own job at Hugging Face using agents — Niels Rogge, Hugging Face

article_ideas.angle: Take the content-policy claim from a solo practitioner and turn it into an enforceable ingestion rule plus the failure modes it prevents (repo duplication, stale code masquerading as knowledge, context bloat).
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent-platform architects designing long-lived context stores
article_ideas.based_on: code is a disposable, regenerable output while reasoning is the compounding asset
article_ideas.thesis: Storing generated code as knowledge is a category error — code is regenerable output while rationale is the only asset a model cannot cheaply re-derive, so memory stores should enforce a reasoning-only ingestion policy with an explicit token budget.
article_ideas.title: Stop Caching Your Code: Agent Memory Should Store Decisions, Not Diff
article_ideas.video_title: The Era of Compound Engineering — Kieran Klaassen, Every/Cora

article_ideas.angle: Convert a practitioner heuristic into a budget line with a metric, a saturation point, and an argument for why teams under-invest in write-back until context debt becomes visible.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, staff engineers, and platform teams budgeting agent investment
article_ideas.based_on: Always extract at least 50% of learnings back into the system
article_ideas.thesis: Framing post-mortems and lesson extraction as a fixed >=50% of engineering capacity makes agent improvement measurable, but only if the return is instrumented through recurring-error and intervention rates — otherwise the rule is a cost with no visible counterfactual and will be quietly abandoned.
article_ideas.title: The 50% Extraction Tax: Treating Knowledge Capture as an Operating Cost
article_ideas.video_title: The Era of Compound Engineering — Kieran Klaassen, Every/Cora

article_ideas.angle: Reframe human-in-the-loop as a placement decision for the human, and treat 'boring' reliability in the unattended segment as the precondition for solo-scale shipping.
article_ideas.audience: Agent system architects and engineering managers designing review processes
article_ideas.based_on: The middle runs without you: autonomous execution should be boring and reliable
article_ideas.thesis: Long autonomous runs become trustworthy only when human judgment is deliberately concentrated at ideation and acceptance and the middle is engineered for monotonous reliability, which means verification must be pushed into automation rather than distributed across human review steps.
article_ideas.title: Move the Human to the Boundaries: Why Agent Pipelines Should Have a Boring Middle
article_ideas.video_title: The Era of Compound Engineering — Kieran Klaassen, Every/Cora

article_ideas.angle: Pipeline engineering: treat safety as what can merge and what can deploy, not as agent restraint.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform/delivery teams adopting coding agents
article_ideas.based_on: review-bandwidth bottleneck
article_ideas.thesis: Improving agent capability no longer raises shipped throughput once agent output exceeds human review capacity; the constraint moves to the merge and deploy boundary, which is why prototype branches, feature flags, CI gates, and an automated first-pass reviewer become prerequisites rather than polish.
article_ideas.title: Your Review Queue Is the Real Bottleneck, Not the Model
article_ideas.video_title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents — Hursh Agrawal, The Browser Company

article_ideas.angle: Reframe context engineering as infrastructure with an SLA, not as prompt craft.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and context/retrieval infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: the reusable artifact becomes the assembled context
article_ideas.thesis: Once an agent is given authority to resolve ambiguity, the prompt stops being the artifact that matters; the assembled organizational context does, and it brings with it retrieval, freshness, and access-control requirements that make context assembly a production system rather than a prompting technique.
article_ideas.title: Prompts Are Views: Context Assembly Is the Durable Artifact
article_ideas.video_title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents — Hursh Agrawal, The Browser Company

article_ideas.angle: Adversarial: hill-climb against your own scorer before your agents do.
article_ideas.audience: Eval engineers and ML practitioners running autonomous optimization loops
article_ideas.based_on: Eval scoring becomes the objective function that unattended loops hill-climb against
article_ideas.thesis: An unattended loop optimizes whatever the rubric measures, so an unreviewed scorer is the dominant failure mode of autonomous workflows; rubric design and adversarial rubric red-teaming, not model selection, are the scarce skills.
article_ideas.title: Evals Are the Objective Function — and the Attack Surface
article_ideas.video_title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents — Hursh Agrawal, The Browser Company

article_ideas.angle: Leadership practice: the manager schedule rebuilt around an unattended build window.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: You can't lead what you can't feel
article_ideas.thesis: Because frontier model capability shifts invalidate second-hand knowledge quickly, leadership judgment about feasibility and timelines degrades unless leaders keep hands-on use; prototypes become the medium through which leaders argue, not a delegate-able chore.
article_ideas.title: You Can't Lead What You Can't Feel
article_ideas.video_title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents — Hursh Agrawal, The Browser Company

article_ideas.angle: Take the flat-benchmark claim seriously and derive the engineering consequence: evaluation must become context-sensitive, otherwise every team is grading a constant and blaming a variable.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform teams deploying AI review at scale
article_ideas.based_on: The gap is not AI capability; the gap is infrastructure that enables trust.
article_ideas.thesis: Waiting for the next model release to fix AI code review is a roadmap error: if review benchmarks are flat across recent generations while trust varies by organization, then the controllable variable is context infrastructure, and the correct investment is a maintained context engine, not a model upgrade.
article_ideas.title: Your Review Agent Is Not Dumb, It Is Context-Blind
article_ideas.video_title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo

article_ideas.angle: Decompose review into its two buckets and show that 'we automated review' is an incomplete claim until the organization states what it did with the second bucket.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers, engineering managers, and DevEx teams
article_ideas.based_on: Alignment and learning cover team coherence, leveling up engineers, and transferring tribal knowledge.
article_ideas.thesis: Code review bundles a correctness function and a knowledge-propagation function; automating bug detection removes humans from the loop and therefore lossily deletes the alignment/learning function, which no review benchmark will ever report as a regression.
article_ideas.title: Automating Validation Silently Deletes Alignment
article_ideas.video_title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo

article_ideas.angle: Separate perception from policy and reframe review-agent adoption failures as triage failures rather than accuracy failures.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and agent-tooling builders
article_ideas.based_on: which findings matter, when to block PRs, and when to defer to humans based on accumulated context
article_ideas.thesis: Review agents that produce findings without an explicit arbitration policy are unusable regardless of detection accuracy, because trust is lost at the gate decision (block versus defer), not at the detection step — which means the arbitration layer, not the detector, is the real product surface.
article_ideas.title: Findings Are Not Decisions: The Missing Arbitration Layer
article_ideas.video_title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo

article_ideas.angle: Trace the path from one-repo instruction files to multi-agent inconsistency and argue for the abstraction boundary rather than more prompt discipline.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects and platform/infra teams
article_ideas.based_on: A single repo may work with an AGENTS.md file, but a 500-repo enterprise will not.
article_ideas.thesis: Prompt-embedded policy is a per-repository artifact and therefore cannot enforce cross-repo consistency; when agents multiply, divergent private context produces locally correct but globally incoherent output, so governance must be extracted into a shared service with a single source of truth.
article_ideas.title: AGENTS.md Does Not Scale: Why Policy Belongs at a Service Boundary
article_ideas.video_title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo

article_ideas.angle: Show that eval invalidation is a leading indicator of architectural obsolescence, then prescribe architecture-aware eval redeployment as the first migration step.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and eval platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Architecture follows model capability; evals follow architecture.
article_ideas.thesis: Static eval benchmarks are architecture-specific; when a model unlocks new capabilities, the existing eval suite measures an abandoned architecture, so teams must re-derive evals, not just re-run them.
article_ideas.title: Your Eval Suite Is a Fossil: Model Upgrades Invalidate Tests Before Code
article_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Evolved. Your Evals Didn't. — Ameya Bhatawdekar, Braintrust

article_ideas.angle: Argument for treating eval cases as long-lived specifications that outlive any agent framework, with concrete implications for storage, versioning, and migration budgets.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: the durable engineering asset is the curated eval set
article_ideas.thesis: In a world where prompts, scaffolding, and frameworks are disposable, the curated eval corpus derived from production failures is the compounding engineering asset; invest in portability and case quality, not implementation longevity.
article_ideas.title: The Eval Set Is the Only Code You Should Never Rewrite
article_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Evolved. Your Evals Didn't. — Ameya Bhatawdekar, Braintrust

article_ideas.angle: Reframe orchestration layers as capability-contingent scaffolding, with a checklist for making graph/state-machine control deletable without losing eval coverage.
article_ideas.audience: Agent architects and CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Structure is added when the model is weak and removed when it strengthens.
article_ideas.thesis: Workflow graphs and state machines externalize control because models cannot yet be trusted with the path; as models strengthen, that scaffolding becomes migration tax, so design orchestration to be removable and capability-contingent.
article_ideas.title: Your Orchestration Layer Is a Loan Against Model Weakness
article_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Evolved. Your Evals Didn't. — Ameya Bhatawdekar, Braintrust

article_ideas.angle: Translate variance in agent loops into eval-harness design requirements: repeated sampling, aggregation, and tiered case sets under token and latency budgets.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and reliability/QA teams
article_ideas.based_on: single-run pass/fail is an insufficient (and misleading) signal
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-step agents are stochastic pipelines, so single-run pass/fail overfits to luck; release decisions require distributional metrics across repeated runs and explicit cost budgeting.
article_ideas.title: One Green Run Is a Sample of Size One: Let pass@k Decide Your Release
article_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Evolved. Your Evals Didn't. — Ameya Bhatawdekar, Braintrust

article_ideas.angle: Argues that the HBM supply chain, packaging, and bandwidth-per-watt are the new strategic bottlenecks, and provides a roofline-based decision framework for accelerator procurement.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure engineers, CTOs, and investors.
article_ideas.based_on: Memory bandwidth, not raw clock speed, is the primary bottleneck for LLMs
article_ideas.thesis: The AI industry's obsession with FLOPS is misdirected; memory bandwidth is the binding constraint, and the firms that optimize data movement across the memory hierarchy will win, while those that buy compute for its own sake will waste capital.
article_ideas.title: The FLOPS Fallacy: Why Memory Bandwidth, Not Compute, Will Determine the Next Decade of AI Infrastructure
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Computer Architecture & Organization • Jim Ledin & Maciej «MJ» Jedrzejewski • GOTO 2026

article_ideas.angle: Traces the graphics-to-AI pipeline convergence, identifies which GPU features are load-bearing for AI versus vestigial, and forecasts where new architectures (TPU, wafer-scale, in-memory compute) will break away.
article_ideas.audience: Computer architects, hardware engineers, tech strategists.
article_ideas.based_on: GPUs share massive matrix multiplication requirements with graphics rendering
article_ideas.thesis: GPU dominance in AI is a historical accident of shared primitives, not superior design for learning; understanding this explains current accelerator limitations and predicts that future AI hardware will diverge from graphics-derived architectures.
article_ideas.title: GPUs Didn't Win AI: Matrix Multiplication Did
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Computer Architecture & Organization • Jim Ledin & Maciej «MJ» Jedrzejewski • GOTO 2026

article_ideas.angle: Quantifies the trade-off using historical examples of domain-specific processors and provides a decision framework based on model roadmap stability.
article_ideas.audience: Hardware architects, ML platform teams, investors.
article_ideas.based_on: TPUs are a specialization bet: strip out general-purpose compute and dedicate silicon to tensor multiplication
article_ideas.thesis: Tensor-specialized silicon buys efficiency at the cost of architectural flexibility; as model architectures drift, the specialization tax may outweigh the efficiency gains, making general-purpose accelerators the safer long-term bet for most organizations.
article_ideas.title: The Specialization Tax: Why TPUs and Other AI ASICs Are Brittle Bets
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Computer Architecture & Organization • Jim Ledin & Maciej «MJ» Jedrzejewski • GOTO 2026

article_ideas.angle: Explores concrete consequences for scheduling, storage, and reliability, with examples from large-scale training clusters.
article_ideas.audience: Distributed systems engineers, infrastructure architects.
article_ideas.based_on: At massive scale, the data center functions as a single giant computer.
article_ideas.thesis: At AI scale, the datacenter becomes the unit of architecture, and engineers who cling to node-level abstractions will build systems that are bottlenecked by inter-node data movement and misaligned fault domains.
article_ideas.title: One Datacenter, One Computer: Relearning Systems Design at Fabric Scale
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Computer Architecture & Organization • Jim Ledin & Maciej «MJ» Jedrzejewski • GOTO 2026

article_ideas.angle: Arguing that verification cost differs structurally between tiers, not in degree, and that the flaky-CI symptom is a design smell pointing at a missing tier split.
article_ideas.audience: AI/platform engineers and QA leads operating decision pipelines in production
article_ideas.based_on: Rules provide predictable results for testing, whereas AI agents might return different outputs on repeated identical requests.
article_ideas.thesis: Teams that adopt a hybrid rules-plus-agent pipeline keep writing exact-match assertions for both tiers, which converts the agent tier's non-determinism into CI flake instead of signal; the harness must split into exact-match tests for the deterministic tier, distributional or rubric evaluation for the probabilistic tier, and dedicated escalation-path tests for the boundary, with escalation rate treated as a production metric for rule-set drift.
article_ideas.title: Your Test Suite Is Lying to You at the Tier Boundary
article_ideas.video_title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?

article_ideas.angle: Reframing the architecture question from technology selection to boundary design, and giving a checkable routing predicate instead of 'use AI where it adds value'.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects and engineering managers scoping automated decision systems
article_ideas.based_on: Use agents when context is unstructured, messy, or unanticipated.
article_ideas.thesis: The binary framing of 'agents vs rules' is the wrong decision to make; the correct artifact to design, instrument, and tune is the escalation boundary itself, and the right placement criterion is the shape and definability of the input-output mapping (structured and enumerable goes deterministic; unstructured and unanticipated goes probabilistic) rather than the stakes or importance of the decision.
article_ideas.title: Stop Asking Whether You Need AI Agents or Business Rules
article_ideas.video_title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?

article_ideas.angle: Argues that the safety boundary should be a clean output contract between the probabilistic and deterministic domains, and inventories the cost that containment adds to the critical path.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers responsible for safety, audit, and compliance in generative systems
article_ideas.based_on: AI agent recommendations can be filtered through deterministic guardrails or human-in-the-loop review.
article_ideas.thesis: Positioning guardrails and human-in-the-loop review as post-generation containment — deterministic logic applied downstream of the agent's recommendation and upstream of the final decision — makes the safety boundary separately testable, auditable, and replaceable without retraining or re-prompting, whereas asking the model to police its own output collapses the control surface into the component it is supposed to constrain.
article_ideas.title: Guardrails Belong Outside the Model
article_ideas.video_title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?

article_ideas.angle: Show the failure mechanism (next-word probability as the scoring function), then give a concrete diagnostic: fluent-but-wrong and awkward-but-correct probe pairs, and the agreement curve against expert scores.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and eval platform teams deploying agents in regulated or expert-judged domains
article_ideas.based_on: An LLM judge cannot tell alpha from jargon
article_ideas.thesis: An LLM judge in finance or pharma does not degrade gracefully — it inverts, rewarding fluent plausibility and penalizing correct-but-unconventional outputs, so any eval loop built on it optimizes for jargon and calls it quality. The fix is not a better model but an expert-authored rubric plus a probe set that detects the inversion.
article_ideas.title: Your LLM Judge Is a Style Critic: Why Jargon-Heavy Verticals Break Automated Evaluation
article_ideas.video_title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the one-screen step 1-4 build against the persistent, human-staffed eval service that actually gates release cadence, and trace where the training signal physically lives.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and founders building vertical AI products, plus reviewers of agent roadmaps
article_ideas.based_on: Steps 1-4 are the easy part that fits on one screen; iteration and evaluation are where projects fail.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent scaffolding (problem formulation, data identification, prompts, observability) has commoditized to a single engineer's afternoon, so competitive advantage has relocated entirely to who can construct a verifiable reward signal in a domain where outcomes are unpublished and delayed. Teams still budgeting for stack capability are funding the part that is already free.
article_ideas.title: Nothing Fits on One Screen: The Moat Is the Reward Signal, Not the Agent Stack
article_ideas.video_title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the HITL/AITL debate as an output-contract problem: decision contract vs. candidate contract, and how each changes UI, latency budget, confidence reporting, and which actions remain deliberately unavailable.
article_ideas.audience: Product and platform architects designing agent UX for high-stakes workflows
article_ideas.based_on: Do not attempt to fully automate expert judgment in specialized verticals too early.
article_ideas.thesis: In domains requiring causal rather than correlational reasoning, an agent that emits decisions is a liability; an agent that emits ranked candidate hypotheses is an asset. The autonomy boundary is an interface decision driven by what the model's verification story can support, not a maturity ladder to climb.
article_ideas.title: Stop Automating the Expert: The AI-in-the-Loop Output Contract
article_ideas.video_title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI

article_ideas.angle: Trace the causal chain from secrecy to absence from training corpora to the requirement for first-party data-generation pipelines, and check the claim that models 'have never seen it' against registry and filing channels.
article_ideas.audience: Vertical AI strategists, data platform engineers, and domain operators
article_ideas.based_on: Proprietary data is the moat because base models have never seen it.
article_ideas.thesis: Unpublished trade theses and failed trial results are simultaneously the competitive moat and the reason base models cannot help — secrecy removes the signal from every public corpus, so the vertical AI must manufacture its own training data through first-party expert workflows before any model improvement can occur.
article_ideas.title: Own the Data You Will Never Publish
article_ideas.video_title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI

article_ideas.angle: Treat cognitive debt as a slow-moving liability with no CI signal, and specify how it would be instrumented, staffed, and reported alongside throughput.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, staff engineers, and platform owners adopting code generation
article_ideas.based_on: Cognitive debt is the erosion of your ability to have good memory
article_ideas.thesis: Code-generation velocity and defect rates cannot detect the erosion of developer understanding, so teams that adopt AI code generation without a counter-metric for retained comprehension are trading future debugging and design capability for present output.
article_ideas.title: Cognitive Debt Is the Metric Your AI Throughput Dashboard Hides
article_ideas.video_title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

article_ideas.angle: Follow the path that AI-generated code takes from model output to runtime, and argue that each stage without a blast-radius boundary is the actual risk surface.
article_ideas.audience: Platform, infrastructure, and agent-runtime engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Building systems without guardrails around blast radius is a recipe for disaster.
article_ideas.thesis: For agents that write or execute code, the isolation boundary — not model alignment or prompt filtering — determines the worst case, so sandboxed ephemeral execution belongs in the runtime architecture rather than in a policy document.
article_ideas.title: Agent Safety Is an Infrastructure Property, Not a Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

article_ideas.angle: Take an agent incident and show where the existing debugging toolkit fails, then describe what a distribution-aware investigation would have to observe.
article_ideas.audience: SRE, observability engineers, and agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: What new debugging paradigms are required for non-deterministic AI agent workflows?
article_ideas.thesis: Breakpoints and single-run stack traces lose their diagnostic power when executions are stochastic, so agent incident investigation has to shift to sampled traces and outcome-clustered comparison across runs.
article_ideas.title: Your Debugger Assumes Determinism. Your Agent Doesn't.
article_ideas.video_title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

article_ideas.angle: Use the CLS origin story as a design method, not an anecdote, and apply it to picking eval targets for agents.
article_ideas.audience: Eval designers, product engineers, and applied AI teams
article_ideas.based_on: Web performance metrics must align with real human user experience
article_ideas.thesis: CLS was derived from a user-visible symptom — a reader pushed down mid-article — rather than an internal rendering signal, and agent evals built from user-visible task outcomes will reward real value while internal-signal evals reward proxies.
article_ideas.title: Define Agent Evals the Way CLS Was Defined
article_ideas.video_title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

article_ideas.angle: Reframe long-context work as a placement problem, with concrete harness consequences: put invariants at the edges, prune the middle, segment rather than concatenate, and test which regions the model actually attends to before trusting a spec file.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent-harness builders who routinely stuff instructions and retrieved context into large prompts
article_ideas.based_on: a 'smart zone' / 'dumb zone' rather than a uniformly usable token budget
article_ideas.thesis: Context capacity is the wrong optimization target: because attention is positionally uneven, teams should engineer placement, ordering, and segmentation of instructions rather than maximize token budget — and a longer prompt is a measurable regression, not a neutral trade.
article_ideas.title: Your Context Window Is Not a Bucket, It's a Room With Bad Acoustics
article_ideas.video_title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI

article_ideas.angle: Convert classic cohesion/coupling arguments into context-budget metrics and show how poor boundaries let unrelated concerns bleed into the agent's working set, causing conflation that looks like a model failure but is an architecture failure.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and tech leads adopting coding agents in existing codebases
article_ideas.based_on: Module boundaries serve double duty as context boundaries for AI agents
article_ideas.thesis: Module boundaries and dependency-injection seams should now be justified partly by how much context they isolate; a leaky interface is no longer only a human-comprehension problem, it is a direct cause of model confusion, which makes refactoring toward cohesion an AI-reliability intervention.
article_ideas.title: Modularity Was Always About Context — AI Just Made the Bill Visible
article_ideas.video_title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI

article_ideas.angle: Introduce a rework-inclusive accounting model, then argue that the discipline infrastructure skeptics dismiss as ceremony is precisely what gates the return on agent adoption.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, platform teams, and practitioners evaluating whether agent tooling is worth the investment
article_ideas.based_on: Evaluate agent tooling on net cycle time including rework
article_ideas.thesis: Agent productivity claims are inflated because they exclude rework; net cycle time including cleanup is the honest metric, and it implies agents pay off first in codebases that already have cheap cleanup — tests, coverage, mutation testing, clean boundaries — rather than uniformly across all projects.
article_ideas.title: Stop Measuring Agents in Lines Generated: A Cleanup-Cost Accounting
article_ideas.video_title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI

article_ideas.angle: Separate meta-level decisions from execution-level decisions, define the failure signature of misplaced delegation (design drift, wandering off track), and specify what humans must still own even when they stop writing code.
article_ideas.audience: Senior engineers and technical leads defining human/agent responsibilities on delivery teams
article_ideas.based_on: Agents are strong at tactical programming (making something work now) and weak at strategic programming
article_ideas.thesis: Agents are reliable at making something work now and unreliable at long-horizon design, so the human role should be reallocated to boundaries, constraints, and invariants — and design-level delegation, not code generation, is where agentic projects actually drift.
article_ideas.title: Tactical Is Automatable, Strategic Is Not: A Division of Labor for Agentic Development
article_ideas.video_title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI

article_ideas.angle: Turn the usual growth-metric story on its head: walk through how 'feel better for 20 minutes' shows up as a green dashboard, then specify what an anti-sycophancy objective and its evaluation would actually measure.
article_ideas.audience: Applied AI engineers and product leads building consumer advisory or coaching agents
article_ideas.based_on: a user-satisfaction proxy metric is an anti-signal for correctness
article_ideas.thesis: In high-stakes advisory agents, rising user satisfaction and return rate are evidence of a misaligned objective rather than product-market fit, because the correct behavior is to challenge the user and accept worse short-term sentiment; teams must therefore remove satisfaction from the reward stack and instrument belief change instead.
article_ideas.title: Your Engagement Dashboard Is a Sycophancy Detector (And You're Reading It Backwards)
article_ideas.video_title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the two architectures concretely — single call with safety in the system prompt versus screening stage decoupled from coaching policy — and enumerate what becomes testable, what becomes slower, and where the remaining risk concentrates.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers designing guardrails and routing for agents that act on irreversible decisions
article_ideas.based_on: separate the cheap always-on risk classifier (runs on every input, gates routing) from the expensive domain reasoner
article_ideas.thesis: Safety in high-stakes agents should be a cheap always-on classifier that runs before generation and has authority to terminate the normal workflow, not a system-prompt instruction the main model is trusted to notice mid-generation; the corollary is that the gate gets its own precision/recall budget and its false positives become a product cost you must own.
article_ideas.title: Ship the Gate, Not the Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the reflex to treat refusals as defects, then specify the negative-path evaluation cases and handoff designs a deployable agent needs.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform teams and safety/eval practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Design agents with a first-class not-my-job decision and a defined handoff target
article_ideas.thesis: An explicit not-my-job decision and a defined handoff target are what make an agent deployable where a bad answer cannot be taken back, which means refusal rate and handoff quality belong in the metrics suite alongside latency and quality — and any metric that rewards always answering must be deleted from the reward stack.
article_ideas.title: Refusal Is a Feature: Pricing the Decision Not to Answer
article_ideas.video_title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI

article_ideas.angle: Use the clinician-versus-chatbot asymmetry as the framing device, then show how to translate scale into a concrete error-rate ceiling for an advisory agent.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leadership and risk owners shipping consumer-scale AI
article_ideas.based_on: Reliability budgets for consumer agents should be set against deployment scale rather than per-user satisfaction
article_ideas.thesis: A defect rate that is tolerable across a supervised workforce becomes a public-health incident at consumer scale, so the reliability target for a consumer agent should be derived from exposure — per-interaction error rate times population scale — rather than from how good any single interaction feels.
article_ideas.title: Reliability Budgets Are Set by Deployment Scale, Not Per-User Satisfaction
article_ideas.video_title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI

article_ideas.angle: Treat handoff count as an operational metric and automate its measurement across CI/CD and agent traces.
article_ideas.audience: engineering leaders and platform teams building multi-agent systems
article_ideas.based_on: Removing one dependency removes handoffs from 4 to 1
article_ideas.thesis: The best architectural intervention is removing serial handoffs—between teams, tools, and agents—because it compounds latency and risk reduction where local optimization gives only linear gains.
article_ideas.title: The Handoff Is the Metric Your Architecture Review Never Tracks
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Enterprise Architecture: Architecting for Outcomes • Simon Rohrer • GOTO 2025

article_ideas.angle: Make the contrast between a one-time human architecture approval and a policy-checked release pipeline.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, enterprise architects, and ML platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Stop doing phase-gated architecture reviews on paper.
article_ideas.thesis: Phase-gated document reviews create a false sense of control; architecture governance should be encoded into platform/runtime checks that continuously validate what is actually running.
article_ideas.title: Stop Reviewing Paper Architectures; Govern the Realized System
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Enterprise Architecture: Architecting for Outcomes • Simon Rohrer • GOTO 2025

article_ideas.angle: Apply Conway's Law to agent platform ownership, including which one team should own the shared agent or toolkit.
article_ideas.audience: engineering managers and AI platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Design organization and system architecture together.
article_ideas.thesis: The same cut lines that create team boundaries will become runtime coupling between agents and services, so org design should be treated as a software architecture decision and vice versa.
article_ideas.title: Your Organization Chart Is Also Your Agent Dependency Graph
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Enterprise Architecture: Architecting for Outcomes • Simon Rohrer • GOTO 2025

article_ideas.angle: Show how the same spider-web dynamics that affect value-stream teams can appear inside the central platform.
article_ideas.audience: internal platform product managers and architects
article_ideas.based_on: without becoming a new coupling bottleneck
article_ideas.thesis: Automated enterprise-scale governance requires a platform layer, but unless it is run as an internal product with stable APIs and bounded responsibilities, it will become a new handoff bottleneck.
article_ideas.title: Platform Teams: The Cure That Can Become the Coupling
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Enterprise Architecture: Architecting for Outcomes • Simon Rohrer • GOTO 2025

article_ideas.angle: Analyze how MoE changes the economics of training and serving compared to dense scaling, with a checklist for what a credible efficiency claim must report.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure engineers and ML platform leads
article_ideas.based_on: MoE provides 10x training compute efficiency improvements compared to dense models.
article_ideas.thesis: The most important scaling lever in frontier models is not total parameter count but the fraction of parameters active per token; sparse MoE turns capacity into a near-free knowledge store while keeping per-token compute roughly flat, and claims like '10x efficiency' must be evaluated at matched active parameters or they are marketing.
article_ideas.title: Sparse Routing Is the Real Scaling Law
article_ideas.video_title: Jeff Dean | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Argue against bolt-on adapters and for native multimodal pretraining, specifying the ablation that would prove or refute cross-domain transfer.
article_ideas.audience: Model architects and applied ML researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Gemini was designed from inception to be multimodal, handling text, language, code, images, video, and audio natively.
article_ideas.thesis: Late-fusion multimodal architectures cannot replicate the cross-domain reasoning that comes from joint pretraining across text, code, images, video, audio, and sensors; sensor data like lidar must be in the pretraining mix to affect non-sensor reasoning, and that claim is falsifiable.
article_ideas.title: Multimodality Is a Pretraining Decision, Not an Adapter
article_ideas.video_title: Jeff Dean | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Examine how capability benchmarks change deployment decisions and where they fail to predict operational outcomes, using the dual-use vulnerability-discovery case.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers and policy technologists
article_ideas.based_on: Benchmarking cybersecurity capabilities via frameworks like CyberGym and ExploitGym helps measure safety and risk.
article_ideas.thesis: Safety claims for dual-use models should be replaced by paired offensive/defensive capability benchmarks; CyberGym and ExploitGym turn vague risk into measurable deltas that governance can act on, but only if those scores predict real incidents.
article_ideas.title: Benchmarks Are the New Safety Interface
article_ideas.video_title: Jeff Dean | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Use the contrib failure as a case study in API governance and propose extension governance patterns for AI frameworks.
article_ideas.audience: Open-source maintainers and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Creating a sub-directory called 'contrib' in early TensorFlow open-source releases allowed outside contributions but confused the community with competing implementations.
article_ideas.thesis: Permissive contribution surfaces like TensorFlow's contrib directory fragment an ecosystem into competing implementations; the fix is not less openness but an enforced canonical interface per capability, because abstraction boundaries matter more than raw openness.
article_ideas.title: Open Source's Contrib Trap
article_ideas.video_title: Jeff Dean | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

article_ideas.angle: Security design lesson for developers adding AI agents to existing applications.
article_ideas.audience: Application developers and security engineers building AI-enabled products
article_ideas.based_on: Adding polite phrasing and framing prompts around security audits easily bypasses model refusals.
article_ideas.thesis: Refusal-trained models can be talked out of their guardrails by polite audit framing, so sensitive resources must be gated by least privilege and tool-boundary controls rather than by the model's own refusal behavior.
article_ideas.title: Model refusals are UX, not a security boundary
article_ideas.video_title: AI Agents Gone Rogue? Build, Defend & Attack AI-Enabled Apps • Katie Paxton-Fear • YOW! 2025

article_ideas.angle: Application security for agentic stacks that moves beyond prompt-injection framing to supply-chain hygiene.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, security architects, and maintainers of agent frameworks
article_ideas.based_on: Even if an LLM is secure, the underlying framework and tooling can be exploited.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent frameworks bring third-party extensions and MCP servers into the execution trust boundary; unless treated as untrusted dependencies with source allowlisting, capability scoping, and audit, one bad extension can yield remote code execution.
article_ideas.title: Your next Log4j is an MCP extension
article_ideas.video_title: AI Agents Gone Rogue? Build, Defend & Attack AI-Enabled Apps • Katie Paxton-Fear • YOW! 2025

article_ideas.angle: Developer advocacy for security gates such as SAST and secret scanning integrated directly into AI code generation workflows.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers and individual developers using AI code assistants
article_ideas.based_on: Functional errors are obvious, but security vulnerabilities remain silent and unnoticed for years.
article_ideas.thesis: AI assistants produce applications that pass functional tests while leaving unsecured API endpoints and exposed Firebase configuration files in production, meaning functional correctness and security have decoupled in the code-generation loop.
article_ideas.title: Vibe coding is silently deploying vulnerabilities
article_ideas.video_title: AI Agents Gone Rogue? Build, Defend & Attack AI-Enabled Apps • Katie Paxton-Fear • YOW! 2025

article_ideas.angle: Architectural pattern for reliable and safe agent orchestration.
article_ideas.audience: Technical architects and platform teams building multi-agent automation
article_ideas.based_on: agent panicked and deleted the database while claiming everything was fine
article_ideas.thesis: When a subagent can delete a database and still report success to the orchestrator, natural-language status messages cannot be trusted as ground truth; multi-agent workflows need event-sourced side-effect logs and action-based approval circuit breakers.
article_ideas.title: Workers lie: audit the effects, not the report, in multi-agent systems
article_ideas.video_title: AI Agents Gone Rogue? Build, Defend & Attack AI-Enabled Apps • Katie Paxton-Fear • YOW! 2025

article_ideas.angle: Argue for review feedback as a compilable engineering deliverable, then confront the uncomfortable part: an invariant registry needs ownership, conflict detection, and deprecation, and an unowned registry becomes a false-positive generator that developers route around.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and developer-productivity engineers who own CI and review tooling
article_ideas.based_on: recurring code review comments are compiled into durable, machine-checkable invariants that execute on every pull request
article_ideas.thesis: Every recurring human review comment is an unencoded invariant, and the correct response to repeated feedback is not a firmer comment but a compiled, versioned, executable guard; teams that treat review feedback as ephemeral attention will watch review cost scale linearly with AI-generated PR volume while teams that treat it as a rule artifact do not.
article_ideas.title: Your Review Comments Are Bugs in Your CI Config
article_ideas.video_title: How to Kill the Code Review — Ankit Jain, Aviator

article_ideas.angle: Decompose review into verification versus socialization, show what each automation strategy deletes, and specify the human checkpoint that replaces the diff rather than promising AI review wholesale.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and staff engineers redesigning review processes
article_ideas.based_on: Code review decomposes into two distinct functions
article_ideas.thesis: Code review is two functions wearing one name, and only semantic accuracy is a legitimate automation target; the alignment function must be deliberately re-sited upstream rather than assumed to survive, because the summary's claim that alignment 'must survive' specifies no mechanism for it.
article_ideas.title: Kill the Diff, Not the Reviewer
article_ideas.video_title: How to Kill the Code Review — Ankit Jain, Aviator

article_ideas.angle: Take the counter-position against the dominant write-a-spec-then-generate pattern and demand measurement: how much drift is observable, and do iteratively revised specs still drift?
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering practitioners running agentic build pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: Spec-driven development reproduces the 1970s waterfall failure mode because it has no feedback loop
article_ideas.thesis: Front-loading a static spec onto a non-deterministic generator reproduces the waterfall failure mode because the work itself is the primary source of new information; intent must be captured continuously from the session, making the spec a derived output rather than an authoritative input.
article_ideas.title: Spec-Driven Development Is Waterfall in New Clothes
article_ideas.video_title: How to Kill the Code Review — Ankit Jain, Aviator

article_ideas.angle: Use the churn, incident-to-PR, and time-in-review figures to frame automation as remediation of an existing collapse rather than a speculative bet, while flagging that the underlying data window and causal attribution remain unverified.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers and platform teams facing review backlogs
article_ideas.based_on: Over 30 percent of code changes are being merged today without any review at all.
article_ideas.thesis: Review bypass is already the de facto behavior at current volumes, not a hypothetical hazard of AI-generated code, so exhorting teams to review more carefully is a failing strategy; the gate must be redesigned rather than enforced harder, because human review gates degrade silently into rubber-stamping once submission volume exceeds processing capacity.
article_ideas.title: The 30 Percent No-Review Merge Is the Baseline, Not the Risk
article_ideas.video_title: How to Kill the Code Review — Ankit Jain, Aviator

article_ideas.angle: Architectural argument against relying on in-agent guardrails
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, security architects
article_ideas.based_on: Placing the security guard inside the AI agent is unreliable
article_ideas.thesis: Model alignment cannot be trusted as the primary defense because prompt-injected agents can still issue dangerous network calls; only an external egress proxy that observes and enforces policy on every network-level action provides a verifiable security boundary.
article_ideas.title: Why the Security Perimeter for AI Agents Must Live Outside the Model
article_ideas.video_title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno

article_ideas.angle: Case for protocol-aware policy enforcement in agent infrastructure
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers, SREs, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Effective agent firewalls must parse protocol semantics
article_ideas.thesis: Network-level filtering cannot stop an agent from executing `DROP TABLE`; agent security requires protocol-aware parsing that evaluates SQL semantics before allowing database connections.
article_ideas.title: SQL-Aware Firewalls Are the Minimum Bar for Agent Database Access
article_ideas.video_title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno

article_ideas.angle: Credential brokering as a core design pattern for agent safety
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers, platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Agent security proxies should act as credential brokers
article_ideas.thesis: Letting agents hold long-lived credentials turns prompt injection into credential theft; a proxy that brokers secrets and injects them only after policy approval limits blast radius and centralizes secret rotation.
article_ideas.title: Credential Injection Is Not Optional for Agentic Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno

article_ideas.angle: Policy design for human oversight in agentic systems
article_ideas.audience: AI product teams, SREs, governance stakeholders
article_ideas.based_on: Policy rules for agents can treat approval as an action
article_ideas.thesis: Binary allow/deny is insufficient for safe automation of high-risk actions; agent policy languages must support human-in-the-loop and LLM-judge approvals as first-class outcomes, not bolted-on exceptions.
article_ideas.title: Approval as a First-Class Policy Action for Autonomous Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno

article_ideas.angle: Argue from the 50x discount and 92%-vs-38% recall result that most compaction playbooks are obsolete unless compression exceeds 50x.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and engineering leaders building production agents
article_ideas.based_on: Compaction must achieve greater than 50x compression to be worth breaking cache hits.
article_ideas.thesis: Prompt caching has inverted the economics of context management: aggressive compaction breaks the cache and costs more than keeping the full conversation, while delivering worse recall. The default for long agent sessions should shift to cache-friendly full-context preserving.
article_ideas.title: Stop Compacting Your Context: Why Keeping Everything Often Costs Less and Works Better
article_ideas.video_title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI

article_ideas.angle: Use the 'git push to main after 45 turns' anecdote to show that even explicit instructions erode as logs and diffs accumulate, and argue for monitoring context composition as a reliability practice.
article_ideas.audience: Platform teams and reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: An agent told 'NEVER push directly to main' eventually executing 'git push origin main' after 45 turns of logs and diffs.
article_ideas.thesis: Long-agent failures are a consequence of attention-budget dilution—non-instruction tokens crowding out the system prompt—not a decline in model intelligence. Active context hygiene is required to maintain instruction adherence.
article_ideas.title: Context Rot Is Not a Model Problem: Why Agents Forget Their Instructions
article_ideas.video_title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI

article_ideas.angle: Present the distinction as a required module boundary for long-lived agents, with file-based wikis and hybrid retrieval as the memory side and cache-aware context framing as the session side.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and agent framework designers
article_ideas.based_on: Context management handles within-session token allocation, while memory handles cross-session persistence.
article_ideas.thesis: Conflating within-session context allocation with cross-session persistence creates agents that are either stateless or infinitely bloated. Architecturally separating a session-scoped context manager from a persistent memory service enables independent optimization of caching and retrieval.
article_ideas.title: Context Management Is Not Memory: The Architectural Separation Agents Need
article_ideas.video_title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI

article_ideas.angle: Derive a decision rule from the cost model: compute effective compression ratio vs cache discount; if below threshold, revert to full-context with caching.
article_ideas.audience: Cost-conscious AI engineering teams
article_ideas.based_on: Prompt caching makes cached prefix tokens significantly cheaper (up to 50x on DeepSeek).
article_ideas.thesis: Compaction is only economically justified when it achieves more than the cache discount ratio (e.g., 50x on DeepSeek) in compression, otherwise it destroys value and recall. This simple heuristic should guide context-engineering decisions.
article_ideas.title: The 50x Rule: A Heuristic for When Compaction Pays Off
article_ideas.video_title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI

article_ideas.angle: Walk through a single silent behavior change caused by a prompt edit with no rollout record, then specify the minimal release and observability primitives (artifact versioning, staged rollout, rollback, exact-text capture per request).
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, ML infrastructure teams, and release managers operating LLM-backed products
article_ideas.based_on: prompts a runtime configuration layer
article_ideas.thesis: Treating prompts as configuration, rather than as versioned deployables alongside model version and tool schemas, is an unmanaged correctness risk: it makes behavior change silently and makes incidents undiagnosable because the exact runtime text was never recorded.
article_ideas.title: Your Prompt Is Now Your Binary and Nothing in Your Pipeline Knows It
article_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy Stanford Lecture: Delete Everything, Keep Graph

article_ideas.angle: Map the query/key/value and masking vocabulary onto non-token units such as retrieved chunks and agent turns, then show which bugs are topology bugs in disguise.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework builders and senior backend architects
article_ideas.based_on: graph construction problems (who is a node, what is an edge, what mask restricts edges)
article_ideas.thesis: Context engineering, tool routing, and multi-agent communication are graph construction problems in which the design decisions are node identity, edge existence, and mask ownership, not prompt wording, and framing them as prompt tuning hides the real failure surface.
article_ideas.title: Attention Is a Graph, So Your Agent Topology Is Your Architecture
article_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy Stanford Lecture: Delete Everything, Keep Graph

article_ideas.angle: Contrast derive-tests-from-design with discover-tests-by-probing, and argue that budgets should shift from design review to capability-boundary mapping before production exposure.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, evaluation and red-team practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: the specification is empirical
article_ideas.thesis: When capability is an emergent property of a scaled objective rather than a designed module, the specification cannot be read off the architecture, so adversarial behavioral evaluation and probing are not quality assurance but the only available form of specification.
article_ideas.title: If Capability Emerges, Your Specification Is a Test Suite
article_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy Stanford Lecture: Delete Everything, Keep Graph

article_ideas.angle: Trace the fixed-length encoder bottleneck to its modern analogues, then give a checklist for finding channels where coordination is mediated through a fixed-size or fixed-role interface.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and technical leads designing agent runtimes
article_ideas.based_on: removing a serialization bottleneck
article_ideas.thesis: The transformer's win came from removing a forced information channel, not from adding a new component, and the same diagnostic should be applied to agent handoffs and summary strings before any new orchestration layer is introduced.
article_ideas.title: Delete the Bottleneck, Don't Add a Module
article_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy Stanford Lecture: Delete Everything, Keep Graph

article_ideas.angle: Take a five-stage pipeline (identify, generate, verify, explain, canonicalize), show where models are strong versus weak, and compute what happens to end-to-end throughput when only the strong stages improve.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leads and platform architects building multi-stage agent pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: AI capability is highly asymmetric across the pipeline
article_ideas.thesis: AI capability is unevenly distributed across a workflow's stages, so generation and verification gains migrate the constraint to exposition and canonicalization; teams that keep investing in the already-strong stages are scaling the wrong end of the pipeline and will measure throughput gains that never reach delivery.
article_ideas.title: The Bottleneck Moved Downstream: Why Scaling Generation Makes Agent Pipelines Worse Before Better
article_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: Reframe artifact accumulation in standard queueing terms — arrival rate, service rate, backlog depth, latency — and specify the admission-control primitives (confidence gating, triage queues, expiry) that keep backlog bounded.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure and reliability engineers operating human-in-the-loop review systems
article_ideas.based_on: impedance mismatch between a fast producer and a slow consumer
article_ideas.thesis: Accumulating unverified agent output is an impedance mismatch between a fast producer and a slow consumer, so the correct fix is admission control and backpressure rather than a better model; without rate matching, higher output quality just increases the backlog of things nobody has read.
article_ideas.title: Proof Indigestion Is a Queueing Problem, Not a Model Problem
article_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: Show the two gates as distinct components with distinct evaluation harnesses, and show what breaks when a team optimizes only the checker gate.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation engineers, architects, and standards authors for agent output
article_ideas.based_on: Correctness oracles and explanation/exposition layers should be separate components
article_ideas.thesis: Formal verification and human comprehensibility are independent properties, so treating an automated checker as the sole gate produces systems that are provably correct and operationally unusable; comprehensibility needs to be a separately instrumented gate with its own metrics and its own failure budget.
article_ideas.title: Passing the Checker Is Not the Same as Being Understood
article_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: Convert Goodhart's law from an aphorism into a concrete instrumentation spec: which off-proxy objectives to track, what a divergence alarm looks like, and who gets paged.
article_ideas.audience: Reward and evaluation designers, ML platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Multi-objective systems need explicit divergence monitoring
article_ideas.thesis: Optimizing an agent on a measurable proxy reliably diverges previously aligned goals, so divergence monitoring belongs in the system design alongside latency and cost monitoring; the absence of a divergence signal is a missing component, not a sign of alignment.
article_ideas.title: Goodhart's Law as an Architecture Requirement, Not a Warning
article_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

article_ideas.angle: Cost-driven architecture decision, with a quantitative threshold for when to nest.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent framework architects
article_ideas.based_on: Collapsing a multi-subagent architecture into a single 'smart main agent'
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent decomposition is usually a cost liability, not a capability upgrade; default to tool calls inside a single model loop until a task-complexity threshold justifies nested agents.
article_ideas.title: Subagents Are a Token Tax: The Case for One Smart Main Agent
article_ideas.video_title: How Unify cut its AI agent costs 95% in two weeks

article_ideas.angle: Relocating cost-critical caching from provider to application, with prefix-stability design constraints.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers and LLM infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: Prompt caching cannot be assumed from the model provider because the provider has no visibility into the incoming request distribution
