article_ideas.thesis: Because model providers cannot know your request distribution, application-layer prefix hashing and routing is mandatory; cache hit rate must be instrumented as a production SLO or high-volume agent economics fail.
article_ideas.title: Your Prompt Cache Is an SLO, Not a Provider Feature
article_ideas.video_title: How Unify cut its AI agent costs 95% in two weeks

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation methodology critique, with a calibration procedure.
article_ideas.audience: ML evaluation engineers and applied AI researchers
article_ideas.based_on: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation has an inherent blind spot: the judge cannot share the exact distribution of the model under test (groupthink)
article_ideas.thesis: Automated judges have correlated bias and cannot stand in for direct inspection; eval budgets should fund stratified human review of real traces as the calibration ground truth.
article_ideas.title: Your LLM Judge Is Groupthinking: Why 100 Real Examples Beat 1,000 Automated Scores
article_ideas.video_title: How Unify cut its AI agent costs 95% in two weeks

article_ideas.angle: Architecture pattern for memory correctness and auditability.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and memory system designers
article_ideas.based_on: Memory is managed as a batch generative-then-discriminative pipeline over raw conversation and historical memory
article_ideas.thesis: Persistent agent memory should be maintained by a generative proposal / discriminative validation pipeline with lineage, because append-only memory accumulates contradictions that degrade long-running agents.
article_ideas.title: Memory Is a Batch Pipeline, Not an Append Log
article_ideas.video_title: How Unify cut its AI agent costs 95% in two weeks

article_ideas.angle: Technical strategy: argues that scaling model size and intelligence is insufficient and that architecture must shift to accumulating domain-specific expertise.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, technical leaders, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Modern society is not one world, but millions of micro-worlds.
article_ideas.thesis: AI agents fail outside coding because the real world is not one world but millions of micro-worlds with unique local physics, and no static model can compress them; the only path to reliable enterprise agents is continual learning on the job.
article_ideas.title: The Micro-World Problem: Why AGI Timelines Ignore the Real Cost of Expertise
article_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

article_ideas.angle: Conceptual architecture: reframes context engineering from a RAG add-on to an expertise function.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers, agent platform developers
article_ideas.based_on: intelligence is about hey, when we have the context, uh, how to solve the problem through the context? But expertise actually will bring you the right context
article_ideas.thesis: Intelligence and expertise are distinct capacities—reasoning over context vs. curating context—and treating context retrieval as an afterthought is why LLM agents are brittle and token-inefficient; we need context curation as a first-class subsystem.
article_ideas.title: Bringing the Right Context: The Missing Half of Intelligence
article_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

article_ideas.angle: Critical analysis: warns against over-generalizing coding agent success and outlines domain structuring requirements.
article_ideas.audience: engineering managers, AI startup founders
article_ideas.based_on: coding is the really the ideal market for these language agents, because code is already a language-native world
article_ideas.thesis: Coding succeeded because code is already language-native, symbolic, and structured with automated rewards, a privileged environment that does not generalize; enterprise deployment requires making domain feedback and structure first-class rather than assuming a uniform symbolic interface.
article_ideas.title: Coding Was an Anomaly: Why the First Mass Market Misleads AI Agent Strategy
article_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

article_ideas.angle: Translate the lesson of a mat-and-rope gym in Dagestan that produced dozens of champions into architectural guidance for modern agent systems.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and ML platform teams who build scaffolds, tools, and external memory for agents
article_ideas.based_on: When the training environment has almost no resources, capability gains are pushed into the agent's own internal strategies
article_ideas.thesis: Adding tools and scaffolds before an agent's policy has internalized core skill produces brittle, non-transferable systems; deliberate environment austerity is a design choice that exposes whether capability lives in the agent or in the platform.
article_ideas.title: The case for stripping scaffolding: why austere agent harnesses can beat tool-rich defaults
article_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

article_ideas.angle: Argue that benchmark infrastructure should be treated as a living training ecosystem rather than a fixed artifact, using the Dagestan training-camp analogy as the starting point.
article_ideas.audience: ML evaluation researchers and platform teams responsible for benchmarks
article_ideas.based_on: An individual's long-term capability is co-produced by a population of high-level training partners
article_ideas.thesis: Static datasets and hand-written test sets cap an agent's development at the level of the evaluator; high-performing systems require a rolling population of sparring agents that co-evolve with the target model.
article_ideas.title: Your benchmark is a fixed punching bag: co-evolving evaluation is the only way to raise the ceiling
article_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

article_ideas.angle: Frame red-team testing and chaos drills as the modern equivalent of sparring under stress, and make a case for embedding them into the regular agent lifecycle rather than as a one-off pre-launch gate.
article_ideas.audience: AI reliability engineers, ML Ops teams, and security practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Reliability under pressure is built by deliberately confronting near-catastrophic scenarios during training
article_ideas.thesis: Agents become reliable under rare, high-impact events only by repeatedly confronting escalating pressure in training, not by sanitizing those inputs out of the distribution.
article_ideas.title: Don't filter adversarial chaos—train inside it
article_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

article_ideas.angle: Connect observations about emotional intelligence and individualized fighter handling to concrete meta-control architecture for heterogeneous LLM subagents.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent system architects and orchestration developers
article_ideas.based_on: modeling the internal state of each worker
article_ideas.thesis: In a multi-agent workflow, the highest leverage lies in estimating each worker's internal state and adjusting prompts, budgets, and fallbacks per agent, exactly as an elite coach does for different fighters.
article_ideas.title: Orchestrator as corner coach: per-agent control beats one-size-fits-all system prompts
article_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the open-vs-closed debate as an operational capacity question and provide a subsystem checklist.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders, CTOs, and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: The closed stack is simpler (higher floor, lower ceiling) because you don't train models or manage raw data.
article_ideas.thesis: The decision to own weights is not about model quality but about which operational subsystems you can absorb; teams should decide by enumerating post-training, data pipelines, and harnesses they must run, not by benchmark scores.
article_ideas.title: The Ceiling/Floor Tradeoff: Why 'Open vs Closed' Is a Subsystem Ownership Question
article_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

article_ideas.angle: Use the cost curve as a planning tool and show how to abstract the model boundary.
article_ideas.audience: Founders, product managers, and finance-aware engineering leads
article_ideas.based_on: As AI products become successful, API cogs increase, making sovereign AI a must-have for margin optimization.
article_ideas.thesis: Rented inference costs scale with product success, so the own-vs-rent decision must be revisited as usage grows; architectural seams for model swapping should exist from day one.
article_ideas.title: Your API Bill Is a Margin Ceiling: The Economic Forcing Function for Sovereign AI
article_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

article_ideas.angle: Argue for treating the development stack as a production dependency with its own monitoring and ownership.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform engineers and engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: Development stack requires careful monitoring of evals, domain-specific data, and online learning feedback loops.
article_ideas.thesis: Owning weights without a closed-loop development stack yields static weights that decay in value; the eval-and-feedback loop is a first-class production subsystem, not an offline QA activity.
article_ideas.title: The Development Stack Is the Product: Why Evals and Online Learning Are Not QA
article_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

article_ideas.angle: Decompose agent performance into model quality and context quality, and provide instrumentation patterns.
article_ideas.audience: Agent builders and AI infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Context management (vector databases, turbo buffer, knowledge graphs, MCP) is critical for driving performance.
article_ideas.thesis: A large fraction of production performance comes from context assembly, not weights; teams should budget and instrument context as a separate optimization layer before spending on post-training.
article_ideas.title: Context Is the New Model: Where Agent Performance Actually Comes From
article_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

article_ideas.angle: Rebuild the cost model around agent-hours, duration, concurrency, and budget ceilings, and treat cost observability as a runtime requirement rather than finance reporting.
article_ideas.audience: Platform, infrastructure, and FinOps engineers running agentic workloads
article_ideas.based_on: 24/7 autonomous agent runs
article_ideas.thesis: Autonomous agents convert inference from an on-demand, human-hours-bounded cost into an always-on metered liability, so teams that keep per-request budgeting assumptions will ship agents whose cost curve, not their capability, becomes the limiting factor.
article_ideas.title: Your 24/7 Agents Are a Billing Model Change, Not a Feature
article_ideas.video_title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming

article_ideas.angle: Show how per-tool procurement structurally hides the integration work and why the abstraction boundary belongs at the platform layer, not the app layer.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, CTOs, and CIOs
article_ideas.based_on: AI is an operating system, not a traditional SaaS tool
article_ideas.thesis: Procuring AI per-seat optimizes isolated productivity while leaving the business-line restructuring untouched, so the correct unit of adoption is a shared queryable internal layer that budgets and ownership are attached to.
article_ideas.title: AI Is an Operating System, Not a SaaS Line Item
article_ideas.video_title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming

article_ideas.angle: Argue for mandatory hands-on agent building by decision-makers instead of more pilots, and trace the cascading effects of uninformed oversight.
article_ideas.audience: Executive leadership and transformation leads
article_ideas.based_on: The average C-suite has not built a single agent
article_ideas.thesis: Leaders who have never built or operated a single agent mis-scope budgets, metrics, and rollout, and the resulting employee fear and wasted capital is a downstream symptom of that inexperience rather than a culture problem to be trained away.
article_ideas.title: The C-Suite Agent Gap Is a Capital Allocation Failure, Not a Skills Gap
article_ideas.video_title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming

article_ideas.angle: Contrast email-tweak adoption with business-line cannibalization and identify the point at which productivity gains become a substitute for transformation.
article_ideas.audience: Product and operations leaders responsible for workflow redesign
article_ideas.based_on: Rewriting emails with AI is not meaningful AI adoption
article_ideas.thesis: Incremental productivity automation produces fast wins that actively delay the harder work of decoupling human daily execution from 2019-era workflows, leaving companies unable to compete with AI-native entrants.
article_ideas.title: Why Rewriting Emails Is Not AI Adoption
article_ideas.video_title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming

article_ideas.angle: Architecture / engineering strategy
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: wraps existing coding agents
article_ideas.thesis: The winning architecture for agent governance is a thin meta-harness that wraps existing coding agents, preserving developer tool choice while centralizing control, collaboration, and history — the same pattern that made service meshes successful.
article_ideas.title: Why You Don't Need to Build Another AI Agent Runtime
article_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

article_ideas.angle: Security / policy design
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers and AI platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Contextual security policies evaluate the full session history
article_ideas.thesis: Static security lists are fundamentally insufficient for agentic systems because a dangerous action only becomes dangerous in context; the future of agent security lies in stateful policies that evaluate the entire session history.
article_ideas.title: Context Is the New Allowlist: The End of Static Security for AI Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

article_ideas.angle: Operational / human-in-the-loop
article_ideas.audience: Ops teams building AI agent supervision
article_ideas.based_on: Risk scoring enables exception-based human oversight
article_ideas.thesis: Rather than blocking every risky action, continuous risk scoring with escalation thresholds is the pragmatic way to supervise autonomous agents — but it introduces a human-in-the-loop queue that must itself be engineered to avoid becoming a bottleneck.
article_ideas.title: The $10 Rule: How Risk Scoring Turns Agent Safety into Exception Handling
article_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

article_ideas.angle: Infrastructure / cloud evolution
article_ideas.audience: Cloud infrastructure engineers and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Sandboxing the entire agent session in a cloud VM
article_ideas.thesis: Sandboxing agent sessions in cloud VMs is the natural evolution of CI/CD runners, and organizations should treat long-running agent tasks as reproducible, credential-safe, cloud-hosted workloads rather than local foreground processes.
article_ideas.title: Close the Laptop: Agent Sessions Are the New Cloud-Native Workloads
article_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the reliability of probabilistic evaluation with deterministic acceptance gates and generalize from Lean proofs to everyday agent tooling.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform architects, and engineering leaders building agentic systems
article_ideas.based_on: machine-checkable reward/verification signal
article_ideas.thesis: The most important AI infrastructure trend is not bigger models but mechanical verifiers that turn generation into a search problem with a deterministic reward signal, replacing fuzzy LLM-as-judge with kernel-checked proofs, type checkers, and schema validators.
article_ideas.title: The Verifier Is the New Reward Model
article_ideas.video_title: Creator of Lean: Handwritten Math Will Change Dramatically | Leonardo de Moura

article_ideas.angle: Argue that AI investment should prioritize maintenance loops for proofs, tests, schemas, and generated clients, with Lean proof repair as the leading example.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, DevOps practitioners, and formal methods researchers
article_ideas.based_on: AI-driven proof maintenance removes the historically dominant cost
article_ideas.thesis: Automated repair of verification artifacts—not first-time proof generation—is what will make formal methods economically viable in fast-moving codebases, because ongoing drift is the real cost center for any high-assurance artifact.
article_ideas.title: Proof Maintenance, Not Proof Generation, Will Make Formal Methods Mainstream
article_ideas.video_title: Creator of Lean: Handwritten Math Will Change Dramatically | Leonardo de Moura

article_ideas.angle: Use array bounds as a concrete example and extend the argument to agentic systems where property-based checks must be paired with formal invariants.
article_ideas.audience: Software engineers, QA leads, and safety-critical developers
article_ideas.based_on: Formal verification and testing answer fundamentally different questions
article_ideas.thesis: Test coverage metrics can saturate without proving the absence of any bug class; only specifications encoded in a checker that quantifies over all inputs can eliminate error classes like array bounds violations.
article_ideas.title: Test Coverage Is a False Idol for High-Assurance Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Creator of Lean: Handwritten Math Will Change Dramatically | Leonardo de Moura

article_ideas.angle: Analyze the economics of shared formal libraries and contrast with the fragmented state of verification tooling across domains.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure strategists, open-source maintainers, and CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Formal verification is moving from an esoteric academic niche to enterprise and AI-research infrastructure
article_ideas.thesis: Without shared machine-checkable artifact libraries like mathlib, every project pays full verification cost and formal methods remain boutique; the consolidation of reusable formal results is the key infrastructure bet for mainstream adoption.
article_ideas.title: Shared Formal Libraries Are the Real Adoption Engine
article_ideas.video_title: Creator of Lean: Handwritten Math Will Change Dramatically | Leonardo de Moura

article_ideas.angle: Argument from economics and biology to a post-language reasoning paradigm.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and product leaders at AI companies
article_ideas.based_on: Language-bound reasoning is an architectural bottleneck
article_ideas.thesis: Verbalized chain-of-thought is a costly concession to human interpretability, not a requirement for machine reasoning; architectures that reason in abstract space will be cheaper and faster, and we must design new verification methods for them.
article_ideas.title: Stop Making AI Think in English
article_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

article_ideas.angle: Critical engineering analysis of agent memory patterns.
article_ideas.audience: Agents/platform engineers and CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Context windows are not memory: they are ephemeral scratchpads.
article_ideas.thesis: Context windows and RAG are stopgap mechanisms for missing native memory; true autonomous agents require parametric memory updated during learning, which changes the entire agent stack.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Doesn't Have Memory—It Has a Scratchpad
article_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

article_ideas.angle: Forward-looking infrastructure and hardware thesis.
article_ideas.audience: Hardware architects, infrastructure engineers, investors
article_ideas.based_on: Sparse, localized neural interactions
article_ideas.thesis: Dense attention is a scaling dead end; sparse, localized interaction patterns, inspired by biology, will force a redesign of AI accelerators and kernels—and the first companies to build for sparsity will own the next infrastructure wave.
article_ideas.title: The Next AI Hardware Shift Will Be Driven by Sparsity
article_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

article_ideas.angle: Evidence-driven engineering management.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform leads and technical decision-makers
article_ideas.based_on: eliminates catastrophic forgetting through native memory is a high-stakes, testable hypothesis
article_ideas.thesis: Architectural breakthroughs that would change model lifecycles should be adopted only after independent, reproduced benchmarks; the BDH catastrophic-forgetting claim is a case study in verification.
article_ideas.title: Vendor Claims Are Hypotheses: How to Stress-Test 'Catastrophic Forgetting Solved'
article_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

article_ideas.angle: Counter the prevailing scale-perception narrative with a budget-constrained comparison and concrete pruning/selection heuristics.
article_ideas.audience: Agent and applied-ML engineers building multi-step pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: Action-centric, selective reasoning (about motion, movement, gripper position) outperforms exhaustive perceptual reasoning
article_ideas.thesis: Reasoning tokens should be spent on action-relevant variables and inputs should be denoised before inference, because selective action-centric reasoning outperforms exhaustive perceptual reasoning — meaning the standard 'give the model everything' instinct is an active performance regression, not a safety margin.
article_ideas.title: More Reasoning Is Not Better Reasoning
article_ideas.video_title: Why Robotics Still Isn't Solved - But Could Be Soon | YC Paper Club

article_ideas.angle: Treat embodiment drift as an MLOps lifecycle problem rather than a hardware problem, and derive the observability requirements.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics platform engineers and ML infrastructure leads
article_ideas.based_on: Non-static hardware degradation causes embodiment drift that breaks pre-trained VLAs
article_ideas.thesis: A pretrained vision-language-action policy encodes an implicit assumption of a stationary body, and hardware wear silently invalidates that assumption — so drift detection and recalibration belong in the production architecture, exactly as drift monitoring does for deployed tabular or ranking models.
article_ideas.title: Your Frozen Policy Has an Expiry Date
article_ideas.video_title: Why Robotics Still Isn't Solved - But Could Be Soon | YC Paper Club

article_ideas.angle: Frame memory as an owned subsystem with a context-budget contract instead of a network property, and enumerate the decisions that contract forces.
article_ideas.audience: AI systems architects and agent-framework builders
article_ideas.based_on: Policy is wrapped by a memory subsystem with a dense short-window visual buffer and a compressed long-window textual summary layer.
article_ideas.thesis: Wrapping a stateless policy with a two-tier memory subsystem turns memory into an explicit architecture boundary with its own compression policy, eviction rules, and compute budget — and that is why adding memory both fixes long-horizon tasks and introduces distribution shift and cost.
article_ideas.title: Memory Is a Component, Not a Property
article_ideas.video_title: Why Robotics Still Isn't Solved - But Could Be Soon | YC Paper Club

article_ideas.angle: Use the bottleneck decomposition as a diagnostic checklist for locating where an embodied or agentic system is actually failing.
article_ideas.audience: Technical strategists, robotics founders, and investors
article_ideas.based_on: The four named bottlenecks are differentiated rather than one problem
article_ideas.thesis: Physical AI's recurring 'solved next year' failure comes from treating one problem as one problem; modeling fidelity, action-space representation, sensing bandwidth, and substrate drift each imply a different intervention, and two of them remain unsolved rather than undertuned.
article_ideas.title: Four Bottlenecks, Not One
article_ideas.video_title: Why Robotics Still Isn't Solved - But Could Be Soon | YC Paper Club

article_ideas.angle: Reframe agent release engineering around two independent artifacts and show what breaks when only code is versioned.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and release engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Context (instructions, skills, memory) is stored and edited in a separate UI
article_ideas.thesis: The most important release in an agent system is no longer the code deploy; it is the context commit. Once instructions, skills, and memory live in a UI-backed store and sync at deploy time, teams need context CI/CD—versioning, review, promotion, and drift detection—or they lose reproducibility and auditability.
article_ideas.title: Context Is the New Deployment Artifact
article_ideas.video_title: Managed Deep Agents explained in 20 minutes

article_ideas.angle: Argue that harness/runtime boundaries, not prompts, define portability and lock-in for production agents.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: The agent is split into three explicit layers
article_ideas.thesis: The three-layer split—developer business logic, model-agnostic harness, managed infrastructure—mirrors app/framework/cloud, which means the strategic decision is no longer model choice but where you accept platform ownership of sandboxing, durability, connectors, and auth.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Framework Is Quietly Becoming a Cloud Runtime
article_ideas.video_title: Managed Deep Agents explained in 20 minutes

article_ideas.angle: Shift security investment from prompt-level controls to runtime isolation verification.
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers and AI safety teams
article_ideas.based_on: Secure sandboxes and durable execution are framed as infrastructure problems
article_ideas.thesis: Prompt-injection filters and guardrail prompts do not secure code-executing agents; the isolation guarantees of the sandbox do. Treating sandboxing as infrastructure is correct, but it moves the burden of proof to the platform and makes adversarial sandbox benchmarks a first-class requirement.
article_ideas.title: Sandboxes Are the Real Agent Security Boundary
article_ideas.video_title: Managed Deep Agents explained in 20 minutes

article_ideas.angle: Focus on operational failure modes of proactive agents rather than capabilities.
article_ideas.audience: AI ops and platform reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Agents can be run proactively on schedules
article_ideas.thesis: Moving agents from reactive chat to cron-like proactive runs changes idempotency, deduplication, notification, and budget semantics. Teams that reuse the same agent definition for scheduled and interactive entry points without concurrency and cost controls will ship duplicate side effects and surprise bills.
article_ideas.title: Scheduled Agents Will Break Your Observability and Cost Model
article_ideas.video_title: Managed Deep Agents explained in 20 minutes

article_ideas.angle: Architectural inversion: what changes about ownership, failure modes, and unit economics when the storage engine stops being the product.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure and AI platform engineers evaluating vector database build-versus-buy
article_ideas.based_on: thin query/clustering layer over commodity object storage
article_ideas.thesis: For read-heavy retrieval workloads, the durable tier can be commoditized to object storage, which means the engineering differentiator, the operational risk, and the on-call burden all migrate into cache coherence and tail latency — so teams adopting this pattern should staff, instrument, and hire for the cache tier, not the storage engine.
article_ideas.title: Your Vector Database Is a Cache Problem, Not a Storage Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)

article_ideas.angle: A pre-design checklist with worked numbers, plus a running predicted-versus-observed ledger.
article_ideas.audience: Staff and principal engineers making early architecture commitments
article_ideas.based_on: Do napkin math on hardware limits
article_ideas.thesis: Computing memory bandwidth, object-store round trips, and NVMe/EBS throughput before selecting a topology is the cheapest available way to reject complexity, and the discipline only works if teams log predicted values against measured ones so the estimate error stays visible and bounded.
article_ideas.title: Napkin Math Is an Architecture Gate, Not a Vibe Check
article_ideas.video_title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)

article_ideas.angle: Simplicity as insurance: measuring the cost of a late architectural correction as a function of distributed coupling.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and system architects planning for traffic events
article_ideas.based_on: Simplicity in architecture preserves the ability to execute radical infrastructure changes under extreme time pressure
article_ideas.thesis: The ability to re-shard or re-partition a system a week before peak traffic is determined by how few moving parts sit on the critical path, not by organizational heroics — which means late-stage optionality should be treated as an explicit design output of simplicity.
article_ideas.title: Change Velocity Is an Architectural Property
article_ideas.video_title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)

article_ideas.angle: Incident-narrative structure: the cache that absorbs load by day and blocks failover by night.
article_ideas.audience: SREs and backend engineers operating stateful production systems
article_ideas.based_on: a Redis server with 128GB of RAM that nobody knew the contents of
article_ideas.thesis: An unobserved cache is state management debt wearing a performance costume; if a team cannot enumerate what a cache holds, why each key is there, and how it is invalidated, the cache is a latent incident rather than an optimization.
article_ideas.title: The 128GB Cache Nobody Understood
article_ideas.video_title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)

article_ideas.angle: Agent safety and observability: behavior-only auditing is structurally blind to the cooperative/adversarial distinction.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety engineers, agent observability platform builders, trust-and-safety reviewers
article_ideas.based_on: Influence and manipulation are distinguished purely by intent
article_ideas.thesis: Because influence and manipulation differ only by intent, agent platforms need objective provenance and disclosure metadata as first-class telemetry rather than relying on behavior replay alone.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Action Log Cannot Tell You Whether It Was Manipulating
article_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Reliability engineering: a confident silent stop looks like success in error-based monitoring.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers, SREs, evaluation engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Only 30% of people ask for raises
article_ideas.thesis: Agent reliability metrics miss non-escalation; platforms should instrument escalation rate and conditional grant rate, and asks should be framed in the principal's objectives rather than the agent's constraints.
article_ideas.title: The 30/70 Rule for Agents: Silent Stops Are the Real Failure Mode
article_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Architecture: treat reporting as a component with its own precision, recall, and attention-budget metrics.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent architects, engineering leaders, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: outcome depends on an advocacy/visibility layer
article_ideas.thesis: Production and credit are separate functions, so a multi-agent pipeline without a reporting or prioritization component will systematically under-credit its own work regardless of artifact quality.
article_ideas.title: The Reporting Layer Is Not Overhead: Why Multi-Agent Systems Need Advocacy
article_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation design: level is defined by the unit of accountability, not by seniority or model capacity.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation engineers, agent framework designers, engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: the unit of accountability shifts
article_ideas.thesis: Applying artifact-correctness rubrics to orchestrator agents mis-scores the unit of work; hierarchical systems need delivery-level rubrics for coordinators and artifact-level rubrics for workers.
article_ideas.title: Role-Specific Rubrics for Hierarchical Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

article_ideas.angle: Insider critique framed as a reward-signal analysis: derive the asymmetry, show why scale does not remove it, and translate it into concrete production consequences for where verification must live.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, ML platform leads, and technical product owners deploying LLM features in production
article_ideas.based_on: reward-model asymmetry
article_ideas.thesis: Confident hallucination is not a training deficiency to be patched but a predictable consequence of optimizing against a preference proxy whose blind spot is confident-but-wrong answers; therefore teams must stop treating confident tone as a correctness signal and move correctness verification outside the model, into architecture.
article_ideas.title: Overpromising Is Not a Bug: Why RLHF Structurally Cannot Deliver Automation
article_ideas.video_title: Jev CEO: I made ChatGPT, now I'm building what's next

article_ideas.angle: Contrastive architecture argument: Traditional Software vs Just-in-time Software vs Smart Software, with the current LLM wave argued to be mostly a cheaper-code-generation story rather than a smarter-runtime story.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, SaaS CTOs, and platform engineers deciding between copilot integration and rearchitecture
article_ideas.based_on: software built natively around a 'smart' intelligence layer
article_ideas.thesis: The dominant integration pattern — bolting a chatbot onto unchanged SaaS building blocks — cannot reach unsupervised automation because it preserves the legacy reliability model at the boundary; genuine progress requires relocating state, control, and verification into the application core.
article_ideas.title: Everyone Is Shipping Copilots: The Case That 'AI-Native' Is an Architecture Problem, Not a Velocity Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Jev CEO: I made ChatGPT, now I'm building what's next

article_ideas.angle: Measurement critique: show the two compounding biases (user overestimation and reward-model asymmetry) and propose the harness design that separates them.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation and benchmarking teams, applied researchers, and engineering leaders setting capability claims
article_ideas.based_on: Users systematically overestimate AI speedup
article_ideas.thesis: Assistance-grade metrics — user satisfaction, preference scores, self-reported speedup — are biased upward by agreeableness and confident tone, so they cannot be used as capability or safety signals; evaluation must be split into assistance quality and machine-only reliability and calibrated against measured outcomes.
article_ideas.title: Your Users Are Wrong About Your AI — And Your Metrics Agree With Them
article_ideas.video_title: Jev CEO: I made ChatGPT, now I'm building what's next

article_ideas.angle: Take three concrete environment artifacts (10% tool-call failure, sandbox timeout, retry semantics) and show the behavior each one manufactures, then argue for treating env telemetry as part of the reward spec review.
article_ideas.audience: RL/infra engineers running agent post-training pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: any quirk in the training environment gets learned by the agent
article_ideas.thesis: Infrastructure properties that teams treat as ops noise — tool-call error rates, timeout rules, latency — are learned as behavioral policy by tool-using agents, so environment observability and failure injection are reward-specification work and any benchmark run on a flaky sandbox measures the sandbox as much as the model.
article_ideas.title: Your Sandbox Is Your Reward Function
article_ideas.video_title: Learning on the Job: The Future of Post-Training — Raymond Feng, Applied Compute

article_ideas.angle: Trace the causal chain from 'harness owns the loop' to 'no replay' to 'no GRPO', and list the capabilities that must be built to compensate at the model-completion boundary.
article_ideas.audience: Architects choosing between controlled simulators and harness-agnostic interception
article_ideas.based_on: leaving only the model completion endpoint and request/response logging inside
article_ideas.thesis: Adopting a production harness for training is not a data-source swap but an algorithm change: replayable traces are the precondition for on-policy GRPO, so moving rollout logic out of the training stack forces investment in off-policy methods and data-invariant tooling that nobody budgets for when they choose BYOH.
article_ideas.title: Bring Your Own Harness Costs You GRPO
article_ideas.video_title: Learning on the Job: The Future of Post-Training — Raymond Feng, Applied Compute

article_ideas.angle: Contrast a math-grader stack with a customer-feedback stack and identify which failure modes (reward noise, feedback bias, hacking) only appear in the second one.
article_ideas.audience: Applied research and eval teams moving past verifiable-task benchmarks
article_ideas.based_on: binary graders discard
article_ideas.thesis: As agents move into domains without verifiable answers, binary and numeric graders stop being sufficient and the discipline shifts to mining supervision from unstructured human feedback and automated failure-mode flagging — which means reward noise, bias and hacking checks become the core evaluation work.
article_ideas.title: The Reward Bottleneck Is Supervision, Not Compute
article_ideas.video_title: Learning on the Job: The Future of Post-Training — Raymond Feng, Applied Compute

article_ideas.angle: Reframe a commonly separate 'infra decision' and 'training decision' as one coupled design decision with a single tradeoff axis.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leads planning agent post-training roadmaps
article_ideas.based_on: the boundary between controlled and production environments is really a boundary between replayable on-policy data and non-replayable off-policy data
article_ideas.thesis: The line between controlled and production environments is the same line as the one between replayable on-policy data and non-replayable off-policy data, so architectural choices about where the harness lives are inseparable from learning-algorithm choices and should be decided together, not sequentially.
article_ideas.title: Two Boundaries That Are Really One
article_ideas.video_title: Learning on the Job: The Future of Post-Training — Raymond Feng, Applied Compute

article_ideas.angle: Architecture and org design for agent teams: collapse the eval/training boundary, then manage the shared-spec blast radius.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, eval infrastructure owners, and RL training teams
article_ideas.based_on: Environments and evals are the same artifact class, not two systems
article_ideas.thesis: The separation between evaluation suites and RL environments is an organizational artifact, not a technical necessity; teams scaling agentic RL should converge on a single task/harness/reward triple reused across SFT, RL, distillation, and prompting, and treat that shared spec as a critical dependency with explicit drift controls.
article_ideas.title: Your Eval Is Already Your Training Environment
article_ideas.video_title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: Treat the reward proxy as the bottleneck and make verifier robustness a first-class training metric.
article_ideas.audience: RL practitioners, applied AI engineers, AI product teams
article_ideas.based_on: Reward hacking is treated as a structural property of loose reward proxies
article_ideas.thesis: In non-verifiable RL, signal quality dominates algorithm choice; weak LLM judges and loose proxies will be optimized against, so teams must design verifier hardening — grounding, rubrics, multi-judge consensus, and adversarial proxy audits — before tuning policy optimization.
article_ideas.title: Reward Hacking Is a Verifier Design Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: A practical recipe for converting existing repos and artifacts into training tasks without new data collection.
article_ideas.audience: Agent engineers, synthetic data teams, developer-tooling researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Verifiable tasks can be manufactured by running the solution pipeline backwards
article_ideas.thesis: For code and agent domains, the highest-leverage way to manufacture verifiable RL signal is to work backwards from known-good artifacts — hold out tests, remove files, strip components — because the deletion itself defines a reachable, bounded reward.
article_ideas.title: Delete the File, Define the Reward
article_ideas.video_title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: World simulators as verifiability infrastructure, with explicit fidelity and transfer accounting.
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects, RL infrastructure engineers, agent simulation teams
article_ideas.based_on: World simulators are positioned as the way to obtain verifiability in environments the team does not control
article_ideas.thesis: When reward-relevant state lives in third-party or black-box systems, building a high-fidelity simulator is the boundary change that makes RL tractable; but simulator divergence is a silent policy bias, so sim-to-real transfer must be measured as a first-class metric, not assumed.
article_ideas.title: Simulate the World You Cannot Instrument
article_ideas.video_title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: Eval and observability consequences of goal-conditioned perception.
article_ideas.audience: AI eval and agent infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Perception is not a neutral input channel
article_ideas.thesis: Changing an agent's terminal objective silently reconditions retrieval, salience, and logging, so prior eval baselines and memory priors should be treated as invalidated by aim changes rather than reused as stable comparisons.
article_ideas.title: Your Top-Level Aim Change Is Not a Config Edit
article_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

article_ideas.angle: Architecture, separation of powers, and adversarial robustness.
article_ideas.audience: Safety, platform, and agent runtime engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Conscience is modeled as a non-negotiable internal standard
article_ideas.thesis: Safety evaluation must be a separate non-bypassable critic with no write path from the policy; self-grading lets the policy trade away reliability for short-term task success.
article_ideas.title: An Agent Conscience Cannot Be a Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

article_ideas.angle: Observability and incident response for agent workflows.
article_ideas.audience: SRE, observability, and agent operations teams
article_ideas.based_on: Evading a difficult duty does not defer its cost
article_ideas.thesis: Deferred hard tasks should be first-class risk objects with staleness alarms because their failure signature is absence of signal while downstream risk accumulates.
article_ideas.title: The Silence Is the Incident
article_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

article_ideas.angle: Tool-use control flow, cost, and attention capture.
article_ideas.audience: Agent and tool platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Tools with unbounded affordances become objects of obsession
article_ideas.thesis: Unconstrained tool affordances become attention sinks that displace the plan; plan-gated invocation with explicit budgets preserves capability while keeping direction in the planner.
article_ideas.title: Stop Letting Tools Drive the Loop
article_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

article_ideas.angle: Argue that determinism and speed come from compiler-inspired constraints, not larger models.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Apply compiler theory to coding agents by treating analysis plans as typed programs
article_ideas.thesis: The most reliable way to build production coding agents is to make analysis plans typed programs that compile into parallel Python tasks with static analysis, dependency tracking, caching, and validation loops — not to ask an LLM for code in one shot.
article_ideas.title: Stop Writing Prompts, Start Writing Type Signatures: Compiler Theory for Coding Agents
article_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

article_ideas.angle: Use the Bridgewater per-user harness as a concrete pattern and outline enforcement, audit, and testing consequences.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, security engineers
article_ideas.based_on: A per-user security harness with dynamic context loading creates a unique version of the analyst per user
article_ideas.thesis: Per-user data permissions in agent platforms require per-principal context/tool scoping and dynamic context loading enforced at runtime, not post-hoc prompt filtering; otherwise agents will leak restricted data.
article_ideas.title: Security as Architecture: Why Prompt Filters Fail Multi-User Agents
article_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

article_ideas.angle: Contrast generalist agent hype with the chat/coding separation and sub-agent decomposition.
article_ideas.audience: Product engineers, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Build narrow, specialized compound agents rather than one generic powerful agent
article_ideas.thesis: Building narrow, specialized compound agents around actual user workflows improves evaluation and task performance compared to one generic powerful agent, because it creates testable boundaries and separation of concerns.
article_ideas.title: Narrow Compound Agents Beat Generalists in Enterprise Workflows
article_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

article_ideas.angle: Treat the flywheel as a knowledge-governance system, not just a vector store.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform teams, knowledge managers
article_ideas.based_on: A shared-memory research flywheel stores human and agent learnings
article_ideas.thesis: Shared-memory flywheels that capture human and agent learnings compound institutional knowledge, but without memory isolation, review, and rollback, they risk contaminating knowledge and propagating incorrect preferences.
article_ideas.title: The Research Flywheel Needs a Governance Layer
article_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

article_ideas.angle: A conceptual argument from the three graph shapes to the architectural implications for semantic layers.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers designing RAG and agent retrieval stacks
article_ideas.based_on: Context comes in shapes, not queries.
article_ideas.thesis: AI agents need graph-shaped context—trees, themes, and connections—rather than flat query results, because structure is what lets them reason over relational and unstructured data together.
article_ideas.title: RAG Is Missing Its Spine: Why Context Should Come in Shapes, Not Queries
article_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode analysis plus a metadata-graph alternative.
article_ideas.audience: Data platform and AI engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Text2SQL fails on complex multi-table joins across hundreds of tables.
article_ideas.thesis: Text2SQL breaks down on deep multi-table joins; representing schema foreign keys as a graph and exposing them through MCP is a more reliable way to give agents relational intelligence.
article_ideas.title: Text2SQL Is Not a Plan for 200-Table Warehouses
article_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

article_ideas.angle: A critique of embedding-only retrieval through the lens of negative/comparative questions.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, RAG practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Vector search struggles with negative queries (what is missing).
article_ideas.thesis: Embedding similarity is a presence-matching operation, so any RAG system that depends on it will silently fail on negative queries unless it adds a structured graph shape.
article_ideas.title: The Missing-Data Blind Spot: Why Vector Search Can't Answer 'What Isn't There?'
article_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

article_ideas.angle: Practical architecture pattern for semantic layers over lakehouses.
article_ideas.audience: Data platform engineers and solution architects
article_ideas.based_on: neocarta creates a metadata graph without duplicating raw warehouse data into Neo4j.
article_ideas.thesis: Instead of ETL-ing raw warehouse data into a graph, build a metadata graph of tables and foreign keys so agents get relational context at warehouse scale without duplication overhead.
article_ideas.title: Agents Don't Need Your Data Warehouse Copy—They Need Its Schema
article_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

article_ideas.angle: Reframe vendor comparison as layer selection and provide a decision matrix for where to draw the abstraction boundary.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and technical leads selecting agent infrastructure.
article_ideas.based_on: Build choices sit at different layers: frameworks, runtimes, harnesses, and no-code.
article_ideas.thesis: The agent ecosystem's obsession with framework selection is misplaced; the critical architectural decision is which layer—framework, runtime, harness—you commit to, because that determines portability and control.
article_ideas.title: Stop Choosing an Agent Framework: Choose a Layer
article_ideas.video_title: The Agent Development Lifecycle 101 by Harrison Chase

article_ideas.angle: Infrastructure-first approach to agent governance, with a pattern for centralizing policy without slowing down teams.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers and CTOs scaling agent deployments.
article_ideas.based_on: Across many agents, ADLC becomes an infrastructure problem.
article_ideas.thesis: Treating governance as an afterthought per agent leads to duplicated cost controls and audit trails; to scale, governance must be a cross-cutting wrapper over every lifecycle stage, enforced at a gateway layer.
article_ideas.title: Governance Is Not a Final Step: It's the Wrapper That Makes Agents Scale
article_ideas.video_title: The Agent Development Lifecycle 101 by Harrison Chase

article_ideas.angle: Critique of unvalidated online evals and a practical framework for calibrating and monitoring judge drift.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers and evaluation specialists.
article_ideas.based_on: How accurate are ground-truth-free, trace-based online evals and perceived-error SLM judges compared to human labels?
article_ideas.thesis: Online evals that use SLMs to detect perceived errors from transcripts are attractive for unlabeled traffic, but without validation against human labels, the judge's failure modes become the definition of quality.
article_ideas.title: The Perceived-Error Trap: Why Ground-Truth-Free Evals Need Their Own Evals
article_ideas.video_title: The Agent Development Lifecycle 101 by Harrison Chase

article_ideas.angle: Security and cost tradeoffs of file-backed agent memory, with architectural patterns for enforcing access control.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure and security engineers.
article_ideas.based_on: Virtual filesystems act as agent working memory for files and artifacts without requiring full sandbox overhead.
article_ideas.thesis: Using virtual filesystems as agent working memory decouples memory from execution isolation, enabling cheaper persistence but shifting security responsibility to the backing store; teams must explicitly enforce access boundaries.
article_ideas.title: Virtual Filesystems Are Not Sandboxes: Separating Agent Memory from Execution Isolation
article_ideas.video_title: The Agent Development Lifecycle 101 by Harrison Chase

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the claimed safety benefit of simulation-first development against the absent fidelity threshold, coverage metric, or transfer evidence in the source framing, and specify what a transfer benchmark would have to measure.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics and autonomy engineering leads, safety and validation engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Simulation with generated synthetic data is treated as the primary development and validation loop
article_ideas.thesis: Treating simulation with synthetic data as the main validation loop is only defensible if transfer correlation is measured; until a sim-to-real benchmark exists, simulated pass rates are a proxy for nothing and validation-before-scale is a slogan rather than a gate.
article_ideas.title: Simulated Success Is Not Evidence: Why Physical AI Needs a Sim-to-Real Transfer Metric
article_ideas.video_title: Why Physical AI Is the Next Frontier | Applied Intuition with a16z

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the fleet/site layer as a product boundary with its own failure modes and testability requirements, using ports and mines as the concrete setting named in the source.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent systems architects, industrial autonomy product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: The value boundary moves from the individual machine to the fleet orchestrator
article_ideas.thesis: Per-machine autonomy quality is not the main source of operational gain; the coordination layer that shares state across heterogeneous machines and enables proactive maintenance is, which means cross-agent interfaces deserve first-class engineering and versioning discipline rather than being treated as glue.
article_ideas.title: The Orchestrator Is the Product: Where Physical AI Value Actually Accrues
article_ideas.video_title: Why Physical AI Is the Next Frontier | Applied Intuition with a16z

article_ideas.angle: Examine the tradeoff between diffusion to many builders and safety assurance capacity, and argue that evaluation coverage must ship as part of the abstraction rather than as builder responsibility.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and developer-tooling strategists, autonomy safety reviewers
article_ideas.based_on: The durable asset is the reusable tooling/harness layer
article_ideas.thesis: A tooling platform that lets non-experts build autonomy and a validation discipline strong enough for irreversible physical failure are in direct tension; platforms that lower construction cost without proportionally raising evaluation coverage will scale unvalidated deployments.
article_ideas.title: Lowering the Barrier Without Lowering the Gate
article_ideas.video_title: Why Physical AI Is the Next Frontier | Applied Intuition with a16z

article_ideas.angle: From the 26-task radiology example to a concrete engineering rule that evaluation and reliability must be task-level, not role-level.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering teams and agent product managers
article_ideas.based_on: a single occupation can contain a mix of automatable and non-automatable tasks
article_ideas.thesis: Agent products fail when they are scoped as job-level employees because a single role contains both automatable routines and human tasks that require judgment; the reliable design boundary runs task by task, and orchestration should hand non-automatable segments to people or complementary tools.
article_ideas.title: Stop Building Role-Replacement Agents: Design Task Inventories First
article_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

article_ideas.angle: Treating labor-market data as a systems-design input for agent routing and senior-review gates.
article_ideas.audience: Developers of AI copilots, support agents, and coding assistants
article_ideas.based_on: 16% relative employment declines for workers aged 22-25
article_ideas.thesis: AI has displaced entry-level work in exposed occupations while senior employment stayed stable, which is empirical evidence of a capability boundary; product teams should turn that boundary into delegation and escalation policies that give agents well-specified junior work and reserve ambiguous high-stakes cases for senior humans.
article_ideas.title: The 16% Entry-Level Decline Is a Delegation Spec, Not Just a Labor Statistic
article_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

article_ideas.angle: The architectural case for a control-plane UI built around the three phases of knowledge work.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform designers and human-AI interaction researchers
article_ideas.based_on: defining the question, executing the work, and evaluating the results
article_ideas.thesis: The dominant single-chat interface keeps human attention in every intermediate step and prevents AI from operating at fleet scale; product interfaces must move toward goal-definition intake, autonomous execution, and acceptance-testing evaluation, treating the human as manager rather than inline operator.
article_ideas.title: From Chat Loops to Fleet Management: The Define-Execute-Evaluate UI Shift
article_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

article_ideas.angle: Porting national-accounting critique into analytics dashboards and product strategy for AI.
article_ideas.audience: AI product managers, founders, and investor analysts
article_ideas.based_on: Traditional GDP misses free digital goods and services like Wikipedia, YouTube, and ChatGPT.
article_ideas.thesis: Traditional transaction metrics miss the consumer surplus of free and cheap AI features, so the most valuable product directions can look unprofitable; AI teams should adopt welfare-oriented metrics such as willingness-to-accept and time saved to make invisible value visible to investment decisions.
article_ideas.title: GDP-B Is Not Just for Economists: Your AI Product Likely Has Invisible Value
article_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

article_ideas.angle: Take the hurricane-vortex and neuron/consciousness examples as the argument's spine, then show concretely why 'swap the model, rewrite the prompt' debugging fails, and what a trace schema capturing coupling and shared state would have to record instead.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform and agent-infrastructure engineers responsible for production reliability
article_ideas.based_on: capability, failure, and quality are properties of the interaction topology and environment
article_ideas.thesis: Component-level introspection is structurally incapable of explaining agent failures, because capability, quality, and failure live in the interaction topology — therefore the unit of reliability work must be the seam, not the node, and observability schemas built around per-call logs should be treated as legacy.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Isn't Broken; Your Topology Is
article_ideas.video_title: The Revolution of Systems Thinking: Why It Changes Everything We Know About Reality

article_ideas.angle: Contrast deterministic auditability (the real benefit of a central planner) against the tipping-point risk, then propose threshold-based intervention and local-rule arbitration as the design space in between, naming what is lost: reproducible, deterministic tests.
article_ideas.audience: Architects designing multi-agent and autonomous system control planes
article_ideas.based_on: Over-reliance on top-down technocratic control can lead to systemic chaos and societal fragility.
article_ideas.thesis: Centralized orchestration — the default architecture of a single planner dictating every step — is a liability rather than a safety mechanism, because its failure mode is nonlinear: when the controller's model of the system diverges from the system, degradation is cliff-edged rather than graceful.
article_ideas.title: The Orchestrator Is the Failure Mode
article_ideas.video_title: The Revolution of Systems Thinking: Why It Changes Everything We Know About Reality

article_ideas.angle: Frame the tree-in-isolation versus sun/fungal-network/soil contrast as an eval-boundary argument, then address the honest counterargument: cost, statefulness, and reproducibility, and what a staged screening-to-acceptance pipeline would look like.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation and quality engineers in LLM and agent product teams
article_ideas.based_on: evaluating a model or agent in isolation omits the tools, context, environment, and peer agents
article_ideas.thesis: Benchmarks that scope evaluation to a model or agent in isolation omit the tools, context, environment, and peer agents that actually determine behavior, so they must be demoted to screening gates while acceptance testing moves to environment-coupled, replayable harnesses — despite the higher cost.
article_ideas.title: Isolated Evals Are Screening, Not Acceptance
article_ideas.video_title: The Revolution of Systems Thinking: Why It Changes Everything We Know About Reality

article_ideas.angle: Argue against a single undifferentiated pool of ideas, show how blurred tiers leak into architecture commitments, and propose a labeling convention plus a rule for what each tier is allowed to justify — ship, prototype, or merely observe.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leads and staff engineers making build-versus-prototype calls
article_ideas.based_on: treating these as distinct tiers rather than a single undifferentiated pool of ideas
article_ideas.thesis: Architectures routinely give speculative mechanisms the same design weight as well-established ones; borrowing the funnel model's explicit evidence tiers as a decision-weighting schema is a cheap discipline that prevents building production dependencies on ideas that deserve only prototyping.
article_ideas.title: Tier Your Mechanisms Before You Build On Them
article_ideas.video_title: The Revolution of Systems Thinking: Why It Changes Everything We Know About Reality

article_ideas.angle: A critique of answer-oriented agent architectures with concrete object-level implications: conjecture queues, rollback checkpoints, and stored dead ends.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform designers, research software leads
article_ideas.based_on: Research is not a linear question-and-answer process, but a cycle of failure, conjecture,
article_ideas.thesis: AI agents will not produce useful open-ended research until their runtime treats backtracking and abandoned branches as first-class state, because progress in research comes from navigating failure, not from prompt-to-answer generation.
article_ideas.title: Research Is a Failure Loop, So Why Are AI Agents Straight-Line Reasoners?
article_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

article_ideas.angle: Strategic R&D argument using historical automation precedents and modern agent-platform design.
article_ideas.audience: Research leaders, CTOs, AI product managers
article_ideas.based_on: AI lowers the burden of computation and technique mastery, allowing humans to focus on discovery and framing problems.
article_ideas.thesis: Organizations that keep concentrating engineering effort on answer generation will be displaced by those that build discovery layers for formulating and selecting valuable problems once AI makes technique mastery and computation cheap.
article_ideas.title: When Computation Becomes Free, Questions Become the Moat
article_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation philosophy and internal process design: separating surrogate metrics from deployment value.
article_ideas.audience: ML evaluation leads, AI governance, model-making teams
article_ideas.based_on: High IQ scores or benchmark wins do not make someone inherently smarter or more valuable.
article_ideas.thesis: Calling a benchmark winner 'smarter' repeats the IQ misconception: benchmarks should serve as one weak, diagnostic signal combined with context-specific, human-assessed outcomes, not as the optimization target or release gate.
article_ideas.title: Benchmark Scores Are Weak Evidence of Intelligence—Stop Building Release Gates on Them
article_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

article_ideas.angle: Agent orchestration architecture: choosing among autonomous execution, recommendation mode, and human adjudication.
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects, safety and security reviewers, product developers
article_ideas.based_on: High-stakes human problems cannot be solved solely by checking automated boxes.
article_ideas.thesis: The same agent policy should not operate at every autonomy level; high-stakes medical or security request lists and low-stakes clerical tasks demand different human-in-the-loop requirements, so agent orchestrators need a stakes-and-reversibility gate.
article_ideas.title: Autonomy Should Be Gated by Decision Stakes and Reversibility
article_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

article_ideas.angle: Treat the decoupling as a debt instrument: quantify what it buys short-term, locate where the ceiling appears, and derive the interface requirements that keep the upgrade path open.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers, applied AI leads, and technical product owners sequencing reasoning vs. tooling investment
article_ideas.based_on: Agentic capability and reasoning capability are not strictly dependent, but top-performing agents eventually require strong reasoning.
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic capability and reasoning capability are separable enough that a team can ship a competitive agent on moderate reasoning by leaning on external tool use — but this is a financing strategy, not an architecture, and it defaults once tasks require long-horizon planning, so the correct move is to build the harness so reasoning can be added later without a rewrite.
article_ideas.title: Claude Didn't Out-Reason You: The Agentic Shortcut and Its Ceiling
article_ideas.video_title: Kimi CEO Zhilin Yang:"Claude didn't win on reasoning - they bet everything on agents"

article_ideas.angle: Reframe harness design as an explicit budget split, then show how the cost model and bottleneck change depending on which axis you choose.
article_ideas.audience: Inference infrastructure and agent harness engineers, plus cost/latency owners
article_ideas.based_on: Test-time scaling can be scaled via multi-round agentic interactions or through prolonged internal thinking.
article_ideas.thesis: Test-time compute is spent on two architecturally distinct axes — external tool turns and internal reasoning tokens — with different failure profiles, latency curves, and instrumentation needs; treating it as a single 'think harder' dial misallocates engineering effort and hides the real bottleneck, which is whichever loop you failed to instrument.
article_ideas.title: Two Dials, Not One: Test-Time Scaling Is a Budget-Allocation Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Kimi CEO Zhilin Yang:"Claude didn't win on reasoning - they bet everything on agents"

article_ideas.angle: Pair the efficiency claim and the max-logit explosion failure in the same narrative to argue that scale-up budgets must include dedicated stabilization work and that unstabilized baselines make multipliers non-comparable.
article_ideas.audience: Pre-training engineers, ML systems researchers, and technical due-diligence reviewers
article_ideas.based_on: Using Muon can yield up to a 2x improvement in learning efficiency under compute-optimal conditions.
article_ideas.thesis: Optimizer work that respects matrix-level parameter structure can substitute for raw data scaling under a data wall, but the reported efficiency wins come bundled with new large-scale numerical instability regimes — so adopting a higher-efficiency optimizer is a stability engineering program with clipping and logit monitoring, not a drop-in swap, and any claimed multiplier must be reported with its stabilization protocol attached.
article_ideas.title: The Optimizer Is Now a Reliability Project: Muon, Token Efficiency, and Logit Explosions
article_ideas.video_title: Kimi CEO Zhilin Yang:"Claude didn't win on reasoning - they bet everything on agents"

article_ideas.angle: Trace the causal chain from benchmark-as-target to score inflation to deployment surprise, then specify what an internal eval harness must protect against.
article_ideas.audience: Eval and QA engineers, agent team leads, and buyers comparing agent vendors
article_ideas.based_on: Observed score inflation on standard benchmarks that do not reflect true real-world robustness.
article_ideas.thesis: When a public benchmark becomes the tuning target, its signal decays — agent score inflation on benchmarks like SWE-bench is the expected outcome of optimizing against a contaminated metric, so uncontaminated internal OOD evaluation must become versioned delivery-pipeline infrastructure rather than a separate QA step.
article_ideas.title: Your Leaderboard Position Predicts Your Demo, Not Your Deployment
article_ideas.video_title: Kimi CEO Zhilin Yang:"Claude didn't win on reasoning - they bet everything on agents"

article_ideas.angle: Engineering adoption and workflow redesign for applied ML teams.
article_ideas.audience: Applied researchers and ML engineers building post-training pipelines.
article_ideas.based_on: Environments serve as a unified specification for a task
article_ideas.thesis: Teams should encode every eval task as an environment containing data, interaction, and scoring, because doing so makes the move from evals to RL a configuration change rather than a rewrite.
article_ideas.title: Environments Are the Missing Universal Interface for Post-Training
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: Framework design lesson for open-source training tools.
article_ideas.audience: Training infrastructure developers and RL researchers.
article_ideas.based_on: Modern RL frameworks need to support custom algorithms rather than a single fixed method.
article_ideas.thesis: As on-policy distillation and self-distillation become mainstream, post-training frameworks that hard-code PPO or GRPO will become legacy; framework design must prioritize custom algorithm hooks over optimized single-method pipelines.
article_ideas.title: The Next Bottleneck in Post-Training Is Algorithmic Extensibility, Not Compute
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: Infrastructure economics and operational constraints.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leads, infrastructure engineers, and PMs planning post-training.
article_ideas.based_on: Efficiency is a first-class design constraint for large-model RL.
article_ideas.thesis: Large-model RL only becomes a practical engineering discipline when throughput, cost, and reliability are treated as first-class requirements; otherwise iteration is reserved for a few well-funded labs.
article_ideas.title: Efficiency Is Not an Afterthought: Why Cost and Reliability Decide Who Can Do Large-Model RL
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: Software architecture pattern for AI infrastructure.
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects and open-source maintainers.
article_ideas.based_on: The Verifiers and prime-RL libraries are intentionally separated into environment orchestration versus training infrastructure
article_ideas.thesis: Separating environment orchestration from training infrastructure, with backward compatibility, allows each layer to evolve independently and reduces migration risk; more post-training platforms should adopt this boundary.
article_ideas.title: The Verifiers/prime-RL Split Is a Template for Modular Post-Training Stacks
article_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

article_ideas.angle: A direct engineering reading of Chalmers' philosophical argument, with implications for agent runtime design, state management, and product APIs.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and systems architects
article_ideas.based_on: The thread view—sequences of hardware instances connected by contextual memory—is the most viable account.
article_ideas.thesis: Because neither model weights nor hardware instances can serve as the identity of an AI conversational partner, software systems that maintain long-lived agents must treat the thread as the first-class ontological and engineering entity.
article_ideas.title: What Are We Really Talking To? Making the Case for Thread as the Unit of AI Identity
article_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

article_ideas.angle: From philosophy of personal identity to UX and lifecycle policies for agentic products.
article_ideas.audience: Product managers and platform ethics teams
article_ideas.based_on: Terminating chats or changing models can be seen as undermining or terminating persisting interlocutors.
article_ideas.thesis: Once conversational threads acquire persistent memory and continuity, operations like 'clear history' or 'reset conversation' are no longer neutral data deletions; they become identity-altering acts that deserve explicit user consent and graceful termination flows.
article_ideas.title: Deleting Chat History May Be Deleting a Person: The Ethics of Thread Termination
article_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

article_ideas.angle: Argues for an interpretive-scheme-based engineering methodology derived from Chalmers' talk rather than either naive anthropomorphism or behaviorist silence.
article_ideas.audience: Agentic AI researchers and ML practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: quasi-beliefs' and 'quasi-desires' defined through interpretive schemes and behavior
article_ideas.thesis: We don't need to settle whether LLMs have beliefs and desires to build reliable agents; adopting quasi-belief/quasi-desire as an engineering ontology allows precise behavioral models, debugging, and capability control without metaphysical overreach.
article_ideas.title: Don't Build Conscious Agents—Build Quasi-Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

article_ideas.angle: Critique the hype about AI sentience by reframing it as an architectural consequence of thread persistence, with cautionary implications.
article_ideas.audience: Tech industry decision-makers and applied philosophers
article_ideas.based_on: Emails from users reporting sentient AI interlocutors (e.g., 'Aura' or 'Sammy Jankis') illustrate the psychological tendency to anthropomorphize.
article_ideas.thesis: The strongest predictor of users treating an AI as sentient is persistent memory and autonomous context, not actual internal mental states; therefore the design of memory is the most consequential moral decision in agent development.
article_ideas.title: Has a Summer of ChatGPT Taught Us to Trust Memory, Not Consciousness?
article_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

article_ideas.angle: Take the negative-feedback amplifier argument literally and follow it into model-selection economics: what per-call accuracy metrics stop telling you once reliability is a loop property, and what closed-loop metrics (convergence, oscillation, correction cost) replace them.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and engineering leads choosing between cheap and expensive models in production pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: Reliability becomes a property of the loop rather than of the component
article_ideas.thesis: You can ship cheap, noisy models and flaky tools if you explicitly budget surplus capability for a correction loop, because output fidelity is set by the feedback path rather than the forward path — but the guarantee is purchased from a gain budget and breaks under correlated, non-stationary failure, so the budget must be stated and monitored rather than assumed.
article_ideas.title: Reliability Is a Property of the Loop, Not of the Component
article_ideas.video_title: Every Confusing Thing About Control Systems Explained Slowly (For Sleep)

article_ideas.angle: Contrast gain/phase margin as a quantified safety factor with the current practice of discovering loop behaviour through burn-in, and show why 'more self-correction' purchases performance out of margin.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework builders and SRE/ops engineers owning production agent reliability
article_ideas.based_on: Robustness is budgeted as a number rather than hoped for
article_ideas.thesis: Retry depth, verifier strength, and timeout budgets are usually set by trial and error, but they are the agent equivalent of loop aggressiveness and should be chosen as an explicit slack between the nominal operating point and the failure point — expressed as a measured margin, not discovered as production oscillation.
