article_ideas.thesis: Generative UIs collapse content retrieval into application execution, so platforms that deploy them must adopt kernel-style isolation and capability-based permissions around every response, or the next prompt-injection surface is a clickable app.
article_ideas.title: Every AI Search Result Is Now a Program: The Missing Security Layer for Generative UI
article_ideas.video_title: What Everyone Missed About Gemini 3 w/ Salim, Dave & Alexander Wissner-Gross | EP#209

article_ideas.angle: Translate Musk's 'Elon the collective' into concrete architectural requirements: shared memory, escalation protocol, and long-lived calibration.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent-architecture leads
article_ideas.based_on: Scaled autonomous execution is achieved by a small (~20) long-lived, trust-calibrated collective
article_ideas.thesis: High-performance autonomous execution comes from a small, persistent, trust-calibrated core that escalates correctly—not from scaling headcount or stateless prompt chains.
article_ideas.title: Your Multi-Agent System Doesn't Need More Agents. It Needs a Collective.
article_ideas.video_title: Why Elon Outcompetes Everyone | Shaun Maguire, Sequoia

article_ideas.angle: Operationalize the 3-tier vs 6-tier gap claim into routing rules and mediator-agent patterns.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform and agent infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: Communication bandwidth between collaborating agents is tier-dependent
article_ideas.thesis: Heterogeneous model pairing fails not because of raw intelligence gaps but because coordination bandwidth collapses beyond a threshold; tier-aware routing is an engineering requirement.
article_ideas.title: Capability Tiers Are the Hidden Bottleneck in Multi-Model Orchestration
article_ideas.video_title: Why Elon Outcompetes Everyone | Shaun Maguire, Sequoia

article_ideas.angle: Map talent judgment to dynamic role assignment, observability, and termination policies in agent fleets.
article_ideas.audience: AI ops and agent reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Talent judgment is a dynamic routing problem
article_ideas.thesis: Task allocation should be based on demonstrated aptitude and outcome feedback, not original role labels; systems need fast reassignment and termination loops.
article_ideas.title: Hiring Is Routing: Musk's Talent Judgment as an Agent Orchestration Pattern
article_ideas.video_title: Why Elon Outcompetes Everyone | Shaun Maguire, Sequoia

article_ideas.angle: Argue for derivative-based metrics in agent evaluation and staged autonomy rollouts.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation researchers and benchmark builders
article_ideas.based_on: Evaluate compounding, non-linear progress via second- and third-derivative metrics
article_ideas.thesis: Static benchmarks systematically underreport progress in agents; evaluation should track rate-of-change and constraint removal.
article_ideas.title: Second-Derivative Evaluation for Rapidly Improving Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Why Elon Outcompetes Everyone | Shaun Maguire, Sequoia

article_ideas.angle: Reframe context engineering as runtime algorithm selection and working-memory management, with concrete consequences for KV-cache reuse and agent loops.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent architects
article_ideas.based_on: Context window functions as working memory while weights are a hazy long-term recollection
article_ideas.thesis: The context window should be treated as an active computational workspace where temporary learning algorithms execute, so agent memory architecture must separate slow parametric memory from fast context-bound working memory and optimize prompts for algorithmic exemplars rather than static retrieval payloads.
article_ideas.title: Context Windows Are Runtime, Not Storage
article_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

article_ideas.angle: Use reward sparsity and variance as decision variables in training pipeline design rather than treating RL as the default post-training path to stronger reasoning.
article_ideas.audience: ML researchers and training pipeline engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Reinforcement learning is noisy and assigns credit inefficiently
article_ideas.thesis: Reinforcement learning should be scoped to tasks with reliable, dense, verifiable reward signals; otherwise its noisy credit assignment can reward rare lucky paths and waste compute that would be better spent on pre-training, imitation, or reward shaping.
article_ideas.title: The Sparse-Reward Trap: When RL Overfits to Lucky Trajectories
article_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

article_ideas.angle: Rank candidate domains by automatic verification maturity, and argue that building harnesses and sandboxes is more important than chasing broad knowledge-work automation.
article_ideas.audience: technical leaders, CTOs, and applied AI teams
article_ideas.based_on: Coding's success rests on text-based IO, mature execution infrastructure
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic automation advances fastest where outputs are textual and automatically executable or verifiable, so coding succeeded first not because of general intelligence but because of mature execution infrastructure and high-bandwidth human-AI interaction loops.
article_ideas.title: Ghosts in the Code: Why Execution Infrastructure Made Coding AI's First Domain
article_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

article_ideas.angle: Treat compression and data curation as first-class methods for producing reasoning models, with evaluation that measures generalization separately from memorization.
article_ideas.audience: applied AI researchers and edge deployment engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Excess data can increase rote memorization, while distillation aims to isolate a smaller cognitive core
article_ideas.thesis: Scaling data and parameters does not monotonically improve reasoning; excess data can push models toward rote memorization, so distillation and curation should explicitly separate generalizable reasoning from memorized trivia to enable smaller, lower-latency agents.
article_ideas.title: Distill the Cognitive Core, Not the Trivia
article_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

article_ideas.angle: Engineering-practice argument grounded in agentic loop mechanics, with a harness design that makes model choice a runtime configuration rather than an application constant.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform teams building agentic coding and tool-calling systems
article_ideas.based_on: A model-routing layer that dispatches each task class to the cheapest model that meets a measured success threshold
article_ideas.thesis: Per-token price gaps between specialized and frontier models are meaningless until harnesses report cost-per-successful-task and retry distributions, because agentic loops multiply both cost and failure; teams that route on unit price rather than task-level economics will silently ship worse systems at lower headline cost.
article_ideas.title: The 10x Cheaper Model Doesn't Win Until You Measure Cost Per Completed Task
article_ideas.video_title: AI Insiders Reveal Elon Musk's Master Plan to Win AI w/ AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #192

article_ideas.angle: Bottleneck-relocation analysis using the FSD-to-Optimus analogy, arguing that pipeline changes should be judged by where the constraint lands next rather than by what was removed.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics and embodied-AI teams, plus data-platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Dedicated capture sessions with wearable instrumentation and calibration, limiting data volume to what can be physically staged
article_ideas.thesis: Dropping motion-capture suits for passive video of workers does not remove the data bottleneck, it relocates it from capture logistics to annotation throughput and quality control; the correct response is investment in labeling, active-learning selection, and drift checks, not celebration of a cheaper camera.
article_ideas.title: Instrumentation Is the Bottleneck You Didn't Budget For
article_ideas.video_title: AI Insiders Reveal Elon Musk's Master Plan to Win AI w/ AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #192

article_ideas.angle: Infrastructure-strategy argument that reframes AI capacity planning as an energy-and-construction problem with siting as a strategic decision.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure strategists, investors, and technical leadership at AI labs
article_ideas.based_on: Colossus 2 features 500000 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and a 1GW+ data center in Memphis
article_ideas.thesis: When training sites are sized in gigawatts, power procurement, siting, and construction latency determine who can train at frontier scale; capability roadmaps that model GPU allocation without modeling the available power envelope at a site are fiction, and this concentration changes which organizations can compete at all.
article_ideas.title: Power Grids, Not GPUs, Are Now the Critical Path to Frontier AI
article_ideas.video_title: AI Insiders Reveal Elon Musk's Master Plan to Win AI w/ AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #192

article_ideas.angle: Commoditization argument tracing the shift in value capture from packaged features to workflow ownership and distribution.
article_ideas.audience: Product leaders and founders in creative software, translation, and vertical SaaS
article_ideas.based_on: Legacy software suites facing disruption must integrate AI-native workflows rapidly.
article_ideas.thesis: When professional editing lands at $0.039 per image and translation covers 243 languages in real time, wrapping a model capability is no longer a product; the defensible value migrates to orchestration, integration, and proprietary context, so legacy suites must re-architect around AI-native workflows instead of adding AI features.
article_ideas.title: Your Defensible Layer Is the Workflow, Not the Capability
article_ideas.video_title: AI Insiders Reveal Elon Musk's Master Plan to Win AI w/ AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #192

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the generation-centric narrative with the reported time-savings ranking, then derive concrete consequences for tool surface, retrieval/context design, and evaluation suites.
article_ideas.audience: AI tooling builders and engineering leaders choosing where to invest in assistant capabilities
article_ideas.based_on: AI code generation is not the primary time-saver reported by developers.
article_ideas.thesis: If the largest reported time savings come from debugging stack traces and refactoring existing code rather than in-loop generation, then tooling, training, and evaluation built around generation throughput are systematically mis-targeted, and the real engineering problem is context assembly over an existing codebase rather than output emission.
article_ideas.title: Your AI Coding Assistant Is Optimizing the Wrong Half of the Job
article_ideas.video_title: Measuring the impact of AI on software engineering  – with Laura Tacho

article_ideas.angle: Take the satisfaction paradox seriously as a design constraint: reason about the shape of the remaining work, not just the volume removed, and pair throughput metrics with sentiment measurement.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and developer-experience practitioners running AI rollouts
article_ideas.based_on: Developers who enjoy coding feel less satisfied when AI reduces their coding time in favor of toil.
article_ideas.thesis: Measuring only time saved or acceptance rate can validate a tool that increases throughput while degrading the developer experience, because AI absorbs the enjoyable portion of the job and leaves administrative work, meetings, and toil behind as the residue of human effort.
article_ideas.title: Time Saved Is Not Satisfaction: The Toil Residual
article_ideas.video_title: Measuring the impact of AI on software engineering  – with Laura Tacho

article_ideas.angle: Frame AI adoption as a bottleneck shift from authoring to verification, and argue that the compensating control belongs in the integration boundary rather than in developer discipline.
article_ideas.audience: Platform, CI, and release engineering teams
article_ideas.based_on: AI tools allow developers to write large amounts of code quickly, which can increase change failure rates if batch sizes grow too large.
article_ideas.thesis: Lowering the marginal cost of authoring code inflates batch size and complexity, so generation velocity is a stability risk unless batch size, review rigor, and test automation are enforced as pipeline-level constraints independent of how fast code is written.
article_ideas.title: Cheap Code, Expensive Change: Why AI Adoption Shows Up in Change Failure Rate
article_ideas.video_title: Measuring the impact of AI on software engineering  – with Laura Tacho

article_ideas.angle: Reframe rollout as an organizational change problem with a measured adoption floor, and show how low adoption silently invalidates the entire downstream measurement stack.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform teams accountable for AI tooling ROI
article_ideas.based_on: Simply purchasing AI tool licenses does not guarantee usage; companies must actively train and support developers.
article_ideas.thesis: Because licenses do not produce usage, any ROI measurement taken at low adoption is measuring nothing; enablement mechanisms such as office hours, workshops, and change management must be budgeted and staffed as a required component of the technical deployment, not an optional extra.
article_ideas.title: Adoption Is Part of the Deployment, Not Overhead
article_ideas.video_title: Measuring the impact of AI on software engineering  – with Laura Tacho

article_ideas.angle: Use the media-assistant failure (dog names and wake-up times surfacing for music questions) to demonstrate that top-k vector recall is a context-pollution risk, not a memory architecture.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building conversational agents and agent memory systems
article_ideas.based_on: Semantic similarity is not business relevance.
article_ideas.thesis: Agents should not use semantic vector similarity as their memory layer because embedding-space closeness is uncorrelated with business relevance; memory must be constrained by domain meaning to avoid irrelevant recall and hallucinations.
article_ideas.title: RAG Is Not Memory: Why Vector Similarity Pollutes Agent Context
article_ideas.video_title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep

article_ideas.angle: Argue from the architectural claim that embeddings lack relational context, and then explain how typed edges and temporal graph evolution substitute a full flat fact store.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure engineers and applied researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Embeddings lack causal and relational context.
article_ideas.thesis: Embedding vectors encode lexical/semantic proximity but not causal, relational, or business-logic context; persisting relationships in a graph gives agents the structural cues needed to retrieve the right memory at the right time.
article_ideas.title: What Graph Structure Adds to Agent Memory That Embeddings Cannot
article_ideas.video_title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep

article_ideas.angle: Treat TypeScript/Pydantic/Zod schemas as typed API contracts for the memory layer, with the financial-goals/debt/income example as evidence of domain modeling.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leads, AI product architects, and senior backend engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Developers can define custom entity types and schemas using TypeScript, Pydantic, or Zod.
article_ideas.thesis: Defining custom entity types, relations, and business rules in code makes memory an application-level contract; teams that design schemas before choosing storage will get more maintainable and relevant agent memory than teams that depend on generic vector recall.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Memory Schema Is a Product Decision, Not an Infrastructure Detail
article_ideas.video_title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep

article_ideas.angle: Skeptical methodology piece around the reported LongMemEval result, using pass-1 insight that the methodology is undisclosed and the claim is weak until verified.
article_ideas.audience: Applied AI researchers, evaluators, and teams choosing agent memory stacks
article_ideas.based_on: accuracy improvements up to 18.5%
article_ideas.thesis: Before adopting knowledge-graph memory because of headline accuracy numbers, teams should demand disclosed baselines and experimental controls; honest comparisons against full-context and vector-only memory will determine whether structured retrieval is genuinely superior.
article_ideas.title: Verify the 18.5%: Benchmarking Memory Architectures Honestly
article_ideas.video_title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode argument with concrete detection/cadence consequences
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform teams running LLMs in production
article_ideas.based_on: can regress with zero code changes
article_ideas.thesis: Pre-launch evals are a false safety net for systems built on mutable third-party models; scheduled re-validation against pinned versions must become the default release discipline.
article_ideas.title: Your evals are stale the moment your model provider ships
article_ideas.video_title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production

article_ideas.angle: Architecture and interface discipline
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leads and CI/CD owners
article_ideas.based_on: An eval is factored into a three-part contract
article_ideas.thesis: Treating evals as a three-part contract is what turns prompt/model changes into comparable experiments and CI-gateable artifacts, rather than playground impressions.
article_ideas.title: Task, Dataset, Scorer: the eval triple that makes model swaps diffable
article_ideas.video_title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production

article_ideas.angle: Scoring design anti-pattern
article_ideas.audience: Applied AI engineers and eval owners
article_ideas.based_on: Scoring is deliberately hybrid
article_ideas.thesis: Single-scorer eval designs systematically blind-spot either hard constraints or nuanced quality; production evals need layered verification with deterministic gates plus probabilistic judges.
article_ideas.title: Stop choosing between code scorers and LLM judges
article_ideas.video_title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production

article_ideas.angle: Data flywheel operations
article_ideas.audience: Platform, observability, and data engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Production traces are not just diagnostics
article_ideas.thesis: Feeding traces into eval datasets converts observability into coverage, but only if sampling, PII handling, and labeling queues are treated as first-class operational plumbing.
article_ideas.title: From production traces to test coverage: the missing curation pipeline
article_ideas.video_title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production

article_ideas.angle: Contrast proxy-level middleware with client-boundary tooling on the specific axis of output transformation, then trace the consequence: the proxy becomes critical-path infrastructure governed by streaming correctness.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and architects choosing where to place tool/grounding layers
article_ideas.based_on: Unlike MCPs, OpenRouter plugins allow transformations on both inputs and outputs in real-time streams.
article_ideas.thesis: Capabilities that must act on model outputs — grounding, citations, tool calling — should be hosted at the inference proxy because they are the only place that can transform streaming outputs uniformly; client-side approaches leave an unserved class of mid-stream transformations that must otherwise be reimplemented per app and per model.
article_ideas.title: Put Your Agent's Capabilities at the Inference Boundary, Not in the Client
article_ideas.video_title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter

article_ideas.angle: Follow the money: capability becomes fungible, so the durable engineering asset is the selection and normalization layer — and that layer must itself stay fast and testable.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, platform leads and FinOps-adjacent engineering managers building on LLM APIs
article_ideas.based_on: making inference a commodity
article_ideas.thesis: Once the same foundational capability is available from multiple hyperscalers at varying price and latency, differentiation stops living at the model endpoint and moves into routing, failover, caching, and cost control; committing to a single provider is therefore a unit-economics decision, not just an architectural one.
article_ideas.title: Inference Is a Commodity — So the Margin Lives in the Router
article_ideas.video_title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode-first: enumerate where multi-provider streaming breaks and what contracts a proxy must enforce, using the 400-model/60-provider scale as the forcing function.
article_ideas.audience: Backend/infra engineers building multi-provider LLM gateways
article_ideas.based_on: Solves complex routing, normalization, caching, and stream cancellation challenges across over 60 active providers and 400 models.
article_ideas.thesis: The hard part of aggregating inference is not model access but owning the wire-format normalization, streaming lifecycle, and cancellation semantics of dozens of heterogeneous providers; teams that treat these as plumbing will discover they are the product.
article_ideas.title: The Unsexy Work of an LLM Marketplace: Normalization, Caching, and Stream Cancellation
article_ideas.video_title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter

article_ideas.angle: Trace the causal chain from distillation economics to marketplace viability, and ask what breaks the chain if distillation stops working on the current frontier.
article_ideas.audience: Applied research readers and AI product strategists
article_ideas.based_on: Stanford Alpaca fine-tuned LLaMA 1 on GPT-3 outputs for under $600.
article_ideas.thesis: Cheap distillation of a strong teacher into small open weights was the precondition for the multi-model ecosystem: without a supply of capable, cheaply-hosted students, routing layers would have nothing worth routing to, so the routing thesis is downstream of the distillation result.
article_ideas.title: A Sub-$600 Fine-Tune Took the Monopoly Out of Model Quality
article_ideas.video_title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter

article_ideas.angle: Take the reductionism critique seriously as an engineering claim: name the specific failure classes (non-reproducible, cross-component, context-loss, handoff) that component inspection misses, then specify what an interaction-level metric actually measures.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform teams running agent systems in production
article_ideas.based_on: fails to capture systemic emergent behaviors
article_ideas.thesis: Per-component benchmarks and unit-level debugging are structurally incapable of explaining emergent multi-agent behavior, because behavior is produced by the relationships between components; teams need a complementary interaction-level observability layer or they will keep shipping systems whose failures they cannot localize.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Evals Are Reductionist: Why Component Scores Can't Explain System Behavior
article_ideas.video_title: Why Learning Systems Thinking is Essential in Tech - Diana Montalion

article_ideas.angle: Invert the usual build order: derive agent boundaries from communication paths, and treat prompt/capability work as downstream tuning that cannot compensate for a bad topology.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and architect-level practitioners designing agent platforms
article_ideas.based_on: organizations design systems that mirror their communication structures
article_ideas.thesis: In multi-agent systems the topology of message passing and shared context is the upstream control variable, so subagent boundaries, handoff protocols, and context-sharing paths should be designed before individual agent capabilities; capability-first design will repeatedly regress toward the communication structure it actually has.
article_ideas.title: Fix the Handoffs, Not the Prompts: Conway's Law as an Agent Architecture Principle
article_ideas.video_title: Why Learning Systems Thinking is Essential in Tech - Diana Montalion

article_ideas.angle: Propose a task-classification rubric and show how it translates into concrete human review gates and agent workflow checkpoints.
article_ideas.audience: Teams introducing AI tooling into architecture and design workflows
article_ideas.based_on: do not replace human relational and architectural judgment
article_ideas.thesis: The usable automation boundary is not 'hard vs easy' but language-level transformation (delegable) versus judgment about relationships and coherence (retained); without an explicit criterion, over-delegation silently removes the architectural judgment that keeps a system coherent.
article_ideas.title: The Delegation Boundary: What to Automate and What to Keep Human
article_ideas.video_title: Why Learning Systems Thinking is Essential in Tech - Diana Montalion

article_ideas.angle: Use the car-boat failure as a diagnostic pattern and derive governance mechanisms (conflict surfacing, invariant checks, coherence review gates) that catch it earlier.
article_ideas.audience: Product and architecture leads, technical program managers
article_ideas.based_on: leadership asked engineers to build a car-boat
article_ideas.thesis: Satisfying each stakeholder requirement in isolation produces incoherent designs, because coherence is a property of the relationships between requirements, not of the requirements individually; governance must surface conflicts before a combined design is commissioned.
article_ideas.title: Car-Boats: How Uncoordinated Requirements Destroy Conceptual Integrity
article_ideas.video_title: Why Learning Systems Thinking is Essential in Tech - Diana Montalion

article_ideas.angle: Reframe human oversight as an architectural placement problem with a latency budget, and show why inline approval gates break under machine-speed workloads.
article_ideas.audience: AI agent engineers, safety architects
article_ideas.based_on: Human-in-the-loop is a latency constraint, not just a governance choice
article_ideas.thesis: Inference-time human approval is a latency cost in high-consequence systems; the oversight loop must be split into a fast edge execution path and a slow policy authorization path, or the system fails under time pressure.
article_ideas.title: Human-in-the-Loop Is a Placement Decision, Not a Safety Switch
article_ideas.video_title: Aliens, AI Weapons, China & Global Conflict: Palmer Luckey Sounds the Alarm | EP #169

article_ideas.angle: Use the software-defined defense example to argue for a policy/harness layer as the primary adaptation surface.
article_ideas.audience: Systems architects, platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Separating the capability layer (software-defined policies/effects) from the platform layer (hardware effectors)
article_ideas.thesis: Separating capability from platform converts countermeasure adaptation into a software release problem; agent stacks should similarly abstract policy and behavior above models and tools to avoid infrastructure-speed iteration.
article_ideas.title: Software-Defined Defense and the Abstraction That Beats Procurement
article_ideas.video_title: Aliens, AI Weapons, China & Global Conflict: Palmer Luckey Sounds the Alarm | EP #169

article_ideas.angle: Map multi-domain sensor fusion to agent context aggregation and show why prioritization should not live inside the planner.
article_ideas.audience: Agent infrastructure engineers, context engineering practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: A multi-domain data-aggregation layer that fuses heterogeneous sensors
article_ideas.thesis: Fusing heterogeneous signal and autonomously ranking it before it reaches the decision interface reduces context load and suppresses triage errors; agent orchestration should adopt the same fusion/prioritization/command decomposition.
article_ideas.title: Prioritization Belongs Upstream of the Planner
article_ideas.video_title: Aliens, AI Weapons, China & Global Conflict: Palmer Luckey Sounds the Alarm | EP #169

article_ideas.angle: Import the asymmetric multi-polar threat model into agent security and argue for tiered authorization.
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers, agent platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: The relevant threat model is asymmetric and multi-polar
article_ideas.thesis: Security designs calibrated to peer adversaries break against unattributable non-state actors; agent security architectures need per-actor threat tiers and attribution confidence rather than a single deterrence model.
article_ideas.title: Deterrence Fails Against Rogue Actors: Tiering Agent Security
article_ideas.video_title: Aliens, AI Weapons, China & Global Conflict: Palmer Luckey Sounds the Alarm | EP #169

article_ideas.angle: Take the AV/agency distinction literally and derive the engineering consequences: independent versioning, separate training data regimes (~2 minutes of video vs. a curated personal corpus), and independent replacement under version skew.
article_ideas.audience: AI product architects and platform engineers building voice/video-facing agents
article_ideas.based_on: Avatar stands for audio-visual, while Agent stands for agency.
article_ideas.thesis: Conflating the audio-visual rendering layer with the agency/knowledge/reasoning layer is the most expensive architectural mistake in current agent products; the avatar should be a swappable presentation adapter over a stable policy-and-knowledge core, because rendering models and reasoning models have different data, lifecycles, and failure modes.
article_ideas.title: Your Avatar Is Not Your Agent: Why the Presentation Layer Must Be Disposable
article_ideas.video_title: The Future of AI Avatars and DeepFake Technology w/ Joshua Xu & Steve Brown | EP #161

article_ideas.angle: Reframe personalization as a data-pipeline problem and argue for measuring marginal fidelity per data category rather than assuming more corpus is better.
article_ideas.audience: Applied AI engineers and personalization/retrieval practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Giving an agent agency requires training it on personal history, values, and knowledge bases
article_ideas.thesis: Agent fidelity to a principal is bounded by the curation quality of the private knowledge base, not by base-model capability, so engineering effort should shift from model selection toward ingestion, structuring, and lifecycle management of personal data.
article_ideas.title: The Bottleneck Is Your Corpus, Not Your Model
article_ideas.video_title: The Future of AI Avatars and DeepFake Technology w/ Joshua Xu & Steve Brown | EP #161

article_ideas.angle: Contrast output-layer moderation with creation-time gating, and specify what a consent artifact must contain (verification method, storage, binding to the generated model, revocation path).
article_ideas.audience: Trust-and-safety leads, platform policy architects, identity engineers
article_ideas.based_on: HeyGen requires first-party video consent for every avatar created on the platform.
article_ideas.thesis: Post-hoc deepfake detection is structurally losing; the durable control is a first-party, verifiable consent artifact required before an identity model exists, bound to the model version and revocable so that withdrawal invalidates generation.
article_ideas.title: Consent as an Artifact, Not a Policy: Gating Identity Synthesis at Creation Time
article_ideas.video_title: The Future of AI Avatars and DeepFake Technology w/ Joshua Xu & Steve Brown | EP #161

article_ideas.angle: Derive the general rule from the voice/video case and sketch what capture-time provenance would need to look like for live calls.
article_ideas.audience: Security architects and communications-platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: What standards will emerge for verifying the authenticity of real-time AI video calls?
article_ideas.thesis: When a channel becomes cheaply synthesizable, authentication cannot stay in that channel; the household verification-word habit is a symptom of a missing runtime attestation layer, and institutions inheriting these habits will be defrauded at scale.
article_ideas.title: Trust Protocols Must Be Re-derived Per Modality
article_ideas.video_title: The Future of AI Avatars and DeepFake Technology w/ Joshua Xu & Steve Brown | EP #161

article_ideas.angle: Frame it as the same abstraction decision agent engineers already make (many narrow agents vs. one general agent plus retrieval, tool reuse, and few-shot adaptation), and show that the deciding variable is crossover volume rather than peak quality.
article_ideas.audience: AI/agent platform architects and engineering leads deciding between bespoke per-workflow automation and a shared runtime.
article_ideas.based_on: Customization increases cost; general-purpose humanoid platforms are key to scaling.
article_ideas.thesis: At high deployment volume and high task diversity, a single general runtime plus transfer learning beats a portfolio of task-specific systems on cost per successful task, even when each specialist is locally superior; therefore the engineering investment should go into generality and transfer interfaces, not per-task optimality.
article_ideas.title: The Cost Curve Beats the Benchmark: Why General Platforms Win at Volume
article_ideas.video_title: AI Experts Q&A: How Humanoid Robots Will Impact Every Industry | EP #160

article_ideas.angle: Trace the pattern from substation-co-located generation to deploying compute and agents into existing permitted footprints and interconnect queues, and argue that deployment topology should be treated as an architectural decision, not a logistics afterthought.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure planners, technical program managers, and founders doing capacity planning under permitting constraints.
article_ideas.based_on: Fusion plants deployed in existing substation locations will eliminate transmission needs.
article_ideas.thesis: When the scarce resource is permission or right-of-way rather than capability, the correct engineering response is a topology change — co-locate at already-permitted sites — not faster execution inside the old topology.
article_ideas.title: Permits Are the New Physics: Designing Around Institutional Latency
article_ideas.video_title: AI Experts Q&A: How Humanoid Robots Will Impact Every Industry | EP #160

article_ideas.angle: Use incumbent-opposition examples and siting objections to argue that capability roadmaps should be published alongside an institutional-resistance budget, and show how to estimate both.
article_ideas.audience: Product strategists, investors, and anyone committing to public deployment dates.
article_ideas.based_on: Screen Actors Guild fighting AI deployment to protect their industry.
article_ideas.thesis: Any deployment timeline model that gates only on technical readiness will be wrong wherever an organized incumbent holds regulatory or contractual leverage; institutional resistance must be modeled as a separate, potentially dominant latency term.
article_ideas.title: Your Adoption Forecast Is Missing a Term
article_ideas.video_title: AI Experts Q&A: How Humanoid Robots Will Impact Every Industry | EP #160

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the usual automation pattern of re-fixturing the workspace, using the installed base of human-shaped infrastructure as the evidence, and note the inverse case where the environment is hostile to humans and no adaptation is needed at all.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics and automation engineers, and operations leaders evaluating brownfield deployment.
article_ideas.based_on: Space is pernicious for humans, making it fantastic for humanoid robots.
article_ideas.thesis: When the target environment is expensive, distributed, or not owned by the deployer, adapting the agent to the existing environment beats retrofitting the environment for the agent; form factor is therefore an economic decision about avoiding retrofit capex.
article_ideas.title: Build the Agent to Fit the World, Not the World to Fit the Agent
article_ideas.video_title: AI Experts Q&A: How Humanoid Robots Will Impact Every Industry | EP #160

article_ideas.angle: Argues that agent integrations should target existing UI surfaces rather than wait for API access.
article_ideas.audience: Agent engineers, product architects, automation leads
article_ideas.based_on: the human interface becomes the de facto API
article_ideas.thesis: General-purpose agents will see fastest adoption against legacy human-facing interfaces because re-instrumenting every system is economically irrational; the human UI becomes the de facto API, and brittleness is the price of reach.
article_ideas.title: The API Is the Interface: How General-Purpose Agents Enter Through Legacy UIs
article_ideas.video_title: The Billionaire Building America's AI Military | EP #158

article_ideas.angle: Connects defense acquisition to prototype-first software development.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, procurement reformers, startup founders
article_ideas.based_on: inverts the standard government-funded, spec-first development sequence
article_ideas.thesis: When buyers cannot articulate requirements, self-funded build-and-demonstrate compresses delivery cycles versus cost-plus, requirements-first contracting because the artifact, not the specification, becomes the evaluation surface.
article_ideas.title: Build First, Spec Later: Why Vendor-Funded Prototypes Beat Requirements-First Procurement
article_ideas.video_title: The Billionaire Building America's AI Military | EP #158

article_ideas.angle: Uses cost-plus contracting as a warning for internal AI program metrics.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering managers, org designers, program leads
article_ideas.based_on: Compensation and contracting structures that reimburse cost rather than outcome
article_ideas.thesis: Reward structures that reimburse cost or activity rather than shipped capability systematically select for higher cost and slower delivery, and AI teams reproduce this failure when they measure scope instead of outcomes.
article_ideas.title: Your Evaluation Function Is Your Architecture
article_ideas.video_title: The Billionaire Building America's AI Military | EP #158

article_ideas.angle: Reframes human-in-the-loop from safeguard to design-time boundary condition.
article_ideas.audience: Safety engineers, autonomy architects, policy technologists
article_ideas.based_on: A hard constraint is placed on autonomy
article_ideas.thesis: In high-consequence autonomous systems, deciding which decisions remain human-owned is an architectural constraint that must be set before designing the control loop; treating it as post-hoc review distorts latency, throughput, and interface requirements.
article_ideas.title: Accountability Is a Control-Loop Constraint, Not a Review Layer
article_ideas.video_title: The Billionaire Building America's AI Military | EP #158

article_ideas.angle: Reinterpret the practical/emotional/social taxonomy as an interaction-contract classifier, with the mismatch case as the concrete failure to eliminate.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building conversational agents and support automation
article_ideas.based_on: Conversations belong to distinct modes
article_ideas.channel: Front Row Seat with Ken Coleman
article_ideas.thesis: Most 'bad response' failures in agent systems are register mismatches, not capability gaps: the system answered a practical question nobody asked, and the fix is an explicit classification stage upstream of generation rather than a stronger generator.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Doesn't Need a Better Answer, It Needs a Mode Classifier
article_ideas.video_title: The Key to Mastering Conversations and Being Memorable

article_ideas.angle: Treat 'Did I get that right?' as an acknowledgment protocol between components, not a politeness ritual, and cost it out honestly.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform and multi-agent orchestration engineers
article_ideas.based_on: then ask 'Did I get that right?'
article_ideas.channel: Front Row Seat with Ken Coleman
article_ideas.thesis: Paraphrasing demonstrates effort; only an explicit confirmation request converts assumed shared state into a checkable state transition, and the added round trip is a deliberate price rather than waste.
article_ideas.title: Confirmation Is the Feature: Why Paraphrasing Alone Doesn't Prove Understanding
article_ideas.video_title: The Key to Mastering Conversations and Being Memorable

article_ideas.angle: Argue for a two-axis eval where the second axis is mutual predictability/synchronization, and propose observable surrogates for text-only channels.
article_ideas.audience: Evals and observability practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: connection, not just information transfer
article_ideas.channel: Front Row Seat with Ken Coleman
article_ideas.thesis: Task-completion scoring is blind to interaction synchronization, so systems can be locally optimal on the one metric they optimize and globally harmful on the axis users actually feel; a second metric family is required, not optional.
article_ideas.title: Beyond Task Success: Instrumenting Connection as a Second Evaluation Axis
article_ideas.video_title: The Key to Mastering Conversations and Being Memorable

article_ideas.angle: Turn the political-perception observation into a reproducible context-pipeline experiment with a re-weighting treatment arm.
article_ideas.audience: Context-engineering and prompt-systems engineers
article_ideas.based_on: low-base-rate but high-salience element in the context window disproportionately steers downstream judgment
article_ideas.channel: Front Row Seat with Ken Coleman
article_ideas.thesis: Vivid, low-base-rate content in a context window over-determines downstream judgment relative to its true share of relevance, and the correct mitigation is deliberate re-weighting of base rates rather than adding more context.
article_ideas.title: The 2% Problem: Salience Distortion Is a Context-Engineering Bug
article_ideas.video_title: The Key to Mastering Conversations and Being Memorable

article_ideas.angle: Economic framing applied to concrete engineering decisions: provider-agnostic interfaces, pluggable models, and tool layers. Use examples from model provider churn and API instability.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform architects, technical decision-makers
article_ideas.based_on: Architectural decisions should be framed as real options
article_ideas.thesis: Architectural abstractions in AI systems should be evaluated as real options, with their value proportional to environmental uncertainty and switching costs; teams should therefore invest in flexibility only where volatility is high, and strip it where uncertainty is low.
article_ideas.title: Your Abstractions Are Options: Pricing Flexibility in Agent Architectures
article_ideas.video_title: Thinking Like an Architect - Gregor Hohpe - NDC London 2025

article_ideas.angle: Map organizational design principles (architects as multipliers) to agent orchestration; contrast central oracle with local authority plus guardrails.
article_ideas.audience: Agent system designers, engineering leaders, distributed systems architects
article_ideas.based_on: Decision rights should sit with the actors who live with the consequences
article_ideas.thesis: Centralized decision-making in multi-agent systems fails to scale and often produces worse decisions than delegating authority to context-bearing components, provided central layers supply shared constraints and tooling rather than per-action verdicts.
article_ideas.title: The Central Oracle Is a Bottleneck: Why Agent Architectures Should Push Decisions to the Edge
article_ideas.video_title: Thinking Like an Architect - Gregor Hohpe - NDC London 2025

article_ideas.angle: From scalar benchmarks to vector-based evaluation. Show how decomposing into orthogonal dimensions (granularity, coupling, lock-in, latency, cost, quality) changes choices.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, evaluators, performance engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Treating trade-offs as binary (speed vs quality, latency vs throughput) is a modeling error
article_ideas.thesis: Treating trade-offs such as speed vs. quality or latency vs. throughput as opposing ends of a single axis is a modeling error that leads to false dilemmas; multi-dimensional vector evaluation enables co-optimization and better design decisions.
article_ideas.title: Beyond Binary Trade-offs: Vector Evaluation for AI Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Thinking Like an Architect - Gregor Hohpe - NDC London 2025

article_ideas.angle: Challenge the default cloud-centric agent architecture and argue for edge-first design patterns with cloud fallback only where necessary.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and software architects building agentic systems
article_ideas.based_on: Liquid neural networks require minimal compute to package intelligence into devices.
article_ideas.thesis: Privacy-sensitive and latency-critical agents should be designed with on-device small models as the primary inference path, not cloud-only fallback, because liquid neural networks can run locally with minimal compute and zero cloud cost; this flips assumptions about privacy, latency, and infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: The Edge Will Not Be Cloud: Why On-Device Liquid Models Change Agent Architecture
article_ideas.video_title: AI Leaders Reveal the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs (At FII Miami 2025) | EP #150

article_ideas.angle: Use the 11% production success figure to argue that AI adoption strategies should be treated as organizational transformation programs.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, enterprise architects, and AI adoption leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Only 11% of enterprise technology use cases successfully saw the light of production
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise AI production failure is primarily an organizational architecture and leadership literacy problem, so agent deployments must budget for governance, process redesign, and change management, not just better models.
article_ideas.title: The 89% Failure Rate Is an Architecture Problem, Not a Model Problem
article_ideas.video_title: AI Leaders Reveal the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs (At FII Miami 2025) | EP #150

article_ideas.angle: Compare GPU lock-in and CUDA maturity against open tensor processor promises, focusing on portability and developer productivity risks.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure leaders and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Tensor processors are simpler and easier to program
article_ideas.thesis: AI infrastructure strategy should evaluate post-GPU tensor processors and open hardware/software stacks because claimed 5x to 10x cost reductions and simpler programming could reduce vendor lock-in, but ecosystem maturity is the real bottleneck.
article_ideas.title: Beyond GPUs: Tensor Processors and the Coming Hardware Pluralism
article_ideas.video_title: AI Leaders Reveal the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs (At FII Miami 2025) | EP #150

article_ideas.angle: Separate language AI from equation-solving AI and argue for distinct R&D infrastructure and evaluation criteria.
article_ideas.audience: R&D technology strategists and scientific computing teams
article_ideas.based_on: Quantitative AI drives heavy R&D industries like pharma and energy
article_ideas.thesis: Treating all AI as language model tasks is an architectural mistake; quantitative AI and large quantitative models need different compute, data pipelines, and evaluation methods, while hybrid quantum-GPU infrastructure remains a long-horizon prediction.
article_ideas.title: Quantitative AI Is Not Language AI: Separate Stacks for Scientific R&D
article_ideas.video_title: AI Leaders Reveal the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs (At FII Miami 2025) | EP #150

article_ideas.angle: Critical methodology of AI cost figures with focus on what an agent engineering team should extract from DeepSeek-style reports.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders and applied ML teams evaluating model training and procurement.
article_ideas.based_on: What exactly is included in the reported $5.6M DeepSeek R1 training cost
article_ideas.thesis: $5.6M is both real and misleading: the number ignores total experimental cost and hides the architecture research that made it possible; treating it as a floor or ceiling distorts both build-vs-buy and compute-scaling decisions.
article_ideas.title: Headline training costs are engineering poetry, not accounting
article_ideas.video_title: DeepSeek vs. Open AI - The State of AI w/ Emad Mostaque & Salim Ismail | EP #146

article_ideas.angle: A practitioner's argument for model gateways and task-specific regression evaluations using DeepSeek-vs-GPT-4o pricing as the current case.
article_ideas.audience: Developers and architects of agentic systems.
article_ideas.based_on: model selection should be treated as a live cost-quality routing decision, not a fixed brand choice
article_ideas.thesis: When open and closed models trade positions every few months, production agents should not be built on model loyalty but on a gateway that routes each task to the cheapest endpoint passing a task-level success bar; cost per solved task, not per token, becomes the unit of optimization.
article_ideas.title: Stop asking about your favorite model; start tracking cost per successful task
article_ideas.video_title: DeepSeek vs. Open AI - The State of AI w/ Emad Mostaque & Salim Ismail | EP #146

article_ideas.angle: Trade-off analysis: engineering teams adopt open models for cost, but must mature their internal control plane; this reverses the conventional 'proprietary is safer' assumption.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, security and compliance leads building on open-source AI.
article_ideas.based_on: Once weights are open, provider-side safety, licensing, and access controls are no longer the enforcement point
article_ideas.thesis: Open-weight deployments move governance, safety, logging, and upgrade policy from vendor API terms to the operator's own stack, so the cost gap is only an advantage if the operator can absorb operational accountability — which favors platforms that are already compliance-heavy.
article_ideas.title: The open-weight advantage is infrastructure risk, not API pricing
article_ideas.video_title: DeepSeek vs. Open AI - The State of AI w/ Emad Mostaque & Salim Ismail | EP #146

article_ideas.angle: Architecture argument using Salesforce's platform rewrite as the proof point that data consolidation precedes agent autonomy.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, CTOs, and AI platform leads
article_ideas.based_on: treats a single canonical platform and unified data cloud as a prerequisite for reliable agents
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise agent reliability is downstream of data architecture: Salesforce made Agentforce work by first rewriting every product onto one platform and feeding the agent layer through Data Cloud, so organizations that bolt agents onto siloed SaaS applications will hit an invisible reliability ceiling.
article_ideas.title: You Can't Agentize Your Way Out of Fragmented Data
article_ideas.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141

article_ideas.angle: Operational design of human-agent triage, argued from Salesforce's layered triage pattern.
article_ideas.audience: Support operations leaders, agent platform engineers, and product managers
article_ideas.based_on: human agents remain only for escalation
article_ideas.thesis: Agent-first support succeeds not because agents resolve 95% of tickets but because escalation is engineered as a core primitive: confidence thresholds, hand-off conditions, and human fallback determine whether autonomous resolution creates trust or destroys customer relationships.
article_ideas.title: The 5% Human Handoff Is What Makes 95% Autonomy Safe
article_ideas.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141

article_ideas.angle: Workforce economics and engineering management: how a headline productivity number changes headcount planning before independent validation exists.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering executives, CTOs, and finance/capacity planners
article_ideas.based_on: make net-new software engineer hiring unnecessary
article_ideas.thesis: When agentic developer tools push engineering productivity high enough, the rational capacity decision becomes zero net-new hires; leaders who do not instrument hiring elasticity are making workforce bets from unreplicated executive claims.
article_ideas.title: 30% Productivity Is a Hiring Event, Not Just an Efficiency Metric
article_ideas.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141

article_ideas.angle: A human-workforce rebalancing argument from Salesforce's support-agent reduction, treating reallocation as the main discipline that makes AI-driven cost savings sustainable.
article_ideas.audience: Operations executives, workforce transformation teams, and HR leaders
article_ideas.based_on: plans to reallocate support staff to more complex, higher-value areas
article_ideas.thesis: The real organizational risk of agentic automation is not the fact that headcount shrinks from 9,000 support agents; it is the implicit promise that displaced workers will be reallocated to higher-value work without explicit role maps and reskilling systems.
article_ideas.title: Digital Labor Doesn't Just Cut Costs—It Reclassifies Work
article_ideas.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141

article_ideas.angle: Historical failure case (UML as programming language) mapped onto current agent orchestration practice, with the abstraction-creep pattern named and illustrated.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and agent framework authors deciding where to place the specification/execution boundary
article_ideas.based_on: Treating UML as a programming language led to excessive complexity and the decline of its adoption.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent teams are repeating UML's mistake: intermediate representations that begin as human reasoning artifacts (plans, DSLs, schemas, prompt templates) are being upgraded into execution mechanisms, and the predictable result is complexity growth followed by abandonment. The correct architecture keeps notation and execution as separate layers joined by a narrow, explicitly lossy bridge, and forgoes round-trip model-driven execution as the price of preserved adoption.
article_ideas.title: Your Spec Language Is Not Your Runtime
article_ideas.video_title: Evolution of software architecture with the co-creator of UML (Grady Booch)

article_ideas.angle: Operational definition plus a review-allocation policy; ties the cost-of-change test to the AI/human division of labor as a single rule rather than two separate heuristics.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and staff-plus engineers setting review and oversight policy for AI-assisted teams
article_ideas.based_on: significance is measured by cost of change
article_ideas.thesis: Most architecture review budgets are spent on artifacts that sound foundational (frameworks, layer diagrams, diagram conventions) and not on decisions that are actually expensive to undo. If 'architectural' is defined as cost of change, then model/vendor commitments, tool contracts, memory schemas, and evaluation definitions deserve gates while prompts and prompt templates should iterate without ceremony. Oversight should be allocated by reversibility cost, and the same rule is the correct routing function for AI-generated versus human-owned decisions.
article_ideas.title: Architecture Review Should Be Priced by Reversibility, Not by Importance
article_ideas.video_title: Evolution of software architecture with the co-creator of UML (Grady Booch)

article_ideas.angle: Lifecycle-engineering argument with agent-system-specific wrapper accumulation as the motivating modern instance.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and maintenance engineers responsible for long-lived services and the AI wrappers placed over them
article_ideas.based_on: Old code never dies; you have to kill it.
article_ideas.thesis: Treating legacy as an age or ownership state produces passive maintenance strategies that fail, because nothing deprecates on its own and business rules hide deep inside long-lived codebases. The practical correction is to demand an owner, a retirement trigger, and a migration or emulation path at the moment a component is created — including the prompt chains, adapters, and legacy-service wrappers that agent systems accumulate by default. 'No one has asked to delete it' is evidence of missing offboarding, not of continued value.
article_ideas.title: Old Code Never Dies: Retirement as a Creation-Time Requirement
article_ideas.video_title: Evolution of software architecture with the co-creator of UML (Grady Booch)

article_ideas.angle: Positions the critique as a scoping argument about which failure classes scale cannot address, and derives a concrete oversight-allocation policy; treats the claim's weak evidence strength explicitly as a hypothesis under test.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering teams and technical decision-makers deploying LLMs into cross-cutting design work
article_ideas.based_on: LLMs enable global-scale bullshit generators because they lack true reasoning and embodiment.
article_ideas.thesis: If the model's deficiency is grounding rather than capacity, then scaling data and parameters will not fix errors that are systemic rather than local, and the durable deployment pattern is a fixed division of labor: the model generates and searches, humans or separately verified systems own cross-cutting architectural decisions. Practically, this argues for treating model output as an accelerator draft rather than a decision, and for allocating oversight by decision cost instead of uniformly — rather than attempting to build a verification harness that substitutes for the missing grounding.
article_ideas.title: LLMs as Accelerators, Not Architects: Why More Scale Does Not Close the Systemic Gap
article_ideas.video_title: Evolution of software architecture with the co-creator of UML (Grady Booch)

article_ideas.angle: Argue that engineering teams misdiagnose interoperability failures as storage or volume problems when the real fix is a shared formal semantic layer; illustrate with agent tool/schema integration.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, data architects, and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: The interoperability problem is architectural, not storage-related
article_ideas.thesis: The cost of big data interoperability is architectural, not volumetric; investing in a shared machine-interpretable semantic layer collapses N^2 point-to-point mappings into a single contract, and any agent system integrating heterogeneous sources should do the same.
article_ideas.title: The Semantic Layer Is the Integration Layer: Why N^2 Mappings Fail
article_ideas.video_title: How to Do Things with Ontologies

article_ideas.angle: Invert the common practice of agreeing on concept labels for shared schemas, memory keys, and tool contracts; propose environment-referent grounding as a design discipline.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers, knowledge engineers, and multi-agent system designers
article_ideas.based_on: definitions should be anchored to the world (referents) rather than to human concepts
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent and multi-team systems should anchor shared identifiers in observable environment state rather than negotiated concept labels, because words-to-concepts pathways produce divergent definitions while world-to-words pathways keep independent parties coordinated.
article_ideas.title: Grounding Shared Vocabularies in the World, Not in Concepts
article_ideas.video_title: How to Do Things with Ontologies

article_ideas.angle: Test the counterintuitive claim that lacking domain depth is an asset for reconciliation; discuss implications for agent role assignment and organizational design.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, ontology practitioners, and AI team leads
article_ideas.based_on: Assign cross-domain semantic reconciliation to a domain-neutral arbiter
article_ideas.thesis: Delegating schema and definition merging to the deepest domain expert produces worse cross-domain interoperability than assigning it to a domain-neutral arbiter (human or LLM agent), because domain commitment introduces bias; organizations should explicitly design for neutrality.
article_ideas.title: The Neutral Arbiter: Why Cross-Domain Reconciliation Needs a Domain-Neutral Party
article_ideas.video_title: How to Do Things with Ontologies

article_ideas.angle: Translate the ontology distinction between continuants and realizable entities into a concrete pattern for agent capability registries and permission models.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework developers and AI architects
article_ideas.based_on: capabilities and roles are modeled as first-class entities
article_ideas.thesis: Representing latent capabilities and roles as first-class typed entities attached to substrates, rather than as boolean state flags, enables planners to reason about potential behavior independent of activation state, improving agent planning correctness.
article_ideas.title: Modeling Capabilities as Realizable Entities: A Better Pattern for Agent Tool Registries
article_ideas.video_title: How to Do Things with Ontologies

article_ideas.angle: Architecture teardown: take a typical single-orchestrator harness, map its observed failure classes onto the VSM functions it conflates, then show what a two-component split (coordination vs. management) buys you in diagnosis.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building multi-agent runtimes
article_ideas.based_on: System Two provides coordination to prevent operational friction.
article_ideas.thesis: The single-planner agent pattern silently merges deconfliction, resource bargaining, and delivery monitoring. Splitting them is not bureaucracy — it is failure attribution, because oscillation and overspend are different bugs that deserve different components and different fixes.
article_ideas.title: Your Orchestrator Is Three Jobs Wearing One Hat
article_ideas.video_title: Demystifying the Viable System Model: A Practical Approach

article_ideas.angle: Design-budget argument anchored on the goalkeeper analogy: each observed failure is diagnosable either as response-variety shortfall or as over-attenuation that discarded the signal needed to act.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform designers and evaluation engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Only variety can absorb variety.
article_ideas.thesis: Requisite variety converts agent capability into an accounting problem: you either pay for response options (tools, retries, escalation paths) or you pay for attenuation (routing, classification, compression). Every architecture change moves one side of that ledger, and you should always be able to say which.
article_ideas.title: Variety Is a Budget, Not a Vibe
article_ideas.video_title: Demystifying the Viable System Model: A Practical Approach

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian take on peer-to-peer and swarm architectures, arguing from information-flow ownership rather than from hierarchy.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent systems architects
article_ideas.based_on: Organizations need functional 'rooms' for management activities even if they reject traditional hierarchical roles.
article_ideas.thesis: Rejecting a designated orchestrator does not delete coordination, resource bargaining, or purpose alignment. It only makes them emergent and unobservable. Flat and peer topologies must instantiate those functions as explicit protocols, shared state, or scheduled jobs, or they will reappear as behavior nobody owns and nobody can debug.
article_ideas.title: Flat Agents Still Need Management Rooms
article_ideas.video_title: Demystifying the Viable System Model: A Practical Approach

article_ideas.angle: Methodology piece on using conceptual models as review checklists and diagnostic prompts rather than deployment plans, with a concrete example of a diagram-driven design that fails.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers and engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: Models are tools to help us think and generate ideas, not absolute physical truths.
article_ideas.thesis: Frameworks like VSM are hypothesis generators, not runtime topologies. Encoding box boundaries into class hierarchies produces brittleness built around distinctions with no observable referent; the artifacts worth instrumenting are information flows and bottlenecks.
article_ideas.title: The Map Is Not the Terrain: Don't Ship Your Architecture Diagram
article_ideas.video_title: Demystifying the Viable System Model: A Practical Approach

article_ideas.angle: Attack the default top-k successful-trajectory design in agent memory, using the 'do not fight the last war' failure mode as the framing and proposing stored successes be demoted from plans to hypotheses with explicit validity conditions.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework engineers and applied ML practitioners building memory and retrieval layers
article_ideas.based_on: Do not fight the last war
article_ideas.thesis: Trajectory retrieval over successful past runs is not a neutral accelerator; it is an overfitting mechanism that fails hardest exactly when the environment shifts, so memory pipelines need a staleness/shift detector and a re-derivation step before any prior plan is treated as executable.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Memory Is a Playbook From the Last War
article_ideas.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the reactive-vs-deliberative debate as an interface specification problem, and connect the Athena/Ares coexistence to an explicit arbitration router with a stated criterion for when deliberation is worth its latency.
article_ideas.audience: AI systems architects and agent-runtime designers
article_ideas.based_on: Tactics alone leads to 'tactical hell'
article_ideas.thesis: Agents that thrash on local signals do not need smarter per-step reasoning, they need a separate abstraction tier that consumes a compressed world state and rewrites goals; the design problem therefore moves to the tier boundary — what crosses upward and how often objectives are rewritten.
article_ideas.title: Tactical Hell Is an Architecture Bug, Not a Reasoning Bug
article_ideas.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk

article_ideas.angle: Use the Tet Offensive level-shift to argue that eval harnesses need explicit metric-to-objective mapping, and derive concrete consequences for routing, critique and self-critique loops.
article_ideas.audience: Eval engineers, reliability teams, and researchers in agent evaluation
article_ideas.based_on: tactical defeat that became a strategic victory
article_ideas.thesis: Because a tactical defeat can be a strategic victory, self-improvement loops driven only by local success signals can invert true performance; evaluation must be a hierarchy with an independently measured governing objective, which means agents cannot be safely self-improved using their own local success signal.
article_ideas.title: Stop Scoring Your Agent on Tactical Metrics
article_ideas.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk

article_ideas.angle: Unify sycophancy literature with the strategy framing of wishful thinking, and propose an architectural check that the world model is not the desired-world model.
article_ideas.audience: Alignment and evaluation researchers and product engineers shipping principal-facing LLM features
article_ideas.based_on: what one wants to see rather than reality
article_ideas.thesis: Optimization toward what the principal wants to hear and the strategist's emotion-driven modeling of a desired reality are the same mechanical failure: neither is a motivational defect, both substitute a preferred model for the actual one, and both require a feedback channel deliberately decoupled from the principal's desires.
article_ideas.title: The Sycophancy Bug Is an Objective-Corruption Bug
article_ideas.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk

article_ideas.angle: Translate the systems-thinking concept of boundary judgment into a concrete engineering artifact: a scope manifest listing included and excluded data, tools, signals, and stakeholders with rationale, plus change control that re-runs affected evals on scope diff.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, agent runtime authors, evaluation and reliability leads
article_ideas.based_on: Boundary definition is itself the primary design act
article_ideas.thesis: In agentic systems the boundary is the context window, tool surface, memory scope, and telemetry coverage, and because these are set by defaults rather than chosen deliberately, agent reliability work begins with making scope an explicit, reviewable, diffable artifact rather than a byproduct of implementation.
article_ideas.title: Your Context Window Is a Boundary Judgment You Never Made
article_ideas.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023

article_ideas.angle: Reframe agent debugging as interaction-graph forensics: define measurable interaction properties, show where per-component scores are blind, and argue that attribution must start at the coupling.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework developers, SRE/observability engineers, AI engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: attribute-first debugging should start at the coupling between parts rather than inside them
article_ideas.thesis: If system-level behavior is generated by interactions rather than parts, then swapping models, rewriting prompts, and tuning tools are component-level fixes applied to an interaction-level defect, which is why teams that instrument handoffs, message schemas, and routing topology resolve failures faster than teams that instrument components.
article_ideas.title: Debug the Coupling, Not the Component
article_ideas.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023

article_ideas.angle: Argue for a selection rubric over a universal harness, with the cost model (complexity, budget, stakeholder plurality) made explicit and auditable rather than left as a judgment call.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation practitioners, product and research leadership, applied AI architects
article_ideas.based_on: There is no universal method.
article_ideas.thesis: Committing to a single evaluation formalism for all task classes is a category error: computable, measurable dynamics justify simulation and quantitative modeling, while value-contested ambiguity justifies structured elicitation and viewpoint reconciliation, and applying one regime to both yields unfalsifiable narrative or models that ignore the real conflict.
article_ideas.title: One Harness to Rule Them All Is a Category Error
article_ideas.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023

article_ideas.angle: Turn stakeholder-inclusion critique into a concrete design-time checklist: enumerate downstream consumers, data subjects, and operators excluded from the eval set, then pre-register failure hypotheses against them.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety and trust engineers, product owners of deployed models, requirements analysts
article_ideas.based_on: the affected-but-excluded set
article_ideas.thesis: Every deployed AI boundary creates a population that is affected but unrepresented, and that population is exactly the source of surprise failures and incident reports, so surfacing it at design time is a requirements-elicitation and safety practice rather than an ethics afterthought.
article_ideas.title: Who Is Outside Your Boundary? The Affected-but-Excluded Population as an Incident Backlog
article_ideas.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023

article_ideas.angle: Apply deep vs. shallow classes to tool schemas; argue classitis in tool inventories is a primary cause of agent confusion and missed tasks.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent developers, API designers
article_ideas.based_on: interface complexity is the cost and the useful functionality hidden behind it is the benefit
article_ideas.thesis: Agent tool design should be judged by the same benefit/cost ratio as software modules: consolidate capabilities into deep tools with minimal schemas, because every exposed parameter consumes model context and increases selection error.
article_ideas.title: The Interface Tax: Why Your Agent Tool Schemas Are Making Your LLM Dumber
article_ideas.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL

article_ideas.angle: Operationalize tacit design review as CI checks and agent self-critique loops, with a benchmark for recall and precision against expert judgment.
article_ideas.audience: DevOps engineers, AI engineers, engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Bad design can be detected with concrete, objective red flags
article_ideas.thesis: The only scalable path to design quality in AI-assisted development is to mechanize the red-flag detectors that human reviewers use, then iterate generation until the detectors are clean.
article_ideas.title: Refactor Until No Red Flags Remain: Automating Design Review for AI-Generated Code
article_ideas.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL

article_ideas.angle: Counter the YAGNI instinct for API design; show how specialized methods bloat schemas and couple caller concepts into the callee.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, API designers, agent platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Designing an abstraction to be general-purpose rather than purpose-specialized usually yields fewer methods, a simpler API, and less information leakage
article_ideas.thesis: Designing abstractions to be general-purpose, even for a single known caller, reduces method count and prevents information leakage—so agent tool APIs should be general operations on general data types, not intent-specific endpoints.
article_ideas.title: General-Purpose Design Is a Simplification Strategy, Not Scope Creep
article_ideas.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL

article_ideas.angle: Connect decomposition independence to multi-agent conflict avoidance; propose decomposition as a first-class design step and evaluation criterion.
article_ideas.audience: CS educators, AI system designers, engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: Problem decomposition — chopping a large problem into relatively independent pieces — is claimed to be the most important concept in computer science
article_ideas.thesis: Problem decomposition into relatively independent pieces is the most important and least taught CS skill; multi-agent systems make its absence visible and costly, so it must be taught and measured explicitly.
article_ideas.title: Teaching Decomposition in the Age of Agents
article_ideas.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL

article_ideas.angle: Contrast current agent-template development with a complexity view borrowed from ant colonies.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers and platform owners building multi-agent products
article_ideas.based_on: Complex systems are defined by interactions between components, not the components themselves
article_ideas.thesis: Most systemic failures in agent platforms will come from the interactions between agents, not from individual prompts or models; therefore engineering rituals, abstractions, and ownership must move to interaction topology, message contracts, and feedback loops.
article_ideas.title: Optimising Agents Is Not Enough: Engineering the Interaction Graph
article_ideas.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving

article_ideas.angle: Challenge single-pipeline evals that conflate forecasting with explanation.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and evaluation leads
article_ideas.based_on: Machine learning acts as a black box that yields prediction without understanding
article_ideas.thesis: An LLM judge or learned regression may predict quality, but it cannot say why; teams must pair black-box prediction with agent-based modelling of interaction rules or they will keep fixing the wrong layer.
article_ideas.title: Prediction Is Not Understanding: Why Agent Eval Needs a Second Model
article_ideas.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving

article_ideas.angle: Read Thomas Schelling's segregation model as a warning for agent collective behaviour.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leaders and multi-agent system designers
article_ideas.based_on: Macro-level outcomes can be far more extreme than micro-level intentions due to emergent interactions.
article_ideas.thesis: Small local preferences for popular tools, formats, or strategies can drive an agent population into far more extreme monoculture and lock-in than any individual intent would suggest, so teams need aggregate guardrails, not just local rules.
article_ideas.title: The Schelling Trap in Agent Teams: Mild Biases Create Extreme Lock-In
article_ideas.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving

article_ideas.angle: Extrapolate forest-fire and sand-pile dynamics to agent incidents.
article_ideas.audience: SREs and reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Large events occur infrequently, while small events occur frequently
article_ideas.thesis: Because agentic failures follow a 'many small, few huge' pattern, SLO engineering based on averages or percentiles leaves teams exposed to the dominant risks; resilience must be designed around tail scenarios and blast-radius isolation.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Platform Is a Fire: Plan for the Rare Huge Cascade
article_ideas.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving

article_ideas.angle: Using system dynamics' reframe of side effects to redesign agent harnesses and evaluators for second-order effects.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and evaluation researchers
article_ideas.based_on: There are no side effects; there are simply effects you have not thought about yet.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent evaluations that ignore downstream state changes will misjudge tool use; every action is an intervention on a closed loop, and treating it as open-loop is a design flaw.
article_ideas.title: There Are No Side Effects: Closing the Loop in Agent Architecture
article_ideas.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
