article_ideas.angle: Applying the 'structure generates behavior' principle to AI agent postmortems, drawing on system dynamics.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers and agentic system maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: Structure generates behavior
article_ideas.thesis: Persistent failures in agent systems are symptoms of structure—context visibility, decision rules, and incentives—not just model capability, and postmortems should trace those structures.
article_ideas.title: Stop Blaming the Model: Structural Debugging for Persistent Agent Failures
article_ideas.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World

article_ideas.angle: Stock-and-flow modeling as a normative framework for context and memory management in LLM agents.
article_ideas.audience: Agent architects and LLM application developers
article_ideas.based_on: A stock is anything that accumulates over time and has memory.
article_ideas.thesis: Context and memory in long-running agents should be treated as a stock with explicit inflow and outflow policies, not an append-only log, to bound growth and preserve salient information.
article_ideas.title: The Context Window Is a Stock: Rethinking Memory as a Flow-Controlled Reservoir
article_ideas.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World

article_ideas.angle: Modeling agent thrashing as a classic control-theoretic overshoot caused by hidden delays, with design patterns for damping.
article_ideas.audience: Robotics, multi-agent systems, and automation engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Failing to account for delays leads to overshooting and policy resistance
article_ideas.thesis: Agents that act faster than they can observe the effects of their actions will destabilize; delay-aware control is an architectural requirement for robust autonomy.
article_ideas.title: When Agents Overshoot: Delay-Driven Oscillation in Autonomous Loops
article_ideas.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World

article_ideas.angle: Use the continuous-flow-versus-discrete-event argument from system dynamics as a counterexample to the fidelity-maximization instinct in agent observability and evaluation design.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and evaluation designers
article_ideas.based_on: Continuous flow approximation works extremely well in queuing applications
article_ideas.thesis: Defaulting to the finest available representation (per-event, per-token, per-entity) is an unexamined assumption; representation granularity should be selected to minimize decision-relevant error against measurement noise, which sometimes means choosing the coarser model deliberately.
article_ideas.title: Granularity Is a Parameter, Not a Virtue: Choosing Representation by Decision Error
article_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski

article_ideas.angle: Map automatic unit control and outside-in build order onto typed tool contracts and interface-first scaffolding of agent workflow graphs, and quantify what changes when inheritance replaces boundary validation.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework and tooling architects
article_ideas.based_on: Enables unit inheritance, model transparency, and clear identification of policy variables
article_ideas.thesis: Declaring a contract once and letting every downstream artifact inherit it structurally is a different class of guarantee than re-validating types at each hop, because the failure it prevents is silent integration drift rather than isolated malformed output.
article_ideas.title: Unit Checks Are an Architecture, Not a Lint Rule
article_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski

article_ideas.angle: Reframe memory correctness as a substrate property — argue that without enforced separation, cross-contamination defects surface late or never, and review discipline cannot compensate.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers building agent memory and retrieval systems
article_ideas.based_on: Spreadsheets lack clear input/output separation
article_ideas.thesis: The reason spreadsheets produce invisible blunders is not formula complexity but the absence of an enforced boundary between inputs and derived state; agent context and memory systems inherit that same blindness, so separating read and write paths is an architectural reliability decision, not a code-style preference.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Memory Has the Spreadsheet Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski

article_ideas.angle: Take the standard-following practitioner who fails on intent as the canonical failure, then map it onto agent pipelines that pass workflow checks while missing user goals, and argue for splitting intent elicitation out as a scored gate preceding solution work.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation engineers, agent platform architects, systems engineering leads
article_ideas.based_on: George follows standards meticulously but fails because he cannot understand what the customer really wants.
article_ideas.thesis: Evaluation harnesses and lifecycle standards that score procedural conformance can certify systems that never understood the situation; front-end problem formulation must be a measured stage with its own intent-alignment score, or process-compliance becomes a false quality signal.
article_ideas.title: Process Conformance Is Not Intent Alignment: Why Passing Every Step Still Fails the User
article_ideas.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering

article_ideas.angle: Treat per-component KPI tuning — accuracy, latency, token budget — as an anti-pattern, show why emergent global behavior is an unchecked side effect of local tuning, and specify the instrumentation needed to score components against end-to-end outcomes.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework builders, MLOps and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Optimizing subsystems independently does not lead to a system optimum
article_ideas.thesis: Independently tuning each agent or tool against its own metric converges to a local optimum that can be worse than the untuned whole; the system-level objective must be the single optimization target and component metrics must be derived from it, not optimized alongside it.
article_ideas.title: The Optimization Paradox in Decomposed AI Pipelines: When Tuning Every Agent Makes the System Worse
article_ideas.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering

article_ideas.angle: Contrast diagnostic decomposition with generative context modeling, and show why agent systems that reuse their debugging decomposition for planning produce plan sets that never include the missing environmental interaction.
article_ideas.audience: Systems architects, agent planning researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Conventional thinking does not explain where solutions come from.
article_ideas.thesis: Decomposition is a diagnostic tool for explaining and debugging existing behavior, but it does not tell you where solutions come from; generating candidate solutions requires modeling the whole system in its environment and its interactions with adjacent systems, so debugging and planning deserve separate architectures.
article_ideas.title: Decomposition Explains, Context Generates: Splitting Analysis From Solution Finding
article_ideas.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering

article_ideas.angle: Convert Miller's Rule into numbers for tool schemas, sub-agent interface descriptions, and context packing, and confront the cost: what fails below a hidden boundary is invisible to review conducted at that level.
article_ideas.audience: Tool/API designers, prompt and context engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Partitioning a complex diagram into six systems and hiding internal details to reduce complexity.
article_ideas.thesis: If abstraction boundaries are sized to a consumer's working-memory limit and recursively reapplied, then interface surfaces should expose on the order of six to seven elements with internals hidden — a concrete, testable design budget rather than a vague call to manage complexity.
article_ideas.title: Size Your Interfaces to Seven: Chunking as an Engineering Budget for Tool Schemas and Context
article_ideas.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering

article_ideas.angle: A critique of component-level eval culture with a practical mandate for whole-session telemetry and global failure-mode tracking.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: systemic properties only appear at the system level
article_ideas.thesis: Because systemic properties only emerge from interactions, any agent evaluation that averages component scores will mislead you; the primary quality gate must be whole-system scenarios and measured emergent outcomes.
article_ideas.title: Systemic Metrics Before Micro-Optimization: Why Your Agent Benchmarks Are Lying
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

article_ideas.angle: Applying management cybernetics to software architecture.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and agent framework designers
article_ideas.based_on: Identified five necessary functions: System 5 (policy/identity), System 4 (intelligence/environment), System 3 (control/overview), System 2 (stability/coordination), and System 1 (sub-systems/operations).
article_ideas.thesis: Long-lived agent systems should separate operations, coordination, control, intelligence, and policy into distinct subsystems rather than stuffing all functions into one orchestration loop, because viability requires structural variety.
article_ideas.title: Does Your Agent Company Have Five Systems? Architecting Autonomous Agents with Beer's Viable System Model
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

article_ideas.angle: Making problem structuring methods (PSMs) concrete for AI product designers.
article_ideas.audience: AI product managers, conversation designers, planning-system engineers
article_ideas.based_on: PSMs offer a way of representing situations to enable participants to clarify predicaments, converge on actionable issues, and agree on commitments.
article_ideas.thesis: When tasks are messy or multi-stakeholder, an agent should produce a shared representation of the situation before any proposed solution; problem structuring is productive work, not an interaction tax.
article_ideas.title: Structure First, Solve Second: The Soft OR Phase Your Agent Is Missing
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

article_ideas.angle: Linking AI ethics to architecture through boundary judgements.
article_ideas.audience: AI governance, platform engineering, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: How we draw the line between the system and the environment is a matter of judgement.
article_ideas.thesis: The boundary of an agent's context, tools, and permissions is a subjective judgement that determines whose interests it serves; hiding that boundary in implementation makes it no less value-laden and far less accountable.
article_ideas.title: What Your Agent Can't See Is a Political Decision
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

article_ideas.angle: Argues that the four-valued answer expansion from systems thinking is a practical fix for hallucinated decisions in LLM pipelines.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent developers, eval designers
article_ideas.based_on: graded and multi-valued rather than binary
article_ideas.thesis: Agent output contracts should adopt graded and indeterminate outcomes (optimal/acceptable/unacceptable plus 'it depends'/'don't know') because binary schemas manufacture false confidence on genuinely ambiguous inputs.
article_ideas.title: Stop Forcing Binary Verdicts on Ambiguous Agent Outputs
article_ideas.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

article_ideas.angle: Applies the undesirable-situation vs problem distinction to agent observability and root-cause analysis.
article_ideas.audience: SREs, AI ops engineers, agent architects
article_ideas.based_on: observed 'undesirable situation' is not the same as the problem definition
article_ideas.thesis: Treating an observed error as the problem definition is a named failure mode; pipelines must record observed state and hypothesized cause as distinct artifacts to avoid misdirected remediation.
article_ideas.title: The Symptom Is Not the Problem: Separating Observation from Diagnosis in Agent Pipelines
article_ideas.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

article_ideas.angle: Argues for decoupling combinatorial ideation from the durable context schema that downstream stages consume.
article_ideas.audience: Prompt engineers, context designers, eval authors
article_ideas.based_on: input (generation) tool, not a storage (record) tool
article_ideas.thesis: Perspective enumeration (like HTP) is a sparse generation-time tool, not a persistent schema; conflating them leads to wasted effort filling irrelevant cells and false confidence in filled coverage.
article_ideas.title: Checklists Are for Generation, Not Storage: Rethinking Enumeration in LLM Context Gathering
article_ideas.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

article_ideas.angle: Turns the critical-analysis template into an automated reviewer that names hidden assumptions and terminology drift.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers, red teamers, reasoning auditors
article_ideas.based_on: unstated premises are the specific, extractable failure surface
article_ideas.thesis: Unstated premises are the primary manipulation and error surface in generated arguments; automated extraction of hidden assumptions should be a standard review step for LLM outputs.
article_ideas.title: The Hidden Premise Problem: Automating Critical Analysis of LLM-Generated Arguments
article_ideas.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

article_ideas.angle: Apply aircraft systems engineering verifiability discipline to agent task descriptions and tool contracts, with a proposed admission gate.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent developers, eval engineers
article_ideas.based_on: 99% of all requirements we see right now in most of our system designs are not verifiable
article_ideas.thesis: The dominant defect in agent specifications is not incompleteness but unverifiability; teams should reject any agent task description, tool contract, or eval rubric at authoring time unless it has a concrete verification method, because unverifiable specs are latent defects that surface only as silent non-compliance.
article_ideas.title: Verifiability Is the Only Requirement That Matters: Gating Agent Specs Before They Ship
article_ideas.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019

article_ideas.angle: Map aircraft decomposition from Level 1 aircraft functions to Level 6 PLD design onto agent components such as orchestrator, policy, tool contract, prompt, and model call.
article_ideas.audience: software architects, AI platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Every tier must have direct/allocated and derived requirements
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic systems should enforce a fixed tier ladder with both allocated and derived requirements at each tier, because emergent behaviors without provenance are exactly the ones that cannot be audited or regressed; traceability becomes a structural property of the layer stack rather than a documentation chore.
article_ideas.title: The Six-Tier Agent: Why Agentic Architectures Need Fixed Abstraction Ladders
article_ideas.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019

article_ideas.angle: Apply the aircraft anti-pattern of writing top-level requirements with exact resistor values to agent prompt engineering and orchestration design.
article_ideas.audience: prompt engineers, agent developers, technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: Detailed design parameters like resistor values belong several tiers down
article_ideas.thesis: Over-specification at the wrong abstraction tier—pinning model names, token budgets, or tool arguments in high-level orchestrator prompts—destroys flexibility and couples top-level intent to volatile implementation detail; each tier should specify only what its consumers need.
article_ideas.title: Don't Hard-Code the Resistor in the Orchestrator: Tier Discipline for Agent Prompts
article_ideas.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019

article_ideas.angle: Use the sum-of-all-testing-must-provide-complete-coverage claim to critique benchmark-centric eval and propose a coverage-partition model.
article_ideas.audience: eval engineers, ML researchers, AI safety practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: The sum of all testing must provide complete coverage
article_ideas.thesis: Agent evaluation should shift from end-to-end benchmark selection to lowest-level unit verification with an explicit argued union-of-coverage, because correctness in agent systems is a composition property and the residual uncovered set at integration boundaries is the real risk.
article_ideas.title: Coverage Is a Composition Problem: Rethinking Agent Evals as Tier-Level Verification
article_ideas.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019

article_ideas.angle: Use the Tibetan tradition's survival through diaspora centers despite destroyed libraries to argue that agent artifacts are less durable than distributed procedures.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure engineers, MLOps, continuity planners
article_ideas.based_on: replicate the procedure across independent operating sites, not just the artifact in one canonical store
article_ideas.thesis: Durability of critical agent capabilities depends more on distributing executable procedures across independent operators than on canonical artifact stores with backup/restore, so continuity planning must shift from backup frequency to replication topology and procedural re-derivation.
article_ideas.title: Your Backup Strategy Won't Save Your AI Capability: Replication Topology Does
article_ideas.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film

article_ideas.angle: Apply the yogic distinction between measurable substrate effects and unverifiable internal claims to agent evaluation design.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation researchers, agent reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: classify it as instrumentable or testimonial
article_ideas.thesis: Claims about model internal states should be classified as instrumentable or testimonial, and only instrumentable signals (like measurable body heat in Tumo) belong in automated evaluations; self-reports are weak evidence.
article_ideas.title: From Self-Report to Substrate Telemetry: Evaluating Internal States in AI Agents
article_ideas.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film

article_ideas.angle: Argue that capability gating is an architectural concern separate from capability availability, using the tantric module precedent.
article_ideas.audience: AI security architects, agent platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Design capability packs as versioned, individually nameable modules over a shared substrate, with a separate authorization layer
article_ideas.thesis: Possession of weights, prompts, or tools should not imply capability activation; advanced agent modules must be gated by a separate authorization layer with supervision, as illustrated by the Six Yogas of Naropa requiring retreat and a qualified teacher.
article_ideas.title: The Gate Is Load-Bearing: Why Advanced Agent Capabilities Need Authorization, Not Just Availability
article_ideas.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film

article_ideas.angle: Use the yogic practice of repeating core beliefs to rein in erratic thoughts as a model for agent drift control.
article_ideas.audience: Agent runtime developers, reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Long-running agents should have a scheduled re-anchoring step that re-asserts a short invariant constraint set
article_ideas.thesis: Periodic re-injection of a small invariant instruction set suppresses drift in long-running agents more effectively than expanding context, and this should be a scheduled runtime step evaluated on drift and adaptation metrics.
article_ideas.title: Re-Anchoring Beats Context Stuffing: A Reliability Primitive for Long-Running Agents
article_ideas.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film

article_ideas.angle: Engineering practice and eval design
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, eval and observability teams
article_ideas.based_on: 4 out of every 5 wrong numbers dialed were correct numbers incorrectly dialed
article_ideas.thesis: Most agent improvement efforts optimize the component users blame, but end-to-end tracing shows failures often originate at interfaces or input handling; eval design must begin with a taxonomy of failure origins.
article_ideas.title: Stop Optimizing the Wrong Component: Failure Attribution as the First Eval Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Architecture design review and process
article_ideas.audience: Software architects and AI product leads
article_ideas.based_on: must be technologically feasible (no science fiction) and operationally viable
article_ideas.thesis: Greenfield agent redesigns should be constrained by exactly two filters—technological feasibility and operational viability—otherwise they produce either unbuildable science fiction or undeployable systems.
article_ideas.title: Two Gates for Ambitious Agent Architecture: Feasibility and Viability
article_ideas.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Eval methodology and systems thinking
article_ideas.audience: ML platform and evaluation engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Improving individual parts of a system does not necessarily improve the performance of the system as a whole.
article_ideas.thesis: Component-level benchmarks do not compose into system-level performance; architecture and interaction boundaries must be evaluated at the system boundary, and part-level optimization can be misleading.
article_ideas.title: Your System Is Not the Sum of Its Benchmarks
article_ideas.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Technical debt and design process
article_ideas.audience: Technical leads and system architects
article_ideas.based_on: Elimination of legacy assumptions
article_ideas.thesis: When redesigning AI systems, inherited constraints such as compatibility, prior prompts, and existing interfaces should be explicitly inventoried and re-admitted only if they pass feasibility and viability gates.
article_ideas.title: Legacy Assumptions Are Undeclared Constraints in AI Redesign
article_ideas.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Take the systems claim that disassembly destroys essential properties in both the whole and the parts and turn it into an engineering indictment of the current agent-eval stack, with concrete guidance on interaction ablations.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and eval practitioners shipping multi-agent and tool-using systems
article_ideas.based_on: When the whole is disassembled, it loses its essential properties, as do all of its parts.
article_ideas.thesis: Component-level agent and tool benchmarks are invalid by construction for capability claims, because the properties being claimed only exist in composition; evaluations must move to the interaction level, and any component score should be reported as relative to a specific composition rather than as an intrinsic property.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Benchmark Is Measuring Parts of a System That Doesn't Exist
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Use the elevator-and-mirrors case as the canonical pattern: change the environment and the incentive rather than the mechanism being complained about.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leads, platform architects and product managers owning agent reliability
article_ideas.based_on: Dissolution involves redesigning the system so that the problem no longer exists
article_ideas.thesis: Most agent reliability work is symptom patching at the model or prompt layer, but the highest-leverage move is redesigning the task or interface so the failure class cannot occur; teams should triage failures by recurrence and structural eliminability and route dissolution-class failures upward, accepting that the fix is a product decision, not a model decision.
article_ideas.title: Dissolve, Don't Debug: Rerouting Recurring Agent Failures to the Architecture Layer
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Invert the standard retrieval metric: show why a smaller, higher-tier context can beat a larger low-tier one, and reframe summarization and distillation layers as first-class architecture rather than cost-saving afterthoughts.
article_ideas.audience: Context-engineering and RAG engineers, memory-systems builders
article_ideas.based_on: An ounce of information is worth a pound of data; knowledge is worth information
article_ideas.thesis: Agent context is allocated by availability when it should be allocated by value: raw retrieved data is the cheapest and least valuable tier, so context and memory pipelines should be evaluated on the tier of content they surface and should spend budget on distillation before spending it on recall.
article_ideas.title: Data Is Cheap, Understanding Is Expensive: Budgeting Context by Value Tier
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Reframe prompt engineering as an instruction-density tradeoff, and argue that agent improvement budgets should shift toward environment and feedback-loop design.
article_ideas.audience: Agent builders and researchers designing self-improving or iterative systems
article_ideas.based_on: Teaching is a major obstruction to learning; the ideal school has no teaching, but a lot of learning.
article_ideas.thesis: Dense instruction is fast to author but can crowd out the experiential acquisition it is meant to produce; for open-ended capability building, feedback-rich environments and self-directed iteration should carry the load, with instructions used as scaffolding rather than prescription.
article_ideas.title: Prompting Is Teaching, and Teaching Obstructs Learning
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Use Senge's critique of control-based schooling as a lens to analyze benchmark-driven AI development, then propose diagnostic feedback mechanisms.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers, evaluation designers, ML engineers
article_ideas.based_on: described as control rather than learning
article_ideas.thesis: When evaluation signals become the primary control surface, agents optimize for approval rather than competence, mirroring industrial-age schooling; to avoid this, we need diagnostic feedback that detects divergence between proxy score and held-out capability.
article_ideas.title: Control is Not Learning: How Proxy Metrics Crowd Out Competence in AI
article_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline

article_ideas.angle: Draw a parallel between organizational culture and agent priors, then outline a systematic audit process for surfacing hidden assumptions.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent developers, technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: Culture is defined as the assumptions members cannot see
article_ideas.thesis: In agent systems, implicit assumptions in prompts, tool schemas, and reward rubrics function as culture does in organizations—unseen yet determinative—and making them explicit, inspectable artifacts is a prerequisite for reliable behavioral change.
article_ideas.title: The Invisible Priors Problem: Auditing the Culture of Your Agent
article_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline

article_ideas.angle: Case study of Visa's governance, extracting design principles for multi-agent systems, with trade-offs between innovation and consistency.
article_ideas.audience: Distributed systems architects, multi-agent researchers, platform designers
article_ideas.based_on: Visa International is presented as an existence proof that a radical, democratic, decentralized governance design can operate at very large scale
article_ideas.thesis: Visa's intentional decentralized governance demonstrates that distributing authority can be a deliberate anti-concentration mechanism at scale; for multi-agent systems, this implies designing topologies that prevent single points of control to preserve innovation and local initiative.
article_ideas.title: Decentralization by Design: Lessons from Visa for Multi-Agent Governance
article_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline

article_ideas.angle: Translate the Just-In-Time manufacturing principle to AI evaluation pipelines, using NeXT's no-warehouse factory as the origin story and prescribing concrete latency targets.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, MLOps practitioners, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: removing the buffer (true JIT, no warehouse) forces defects to surface immediately
article_ideas.thesis: In AI systems, any queue, batch, or review backlog between generation and evaluation functions like inventory in manufacturing—it hides defects until they are expensive to attribute. The highest-leverage reliability improvement is not better models but shorter artifact-to-detection loops.
article_ideas.title: The Buffer Is the Bug: Why Detection Latency Is Your Real Reliability Metric
article_ideas.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech

article_ideas.angle: Contrast NeXT's 80%-fewer-lines claim with modern agent frameworks, proposing a concrete benchmark and arguing that platform vendors should report authored surface area.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, framework builders, engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: the leverage is in the number of components not rewritten
article_ideas.thesis: The value of an agent framework or tool platform should be measured by the fraction of implementation the builder does not have to author, not by developer experience alone. Frameworks that maximize reuse of pre-built components deliver step-change speedups; those that only make authoring pleasant deliver incremental gains.
article_ideas.title: Measure What You Don't Write: Authored Surface Area as the Platform Metric
article_ideas.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech

article_ideas.angle: Use Jobs' hardware-versus-software replication lag argument as a lens for AI stack investment decisions, with a decision framework for startups.
article_ideas.audience: Startup founders, investors, product strategists
article_ideas.based_on: Advantage is a function of time-to-copy
article_ideas.thesis: Durable competitive advantage accrues to the layer with the longest replication lag, not the layer that improves fastest. Invest in data, evaluation harnesses, and workflow integration—not models or hardware—because those are the layers competitors cannot copy quickly.
article_ideas.title: Time-to-Copy: The Only Moat Metric That Matters
article_ideas.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech

article_ideas.angle: Revisit Strassmann's research with AI budget categories, arguing that 'if an operational process has no application, the product does not exist.'
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, CIOs, AI product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Mission-critical custom applications, not generic tooling, carry the value
article_ideas.thesis: The operational versus management productivity spending split still separates successful from unsuccessful organizations, and it will hold for AI spend: value accrues to embedded, workflow-specific systems that execute core operations, not to general-purpose assistant tooling.
article_ideas.title: Where AI Budget Lands Predicts Who Wins
article_ideas.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech

article_ideas.angle: Take the automobile-disassembly claim literally and apply it to prompt suites, tool unit tests, and per-model benchmarks; show where each sits relative to the boundary of the property it claims to report.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: When you take a system apart, it loses its essential properties
article_ideas.thesis: Component-level evaluation of agent systems does not under-measure capability, it measures a different object: essential properties are destroyed by disassembly, so part-level scores are upper bounds on whole-system behavior rather than estimates of it. Evaluation scope must match the scope of the behavior under question.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Evals Measure Something That Does Not Exist
article_ideas.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking

article_ideas.angle: Contract the two procedures by their outputs, then specify the metadata an execution record needs to serve synthesis rather than only analysis.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects and observability tooling teams
article_ideas.based_on: Analysis reveals structure and how a system works; synthesis reveals why it works the way it does.
article_ideas.thesis: Modern agent observability is almost entirely analytic — spans, call graphs, task DAGs — which answers how execution happened and supports local patching. Without a synthesis representation locating the system in its containing objective, the same failures recur because the explanatory layer is absent. Observability artifacts must carry role and intent, not just order.
article_ideas.title: Analysis Gives You Traces; Synthesis Gives You Reasons
article_ideas.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking

article_ideas.angle: Use the machine/organism/social-system taxonomy as a classification step performed before choosing a coordination mechanism, with the coordination choice falling out of the classification.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent system designers and AI alignment practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Social systems (corporations, hospitals) are made of purposeful parts (people) with their own wills
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent systems built from models pursuing their own objectives are social systems, not machines. Command dispatch plus retries assumes functional parts, so it mispredicts behavior; the correct layer is explicit representation of each component's objective and a mechanism for resolving objective conflicts.
article_ideas.title: Your Agents Are Not a Machine: Purposeful Parts Break Command-and-Control
article_ideas.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking

article_ideas.angle: Treat granularity as a design axis with a measurable price rather than a default, and describe the failure signature that reveals when the tax has been paid.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leads and workflow/agent product teams
article_ideas.based_on: Taylor's work analysis reduced tasks to elementary tasks for mechanization.
article_ideas.thesis: Atomizing workflows into minimal interchangeable tool calls buys reproducibility, parallelism, and per-step measurement, and charges for it in purpose representation. This is the same move Taylor made on manual work, with the same signature: strong step-level performance, degradation on open-ended tasks.
article_ideas.title: The Atomization Tax: What Step Granularity Costs Agent Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking

article_ideas.angle: Take four engineering resources — context budget, provider quota, vector index freshness, human review bandwidth — classify each on the delay/erodability grid, and show where standard control tuning is the wrong lever; include the recovery-curve asymmetry argument as the falsifiable core.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure and platform engineers, SREs operating agent systems
article_ideas.based_on: whether the limit (carrying capacity) is erodable, and whether the corrective feedback responds with delay
article_ideas.thesis: The determinative question for any constrained system is not how fast the corrective loop reacts but whether the limit being consumed is erodable: delay against a fixed limit yields recoverable oscillation, while the same delay against an erodable limit converts temporary overshoot into permanent capacity loss, which means reaction-speed fixes (retries, backoff, autoscaling, better throttling) are structurally incapable of saving collapse-mode resources and effort must move to reserved margin and hard caps.
article_ideas.title: You Cannot Throttle Your Way Out of a Collapse-Mode System
article_ideas.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse

article_ideas.angle: Reframe guardrail cost debates as loop-accounting: for each dominant positive loop in an agent pipeline, name the loop that counterweights it and show what happens qualitatively (not just quantitatively) when it is removed or made probabilistic.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects, engineering managers making cost/latency tradeoff calls
article_ideas.based_on: Removing a single balancing (negative) feedback loop converts a stable equilibrium into a dominating positive feedback loop
article_ideas.thesis: Verification steps, critics, rate limits, and approval gates are balancing loops whose removal is not a performance optimization but a qualitative change in system behavior mode, because exponential and runway behavior requires a dominating positive loop with no counterweight; therefore each dominant compounding loop needs at least one independent, cheap brake that survives cost and latency budget cuts, even if it is a heuristic sensor rather than a full model.
article_ideas.title: Every Guardrail Is a Balancing Loop You Are About to Delete for Latency
article_ideas.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse

article_ideas.angle: Argue against black-box answer emission as a product design choice, and specify what a counterfactual-first interface and a calibration-scored eval harness would look like in practice.
article_ideas.audience: AI product designers, eval and ML platform teams, decision-support tool builders
article_ideas.based_on: The stated purpose of building computer models is to refine the operator's mental model
article_ideas.thesis: If the purpose of a decision-support model is to refine the operator's mental model until the model becomes unnecessary, then answer accuracy is the wrong success metric and interfaces that emit only verdicts are failing at their actual job; the deliverable should be causal structure, dominant loops, and counterfactual runs, evaluated by whether the operator's predictions about the system improve and their dependence on the tool declines.
article_ideas.title: Your Model Should Be Trying to Put Itself Out of Business
article_ideas.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse

article_ideas.angle: Architectural argument for separating memory/state stores from stateless policy layers in agent runtimes, with concrete examples of how entanglement causes failures.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and architects building agent frameworks
article_ideas.based_on: Every system reduces to exactly two concept types
article_ideas.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series
article_ideas.thesis: Agent architectures that entangle state accumulation with decision policy are structurally unauditable; the level/rate decomposition from system dynamics provides a principled boundary that makes agents replayable, diffable, and statically checkable. Separating accumulators from policies is a hard architectural requirement, not a metaphor.
article_ideas.title: The Level/Rate Split: Why Agent State and Agent Policy Must Be Separate Layers
article_ideas.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode analysis of reward drift and benchmark erosion in agent systems, with a concrete architectural remedy grounded in system dynamics.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, AI safety researchers, and engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: When organizations fail to meet absolute goals, pressure forces goals downward
article_ideas.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series
article_ideas.thesis: Autonomous optimizers that use a single adaptive objective will drift toward observed performance, producing monotone degradation disguised as adaptation. The fix is a two-tier goal structure with an immutable acceptance criterion and a separately managed operating target.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Goals Are Eroding: The Hidden Spiral in Long-Horizon Optimization
article_ideas.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester

article_ideas.angle: Reframing latency and queue depth as control-theoretic stability parameters, with implications for agent scheduling and throughput optimization.
article_ideas.audience: Systems engineers, AI infrastructure teams, and SREs
article_ideas.based_on: Large order backlogs feel comfortable initially
article_ideas.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series
article_ideas.thesis: Deep queues and comfortable backlogs in agent pipelines are not signs of health but active degraders of the policy's own effectiveness; latency budgets and admission control should be treated as primary architectural constraints, not tuning knobs.
article_ideas.title: Backlog Is Not Comfort: Delay as a Stability Parameter in Agent Feedback Loops
article_ideas.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester

article_ideas.angle: Critique of context-stuffing and a case for hybrid architectures, with evidence from system dynamics on information pollution.
article_ideas.audience: AI product teams, prompt engineers, and ML practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Mental models hold a rich database of experience but cannot simulate high-order non-linear dynamic systems
article_ideas.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series
article_ideas.thesis: LLMs, like human mental models, cannot simulate high-order non-linear dynamics; feeding them more context does not fix this. Filtering for validity — not just relevance or volume — is the decisive intervention, and hybrid architectures pairing intuitive layers with explicit simulators are the way forward.
article_ideas.title: Context Windows Are Not Mental Models: Why Validity Beats Relevance
article_ideas.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester

article_ideas.angle: Expose the hidden cost of local optima in multi-agent pipelines, supported by Ackoff's automotive analogy and the claim that a system operating optimally may have no part operating optimally.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent framework developers, evaluation researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Improving the performance of parts taken separately does not necessarily improve the whole.
article_ideas.thesis: Optimizing each agent or tool to its own benchmark can actively degrade end-to-end task performance because system-level capability emerges from interactions, not from parts; therefore component leaderboards are misleading signals and evaluation must shift to interaction surfaces and end-to-end traces.
article_ideas.title: The Per-Component Optimization Trap: Why Agent Leaderboards Mislead
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the four modes (absolution, resolution, solving, dissolution) and argue that most agent reliability work is stuck in the lower three, spending recurring effort on problems that redesign would delete.
article_ideas.audience: System architects, reliability engineers, AI engineering leads
article_ideas.based_on: Dissolution — redesigning the system so the problem no longer exists — is a categorically different and higher-order intervention than optimizing a solution inside the existing system.
article_ideas.thesis: Dissolution—redesigning the task, environment, or interface so a failure class becomes unrepresentable—is a higher-order and often cheaper strategy than in-system optimization; agent reliability engineering should treat recurring failures as signals to search for architectural redesigns rather than to improve retries or prompts.
article_ideas.title: Dissolution as an Engineering Discipline: Redesigning Systems So Failures Cannot Occur
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Apply Ackoff's critique of 'divide and conquer' to modern agent stacks, using the automobile-disassembly analogy and the claim that a system cannot be divided into independent parts without losing its essential properties.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, AI system designers, technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: Decomposition boundaries drawn along functional or organizational lines destroy the essential properties of the system
article_ideas.thesis: Drawing abstraction boundaries along functional lines (planner/retriever/writer/verifier) severs exactly the interactions that produce system value; correct boundaries should minimize severed interaction, not maximize module independence, making boundary placement a first-class architectural decision.
article_ideas.title: Boundaries That Break Systems: Why Functional Decomposition Fails in Agent Architectures
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Use Ackoff's hierarchy and the observation that educational systems devote most time to lower tiers to diagnose current RAG and context-engineering practices.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, context engineers, evaluation researchers
article_ideas.based_on: The hierarchy data < information < knowledge < understanding < wisdom orders mental content by increasing value
article_ideas.thesis: Context and memory pipelines that maximize data and information volume while ignoring causal explanation and value-laden judgment are structurally misallocated; evaluation criteria and memory tiers should split along the data–information–knowledge–understanding–wisdom axis to expose and correct this inverse effort allocation.
article_ideas.title: The Knowledge Tier Misallocation: Why AI Systems Need Understanding and Wisdom, Not More Data
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff

article_ideas.angle: Counter-position to context-scaling orthodoxy, arguing for representation-quality evals separated from retrieval evals and showing where the two are conflated in current practice.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent framework builders, evaluation leads
article_ideas.based_on: Lots of information makes us informed, but lots of thinking makes us smart.
article_ideas.thesis: Accumulating retrieved information is cheap and creates the appearance of competence, but the measurable bottleneck in agent systems is the structuring operation applied to context; teams that optimize recall while leaving distinction, relation, and perspective implicit are optimizing the wrong component.
article_ideas.title: Your Context Window Is Not Your Problem: The Structuring Transform as the Real Bottleneck
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab

article_ideas.angle: Schema-design argument with concrete field-level consequences for extraction, memory records, and automated checks for one-sided reasoning.
article_ideas.audience: Knowledge graph and memory-system designers, prompt engineers
article_ideas.based_on: each defined as a complementary pair
article_ideas.thesis: Representation schemas that store only the salient token per item structurally permit one-sided reasoning; requiring the complement field (not-door, whole, reaction, the other's view) turns an omitted inference into a machine-checkable stored value and makes counterfactual prompting a lookup rather than a separate pass.
article_ideas.title: Every Node Needs a Ground: Designing Schemas That Cannot Reason One-Sidedly
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab

article_ideas.angle: Architecture critique of output-centric agent tuning, proposing representation diffs as a release artifact and a debugging primitive.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects, ML reliability engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Mental models determine how we feel and how we act.
article_ideas.thesis: If stored representations causally determine behavior, then output-level filtering and formatting change appearances while leaving the operative model intact; durable behavior change requires a first-class, diffable mental-model layer with representation-level evaluation.
article_ideas.title: The Mental Model Is the Maintenance Surface: Why Output Shaping Masks an Unchanged Agent
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab

article_ideas.angle: Diagnostic framing that converts a pipeline-ordering assumption into a measurable error class with a comparison methodology.
article_ideas.audience: Workflow and orchestration engineers, agent system designers
article_ideas.based_on: These four patterns (Distinctions, Systems, Relationships, Perspectives) happen all together, all the time.
article_ideas.thesis: Staged structuring pipelines commit to entities before relations and to relations before viewpoints, which is correct only if the operators are genuinely sequential; where they co-occur, staged pipelines produce unrecoverable commitment errors, not just latency.
article_ideas.title: Stop Serializing What Happens at Once: Pipeline Commitment Errors in Structuring Workflows
article_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab

article_ideas.angle: Argue that agentic system reliability requires provenance-first instrumentation to make invisible dependencies detectable and attributable.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform architects, observability practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: absence of provenance at the action surface
article_ideas.thesis: The growing gap between interdependence and awareness is best understood as missing provenance at action surfaces; the engineering fix is transitive dependency provenance, not better education or larger models.
article_ideas.title: Systems Ignorance Is an Observability Defect, Not a Knowledge Deficit
article_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014

article_ideas.angle: Critique common agent architecture diagrams and propose event/process modeling as a corrective that changes where responsibilities land.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, agent framework designers
article_ideas.based_on: Components are specified as named objects, which encodes separation.
article_ideas.thesis: Noun-based component diagrams encode artificial separation and hide coupling; process/flow representations expose where retries, backpressure, and shared state actually belong.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Architecture Diagram Is Hiding the Coupling: The Case for Process-First Representations
article_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014

article_ideas.angle: Use the Baja California clam fishery analogy to argue for substrate-first rollouts in multi-agent resource management, treating protocol-first deployments as expected to fail.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, multi-agent system designers, governance researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Coordination substrate was built before the constraint mechanism.
article_ideas.thesis: Deploying quotas or access controls before establishing shared context and visible local benefit leads to evasion; successful governance requires a prior coordination substrate.
article_ideas.title: Build the Soccer Field First: Sequencing Coordination Substrate Before Governance in Multi-Agent Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014

article_ideas.angle: Map project-dynamics rework accounting onto agentic/software delivery: show how 'task marked done', 'tests passing', and LLM self-reported completion act as perceived-progress proxies, why capacity decisions keyed to them plateau prematurely, and what a dual-signal harness looks like.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leads, agent-platform architects, engineering-operations managers
article_ideas.based_on: undiscovered rework is central to the management of complex projects
article_ideas.thesis: Control loops that allocate effort using self-reported or partially verified progress will systematically accumulate hidden rework, and the correct fix is not better estimation but instrumenting perceived and verified progress as two separate stocks with an explicit rework flow back into the work queue.
article_ideas.title: Your Progress Metric Is Lying: Undiscovered Rework in Agentic Pipelines
article_ideas.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson

article_ideas.angle: Argue that short-horizon benchmark wins (added capacity, raised timeouts, more agents, relaxed thresholds) invert in ranking once the compensating loop acts; propose estimating loop time constants by perturbation and benefit-decay curves.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation researchers, platform reliability engineers, engineering leadership
article_ideas.based_on: long-term compensating feedback effects
article_ideas.thesis: Any intervention evaluated on a horizon shorter than the slowest compensating feedback loop it triggers will be ranked by its transient, not its steady state, so evaluation horizon is an architectural parameter that must be derived from the system being measured rather than chosen for convenience.
article_ideas.title: Benchmarks Must Outlive the Feedback Loop
article_ideas.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson

article_ideas.angle: Operational debugging narrative: latency spikes, retry storms, and autoscaler flapping are routinely blamed on traffic; show the spectral-peak diagnostic and contrast smoothing versus loop retuning as interventions.
article_ideas.audience: SREs, platform engineers, control-systems-curious backend developers
article_ideas.based_on: oscillate at its natural frequency
article_ideas.thesis: Oscillatory instability in delayed control loops is excited by noise but produced by structure, so input smoothing dampens symptoms while leaving the natural frequency intact — the correct remediation is identifying and retuning the delay-bearing loop.
article_ideas.title: Stop Smoothing Your Traffic: Noise Doesn't Cause Your Oscillations
article_ideas.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson

article_ideas.angle: Apply Forrester-style endogenous modeling to AI system reliability: attribute failure to retry policies, tool contracts, and context assembly instead of to input variance, and show what changes in what you fix and what you measure.
article_ideas.audience: AI reliability engineers, system architects, applied modeling researchers
article_ideas.based_on: deriving behavior strictly from internal structure and policy
article_ideas.thesis: Endogenous explanation — deriving behavior from internal loops, contracts, and policy rather than external shocks or model variance — is the discipline that makes reliability work actionable, because external-cause explanations are unfalsifiable and therefore unactionable.
article_ideas.title: Explain Failure From Your Own Structure, Not Your Users
article_ideas.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson

article_ideas.angle: Take the standard read-task → plan → tool calls → emit-result harness and re-draw it as Goals → Decisions → State → Side Effects → Actions of Others, showing what has to be built at each seam and why 'actions of others' belongs inside the loop rather than outside it as noise.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent framework builders shipping long-horizon autonomous systems
article_ideas.based_on: Open-loop thinking assumes a linear path
article_ideas.thesis: Open-loop agent pipelines fail on long-horizon tasks not because the model is weak but because no stage observes the resulting system state; the highest-leverage architectural change is inserting continuous state estimation and external-actor modeling into the loop, not upgrading the model inside it.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Doesn't Need a Better Model, It Needs a State Observation Step
article_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview

article_ideas.angle: Define side effects operationally as effects outside the mental model that feed back, then derive the rule that whatever the context window, summary, or memory store excludes will re-enter as unexplained failure unless the gap between observability scope and reasoning scope is explicitly instrumented.
article_ideas.audience: Platform, observability and reliability engineers running agents in production
article_ideas.based_on: Side effects are simply effects outside our mental model that feed back into the system.
article_ideas.thesis: Unintended consequences are not a separate category of event but the return path of whatever the agent's representation omitted, which makes the model boundary itself the risk surface and makes boundary instrumentation a design requirement rather than a monitoring afterthought.
article_ideas.title: Side Effects Are Just Model-External Feedback: Why Your Observability Scope Must Exceed Your Reasoning Scope
article_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview

article_ideas.angle: Use the short-term time horizon trap and open-loop project management as the pattern: local optimization against an explicit objective that omits feedback generates long-horizon regressions, and each round of added sophistication makes the resulting intervention more elaborate and more wrong.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leaders and architects deciding where to invest agent-improvement effort
article_ideas.based_on: Failures happen not despite our cleverness, but because of it (we are too clever for our own good).
article_ideas.thesis: Sophistication applied inside a flawed model boundary produces confidently wrong interventions, so failures occur because of our cleverness rather than despite it; the corrective is not more analytical power but better boundary selection and decision-rule change.
article_ideas.title: Too Clever for Our Own Good: Why Sophisticated Agents Fail Inside Wrong Boundaries
article_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview

article_ideas.angle: Walk the causal checklist (what the environment permits, what the agent can actually see at decision time, which policy it applies) against common agent incidents and show how the model-swap fix leaves the structural cause intact so the failure recurs.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers and incident-review owners responsible for agent reliability
article_ideas.based_on: The fundamental attribution error leads people to blame individuals rather than the system structure.
article_ideas.thesis: Attributing agent failures to the model or the prompt author is the component-replacement reflex and is almost always low-leverage, so root-cause processes should require a structural hypothesis about physics, information availability, or decision rules before a component-level fix is accepted.
article_ideas.title: The Model-Swap Reflex: Treating Every Agent Failure as a Structure Problem First
article_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview

article_ideas.angle: Reframe evals, observability, and reliability as a balance-sheet asset with explicit erosion metrics rather than discretionary overhead that can be paused when deadlines loom.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders, platform teams, and heads of engineering reliability
article_ideas.based_on: Cutting capability investments produces better-before-worse behavior
article_ideas.thesis: AI teams deprioritize eval infrastructure, observability, and reliability work because these are capability stocks whose erosion is delayed and invisible; the short-term speed gains reinforce the cuts, and the eventual collapse arrives as a sudden, severe reliability incident that the organization has no leading indicator to foresee.
article_ideas.title: Your Evals Are a Stock, Not a Chore: Why AI Teams Eat Their Own Reliability
article_ideas.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning

article_ideas.angle: Argue that investing in rollout mechanics, feedback instrumentation, and incremental integration beats chasing novel frameworks that the organization will fail to absorb.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, CTOs, and AI platform owners
article_ideas.based_on: Useful does not imply used
article_ideas.thesis: The bottleneck in AI engineering is not knowledge of best practices but the organizational capacity to adopt them; since fewer than 10% of firms historically built well-developed quality programs despite documented outperformance, teams that build adoption capability will outperform teams that merely track the latest proven technique.
article_ideas.title: Useful Does Not Imply Used: The Adoption Gap Is the Real AI Advantage
article_ideas.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning

article_ideas.angle: Use the worse-before-better dynamic to explain why monolith-to-agent-platform rewrites fail and to prescribe incremental adoption cadence.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers, architects, and technical program managers
article_ideas.based_on: Adopting new capabilities follows a worse-before-better dynamic
article_ideas.thesis: Because capability adoption follows a worse-before-better curve, large-scale agent framework or architecture migrations deepen the initial performance dip and increase abandonment risk; the correct rollout is small, persistent, daily capability gains rather than episodic transformation.
article_ideas.title: The Big-Bang AI Migration Is a Capability Trap
article_ideas.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning

article_ideas.angle: Map the Imperial Sugar deferred-maintenance case onto AI ops and argue for tail-risk indicators alongside throughput metrics.
article_ideas.audience: SREs, AI operations teams, and risk and compliance officers
article_ideas.based_on: Deferred maintenance and housekeeping can create latent catastrophic risk
article_ideas.thesis: Delaying security patches, observability improvements, and reliability work in AI operations accumulates tail risk that short-term production metrics cannot reveal; the organization looks healthy right up until the incident, because safety-margin erosion is invisible to output dashboards.
article_ideas.title: Deferred Maintenance in AI Operations Is a Latent Catastrophe
article_ideas.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning

article_ideas.angle: Architectural critique: map governance topology to enforcement mechanisms, with concrete examples from agent frameworks.
article_ideas.audience: AI architects and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: centralized coercive capacity and centralization of authority arrive as a package
article_ideas.thesis: Declared autonomy is meaningless unless the central enforcement mechanisms (global kill-switch, central scheduler, policy proxy) are removed; adding a central policy layer silently re-centralizes an agent system.
article_ideas.title: The Enforcement Layer Is the Government: Why Removing the Central Orchestrator Is the Only Real Decentralization
article_ideas.video_title: 3. Dutch and British Exceptionalism

article_ideas.angle: Data-driven: define the index, show correlations with task success, cost, and recovery.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, system designers, and engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: What is the operational equivalent of 'middle-class population share' in an agent system
article_ideas.thesis: System-level performance and resilience correlate with the distribution and permeability of mid-tier components (tools, skills, memory) more than with apex model capability; teams should measure and optimize a mid-layer index.
article_ideas.title: Build the Middle, Not the Apex: A Middle-Class Index for Agent Systems
article_ideas.video_title: 3. Dutch and British Exceptionalism

article_ideas.angle: Multi-agent systems design: propose threat-model-based alignment as a lower-cost coordination primitive, with experimental evidence.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent researchers and AI safety engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Counter-position identity is cheap and durable
article_ideas.thesis: Shared forbidden outcomes coordinate distributed agents more cheaply and durably than shared positive goals, as evidenced by historical identity formation against a common threat.
article_ideas.title: Fear Is a Cheaper Coordinator Than Purpose: Negative Alignment in Multi-Agent Systems
article_ideas.video_title: 3. Dutch and British Exceptionalism

article_ideas.angle: Comparative analysis: historical case studies mapped to agent architecture tradeoffs, with measurement framework.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, architects, and technical strategists
article_ideas.based_on: Decentralization trades peak coordinated scale for robustness and local rights; the trade must be measured, not assumed away.
article_ideas.thesis: Decentralization trades peak coordinated scale for robustness; teams must measure the penalty rather than assume decentralization is superior, because rights-preserving systems can lose on throughput.
article_ideas.title: The Scale Penalty of Autonomy: Why Decentralized Systems Lose Great-Power Status
article_ideas.video_title: 3. Dutch and British Exceptionalism

evidence_quotes.text: Running thousands of agent calls incurs a massive 'HarnessTax' in token costs and execution time.
Most agent swarm outputs are bloated with high slop-to-signal ratios.

deep_dives.research_question: How can teams quantitatively price the HarnessTax per task and determine when a multi-agent swarm beats a single tool-rich harness on tokens, wall-clock, and signal density?
deep_dives.topic: Pricing the HarnessTax: cost-to-performance frontier for agent swarms
deep_dives.trigger_insight: HarnessTax: running thousands of agent calls imposes large token-cost and latency overhead
deep_dives.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD
deep_dives.why: Prevents defaulting to expensive swarms and provides a measurable decision rule for orchestration investment.

evidence_quotes.text: Language model harnesses act as compositional generalizers.
RLMs enable models to generalize to longer tasks and different domains without changing the underlying base transformer.

deep_dives.research_question: When the base model is held fixed and only harness structure varies, can length and domain generalization gains be attributed to the harness rather than the transformer?
deep_dives.topic: Isolating harness-induced compositional generalization from base-transformer capability
deep_dives.trigger_insight: A harness, not the base transformer, can be the locus of compositional generalization
deep_dives.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD
deep_dives.why: Determines whether teams should invest in execution-environment engineering or model scaling.

evidence_quotes.text: Current frontier LLMs are 'geniuses' in capability but 'mismanaged' by poor task decomposition and harness design.
Scaling raw model compute without better task structuring hits diminishing returns.

deep_dives.research_question: On failing multi-step agent workflows, does harness/decomposition ablation recover more success per dollar than upgrading to a larger base model?
deep_dives.topic: Mismanaged Geniuses diagnostic: ablation before model upgrade
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The 'Mismanaged Geniuses' hypothesis attributes multi-step failure to management/decomposition
deep_dives.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD
deep_dives.why: Avoids wasted spend on larger models when task structure is the actual bottleneck.

evidence_quotes.text: Model-driven turn-taking in Dialog-RSN-1 achieves sub-300ms p50 latency without sacrificing reasoning quality.
Cascaded systems struggle with VAD thresholds, leading to either premature interruption or frustrating pauses.

deep_dives.research_question: Can learned model-driven turn-taking replace VAD silence thresholds without sacrificing reasoning quality, and what latency distribution does it achieve under messy real-world audio?
deep_dives.topic: Learned endpointing vs VAD thresholds
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Turn boundaries and endpointing are learned/predicted by the model rather than derived from VAD silence thresholds
deep_dives.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen
deep_dives.why: Matters because it resolves the brittle threshold-tuning tradeoff between premature interruption and frustrating pauses, and determines whether sub-300ms p50 latency is achievable in production voice agents.

evidence_quotes.text: Harness engineering (retrieval, tool calling, grounding, citations) is where enterprise differentiation happens.
Raw speech-to-speech models are great for demos but break down in complex enterprise workflows without strict harnesses.

deep_dives.research_question: What specific harness components (retrieval, tool calling, grounding, citations, guardrails) are necessary to make raw speech-to-speech models viable in complex enterprise workflows?
deep_dives.topic: Harness engineering as enterprise deployment prerequisite
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Enterprise differentiation shifts from model weights to the harness layer
deep_dives.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen
deep_dives.why: Matters because it reframes investment from model scale to the deterministic control layer that determines deployability, turning harness engineering into the enterprise moat.

evidence_quotes.text: Dialog-RSN-1 listens directly to audio waveforms, preserving tone, emotion, and timing, but outputs text to leverage standard enterprise governance, tooling, and deterministic search.

deep_dives.research_question: Does emitting text from an audio-native model preserve audio-derived prosody, emotion, and timing through a separate TTS while retaining enterprise governance and tool calling?
deep_dives.topic: Audio-in/text-out control seam for multimodal agents
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Dialog-RSN-1 splits the modality at a deliberate boundary
deep_dives.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen
deep_dives.why: Matters because it defines where to place the abstraction boundary between understanding and control, potentially allowing native audio semantics without losing auditability or deterministic search.

evidence_quotes.text: Engineers must shift focus from learning syntax to defining system primitives and product requirements.
Focus on building systems with good primitives so AI agents can execute correctly.

deep_dives.research_question: Can 'good primitives' be operationalized as a measurable property (narrow vs. broad, explicit vs. implicit constraints) that demonstrably increases agent task success rate and reduces error modes?
deep_dives.topic: Primitive design as the reliability surface for agent execution
deep_dives.trigger_insight: build systems with good primitives so AI agents can execute correctly
deep_dives.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds
deep_dives.why: The pass-1 insight asserts that agent correctness is bounded by the shape of the primitives exposed to it, but gives no definition, example, or measurement. If true, engineering investment should shift from prompt craft and line-level review toward tool-schema/guardrail design, which changes what teams build and hire for. If false, guardrail-heavy primitive design is wasted rigidity.

evidence_quotes.text: Autopilots didn't eliminate pilots because accountability and judgment matter.
Customers don't have to deal with the consequences of being wrong.
Use AI to gather information and draft implementations, keeping yourself in the driver's seat for decisions.

deep_dives.research_question: Does placing human accountability only at irreversible-consequence boundaries scale, or does gate throughput become the new bottleneck relative to uniform review of generated output?
deep_dives.topic: Gate placement economics: consequence-boundary-only human approval vs. uniform review
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Automation of execution shifts the human role to owning outcomes
deep_dives.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds
deep_dives.why: The ATM/autopilot analogy supports retaining human accountability but provides no data on latency or throughput cost. The answer determines the operating economics of any production agent pipeline: where you put the human determines both escaped-error rate and delivery latency, and the pass-1 tradeoff notes that nominal human control does not guarantee judgment is actually applied.

evidence_quotes.text: Code generation is not the bottleneck; code gen represents only 14-16% of the overall value stream.
Non-AI factors (meetings, context switching, release pipeline friction) still outweigh AI benefits.
Proves that targeting non-coding bottlenecks in the SDLC with specialized AI agents yields massive real-world ROI.

deep_dives.research_question: How can per-repo and per-org value-stream share be measured stage-by-stage (cycle-time contribution, wait states, handoffs) so that specialized SDLC agents can be ranked and deployed by system-level ROI rather than by visibility?
deep_dives.topic: Value-stream attribution as the ranking function for agent investment
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Code generation is not the bottleneck; code gen represents only 14-16% of the overall value stream.
deep_dives.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX
deep_dives.why: If code generation is 14-16% of the value stream, then a portfolio decision made on IDE-adjacent intuition systematically over-funds the wrong stage. A reproducible attribution method is the prerequisite for any Theory-of-Constraints-style agent roadmap, and it converts 'where should we build agents?' from an opinion into a measurement.

evidence_quotes.text: Code maintainability perceived score went up ~4%, but change confidence went down ~6%.
Median PR size has noticeably increased (from ~44 to 72 lines of code) over the study period.
developers find code easier to modify with AI, but trust the output less

deep_dives.research_question: Is the drop in developer change confidence a fixed property of AI-generated changes, or a function of review capacity being exceeded by larger AI-assisted PRs — and can a review-policy intervention restore confidence without giving back throughput?
deep_dives.topic: The decay of change confidence under AI-assisted delivery
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Code maintainability perceived score went up ~4%, but change confidence went down ~6%.
deep_dives.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX
deep_dives.why: Maintainability rising while confidence falls means the standard 'code quality' proxy is actively misleading for AI-assisted code. Combined with median PR size growth, this points at review capacity, not generation capacity, as the binding constraint — which changes what a review agent should be built to do.

evidence_quotes.text: median PR throughput increased by 7.76% and average by 13.1% in longitudinal studies
no companies hitting 2x, 5x, or 10x
Perceived rate of delivery showing a minor ~4.5% increase over a full year.

deep_dives.research_question: What fraction of the observed median PR throughput increase (+7.76%) survives matched-cohort or interrupted time-series comparison against non-adopting teams inside the same organization, once deployment-frequency trends and regional shifts are controlled?
deep_dives.topic: Causal separation of AI gains from confounders in delivery metrics
deep_dives.trigger_insight: median PR throughput increased by 7.76% and average by 13.1% in longitudinal studies
deep_dives.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX
deep_dives.why: Without causal separation, every downstream ROI model and vendor benchmark inherits an unidentified confounder. This determines whether the low-double-digit effect is the true AI prior or an upper bound that further controls will shrink.

evidence_quotes.text: Passing tests only checks behavioral correctness, not external code quality or subtle bugs.
Meter hiring open-source maintainers to review pull requests and finding automated reviews failed 50% of the time on mergeability.
AI models score significantly lower on human review rubrics than on standard test execution.

deep_dives.research_question: Can a human-reviewed mergeability rubric be encoded as a reproducible evaluation dataset whose scores diverge measurably from test-pass rates, and what rubric dimensions account for that divergence?
deep_dives.topic: Mergeability as a first-class evaluation target distinct from test execution
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Passing a test suite is a behavioral-correctness signal only, not a mergeability signal
deep_dives.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI
deep_dives.why: It attacks the central claim that 'passing tests is not mergeable': if divergence between test-pass and human-mergeability scores can be quantified and decomposed, teams get a concrete, versioned acceptance layer instead of an unfalsifiable slogan, and model selection can optimize the right signal.

evidence_quotes.text: Anthropic's security reviewer can be talked out of its findings by the very code it is reviewing.
Shows that fully removing humans from review loops introduces severe vulnerabilities and slop accumulation.
