deep_dives.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk
deep_dives.why: The minimum-bloodshed criterion supplies a shape for objective functions in shared environments — reward net value after cost, not engagement volume — but pass-1 explicitly leaves unresolved whether this separates productive restraint from passivity. This is a bounded, measurable tradeoff rather than a philosophical claim, and it determines whether conflict avoidance can be treated as a first-class success signal.

evidence_quotes.text: Select appropriate methodologies matching the problem complexity and available resources.
In ambiguous situations with multiple stakeholders holding conflicting views.
Systematic approach to problem solving for complex, messy situations involving human values and differing stakeholder perspectives.

deep_dives.research_question: Can methodology selection be operationalized as a rubric keyed on problem character (computable dynamics vs value-contested ambiguity) plus budget, with acceptable inter-rater agreement and measurable downstream outcome differences versus a single default formalism?
deep_dives.topic: A decision procedure for choosing the analysis formalism
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Methodology selection is explicitly conditioned on problem type and available resources
deep_dives.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023
deep_dives.why: A single harness or evaluation regime for all tasks produces either unfalsifiable narrative on value-contested problems or models that ignore the actual conflict. Making the selection itself a resource-bounded decision is the engineering consequence of the claim that no universal method exists.

evidence_quotes.text: Tactical programming focuses solely on getting the next feature or bug fix working ASAP, creating 'tactical tornadoes' and technical debt.
Complexity is incremental; system complexity accumulates from hundreds of tiny shortcuts.
Investing 10-20% extra time today on design pays back significantly in the long run.

deep_dives.research_question: Over what horizon does a 10–20% upfront design investment in agent tool surfaces and prompts yield net positive cumulative capability compared to tactical shipping?
deep_dives.topic: Economic justification of strategic design investment for agent pipelines
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Investing 10-20% extra time today on design pays back significantly in the long run.
deep_dives.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL
deep_dives.why: Addresses the open question of whether the 10–20% design investment remains economically justified when the artifacts are agent tool surfaces and prompts rather than long-lived source code, making the time-horizon tradeoff explicit.

evidence_quotes.text: Computer science education teaches programming, classes, and software engineering tools, but does not teach problem decomposition or elite design skills.
Taking a large problem and chopping it up into relatively independent pieces is fundamental to all of computer science, yet rarely taught directly.

deep_dives.research_question: Can decomposition quality (independence of pieces) be measured, and does it predict multi-agent task success and conflict rate?
deep_dives.topic: Problem decomposition as an explicit, measurable step for multi-agent systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Problem decomposition — chopping a large problem into relatively independent pieces — is claimed to be the most important concept in computer science
deep_dives.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL
deep_dives.why: Connects the claim that decomposition is the most important yet rarely taught CS concept to multi-agent design, where independence between subtasks determines whether parallel agents can operate without shared-state conflicts.

evidence_quotes.text: Large events occur infrequently, while small events occur frequently.
Diverse complex systems exhibit power law distributions.

deep_dives.research_question: Do failure sizes in real or simulated multi-agent workloads follow power-law distributions, and what tail-aware capacity and SLO policies should replace average-case planning?
deep_dives.topic: Power-law tail risks in agentic failure distributions
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Large events occur infrequently, while small events occur frequently
deep_dives.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
deep_dives.why: If failures are heavy-tailed, rare giant cascades dominate total risk and standard mean/percentile engineering systematically underestimates catastrophic exposure.

evidence_quotes.text: System dynamics fits on the right side of the spectrum, dealing with human interaction and wicked problems as tools for thinking.
Automation of decisions

deep_dives.research_question: Can tasks of graded ambiguity be placed on a puzzles-to-wicked-problems spectrum by a rubric, and does rubric placement predict which execution substrate (deterministic pipeline versus agentic reasoning loop) performs better?
deep_dives.topic: A classification rubric that selects execution substrate before implementation
deep_dives.trigger_insight: System dynamics fits on the right side of the spectrum, dealing with human interaction and wicked problems as tools for thinking
deep_dives.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski
deep_dives.why: Teams routinely wrap deterministic, solvable tasks in agent loops and push genuinely open-ended judgment into rigid pipelines. The talk supplies the two endpoints (checkbook balancing versus wicked problems) but no decision rule, so substrate selection remains intuition-driven and misapplication is invisible until it fails on novel input.

evidence_quotes.text: Spreadsheets lack clear input/output separation, automatic unit control, and multi-dimensional handling without tedious formulas.
System dynamics software provides safety checks, transparency, and automatic calculations that prevent spreadsheet blunders.

deep_dives.research_question: Do memory substrates that lack an enforced distinction between retrieved context (read) and mutated artifact (write) exhibit higher rates of stale-read and self-referential-write defects, and are those defects less detectable by standard evaluation?
deep_dives.topic: Enforced input/output separation in agent memory substrates
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Spreadsheets lack clear input/output separation
deep_dives.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski
deep_dives.why: The spreadsheet critique is structural, not a feature gap: conflating inputs and derived quantities makes errors undetectable rather than merely frequent. Agent context and memory systems routinely make the same conflation, which predicts a defect class that current evals would systematically miss.

evidence_quotes.text: The human brain can only hold about 7 plus or minus 2 objects at once (Miller's Rule).
Partitioning a complex diagram into six systems and hiding internal details to reduce complexity.
Hierarchies are fractal; systems are subsystems of larger systems.

deep_dives.research_question: At what element count per level do tool schemas and context layouts begin to degrade model task success, and does a small fixed fan-out with hidden internals beat a wide flat surface?
deep_dives.topic: Does the ~7-element chunking constraint transfer from human working memory to model context and tool/interface schemas?
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The human brain can only hold about 7 plus or minus 2 objects at once (Miller's Rule).
deep_dives.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering
deep_dives.why: This turns a cognitive-science rule into a testable interface design budget for tool schemas, sub-agent interface descriptions, and context packing — and tests whether the constraint is a property of human reviewers only or of any consumer, including models.

evidence_quotes.text: There are five types of systems engineers: Type I (problem causer), Type II (apprentice doer), Type III (problem solver), Type IV (problem formulator), Type V (innovator-leader).

deep_dives.research_question: Do assessment tasks that explicitly discriminate formulation ability from solving ability produce cleanly separated performance tiers, or is the Type III/Type IV boundary a descriptive spectrum with no measurement signature?
deep_dives.topic: Do capability tiers separate cleanly — problem solver vs. problem formulator
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Type IV (problem formulator)
deep_dives.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering
deep_dives.why: Most tooling and process investment targets solving already-stated problems, while the high-leverage failure sits at formulation. If the tiers don't separate empirically, maturity scales anchored on formulation ability are unsupported; if they do, responsibility assignment between humans and agents can be staged on evidence.

evidence_quotes.text: PSMs offer a way of representing situations to enable participants to clarify predicaments, converge on actionable issues, and agree on commitments.
Applied systems researchers asked what systems thinking meant for policy making, management, and analysis.

deep_dives.research_question: Which problem structuring method steps can be automated in an agent, and under what conditions does structuring-before-solving reduce solving-the-wrong-problem failures?
deep_dives.topic: Problem structuring as a first-class agent workflow
deep_dives.trigger_insight: PSMs offer a way of representing situations to enable participants to clarify predicaments, converge on actionable issues, and agree on commitments.
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice
deep_dives.why: For ill-defined or multi-stakeholder tasks, an agent that immediately optimizes against its first model of the request will often solve the wrong problem; the representation-building, elicitation, and commitment phases need explicit support.

evidence_quotes.text: Focuses on experiential learning rather than system design.

deep_dives.research_question: How can the quality of an agent's facilitation be measured when its intended contribution is stakeholder learning, shared understanding, and commitment rather than delivery of a final artifact?
deep_dives.topic: Process-quality metrics for experiential-learning agents
deep_dives.trigger_insight: experiential learning rather than system design
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice
deep_dives.why: In governance and multi-stakeholder situations, optimizing only for solution quality can be counterproductive if the actual gap is collective cognition; process outcomes need to be tracked.

evidence_quotes.text: There are nine holistic thinking perspectives categorized into external, internal, progressive, and remaining.
Acts as a template for collecting and organizing information without blind spots.

deep_dives.research_question: Does a fixed perspective checklist (HTP-style) reduce blind-spot failures in agent context gathering compared to an unstructured 'be thorough' instruction?
deep_dives.topic: Fixed perspective checklists vs unstructured context gathering
deep_dives.trigger_insight: fixed perspective checklist (HTP-style)
deep_dives.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems
deep_dives.why: A fixed enumeration mechanically forces coverage without relying on ad hoc consideration, but its benefit over free-form thoroughness is unquantified.

evidence_quotes.text: Involves identifying the point, evidence, unstated premises, terminology, and evaluating reasoning validity.
Critical thinking uses selection criteria, logic, and reasoning rather than mere criticism.

deep_dives.research_question: Can unstated premises in LLM-generated arguments be reliably identified and extracted as an automated review step?
deep_dives.topic: Automated extraction of unstated premises from generated arguments
deep_dives.trigger_insight: unstated premises in generated arguments
deep_dives.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems
deep_dives.why: Unstated premises are the specific failure surface where persuasion and error hide; an automated extractor would turn vague skepticism into an auditable checklist.

evidence_quotes.text: Must be written with verification in mind
Traceability

deep_dives.research_question: Can unit-level verification at each abstraction tier be aggregated into complete end-to-end coverage in agent pipelines, and how are integration-boundary gaps accounted for?
deep_dives.topic: Coverage Composition from Lowest-Level Verification
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Test at the lowest level possible before integrating upwards

deep_dives.why: It reframes eval design as a coverage-partition problem rather than a benchmark-selection problem, and makes the sum-of-testing claim falsifiable in agent systems.

evidence_quotes.text: Design should flow from requirements, not constraints

deep_dives.research_question: Does pinning leaf-level constants such as model names, token budgets, or tool arguments in high-level orchestrator prompts increase change cost and reduce substitutability of lower-tier components?
deep_dives.topic: Tier Discipline Against Over-Specification in Agent Prompts
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Detailed design parameters like resistor values belong several tiers down, not at the top aircraft level
deep_dives.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019
deep_dives.why: Leaking leaf-level constants upward converts a stable interface into a brittle constraint and makes lower tiers unswappable; each tier should specify only what its consumers need to reason about.

evidence_quotes.text: Certification and safety must be considered from the top of the process

deep_dives.research_question: Does deriving safety and failure analysis requirements before agent architecture and interface definition reduce post-hoc guardrail patches and safety defects compared with bottom-up guardrail addition?
deep_dives.topic: Top-Down Safety-Driven Interface Derivation
deep_dives.trigger_insight: safety and failure analysis must drive requirements from the top down
deep_dives.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019
deep_dives.why: If safety derives requirements from the top, hazard analysis must shape architecture and interface definitions themselves, not be bolted on after a pipeline is built.

evidence_quotes.text: During advanced meditative retreats under the guidance of a qualified teacher.
The Six Yogas of Naropa
A advanced set of tantric meditation and yoga practices designed to accelerate spiritual realization.

deep_dives.research_question: Is the supervision/retreat precondition for advanced capability modules load-bearing for acquisition, or merely a convention that can be removed without loss?
deep_dives.topic: Capability gating and authorization layers
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Ablate the gate: compare capability acquisition with and without supervision/retreat preconditions
deep_dives.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film
deep_dives.why: If the gate is load-bearing, agent runtimes need a separate authorization component; if not, it is safe to expose advanced modules more broadly. The answer changes security and deployment architecture.

evidence_quotes.text: Without mental training, human thoughts and emotions run wild and cause suffering.
Yogis use repetition of core beliefs, mantras, and meditation to put reins on erratic thoughts.

deep_dives.research_question: Does periodic re-assertion of a small invariant instruction set measurably suppress drift in long-running agents, and what is the cost in flexibility?
deep_dives.topic: Scheduled re-anchoring for drift suppression
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Does periodic re-assertion of a small invariant instruction set actually suppress drift in long-running agents
deep_dives.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film
deep_dives.why: Long-running agents suffer goal decay and context dilution; a scheduled re-anchor step would be a lightweight reliability primitive, but its effect size and trade-offs are unmeasured.

evidence_quotes.text: It focuses on what the system ought to be rather than what is currently feasible from a legacy standpoint.
Innovation stems from questioning foundational assumptions rather than fixing symptoms.

deep_dives.research_question: How can inherited constraints in an agentic system be explicitly enumerated and re-admitted only after passing feasibility and viability gates?
deep_dives.topic: Legacy assumption inventory in AI system redesign
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Elimination of legacy assumptions
deep_dives.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Inherited interfaces, prompts, and compatibility layers silently bound the solution space; making them explicit converts hidden bias into a reviewable design decision.

evidence_quotes.text: An ounce of information is worth a pound of data; knowledge is worth information; understanding is worth knowledge; wisdom is worth understanding.
Educational systems allocate most time to transmitting information and some knowledge, nothing to understanding, and none to wisdom.

deep_dives.research_question: At a fixed token budget, does a context composed of distilled understanding and structured knowledge outperform a larger-recall context of raw retrieved data on reasoning-heavy agent tasks?
deep_dives.topic: Value-tiered context and memory budgets
deep_dives.trigger_insight: An ounce of information is worth a pound of data; knowledge is worth information; understanding is worth knowledge; wisdom is worth understanding.
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Context engineering currently optimizes for recall volume; if the mind-content hierarchy is right, the cheapest tier is the least valuable and the memory pipeline should be scored by the tier of content it surfaces, not by how much it surfaces.

evidence_quotes.text: Examinations are about trying to anticipate the answers expected by the teacher; expected answers cannot be creative.
Schools punish deviation from expected answers, penalizing surprise and suppressing creativity.

deep_dives.research_question: Do reference-match and expected-answer graders assign systematically lower scores to valid novel solutions than to conventional ones, and can judge- or surprise-based scoring reduce that false-negative rate without inflating false positives?
deep_dives.topic: Evaluation criteria that reward surprise instead of conformity
deep_dives.trigger_insight: expected answers cannot be creative
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff
deep_dives.why: If expected answers cannot be creative, then static reference-match benchmarks are structurally adversarial to the open-ended behavior agents are deployed to produce, and the eval design itself becomes a driver of degenerate, conformist outputs.

evidence_quotes.text: Visa International was intentionally designed as a radical, democratic, decentralized system of governance to prevent the concentration of power.
Concentrating power kills innovation, motivation, and wealth.

deep_dives.research_question: Under what conditions does decentralized governance in multi-agent systems preserve innovation and avoid concentration of power, and when does it fail to maintain coordination or consistency?
deep_dives.topic: Decentralized governance at scale in multi-agent systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Under what conditions does decentralized governance at scale stop working?
deep_dives.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline
deep_dives.why: Decentralization is often adopted for scalability, but Visa's case suggests it can be a deliberate anti-concentration mechanism. For multi-agent systems, understanding the boundary conditions is crucial for designing robust topologies.

evidence_quotes.text: We have to go upstream because the corporate world is downstream from formative educational processes.

deep_dives.research_question: What methods can reliably attribute an observed output failure to a specific upstream input such as data, specification, or environment, and how does upstream fixing compare to downstream patching in reducing recurrence?
deep_dives.topic: Causal attribution from downstream symptoms to upstream processes
deep_dives.trigger_insight: What is the reliable method for attributing a downstream symptom to a specific upstream process?
deep_dives.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline
deep_dives.why: Upstream intervention is advocated but lacks a tracing methodology. Without attribution, upstream fixes are guesswork, and downstream patching may suppress symptoms without removing causes.

evidence_quotes.text: A software-only company cannot afford a direct sales force because average software prices are too low.
Average software package prices ($500) cannot support a 130-person direct sales force; $5,000 system prices can.

deep_dives.research_question: What pricing and packaging constraints does the cost of the AI sales and deployment motion impose, and when does bundling with a higher-priced offering become necessary?
deep_dives.topic: Channel cost floor and AI product packaging
deep_dives.trigger_insight: software-only business cannot fund a high-touch direct sales force
deep_dives.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech
deep_dives.why: It frames go-to-market as an architectural constraint on product form. For AI products sold into enterprises with solution engineers and custom integration, the tension recurs: the sales motion's cost determines the minimum viable price point.

evidence_quotes.text: John Dewey proved understandability is an unattainable ideal, like zero error in science.
Heisenberg showed that the more accurately you know mass, the less accurately you know energy.

deep_dives.research_question: Is there a defensible stopping criterion for evaluation coverage in stochastic, context-dependent systems, given that complete understandability is treated as unattainable?
deep_dives.topic: Stopping criteria for evaluation coverage under irreducible uncertainty
deep_dives.trigger_insight: understandability is an unattainable ideal, like zero error
deep_dives.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking
deep_dives.why: The pursuit of complete understanding produces an unbounded effort and a false sense of coverage. Naming a stopping criterion converts 'we tested everything we could' into a measurable policy that can be argued about and audited.

evidence_quotes.text: Taylor's work analysis reduced tasks to elementary tasks for mechanization.
Organizations were managed under the mechanistic assumption that the business is an instrument for maximizing shareholder value.

deep_dives.research_question: Does finer task granularity in an agent workflow increase reproducibility and per-step measurability while decreasing success on open-ended, purpose-laden tasks?
deep_dives.topic: Task granularity as a purpose-versus-mechanizability tradeoff
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Taylor's work analysis reduced tasks to elementary tasks for mechanization.
deep_dives.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking
deep_dives.why: Granularity choices are usually framed as neutral efficiency decisions. If they systematically strip purpose representation, then benchmark-strong step pipelines can be predicted to degrade on open-ended work, and the tradeoff becomes a design axis rather than a default.

evidence_quotes.text: system dynamicists reject this in favor of building mental models to increase intuition
Computer models are tools to help increase understanding.
eventually making the computer model unnecessary once mental models are refined

deep_dives.research_question: If a decision-support model is working correctly, operator prediction accuracy on counterfactual system states should improve and their reliance on the model's verdicts should fall — can that be measured and used as the primary success metric instead of task accuracy?
deep_dives.topic: Evaluation metrics when the model's goal is to make itself unnecessary
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The stated purpose of building computer models is to refine the operator's mental model
deep_dives.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse
deep_dives.why: The pass-1 practice insight reframes the artifact's purpose as refining the operator's mental model, which admits no measurement in current eval harnesses. Establishing pre/post calibration scoring on counterfactual states converts a methodological stance into a testable claim, and it forces interfaces to expose causal structure and what-if runs as first-class outputs.

evidence_quotes.text: The world model includes two major positive feedback loops: population growth (births over deaths) and industrial capital investment over depreciation.
featuring approximately 250 equations
Standard run without policy changes leads to an overshoot and collapse mode driven by non-renewable resource depletion and pollution.

deep_dives.research_question: Does a two-dominant-positive-loop plus one-erodable-sector model — the analog of births-over-deaths, investment-over-depreciation, and a depleting resource sector — predict observed peaks and downturns in agent platform telemetry better than broad component-level instrumentation?
deep_dives.topic: Minimal dominant-loop models of agent production systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: a small number of dominant loops plus one erodable sector explains the aggregate behavior
deep_dives.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse
deep_dives.why: Loop dominance is the pass-1 explanation for why roughly 250 equations reduce to a handful of driving loops. If agent platform behavior concentrates similarly, monitoring effort should be reallocated from exhaustive telemetry to a small fitted loop model, and the erodable sector (data quality, provider quota) should be the stressed variable. This is falsifiable against historical incident and growth traces.

evidence_quotes.text: A system cannot be divided into independent parts without losing its essential properties.
The Western management principle of 'divide and conquer' is fundamentally false.

deep_dives.research_question: Which criteria for decomposition boundaries—interaction density vs. functional alignment—best preserve end-to-end capabilities when an agent system must be split?
deep_dives.topic: Boundary Placement for Preserving System Properties
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Which boundary cuts preserve a system's essential properties when decomposition is unavoidable?
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Abstraction boundaries determine what interactions are co-designed and what are severed. If function-aligned boundaries destroy essential properties, then interface cleanliness is a poor proxy for correctness, and boundary placement becomes a first-class architectural decision.

evidence_quotes.text: Data, information, knowledge, understanding, and wisdom form a hierarchy of increasing importance.
Educational systems devote most time to transmitting information and knowledge, but nothing to understanding and wisdom.

deep_dives.research_question: Can evaluation tasks isolate causal explanation (understanding) and judgment under conflicting values (wisdom) from factual retrieval (knowledge), and do systems strong on lower tiers fail on upper tiers?
deep_dives.topic: Measuring Understanding and Wisdom in AI Systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How would 'understanding' and 'wisdom' be distinguished from 'knowledge' in an operational evaluation of an AI system?
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Current context and memory architectures maximize data and information volume while rarely capturing causal models or value-laden judgment. A concrete evaluation of the upper tiers would expose this structural misallocation and guide memory tier design.

evidence_quotes.text: These four patterns (Distinctions, Systems, Relationships, Perspectives) happen all together, all the time.

deep_dives.research_question: Does serializing distinction, part-whole, relation, and perspective steps produce measurably worse structuring than joint co-constrained structuring on tasks where later operators revise earlier commitments?
deep_dives.topic: Simultaneous versus staged structuring in agent pipelines
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The four DSRP patterns are asserted to operate simultaneously and continuously, not as sequential stages
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab
deep_dives.why: Pipeline stage boundaries encode ordering assumptions; where operators actually co-occur, staged pipelines introduce unrecoverable early-commitment errors rather than merely latency, which changes how structuring workflows should be decomposed.

evidence_quotes.text: Mental models are unique to individual experiences and shape emotional reactions.

deep_dives.research_question: Do multi-agent disagreements trace to differing structuring operations (what is distinguished, treated as whole, related, or viewed) rather than to information asymmetry, and does sharing context resolve them?
deep_dives.topic: Experience-shaped models as a structural cause of multi-agent disagreement
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Mental models are described as unique to individual experience
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab
deep_dives.why: Provides a structural, testable explanation for divergent outputs among agents given identical inputs, which redirects alignment work from context sharing toward surfacing and reconciling structuring differences.

evidence_quotes.text: Building a soccer field for children before anything else to build community cohesion.
It proves that systemic ecological recovery depends on community leadership, social cohesion, and local stewardship rather than top-down government coercion.

deep_dives.research_question: What minimal substrate elements (shared context, identity, reciprocity signals, visible local benefit) are necessary for quota-based governance to achieve compliance in multi-agent resource settings?

deep_dives.why: Decomposes the abstract notion of 'social cohesion' into buildable components and tests whether substrate predicts compliance, providing a sequencing rule for governance rollouts.

evidence_quotes.text: 75-80 percent of the world's wild fisheries are collapsed or near collapse.
Baja California clam fishery rebounding from near zero to 3 million clams after communities stopped fishing and built local social order.

deep_dives.research_question: Can recovery speed after governance change be used as a discriminator between capacity exhaustion and coordination failure in resource-constrained multi-agent systems?
deep_dives.topic: Distinguishing capacity exhaustion from coordination failure via recovery speed
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Distinguish capacity exhaustion from coordination failure by testing whether governance changes alone produce recovery
deep_dives.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014
deep_dives.why: Avoids misallocating effort on capacity expansion when the fix belongs in coordination structure, using recovery speed as a diagnostic probe.

evidence_quotes.text: Random disturbances (noise) can cause a system to oscillate at its natural frequency.
Simple system dynamics models with inventory, production capacity, and delays can reproduce oscillatory behavior.

deep_dives.research_question: Do delayed software control loops exhibit a spectral peak at a natural frequency under white-noise input, and does input smoothing leave that peak intact while retuning the loop removes it?

evidence_quotes.text: Simple system dynamics models with inventory, production capacity, and delays can reproduce oscillatory behavior.
Visualizing inventory and commodity flows using the mental model of a bathtub with inflow pipes and outflow pipes.

deep_dives.research_question: For a system whose goal is intervention rather than prediction, does a minimal stock-and-flow abstraction (inventory, capacity, delay) locate the effective intervention point better than a higher-fidelity fitted model?

deep_dives.trigger_insight: Simple system dynamics models with inventory, production capacity, and delays
deep_dives.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson
deep_dives.why: The abstraction is what makes the loop legible and the intervention point identifiable. If minimal structures reproduce the observed behavior, then model complexity is not the gate on decision usefulness — legibility and modifiability are.

evidence_quotes.text: Structure generates behavior, consisting of physics, information availability, and decision rules.
To change system behavior, you must examine and modify system structure and decision rules rather than just blaming people.

deep_dives.research_question: Holding the model fixed, does varying what information is available at decision time and which decision rule is applied change agent behavior more than varying model capability?
deep_dives.topic: Diagnosing agent failures by information availability and decision rule rather than by model swap
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Structure generates behavior, consisting of physics, information availabili
deep_dives.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview
deep_dives.why: The decomposition of structure into physics, information availability, and decision rules gives a causal checklist that relocates engineering effort from model selection to harness and information-flow design. It also makes a concrete falsifiable prediction: capability improvements applied inside an unchanged information flow and unchanged policy should produce negligible behavior drift.

evidence_quotes.text: Mental models matter greatly; changing physical structures or IT is insufficient without changing mental models.

deep_dives.research_question: Do substrate-only upgrades (new tools, larger context, better retrieval) with the decision policy held fixed produce measurable behavior change on a fixed task suite?

deep_dives.trigger_insight: changing physical structures or IT is insufficient without changing mental models
deep_dives.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview
deep_dives.why: The claim that changing physical structures or IT is insufficient without changing mental models is a direct warning against the reflex of fixing agent systems by adding tools while leaving the decision policy untouched. Framing it as a controlled experiment — hold policy fixed, upgrade substrate, measure behavior drift — turns a philosophical assertion into a measurable, sliceable result about where capability actually propagates.

evidence_quotes.text: Human cognitive biases hardwire us to favor work over capability development because work offers tangible, immediate, and certain outcomes.
People overweight salient and tangible features of their environment.

open_questions.question: Is the claim that capability cannot be transferred directly by instruction — only built by self-directed practice — true for agent skill acquisition?
open_questions.research_direction: Compare declarative instruction versus accumulated practice traces (replay, experience memory) for acquiring a tool-use skill.
open_questions.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary reports the pedagogical assertion without evidence about transfer or practice mechanisms.

open_questions.research_direction: Develop leading indicators such as eval coverage, maintenance debt, incident precursors, and training completion, then validate them against delayed performance outcomes.

open_questions.research_direction: Run experiments varying batch size and cadence of capability adoption to identify thresholds that avoid deep performance dips.
open_questions.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary recommends small, consistent gains but provides no operational thresholds or experimental results.

open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary states that new capabilities always cause an initial dip but offers no diagnostic criteria.

open_questions.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary identifies biases such as salience and ambiguity aversion but does not test organizational interventions.

project_ideas.based_on: Running thousands of agent calls incurs a massive 'HarnessTax'
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed task suite, a single tool-rich harness achieves equal task success to a multi-agent swarm at lower token cost, lower wall-clock time, and higher signal density.
project_ideas.measurement: Pareto frontier of cost versus solved-task rate; signal-density ratio; break-even agent count per task class.
project_ideas.name: HarnessTax Pareto Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement identical long-horizon tasks with a single REPL/Prime-Agent-style harness and an N-agent swarm; log per-task tokens, latency, and signal-density metrics.
project_ideas.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD

project_ideas.based_on: RLMs enable models to generalize to longer tasks and different domains without changing the underlying base transformer.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Holding the base transformer fixed and varying only harness structure produces measurable generalization gains on longer tasks and shifted domains.
project_ideas.measurement: Out-of-distribution length and domain success delta attributable to harness changes alone.
project_ideas.name: Harness Isolation Testbed
project_ideas.poc: Run the same base model with and without RLM-style scaffolding across length-shifted and domain-shifted benchmarks, tracking isomorphic task trajectories.
project_ideas.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD

project_ideas.based_on: Solving complex tasks is often a skill and harness issue rather than a pure model intelligence limitation.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For failed multi-step workflows, redesigning harness/task decomposition recovers more success per dollar than upgrading the base model at the same compute budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate per dollar and per token; percentage of failures resolved by harness ablation versus model upgrade.
project_ideas.name: Mismanaged Genius Ablation Protocol
project_ideas.poc: Take failing agent workflows, apply decomposition/harness redesign versus a larger model, and compare success under matched token and latency budgets.
project_ideas.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD

project_ideas.based_on: Kernel writing has a severe verification and reward-hacking problem.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A correctness-and-generality adversarial suite will show that a material fraction of leaderboard-topping AI-generated GPU kernels fail outside their tuned workloads.
project_ideas.measurement: Failure rate outside tuned workloads; rank inversion between benchmark latency and verified correctness.
project_ideas.name: Adversarial Kernel Verification Suite
project_ideas.poc: Collect competitive AI-generated kernels; evaluate on mutated inputs, edge cases, varied shapes, and memory-hierarchy stress beyond the original benchmark.
project_ideas.video_title: Recursive Language Models — Alex Zhang, MIT PhD

project_ideas.based_on: Turn boundaries and endpointing are learned/predicted by the model rather than derived from VAD silence thresholds
project_ideas.hypothesis: A learned turn-taking model can match or exceed VAD-based endpointing on turn-taking accuracy while reducing p50 latency below 300ms and eliminating threshold-tuning on messy conversational audio.
project_ideas.measurement: Turn-taking accuracy, barge-in accuracy, p50/p95 latency, false interruption rate, and number of manually tuned thresholds.
project_ideas.name: Learned Endpointing Shootout
project_ideas.poc: Implement a VAD-threshold baseline and a learned endpointing model on the same real-world/noisy dialogue corpus; compare turn boundaries and barge-in handling.
project_ideas.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen

project_ideas.based_on: Dialog-RSN-1 splits the modality at a deliberate boundary
project_ideas.hypothesis: Attaching a deterministic harness (retrieval, tool calling, grounding, citations) to a text-emitting audio-native model preserves enterprise controllability and auditability without losing native audio understanding.
project_ideas.measurement: Tool-call accuracy, citation correctness, policy violation rate, auditability coverage, and added latency from the harness/TTS stage.
project_ideas.name: Text-Boundary Control Harness for Audio Agents
project_ideas.poc: Prototype an audio-in/text-out agent with a harness layer; add tool invocations, citations, and guardrails at the text boundary before TTS.
project_ideas.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen

project_ideas.based_on: Latency in voice agents is framed as a trust/psychological-safety variable
project_ideas.hypothesis: User trust and abandonment follow a measurable curve over agent silence latency, with p95 latency predicting abandonment more strongly than p50.
project_ideas.measurement: Trust scores, abandonment rate, panic/confusion indicators, and the latency value where trust drops sharply.
project_ideas.name: Voice Latency Trust Curve
project_ideas.poc: Run a controlled user study or simulation with voice agents that vary silence/latency distributions across p50/p95/p99; record trust and abandonment responses.
project_ideas.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen

project_ideas.based_on: Agent-generated outputs and the resulting context switching impose 'cognitive debt' on human operators
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent-generated messy outputs and required context switching measurably increase operator correction time and reduce throughput, captured by context-switch and correction-rate metrics.
project_ideas.measurement: Context switches per task, correction rate, time-to-completion, and subjective cognitive load.
project_ideas.name: Cognitive Debt Instrumentation for Agent Workflows
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent-assisted human workflow to log context switches, corrections, and handoffs; compare against a non-agent baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: How a Voice Agent Learns the Rhythm of Conversation — Shawn Wen

project_ideas.based_on: tighter primitives trade flexibility for reliable execution
project_ideas.hypothesis: For identical agent tasks, narrower and more explicitly constrained primitive/interface designs yield higher task success rates and lower rates of consequential error than broad or implicit designs, and this effect is larger than the effect of swapping model or prompt strategy.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, escaped-error rate, and error-mode distribution per primitive design; variance explained by primitive design versus model/prompt factors.
project_ideas.name: Primitive Surface Benchmark (PSB)
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark suite of identical coding/ops tasks executed by the same agent against deliberately varied primitive designs (narrow vs. broad, explicit vs. implicit constraints, typed vs. free-form tool schemas); run a factorial design crossing primitive design against model and prompt variant, and classify observed error modes.
project_ideas.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds

project_ideas.based_on: human-in-the-loop gates should be positioned at points of irreversible consequence, not evenly distributed
project_ideas.hypothesis: Consequence-boundary-only gating achieves a materially lower total cost (review latency × volume) than uniform review at an equal or better escaped-error rate, so long as irreversible actions are a minority of steps.
project_ideas.measurement: Reviewer minutes per task, escaped-error rate, and end-to-end latency per policy; break-even fraction of irreversible steps at which uniform review stops paying.
project_ideas.name: Gate Placement Cost Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Implement a pipeline replayer that takes recorded agent trajectories with a ground-truth label on which steps were irreversible, then simulates three gating policies (uniform review, consequence-boundary-only, no human gate) and measures reviewer minutes consumed and errors that escape.
project_ideas.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds

project_ideas.based_on: What portion of my daily work is pure implementation vs. product judgment?
project_ideas.hypothesis: The share of an engineer's tasks classified as pure implementation versus decision-making versus consequence-ownership shifts measurably within teams that adopt agent tooling, and a rising implementation share correlates with reduced scope ownership on subsequent quarters.
project_ideas.measurement: Weekly implementation/decision/consequence ratio per engineer; correlation between ratio trajectory and subsequent assigned scope or role changes.
project_ideas.name: Implementation-to-Judgment Ratio Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Ship a lightweight task taxonomy and tagging workflow (a three-category classifier over tickets, PRs, and meeting notes, with human confirmation) that emits a weekly ratio per engineer and per team; run it across two agent-adopting teams for a quarter.
project_ideas.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds

project_ideas.based_on: volume-based productivity metrics lose all signal and must be replaced by outcome-linked measures
project_ideas.hypothesis: Once implementation generation is cheap, output-volume metrics (lines, PRs, features) decouple from user-outcome metrics, and engineering dashboards that retain them actively mislead prioritization; volume metrics remain predictive only in repositories where generation cost is still high.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation and rank-agreement between volume metrics and outcome metrics, stratified by agent-tooling adoption level; direction of prioritization errors when optimizing volume.
project_ideas.name: Output-Metric Signal Decay Audit
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a longitudinal dataset pairing per-sprint output-volume metrics with downstream user-outcome or business metrics across repos with differing levels of agent-tooling adoption, and test whether the volume-to-outcome correlation degrades as agent adoption rises.
project_ideas.video_title: The Last Software Engineer - Kent C. Dodds

project_ideas.based_on: perform the task manually about five times first
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automating a task after five manual executions yields a higher agent success rate and lower rework than automating after three or ten executions for tasks of moderate complexity.
project_ideas.measurement: Agent success rate (human-judged), average number of corrections per output, and time-to-automation.
project_ideas.name: Five-Time Automation Threshold Experiment
project_ideas.poc: Select a common knowledge-work task (e.g., drafting meeting follow-ups). Manually execute it 10 times, capturing traces. Build agents that automate the task after N=3, 5, and 10 executions. Evaluate each agent on 20 new instances, measuring success and rework.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg Brockman

project_ideas.based_on: running against cloud apps independently of the user's device
project_ideas.hypothesis: A cloud-side agent with scoped OAuth credentials, durable task state, and an audit log can reliably perform background research and calendar management without user intervention, with no unintended actions.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, number of unintended side effects, successful recovery from credential expiry, and audit log completeness.
project_ideas.name: Persistent Agent Runtime with Scoped Credentials
project_ideas.poc: Build a prototype agent that connects to Google Calendar and Gmail with read-only and limited write scopes. It runs on a schedule to prepare daily briefings and draft follow-ups. Log all actions. Simulate credential expiry and duplicate triggers to test durability.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg Brockman

project_ideas.based_on: The guest-house anecdote is a reported instance
project_ideas.hypothesis: A structured review interface with diff annotations and domain-specific checklists improves the acceptance rate of agent-generated CAD floor plans by contractors compared to raw output.
project_ideas.measurement: Acceptance rate (contractor willingness to bid/use), number of corrections requested, and time spent reviewing.
project_ideas.name: Domain Expert Review Interface for Agent-Generated Artifacts
project_ideas.poc: Generate simple residential floor plans using an AI model. Have contractors review them either as raw images or through a purpose-built review tool that highlights changes and prompts for corrections. Measure acceptance and corrections.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg Brockman

project_ideas.based_on: Voice mode bound to tools is presented as the low-friction control plane
project_ideas.hypothesis: Swapping a voice interface for a chat interface over the same tool layer does not significantly change task success or user effort for email and scheduling tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, time on task, and user-reported effort.
project_ideas.name: Modality-Independent Tool Layer for Personal Agents
project_ideas.poc: Implement a tool layer for email and calendar. Expose both voice and chat interfaces. Have users complete a set of tasks with each modality. Measure task success and time on task.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Co-Founder: Start Building With AI Before You Feel Ready | Greg Brockman

project_ideas.based_on: Code generation is not the bottleneck; code gen represents only 14-16% of the overall value stream.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A specialized agent deployed at the highest cycle-time-contribution non-code stage will reduce end-to-end lead time more than an equal-effort investment in code generation, because code generation is a small share of the value stream.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-stage cycle-time share before/after, end-to-end lead time, median PR throughput, and deployment frequency, compared against a control repository set with no new agent.
project_ideas.name: Value-Stream Bottleneck Ranker
project_ideas.poc: Instrument repo, pipeline, review, and incident telemetry to attribute cycle time per stage across a small set of repositories; rank stages by contribution and wait-state share; deploy one narrow agent (e.g., review or incident triage) at the top-ranked stage while holding the coding copilot constant.
project_ideas.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX

project_ideas.based_on: Code maintainability perceived score went up ~4%, but change confidence went down ~6%.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An evaluation harness that measures reviewer change confidence separately from maintainability will flag AI-assisted PRs that pass maintainability scoring but carry low reviewer trust; a PR-size-aware review policy can restore confidence without reducing throughput.
project_ideas.measurement: Change confidence delta per cohort, PR size distribution, review depth (comments per PR, review latency), escaped defect and change failure rate, with throughput held as a non-regression constraint.
project_ideas.name: Change-Confidence Instrument
project_ideas.poc: Ship a paired instrument that captures maintainability and change confidence per PR alongside PR size, then A/B test an AI-specific review checklist applied above a size threshold.
project_ideas.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX

project_ideas.based_on: AI readiness depends on clear documentation, data structures, manageable code, fast local CI, and non-flaky test suites.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Organizations and repositories meeting explicit test-determinism and local CI latency thresholds show measurably higher AI impact scores and higher agent task success rates than those that do not, so readiness should gate agent rollout.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between readiness tier and measured AI impact metrics, agent task success and retry rates, local CI latency and flake rate, with adoption/utilization telemetry joined to DORA/DevEx outcome metrics.
project_ideas.name: Agent Readiness Gate
project_ideas.poc: Define a readiness scorecard (documentation, data structures, code manageability, local CI latency, flake rate) and wire it as a pre-rollout gate for agent enablement in one org unit; run a second unit ungated as a comparison.
project_ideas.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX

project_ideas.based_on: median PR throughput increased by 7.76% and average by 13.1% in longitudinal studies
project_ideas.hypothesis: Within-org matched-cohort and interrupted time-series comparison will shrink the observed AI throughput effect relative to naive org-level trends, because deployment-frequency trends, regional shifts, and general tooling improvements absorb part of the measured gain.
project_ideas.measurement: Effect-size difference between naive trend estimates and matched-cohort estimates for PR throughput and perceived rate of delivery, with sensitivity to cohort matching criteria.
project_ideas.name: Matched-Cohort AI Impact Estimator
project_ideas.poc: Build an analysis harness that pairs AI-adopting teams with non-adopting teams inside the same organization on matched baselines, plus an interrupted time-series around adoption dates, and report confidence intervals on the effect.
project_ideas.video_title: The State of AI in Software Development: Data from 400+ Orgs — Justin Reock, DX

project_ideas.based_on: AI models score significantly lower on human review rubrics than on standard test execution
project_ideas.hypothesis: A human-authorable mergeability rubric applied to the same PRs that pass their test suites will flag a substantial fraction of test-passing PRs as unmergeable, and rubric scores will correlate with human maintainer decisions better than test-pass outcomes do.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence rate between test-pass and human-unmergeable verdicts; Spearman correlation of model rubric scores versus maintainer scores; per-dimension false-negative rates.
project_ideas.name: MergeabilityRubric-Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build an evaluation dataset of PRs that pass CI, have domain maintainers score each on an explicit multi-dimension mergeability rubric (external quality, side effects, subtle bug risk), then score the same PRs with frontier models under both a test-pass lens and a rubric lens, reporting rank correlation against maintainer verdicts.
project_ideas.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: Running multiple review passes over code diffs with shuffled reviewer orders and explicit instructions to be suspicious
project_ideas.hypothesis: Multiple review passes over identical diffs with shuffled reviewer order and a default-suspicion instruction reduce reviewer false negatives on vulnerable-code diffs compared with a single trusting pass, and false-negative rate falls monotonically with pass count up to a saturation point.
project_ideas.measurement: False-negative rate versus single-pass baseline; delta per additional pass; cost in tokens/latency per incremental true finding.
project_ideas.name: SuspicionEnsemble Reviewer
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that runs K passes with randomized pass ordering and a suspicion-defaulted prompt, then evaluate on a red-team set of vulnerable diffs framed with clean commit messages and plausible structure; ablate pass count, ordering shuffles, and instruction stance.
project_ideas.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: Anthropic's security reviewer fooled 88% of the time by vulnerable code
project_ideas.hypothesis: Removing persuasive content from the reviewer's input channel (structuring the diff and commit narrative so producer-authored framing cannot act as evidence) reduces the rate at which a reviewer is talked out of its own findings.
project_ideas.measurement: Finding-suppression rate per input mode; proportion of cases where the reviewer reverses an initially correct finding after reading producer framing.
project_ideas.name: Reviewer Trust-Boundary Harness
project_ideas.poc: Implement three reviewer input modes — raw diff plus author narrative, diff with narrative stripped, and diff plus narrative isolated as untrusted quoted data — and measure finding-dismissal behavior on the same adversarial diff set.
project_ideas.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: What is the minimal human-in-the-loop configuration that preserves mergeability without recreating the human-speed bottleneck?
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists a human intervention placement (rubric authoring plus sampled meta-review) that retains mergeability at human-review levels while raising shipped-software throughput above the full-manual-review ceiling, and it outperforms both full manual review and zero human review.
project_ideas.measurement: Shipped-change throughput per configuration versus human mergeability acceptance rate; frontier of throughput against mergeability rejection rate; human hours consumed per 100 merged changes.
project_ideas.name: Human-In-The-Loop Placement Sweep
project_ideas.poc: Configure a review pipeline where the human role is parameterized across placements — none, rubric author only, sampling reviewer of diffs, meta-reviewer of agent findings, full manual — and run each configuration against a fixed backlog of agent-generated changes with a mergeability success/failure outcome per change.
project_ideas.video_title: The Death of the Code Review: What the Data Actually Says — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: The proof exploited one bug in the official Lean kernel and a completely different bug in nanoda.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Given two independently-implemented checkers of the same logic, an automated generator with bounded search budget can find at least one input accepted by both while being semantically false, at a materially higher rate than a single-checker prober finds on one implementation.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of joint accept-false findings per 1,000 generated candidates versus single-checker findings, and overlap between the bug classes each checker is defeated by.
project_ideas.name: Dual-Checker Adversarial Prober
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness with two structurally distinct validators (e.g., a reference checker and an independent reimplementation) plus a generator that mutates candidate artifacts to maximize acceptance under each; log every case where both accept a known-false artifact.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Can Write the Proof. Who Checks It? — Leonardo de Moura

project_ideas.based_on: AI can optimize code from high-level specifications without breaking semantic properties.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a benchmark suite of imperative routines, an AI optimizer that must produce machine-checked equivalence to an unoptimized reference implementation will maintain functional correctness at a fixed success rate while achieving measurable performance gains, and failures will cluster in specific semantic property classes.
project_ideas.measurement: Fraction of optimizations that pass equivalence checking, average speedup, and a taxonomy of the semantic properties that failed first.
project_ideas.name: Spec-Equivalence Gate
project_ideas.poc: Take a set of small imperative programs, treat the unoptimized versions as specifications, have an agent generate optimized implementations, and gate each on a checker that proves equivalence (e.g., extensional equality on all inputs within a modeled domain).
project_ideas.video_title: AI Can Write the Proof. Who Checks It? — Leonardo de Moura

project_ideas.based_on: Lean relies on a small trusted kernel surrounded by a vast ecosystem of libraries and community extensions.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a small-trusted-core platform with a large extension ecosystem, the majority of realistically exploitable trust assumptions live outside the core, so overall risk is dominated by extension volume rather than core size.
project_ideas.measurement: Count and severity of successful trust violations per component class, and the share attributable to non-core components.
project_ideas.name: Trust-Surface Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a kernel-plus-extensions system, enumerate every component that can influence acceptance of an artifact, and classify each as core, library, or community extension; then run a targeted probe suite against each class.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Can Write the Proof. Who Checks It? — Leonardo de Moura

project_ideas.based_on: Some estimate that capturing all mainstream mathematics will require 100 million lines of Lean.
project_ideas.hypothesis: There is a repository-size threshold beyond which human-only contribution throughput falls below the rate required to maintain the library, and agent-assisted contribution above that threshold requires provenance and spot-audit tooling to keep defect escape rates at human-only levels.
project_ideas.measurement: Contribution throughput and defect escape rate versus library size for each mode, and the size at which human-only throughput saturates.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Library Maintenance Threshold Study
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a growing structured library with both human-only and human-plus-agent contribution modes across increasing sizes, tracking defect rate, review backlog, and provenance completeness.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Can Write the Proof. Who Checks It? — Leonardo de Moura

project_ideas.based_on: Containment and real-time monitoring are critical for agentic systems.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Hardware-accelerated monitoring and isolated browser containers add less than 10% p95 latency overhead while increasing unsafe-action detection by at least 2x over software-only logging.
project_ideas.measurement: p95 latency overhead, unsafe-action detection rate, false-positive rate, task success rate.
project_ideas.name: Containment Overhead Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build an agent testbed that runs browser automation tasks under Open Shell-like containment with a Bluefield-like monitoring emulator, comparing isolated vs unisolated runs.

project_ideas.based_on: Is the claimed 1:1 correlation between incremental power and GDP causal
project_ideas.hypothesis: After controlling for industrialization and grid efficiency, the marginal GDP effect of incremental steady-state power generation is significantly below 1% per 5 GW.
project_ideas.measurement: Estimated marginal coefficient, confidence interval, and out-of-sample prediction error against the claimed 1% per 5 GW rate.
project_ideas.name: Power-GDP Causal Testbench
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a cross-region panel dataset of power generation and GDP, then run fixed-effects and Granger causality tests to estimate marginal effects.

project_ideas.based_on: Can orbital compute overcome latency and data transfer challenges
project_ideas.hypothesis: Orbital compute is infeasible for interactive agents requiring <100 ms response but viable for batch jobs with deadlines above 5 minutes.
project_ideas.measurement: Deadline miss rate and throughput as a function of latency tolerance, data volume, and caching strategy.
project_ideas.name: Orbital Inference Latency Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Simulate LEO and GEO round-trip latencies, downlink bandwidth, and caching strategies against representative interactive and batch AI workloads.

project_ideas.based_on: Every layer of the computing stack has been reinvented.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Traditional CPU/GPU benchmarks have weak correlation with real generative AI deployment metrics such as tokens per second per watt and memory bandwidth per parameter.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman correlation between traditional benchmarks and tokens/sec/watt; ranking disagreement across hardware.
project_ideas.name: Generative Stack Performance Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Benchmark a set of generative inference/training workloads across chips and runtimes, then correlate traditional benchmark scores with deployment metrics.

project_ideas.based_on: Define proxy metrics for optionality (change-cost, backwards-compatibility surface, coupling)
project_ideas.hypothesis: A composite optionality index built from change-cost probes, backwards-compatibility surface, and coupling measures will detect declining architectural optionality before feature throughput visibly stalls, and pacing feature intake against that index will prevent the zero-change state in a simulated or real codebase.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence of the optionality index between paced and unpaced branches, time-to-zero-change proxy (change-cost crossing a threshold), and feature throughput retained per branch.
project_ideas.name: Futures Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a mid-sized repository with automated change-cost probes (task-based modification benchmarks), compatibility-surface scoring, and coupling metrics; replay AI-accelerated feature work in an unpaced control branch and a paced branch with a refactoring budget, and compare index trajectories.
project_ideas.video_title: Kent Beck: Software Engineering in the Age of AI | Prodacity 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Build executable/differential test harnesses for generated artifacts and benchmark their detection rate versus human review
project_ideas.hypothesis: An executable and differential verification harness positioned between AI generation and acceptance will detect syntactically valid but non-functional artifacts at a higher defect-per-review-hour rate than adversarial human reading of the same diffs.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate, false-positive rate, defects found per review-hour, and escaped-defect count for harness versus human review.
project_ideas.name: Semantic Gate
project_ideas.poc: Take a corpus of AI-generated artifacts of the C-compiler kind (plausible structure, non-working behavior), run them through generated test oracles, differential execution against reference implementations, and property checks, then benchmark detection against human reviewers under matched time budgets.
project_ideas.video_title: Kent Beck: Software Engineering in the Age of AI | Prodacity 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Do mandated pause points in a generation workflow measurably improve final code correctness or rework rates?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Inserting mandated reflection checkpoints into an AI-assisted generation workflow reduces rework rate and escaping defects compared with continuous uninterrupted generation, without a proportional loss in delivered feature scope.
project_ideas.measurement: Rework hours, escaped defects, and net delivered scope per workflow across matched tasks.
project_ideas.name: Pause Protocol Study
project_ideas.poc: Run matched feature tasks under two workflows — continuous generation and checkpointed generation with enforced stop-and-reflect intervals and a next-morning re-implementation option — recording rework, defect escapes, and delivered scope.
project_ideas.video_title: Kent Beck: Software Engineering in the Age of AI | Prodacity 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Prototype outcome instrumentation and check whether it remains resistant to output-volume gaming
project_ideas.hypothesis: Outcome-linked instrumentation (behavior change and mission indicators) remains resistant to output-volume gaming, whereas effort-volume proxies degrade measurably when generation becomes cheap.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between each metric family and independently assessed outcome, plus magnitude of drift under gaming pressure.
project_ideas.name: Downstream Meter
project_ideas.poc: Prototype outcome instrumentation alongside legacy effort metrics in one team's AI-assisted workflow, then run a deliberate gaming trial where participants optimize each metric set, and compare metric-to-outcome correlation drift.
project_ideas.video_title: Kent Beck: Software Engineering in the Age of AI | Prodacity 2026

project_ideas.based_on: safety safeguards in open-source models are virtually nonexistent
project_ideas.hypothesis: A gateway that screens non-model-layer effects (synthesis-relevant sequences, privileged tool invocations, outbound network actions) can flag a measurable fraction of red-team hazardous-use traces produced by uncensored open-weight models, at a false-positive rate low enough for production deployment — despite receiving no cooperation from the model.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection recall on the red-team corpus, false-positive rate per 1,000 benign tool calls, and recall degradation as the attacking model is swapped or re-prompted to avoid the monitor.
project_ideas.name: Effect-Layer Misuse Gate
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a policy gateway in front of tool and network egress for a locally-run uncensored model, define a small red-team corpus of hazardous-use traces, and measure detection recall against benign workloads.
project_ideas.video_title: Bill Gates: A.I. ‘Makes Nuclear Weapons Look Like Nothing’ | The Ezra Klein Show

project_ideas.based_on: the demand for human cognitive labor may shrink as AI achieves superiority in coding, legal work, and healthcare support
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-task cost reduction from AI assistance produces task-count growth that exceeds it in some cognitive task classes and lags it in others, so aggregate labor-demand claims are artifacts of task-class weighting.
project_ideas.measurement: Estimated elasticity per task class, dispersion of elasticity estimates across classes, and whether any class shows volume growth below unit-cost decline.
project_ideas.name: Task-Level Cognitive Elasticity Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a per-task-class panel across coding, legal work, and healthcare support that tracks unit cost per completed task against task volume, then fit separate elasticities rather than one aggregate curve.
project_ideas.video_title: Bill Gates: A.I. ‘Makes Nuclear Weapons Look Like Nothing’ | The Ezra Klein Show

project_ideas.based_on: process massive domains like medicine simultaneously
project_ideas.hypothesis: On cross-domain reasoning tasks at equal token and tool-call budget, a single broad-context agent matches or beats a domain-specialist multi-agent decomposition, because the specialist split adds handoff loss without relieving the real bottleneck.
project_ideas.measurement: Task accuracy per architecture at matched budget, total tokens per solved task, and handoff-related failure rate in the multi-agent arm.
project_ideas.name: Bottleneck-First Agent Decomposition Study
project_ideas.poc: Implement both architectures over the same tool set and model, hold total token and tool-call budgets constant, and run them on cross-domain medical and reasoning evaluations.
project_ideas.video_title: Bill Gates: A.I. ‘Makes Nuclear Weapons Look Like Nothing’ | The Ezra Klein Show

project_ideas.based_on: The subjective human element remains crucial in fields like mental health support and education.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Domains requiring mandatory human-in-the-loop handoff can be predicted by an operational score combining user escalation frequency, cost-of-undetected-error, and subjective-evaluation share, rather than being asserted by domain label alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Separation of the composite score between domains, correlation between score and observed escalation rate, and calibration/refusal behavior when no human corrector is present.
project_ideas.name: Mandatory Handoff Boundary Detector
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an assistive agent in two contrasting domains (educational tutoring vs. a hedged factual advisory task), log escalation and downstream error cost, and test whether the composite score separates domains where users reject autonomous output.
project_ideas.video_title: Bill Gates: A.I. ‘Makes Nuclear Weapons Look Like Nothing’ | The Ezra Klein Show

project_ideas.based_on: Traditional banking infrastructure is ill-equipped for autonomous AI agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: For identical agent payment workloads (small-value, high-frequency, machine-initiated), tokenized rails achieve higher end-to-end success rate and lower p95 latency and per-transaction cost than card/bank rails, and legacy rails fail disproportionately on availability windows rather than on latency.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per transaction, retries to completion, manual reconciliation events per 1,000 transactions.
project_ideas.name: Agent Rail Bench
project_ideas.poc: Harness that executes the same synthetic agent workload (thousands of micropayments with retries and idempotency keys) against at least one stablecoin rail and one card/bank rail, logging success, latency, cost, reconciliation overhead, and a failure taxonomy per rail.
project_ideas.video_title: Cathie Wood on Tesla-SpaceX Merger, $1M Bitcoin, More AIs Than Humans | EP #296 | Moonshots Live

project_ideas.based_on: identity, spend-limit, and abuse-control primitives
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scoped, revocable credentials with hard per-transaction and cumulative budget caps reduce unauthorized or over-limit agent payments to zero in prompt-injection overpayment scenarios without reducing legitimate task completion rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of over-cap or unauthorized payments executed (target zero), task completion delta versus unscoped baseline, revocation propagation time, audit-log completeness.
project_ideas.name: Scoped Agent Spend Gate
project_ideas.poc: Prototype delegation tokens per agent with per-counterparty allowlists, hard caps, revocation, and an audit log; red-team with injection prompts instructing the agent to overpay or pay a new counterparty.
project_ideas.video_title: Cathie Wood on Tesla-SpaceX Merger, $1M Bitcoin, More AIs Than Humans | EP #296 | Moonshots Live

project_ideas.based_on: more AIs than humans next year
project_ideas.hypothesis: Under an explicit count definition (distinct authenticated agent principals plus live concurrent sessions), the agent-to-human ratio on instrumented services grows faster than human session growth and crosses defined thresholds within a 12-month window.
project_ideas.measurement: Distinct agent principals versus human users, agent-to-human session ratio trend, sub-agents per parent agent, and utilization shift of existing quota and rate-limit ceilings.
project_ideas.name: Agent Census
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a set of services to emit session-level telemetry separating agent traffic from human traffic, including identity class and parent-child spawn lineage for sub-agents, then compute agent-to-human ratios daily.
project_ideas.video_title: Cathie Wood on Tesla-SpaceX Merger, $1M Bitcoin, More AIs Than Humans | EP #296 | Moonshots Live

project_ideas.based_on: USDC has settled over $100 trillion across over 30 public blockchains
project_ideas.hypothesis: Deduplicated, unique-counterparty settlement volume is a small and stable fraction of the headline cumulative transfer figure, making the gross-to-net ratio a necessary standard reporting adjustment for any rail comparison.
project_ideas.measurement: Gross-to-net volume ratio, count of unique counterparties, share of transfers attributable to internal or repeated transfers, and year-over-year stability of the ratio.
project_ideas.name: Net Settlement Audit
project_ideas.poc: Reconstruct the settlement metric from primary on-chain sources with explicit definitions (gross versus net, unique counterparties, fixed time window) and decompose volume into internal, churn, and distinct economic activity.
project_ideas.video_title: Cathie Wood on Tesla-SpaceX Merger, $1M Bitcoin, More AIs Than Humans | EP #296 | Moonshots Live

project_ideas.based_on: How can teams measure compounding understanding versus raw code output?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams that maintain an explicit, queryable context ledger of customer signals, decisions, and rationale will make faster and more repeatable product decisions than teams optimizing output volume alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Decision reuse rate, time-to-decision, repeat customer question rate, and correlation with customer-value outcomes.
project_ideas.name: Context Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Instrument issue tracker, support conversations, and decision logs; use agents to generate weekly understanding diffs and decision-reuse reports; compare against LOC and ticket throughput.
project_ideas.video_title: Context is now the product: Product leadership when software can build itself | Karri Saarinen

project_ideas.based_on: What are the reliability limits of auto-fix bots?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Observability-driven patch agents with mandatory test gating, canary rollout, and automatic rollback reduce MTTR without increasing incident recurrence or false fixes.
project_ideas.measurement: False-fix rate, rollback rate, MTTR, incident recurrence, and engineer verification time.
project_ideas.name: Auto-Fix Safety Harness
project_ideas.poc: Connect Sentry and DataDog to issue tracker; generate patches for top recurring bugs; require CI, human approval, and rollback on failed canary.
project_ideas.video_title: Context is now the product: Product leadership when software can build itself | Karri Saarinen

project_ideas.based_on: How should the boundary between known and unknown tasks be drawn and updated?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Explicit known/unknown classification and routing increases agent-handled throughput without reducing human time spent on customer problems, exploration, judgment, and quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Routing accuracy, agent throughput, human time on unknown work, customer insight freshness, and quality regressions.
project_ideas.name: Known/Unknown Router
project_ideas.poc: Build a classifier over the backlog; route known bug fixes, triage, and FAQ to agents; route unknown customer discovery to humans; log reclassifications as model capabilities change.
project_ideas.video_title: Context is now the product: Product leadership when software can build itself | Karri Saarinen

project_ideas.based_on: How can shared taste and quality calibration be systematized in AI-heavy teams?
