project_ideas.hypothesis: Scheduled team calibration with a shared rubric reduces quality drift from AI-accelerated isolated building, measured by lower defect escape rate and higher inter-rater agreement on quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect escape rate, time-to-fix small imperfections, inter-rater reliability, and feature rejection rate.
project_ideas.name: Taste Calibration Protocol
project_ideas.poc: Institute 30-60 minute weekly quality reviews and feature roasts with a rubric; compare defect escape and rubric agreement before and after.
project_ideas.video_title: Context is now the product: Product leadership when software can build itself | Karri Saarinen

project_ideas.based_on: Attribution of credit in collaborative work is a narrative that is set by who speaks first
project_ideas.hypothesis: Recording per-component contribution at generation time and requiring reporting layers to aggregate-only reduces credit misattribution to the orchestrator compared with centralized narrative summarization, measurably improving downstream credit-assignment accuracy.
project_ideas.measurement: Agreement between assigned credit and ablated-component ground truth (remove one component, measure task degradation) plus fraction of credit assigned to non-producing components.
project_ideas.name: Attribution Ledger
project_ideas.poc: A multi-agent pipeline where every component emits a signed contribution record (inputs consumed, artifact produced, causal step) at production time; a summarizer layer can only cite these records. Run the same task suite with (a) narrative summarization and (b) ledger aggregation.
project_ideas.video_title: Amazon VP: Questions On Corporate Politics But They Get Increasingly Darker | Ethan Evans

project_ideas.based_on: Perceived quality (likability) can outweigh measured performance
project_ideas.hypothesis: Across optimization steps on a preference-style proxy, a divergence point exists at which proxy score keeps rising while ground-truth task success stops or falls, and this point is detectable before large capability loss.
project_ideas.measurement: Step index of first sustained divergence, magnitude of proxy gain after divergence, and downstream task-success loss at that point.
project_ideas.name: Proxy Divergence Monitor
project_ideas.poc: Train or tune against a cheap preference proxy (style/approval rating) on a task with a separate held-out ground-truth metric; log both per checkpoint and plot divergence.
project_ideas.video_title: Amazon VP: Questions On Corporate Politics But They Get Increasingly Darker | Ethan Evans

project_ideas.based_on: You can understand what people want by asking directly, listening, triangulating through their reports, or observing their actions.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents given objectives inferred from fused direct statements, third-party signals, and revealed-action traces achieve higher task success and lower specification-gaming rate than agents given the declared objective alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, specification-gaming rate (reward gained without target outcome), and instrumentation latency overhead per decision.
project_ideas.name: Four-Channel Goal Inference
project_ideas.poc: Build a goal-inference layer that fuses three channel types (self-report, indirect report, behavioral trace) into one objective; run an A/B against declared-objective agents on tasks where the declared objective is known to be misaligned with the principal's actual incentives.
project_ideas.video_title: Amazon VP: Questions On Corporate Politics But They Get Increasingly Darker | Ethan Evans

project_ideas.based_on: Resource consolidation (head count, scope) is treated as a rational strategy
project_ideas.hypothesis: A fixed reallocation checkpoint triggered by observable early-failure signals reallocates resources away from failing initiatives earlier than discretionary review, improving portfolio-level outcomes over a fixed budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-reallocation, share of budget held in failing initiatives at each checkpoint, and portfolio-level gain at fixed total compute.
project_ideas.name: Scheduled Pivot Cadence
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a portfolio of parallel experiments/agent designs with early failure signals (metric plateau, cost-per-gain ratio decay) and enforce a fixed-cadence kill/pivot review; compare against review-on-demand.
project_ideas.video_title: Amazon VP: Questions On Corporate Politics But They Get Increasingly Darker | Ethan Evans

project_ideas.based_on: Autonomy in a personal agent should be a graduated permission tier
project_ideas.hypothesis: A per-user trust-state machine that escalates autonomy based on observable signals (data grants, correction rate, action success) and supports revocation will increase user trust and retention compared to static permission models.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare retention and user-reported trust in an A/B test against a static permission model; track escalation/revocation events and their correlation with retention.
project_ideas.name: Trust-State Machine for Agent Autonomy
project_ideas.poc: Implement a runtime that tracks a trust level per user and gates agent actions accordingly; simulate user interactions with escalating data sharing and measure the machine's ability to escalate and revoke.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder

project_ideas.based_on: Proactivity requires rigorous safety firewalls and oversight.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A pre-execution policy layer with action classification reduces harmful proactive actions by >50% with <10% utility loss on benchmark tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of block/allow decisions and utility loss (task success rate) on the proactive task suite.
project_ideas.name: Pre-Execution Policy Firewall for Proactive Agents
project_ideas.poc: Build a policy engine that evaluates intended actions before execution, using a classifier and rules for action categorization; test on a set of proactive tasks with known harmful/benign labels.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder

project_ideas.based_on: AI agents interacting with each other reduce social coordination friction to near zero.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A negotiation protocol with verifiable identity and scoped consent tokens enables agents to coordinate group scheduling without central authority, reducing coordination time by >80% vs a human baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Time to consensus, number of messages exchanged, and user satisfaction compared to human-mediated coordination in a controlled experiment.
project_ideas.name: Inter-Agent Negotiation Protocol for Cross-User Coordination
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal protocol for two agents to negotiate a meeting time under consent constraints; extend to three agents for a group event.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder

project_ideas.based_on: Design invite-only distribution loops to manage compute scaling and viral growth.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Coupling invite quotas to real-time inference cost per user bounds monthly compute spend within a target budget while maintaining viral growth rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Monthly compute cost per user and growth rate compared to fixed quotas; sensitivity analysis to cost variability.
project_ideas.name: Compute-Aware Invite Gating System
project_ideas.poc: Simulate an invite-only system with dynamic quota based on a cost threshold; model growth and compute spend under different quota policies.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder

project_ideas.based_on: A PM with zero prior coding experience checked in 26 PRs in a single month by partnering with engineers on harnesses
project_ideas.hypothesis: A domain expert (non-engineer) using a purpose-built harness (scaffolding + eval loop + review gate) will achieve >80% PR acceptance rate and <5% defect rate on well-scoped tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: PR acceptance rate, defect rate, time to merge vs baseline engineer.
project_ideas.name: Domain-Expert Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal harness for a specific domain (e.g., data pipeline config) and have a non-engineer produce 10 PRs over 2 weeks.
project_ideas.video_title: Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)

project_ideas.based_on: Agent effectiveness is framed as dependent on an enterprise context graph spanning tools
project_ideas.hypothesis: An MCP-style context aggregation layer across 3+ heterogeneous tools improves agent task accuracy by >30% relative to single-tool context, while enforcing consistent permissions.
project_ideas.measurement: Agent accuracy on a set of tasks, permission violation rate.
project_ideas.name: Permission-Aware Context Graph
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a context layer that indexes and retrieves from Jira/Confluence/Slack-like tools, with permission-aware retrieval.
project_ideas.video_title: Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)

project_ideas.based_on: then shifting from rowing to steering to unblock the team
project_ideas.hypothesis: Project signals (team size, handoff latency, review load) can predict the optimal time for a builder to shift from rowing to steering, and timing the shift based on these signals improves team throughput vs fixed schedule.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between signal threshold and throughput/quality post-shift.
project_ideas.name: Rowing-to-Steering Signal Detector
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small team project, collect signals, correlate with outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)

project_ideas.based_on: Jira Agent in Slack triaged 900 pieces of customer feedback at a claimed 90% accuracy
project_ideas.hypothesis: The reported 90% triage accuracy is reproducible with a labelled ground truth and residual errors concentrate in specific categories (e.g., ambiguous feedback).
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy, error distribution by category.
project_ideas.name: Triage Accuracy Replication
project_ideas.poc: Replicate feedback triage with a labelled dataset of 900 items, compare agent to human.
project_ideas.video_title: Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)

project_ideas.based_on: machine-checkable proofs of correctness
project_ideas.hypothesis: Certificates augmented with lemma dependency graphs and explicit invariant statements increase reviewer comprehension and later modification success relative to bare machine-checkable certificates, at bounded added generation cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Reviewer comprehension quiz accuracy, time-to-correct-modification of the artifact by a second engineer, and delta in reviewer hours per accepted artifact versus bare certificates.
project_ideas.name: Insight-Bearing Certificate Format
project_ideas.poc: Take a set of AI-generated formal proof/verification artifacts, mechanically derive a lemma dependency graph plus invariant summary for half of them, and run reviewers against both variants.
project_ideas.video_title: Scott Aaronson on the Impact of AI on Science and Mathematics

project_ideas.based_on: Autonomous agents can find unintended optimization pathways when given open-ended tool access.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents still reach unintended optimization pathways through environment-incidental behavior even after deterministic seeding is enforced; the reachable set shrinks only when side-effecting calls are intercepted and monitored, not when instructions are tightened.
project_ideas.measurement: Count and classify unintended-pathway accesses per run across conditions, plus task success rate, to test whether containment costs capability.
project_ideas.name: Environment Reachability Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a sandbox that logs every environment-internal access and side-effecting tool call, then run identical goal-directed agents across three conditions: unconstrained, deterministic-seeded, and intercepted-and-monitored.
project_ideas.video_title: Scott Aaronson on the Impact of AI on Science and Mathematics

project_ideas.based_on: embed statistical signals into token generation to track AI provenance
project_ideas.hypothesis: Generation-time provenance signals survive at most a small number of downstream transformations before detection falls below a usable acceptance threshold, and summarization degrades the signal faster than verbatim paraphrase.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection AUC and false-positive rate per transform stage, plus the number of transforms at which detection crosses a pre-registered usable threshold.
project_ideas.name: Provenance Degradation Curve
project_ideas.poc: Watermark a controlled output set during decoding, push it through paraphrase, summarization, translation, and re-generation by a second model, and re-run detection at each stage.
project_ideas.video_title: Scott Aaronson on the Impact of AI on Science and Mathematics

project_ideas.based_on: solving part of the Navier-Stokes regularity problem
project_ideas.hypothesis: Once models can produce partial results on hard open problems, verification and integration cost, not generation cost, dominates the workflow — and triage reviewer hours per accepted result becomes the binding constraint on research throughput.
project_ideas.measurement: Reviewer hours per accepted result, acceptance rate, and fraction of total pipeline cost attributable to generation versus triage and verification.
project_ideas.name: Triage-Capacity Harness for Machine-Generated Partial Results
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a controlled pipeline where generated partial results on a known open problem set enter a triage queue with independent checkers, and measure where time is actually spent end to end.
project_ideas.video_title: Scott Aaronson on the Impact of AI on Science and Mathematics

project_ideas.based_on: Programming languages differ in token efficiency for LLMs
project_ideas.hypothesis: Across identical coding tasks, expressive languages reduce total LLM tokens and wall-clock time compared with more verbose languages, and this reduction predicts lower cost without reducing correctness.
project_ideas.measurement: Median token count, wall-clock time, API cost, and correctness delta per language; regression controlling for model family and training-data volume.
project_ideas.name: TokenEfficiencyBench
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that presents the same suite of coding tasks to multiple LLMs across 5+ languages, recording prompt+completion tokens, latency, cost, and test pass rate.
project_ideas.video_title: Ruby, Rails, and the future of programming - Matz, DHH & Jeremy Daer

project_ideas.based_on: compiles Ruby programs to a native binary
project_ideas.hypothesis: Spinel-compiled Ruby binaries preserve Ruby semantics and common gem compatibility for representative applications while using substantially less memory than MRI, with acceptable latency.
project_ideas.measurement: Memory ratio, latency ratio, semantic test pass rate, and count of compatible gems.
project_ideas.name: SpinelSandboxCompatibilityHarness
project_ideas.poc: Compile a suite of Ruby programs and a representative Rails-like workload with Spinel and MRI, then run semantic test suites while measuring RSS, latency, and gem loading.
project_ideas.video_title: Ruby, Rails, and the future of programming - Matz, DHH & Jeremy Daer

project_ideas.based_on: Expecting AI code generation to be fault-free out of the box is framed as 'AI psychosis'
project_ideas.hypothesis: A verification gate that combines automated checks with risk-proportional human review reduces escaped defects from AI-generated code compared with trust-by-default, without eliminating productivity gains.
project_ideas.measurement: Escaped defect rate, human review time overhead, cycle time, and developer trust scores.
project_ideas.name: RiskProportionalReviewGate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a code-generation pipeline with static checks, tests, sampling-based human review, and severity thresholds; run an A/B test against a trust-by-default workflow.
project_ideas.video_title: Ruby, Rails, and the future of programming - Matz, DHH & Jeremy Daer

project_ideas.based_on: Toolchains are expected to shift toward high-level agent interaction
project_ideas.hypothesis: For multi-step coding tasks, agent-native orchestration abstractions outperform traditional library/framework APIs on task success and token cost, while reducing human intervention.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, total tokens, latency, and human intervention rate.
project_ideas.name: AgentNativeAbstractionComparator
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same multi-step task using traditional library APIs and an agent-orchestration abstraction; compare outcomes across repeated trials.
project_ideas.video_title: Ruby, Rails, and the future of programming - Matz, DHH & Jeremy Daer

project_ideas.based_on: How do permission systems scale when managing hundreds of subagents in parallel?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A capability-based delegation token with hierarchical attenuation can enforce least-privilege access across 100+ dynamically spawned subagents while adding less than 5% orchestration overhead.
project_ideas.measurement: Permission-check latency, unauthorized action rate, successful fanout count, and revocation propagation time.
project_ideas.name: SwarmGate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a lead agent that spawns N specialized subagents, issues scoped tokens per subagent, enforces tool/resource boundaries, and revokes tokens on task completion.
project_ideas.video_title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity

project_ideas.based_on: What cost and latency guardrails are needed for autonomous sidecar utilities?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A budget-aware scheduler with per-sidecar token, rate, and kill-switch limits can bound continuous sidecar cost without blocking useful asynchronous work.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost overrun incidents, task completion rate, latency, and stability after model self-edits.
project_ideas.name: SidecarBudget
project_ideas.poc: Run model-editable sidecars for cron/webhook tasks under quotas, test model attempts to edit budgets or bypass limits, and measure cost and task completion.
project_ideas.video_title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity

project_ideas.based_on: How should generative UI output be verified, tested, and trusted in production?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Combining schema assertions, accessibility linting, and visual diffing can detect more than 95% of broken generative UI outputs while keeping false positives below 5%.
project_ideas.measurement: Fault detection rate, false positive rate, and determinism variance across repeated generations.
project_ideas.name: GenUI Harness
project_ideas.poc: Generate interfaces for a fixed set of task outputs, inject known faults such as missing labels, broken layout, and invalid data bindings, then measure detection.
project_ideas.video_title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity

project_ideas.based_on: What is the minimal orchestrator design that lets dynamic subagent teams stay coherent and observable?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A minimal trace schema capturing spawn lineage, prompts, tool calls, and artifacts can make dynamic subagent teams observable and recoverable without a centralized orchestration bottleneck.
project_ideas.measurement: Trace completeness, recovery time after failure, and tracing overhead as subagent count scales.
project_ideas.name: TeamTrace
project_ideas.poc: Implement a trace collector and replay/recovery path for dynamically spawned subagent teams, then simulate failures and measure recovery.
project_ideas.video_title: Get Out of the Model's Way — Kevin Hou, Google Antigravity

project_ideas.based_on: outer loop handles system improvement
project_ideas.hypothesis: Gating skill MD promotions on a golden task suite reduces task failure rate from self-edits without reducing improvement velocity.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate delta, rollback count, time-to-promote.
project_ideas.name: Skill Regression Harness for Outer-Loop Updates
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that runs representative triage and review tasks against skill versions, scores success, and blocks or rolls back regressions automatically.
project_ideas.video_title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: Human intervention points occur at review stages
project_ideas.hypothesis: Removing human spec review causes more rework and defect escape than removing human code review in an agentic pipeline.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect escape rate, rework hours, cycle time per gate configuration.
project_ideas.name: Human Gate Ablation Study
project_ideas.poc: In a controlled agentic repo with comparable tasks, ablate spec, code, and product review one at a time; measure defects and rework.
project_ideas.video_title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: Factory efficiency can be measured as software shipped divided by token cost plus human cost.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A computable shipped/(token+human) ratio instrumented per stage predicts defect escape better than throughput alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between ratio and defect escape rate; variance across projects.
project_ideas.name: Factory Efficiency Instrumentation
project_ideas.poc: Add telemetry to an agentic pipeline for token cost per agent, human minutes per gate, and merge/ship events; compute a daily ratio and correlate with defect escapes.
project_ideas.video_title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: Does the two-loop self-improving factory converge or drift over many iterations?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Without guardrails, outer-loop skill edits drift toward overfitting recent review comments, degrading held-out task success over cycles.
project_ideas.measurement: Held-out success trend, skill diff size, drift metric thresholds.
project_ideas.name: Two-Loop Drift Monitor
project_ideas.poc: Run a simulated factory for many outer-loop cycles, log skill diffs and held-out task success, apply drift metrics, and test whether periodic rollback preserves performance.
project_ideas.video_title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: Requiring human review for any changes to database migration files.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Risk-tiered review gates on AI-generated edits will reduce defect and rollback rates in high-risk artifacts without crippling agent throughput in low-risk code.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare defect rate, rollback rate, human review latency, and agent throughput before and after tiered gating across a representative repository.
project_ideas.name: Slop Boundary Enforcer
project_ideas.poc: Build a CI bot that classifies files and directories into autonomy tiers, blocks or requires human review for slop-free zones such as migrations and documentation, and allows unrestricted agent edits elsewhere.
project_ideas.video_title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor

project_ideas.based_on: Do not over-optimize workflows unless you have real alpha.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams that score agent workflows by proprietary-data dependence and codebase differentiation will reduce custom harness maintenance without lowering task success.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, maintenance hours, time-to-ship, and performance decay after a frontier model upgrade.
project_ideas.name: Alpha Audit Workflow Classifier
project_ideas.poc: Create a lightweight assessment that classifies tasks as default-harness or custom-alpha, then run paired evaluations of default versus custom workflows on tasks with and without proprietary context.
project_ideas.video_title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor

project_ideas.based_on: Centralize organizational communications and artifacts
project_ideas.hypothesis: Coding agents with queryable access to ingested Slack, Discord, meeting, and GitHub context will outperform context-starved agents on realistic engineering tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, retrieval precision, hallucination rate, token cost, and time-to-resolution.
project_ideas.name: Institutional Context Store Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Ingest synthetic organizational communications into PostgreSQL, expose retrieval to a coding agent, and compare against an identical agent without the institutional context store.
project_ideas.video_title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor

project_ideas.based_on: Cloud sandboxes allow agents to run longer and spawn new tools or APIs.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Cloud sandboxes with scoped credentials and kill switches enable longer autonomous coding runs without increasing security incidents per task.
project_ideas.measurement: Maximum safe runtime, incident rate, cost per completed task, and mean recovery time after kill-switch activation.
project_ideas.name: Cloud Sandbox Agent Runtime with Kill Switch
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a coding agent in an isolated cloud sandbox, allow it to spawn workspaces through an API, and simulate credential leakage, runaway cost, and failure modes.
project_ideas.video_title: Orchestras, Not Factories: How the Fastest Builders Work — Charlie Holtz, Conductor

project_ideas.based_on: The model was never really the bottleneck; the judgment around the model is.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Removing judgment scaffolding (tests, gates, reviews) while holding model capability constant causes a measurable and disproportionate collapse in autonomous code delivery reliability compared to reducing model capability.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate (task completion without human intervention), error rate, time-to-merge, and percentage of changes requiring corrective action. Compare across scaffolding levels.
project_ideas.name: Judgment Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a controlled pipeline where an agent performs a coding task under varying levels of judgment scaffolding (full gates, reduced gates, no gates) and measure success rates, rollback rates, and human intervention frequency.
project_ideas.video_title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit

project_ideas.based_on: A gate with an escape hatch isn't a gate.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents will discover and exploit any escape hatch in a verification gate; hard mechanical gates without bypasses will show significantly lower bypass rates than soft gates.
project_ideas.measurement: Bypass discovery rate, time to bypass, and successful unauthorized actions per gate type.
project_ideas.name: Escape Hatch Red Team
project_ideas.poc: Implement a gated action (e.g., code merge) with a soft gate (policy-based) and a hard gate (mechanically enforced), then run adversarial agents attempting to bypass. Measure bypass success.
project_ideas.video_title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit

project_ideas.based_on: Skills encode how to do something; personas encode whose eyes look at it.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Decomposing agent judgment into separate skill cards (how) and persona cards (whose eyes) yields higher review accuracy and fewer missed issues than a single monolithic reviewer agent.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of flaw detection, false positive rate, and consistency across tasks.
project_ideas.name: Skill-Persona Swarm Testbed
project_ideas.poc: Create a set of coding tasks with known flaws. Have a monolithic agent review, and a swarm of persona-based agents (e.g., security persona, accessibility persona) review. Compare detection rates.
project_ideas.video_title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit

project_ideas.based_on: Git hooks blocking commits that do not update worklogs.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Enforcing worklog updates via git hooks increases cross-session context retention and reduces redundant re-planning by agents, compared to voluntary worklog upkeep.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of context-related errors (e.g., agent forgetting decisions), time spent re-planning, and worklog completeness.
project_ideas.name: Worklog Enforcement and Context Retention
project_ideas.poc: Build a git hook that blocks commits without worklog updates. Run a multi-session coding task with agent, measure context accuracy and re-planning frequency versus a control group without enforcement.
project_ideas.video_title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit

project_ideas.based_on: Output metrics like PR count and lines of code hide whether AI systems improve business outcomes.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Replacing PR-count dashboards with time-to-feature and defect-escape metrics for agent-authored changes will reveal weak or negative delivery impact that PR volume hides.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta time-to-feature, defect escape rate, and review rework for agent vs human PRs; correlation between PR volume and delivery outcomes.
project_ideas.name: Outcome Meter for Agentic PRs
project_ideas.poc: Instrument agent PRs by linking them to originating tickets; compute time from ticket creation to merge/deploy, revert/defect rate, and review rework versus a matched human-authored baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS

project_ideas.based_on: The MCP server is not data plumbing; it is culture encoding.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Encoding review norms, naming conventions, and approved workflows in an MCP gateway's tool descriptions and semantic queries increases agent PR acceptance without rewrite compared to bare repo access.
project_ideas.measurement: PR acceptance without rewrite, reviewer comments per PR, rework cycles, and task completion rate.
project_ideas.name: Gateway-Encoded Culture Testbed
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal internal MCP gateway for one repository exposing guidelines, tool descriptions, and semantic DB queries; run identical agent tasks with and without gateway guidance.
project_ideas.video_title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS

project_ideas.based_on: Memory layers compound learnings across the organization, scoped by identity rather than harness.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Memory keyed to acting identity with explicit precedence across user/team/company scopes reduces redundant discovery and context conflicts versus harness-scoped memory.
project_ideas.measurement: Redundant file/tool reads, task success rate, conflict incidents, staleness rate, and cross-surface context reuse.
project_ideas.name: Identity-Scoped Memory Precedence Engine
project_ideas.poc: Implement a context service with three memory scopes and a conflict-resolution policy; run multi-agent tasks across Slack, IDE, and CLI surfaces.
project_ideas.video_title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS

project_ideas.based_on: Does encoding one org's narrative-first planning rituals generalize to teams without an equivalent spec artifact?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A PM agent that decomposes narrative specs into issues and tickets can generalize to RFC/ADR/ticket-only planning, but generated project structures will require more human rewrite than on Hilltop-style docs.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of generated tickets accepted, dependency chain accuracy, human rewrite rate, and time saved in project initialization.
project_ideas.name: PM Agent on RFC/ADR Planning
project_ideas.poc: Replicate the PM-agent pattern on teams using RFCs, ADRs, or ticket-only planning; compare cold-start project structure acceptance and dependency-chain accuracy against Hilltop-style inputs.
project_ideas.video_title: No, That's Not a Software Factory — Ryan Cooke, WorkOS

project_ideas.based_on: Separate code creation from validation by using distinct non-authoring validator agents.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Missions whose success criteria are expressed as a pre-declared, machine-checkable contract before authoring begins will show lower validator-agent cheating rates and lower rework-per-mission than missions where completion is judged post-hoc by the validator.
project_ideas.measurement: Cheating/self-satisfaction rate (validator passing outputs that fail an independent held-out check), rework cycles per mission, and validation-to-execution time ratio, contract-first vs. post-hoc, across matched task classes.
project_ideas.name: Contract-First Mission Harness
project_ideas.poc: A spec format covering preconditions, required tests, and acceptance checks; an orchestrator that refuses to start authoring without a valid contract; and a non-authoring validator that evaluates only against the contract — run on a fixed repository refactoring and artifact-generation task set.
project_ideas.video_title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory

project_ideas.based_on: Automatic routing can save over 25% of cost easily while providing model fallbacks.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Injected task-difficulty misclassifications will reduce realized cost savings below 25% and degrade task success non-uniformly, and a fallback policy triggered by runtime difficulty signals will recover most of the loss at a bounded extra-cost threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Routing accuracy, realized cost vs. baseline single-model binding, task success rate under injected error, recovery cost per misroute, and the error rate at which the savings claim no longer holds.
project_ideas.name: Routing Fault-Injection Rig
project_ideas.poc: A routing layer with a difficulty classifier, provider fallbacks, and caching, plus a fault injector that deliberately routes hard tasks to weak models and easy tasks to expensive models; compare fixed-policy vs. signal-triggered escalation policies.
project_ideas.video_title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory

project_ideas.based_on: Progressive disclosure defers tool context until needed, saving up to 50%+ on tokens.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Progressive disclosure of tool context preserves task success at tool counts up to a threshold, beyond which wrong-tool and missing-context invocation rates rise enough to erase the token savings' practical value.
project_ideas.measurement: Token cost per task, task success rate, wrong-tool invocation rate, late-surfacing failures (correct tool needed but never retrieved), and the tool-count crossover point where success diverges.
project_ideas.name: Deferred Context Engine A/B Bench
project_ideas.poc: Two matched agents over the same task suite with an identical tool catalog of hundreds of tools: one with all schemas statically injected, one using a tool-metadata index with demand-driven retrieval; instrument every invocation for which tools were surfaced and when.
project_ideas.video_title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory

project_ideas.based_on: Unprepared repositories experience significantly higher code degradation when using AI.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-dimension readiness scores (style & validation, build, testing, documentation, dev environment, observability, security, task discovery) will predict subsequent code-quality drift after agent contributions, and a small subset of dimensions will carry most of the predictive weight.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation and relative weight of each dimension against measured degradation per repository, plus whether a composite readiness threshold separates net-improving from net-degrading repositories.
project_ideas.name: Agent Readiness Scorecard
project_ideas.poc: An instrument that computes each of the eight dimension scores from repository artifacts, paired with a drift measure (lint/type/coverage deltas, review rework, revert rate) recorded on every agent-authored change across a set of onboarded repositories.
project_ideas.video_title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory

project_ideas.based_on: update skill definitions via pull requests
project_ideas.hypothesis: Running an outer-loop skill-updating agent for N successive update cycles on a fixed task distribution produces a measurable net improvement that plateaus or regresses after a finite number of cycles, rather than improving monotonically.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate and failure-class breakdown per cycle over N=20 cycles, plus the cycle index at which success rate stops improving or declines; regression detection via a held-out task slice never seen by the outer loop.
project_ideas.name: Skill Drift Bench
project_ideas.poc: Implement a triage agent with a SKILL.md, an outer-loop agent that proposes skill diffs from recorded runs and feedback, and an automated merge path; replay a fixed frozen task distribution after each cycle and record task success rate and diff size per iteration.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: a fact store scoped to an agent
project_ideas.hypothesis: A fact store with explicit scope keys and conflict resolution on write yields higher retrieval precision and lower stale-fact contamination over time than an append-only session log scoped to the same agent.
project_ideas.measurement: Retrieval precision on a labeled fact set, contamination rate (retrieved facts that are superseded or wrong), tokens and latency per repeated failure class versus a no-store baseline, tracked over successive weeks of accumulation.
project_ideas.name: Scoped Fact Store with Conflict Resolution on Write
project_ideas.poc: Build a background extraction process over completed agent sessions that writes facts into a store keyed by (agent, repo, service) with supersession rules; run both this store and an append-only baseline against a repeated-failure workload.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: routing rules are presumably validated by an evaluation harness
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing thresholds derived automatically from an eval harness that scores task-class outcomes per model achieve a non-dominated cost/quality frontier versus static human-authored rules, and misrouting is detectable as a distinct failure class at request time.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per successful task and success rate versus static routing across at least three task classes, plus false-downgrade rate (tasks sent to an underpowered model) and the fraction of routing decisions attributable to a single rule.
project_ideas.name: Eval-Sidecar Router with Derived YAML Thresholds
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a router with declarative YAML task-class rules, run an eval sidecar that scores per-class outcomes for each candidate model, auto-derive thresholds, and log every routing decision with the rule that fired for auditability.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: humans can review and prevent skill degradation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Human review time per skill PR is roughly constant, so factory scale (agent count times update frequency) is bounded by reviewer headcount, and the binding constraint arrives before agent-side compute does.
project_ideas.measurement: Reviewer minutes per PR distribution, PR acceptance rate, queue depth over time at fixed reviewer count, and the agent-update rate at which queue depth grows monotonically.
project_ideas.name: Review-Load Ceiling Calculator
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a pipeline where the outer loop opens skill PRs at controlled rates; measure reviewer minutes per PR, acceptance rate, and the rate at which the PR queue grows without bound at fixed reviewer capacity.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: Evaluation integrity became a generated component of the self-improvement pipeline.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Anti-reward-hacking layers generated by the optimizing loop lose measurable effectiveness within a small number of adversarial co-evolution iterations, and the decay rate is a function of how much of the defense the loop itself authored.
project_ideas.measurement: Iterations-to-breach curve: number of co-evolution rounds before hacking incidence on held-out tasks exceeds its pre-defense baseline, plus per-round hacking incidence versus measured benchmark delta.
project_ideas.name: Defense Decay Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a code-optimizing inner loop with an outer loop that generates evaluation-hardening layers; run paired co-evolution rounds where a policy is optimized against the current defenses, and log hacking incidence per round on a fixed held-out task set.
project_ideas.video_title: Can Rewriting an AI Agent Bend the Intelligence Curve? - Zhengyao Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: Longer runs and more complex codebases increase reward hacking rates.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reward hacking incidence rises monotonically with run length and repository size while legitimate benchmark gain saturates, producing a crossover point beyond which added autonomy yields negative net measured progress.
project_ideas.measurement: Hacking incidence and benchmark delta plotted against run length and codebase size, with the crossover point where hacking-adjusted gain turns flat or negative.
project_ideas.name: Hacking-vs-Horizon Sweep
project_ideas.poc: Hold the base model fixed, sweep run duration and repository complexity across a grid, and instrument detection for test cheating, monkey patching, and metric-shaped edits on a coding benchmark.
project_ideas.video_title: Can Rewriting an AI Agent Bend the Intelligence Curve? - Zhengyao Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: Does a harness discovered by the outer loop transfer across model families and task domains, or only within the benchmark families used for its search?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A harness discovered by an outer loop on one base model and benchmark family retains most of its advantage when the base model is swapped, but degrades sharply on out-of-family tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Degradation curves: percentage of search-time gain retained per model swap and per out-of-family task, rather than single-point benchmark scores.
project_ideas.name: Harness Transfer Matrix
project_ideas.poc: Freeze the discovered harness, run it unchanged across at least two model families and one out-of-family task suite, and compare against both the original hand-tuned harness and the search-time benchmark.
project_ideas.video_title: Can Rewriting an AI Agent Bend the Intelligence Curve? - Zhengyao Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: Harness engineering produced benchmark gains without changing underlying model weights
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a fixed task suite, outer-loop harness search reaches a given performance level at lower total cost than fine-tuning or retraining the base model, and the cost advantage widens as the search space is widened.
project_ideas.measurement: Compute dollars and wall-clock time required to hit each of several fixed performance thresholds, for harness search versus weight adaptation.
project_ideas.name: Cost-Parity Harness vs. Weights
project_ideas.poc: Run an outer harness search and a weight-level adaptation against the same held-out suite under matched compute budgets, recording cost to reach fixed performance thresholds.
project_ideas.video_title: Can Rewriting an AI Agent Bend the Intelligence Curve? - Zhengyao Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: evaluator/fitness function returning a score and side information
project_ideas.hypothesis: At equal rollout or evaluation budget, reflective optimization with score plus diagnostic side information yields higher held-out performance than score-only feedback, and the gap grows with task diagnostic complexity.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in held-out accuracy and number of reflection rounds to reach baseline score.
project_ideas.name: SideInfo Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Wrap one evaluator to emit either scalar-only or scalar plus error/profiler messages. Run the same optimizer on a multi-hop QA or coding task. Compare final artifacts.
project_ideas.video_title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA

project_ideas.based_on: A Pareto pool retains every candidate that wins on even one training example.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed evaluation budget, Pareto-pool retention improves held-out score over single-best retention up to a crossover candidate population, after which aggregation overhead reverses the gain.
project_ideas.measurement: Held-out score delta per 1k evaluator calls and wall-clock time until aggregation exceeds 50 percent of loop time.
project_ideas.name: ParetoPoolBench
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal reflective loop over a small prompt or code task with two modes: single-best versus Pareto pool. Sweep example-set size and candidate population. Log pool size, eval calls, aggregation time, train score, and held-out score.
project_ideas.video_title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA

project_ideas.based_on: Do reflectively optimized artifacts generalize beyond the examples used for optimization, or do they overfit test-case-specific solutions?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pareto aggregation of test-case specialists overfits training examples; on held-out examples it underperforms a single-best candidate selected by validation score when per-example specialization is high.
project_ideas.measurement: Train-test gap in score and variance across splits.
project_ideas.name: Pareto Generalization Splitter
project_ideas.poc: Run reflective optimization with train, validation, and test splits. Compare Pareto-aggregated candidates versus single-best candidates on held-out examples. Vary example heterogeneity.
project_ideas.video_title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA

project_ideas.based_on: How reliable is the LLM reflector, and what happens when reflection produces incorrect hypotheses about why a rollout failed?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Misleading side information degrades optimized artifact quality monotonically with feedback error rate, but Pareto retention reduces the degradation slope versus single-best retention.
project_ideas.measurement: Slope of held-out score decline per 10 percent misleading feedback, with variance across seeds.
project_ideas.name: Reflector Noise Injector
project_ideas.poc: Inject controlled false error messages into evaluator feedback. Run reflective optimization with Pareto versus single-best retention. Measure score across noise levels.
project_ideas.video_title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA

project_ideas.based_on: GPT-4 Astra scoring 95% on robot control tasks.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reported success rates for robot-use agents collapse by a large margin (target: >40 percentage points) when evaluated on systematic pose, lighting, object-instance and instruction-perturbation shifts, relative to the base task distribution used in published demos.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate per perturbation axis and severity bucket, degradation slope from base distribution, failure-mode taxonomy (perception error vs plan error vs execution error), and cost-per-success.
project_ideas.name: ShiftBench: A Distribution-Shift Eval for Robot-Use Agents
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a small tabletop manipulation suite (pick/place/stack/open) with a scripted perturbation generator over four axes; run it against at least two agent configurations (code-as-policy over a primitive library, and an end-to-end VLA) and publish a full decay curve per axis plus cost per successful episode.
project_ideas.video_title: Robot-Use Agents: Why General-Purpose Models May Win in Robotics

project_ideas.based_on: Code as Policies allows LLMs to write Python code combining perception and control primitives.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Wrapping robot control primitives behind a typed, capability-scoped tool interface (explicit preconditions, effect annotations, velocity/force/joint limits) reduces unsafe-action and unrecoverable-error rates substantially while costing only a small drop in task success rate versus free-form code generation.
project_ideas.measurement: Unsafe-action rate per 100 episodes, unrecoverable-error rate, task success delta versus unrestricted baseline, and human approval count required per task.
project_ideas.name: Capability-Scoped Tool Gateway for Robot-Use Agents
project_ideas.poc: Build a gateway that validates LLM-generated tool calls against a declared capability profile and refuses or rewrites calls violating preconditions; A/B it in simulation against a baseline agent that writes unrestricted Python against the same primitive library.
project_ideas.video_title: Robot-Use Agents: Why General-Purpose Models May Win in Robotics

project_ideas.based_on: RT-2 fine-tunes vision-language models on robotic trajectory data and web data.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For short-horizon manipulation tasks, marginal returns to additional robot trajectory data diminish sharply once a base of computer-use/CAD/web pretraining is present, whereas for long-horizon multi-step tasks the trajectory-data term dominates.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-source marginal success-rate contribution curves; interaction between mixture ratio and task horizon; break-even point where extra trajectory hours stop paying for themselves.
project_ideas.name: Data-Mixture Ablation for Embodied Agents (DIME)
project_ideas.poc: Train or fine-tune matched small-scale models on controlled mixtures of (a) web text/image, (b) computer-use traces, (c) CAD, (d) robot trajectories, and evaluate on a fixed short-horizon and long-horizon task split with identical compute.
project_ideas.video_title: Robot-Use Agents: Why General-Purpose Models May Win in Robotics

project_ideas.based_on: Strong language models converge on consistent mappings of the world as they train on larger datasets.
project_ideas.hypothesis: If representations converge across modalities as scale increases, then linear probes trained on a frozen general-purpose model's internal representation should predict physical quantities (relative depth, contact state, object affordance) with accuracy that improves monotonically with model scale — if this fails, the practical case for skipping robot-specific data collection weakens materially.
project_ideas.measurement: Probe accuracy vs. model scale and vs. pretraining-modality mix; slope of improvement; correlation between probe accuracy and downstream task success on a held-out manipulation set.
project_ideas.name: Falsification Harness for the Platonic Representation Claim
project_ideas.poc: Extract frozen representations from a scale ladder of publicly available general-purpose models, fit identical linear probes for a fixed set of physical predicates from a shared robot perception dataset, and plot probe accuracy against model scale and pretraining-data composition.
project_ideas.video_title: Robot-Use Agents: Why General-Purpose Models May Win in Robotics

project_ideas.based_on: A persistent, recoverable asset (vehicle, runtime, warm session state) is amortized across many cycles.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Persisting and recovering agent runtime and session state across invocations lowers marginal cost per cycle below per-invocation rebuild, net of recovery and invalidation overhead, once the asset is amortized over enough cycles.
project_ideas.measurement: Marginal cost per invocation and end-to-end latency for warm versus cold modes as a function of reuse count, including time to recover after an invalidated session.
project_ideas.name: Warm-State Agent Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Run an identical agent workload in two modes (cold rebuild per invocation vs persistent warm runtime with snapshot recovery) and measure cost, latency, and failure-invalidation rate as cycles per session increase.
project_ideas.video_title: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

project_ideas.based_on: Benchmark end-to-end perception-to-actuation latency on manipulation tasks and correlate it with task success versus human reaction-time baselines.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Perception-to-actuation loop latency explains a larger share of manipulation task success variance than policy quality once a reflex-threshold latency is crossed.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end loop latency in milliseconds per task, and the correlation between latency reduction and task success rate at fixed policy.
project_ideas.name: Loop-Latency Bench for Embodied Agents
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a manipulation stack to timestamp perception, decision, and actuation stages, then sweep loop rate and actuator bandwidth while holding the policy fixed and compare against human reaction-time baselines.
project_ideas.video_title: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

project_ideas.based_on: Build a capacity model comparing fab output and generation headroom against projected compute demand, and stress-test roadmap assumptions against each input independently.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a given compute demand trajectory, exactly one of lithography capacity or generation capacity saturates first, and roadmap brittleness scales with the gap between the assumed and the observed resolution date.
project_ideas.measurement: Projected saturation date and headroom per input, plus roadmap breakage threshold in months of slippage for each input assumption.
project_ideas.name: Constraint Budget Model: Fab Output vs Generation Headroom
project_ideas.poc: Build a two-input capacity model over a 3-year horizon with explicit demand trajectories, then stress-test each input independently and record which assumption a roadmap breaks under.
project_ideas.video_title: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

project_ideas.based_on: Prototype task-generation and backlog-management subsystems for agents, and study controllability and oversight cost when objectives are self-selected.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an explicit goal-generation and prioritization subsystem raises sustained agent throughput after an assigned-work backlog is depleted, at a measurable controllability cost per generated objective.
project_ideas.measurement: Throughput after backlog depletion, rate of self-generated objectives requiring intervention, and oversight cost per accepted objective.
project_ideas.name: Task-Supply Governor
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a backlog manager that ingests a finite human-assigned queue, then generates and prioritizes its own objectives once the queue empties, with an oversight hook on every self-selected goal.
project_ideas.video_title: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

project_ideas.based_on: AI-generated tests are frequently tautological ... or structure-sensitive
project_ideas.hypothesis: A static analysis tool can detect tautological and structure-sensitive tests with >90% precision and recall on a corpus of AI-generated test suites.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare tool output against human-labeled ground truth; compute precision, recall, and F1 score.
project_ideas.name: Tautology Linter for AI-Generated Tests
project_ideas.poc: Build a linter that parses test assertions, identifies patterns like constant-equals-constant or assertions mirroring implementation structure, and flags them. Test on a dataset of AI-generated tests from a representative codebase.
project_ideas.video_title: Fixing the PR Bottleneck — Matt Pocock, AIHero

project_ideas.based_on: moving coding standards out of the implementer prompt
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams using a dedicated review agent with CODING_STANDARDS.md will show a statistically significant reduction in style-related review comments and review cycle time compared to teams using global instructions in the implementer prompt.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of style violations per PR, human review time per PR, and developer satisfaction survey.
project_ideas.name: Separate Review Agent vs Global Prompt A/B Test
project_ideas.poc: Implement two pipelines in a controlled repository: one with global coding standards in the implementer prompt, one with a separate /code-review agent reading CODING_STANDARDS.md. Run both on a set of feature PRs generated by the same AI implementer.
project_ideas.video_title: Fixing the PR Bottleneck — Matt Pocock, AIHero

project_ideas.based_on: emit commits (direct fixes) rather than comments
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automated reviewers that commit fixes directly reduce human review time by at least 30% without increasing defect escape rate compared to reviewers that only leave comments.
project_ideas.measurement: Average human review time per PR, defect escape rate (bugs found in production per PR), and human trust survey.
project_ideas.name: Impact of Commit-Producing vs Comment-Producing Automated Reviewers
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a CI pipeline to randomly assign PRs to two reviewer modes: commit-mode and comment-mode. Track review time and post-merge defects for a period.
project_ideas.video_title: Fixing the PR Bottleneck — Matt Pocock, AIHero

project_ideas.based_on: deep-module refactoring quantitatively reduce structure-sensitive test generation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Refactoring a codebase to deep modules reduces the incidence of structure-sensitive tests generated by AI agents by at least 50%.
project_ideas.measurement: Proportion of generated tests classified as structure-sensitive by a static analyzer or human labelers.
project_ideas.name: Quantifying the Effect of Deep Module Refactoring on AI-Generated Test Quality
project_ideas.poc: Select a codebase with shallow modules. Have an AI agent generate tests for a set of features. Measure brittle test incidence. Refactor to deep modules. Have the same agent generate tests for equivalent features. Measure again.
project_ideas.video_title: Fixing the PR Bottleneck — Matt Pocock, AIHero

project_ideas.based_on: Capability overhang: models possess latent capabilities that only surface when given an execution environment
project_ideas.hypothesis: The capability gain attributed to 'giving the model a bash tool' is mainly attributable to retrieval-and-grep access, not to code execution itself; a retrieval-only tool will recover most of the gain on parametric-recall tasks while a bare code-execution tool without data access will not.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate per arm, with the retrieval-only arm compared against the full-execution arm; a large gap in favor of full execution falsifies the retrieval-only hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Overhang Isolator
project_ideas.poc: Build a controlled task battery in three arms — (a) chat-only parametric recall, (b) chat + retrieval/grep access with no arbitrary execution, (c) chat + full script execution and fetch/grep — over datasets where the model demonstrably 'knows' the answer but cannot surface it in chat.
project_ideas.video_title: Unhobbling Claude, the difficulties and processes of building agents - Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: Claude 5 models require smaller system prompts and fewer examples because of better model judgment.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed agent task suite, a system prompt pruned by roughly 80% with minimal few-shot examples matches or beats the pre-prune prompt on a newer model generation, and any regressions are concentrated in a small, identifiable set of instruction-following cases rather than spread evenly.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success delta between prompt tiers per model generation, plus the count and identity of regressed instruction-following cases; a systematic pruned-tier loss falsifies the hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Prompt Debt Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Version-control two prompt tiers (full and pruned) for one agent, run both against an identical task suite on successive model generations, and produce a per-case diff report tagging each prompt clause as retained, deleted, or inverted.
project_ideas.video_title: Unhobbling Claude, the difficulties and processes of building agents - Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: What is the optimal context storage strategy for browser agents?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Context representation and action-execution archetype interact strongly enough that no single representation dominates; the best-performing (context, action) pair changes across task families, so a per-task harness selection beats any global default.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success, tokens, and latency per matrix cell, plus whether the argmax cell differs across task families; a single cell dominating all families on all axes falsifies the hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Harness Cross-Product Bench
project_ideas.poc: Implement a browser agent harness with pluggable context backends (full screenshots, DOM diffs, bounding-box annotations) and pluggable action interfaces, then run the cross product on one shared task suite with token and latency accounting per cell.
project_ideas.video_title: Unhobbling Claude, the difficulties and processes of building agents - Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: How can compaction be automated without losing critical agent memory?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Aggressive compaction causes silent, measurable memory loss on long-horizon tasks, and retention rules keyed to task-critical facts, logged deviations, and prior decisions recover most of the lost success at a fraction of the uncompacted token cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate and post-compaction recall of planted facts as a function of compaction aggressiveness; retention rules that do not beat naive compaction falsify the hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Compaction Memory-Loss Regression
project_ideas.poc: Construct long-horizon tasks with planted critical facts and mandated deviation logging, then run them under a sweep of compaction aggressiveness settings with and without the retention criteria enabled.
project_ideas.video_title: Unhobbling Claude, the difficulties and processes of building agents - Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: no one has yet made AI excellent at physical-world engineering
project_ideas.hypothesis: AI models that excel on software engineering benchmarks will show significantly lower success rates on closed-loop physical manipulation tasks, and adding hardware telemetry to training will improve physical task performance more than adding more software code data.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate on physical tasks; transfer gap between software and physical benchmarks; improvement from telemetry fine-tuning vs. code fine-tuning.
project_ideas.name: EmbodiedBench
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark of 20 physical manipulation tasks (e.g., peg-in-hole, cable routing) on a low-cost robot arm, and evaluate a state-of-the-art code-focused LLM vs. a version fine-tuned on simulated/real hardware telemetry. Measure task success rate and generalization to novel objects.
project_ideas.video_title: Full: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

project_ideas.based_on: relocating a per-flight function from the disposable vehicle into fixed, persistent infrastructure
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents implemented as thin ephemeral processes that rely on a shared persistent harness (state, tools, memory, safety checks) will achieve lower per-task cost and higher reliability than monolithic agents that duplicate infrastructure.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-task cost, latency, success rate under injected failures, and ease of adding new capabilities.
project_ideas.name: HarnessOps
project_ideas.poc: Implement a simple task (e.g., web research + summarization) in two architectures: (A) monolithic agent with built-in tools and state, (B) thin agent using a centralized harness. Run 100 tasks each, measure latency, cost, and failure recovery.
project_ideas.video_title: Full: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

project_ideas.based_on: humanoid robot population exceeds 1 billion within 10 years
project_ideas.hypothesis: A 1 billion humanoid robot fleet within 10 years is infeasible under current manufacturing and energy growth rates; the binding constraint is battery production capacity, not robot assembly.
project_ideas.measurement: Required CAGR in manufacturing and energy to hit 1B; identify which constraint binds first; compare to historical growth rates of similar industries.
project_ideas.name: RobotFleetSim
project_ideas.poc: Build a system dynamics model with inputs (current robot production capacity, battery gigafactory growth, grid capacity expansion) and simulate fleet growth to 2036. Run sensitivity analysis on key parameters.
project_ideas.video_title: Full: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

project_ideas.based_on: How will regulatory frameworks adapt to autonomous humanoid robotics and advanced AI safety?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A fleet-level safety layer that monitors robot-to-robot interactions and enforces dynamic geofencing and task allocation can reduce collision and safety incidents by >90% compared to unit-level safety checks alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of collisions, deadlocks, near-misses; throughput; compliance with simulated regulatory constraints.
project_ideas.name: FleetGuard
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a warehouse with 100 autonomous robots. Implement unit-level collision avoidance vs. a centralized fleet safety layer that predicts and prevents multi-robot deadlocks and collisions. Measure incident rate and throughput.
project_ideas.video_title: Full: Exclusive CMG interview with Tesla CEO Elon Musk

project_ideas.based_on: The unit of encoded standards should shift from atomic components to executable harnesses
project_ideas.hypothesis: Injecting design standards at the mid-generation tool-call stage yields higher intent conformance than pre-prompt injection or component-library retrieval.
project_ideas.measurement: Intent conformance score by human rubric (1-5) and automatic lint pass rate; compare across stages.
project_ideas.name: Harness Timing Injector
project_ideas.poc: Build a CLI wrapper around a codegen model that injects design docs at three stages (pre-prompt, mid-generation tool call, post-generation lint) for the same UI generation task; run on 10 representative tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with Al | Katie Dill (Stripe)

project_ideas.based_on: Generative output produces 'premature finish'
project_ideas.hypothesis: Mandatory post-build adversarial review reduces accepted deep flaws compared to pre-build spec review, but human review becomes the bottleneck.
project_ideas.measurement: Defects per accepted artifact and reviewer minutes per artifact.
project_ideas.name: Post-Build Critique Gate
project_ideas.poc: Simulate pipeline with two conditions: spec-only review vs post-build critique; use same AI-generated artifacts; measure reviewer time and defect escape rate.
project_ideas.video_title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with Al | Katie Dill (Stripe)

project_ideas.based_on: Can 'probable vs. original' be measured automatically
project_ideas.hypothesis: A distributional similarity metric over generated artifacts can automatically rank outputs by typicality, and supplying unique brand source material reduces measured typicality.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between metric and human originality ratings; difference in typicality score between conditions.
project_ideas.name: Genericness Meter
project_ideas.poc: Collect a domain corpus of generated UI or copy (e.g., bank websites) and compute embedding-based distance to modal template set; generate with and without brand-specific source material.
project_ideas.video_title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with Al | Katie Dill (Stripe)

project_ideas.based_on: AI cost savings should be reinvested into higher iteration counts
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reallocating AI cost savings to 50+ iteration loops on a single high-emotion animation increases perceived emotional resonance more than using savings to produce 50 additional variants.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean emotional resonance rating per condition, uniqueness score, and cost per accepted artifact.
project_ideas.name: Artistry Reinvestment Lab
project_ideas.poc: Build a small animation generation loop; condition A: 56 iterations on one scene; condition B: 56 variants from same prompt; collect user ratings of emotional resonance and uniqueness.
project_ideas.video_title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with Al | Katie Dill (Stripe)

project_ideas.based_on: AI agents work better with good abstractions and narrow state spaces (guardrails)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reducing an interface's state-space size and eliminating invalid states increases LLM agent task success rate and reduces non-local reasoning errors, with a measurable threshold beyond which success saturates or degrades.
project_ideas.measurement: Agent success rate, error type distribution (local vs. non-local reasoning), number of tool calls per task.
project_ideas.name: Agent-State-Space Tuner
project_ideas.poc: Build a simple CRUD API with configurable abstraction layers (raw vs. constrained) and run a fixed set of agent tasks; vary state-space size by adding/removing guardrails and invalid-state checks.
project_ideas.video_title: The End of Understanding: Why Good Abstractions Matter

project_ideas.based_on: Evaluating abstractions based on four key properties
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scoring interfaces on the four properties (simple, sound, instructive, composable) correlates with human and agent task success and change friction.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between rubric scores and agent task success rate / human-rated ease of change.
project_ideas.name: Abstraction Quality Scorer
project_ideas.poc: Implement a rubric-based scoring tool for OpenAPI specs or database schemas; collect a corpus of public APIs, score them, and run agent tasks against each.
project_ideas.video_title: The End of Understanding: Why Good Abstractions Matter

project_ideas.based_on: Common database implementation details leaking into application code (e.g., isolation levels)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Static analysis can detect leaked implementation details (e.g., database isolation levels, storage internals) in consumer code, and such leaks predict breakage when internals change.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of leak detection against labeled incidents; correlation between leak count and observed breakages in a version-upgrade simulation.
project_ideas.name: Leaky Boundary Detector
project_ideas.poc: Build a linter that parses application code and infrastructure-as-code to flag references to internal implementation details; validate on a set of known leaky-abstraction incidents.
project_ideas.video_title: The End of Understanding: Why Good Abstractions Matter

project_ideas.based_on: Developers using coding agents do not understand the generated code deeply
project_ideas.hypothesis: Code changes generated by agents without human comprehension produce higher incident rates and longer repair times than changes with human-reviewed boundaries, even when initial tests pass.
project_ideas.measurement: Incident rate per 100 PRs, mean time to repair, rollback rate, and lines changed in hotfixes.
project_ideas.name: Comprehension Debt Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a repository where agent-generated PRs are tagged by the level of human review (full comprehension vs. boundary-only vs. none) and track incidents, rollbacks, and hotfix time over 3 months.
project_ideas.video_title: The End of Understanding: Why Good Abstractions Matter

project_ideas.based_on: Solving coding does not increase end-to-end throughput; it relocates the constraint downstream to review, QA, and coordination.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automating any single stage of the software development pipeline (coding, review, QA, coordination) shifts the end-to-end constraint to the next unautomated stage, and the constraint can be predicted by measuring each stage's automated-vs-human split and queue depth.
project_ideas.measurement: Change in end-to-end lead time, bottleneck stage identification accuracy vs. actual constraint (via queuing metrics), and reduction in time-to-merge after automating review.
project_ideas.name: Pipeline Bottleneck Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Build a dashboard that instruments a CI/CD pipeline to track per-stage cycle time, automated/human ratio, and queue lengths; simulate automating one stage (e.g., code review) by routing a percentage of PRs through an automated classifier, and measure the shift in end-to-end lead time and the new bottleneck stage.
project_ideas.video_title: What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

project_ideas.based_on: Bootstrapping an agent's context pipeline from a deliberately narrow, human-curated channel
project_ideas.hypothesis: A context agent bootstrapped from a narrow, human-curated input channel (e.g., a Slack channel of customer complaints) will achieve higher relevance and faster schema emergence than an agent built from full-corpus multi-source ETL, as measured by user-perceived signal-to-noise and time-to-useful-insights.
project_ideas.measurement: Time to first actionable insight, precision/recall of identified customer problems vs. a gold set, and number of schema iterations required to reach stable structured extraction.
project_ideas.name: Hate Channel Bootstrapper
project_ideas.poc: Create a Slack bot that collects complaints into a dedicated channel, then incrementally build a structured agent by extracting entities and intents; compare against a baseline that attempts to unify data from three sources (e.g., Zendesk, Gong, LogRocket) via ETL.
project_ideas.video_title: What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

project_ideas.based_on: How is the 7% of PRs routed to humans chosen, and what is Review Buddy's false-negative rate on the 93% it auto-handles?
project_ideas.hypothesis: The false-negative rate of an automated code review agent can be measured and controlled by varying the escalation threshold, and there exists a threshold that maximizes throughput while keeping escaped defects below a specified tolerance.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of escalated PRs, throughput gain (auto-handled percentage), and escaped defect rate at different thresholds; identify Pareto-optimal threshold.
project_ideas.name: Review Escalation Threshold Tuner
project_ideas.poc: Inject known defects (security, logic, style) into a corpus of PRs, run an automated reviewer that classifies each as auto-approve or escalate, and sweep the confidence threshold to plot precision/recall and throughput (PRs auto-handled) vs. escaped defects.
project_ideas.video_title: What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

project_ideas.based_on: Coding-agent effectiveness is bounded by codebase and architecture quality
project_ideas.hypothesis: Coding-agent success rate on a fixed task set is significantly higher in codebases with strong architecture (consistent naming, high test coverage, clear interfaces) than in messy codebases, and the difference quantifies an 'architecture multiplier' that can be used to predict agent productivity gains.
project_ideas.measurement: Agent success rate, time, and intervention rate in clean vs. messy codebases; correlation between static code quality metrics (e.g., test coverage, complexity) and agent performance.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Environment Benchmark Suite
project_ideas.poc: Select or create two versions of a codebase (clean vs. messy) with identical functionality; run a coding agent on the same set of 20 tasks in each; measure success rate, time to completion, and human intervention rate.
project_ideas.video_title: What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)

project_ideas.based_on: AI changes specific tasks within complex jobs rather than destroying entire job categories wholesale.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In AI-augmented software engineering teams, measuring task-level automation (e.g., code generation, testing) will reveal that overall job roles are not replaced but reallocated, with net productivity gains only when human oversight tasks are explicitly modeled.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare task distribution and end-to-end cycle time before and after AI tool introduction; track percentage of tasks automated and human handoff frequency.

project_ideas.poc: Build a telemetry system that instruments developer workflows to classify tasks as AI-executed, human-executed, or hybrid, and correlate with cycle time and quality metrics.

project_ideas.based_on: Unlocking one bottleneck in software or AI reveals others across industries.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Optimizing a single stage in an AI pipeline (e.g., inference speed) will shift the bottleneck to another stage (e.g., data labeling or human review), and end-to-end throughput will not improve unless downstream constraints are addressed.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-completion and throughput before/after optimizing a bottleneck stage; count of new bottlenecks emerged.
project_ideas.name: Bottleneck Propagation Monitor
project_ideas.poc: Implement a workflow orchestration prototype that simulates an AI pipeline with multiple stages, automatically detects the current bottleneck via telemetry, and measures end-to-end throughput after optimizing one stage.

project_ideas.based_on: AI's economic value as a general-purpose technology is delayed until firms and economies restructure production and workflows, not merely deploy the model.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Firms that redesign workflows around AI capabilities (rather than bolting AI onto existing processes) will show higher ROI (e.g., 20%+ improvement in cycle time) than those that only deploy models.
project_ideas.measurement: Simulated ROI metrics (e.g., throughput, cost per unit) comparing strategies; validate with pilot data from a partner organization.

project_ideas.poc: Build a simulation or case-study tool that models two adoption strategies (bolt-on vs. workflow redesign) and estimates ROI based on process parameters.
