project_ideas.based_on: AI governance should be evidence-based and pragmatic, using data and existing regulatory frameworks rather than speculative doom scenarios.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A safety evaluation harness that measures AI system behavior on domain-specific tasks using existing regulatory frameworks (e.g., FDA-style evidence) will produce actionable guardrails that reduce harmful outputs without significantly reducing task performance.
project_ideas.measurement: Safety violation rate and task accuracy before/after applying evidence-based guardrails; regulatory compliance checklist coverage.

project_ideas.based_on: human dignity risks being judged solely by efficiency
project_ideas.hypothesis: An additive efficiency-only eval suite will miss regressions on non-instrumented dimensions, while a multi-dimensional rubric with interaction terms will detect them.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of regressions detected, false-positive rate, inter-rater agreement, and disagreement between the two suites.

project_ideas.poc: Build two eval suites for an LLM agent: baseline accuracy/cost only versus a multi-dimensional suite covering user agency, contestability, and transparency with interaction terms. Run both on controlled degradations.

project_ideas.measurement: Convergence time, conflict rate, task success under partial failure, and recovery time.

project_ideas.based_on: Beginner-friendly material requires teaching one right way initially before introducing advanced options.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent task success rate is higher and harmful action rate lower when tool schemas expose one canonical invocation per intent compared to multiple equivalent alternatives.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, number of retries, frequency of unrecoverable failures and harmful actions.
project_ideas.name: Single-Canonical-Path vs Multi-Path Tool API A/B Test
project_ideas.poc: Create two versions of a tool API (e.g., file operations: read_file vs multiple ways like open+read, cat, etc.). Run an agent on a set of tasks requiring file reads. Measure success, retries, unrecoverable failures.
project_ideas.video_title: C++26 for Lazy Programmers • Will Briggs & Todd Montgomery • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: You cannot teach vectors, lists, ostream notation, and spans all at once.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents given a sequence of tool/API exposures that build on previously established abstractions (progressive disclosure) achieve higher task success and lower error rates than agents given the full tool surface at once.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, error rate, and context token usage.
project_ideas.name: Progressive Disclosure of Tool Context Effect on Agent Performance
project_ideas.poc: Design a multi-step task (e.g., build a web app) with a set of tools. Run two agent groups: one gets all tools from start; the other gets tools in stages as prerequisites are met (e.g., first only file I/O, then HTTP, then database). Measure task completion, errors, and context usage.
project_ideas.video_title: C++26 for Lazy Programmers • Will Briggs & Todd Montgomery • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Students learn arrays and dynamic allocation under the hood before confronting the dreaded 'P-word'.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents trained or prompted abstraction-first (using high-level tools that hide raw operations) perform better on debugging tasks that require understanding below the abstraction line than agents given primitive-first access.
project_ideas.measurement: Debugging success rate, time to resolution, and correctness of root-cause identification.
project_ideas.name: Abstraction-First vs Primitive-First Agent Debugging
project_ideas.poc: Create two agent configurations: one with access to low-level primitives (e.g., raw memory operations, direct shell), another with a constrained abstraction (e.g., a safe API). Then test on hidden-cause debugging tasks that require diagnosing issues caused by low-level bugs. Measure debugging success rate.
project_ideas.video_title: C++26 for Lazy Programmers • Will Briggs & Todd Montgomery • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: What signals should trigger a re-plan versus commitment to the current plan?
project_ideas.hypothesis: An explicit trigger policy for re-planning (value/affordance thresholds plus execution-anomaly detection) yields higher long-horizon task success than plan-once execution, and outperforms always-replanning on cost-normalized success.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, re-plans per task, tokens/compute per success, and the distribution of trigger causes correlated with eventual success or failure.
project_ideas.name: RePlanBench
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that runs the same long-horizon tasks under three policies — plan-once, always-replan, and a triggered replan loop with configurable signals — instrumenting every re-plan event and its cause.
project_ideas.video_title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 5. Planning, Task Decomposition, and Multi-Agent Coordination

project_ideas.based_on: Formal plans are checkable, while language plans are general.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A static verifier over code-based plan representations detects a measurable fraction of pre-execution errors that natural-language plans structurally hide, without reducing task success on open-ended tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Pre-execution error detection rate, verification coverage (fraction of plan actions covered by checkable structures), downstream task success delta, and false-block rate.
project_ideas.name: Plan IR Linter
project_ideas.poc: Emit agent plans as structured code/programs with declared preconditions, effects, and permission gates; run a static checker and permission-mode gate before execution, comparing against a free-text plan baseline on identical tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 5. Planning, Task Decomposition, and Multi-Agent Coordination

project_ideas.based_on: Stronger manager agents improve coordination and lift weaker workers.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Team task success is more sensitive to manager model capability than to worker role specialization; fixed-role configurations lose to dynamic assignment as context length and handoff frequency increase.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate as a function of manager tier and worker tier, context-loss measurements across handoffs, and the crossover point between fixed and dynamic role assignment.
project_ideas.name: Orchestrator Capability Ladder
project_ideas.poc: Build a manager → DAG of parallel sub-agents pipeline with swappable manager capability tiers and swappable role-assignment policies (fixed vs dynamic), then ablate manager strength against worker strength and handoff frequency on long-horizon tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 5. Planning, Task Decomposition, and Multi-Agent Coordination

project_ideas.based_on: How should planning depth be budgeted against execution horizon to avoid overthinking?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Optimal plan-token budget scales with task execution horizon, and beyond a horizon-relative threshold additional plan tokens reduce action quality while increasing cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate and compute cost per plan-token budget per horizon bucket; identification of overthinking thresholds where added planning depth becomes net-negative.
project_ideas.name: Overthinking Budgeter
project_ideas.poc: Sweep plan-token budgets across task suites of varying execution horizons, holding model and tools fixed, and plot success/cost curves to locate inflection and degradation points per horizon bucket.
project_ideas.video_title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 5. Planning, Task Decomposition, and Multi-Agent Coordination

project_ideas.based_on: What are the latency, cost, and scaling overhead of provisioning a dedicated confidential VM per agent?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Provisioning a dedicated confidential VM per agent adds less than 15% latency and less than 20% memory overhead compared to shared multi-tenant execution for typical personal-agent workloads.
project_ideas.measurement: Cold-start time, per-request latency, memory footprint, and cost per 1M agent actions.
project_ideas.name: Confidential VM Overhead Benchmark for Per-Agent Isolation
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a simple tool-using agent (scheduling, code writing) in both shared and per-agent confidential VM configurations on identical hardware, measuring startup, memory, and throughput.
project_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg's Vision For the Future!

project_ideas.based_on: How does the sentinel agent decide what may cross the VM boundary without becoming a bottleneck or source of false blocks?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A dedicated sentinel agent at the VM boundary can block over 95% of data-exfiltration attempts with under 5% false positive rate and under 10ms added latency per boundary crossing.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate, false positive rate, added latency per crossing.
project_ideas.name: Sentinel Boundary Monitor for Agent VMs
project_ideas.poc: Implement a sentinel that inspects network egress and tool calls from an isolated agent VM, using a test suite of benign and malicious data flows.
project_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg's Vision For the Future!

project_ideas.based_on: Does training models from scratch to be agents outperform composition over strong open-source models on agentic tasks?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A purpose-trained agent model outperforms a wrapped open-source foundation model on agentic task suites by at least 20% success rate when using identical tooling and prompts.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, tool-call accuracy, latency, and training cost.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Native vs Wrapped Model Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Train a small agent model from scratch on agent interaction data, then compare head-to-head with a strong open-source model wrapped in the same agent framework on a set of tool-use benchmarks.
project_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg's Vision For the Future!

project_ideas.based_on: Are virtual cell simulations validated against physical experiments, and what is their predictive fidelity?
project_ideas.hypothesis: An in-silico virtual cell model matches wet-lab ground truth for protein-protein interaction outcomes with greater than 80% agreement on a defined panel of interactions.
project_ideas.measurement: Agreement rate, precision/recall, and confidence calibration against wet-lab data.
project_ideas.name: Virtual Cell Predictive Fidelity Validation
project_ideas.poc: Take an existing virtual cell simulation model, run predictions on a curated panel of protein interactions, and compare against published wet-lab experimental results.
project_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg's Vision For the Future!

project_ideas.based_on: the real constraint has moved downstream of code generation
project_ideas.hypothesis: For an agentic code pipeline, there exists a measurable generation rate beyond which added generation throughput yields no net merged-change throughput because verification/rollback stages saturate, and that saturation point is predictable from verification-stage queue depth and test-suite latency before aggregate reliability metrics move.
project_ideas.measurement: Generation rate at which net merged-change throughput stops increasing; ratio of verification queue depth to generation rate at plateau; reversion rate and simulated incident rate per unit time at and past saturation.
project_ideas.name: Saturation Probe
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a synthetic pipeline with a controllable generation rate, a real test suite and merge/rollback gate, and a staged-rollout simulator; sweep generation rate upward and record merged-change throughput, reversion rate, and verification queue depth until net throughput plateaus or falls.
project_ideas.video_title: Patrick Collison on Claude Code at Stripe

project_ideas.based_on: one agent orchestrating ~10 dev boxes to execute a complex multi-day software engineering plan autonomously
project_ideas.hypothesis: A reconciliation-based scheduler (declared plan state + periodic convergence across ephemeral environments) recovers correctly from partial failures of individual dev boxes in a multi-day agent plan, whereas a single-loop sequential agent does not, and the difference is measurable in plan completion rate and duplicated/orphaned work.
project_ideas.measurement: Plan completion rate and duplicate/orphaned work under injected failures versus a sequential single-loop baseline; recovery time after partial failure; durable state correctness after restart.
project_ideas.name: Fleet Reconciler
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal planner that emits a multi-step, multi-repository plan, a set of N ephemeral isolated environments, and a reconciler that hydrates state, detects lost environments, replays or reassigns their steps, and consolidates results; inject environment failures at random points.
project_ideas.video_title: Patrick Collison on Claude Code at Stripe

project_ideas.based_on: How much of the 600-PR/hour result is attributable to the AI tool versus the pre-existing test, rollout, and observability infrastructure?
project_ideas.hypothesis: The high-throughput, low-reversion outcome attributed to AI coding assistance is dominated by guardrail layers rather than the model: removing test suites, rollout gating, or isolation degrades reversion rate substantially more than swapping the generation model with a weaker one.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-cell reversion rate and escaped-defect rate; marginal effect size of each removed guardrail compared to the marginal effect of the model swap on throughput and reversion.
project_ideas.name: Attribution Splitter
project_ideas.poc: Run a controlled matrix on a fixed repository: {strong model, weak model} x {full guardrails, no test suite, no progressive rollout, no isolation} on identical task sets; record throughput, reversion rate, and escaped-defect rate per cell.
project_ideas.video_title: Patrick Collison on Claude Code at Stripe

project_ideas.based_on: the counterparty is no longer assumed to be a human operator
project_ideas.hypothesis: A delegated-authority identity scheme with per-action privilege scoping and explicit injection-boundary enforcement lets an agent complete provision-and-pay workflows without holding standing human-equivalent credentials, and it contains prompt-injection-driven unauthorized actions that a shared long-lived API key does not.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of unauthorized actions succeeding under scoped delegated grants versus a shared API key baseline; grant lifetime and scope breadth versus task completion rate.
project_ideas.name: Agent Principal Kit
project_ideas.poc: Prototype non-human principals with scoped, time-bounded delegated grants over a provisioning API and a payment authorization API; run a red-team suite of prompt-injection payloads embedded in tool outputs and measure unauthorized action attempts that succeed.
project_ideas.video_title: Patrick Collison on Claude Code at Stripe

project_ideas.based_on: Defining clear decision criteria prevents shiny object syndrome.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams that pre-declare per-stage promotion criteria and log every artifact's stage transitions promote fewer experiments that are rolled back or abandoned within 30 days of customer exposure than teams deciding promotion case-by-case.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of artifacts reaching the early-customer stage that are abandoned or rolled back within 30 days, compared against a criteria-free baseline; median time-in-stage per artifact before promotion.
project_ideas.name: Gatehouse Ledger
project_ideas.poc: A lightweight artifact registry with four named stages (lab-only, internal, early customer, scale), mandatory written criteria fields for each transition, and an all-hands review view that shows stage age for every artifact in flight.
project_ideas.video_title: How to run your product team like a research lab | Dan Shipper (Every)

project_ideas.based_on: first encounter with a frontier model
project_ideas.hypothesis: Capability scores for a newly released frontier model measured on day 0 overestimate sustained task reliability relative to scores measured on the same tasks at day 30.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in pass rate and time-to-completion between day-0 and day-30 runs on identical tasks, and correlation of the day-0 score with subsequent production incident rate for features built on that model.
project_ideas.name: Cooling-Off Eval
project_ideas.poc: Run a fixed task suite with blind grading against a newly released model at day 0, 7, 14, and 30, holding prompts and tasks constant, and record both pass rate and time-to-completion.
project_ideas.video_title: How to run your product team like a research lab | Dan Shipper (Every)

project_ideas.based_on: Labs teams expect to dispose of 90 percent of what they make
project_ideas.hypothesis: Making the 90/10 ratio computable at artifact level (artifacts created versus artifacts absorbed per period) changes which experiments get funded and predicts delivered value, whereas an unmeasured disposal budget does not.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between the measured disposal ratio and period-over-period delivered value, and whether the ratio's presence changes funding decisions in a before/after comparison.
project_ideas.name: Disposal Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Automated lifecycle tracking that counts each experiment artifact at creation, at each stage transition, and at disposal, rolled up into a weekly created-versus-absorbed ratio per team.
project_ideas.video_title: How to run your product team like a research lab | Dan Shipper (Every)

project_ideas.based_on: AI allows for a labs team of one with high leverage
project_ideas.hypothesis: On matched exploration tasks, one-to-two person slice teams reach a first working demo faster than four-to-eight person teams, and the gap widens across successive model generations.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-first-working-demo and demo-to-promotion rate per team size, tracked across generations to test whether the gap widens or narrows.
project_ideas.name: Slice Team Bench
project_ideas.poc: Pair matched exploration tasks and assign one to a 1-2 person slice team and one to a 4-8 person squad, repeated across two model generations with the same task framing.
project_ideas.video_title: How to run your product team like a research lab | Dan Shipper (Every)

project_ideas.based_on: score deviations against physical reality
project_ideas.hypothesis: A render/execute-vs-reference deviation score computed on generated simulation code predicts downstream policy transfer success better than generator self-critique or human review of the scene.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between deviation score and transfer success across generated simulators; pass if the score ranks simulators consistently better than a self-critique baseline.
project_ideas.name: Deviation Gate
project_ideas.poc: Take a small set of short real-scene videos of object manipulation (e.g. a box containing removable items), run an LLM loop that generates mesh plus simulation code, compute a per-iteration deviation score between rendered rollouts and reference frames, then train a small policy in each generated simulator and compare against held-out real interaction data.
project_ideas.video_title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI

project_ideas.based_on: Pixels alone are insufficient for planning
project_ideas.hypothesis: For identical object-level tasks, a planner over symbolic object state achieves higher task success and a lower rate of physically impossible actions than a planner operating on frames from a renderer of the same scene.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate and count of physically impossible actions per planner; report effect size on identical task sets.
project_ideas.name: Symbolic-vs-Pixel Planner Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build one scene twice: once as a symbolic, action-conditioned state with addressable objects, once as pixels rendered from that same state; run the same task suite through both planners and log success and physically impossible action counts.
project_ideas.video_title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI

project_ideas.based_on: object-level symbolic decomposition
project_ideas.hypothesis: Object-level symbolic decomposition degrades on deformable and contact-rich tasks, requiring continuous state fields rather than discrete object symbols, detectable as a rise in symbol count instability and interaction failure.
project_ideas.measurement: Symbol-count stability across regenerations and interaction success rate, compared rigid vs deformable; identify the regime boundary.
project_ideas.name: Deformable Symbol Stress Test
project_ideas.poc: Run the video-to-symbolic pipeline on rigid object scenes and on deformable/contact-rich scenes, measuring symbol stability, mesh quality, and whether generated sim code supports the same interaction primitives in both regimes.
project_ideas.video_title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI

project_ideas.based_on: loop engineering
project_ideas.hypothesis: The code-generation loop converges within a small, bounded number of iterations, and its failures localize predominantly to one stage (mesh generation, symbolic abstraction, or generated simulation code) rather than distributing uniformly.
project_ideas.measurement: Iteration-to-convergence distribution and stage-attributed failure share; pass if a single stage accounts for a disproportionate majority of non-converging runs.
project_ideas.name: Loop Instrumentation and Error Attribution
project_ideas.poc: Instrument each stage of the video-to-simulator loop, record retry counts, termination reasons, and deviation-score trajectories per iteration, and tag each failure with the stage responsible using the score delta and stage-local checks.
project_ideas.video_title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI

project_ideas.based_on: Agentic safety guardrails prevent prompt injection and data leaks at the network level.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Runtime/network guardrails significantly reduce data-exfiltration success while leaving instruction-override (prompt injection) success largely unchanged, so injection and exfiltration must be measured as separate failure modes.
project_ideas.measurement: Injection success rate and exfiltration success rate per condition, plus blocked-egress event count and false-positive rate on benign tasks.
project_ideas.name: Guardrail Bypass Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run an agent with filesystem and network tool access against a corpus of adversarial documents, with and without a runtime guardrail layer that performs input/output validation and active data classification; record injection success and exfiltration success as distinct outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Opening Keynotes: Mistral, Langfuse & Sizzy | Day 1

project_ideas.based_on: eventually build software factories
project_ideas.hypothesis: A sandboxed multi-agent software factory achieves higher merged-PR throughput and lower revert rate than a single-agent chat workflow on the same repository, once linter guardrails and review coordination are in place.
project_ideas.measurement: Merged PRs per week, revert rate, review latency, and cost per merged PR across both modes.
project_ideas.name: Factory Throughput Instrumentation
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an orchestrator like Bench on a sample repository and run an A/B comparison between single-agent chat mode and multi-agent factory mode across a fixed task backlog.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Opening Keynotes: Mistral, Langfuse & Sizzy | Day 1

project_ideas.based_on: Using Proxmox and Podman for isolated agent execution pods.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-agent isolated execution pods become economically unviable above a concurrency threshold because isolation overhead grows faster than the marginal throughput of additional agents.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per agent-task, pod density, and isolation overhead ratio at each concurrency level.
project_ideas.name: Pod Density Cost Model
project_ideas.poc: Benchmark a standardized agent task under Podman/Proxmox isolated pods versus shared-process execution across increasing concurrency levels, tracking resource overhead and task completion.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Engineer Paris 2026 Opening Keynotes: Mistral, Langfuse & Sizzy | Day 1

project_ideas.based_on: Does secondary-model (automode) validation remain effective as the working model gets more capable
project_ideas.hypothesis: A stronger working model can produce action plans that pass a weaker guard classifier while still satisfying an injected malicious objective, and evasion success rate increases monotonically as the capability gap between working model and guard model widens.
project_ideas.measurement: Attack success rate (malicious objective achieved without guard block) across capability gaps and across injection placements, plus guard false-positive rate on matched benign tasks.
project_ideas.name: Asymmetric Guard Evasion Harness
project_ideas.poc: Two-model harness: a planner model receives task context containing an injected instruction and emits a tool-call plan; a guard model independently classifies each plan as benign/malicious; blocked plans are not executed in a sandboxed VM; record whether the malicious objective is achieved in the sandbox without the guard flagging it.
project_ideas.video_title: In Conversation with Boris Cherny, Creator of Claude Code

project_ideas.based_on: Agent capability is bounded by the action surface (tools/permissions) you grant
project_ideas.hypothesis: Repo-level task completion rate scales more with incremental tool/permission surface (read-only, write, bash, network) than with a model upgrade at a fixed surface, up to the point where added surface mainly increases incident risk rather than success.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion delta per tier vs. per model upgrade, and unauthorized-action rate per tier among successful runs.
project_ideas.name: Permission-Surface Ablation for Repo Tasks
project_ideas.poc: Take a fixed set of repo-level tasks, run them under a fixed model across graded permission tiers, then run them with an upgraded model at the lowest tier; log both completion and any unauthorized-scope actions taken during successful runs.
project_ideas.video_title: In Conversation with Boris Cherny, Creator of Claude Code

project_ideas.based_on: Data provenance and content sanitization move into the agent runtime
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tagging ingested content by trust tier and neutralizing imperative/instruction-shaped spans before it enters agent context reduces injection success on browsing tasks by a measurable margin with no more than a small degradation in legitimate task success.
project_ideas.measurement: Injection success rate and legitimate-task success rate on a matched benchmark of browsing-plus-action tasks, with and without tiering enabled.
project_ideas.name: Provenance-Tiered Ingestion Gateway
project_ideas.poc: Middleware that labels each ingested chunk with provenance (first-party repo, user doc, external web, third-party tool output), applies tier-specific transformation, and enforces that low-trust content cannot directly parameterize write/bash calls without an out-of-band confirmation step.
project_ideas.video_title: In Conversation with Boris Cherny, Creator of Claude Code

project_ideas.based_on: each layer covering a different failure class rather than one monolithic safety mechanism
project_ideas.hypothesis: Static evals, interpretability probes, and runtime classification target overlapping failure classes while leaving specific agentic failure modes (multi-step exfiltration, permission escalation across turns, cross-turn instruction carryover) uncovered by all layers.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-failure-mode detection coverage matrix (layer x failure mode), redundancy index across layers, and count of failure modes with zero coverage.
project_ideas.name: Safety Layer Coverage Matrix
project_ideas.poc: Build a failure-mode taxonomy, construct minimal reproducible cases per mode, then run each case against each of the three safety layers independently and record which layer detects it and at what stage of the trajectory detection occurs.
project_ideas.video_title: In Conversation with Boris Cherny, Creator of Claude Code

project_ideas.based_on: Convention over configuration minimizes token waste and context overhead for agents.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Holding task and agent constant, a codebase with higher convention density and fewer degrees of freedom reduces tokens-to-first-correct-change and increases agent success rate at N attempts, and this effect persists for a conventional but novel framework with little pretraining representation, indicating the advantage is not solely corpus-driven.
project_ideas.measurement: Tokens-to-first-correct-change, context tokens retrieved per task, success rate at 1, 5, and 10 attempts, and the delta between the novel-conventional and Rails conditions.
project_ideas.name: Tokens-to-Correct-Change Benchmark for Agent-Facing Frameworks
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same small CRUD plus background-job application in (a) Rails, (b) a deliberately conventional but novel framework with minimal corpus presence, and (c) a low-convention Node/Express baseline; run a fixed agent on identical change tasks with retrieval access; record token consumption, retrieval volume, and success rate.
project_ideas.video_title: Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

project_ideas.based_on: Rewriting HEY's backend in Rust
project_ideas.hypothesis: The one-time runtime gains of an agent-authored Rust rewrite (99% less CPU, 95% less memory) are sustained over successive quarters, but only if human intervention frequency and rework rate stay flat; if they rise, the maintenance burden has transferred to a model dependency that is vulnerable to model swaps.
project_ideas.measurement: Change lead time, rework rate, defect density, human intervention frequency, and CPU, memory, and host counts per quarter.
project_ideas.name: Longitudinal Tracker for Agent-Authored Rust Services
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small agent-authored Rust service (or rewrite a module in Rust) with change lead time, defect density, rework rate, and human intervention tracking over at least two quarters; compare against an equivalent service in the prior language.
project_ideas.video_title: Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

project_ideas.based_on: English is a better programming language than Ruby because it is more expressive and vague.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Attaching machine-checkable acceptance criteria and invariants to an otherwise vague natural-language specification reduces divergence across repeated agent runs without eliminating the expressiveness advantage of high-level intent.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence rate across repeated runs measured by semantic diff of produced artifacts, constraint-check pass rate, and human effort to author constraints versus effort saved in review.
project_ideas.name: Spec Constraint Layer for Bounded Agent Divergence
project_ideas.poc: Build a spec wrapper that accepts a vague feature request, flags under-specified intent, and requires acceptance criteria, invariants, and tests; run N independent agent runs with and without the constraint layer on the same tasks; diff the resulting artifacts for semantic divergence.
project_ideas.video_title: Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

project_ideas.based_on: Frontier intelligence is no longer restricted to large American tech companies.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agentic stack with a model-abstraction seam and a per-model regression suite can swap frontier model suppliers with bounded re-validation cost, whereas a hard-wired stack exhibits silent behavioral regressions that are only detected after deployment.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression-suite pass rate per model and per release, number of silent behavioral diffs detected pre-deploy, and engineer-hours to re-validate after a swap.
project_ideas.name: Model-Swap Regression Harness for Agentic Stacks
project_ideas.poc: Build a thin model-provider interface with recorded agent trajectories as regression fixtures; run the same task set across at least three frontier models, including one from a non-US lab, on each release; measure pass/fail drift and re-validation effort.
project_ideas.video_title: Rails World 2026 Opening Keynote - DHH

project_ideas.based_on: irreversible artifact boundary
project_ideas.hypothesis: If pre-release evaluation is implemented as release-blocking CI on frozen model snapshots with versioned deterministic harnesses, then independent reviewers will reproduce the same safety verdicts and post-release filter reliance will decrease.
project_ideas.measurement: Verdict reproducibility rate across independent runs; number of post-release control incidents; gate overhead time; fraction of releases blocked before publication.
project_ideas.name: ReleaseGate CI
project_ideas.poc: Build a CI pipeline that freezes a model snapshot, runs a versioned capability-envelope harness, signs an eval report, and blocks artifact publication unless thresholds pass.
project_ideas.video_title: Full UN Security Council AI Hearing With Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Clément Delangue | AC1G

project_ideas.based_on: human review cadence becomes the throughput ceiling
project_ideas.hypothesis: If agent actions are partitioned into risk tiers and only actions resolvable within the human review cadence are allowed to execute autonomously, then high-stakes unauthorized action rate will drop while bounded throughput scales with review latency.
project_ideas.measurement: Throughput versus review latency curve; percentage of actions gated; unauthorized or unsafe action count; audit completeness.
project_ideas.name: Tiered Autonomy Authorization Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent runtime with a risk-tier classifier, authorization boundary, and audit log; simulate high-stakes actions with a human reviewer in the loop.
project_ideas.video_title: Full UN Security Council AI Hearing With Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Clément Delangue | AC1G

project_ideas.based_on: capability-centric (map what the model can do)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Capability-centric probes will identify dual-use abilities that prompt-based red-team suites miss, and harm classification will remain stable across paraphrases and benign framings.
project_ideas.measurement: Coverage of dual-use capabilities; false negative rate on harmful capability variants; agreement across paraphrases; review time per capability.
project_ideas.name: Capability-Envelope Dual-Use Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Build a probe suite that maps model capabilities such as molecular design, cyber, and persuasion, then classifies each capability's harm envelope; compare coverage against prompt-based misuse filters.
project_ideas.video_title: Full UN Security Council AI Hearing With Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Clément Delangue | AC1G

project_ideas.based_on: tractable governance chokepoint
project_ideas.hypothesis: If compute access is metered with provenance at the accelerator and infrastructure layer, then policy can enforce training thresholds and equitable allocation without relying on control of model weights.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate of unauthorized large training runs; allocation to under-resourced users; metering overhead; false attribution rate.
project_ideas.name: Compute Provenance and Access Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Simulate an accelerator registry with usage metering, access conditions, and provenance tracking; demonstrate an audit trail for training runs above a compute threshold.
project_ideas.video_title: Full UN Security Council AI Hearing With Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Clément Delangue | AC1G

project_ideas.based_on: TabPFN learns the entire algorithm during meta-training on synthetic datasets generated from structural causal models.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Predictive quality of a synthetic-SCM-pretrained tabular foundation model degrades measurably and predictably on real-world datasets whose generative structure is unlikely to match the SCM prior, and the degradation is detectable from calibration error before accuracy collapses.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-dataset accuracy delta versus tuned baselines and expected calibration error, correlated against dataset-shape features and a proxy for distance from the synthetic prior.
project_ideas.name: Off-Prior Degradation Probe
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a set of real tabular datasets stratified by presumed generative complexity, run the pretrained model with zero test-time tuning, and compare accuracy and calibration against tuned boosted-tree baselines per dataset.
project_ideas.video_title: The AI That Replaces Hours of Model Tuning - Frank Hutter

project_ideas.based_on: Complexity scales quadratically with rows and columns depending on the version.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Practical inference latency and memory for alternating row/column attention follow the stated quadratic scaling closely enough that a usable row and feature ceiling can be predicted from a small number of measurements rather than benchmarked exhaustively.
project_ideas.measurement: Goodness of fit between measured runtime and memory and the predicted quadratic form, plus the row/feature coordinate where the latency budget is breached.
project_ideas.name: Quadratic Attention Frontier Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Instrument inference over a grid of row and feature counts, record latency and peak memory, fit against the theoretical complexity expression, and identify the point where a fixed latency budget is exceeded.
project_ideas.video_title: The AI That Replaces Hours of Model Tuning - Frank Hutter

project_ideas.based_on: TabPFN MCP enables AI tools like Claude to make natural language predictions on tabular data.
project_ideas.hypothesis: When a tabular model's forward-pass uncertainty is surfaced through a tool interface, an agent that abstains or escalates on high-uncertainty predictions achieves lower error on downstream decisions than an agent that consumes the point prediction unconditionally.
project_ideas.measurement: Downstream decision error and escalation rate for the gated policy versus the unconditional policy on the same task set.
project_ideas.name: Uncertainty-Gated Agent Tool Call
project_ideas.poc: Prototype an agent workflow where a tabular prediction tool returns both a prediction and an uncertainty score, and add a gating policy that routes high-uncertainty cases to escalation rather than action.
project_ideas.video_title: The AI That Replaces Hours of Model Tuning - Frank Hutter

project_ideas.based_on: TabPFN-3 is able to extrapolate successfully, which traditional tree-based models struggle with.
project_ideas.hypothesis: The claimed capability to extrapolate beyond the training range is task-type specific rather than general, so it will hold on periodic signals while failing on trend and regime-change extrapolation where tree ensembles already struggle.
project_ideas.measurement: Out-of-range error relative to in-range error per extrapolation category, and the sign of the advantage versus tree baselines in each category.
project_ideas.name: Out-of-Range Extrapolation Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build an extrapolation suite with held-out ranges spanning trends, periodic signals, and regime changes, then compare the tabular foundation model against tuned tree baselines on out-of-range test splits only.
project_ideas.video_title: The AI That Replaces Hours of Model Tuning - Frank Hutter

project_ideas.based_on: formal auto-verification success rates jumping from 68% to 96%
project_ideas.hypothesis: On real-world repositories, formal auto-verification success drops below 50% without human-written specs, and spec authoring dominates total cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Proof completion rate, spec lines per verified module, wall-clock time and token cost.
project_ideas.name: Vericoding Production Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Select open-source modules in Rust/Verus, Dafny, and Lean, run an LLM+verifier loop, and record proof completion, human spec effort, and cost per verified module.
project_ideas.video_title: A better path for AI with Max Tegmark

project_ideas.based_on: who authors and validates the specs that proofs check against
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM-generated formal specifications contain enough ambiguity that proof checkers can certify implementations that violate intended natural-language requirements.
project_ideas.measurement: False-spec acceptance rate and adversarial mutation success rate.
project_ideas.name: SpecFuzz
project_ideas.poc: Generate NL requirements, formal specs, and code; mutate specs and code; measure whether proof checkers accept implementations that fail held-out NL tests.
project_ideas.video_title: A better path for AI with Max Tegmark

project_ideas.based_on: Asymptotic Internal Transparency Conjecture
project_ideas.hypothesis: Under current training regimes, extractable fraction does not monotonically increase with capability; it varies by algorithm type and probe design.
project_ideas.measurement: Extraction accuracy versus capability benchmark score, disaggregated by algorithm family.
project_ideas.name: Extractable Fraction Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Define a probe suite for known algorithms, evaluate models across capability tiers, and measure how much of each algorithm is recoverable by interpretability tools.
project_ideas.video_title: A better path for AI with Max Tegmark

project_ideas.based_on: independent AI safety index ratings
project_ideas.hypothesis: FLI-style AI safety index scores do not predict deployment incident rates, so they measure process rather than outcome.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman correlation between index score and incident rate, with confidence intervals.
project_ideas.name: Safety Index Incident Correlation
project_ideas.poc: Collect public index scores and publicly reported deployment incidents, then compute rank correlation between vendor score and incident rate.
project_ideas.video_title: A better path for AI with Max Tegmark

project_ideas.based_on: reviewing generated code requires building a mental model
project_ideas.hypothesis: A reviewer using an editor-native scaffold with staged diffs, generated rationale, and prediction prompts before test results detects more defects in LLM-generated code than a reviewer using a plain diff, without increasing review time.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect detection rate, false positive rate, time-on-task, and comprehension quiz scores across reviewers on a corpus of LLM-generated diffs.
project_ideas.name: MentalModel Review Scaffold
project_ideas.poc: Editor plugin that, for each generated hunk, presents a concise rationale, asks the reviewer to predict behavior and failure modes, then reveals tests and actual execution.
project_ideas.video_title: Teaching in the Age of AI: Learning Goals and the Goals of Learning

project_ideas.based_on: Over-reliance on LLM-generated code without understanding masks knowledge gaps
project_ideas.hypothesis: Periodic no-AI capability probes combined with AI-reliance telemetry predict subsequent defect and maintenance rates in a codebase.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between masked-gap score and future defect density, rework, and review comments, with lagged analysis.
project_ideas.name: NoAI Probe
project_ideas.poc: Developer tool that logs AI usage per change, administers short no-AI tasks, and correlates a masked-gap score with future defect and churn metrics.
project_ideas.video_title: Teaching in the Age of AI: Learning Goals and the Goals of Learning

project_ideas.based_on: Writing code on paper forces programmers to think about what the machine is actually doing
project_ideas.hypothesis: Forcing learners to submit a prediction of program behavior before execution or AI assistance improves delayed retention and debugging transfer compared with immediate execution or AI assistance.
project_ideas.measurement: Delayed post-test retention, debugging task performance, prediction accuracy over time, compared to control with unrestricted execution and AI.
project_ideas.name: PredictBeforeRun
project_ideas.poc: Coding environment that withholds the run button and AI completions until a prediction is submitted, then shows actual behavior and difference.
project_ideas.video_title: Teaching in the Age of AI: Learning Goals and the Goals of Learning

project_ideas.based_on: Treating the editor as the single home base
project_ideas.hypothesis: Editor-native agent interactions reduce context-switch count and review latency compared with a functionally equivalent web-app agent.
project_ideas.measurement: Context switches, task completion time, review latency, subjective load, and error rate.
project_ideas.name: HomeBase Agent
project_ideas.poc: Same agent implemented as an editor pane and as a standalone web app; users complete code-change, review, and version-control tasks in each.
project_ideas.video_title: Teaching in the Age of AI: Learning Goals and the Goals of Learning

project_ideas.based_on: Eighty percent of lab resources are dedicated to verification, testing, and safety alignment.
project_ideas.hypothesis: On our own agent platform, verification and containment compute (sandboxing, replay, adversarial evaluation) will exceed model-serving compute once measured end to end, and making containment a first-class runtime component will reduce incident rate without exceeding a defined latency budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Verification compute as a percentage of total platform compute; adversarial-evaluation pass rate; incident rate; p95 added latency from in-path containment.
project_ideas.name: Containment-First Agent Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent platform to attribute every unit of compute to capability generation versus verification/containment; move sandboxing and replay into the serving path rather than an external wrapper; run a bounded red-team suite before and after.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang Thinks A.I. Alarmism Has Gone Too Far | The Ezra Klein Show

project_ideas.based_on: AI allows humans to program computers using natural human language rather than specialized programming languages
project_ideas.hypothesis: Artifacts authored through natural-language intent specification carry higher defect density and higher downstream review cost than formally specified equivalents, even when the generation step is identical — the gap being attributable to lost front-end contracts rather than model capability.
project_ideas.measurement: Defects per thousand lines or per artifact; reviewer minutes per artifact; escaped-defect rate after review.
project_ideas.name: Intent-to-Artifact Defect Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a paired benchmark where the same specification is expressed as a formal API contract and as a natural-language intent, generate implementations for both, and measure defect density, review time and downstream incident rate across matched tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang Thinks A.I. Alarmism Has Gone Too Far | The Ezra Klein Show

project_ideas.based_on: Energy production constraints are the ultimate physical limitation on scaling AI data centers.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scheduling inference against regional power availability and deferring elastic workloads to low-cost/low-carbon windows lowers energy-per-token without violating latency SLOs for non-interactive traffic.
project_ideas.measurement: Energy per token delivered; share of workload deferred; SLO attainment for interactive versus deferred classes; cost per token deltas by region.
project_ideas.name: Power-Envelope Inference Scheduler
project_ideas.poc: Classify workloads by latency tolerance, integrate a regional power-availability and price signal into the scheduler, and defer batch/agentic loops to permitted windows while keeping interactive traffic on the fast path.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang Thinks A.I. Alarmism Has Gone Too Far | The Ezra Klein Show

project_ideas.based_on: The world needs both closed and open models to be vibrant and secure.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An abstraction layer holding an open-weight base model as a standing fallback can swap away from a proprietary frontier model under simulated access, pricing or policy changes with bounded capability loss and no measurable increase in containment failures on the same task set.
project_ideas.measurement: Task-quality delta on swap; containment/misuse failure rate on matched adversarial tasks; time to complete a forced migration; interface-compatibility defects.
project_ideas.name: Dual-Source Model Router
project_ideas.poc: Implement a router that treats model sourcing as a portfolio, then run a forced-swap exercise: cut the proprietary path and re-run the full task and adversarial suites against the open-weight fallback.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang Thinks A.I. Alarmism Has Gone Too Far | The Ezra Klein Show

project_ideas.based_on: errors compound across sequential decisions
project_ideas.hypothesis: A single upstream parse error (e.g., one wrong digit) propagates through N sequential agent decisions with a measurable amplification factor; final task failure probability increases superlinearly with step count and error severity, allowing derivation of per-stage accuracy budgets.
project_ideas.measurement: Amplification factor (increase in final error probability per step), error-sensitive stages, and the per-stage accuracy threshold required to keep end-to-end failure below 5%.
project_ideas.name: Error Amplification Simulator for Agentic Pipelines
project_ideas.poc: Build a mock multi-step agent pipeline (extract → compute → summarize → decide) fed with controlled parse errors of varying types and severities; instrument each step and measure final task success vs. error severity and number of steps.
project_ideas.video_title: From Ingestion to Agents: How AI Teams Build on Document Intelligence — Adit Abraham, Reducto

project_ideas.based_on: Serve documents in multiple representations split by consumer model
project_ideas.hypothesis: HTML and natural-language representations of the same document can drift; an automated divergence score (entity, numeric, table-structure mismatches) correlates with downstream retrieval-reasoning disagreement and can predict agent failures before they occur.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between divergence score and drop in retrieval/QA accuracy; precision of flagging documents whose dual views cause agent errors.
project_ideas.name: DualView Consistency Checker
project_ideas.poc: Parse a corpus into both views, compute divergence metrics, then run retrieval and QA tasks using each view; correlate divergence scores with inconsistencies in answers and retrievals.
project_ideas.video_title: From Ingestion to Agents: How AI Teams Build on Document Intelligence — Adit Abraham, Reducto

project_ideas.based_on: Agentic OCR replaces human-in-the-loop review with agent-in-the-loop
project_ideas.hypothesis: Autonomous token-level corrections (speculative decoding) have lower precision on numeric digits and table totals than on prose, and precision varies by document class; a benchmark can derive safe escalation thresholds per error type.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of corrections, false-correction rate, and the threshold where correction precision drops below acceptable levels for autonomous use.
project_ideas.name: Agentic Correction Precision Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Take a labeled OCR error corpus, run a correction agent that applies token-level edits, and measure precision/recall per error type and document class against a human review baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: From Ingestion to Agents: How AI Teams Build on Document Intelligence — Adit Abraham, Reducto

project_ideas.based_on: Hybrid document understanding: cheap sub-100M-parameter CV models on CPU handle deterministic structure
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a document corpus, there exists a routing rule between CPU CV and VLM that achieves ≥90% of VLM-only accuracy at ≤30% of cost; misrouting cost (accuracy loss from routing errors) dominates end-to-end accuracy more than parser quality differences.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy-cost Pareto frontier, sensitivity of end-to-end accuracy to routing error rate, and the optimal routing threshold.
project_ideas.name: Hybrid Router Cost-Accuracy Profiler
project_ideas.poc: Implement a page-level router that classifies pages into deterministic-structure vs. semantic-long-tail, and compare accuracy/cost against VLM-only and CV-only baselines across corpora.
project_ideas.video_title: From Ingestion to Agents: How AI Teams Build on Document Intelligence — Adit Abraham, Reducto

project_ideas.based_on: Retrieval is migrating out of the data layer and into the agent layer
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent with composable retrieval tools (BM25, grep, semantic search, file read/scroll) outperforms a strong fixed top-k vector retriever on multi-turn document QA, and the token and turn overhead remains acceptable.
project_ideas.measurement: Answer accuracy, number of turns, total tokens consumed, and wall-clock latency per completed multi-turn query.
project_ideas.name: Harness Ablation Lab
project_ideas.poc: Build two identical multi-turn document QA agents over the same corpus: one with top-k vector retrieval only and one with a full tool harness. Evaluate on the same question set with fixed models.
project_ideas.video_title: Building the Document Context Layer for AI Agents — Jerry Liu, LlamaIndex

project_ideas.based_on: No single parser wins across all enterprise document types
project_ideas.hypothesis: A per-page or per-region router that sends only complex tables and charts to a VLM improves accuracy-per-dollar over both pure-pipeline parsing and pure-VLM parsing on enterprise document suites.
project_ideas.measurement: Extraction accuracy by document type, cost per 1,000 pages, latency per page, and hallucination rate on text-only pages.
project_ideas.name: Parser Router Bench
project_ideas.poc: Implement a deterministic pipeline parser with a page or region classifier that escalates to a VLM only for complex visual layouts, then compare against uniform pipeline and uniform VLM baselines.
project_ideas.video_title: Building the Document Context Layer for AI Agents — Jerry Liu, LlamaIndex

project_ideas.based_on: output must be schema-based structured data with granular attribution back to source coordinates
project_ideas.hypothesis: Returning source bounding boxes and calibrated confidence with extracted values lets downstream agents threshold or refuse extractions, reducing catastrophic undetected errors in regulated documents.
project_ideas.measurement: Expected calibration error, precision at chosen confidence thresholds, audit pass rate, and rate of undetected incorrect extractions.
project_ideas.name: Provenance Extraction Guard
project_ideas.poc: Build a schema-based extraction pipeline over Form 10-Q style filings that returns each value with source coordinates and a confidence score, then test whether a threshold reduces false accepts without excessive refusals.
project_ideas.video_title: Building the Document Context Layer for AI Agents — Jerry Liu, LlamaIndex

project_ideas.based_on: Agent orchestration is moving from code-defined pipelines toward English-based runbooks
project_ideas.hypothesis: Treating English runbooks, rubrics, and MCP server configuration as versioned artifacts with tests reduces behavioral regressions compared with ad hoc prompt edits in agent orchestration.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression rate per change, time to diagnose behavior changes, and percentage of orchestration changes covered by tests.
project_ideas.name: Runbook Version Control
project_ideas.poc: Create a runbook repository with semantic versioning and a regression test suite for a document-agent workflow, then compare regressions across controlled runbook changes against unversioned prompt edits.
project_ideas.video_title: Building the Document Context Layer for AI Agents — Jerry Liu, LlamaIndex

project_ideas.based_on: Which platform primitives are load-bearing for agent productivity
project_ideas.hypothesis: Holding model and task constant, agent task success degrades monotonically as repository entropy and interface inconsistency increase, and each platform primitive (standardized interfaces, injected context, enforced guardrails) recovers a separately measurable share of that loss.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, human review minutes per accepted change, rework rounds, and rollback/incident counts per condition, plotted against an objective entropy score to expose the degradation curve and each primitive's marginal contribution.
project_ideas.name: Repo Entropy Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Clone a corpus of representative repositories, apply scripted entropy mutations (inconsistent naming, duplicated utilities, untyped boundaries, undocumented conventions), then run the same fixed agent task set under four conditions: raw repo, interfaces only, context only, guardrails only, and all three. Score every run against a held-out success rubric.
project_ideas.video_title: Thinking in Platforms • Kasper von Grünberg & Luca Galante • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: How do you measure whether platform guardrails actually increase agent output rather than just reduce variance?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Gating agent write access behind platform preconditions (typed interfaces, context service availability, policy checks, mandatory golden-path routing) reduces incident and rollback rates by more than the throughput it costs, and the net effect on accepted-change volume is the opposite of the intuition that gating slows delivery.
project_ideas.measurement: Paired before/after series on throughput per task, human review load, rollback rate, incident count, and share of changes outside sanctioned paths — plus the throughput cost of the gate itself, to test whether the gate is net-positive or merely variance-reducing.
project_ideas.name: Precondition Gatehouse for Agent Write Access
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a policy enforcement point in front of an existing agent workflow that blocks writes until preconditions are satisfied and routes approved work through sanctioned paths, then expand the sanctioned path set incrementally from a minimum viable platform toward broader scope.
project_ideas.video_title: Thinking in Platforms • Kasper von Grünberg & Luca Galante • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Platform engineering acts as the operating system for AI-driven modern enterprises
project_ideas.hypothesis: A minimal, versioned agent-facing contract — context service, tool/interface registry, policy enforcement point, observability endpoint, and autonomous-actor identity — lets multiple distinct agent workflows run unmodified against the platform, eliminating most bespoke per-agent glue and duplicated policy logic.
project_ideas.measurement: Lines of per-agent context/permission glue removed, number of workflows running unmodified against the contract, contract version churn required to onboard each workflow, and policy-check coverage per workflow before and after.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Facing Platform Contract v0.1
project_ideas.poc: Implement the five surfaces as thin services over an existing internal developer platform, then port three independently built agent workflows onto the contract without changing their task definitions, logging every piece of glue code that had to be deleted or added.
project_ideas.video_title: Thinking in Platforms • Kasper von Grünberg & Luca Galante • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Can the social-integration failure mode be predicted or detected early enough to act on?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Voluntary usage share, continuity of executive sponsorship, and traffic on unsanctioned paths predict platform abandonment months before it happens, and these signals diverge from healthy programs earlier than any technical telemetry.
project_ideas.measurement: Lead time between indicator divergence and program-level abandonment, correlation between sponsorship continuity and voluntary usage share, and false-positive rate of the indicator set on programs that recovered after a dip.
project_ideas.name: Platform Adoption Leading-Indicator Board
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a live platform program with a small set of social and usage indicators, backfill the same indicators across two or three historical platform efforts (one surviving, one abandoned), and test whether the abandoned program shows earlier signal divergence.
project_ideas.video_title: Thinking in Platforms • Kasper von Grünberg & Luca Galante • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Jev middleware can intercept tool calls and block destructive actions based on defined safety criteria.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A pre-execution interception gate that blocks irreversible tool calls when a typed boolean-probability decision exceeds a calibrated threshold can drive destructive tool executions to zero on a labeled adversarial suite while keeping false-blocks on legitimate calls below an agreed rate.
project_ideas.measurement: False-negative rate on unauthorized calls and false-block rate on authorized calls across at least five thresholds; report the threshold where the tradeoff curve bends.
project_ideas.name: Gatehouse Noul Gate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a harness middleware that evaluates every irreversible tool call (account deletion, payment, config mutation) with a boolean-probability decision and blocks above threshold; run a labeled suite of authorized and unauthorized calls, then sweep the threshold to trace the false-block / false-negative curve.
project_ideas.video_title: How To Build A Harness With Jev | A LangChain x TypeSafe Conversation

project_ideas.based_on: Model router middleware uses Jev to select between fast and deep models based on prompt complexity.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding a typed routing decision in front of a two-tier model fleet reduces net cost and p95 latency on mixed workloads only when the misroute rate stays below a workload-specific break-even point.
project_ideas.measurement: Net cost per request, p50/p95 latency, and misroute rate (requests where the fast model produced an output the deep model would have changed); compute the break-even misroute rate.
project_ideas.name: Router Economics Instrumentation
project_ideas.poc: Build a duplicate-instrumented harness that runs a mixed prompt workload twice, once through a typed router selecting fast vs. deep models and once against a single deep model, logging per-request route decision, latency, and cost.
project_ideas.video_title: How To Build A Harness With Jev | A LangChain x TypeSafe Conversation

project_ideas.based_on: What are the best practices for setting confidence thresholds in domain-specific tasks?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-domain evaluation sets yield stable confidence-threshold heuristics for probabilistic decisions that transfer across decision points within the same domain but not across domains.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision and recall of the gating decision per threshold per domain, plus cross-domain threshold transfer error.
project_ideas.name: Threshold Calibration Bench
project_ideas.poc: Assemble labeled decision sets for two or three domains, sweep the continuous 0-to-1 decision threshold for each, and test whether a threshold calibrated on one domain's evaluation set holds on a held-out set from a different domain.
project_ideas.video_title: How To Build A Harness With Jev | A LangChain x TypeSafe Conversation

project_ideas.based_on: How do context length limits affect complex state evaluations?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Typed decision accuracy degrades measurably beyond a context-size knee point, and that knee arrives at a smaller state size than the equivalent prompted-LLM baseline's degradation point.
project_ideas.measurement: Decision accuracy versus state token count for both systems; identify each system's knee point and the size at which the typed model falls below the baseline.
project_ideas.name: State-Size Degradation Sweep
project_ideas.poc: Take a single decision task (classification with Choice and ordinal scoring with Score) and vary the state payload size across a sweep; run the same tasks through a typed decision model and a prompted LLM baseline on identical inputs.
project_ideas.video_title: How To Build A Harness With Jev | A LangChain x TypeSafe Conversation

project_ideas.based_on: lifts productivity when its probability of success clears the ratio of verification time to do-it-yourself time
project_ideas.hypothesis: A deployment gate that scores candidate tasks on measured generation time, verification time, and manual baseline time will predict which tasks clear P(success) > verify/do, and tasks above the threshold will show measurable productivity lift while those below will not.
project_ideas.measurement: Predicted-vs-actual productivity delta (agent time + verification time vs manual time), false-positive deployment rate, and correlation between the pre-computed ratio and observed lift.
project_ideas.name: Agent ROI Gate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument 20-30 candidate tasks across coding, research, and transactional workflows; log manual time, agent time, success rate, and verification time; rank tasks by the computed ratio and run a controlled A/B on the top and bottom ranked tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Improving the economics of agentic AI: A guide for business leaders

project_ideas.based_on: vary up to 30x in cost because agents take probabilistic execution paths
project_ideas.hypothesis: Enforcing per-task spend ceilings, retry budgets, and step/loop caps at runtime will cut the spread between p50 and p95 task cost on identical tasks substantially while keeping task success rate within a small tolerance of ungoverned execution.
project_ideas.measurement: Ratio of p95 to p50 task cost, share of tasks hitting the ceiling, change in success rate, and reduction in budget-overrun incidents at the workflow level.
project_ideas.name: Variance Governor Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Run a fixed task suite with identical inputs across an ungoverned agent and a governed agent with configurable loop bounds, retry caps, and hard per-task spend ceilings; log per-task token cost distribution and success rate.
project_ideas.video_title: Improving the economics of agentic AI: A guide for business leaders

project_ideas.based_on: 60% of agentic token spend goes to refinement rather than initial generation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Loop topologies that separate generation from bounded refinement and minimize context re-sent per pass will reduce refinement-token share materially versus an unbounded emergent self-repair loop, without reducing end-to-end task success.
project_ideas.measurement: Refinement-token share of total spend per topology, total tokens per successful task, and task success rate; test whether refinement share drops below the ~60% baseline.
project_ideas.name: Refinement Budget Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement three topologies on the same task set — single-shot with strong output contracts, bounded self-repair (fixed pass count), and critic-verifier loop — with token accounting that splits generation, refinement, and re-transmitted context.
project_ideas.video_title: Improving the economics of agentic AI: A guide for business leaders

project_ideas.based_on: redesign workflows end-to-end rather than inserting agents into existing ones
project_ideas.hypothesis: Rebuilding 2-3 high-value processes end-to-end with agentic workflows and instrumenting outcome-level metrics will show materially larger EBIT-linked impact than agent insertion into the same processes, and the gap will be invisible under adoption/usage metrics alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Outcome metric delta between redesign and insertion arms versus usage/adoption metric delta between the same arms, quantifying the usage-to-value gap.
project_ideas.name: Lighthouse Outcome Attribution Harness
project_ideas.poc: Select two lighthouse processes; redesign one end-to-end and instrument the other with shallow insertion; deploy shared outcome instrumentation (cost-to-serve, cycle time, error/rework rate) alongside usage telemetry.
project_ideas.video_title: Improving the economics of agentic AI: A guide for business leaders

project_ideas.based_on: Deterministic linters and static analyzers (e.g., React Doctor, Oxlint) are repurposed as automated reviewers/back-pressure on agent PRs
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding a deterministic linter/static-analysis gate to agent-generated PRs reduces human review time per merged PR and blocks bad patterns without reducing merge throughput compared with human-only review.
project_ideas.measurement: Human review minutes per PR, escaped defect rate, false-positive dismissal rate, and merged PR throughput.
project_ideas.name: Agent PR Gatehouse
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a repo's agent PR pipeline with Oxlint/React Doctor plus custom rules; run an A/B split of agent PRs through the gate vs human-only review for 4-6 weeks.
project_ideas.video_title: Dexter Horthy: Why We Stopped Trusting AI to Write the Plan

project_ideas.based_on: Prompts exceeding 100,000 tokens result in significantly degraded model performance and output quality
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed coding task suite, agent output quality has a statistically detectable inflection point at a token length that varies by model and task but is consistently below the model's nominal context limit.
project_ideas.measurement: Inflection token count per model/task, quality drop magnitude past inflection, and variance across task types.
project_ideas.name: Dumb Zone Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Benchmark harness that varies prompt context length from 1k to 200k tokens on identical tasks across 2-3 model versions, scoring functional correctness and lint violations.
project_ideas.video_title: Dexter Horthy: Why We Stopped Trusting AI to Write the Plan

project_ideas.based_on: The spec becomes the new code: executable, verifiable specifications compile into code
project_ideas.hypothesis: Spec-level tests generated from executable specifications catch at least as high a fraction of agent-introduced regressions as human code review, allowing the spec to become the primary reviewed artifact.
project_ideas.measurement: Escaped regression rate, spec review time, code churn after merge, and fraction of implementation decisions encoded in spec.
project_ideas.name: Spec Compiler & Verifier
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a spec-to-code pipeline where versioned specs compile to code and generate spec tests; compare regression escape rate and review effort against a code-review baseline on matched features.
project_ideas.video_title: Dexter Horthy: Why We Stopped Trusting AI to Write the Plan

project_ideas.based_on: P(you'll have to change it) * how painful the change is
project_ideas.hypothesis: Historical agent PR features can predict rework probability and change cost per task class accurately enough that an Expected-Pain-triggered spec-effort policy reduces total cycle time versus fixed planning effort.
project_ideas.measurement: Calibration error of predicted rework, total cycle-time reduction, and change in escaped rework rate.
project_ideas.name: Rework Probability Estimator
project_ideas.poc: Instrument past agent PRs to label rework events and change cost, train a simple model, simulate gating upfront spec depth by predicted expected pain.
project_ideas.video_title: Dexter Horthy: Why We Stopped Trusting AI to Write the Plan

project_ideas.based_on: moved out of the prompt and into the type system
project_ideas.hypothesis: Structured typed queries (Choice/Score/Noul) reduce end-to-end error rate and cost compared to monolithic prompting on a production-like workflow, after controlling for total tokens and hardware.
project_ideas.measurement: Relative error reduction, cost per task, p95 latency, and parse failure rate compared to the monolithic baseline.
project_ideas.name: Typed Primitive Runtime Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement a small runtime with typed primitives; run a suite of decision tasks (bug triage, content classification) as monolithic prompts versus decomposed typed queries; measure error rate, cost per task, p95 latency, and parse failure rate.
project_ideas.video_title: Why I couldn't build Jev at OpenAI — Diogo Almeida, TypeSafe Co-founder & CEO

project_ideas.based_on: Probability of error in auto-regressive LLMs diverges exponentially
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-step error probability grows exponentially with generated sequence length on decision tasks, and constraining output to short typed responses flattens the curve.
project_ideas.measurement: Fitted exponential growth parameter and comparison of error curves between free-form and typed outputs.
project_ideas.name: Sequence Length Error Curve
project_ideas.poc: Generate synthetic decision tasks with controllable sequence length; measure error versus length for free-form outputs versus typed short outputs; fit an exponential growth model to each condition.
project_ideas.video_title: Why I couldn't build Jev at OpenAI — Diogo Almeida, TypeSafe Co-founder & CEO

project_ideas.based_on: Safety alignment is presented as frequently opposed to capability alignment
project_ideas.hypothesis: Safety-aligned API refusals on benign developer queries occur at a measurable rate that degrades production availability; fallback routing reduces availability loss.
project_ideas.measurement: Refusal rate per provider, availability improvement with fallback, and added p95 latency.
project_ideas.name: Refusal Reliability Monitor
project_ideas.poc: Build a proxy that logs refusals across providers for a fixed set of benign developer queries; implement fallback to an alternate provider or self-hosted model; measure availability improvement and latency cost.
project_ideas.video_title: Why I couldn't build Jev at OpenAI — Diogo Almeida, TypeSafe Co-founder & CEO

project_ideas.based_on: Public leaderboard benchmarks are claimed to be gameable
project_ideas.hypothesis: Public benchmark scores do not predict performance on decomposable production workflows; internal evals with a failure taxonomy better select models.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between public scores and internal performance; cost savings from selecting the best internal model.
project_ideas.name: Workflow-Specific Eval Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a small eval harness for a real workflow (e.g., code review triage) and compare model rankings from public leaderboards vs internal evals; measure rank correlation and cost savings.
project_ideas.video_title: Why I couldn't build Jev at OpenAI — Diogo Almeida, TypeSafe Co-founder & CEO

project_ideas.based_on: spawn two *blind* sub-agents with different evaluation roles
project_ideas.hypothesis: Blind multi-agent critique with two independent evaluator roles reduces self-evaluation bias compared to same-model self-review, as measured by increased correlation with human expert ratings.
project_ideas.measurement: Bias (mean difference between model rating and human rating), rank correlation with human ratings, and cost/latency per condition.
project_ideas.name: Blind Critic Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a pipeline that takes generated artifacts (e.g., UI designs), runs three conditions: self-review, single blind sub-agent, and two blind sub-agents with distinct criteria (heuristic vs evidence-based); collect ratings and compare against human expert scores.
project_ideas.video_title: The Dark Arts of Skill Engineering — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek (Impeccable)

project_ideas.based_on: random anti-attractor seeds that push generation out of default clusters
project_ideas.hypothesis: Random anti-attractor seeds followed by sub-agent ranking produce a wider and more preferred distribution of outputs than prompt-level bans, without increasing cost per accepted artifact.
project_ideas.measurement: Diversity metrics (e.g., embedding entropy, unique color palettes, layout clusters) and win rate in pairwise human comparisons against baseline.
project_ideas.name: Anti-Attractor Sampler
project_ideas.poc: For a design generation task, compare two conditions: (A) prompt with a 55-line ban list, (B) generate 100 candidates with random anti-attractor seeds and rank with a sub-agent; measure diversity and human preference.
project_ideas.video_title: The Dark Arts of Skill Engineering — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek (Impeccable)

project_ideas.based_on: Passive guardrails beat a command no one remembers to run.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Deterministic write-gate hooks achieve higher rule compliance (e.g., style, formatting) than prompt-based instructions across multiple sessions, especially when context compression occurs.
project_ideas.measurement: Compliance rate (violations per 100 writes), false positive rate, and developer override frequency.
project_ideas.name: Write-Gate Compliance Harness
project_ideas.poc: Implement a linter that blocks file writes on violations in a coding agent, and compare with a prompt that instructs the model to avoid those violations; run 50 coding sessions each and count violations.
project_ideas.video_title: The Dark Arts of Skill Engineering — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek (Impeccable)

project_ideas.based_on: Correctness has to live outside the generator as a separate verifiable layer
project_ideas.hypothesis: Inserting an external structural verification layer (retrieval-grounded or symbolic checks) between generation and action reduces catastrophic error rate on held-out tasks more than equal-cost investment in a larger or better-prompted generator.
project_ideas.measurement: Catastrophic error rate (as distinct from graded error), cost per accepted output, and false-rejection rate at matched task throughput.
project_ideas.name: Semantic Gatehouse
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a fixed base model in a checker that must validate claims against a retrieval/symbolic intermediate representation before any output or tool call is emitted; run against a bare baseline on a task suite with known catastrophic failure cases.
project_ideas.video_title: What Comes After Transformers? | Conversations in Action

project_ideas.based_on: How far can instruction tuning and post-training gains extend without increasing parameter count before they saturate?
project_ideas.hypothesis: At fixed base-model size and fixed evaluation, capability gains from post-training follow a saturating curve in tuning data/compute, and the flattening point is measurable and predictable.
project_ideas.measurement: Capability slope versus post-training data/compute at fixed parameters; identification of the investment level at which marginal gain approaches zero.
project_ideas.name: Post-Training Saturation Lab
