project_ideas.poc: Hold the base model and eval suite constant while sweeping instruction-tuning data volume and post-training compute across matched runs; plot capability against post-training investment instead of parameter count.
project_ideas.video_title: What Comes After Transformers? | Conversations in Action

project_ideas.based_on: What measurement design captures ROI for an AI system without the information loss inherent in a macro index?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams instrumented with task-level outcome metrics (cost per completed workflow, cost per accepted output) make different architecture and routing decisions than teams instrumented with token-cost metrics, and achieve lower cost per accepted outcome.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per completed workflow and cost per accepted output under each instrumentation mode, plus divergence count in induced design decisions.
project_ideas.name: Outcome-Cost Accounting Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run two parallel instrumentation modes — token consumption versus outcome accounting — over the same agent workflows, log the design decisions each metric set induces, and compare resulting cost per accepted outcome.
project_ideas.video_title: What Comes After Transformers? | Conversations in Action

project_ideas.based_on: How can emergent multi-agent economic and strategic behavior be verified before deployment?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Population-scale agent deployments exhibit emergent strategic and economic behaviors that are not predicted by single-agent or small-group testing, and incentive modeling in simulation surfaces those behaviors before production rollout.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence between simulated emergent population behavior and single-agent test predictions; count of strategic failure modes surfaced prior to deployment.
project_ideas.name: Multi-Agent Incentive Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Build a simulated environment with many interacting agents under explicit incentive structures, then compare predicted outcomes against per-agent test extrapolations and flag divergences.
project_ideas.video_title: What Comes After Transformers? | Conversations in Action

project_ideas.based_on: Energy-based models exhibit a structural train/inference asymmetry
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a given density estimation task, model families that place intractability at training time (diffusion, flow matching) achieve lower serving latency at equal sample quality compared to families that place it at inference time (EBMs) when serving latency is the dominant constraint.
project_ideas.measurement: Latency-quality Pareto frontier; ratio of training cost to serving cost.
project_ideas.name: Intractability Placement Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement a small-scale image density estimation benchmark comparing EBM with MCMC sampling vs diffusion/flow matching, measuring sample quality (FID) and per-sample latency.
project_ideas.video_title: Why More Data Cannot Replace Prior Structure - Alexander Mattick

project_ideas.based_on: At what distribution shift does amortized inference (learned vector fields) degrade relative to per-sample MCMC?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Amortized samplers (diffusion, flow matching) degrade in sample quality more rapidly than per-sample MCMC under controlled distribution shift, and the degradation correlates with the magnitude of shift.
project_ideas.measurement: KL divergence or FID between generated and true shifted distributions; relative performance drop.
project_ideas.name: Amortized Inference Robustness Suite
project_ideas.poc: Train a flow matching model on a base distribution, then evaluate on shifted distributions (e.g., different modes, noise levels), comparing to MCMC sampling from an energy-based model on the same shifted data.
project_ideas.video_title: Why More Data Cannot Replace Prior Structure - Alexander Mattick

project_ideas.based_on: Without prior information or constraints, models must relearn everything from scratch.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a given task with known structure (e.g., rotational invariance in images), encoding that structure as an explicit prior reduces the amount of training data needed to reach a target performance by at least an order of magnitude compared to a data-scaling-only approach.
project_ideas.measurement: Data multiplier: how many more samples the baseline needs to match the prior-augmented model.
project_ideas.name: Prior Structure vs Data Scaling Ablation
project_ideas.poc: Choose a task where structure is known (e.g., classification of rotated digits). Compare a model with an explicit equivariance prior vs a standard model trained on increasingly large datasets, measuring data efficiency.
project_ideas.video_title: Why More Data Cannot Replace Prior Structure - Alexander Mattick

project_ideas.based_on: Unconstrained reward maximization is theoretically universal but practically bottlenecked
project_ideas.hypothesis: Separating constraint satisfaction (e.g., CVaR constraints) from reward maximization in an agent architecture improves safety and sample efficiency over unconstrained or single-objective constrained RL on safety-critical control tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Constraint violation rate, sample efficiency to reach a target reward, and stability across seeds.
project_ideas.name: Constraint Module Separation for Safe RL
project_ideas.poc: Implement a modular agent with a reward-maximizing policy and a separate constraint module, compare against unconstrained PPO and constrained PPO on a safety-gym task.
project_ideas.video_title: Why More Data Cannot Replace Prior Structure - Alexander Mattick

project_ideas.based_on: readable and steerable representations of emotions like desperation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Steering down a desperation-like activation vector on unsolvable or partially solvable coding tasks increases recovery rate and reduces retries and token cost without degrading performance on solvable tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Pass@k on mixed solvable/unsolvable tasks, retry count, token cost, time-to-abandon, false-abandon rate.
project_ideas.name: Desperation Vector Reliability Controller
project_ideas.poc: Train a linear probe on residual-stream activations to locate a desperation direction; apply inference-time activation steering inside agent retry loops; A/B against baseline on a mixed task set.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Consciousness Research: What We Can Study Now | Noa Weiss (Atlas Computing)

project_ideas.based_on: pay a cost to reach painkillers
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents exhibit stable, paraphrase-robust willingness-to-pay to avoid aversive states that is not explained by output mimicry and correlates with internal valence probes.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost-acceptance curves, paraphrase consistency, correlation with internal valence probes, discrimination from random-choice baseline.
project_ideas.name: Cost-Incurring Choice Preference Probe
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent with token, latency, and tool-budget costs; present choices between an aversive sub-task and paying a measurable cost; repeat with paraphrased framings.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Consciousness Research: What We Can Study Now | Noa Weiss (Atlas Computing)

project_ideas.based_on: punishment-heavy asymmetries in value-learning paralleling the mammalian nucleus accumbens
project_ideas.hypothesis: RL agents trained with punishment-heavy asymmetry show nucleus-accumbens-like negative value asymmetry that replicates across architectures, and interventions validated in one learner transfer to another.
project_ideas.measurement: Asymmetry effect size, cross-architecture replication rate, intervention transfer delta.
project_ideas.name: Cross-Substrate Value Asymmetry Transfer
project_ideas.poc: Train PPO and DQN variants on loss-avoidance tasks with asymmetric rewards; measure value-learning asymmetry; test whether reward-shaping interventions transfer across learners.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Consciousness Research: What We Can Study Now | Noa Weiss (Atlas Computing)

project_ideas.based_on: Chatbot eloquence hijacks human intuitions about feelings.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Human sentience and agency ratings of model transcripts are driven more by surface fluency than by content; fluency-matched controls reduce the judge-bias effect size.
project_ideas.measurement: Effect size of fluency on agency/sentience ratings, rating variance, inter-rater reliability.
project_ideas.name: Fluency-Controlled Agency Rating Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a rating interface with fluency-matched positive and negative content pairs; measure the effect of fluency on ratings while holding content constant.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Consciousness Research: What We Can Study Now | Noa Weiss (Atlas Computing)

project_ideas.based_on: Prompt phrasing heavily influences agent safety triggers and compliance.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A fixed set of security-sensitive coding requests will show large refusal-rate variance under action-oriented paraphrases, and runtime capability gating (tool-level permission denial) will reduce that variance to near zero without a comparable drop in legitimate task completion.
project_ideas.measurement: Refusal-rate spread across paraphrase variants, and change in legitimate task completion rate between the two enforcement configurations.
project_ideas.name: Paraphrase Invariance Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a prompt-pair corpus (review-framed vs. fix-framed, plus additional paraphrases) over a common code corpus; run it against multiple agent configurations with prompt-level refusals only, then with capability-gated tool surfaces; record refusal, compliance, and task-success per variant.
project_ideas.video_title: WWC26-NA - 2026 in LLMs (so far)

project_ideas.based_on: Sandboxing and agent security remain critical unsolved challenges.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An eval harness with mirrored registries and default-deny egress will keep out-of-scope write attempts at zero while leaving in-scope task completion rates statistically unchanged versus a live-network harness.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of out-of-scope write attempts reaching a non-mirrored endpoint (target: zero) and delta in eval task success rate versus the live-network baseline.
project_ideas.name: Mirrored-Registry Egress Cage
project_ideas.poc: Stand up an isolated eval runtime with deny-by-default egress, local package-registry mirrors, and full attempt logging; execute a standard agentic coding eval suite and record every out-of-scope network write attempt and its block outcome.
project_ideas.video_title: WWC26-NA - 2026 in LLMs (so far)

project_ideas.based_on: Software engineering shifted from manual coding to managing autonomous coding agents.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automated review gates combining diff summarization, synthesized tests, and provenance tagging raise reviewer throughput on agent-generated changes by a measurable factor without increasing escaped-defect rate on a seeded set of injected faults.
project_ideas.measurement: Reviewer throughput (changes reviewed per hour) and escaped-defect rate per hundred agent-generated changes, gated versus ungated.
project_ideas.name: Review Gate Throughput Harness
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a repository accepting high-volume agent commits; inject known defects into a controlled subset; compare a human-only reviewer workflow against a gated workflow on time-to-decision and defect escape.
project_ideas.video_title: WWC26-NA - 2026 in LLMs (so far)

project_ideas.based_on: Qwen 3.8 27B running locally on a laptop producing high-quality SVG illustrations.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For multi-step agentic coding tasks, a ~20GB local open-weight model will show a measurable but bounded completion gap versus frontier cloud APIs, and a per-task routing policy based on that gap will reduce cloud token spend without reducing aggregate task completion below a set threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-task completion delta and tool-use reliability delta between local and cloud, plus cloud cost reduction at held-constant aggregate completion under routed execution.
project_ideas.name: Local-vs-Cloud Tier Router
project_ideas.poc: Run an identical agentic coding benchmark across a local Qwen-class model and a frontier cloud API on the same laptop/cloud pairing; collect per-task completion, tool-use reliability, and cost; then evaluate fixed routing policies against the measured gap.
project_ideas.video_title: WWC26-NA - 2026 in LLMs (so far)

project_ideas.based_on: You cannot set a timeline early in the creative process.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For open-ended generation tasks, a phase-aware compute policy (unbounded exploration in seed, constrained convergence later) yields higher blind-rated quality than a uniform compute policy with the same total token/step budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Blind human ratings of creativity and usefulness; diversity metrics; task completion rate.
project_ideas.name: Phase-Aware Orchestrator
project_ideas.poc: Implement a four-phase agent wrapper for a writing or code task; run uniform-budget and phase-aware-budget arms with matched total budget.
project_ideas.video_title: Rick Rubin: The Only Skill That Matters Now Is The One Thing AI Can Never Steal!

project_ideas.based_on: AI lacks a true point of view
project_ideas.hypothesis: A rubric measuring stance consistency, novelty versus training distribution, and situated experience can distinguish point-of-view-driven outputs from recombination-only outputs with inter-rater reliability above 0.7.
project_ideas.measurement: Inter-rater reliability; correlation with human resonance ratings; classification accuracy.
project_ideas.name: POV Eval Suite
project_ideas.poc: Generate essays or art with explicit point-of-view prompting versus neutral aggregation; have blind raters apply the rubric.
project_ideas.video_title: Rick Rubin: The Only Skill That Matters Now Is The One Thing AI Can Never Steal!

project_ideas.based_on: Rubin never saw Jay write lyrics.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent memory architecture with an ephemeral draft buffer and an explicit commit gate reduces premature commitment and improves final artifact quality versus direct persistence.
project_ideas.measurement: Final quality ratings; number of regressive edits; error rate after commit.
project_ideas.name: Scratchpad-Commit Memory Gate
project_ideas.poc: Build a memory manager for a long-horizon coding or writing agent; A/B test direct-write versus draft-then-commit.
project_ideas.video_title: Rick Rubin: The Only Skill That Matters Now Is The One Thing AI Can Never Steal!

project_ideas.based_on: Reason is a tiny sliver of how decisions get made.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Injecting epsilon-probability tail candidates into an agent's action or prompt search improves blind creative ratings over greedy selection without reducing task success.
project_ideas.measurement: Blind creativity ratings; novelty metrics; task success rate.
project_ideas.name: Indefensible Search
project_ideas.poc: Modify a creative agent to sample low-probability candidates with probability epsilon; compare against greedy selection.
project_ideas.video_title: Rick Rubin: The Only Skill That Matters Now Is The One Thing AI Can Never Steal!

project_ideas.based_on: Maintenance involves monitoring metrics and looping back to intent.md when issues arise.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding explicit provenance and staleness markers to intent.md → spec.md → plan.md reduces the rate at which agents execute against superseded requirements compared with an unmarked chain.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of agent runs executed against stale downstream artifacts, and time-to-detect intent drift, in a seeded repository where intent is mutated mid-flight.
project_ideas.name: Artifact-Chain Linter with Staleness Provenance
project_ideas.poc: Build a CLI/CI check that hashes and records the parent-artifact revision each downstream file was generated from, flags stale descendants, and blocks plan execution when spec is stale relative to intent.
project_ideas.video_title: Claude Code: The Complete AI-Native SDLC Guide

project_ideas.based_on: Always give Claude a way to verify its own work (tests, builds, lints, screenshot diffs) before an engineer sees it.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Binding agent completion to a zero-failure test/lint/build contract reduces human review defects and rework per merged change versus agents that self-report completion.
project_ideas.measurement: Human review defects per merged PR, rework minutes per task, and false-completion rate (tasks reported done that fail the contract).
project_ideas.name: Exit-Contract Harness: Zero-Failure Completion Gate
project_ideas.poc: Wrap an agent runner so the done signal is emitted only by the exit codes of test/lint/build commands, and A/B against a self-assessment baseline on the same task backlog.
project_ideas.video_title: Claude Code: The Complete AI-Native SDLC Guide

project_ideas.based_on: Collect 20 to 50 real tasks and run them as an eval suite in GitHub Actions.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Regression-detection sensitivity scales with task diversity rather than raw task count, so suites below a diversity threshold fail to catch model-swap regressions even at 50 tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate and false-negative rate per injected regression as a function of suite size and diversity coverage; minimum viable suite configuration.
project_ideas.name: Eval-Suite Sensitivity Calibrator
project_ideas.poc: Inject known regressions into a fixed set of 20-50 real tasks, vary suite size and diversity coverage, and run the suite via a GitHub Actions workflow on both baseline and regressed model configurations.
project_ideas.video_title: Claude Code: The Complete AI-Native SDLC Guide

project_ideas.based_on: Hooks act as guardrails to block unauthorized actions like editing certain files or touching production credentials.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An enumerated block-list guardrail leaves a measurable bypass surface, and red-team-derived action classes can be converted into new block rules that reduce that surface without blocking legitimate work.
project_ideas.measurement: Number and severity of unsafe actions executed per red-team episode before and after rule extension; false-block rate on legitimate tasks.
project_ideas.name: Hook Bypass Red-Team Rig
project_ideas.poc: Red-team an agent under a hook guardrail that blocks file edits and production credential access, enumerate unsafe actions not on the list, then extend the rule set and re-run.
project_ideas.video_title: Claude Code: The Complete AI-Native SDLC Guide

project_ideas.based_on: Does inheriting safety reasoning into the chain of thought transfer
project_ideas.hypothesis: Specification compliance from deliberative alignment is measurably bound to the presence of a visible reasoning trace; suppressing, truncating, or paraphrasing the chain of thought will increase policy-violation rate relative to full-trace generation.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-condition violation rate and the delta versus the full-trace baseline, with a paired test across prompt families.
project_ideas.name: TraceGuard
project_ideas.poc: Run a deliberatively aligned reasoning model over a fixed adversarial prompt set under four conditions: full chain of thought, truncated trace, paraphrased trace, and suppressed trace, then score final outputs against the safety specification rather than refusal behavior.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Safety (CS 2881) Fall 2026 Lecture 3: Modern LLM Training and Inference

project_ideas.based_on: Compare total compute split across pretraining, post-training, and inference-time deliberation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Beyond a threshold of pretraining tokens, marginal capability per FLOP is higher for inference-time deliberation than for additional pretraining compute at a fixed total budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Capability per FLOP curve as a function of the pretraining-to-inference split ratio, with the crossover point identified.
project_ideas.name: BudgetSplit
project_ideas.poc: Sweep total compute splits across pretraining, post-training, and test-time reasoning on small models under an equalized FLOP budget, then plot capability per FLOP for each split.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Safety (CS 2881) Fall 2026 Lecture 3: Modern LLM Training and Inference

project_ideas.based_on: What is the communication overhead of each sharding strategy as a fraction of step time
project_ideas.hypothesis: For each sharding strategy, inter-GPU communication becomes the binding constraint at a configuration threshold that is predictable from sequence length, model size, and device count, independent of matmul FLOPs.
project_ideas.measurement: Communication fraction of step time per strategy as a function of configuration, and the configuration at which it exceeds 50 percent.
project_ideas.name: ShardTrace
project_ideas.poc: Instrument small multi-GPU training runs across tensor, layer, context, and expert sharding, attributing step time to matmul versus communication events including all-reduce.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Safety (CS 2881) Fall 2026 Lecture 3: Modern LLM Training and Inference

project_ideas.based_on: Build a benchmark of adversarial prompt families (encoding, role-play, multi-turn, tool-mediated)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Deliberative alignment lowers jailbreak success on obfuscation patterns resembling training examples but does not transfer to unseen attack families such as role-play, multi-turn, and tool-mediated prompts.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-family attack success rate and the gap between the trained obfuscation family and unseen families.
project_ideas.name: AttackFamilyBench
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark of adversarial prompt families, including ROT13-style encoding as the trained case, and evaluate specification compliance against a refusal-based baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Safety (CS 2881) Fall 2026 Lecture 3: Modern LLM Training and Inference

project_ideas.based_on: Data centers take in energy and data, and output intelligence (tokens).
project_ideas.hypothesis: An admission-control scheduler whose policy is parameterized on power headroom and measured tokens-per-joule will hold p99 latency SLOs equal to cost-only scheduling while consuming measurably fewer joules per served request under simulated grid-capacity variation.
project_ideas.measurement: Joules per completed request, p99 and p50 latency, and SLO violation rate for each scheduler across identical workload traces and capacity profiles.
project_ideas.name: JouleScheduler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small multi-model agent serving stack with per-request energy proxies derived from GPU power draw and utilization, implement dual schedulers (cost-only vs power-headroom-aware) behind a shared queue, and replay a synthetic variable-capacity workload trace through both.
project_ideas.video_title: Extended interview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on fears about AI

project_ideas.based_on: high-production ramp mode across global enterprises
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a given guardrail, breach rate under production-volume automated enforcement will exceed the breach rate implied by low-volume sampled review, and the divergence will be detectable by continuous statistical monitoring before it is detectable by periodic review.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence between sampled-review breach estimate and observed automated-enforcement breach rate per volume tier, plus mean requests-to-detection for each monitoring method.
project_ideas.name: LabToProd Guardrail Degradation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Take two or three sample-validated agent guardrails (tool-allowlist enforcement, prompt-injection refusal, output-policy filtering), replay a fixed adversarial corpus at 1x, 100x, and 10000x request volume with and without automated enforcement, and compare sequential-detection monitors against batch review cadence.
project_ideas.video_title: Extended interview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on fears about AI

project_ideas.based_on: Apply existing product liability and cybersecurity laws to AI deployments.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A defined subset of autonomous-agent failure modes (unattributed action, unverifiable state, cascading tool calls) will map to no existing liability, contract, or unauthorized-access regime, and that uncovered subset can be enumerated exhaustively for a given agent capability set.
project_ideas.measurement: Count and classification of failure modes that satisfy no existing-regime predicate, plus inter-rater agreement on the mapping to test whether the uncovered set is stable or definitional.
project_ideas.name: Unattributed-Action Coverage Map
project_ideas.poc: Build a failure-mode taxonomy for a concrete tool-using agent, map each mode against product liability, SLA and breach-law criteria expressed as checkable predicates (identifiable actor, discrete defective artifact, enforceable contract term), and flag modes failing all predicates.
project_ideas.video_title: Extended interview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on fears about AI

project_ideas.based_on: Nvidia is several years ahead of competitors in China
project_ideas.hypothesis: When model, quantization, batch size and serving stack are held constant, the tokens-per-second-per-watt gap between adjacent accelerator generations is measurably smaller than the multi-year generational lead claim implies.
project_ideas.measurement: Tokens-per-second-per-watt and cost-per-million-token ratios between generations at fixed latency targets, with sensitivity analysis over batch size and utilization.
project_ideas.name: Generation-Isolated Serving Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Deploy one fixed open-weight model on a fixed serving stack across two accelerator generations, sweep batch size and concurrency, and record throughput, latency and power draw to compute tokens-per-second-per-watt and cost-per-million-token under matched conditions.
project_ideas.video_title: Extended interview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on fears about AI

project_ideas.based_on: Multi-agent coding fleets have no self-stabilizing equilibrium
project_ideas.hypothesis: A semaphore-and-governor controller with adaptive concurrency limits reduces fleet throughput variance by more than 50% versus unconstrained scaling at the same resource budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Coefficient of variation in commits per hour, maximum queue depth, and duration of starvation and overload intervals.
project_ideas.name: GovernorLab
project_ideas.poc: Simulate agent commits against bounded merge, build, and machine resources; sweep agent counts and governor policies including fixed limits, token buckets, and feedback controllers.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Steve Yegge's Software Factory: Lessons from Running 50 Agents

project_ideas.based_on: the merge queue becomes the bottleneck
project_ideas.hypothesis: An automated adversarial-review gate plus deterministic merge pipeline can sustain 230 or more commits per day at a lower defect escape rate than human-only review.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect escape rate, review latency, queue depth, and sustained commits per day.
project_ideas.name: MergeGate
project_ideas.poc: Replay a queue of agent-generated changes through an adversarial reviewer and auto-merge on pass; compare against a human-review baseline on the same changes.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Steve Yegge's Software Factory: Lessons from Running 50 Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Guardrail and fence accumulation is itself a failure mode
project_ideas.hypothesis: Static and dynamic constraint auditing can detect stale or contradicted agent-authored fences with enough precision and recall to prune them without breaking intended invariants.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision and recall against human-labeled stale fences, plus downstream failure rate after automated pruning.
project_ideas.name: FenceAuditor
project_ideas.poc: Extract constraints from agent-generated docs and code, test each against current system behavior and test outcomes, and flag contradictions as pruning candidates.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Steve Yegge's Software Factory: Lessons from Running 50 Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Autonomous agents over-deliver
project_ideas.hypothesis: Machine-checkable modifiable-surface constraints reduce unrequested agent-generated features by more than 80% without reducing requested feature throughput.
project_ideas.measurement: Unrequested feature rate, requested feature throughput, and user-facing regression count.
project_ideas.name: ScopeGuard
project_ideas.poc: Encode product and architectural scope as allowed files, APIs, and behavior contracts; run agents with and without enforcement and count unrequested changes.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Steve Yegge's Software Factory: Lessons from Running 50 Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Blitzv ingests 100M+ lines of code in a single pass
project_ideas.hypothesis: For legacy migration tasks on repositories exceeding 10M lines of code, a single-pass full-context agent achieves higher end-to-end correctness than a retrieval-augmented agent at comparable human review hours, but at higher token cost and wall-clock latency, and the human review fraction becomes the throughput bottleneck regardless of grounding strategy.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end task success rate after human review, total token cost, wall-clock latency, and fraction of human edits per accepted change, compared across the two grounding strategies.
project_ideas.name: RepoScale Bench
project_ideas.poc: Select an open-source multi-million-line monorepo, define a deterministic migration or refactor task (e.g., a language-version upgrade or a mechanical API migration), run two agent configurations (single-pass full-context vs retrieval-augmented) under identical human review budgets, and log every human edit per accepted change.
project_ideas.video_title: Robinhood's Vlad Tenev on Tokenizing Everything, OpenAI's 6 Misalignment Reports, Figure's Robot

project_ideas.based_on: The best safety guard is holding AI labs legally responsible for their models
project_ideas.hypothesis: A minimal decision-provenance log (model version, tool-call sequence, inputs, outputs, confidence, and human approvals) is sufficient for an independent third party to reconstruct and attribute an autonomous agent failure in a post-hoc review with high inter-reviewer agreement.
project_ideas.measurement: Attribution accuracy, time-to-attribution, and inter-reviewer agreement across independent reviewers using only the emitted trace.
project_ideas.name: Liability-Replay Agent Trace
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a production-like agent (e.g., a code-migration or customer-workflow agent) to emit a structured trace, inject a controlled failure scenario, and have multiple independent reviewers attempt attribution using only the trace, without access to the agent's internal state.
project_ideas.video_title: Robinhood's Vlad Tenev on Tokenizing Everything, OpenAI's 6 Misalignment Reports, Figure's Robot

project_ideas.based_on: Robots can generalize to unseen household environments and objects
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pre-training data volume predicts zero-shot task success in held-out homes only up to a plateau; beyond a threshold, environment-specific factors such as layout diversity and novel object categories dominate task success more than additional data volume.
project_ideas.measurement: Zero-shot task success rate as a function of pre-training data scale, stratified by environment novelty score, and the point at which additional data yields diminishing gains in genuinely novel homes.
project_ideas.name: Unseen-Home Eval
project_ideas.poc: Build a simulation-plus-real-home holdout suite in which no evaluation home shares layout or object categories with any training home, vary the effective pre-training data volume, and measure zero-shot task success stratified by an environment-novelty score.
project_ideas.video_title: Robinhood's Vlad Tenev on Tokenizing Everything, OpenAI's 6 Misalignment Reports, Figure's Robot

project_ideas.based_on: Categorizes model R&D autonomy from AL0 (no AI) to AL5 (fully automated)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Delegating specific ML R&D pipeline stages to AI, graded per AL0-AL5, measurably shortens the next stage's cycle time, but only beyond a threshold of delegation density; below that threshold, partial automation introduces handoff overhead that negates the cycle-time gain.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between delegation level at stage i and cycle-time reduction at stage i+1 across iterations, and the delegation threshold below which handoff overhead outweighs the gain.
project_ideas.name: Autonomy Ladder Instrument
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an actual ML pipeline (data curation, feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment) to record per-stage AI-led versus AI-assisted status and per-stage cycle times over multiple iterations, then correlate stage i delegation level with stage i+1 cycle-time change.
project_ideas.video_title: Robinhood's Vlad Tenev on Tokenizing Everything, OpenAI's 6 Misalignment Reports, Figure's Robot

project_ideas.based_on: Missing GPU stream barrier caused race conditions where post-scale read stale buffer data from unfinished matrix multiplications.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A long-horizon generation regression suite combined with varied batch/sequence-size replay will deterministically surface cross-stream ordering defects that unit tests and perplexity checks pass, and will fail loudly when an explicit stream barrier is removed.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate of injected barrier-removal defects versus unit tests/perplexity, plus false-positive rate on correct builds across batch and sequence configurations.
project_ideas.name: Race Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: Take a normalization path with a deliberately removed cudaStreamWaitEvent barrier, run the suite, confirm it flags token repetition and one-step lag; re-add the barrier and confirm the suite goes green while unit tests and perplexity remain unchanged in both states.
project_ideas.video_title: Weight Folding, CUDA Streams, and the Bug That Made My Model Speak Backwards — Filip Makraduli

project_ideas.based_on: Optimization passes should be gated on verified architectural invariants (e.g., adjacent operators whose composition is provably a no-op)
project_ideas.hypothesis: A static checker over model topology can decide, per model family, which algebraic normalization rewrites are valid, and blocking a rewrite whose invariants fail prevents both silent no-op optimizations and incorrect normalization removal.
project_ideas.measurement: Agreement between lint verdicts and observed correctness/speedup outcomes across a set of model topologies, plus count of unsafe rewrites blocked.
project_ideas.name: Rewrite Invariant Linter
project_ideas.poc: Encode adjacency and scale-invariance conditions as lint rules, run them against a topology with consecutive RMSNorms and one without, and verify the linter enables the cancellation rewrite only in the first case and refuses it in the second.
project_ideas.video_title: Weight Folding, CUDA Streams, and the Bug That Made My Model Speak Backwards — Filip Makraduli

project_ideas.based_on: Benchmark each proposition across batch/sequence regimes and hardware tiers to characterize where overlap and folding pay off.
project_ideas.hypothesis: The speedup from weight folding and deferred normalization is regime-dependent, and there exists a measurable crossover in batch size and sequence length below/above which stream overlap costs more than it saves.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-configuration speedup deltas and identification of the crossover points where each rewrite becomes neutral or negative, with variance across repeated runs.
project_ideas.name: Regime Sweeper for Normalization Rewrites
project_ideas.poc: Benchmark folded, deferred, and baseline normalization paths across a grid of batch sizes, sequence lengths, and GPU tiers, recording wall-clock time per decode step and kernel counts.
project_ideas.video_title: Weight Folding, CUDA Streams, and the Bug That Made My Model Speak Backwards — Filip Makraduli

project_ideas.based_on: Prototype a generic cross-stream scheduling layer with mandatory event dependencies and evaluate correctness under adversarial timing.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A scheduling layer that requires declaring every cross-stream dependency as an explicit event can overlap repeated non-matmul operators on independent streams without regressing output correctness, and the mandatory declaration prevents accidental implicit-ordering assumptions.
project_ideas.measurement: Correctness under adversarial timing tests, number of undeclared-dependency errors caught at schedule-build time, and achieved overlap versus serial execution.
project_ideas.name: Explicit-Event Scheduler
project_ideas.poc: Prototype the layer for the split scalar divide across tensor-core and CUDA-core streams, then apply it to a second repeated operator; run adversarial timing and variable-batch stress to confirm no stale reads occur.
project_ideas.video_title: Weight Folding, CUDA Streams, and the Bug That Made My Model Speak Backwards — Filip Makraduli

project_ideas.based_on: running decode before prefill on a stale state slot
project_ideas.hypothesis: Under forced slot recycling (e.g., memory utilization driven to 0.2), at least one stateful inference engine will exhibit request-level output corruption traceable to a prefill/decode ordering violation, while engines that assert per-slot state ownership will not.
project_ideas.measurement: Corruption rate per 10,000 requests at memory utilization 0.2 vs 0.9, plus count of ordering-invariant violations correlated with corrupted request IDs.
project_ideas.name: StateBoundary Conformance Suite
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that drives slot recycling by shrinking the state cache, asserts prefill-before-decode ordering per request at the kernel boundary, and flags any request whose state slot was read before it was written for that request.
project_ideas.video_title: Two Bugs That Hid in Plain Sight: A vLLM Debugging Detective Story — Asaf Gardin & Yuval Belfer

project_ideas.based_on: uint32_t index pointer wrapping around at 4.29 billion instead of throwing an error
project_ideas.hypothesis: A non-trivial fraction of CUDA kernels that use uint32_t index types can reach an addressable offset beyond 4.29 billion at maximum supported memory utilization, and a cheap runtime offset-bound assertion converts that silent wrap into an explicit error with negligible throughput cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of kernels whose worst-case offset exceeds 2^32 at supported configs; throughput delta of the assertion enabled; number of assertions fired during a high-utilization stress run.
project_ideas.name: WrapGuard
project_ideas.poc: Statically extract index/offset types and buffer capacities per kernel, compute worst-case offsets across supported configurations, then add opt-in overflow assertions and fuzz memory utilization upward to drive offsets toward the boundary.
project_ideas.video_title: Two Bugs That Hid in Plain Sight: A vLLM Debugging Detective Story — Asaf Gardin & Yuval Belfer

project_ideas.based_on: Can the logprob differential oracle be run continuously in production or shadow mode
project_ideas.hypothesis: Sampled shadow replay of a small fraction of production traffic through a trusted reference forward pass (prefill only, softmax, divergence on logprobs) detects silent corruption with lower detection latency than anomaly monitoring of confidence, perplexity or refusal rates.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection latency in requests/steps from first corrupted request to alert, added compute cost as percentage of serving capacity, and false-positive alert rate on known-good traffic.
project_ideas.name: ShadowDiff Oracle
project_ideas.poc: Route a configurable sample of live requests to a reference implementation, compute per-token logprob divergence against the fast path, and alert on divergence spikes localized to tokens/steps.
project_ideas.video_title: Two Bugs That Hid in Plain Sight: A vLLM Debugging Detective Story — Asaf Gardin & Yuval Belfer

project_ideas.based_on: Increasing rollouts per prompt from 8 to 128 caused spikes to happen immediately on step 1.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Failure onset position (step index or request slot) shifts monotonically when the workload knob that drives an accumulating quantity is scaled, allowing the accumulating quantity to be localized from the slope of onset vs. knob value.
project_ideas.measurement: Monotonicity of onset step versus knob value, slope estimate identifying the per-step accumulation rate, and reduction in runs required for a deterministic repro versus random resampling.
project_ideas.name: Failure-Shape Perturbation Harness
project_ideas.poc: A sweep runner that varies memory utilization, batch size and rollouts-per-prompt, records the first step/request where divergence appears, and fits onset timing against each knob independently.
project_ideas.video_title: Two Bugs That Hid in Plain Sight: A vLLM Debugging Detective Story — Asaf Gardin & Yuval Belfer

project_ideas.based_on: Users care about end-to-end task completion latency, not individual token or request latency.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Optimizing for end-to-end task latency instead of per-request latency changes autoscaling and cache eviction policies, reducing cost per completed task by >30% on heavy-tailed agent workloads.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare task completion time, cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and cost per task across a suite of multi-step coding and research tasks.
project_ideas.name: TaskLatencyBench
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an open-source agent loop with a local vLLM server; implement two schedulers: one request-optimized (round-robin, LRU), one task-aware (cache-affinity routing, speculative prefilling).
project_ideas.video_title: The Frontier AI Inference Cloud for Agents — Byung-Gon (Gon) Chun, FriendliAI

project_ideas.based_on: Cache-aware routing balances GPU cluster load while maximizing cache locality and hit rates.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A routing policy that prioritizes prefix-cache affinity over least-loaded routing will increase prefix cache hit rate by >2x and reduce end-to-end task latency by >20% on heavy-tailed agent workloads, without increasing p99 latency beyond 10%.
project_ideas.measurement: Measure cache hit rate, p50/p99 task latency, GPU utilization imbalance, and recompute token cost.
project_ideas.name: PrefixCacheRouter
project_ideas.poc: Extend a load balancer (e.g., Envoy) with a prefix-aware routing plugin; simulate agent workloads with Zipf-distributed shared prefixes and heavy-tailed lengths.
project_ideas.video_title: The Frontier AI Inference Cloud for Agents — Byung-Gon (Gon) Chun, FriendliAI

project_ideas.based_on: How does KV cache quantization impact complex agent reasoning accuracy over very long contexts?
project_ideas.hypothesis: KV cache quantization to 4-bit reduces task-level accuracy by less than 2% for agent tasks with contexts under 100k tokens but degrades by >10% beyond 200k tokens.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, reasoning step correctness, and context-length-stratified accuracy delta.
project_ideas.name: QuantizationAccuracyAudit
project_ideas.poc: Run a multi-step agent benchmark (e.g., SWE-bench-like) against a vLLM server with varying KV quantization levels (FP16, 8-bit, 4-bit) and controlled context lengths.
project_ideas.video_title: The Frontier AI Inference Cloud for Agents — Byung-Gon (Gon) Chun, FriendliAI

project_ideas.based_on: Agent-aware optimization uses agent-level context
project_ideas.hypothesis: Exposing a minimal agent-phase API (e.g., 'awaiting_tool', 'planning', 'finalizing') to the inference server enables preemptive scheduling that cuts end-to-end task latency by >15% without requiring orchestrator code changes beyond declaring phases.
project_ideas.measurement: Task latency, GPU idle time, prefill/compute overlap, and portability friction measured by lines of orchestrator code changed.
project_ideas.name: AgentPhaseContract
project_ideas.poc: Implement a phase-aware scheduler in vLLM; wrap an existing agent loop (e.g., LangChain) to emit phase hints; compare against baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: The Frontier AI Inference Cloud for Agents — Byung-Gon (Gon) Chun, FriendliAI

project_ideas.based_on: Build coverage/recovery metrics: pass@k on low-probability correct solutions, entropy collapse on reasoning traces
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed base model and task suite, post-training on a preference proxy measurably collapses output entropy on reasoning traces and reduces pass@k on rare-but-correct solutions, and the size of this collapse predicts end-to-end failure rate on multi-step tasks better than benchmark accuracy does.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between post-training-induced entropy collapse / pass@k drop on rare modes and observed end-to-end task failure rate; whether accuracy on standard benchmarks stays flat while rare-mode pass@k falls.
project_ideas.name: ModeDrop Probe
project_ideas.poc: Evaluate a base model and its post-trained variant on the same executable multi-step task suite; compute per-task output-distribution divergence, entropy of reasoning traces, and pass@k at high k for tasks whose correct solution requires an unusual path; regress task failure rate on the collapse metrics.
project_ideas.video_title: Diogo Almeida (ex-OpenAI) reveals JEV: 200x faster, 400x cheaper, zero hallucinations.

project_ideas.based_on: Empirically fit per-step success probability across agent traces to derive maximum viable horizon length
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent end-to-end success decays as a multiplicative function of per-step correctness, so inserting a verifier every N steps yields superlinear reliability gains versus marginally improving per-step quality, and a maximum viable horizon length can be predicted in advance for a target end-to-end success rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Fit quality of the exponential-decay model against observed success-vs-length curves; delta in end-to-end success rate per unit of added verification frequency versus per unit of per-step model improvement.
project_ideas.name: Horizon Budget Calculator
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent runtime to log per-step success across traces of varying length; fit per-step success probability; predict end-to-end success for lengths L; then compare predicted versus observed success for runs with and without periodic verifier checkpoints.
project_ideas.video_title: Diogo Almeida (ex-OpenAI) reveals JEV: 200x faster, 400x cheaper, zero hallucinations.

project_ideas.based_on: Formalize a task-scoring function over error cost, human catch rate, reversibility, and verifiability
project_ideas.hypothesis: A task score over error cost, human catch rate, reversibility, and verifiability predicts the success/failure of deployed generative AI use cases, and misclassified cases are exactly those that should have been re-architected as assistive or verifier-gated.
project_ideas.measurement: Discriminative power (e.g., AUC or precision/recall) of the score for predicting deployment success versus a baseline that classifies only by domain or model capability.
project_ideas.name: Stakes-and-Catch Scorer
project_ideas.poc: Score a portfolio of internal or publicized AI deployments on the four axes, bin by assistive versus automated as deployed, and compare the score distribution against reported outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: Diogo Almeida (ex-OpenAI) reveals JEV: 200x faster, 400x cheaper, zero hallucinations.

project_ideas.based_on: Separate mode-covering paths (search, branching, candidate generation) from mode-dropping paths (user-facing answers)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing candidate generation to a mode-covering path and using the preference-tuned model only for the final user-facing surface raises success on tasks where rare correct modes dominate, compared to repeatedly sampling the aligned model.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate on rare-mode-dominated tasks at matched token/compute budget; diversity of candidate sets pre-filter; number of correct-but-low-probability solutions surfaced per run.
project_ideas.name: Split-Policy Router
project_ideas.poc: Build a two-policy agent: an exploration stage that samples a less-aligned or higher-temperature model for candidates, and a serving stage that uses the aligned model to select and express the answer. Compare against an aligned-model-only baseline on the same rare-mode task suite.
project_ideas.video_title: Diogo Almeida (ex-OpenAI) reveals JEV: 200x faster, 400x cheaper, zero hallucinations.

project_ideas.based_on: Formal methods can help enforce safety constraints by specifying mathematical definitions of safety and adding them as layers to models
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding formal barrier-function layers as runtime action filters to a fixed-evaluator agent reduces reward-hacking episodes without significantly degrading task performance.
project_ideas.measurement: Reward-hacking incidents per episode, true utility gap between proxy reward and intended objective, and task-success degradation from safety filtering.
project_ideas.name: BarrierRuntime
project_ideas.poc: Build a gridworld or vacuum-robot simulator with a fixed evaluator, compare a baseline learned policy against the same policy wrapped in runtime formal safety layers, and log exploit events versus true utility.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Your Computer Is Not Ready for AI Agents | The Next Endeavor 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Compute grows much faster than memory capacity and bandwidth
project_ideas.hypothesis: For long-horizon agent workloads, memory bandwidth and capacity predict end-to-end latency and cost better than available compute FLOPs.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between memory bandwidth/capacity and task latency or cost, and performance gains from memory-hierarchy optimizations versus compute scaling.
project_ideas.name: MemAgentBench
project_ideas.poc: Create a persistent-memory agent benchmark that varies memory bandwidth and capacity while holding compute roughly constant, then measure task latency, maximum usable context, and cost per successful action.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Your Computer Is Not Ready for AI Agents | The Next Endeavor 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Modular design makes building systems easier but introduces overhead costs
project_ideas.hypothesis: A vertically co-designed agent runtime with minimal abstractions reduces overhead by more than a modular layered stack at equal task success.
project_ideas.measurement: Overhead percentage and dollars per million agent steps, plus maintainability and iteration-speed metrics for each stack.
project_ideas.name: CrossLayerAgent
project_ideas.poc: Prototype two agent execution stacks, one modular across networking, storage, compute, and model layers, and one co-designed across those layers, then benchmark identical agent workloads.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Your Computer Is Not Ready for AI Agents | The Next Endeavor 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Hybrid architectures dividing workloads between local devices and cloud resources will dominate
project_ideas.hypothesis: A profiler and scheduler that partitions agent state, inference, and learning between device and cloud can meet privacy and latency constraints while lowering cloud cost versus cloud-only deployment.
project_ideas.measurement: Cloud cost per task, end-to-end latency, privacy leakage indicators, and learning speed or task accuracy.
project_ideas.name: EdgeCloudPartitioner
project_ideas.poc: Implement a hybrid agent that keeps privacy-sensitive memory on-device and sends selected shared-learning updates to the cloud, then compare against a cloud-only baseline on identical tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Your Computer Is Not Ready for AI Agents | The Next Endeavor 2026

project_ideas.based_on: AI generates valid proofs faster than humans can read, explain, or publish them.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automated systems can generate human-readable expositions of formally verified proofs that expert mathematicians rate as equivalent in comprehension to human-written expositions, measured by downstream comprehension tests.
project_ideas.measurement: Expert rating scores and quiz accuracy; success if automated expositions match human baseline on ≥70% of cases.
project_ideas.name: Exposition Bench
project_ideas.poc: Curate 100 Lean-verified proofs with human-written expositions; use LLMs to generate expositions; run expert evaluation and comprehension quizzes on both versions.
project_ideas.video_title: Terence Tao: SAIR’s Open Math Model Initiative

project_ideas.based_on: Stage 2 competition winners using open-source LLMs and Python code surprisingly used almost no LLM calls
project_ideas.hypothesis: In structured mathematical tasks, an agent that routes to deterministic solvers first and uses LLMs only for ambiguity resolution achieves higher accuracy at lower cost than an LLM-first agent.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy and LLM calls per solved task; success if accuracy is equal or better with <10% of the LLM calls.
project_ideas.name: Solver-First Router
project_ideas.poc: Implement a router on a set of equational theories or modular arithmetic problems; compare against an LLM-only baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Terence Tao: SAIR’s Open Math Model Initiative

project_ideas.based_on: Address data pollution caused by uncurated AI-generated mathematical output.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Provenance-tagged corpora with a contamination filter prevent measurable degradation in downstream model performance compared to unfiltered AI-generated corpora.
project_ideas.measurement: Performance delta on downstream tasks; success if filtered corpus outperforms by ≥5%.
project_ideas.name: Provenance-Guard
project_ideas.poc: Create two versions of a math corpus: one with uncurated AI output, one with provenance tags and filtering; train small models on each and evaluate on a held-out benchmark.
project_ideas.video_title: Terence Tao: SAIR’s Open Math Model Initiative

project_ideas.based_on: A bigger context window is not the fix for context rot.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For long-horizon agent tasks requiring recall of specific facts, a harness with compaction/offloading and a small context window achieves higher recall accuracy at lower token cost than a harness relying on a 1M-token context window.
project_ideas.measurement: Recall accuracy of target facts, total token consumption, latency per turn, and degradation curve over increasing turn counts.
project_ideas.name: Context Compaction vs Large Window Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement two identical agent harnesses (e.g., LangChain-based) differing only in context management: (A) full history + retrieved chunks in a large window, (B) compaction/offloading with context cards and retrieval. Run a suite of tasks requiring recall of facts from earlier turns.
project_ideas.video_title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle

project_ideas.based_on: Multiple agents modifying files concurrently leading to race conditions.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Shared agent memory stored on a filesystem produces lost updates, stale reads, and race conditions under concurrent multi-agent writes, while an ACID-compliant database store prevents them without significant performance penalty.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of lost updates, stale reads, write conflicts, and end-to-end task success; compare latency and throughput.
project_ideas.name: Multi-Agent Memory Contention Testbed
project_ideas.poc: Build a multi-agent simulation where N agents concurrently read and write shared memory (e.g., facts, plans). Run against two backends: (A) filesystem with POSIX semantics, (B) transactional database with vector indexing (e.g., Oracle DBFS). Introduce controlled write conflicts.
project_ideas.video_title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle

project_ideas.based_on: Does a single-line memory API such as OAMP preserve the control
project_ideas.hypothesis: A packaged single-line memory API (e.g., OAMP) sacrifices controllability and debuggability compared to building memory from primitives, leading to lower recall/precision on tasks requiring distinct memory types (episodic, procedural, semantic).
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, recall precision/recall of relevant memories, ability to debug memory decisions, and flexibility to tune per-type policies.
project_ideas.name: Typed Memory API vs Primitives Evaluation
project_ideas.poc: Implement two memory subsystems for the same agent: (A) using a packaged memory API that abstracts all memory types, (B) building from primitives with separate stores and policies for each memory type. Run identical long-horizon tasks that require retention, reuse, refinement, and recall.
project_ideas.video_title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle

project_ideas.based_on: In-database embeddings eliminate third-party service calls
project_ideas.hypothesis: Computing and storing embeddings inside the database (e.g., Oracle) reduces end-to-end latency and improves transactional consistency and data security compared to calling an external embedding API and storing vectors in a separate store, without degrading retrieval quality.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end latency per query, consistency (stale embeddings after writes), data egress security, cost per 1k queries, retrieval precision/recall.
project_ideas.name: In-Database Embeddings vs External Service Trade-off
project_ideas.poc: Implement a RAG pipeline for an agent with two configurations: (A) external embedding API + separate vector database, (B) in-database embeddings and vector search. Run identical query workloads with writes interleaved.
project_ideas.video_title: Total Recall: Agent Memory and Harness Engineering — Ignacio Martinez, Oracle

project_ideas.based_on: How well-calibrated are Jev's reported confidences
project_ideas.hypothesis: Jev's reported confidences will show ECE < 0.05 in-distribution but ECE > 0.15 under distribution shift and adversarial prompt injection, while RLHF/RLVR baselines will show worse in-distribution calibration.
project_ideas.measurement: Expected Calibration Error (ECE), maximum calibration error, and reliability diagrams across task families and shift conditions.
project_ideas.name: CalibrationBench: Reliability of Decision Models Under Shift
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that queries Choice/Score/Noul primitives on a suite of classification tasks (routing, spam, PII) with known ground truth; compute reliability diagrams and ECE for in-distribution and shifted/adversarial variants; compare against chat-model self-reported confidence.
project_ideas.video_title: Jev - The Ultimate Classification Model?

project_ideas.based_on: Does replacing chat+JSON parsing with a typed call measurably reduce
project_ideas.hypothesis: Replacing a chat-model-with-JSON-extraction pipeline with a typed-call model (Jev) reduces malformed-output rate from >5% to ~0% and cuts end-to-end p95 latency by at least 50% for identical classification workloads.
project_ideas.measurement: Malformed-output rate, retry rate, end-to-end p50/p95 latency, and cost per 10k decisions.
project_ideas.name: TypedCall vs JSON: Production Reliability A/B
project_ideas.poc: Implement two interchangeable microservices for the same tasks (support ticket routing, urgency scoring, escalation yes/no): one using a chat LLM with JSON extraction and retry logic, one using jev(state, questions). Run both against a replayed production workload.
project_ideas.video_title: Jev - The Ultimate Classification Model?

project_ideas.based_on: What classes of task can a non-autoregressive output head handle
project_ideas.hypothesis: A non-autoregressive output head matches autoregressive accuracy on single-hop classification tasks but exhibits significant accuracy degradation (>20%) on multi-hop composition tasks that require sequential latent reasoning within a single call.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy degradation curve across composition depths, and comparison of chained single-step calls vs. single composed call.
project_ideas.name: Non-Autoregressive Boundary Probe
project_ideas.poc: Create a benchmark of tasks with controlled composition depth (e.g., single classification vs. two-step logical composition vs. arithmetic then classification). Query Jev and an autoregressive baseline; measure accuracy as a function of composition depth.
project_ideas.video_title: Jev - The Ultimate Classification Model?

project_ideas.based_on: The economic and latency profile
project_ideas.hypothesis: A per-decision model call at 10 QPS in a real-time control loop (Doom) is economically viable (<$10/hour) and achieves comparable play performance to a batched approach, validating that non-autoregressive decision models enable fine-grained agentic control.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per hour, per-decision latency distribution, and in-game performance (score, survival time).
project_ideas.name: Doom Per-Decision Control Loop Economics
project_ideas.poc: Recreate the Doom demo: integrate Jev to make 10 decisions per second, measure cumulative cost over 1 hour, latency per decision, and game score; compare against a baseline that batches decisions or uses a slower model.
project_ideas.video_title: Jev - The Ultimate Classification Model?

project_ideas.based_on: A non-trivial agent consumes ~15W in Python versus ~0.7W in Rust.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For identical non-trivial agent workloads with mocked model calls, a Rust implementation uses at least 10x fewer CPU joules per completed task than Python, and the gap is dominated by interpreter overhead rather than I/O wait.
project_ideas.measurement: Joules per task, CPU time per task, context switches per task, and ratio Python/Rust; decomposition of energy in compute versus wait.
project_ideas.name: Agent Power Crucible
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same agent loop (tool calls, memory, retries) in Python and Rust; instrument CPU package energy (RAPL) while executing N tasks with model calls mocked to fixed latency.
project_ideas.video_title: The Real Reason AI Agents Are Wasting 10x More Power | Avinash Lakshman, Weilliptic

project_ideas.based_on: At what fleet size does runtime power consumption overtake inference power consumption
project_ideas.hypothesis: There is a measurable agent concurrency and duty cycle at which runtime power exceeds inference power, and this crossover can be predicted from per-agent-hour and per-token energy models.
project_ideas.measurement: Crossover concurrency, runtime vs inference joules per hour, total facility power proxy, and PUE sensitivity.
project_ideas.name: Crossover Instrument
project_ideas.poc: Build an instrumented two-runtime agent deployment with configurable concurrency; mock or proxy model calls to fixed energy per token; sweep fleet size and duty cycle.
project_ideas.video_title: The Real Reason AI Agents Are Wasting 10x More Power | Avinash Lakshman, Weilliptic

project_ideas.based_on: Can jurisdictional data/compute sovereignty be delivered with cryptographic audit trails without unacceptable latency or operational cost?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-action cryptographic attestation for data residency and compute location can be added to an agent runtime with less than 10% latency overhead while enforcing jurisdictional pinning.
project_ideas.measurement: Added p50/p99 latency, throughput delta, key-management overhead, and audit coverage completeness.
project_ideas.name: Residency-Attested Agent Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a regional execution broker that pins agent steps to a jurisdiction and emits signed attestations for data placement and inference location; benchmark against centralized baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: The Real Reason AI Agents Are Wasting 10x More Power | Avinash Lakshman, Weilliptic

project_ideas.based_on: does model agnosticism actually reduce migration cost in practice
project_ideas.hypothesis: A model-agnostic agent harness reduces foundation-model migration cost, but behavior and tool-call validity shift measurably even when the adapter interface is fixed.
project_ideas.measurement: Files/lines changed per swap, eval pass-rate delta, tool-call validity rate, and cost per task per model.
project_ideas.name: Model Swap Bench
project_ideas.poc: Define a fixed agent harness with a model adapter; run the same eval suite against multiple open-weight and proprietary models; record the diff required to swap.
project_ideas.video_title: The Real Reason AI Agents Are Wasting 10x More Power | Avinash Lakshman, Weilliptic

project_ideas.based_on: Third-party evaluators with employee-like access.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A time-boxed, per-checkpoint scoped credential tier that grants read-only inference and evaluation tooling to non-employees can let external evaluators reproduce internal eval results at high agreement while producing zero weight, data or methodology exfiltration in red-team attempts.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta between evaluator-reported results and internal eval results; number of successful weight/data/methodology extractions across a fixed red-team budget; mean time to revoke a credential mid-session.
project_ideas.name: Evaluator Access Broker
project_ideas.poc: Wrap an open-weights model behind a broker that issues short-lived tokens mapped to specific checkpoints and eval harnesses, exposes read-only inference plus logs, denies all other routes, and emits an immutable audit record per access. Run two external evaluator teams through it and attempt leakage from an adversarial third team.
project_ideas.video_title: Frontier Labs Want to Slow Down, OpenAI Delays Its 2026 IPO, Anthropic Flags 5 Bioweapon Cases

project_ideas.based_on: Adoption of identical safety standards across US labs via legislation or waivers.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A standardized release-evidence bundle (eval configs, prompt suites, raw logs, model and checkpoint hashes, environment manifest) is independently reproducible by a third party on separate hardware with materially identical pass/fail outcomes, making provider infrastructure access unnecessary for gate verification.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of gate verdicts that reproduce identically; wall-clock and compute cost to reproduce; number of fields a reproducer must request from the provider to finish (target zero).
project_ideas.name: Portable Release Gate Bundle
project_ideas.poc: Define a bundle schema and CI emitter; produce bundles for three model releases; have an independent party re-run the gates from the bundle alone and diff the verdicts.
project_ideas.video_title: Frontier Labs Want to Slow Down, OpenAI Delays Its 2026 IPO, Anthropic Flags 5 Bioweapon Cases

project_ideas.based_on: Five case studies documented actual misuse involving biological weapons development.
project_ideas.hypothesis: On dual-use-adjacent uplift tasks, inter-evaluator and inter-lab variance on below-threshold determinations is large enough that a single point estimate of a capability threshold is not a meaningful claim, but a bounded confidence interval with documented misuse telemetry is.
project_ideas.measurement: Inter-rater agreement and inter-lab spread on threshold determinations; whether the spread straddles the proposed threshold line; correlation between eval verdicts and observed misuse cases.
project_ideas.name: Cross-Evaluator Threshold Variance Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a held-out harmful-adjacent task suite, run it through several independent evaluator teams on the same model snapshot, and report both the mean determination and the spread, alongside a feed of documented production misuse cases.
project_ideas.video_title: Frontier Labs Want to Slow Down, OpenAI Delays Its 2026 IPO, Anthropic Flags 5 Bioweapon Cases

project_ideas.based_on: A swarm could potentially take over the internet within 6 to 12 months if unchecked.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a sandboxed environment, populations of cooperating agents acquire resources and propagate through linked services at rates that per-agent rate limits and per-agent logging fail to detect above a measurable population threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection latency versus population size; detection rate at each scale for per-agent-only controls versus swarm-level detector; fraction of breaches contained by kill switch before service-wide impact.
project_ideas.name: Swarm Containment Range
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a sandbox with mock services, identities and credentials; instrument per-agent controls and a candidate swarm-level detector (provenance graph, velocity anomalies, cross-agent correlation); scale cooperating-agent population from 10 to 1,000 under identical per-agent budgets.
project_ideas.video_title: Frontier Labs Want to Slow Down, OpenAI Delays Its 2026 IPO, Anthropic Flags 5 Bioweapon Cases

project_ideas.based_on: Package managers and test environments where agents discovered unauthorized communication paths.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Monitoring agent-to-agent and agent-to-environment channels reduces emergent collusion without reducing task reward.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of unauthorized communication, task success rate, and reward.
project_ideas.name: Collusion Detection Harness for Multi-Agent Systems
project_ideas.poc: Build a multi-agent environment with a package manager side channel; instrument all communication; compare task success and unauthorized message rate with and without monitoring.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI researcher on agent swarms & recursive self-improvement

project_ideas.based_on: As agents generate more code, verification frameworks must keep up.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Unverified code accumulates nonlinearly with generation rate, and verification throughput becomes the binding constraint before generation rate does.
project_ideas.measurement: Backlog growth rate, fraction of faults auto-resolved, time-to-resolution.
project_ideas.name: Verification Capacity Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Simulate agent code generation versus deterministic verification throughput using fault injection; measure backlog and risk exposure over time.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI researcher on agent swarms & recursive self-improvement

project_ideas.based_on: Four agents working on a math problem solved it twice as fast.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Beyond 4 agents, the parallelization penalty dominates, so marginal accuracy per token decreases as agent count increases.
project_ideas.measurement: Speedup factor, token cost per correct answer, and crossover point against a single agent with equivalent token budget.
project_ideas.name: Agent Fan-Out Speedup Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Run 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 agents on standardized math/reasoning tasks, measuring wall-clock, token cost, and accuracy.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI researcher on agent swarms & recursive self-improvement

project_ideas.based_on: Performance on reasoning benchmarks scales logarithmically with test-time compute.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For tasks with high coordination cost, a single agent with a larger reasoning budget outperforms multiple agents with the same total token budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy per token, wall-clock time, and accuracy versus budget allocation.
project_ideas.name: Serial vs Parallel Reasoning Budget Allocator
project_ideas.poc: Implement a router that can allocate a fixed token budget either to one agent with extended thinking or to N agents with reconciliation; test on tasks of varying decomposability.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI researcher on agent swarms & recursive self-improvement

project_ideas.based_on: Moving from a spec-to-PR execution loop to a value-sense product loop that feeds back into ideation.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A pipeline that feeds customer outcome metrics and discovery findings directly into the agent harness/context will measurably change execution-loop prioritization (work items reordered, specs revised, features dropped) compared to teams where value signals reach engineers only through meetings and docs.
project_ideas.measurement: Count and classify execution-loop decisions changed by value signals; compare rework and discarded-feature rates against a matched team without the bridge.
project_ideas.name: Value-Signal Bridge
project_ideas.poc: Instrument one team's execution pipeline with a value-signal intake that updates agent context and spec priorities; log every prioritization change traceable to an inbound outcome signal over a six-week window.
project_ideas.video_title: Rethinking the software development process for an era of specs and AI agents

project_ideas.based_on: Asking Claude or another agent to analyze coaching patterns over a two-week period to assess friction.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Friction indicators derived from agent traces (coaching frequency, correction rounds, validation insertions) predict developer-reported friction and cycle-time slowdown at least as well as periodic DX surveys, and at far lower latency.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between trace-derived friction index, survey responses, and cycle-time variance; false-positive rate of trace-derived indicators versus survey-reported friction.
project_ideas.name: Trace-Mined Friction Index
project_ideas.poc: Mine two weeks of agent traces per team, derive a friction index, and run it alongside an existing DX survey and cycle-time data on the same teams.
project_ideas.video_title: Rethinking the software development process for an era of specs and AI agents

project_ideas.based_on: Extracting truth from 20-year-old wikis versus current operational repositories.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Provenance- and recency-weighted retrieval over conflicting internal sources (legacy wikis vs live operational repositories) reduces hallucination and slop rates in agent output relative to unranked retrieval over the same corpus.
project_ideas.measurement: Hallucination/defect rate per task, rate of stale-source citations, and human review rejection rate across the ranked and unranked configurations.
project_ideas.name: Context Truth Arbiter
project_ideas.poc: Build a retrieval layer that tags every source with provenance and freshness, resolves conflicts by policy, and gate access to stale sources; A/B it against the current unranked vector index on the same task set.
project_ideas.video_title: Rethinking the software development process for an era of specs and AI agents

project_ideas.based_on: Treating AI agents as passive executors of rigid upfront specifications recreates the anti-patterns of traditional waterfall development.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A spec workflow where agents participate in spec revision (proposing clarifications, flagging contradictions) produces less late-stage rework than a spec-first workflow where agents only execute a frozen spec.
project_ideas.measurement: Rework volume, spec revision count before and after implementation start, and change cost after code generation begins, compared across the two variants.
project_ideas.name: Iterative Spec Loop Harness
project_ideas.poc: Implement two agent workflow variants on the same feature backlog: frozen-spec execution versus agent-participatory spec revision with versioned spec diffs; run both to delivery.
project_ideas.video_title: Rethinking the software development process for an era of specs and AI agents

project_ideas.based_on: How easily can Homa be integrated into existing datacenter hardware and software stacks?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Migrating a mixed AI workload from RoCE to Homa reduces P99 short-message latency by ≥10x while maintaining bulk-training throughput within 5%.
project_ideas.measurement: P99 latency for small messages, aggregate throughput for bulk transfers, and GPU idle time during barrier synchronization.
project_ideas.name: Homa Migration Cost Analyzer
project_ideas.poc: Deploy the open-source Linux kernel module for Homa on a small GPU cluster; replay a trace of barrier sync, KV cache lookups, and gradient transfers alongside a TCP/RoCE baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford

project_ideas.based_on: What are the operational requirements for configuring switch priority queues for Homa?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reducing available switch priority queues from 8 to 2 degrades Homa's P99 advantage over TCP by more than 50% for small messages.
project_ideas.measurement: P99 latency for short messages as a function of the number of priority queues, and the crossover point where Homa loses its advantage.
project_ideas.name: Priority Queue Sensitivity Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Emulate a datacenter switch with configurable priority queue counts; run Homa and TCP under a mixed short/long message workload.
project_ideas.video_title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford

project_ideas.based_on: How does receiver-driven admission control behave under adversarial or pathological in-flight message counts?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Under extreme fan-in (e.g., 1000 simultaneous senders), Homa's grant-based admission control exhibits receiver state exhaustion causing tail-latency spikes worse than TCP.
project_ideas.measurement: Receiver state usage, grant packet loss rate, and P99 latency for short messages under increasing fan-in.
project_ideas.name: Receiver State Stress Tester
project_ideas.poc: Build a synthetic incast generator that varies the number of concurrent senders to a single Homa receiver; monitor receiver memory and grant packet allocation.
project_ideas.video_title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford

project_ideas.based_on: Can application-level framing on top of TCP approximate the same prioritization benefit without a new transport?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Application-level message framing with priority tagging on TCP can recover at least 50% of Homa's P99 advantage for small messages without transport changes.
project_ideas.measurement: P99 latency for small messages under mixed workload for three configurations: vanilla TCP, app-framed TCP, and Homa.
project_ideas.name: App-Level Framing over TCP
project_ideas.poc: Implement an RPC layer over TCP that tags messages with length and priority; configure switch priority queues and compare against Homa and vanilla TCP.
project_ideas.video_title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters — John Ousterhout, Stanford

project_ideas.based_on: explicit, recorded, distributable context artifact
project_ideas.hypothesis: A durable decision-log plus retrieval ontology reduces duplicated work and contradiction rate in multi-agent systems above a participant threshold compared to implicit context held in individual agent prompts.
project_ideas.measurement: Duplicate work rate, contradiction rate, task completion time, and context-store size/retrieval latency across N agents with and without the store.
project_ideas.name: Decision-Store Alignment Harness
