project_ideas.poc: Implement a simple metalearning agent that updates its own hyperparameters or architecture on a stream of tasks; track performance on a held-out set of previous tasks; compare with and without a human-in-the-loop objective specification.
project_ideas.video_title: AI researchers debate how close we are to recursive self-improvement

project_ideas.based_on: Pretraining progress is 12.0x from data and 3.7x from models.
project_ideas.hypothesis: The data-driven compute multiplier exceeds the model-driven multiplier at all measured scales up to 10B parameters, but the gap narrows as scale increases.
project_ideas.measurement: Compute multiplier ratios (data/model) at each scale.
project_ideas.name: Data vs Model Compute Multiplier Decomposition Across Scales
project_ideas.poc: Replicate pretraining runs with controlled data recipe changes vs architectural changes at multiple scales (e.g., 100M, 1B, 10B), measuring compute efficiency gains.
project_ideas.video_title: AI researchers debate how close we are to recursive self-improvement

project_ideas.based_on: Combining multi-armed bandit reward scoring with influence functions efficiently identifies valuable training data.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Across at least three tabular datasets and two model families, bandit-plus-influence top-K selection reaches a target fairness improvement with strictly fewer valuation calls and no larger accuracy drop than random, uniform-representation, or volume-based expansion at matched compute.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of influence/valuation calls and wall-clock to target fairness; Pareto frontier of (fairness metric, accuracy); post-selection accuracy and fairness on a held-out distribution shift.
project_ideas.name: Selector Gate Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a candidate pool expander with group-level bandit reward (joint fairness-accuracy) wrapping within-group influence ranking for top-K; run it head-to-head against random addition, uniform-representation addition, and add-all baselines at matched augmentation budget.
project_ideas.video_title: 2026-09-09 CERIAS - Reasoning About Interventions in Data and Machine Learning Systems

project_ideas.based_on: Repair candidates can be ranked using historical execution logs and data profiles without re-executing the full pipeline
project_ideas.hypothesis: Cheap proxy ranking from historical runs and data profiles places the true best repair in the top-3 far above chance and cuts full pipeline executions by more than 80% versus exhaustive search, but its hit rate collapses when the current shift type is absent from the logs.
project_ideas.measurement: Top-K hit rate of the best repair, number of full executions saved, F1 recovery versus exhaustive search, and hit-rate degradation on held-out shift types not present in logs.
project_ideas.name: PipeLens-mini Repair Ranker
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a small pipeline graph (ingest, entity resolution, classifier), inject faults including an unstated-language assumption break, log data profiles and historical runs, rank candidate structural and parametric repairs with an optimistic estimator, then verify only top-K candidates by execution.
project_ideas.video_title: 2026-09-09 CERIAS - Reasoning About Interventions in Data and Machine Learning Systems

project_ideas.based_on: What are the privacy implications of computing influence functions over training data?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Influence scores exposed by a data-valuation service leak membership and attribute information above a chance baseline, and score aggregation plus calibrated noise reduces that leakage at a bounded cost to selection quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Membership-inference AUC and attribute-inference accuracy against the exposed scores; change in fairness-accuracy outcome of top-K selection under each mitigation.
project_ideas.name: Influence-Leak Audit
project_ideas.poc: Compute influence scores for a trained model, expose the top-K ranked points and their scores through a mock valuation service, train a membership-inference attacker against the exposure, then compare against aggregation and DP-noised score variants.
project_ideas.video_title: 2026-09-09 CERIAS - Reasoning About Interventions in Data and Machine Learning Systems

project_ideas.based_on: the repair space must be heterogeneous — adding/shifting stages as well as tuning parameters
project_ideas.hypothesis: Parameter-only intervention search fails to recover utility on assumption-violation faults while mixed structural search recovers it, and a classifier over intermediate data profiles can separate assumption-violation from parameter-drift faults before repair search starts.
project_ideas.measurement: Utility recovery per fault class, number of interventions applied per repair, re-failure rate under repeated shifts, and classifier accuracy in routing faults to the correct search space.
project_ideas.name: Assumption-Debt Fault Library
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a fault library over one real pipeline (schema drift, unit change, language/locale assumption, upstream distribution shift), run three search spaces (parametric-only, structural-only, mixed), and train a profile-based fault classifier used to route the repair search.
project_ideas.video_title: 2026-09-09 CERIAS - Reasoning About Interventions in Data and Machine Learning Systems

project_ideas.based_on: rerouted through Claude
project_ideas.hypothesis: Signed routing manifests combined with per-request fingerprintable canary payloads can detect which provider actually processed a request across a multi-hop model chain, reducing undetected silent re-routing to a measurable low rate that client-side configuration alone cannot achieve.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection false-negative rate for simulated re-routing, observed fraction of requests traversing undeclared providers, and per-request latency and token overhead introduced by canary and manifest handling.
project_ideas.name: RouteProof
project_ideas.poc: Build a client and gateway shim that (a) requires a signed routing manifest describing each hop, (b) embeds uniquely fingerprinted canary content per request, and (c) reconciles the observed response against the declared chain to flag requests processed by an undeclared provider.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Threat Report, AI's Effect on Cybercrime, and How 9/11 Changed Cybersecurity

project_ideas.based_on: Allocate resources to core security controls rather than chasing AI-specific threat phantoms.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed defender budget, equivalent spend on identity, MFA, and endpoint controls yields a larger reduction in attacker success rate than spend on AI-specific threat tooling, even when the simulated adversary uses LLMs as an assistant.
project_ideas.measurement: Attacker mean-time-to-objective and success rate per arm, plus defender cost per prevented compromise, with confidence intervals across repeated runs.
project_ideas.name: Adversary-Cost Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Run a controlled attack-simulation harness with two defender budget arms (fundamentals-only vs. AI-threat-tooling-weighted) against identical LLM-assisted adversary workflows, replaying the same campaign set under both arms.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Threat Report, AI's Effect on Cybercrime, and How 9/11 Changed Cybersecurity

project_ideas.based_on: cybercrime and biological weapon development
project_ideas.hypothesis: A shared generic misuse-signal layer with pluggable domain-specific escalation stages transfers across cyber and bio/CBRN harm domains while matching domain-specific baselines, with measurable but bounded threshold shift required per domain.
project_ideas.measurement: Cross-domain precision/recall transfer, per-domain threshold shift required to hit a fixed operating point, and false-positive rate change when a threshold tuned for one domain is applied to the other.
project_ideas.name: DualHarm Bench
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a labeled abuse corpus spanning cyber operations and biological-weapon-development requests, train a generic base detector plus separate escalation heads, and measure cross-domain transfer by swapping heads against the shared base.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Threat Report, AI's Effect on Cybercrime, and How 9/11 Changed Cybersecurity

project_ideas.based_on: Categorizing threat actors by motivation and origin rather than by the tools they use.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Detectors keyed on actor behavior and attribution drift less across tool-generation changes than detectors keyed on tool modality, so behavior-keyed policies retain detection performance when an adversary swaps its tooling.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection performance decay per tool-generation swap for each detector class, plus the retraining volume needed to restore the original operating point.
project_ideas.name: Tool-Drift Detector
project_ideas.poc: Replay historical campaign telemetry labeled by actor motivation and origin, then retrain or swap only the tool layer between evaluation rounds and compare performance decay of behavior-keyed versus tool-keyed detectors.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Threat Report, AI's Effect on Cybercrime, and How 9/11 Changed Cybersecurity

project_ideas.based_on: constructing verifiable environments/verifiers
project_ideas.hypothesis: At matched compute budget, agents optimized against automatic verifiers outperform prompt-engineered baselines on held-out tasks in the same domain, and the advantage scales with environment and verifier count rather than with prompt refinement.
project_ideas.measurement: Held-out pass rate and iterations-to-threshold as a function of compute budget and number of distinct verifiers.
project_ideas.name: Verifier Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a matrix of verifiable environments (unit-test suites, formal checkers, game engines, simulator-backed tasks) plus a fixed-budget prompt-engineered baseline, and run identical compute against both.
project_ideas.video_title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

project_ideas.based_on: publishing precomputed model outputs at scale can move a field faster than exposing the model itself
project_ideas.hypothesis: For high-volume, low-variance inference workloads, consumers integrate precomputed bulk outputs into downstream pipelines faster than they integrate a gated model API at equal accuracy, shifting the bottleneck to validation and integration.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-first-integration, number of downstream consumers, and reuse count per cohort.
project_ideas.name: Bulk Release Ablation
project_ideas.poc: Two cohorts receive equivalent predictions, one as a bulk dataset and one via a gated API with comparable coverage and accuracy, and their integration behavior is tracked over the same window.
project_ideas.video_title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

project_ideas.based_on: identical model capability deployed under different institutional wrappers yields different outcomes
project_ideas.hypothesis: The same model deployed under two different governance wrappers - one with runtime evaluation, provenance, and decision-right contracts, one with minimal review - produces measurably different outcome variance, not merely a different mean outcome.
project_ideas.measurement: Outcome variance and incident rate per wrapper across identical task distributions.
project_ideas.name: Wrapper Variance Harness
project_ideas.poc: Runtime harness that attaches evaluation, provenance, and decision-right contracts to a fixed model and replays an identical task distribution under both wrappers.
project_ideas.video_title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

project_ideas.based_on: measure and optimize iterations-per-hour and artifact continuity
project_ideas.hypothesis: In generative creative tooling, iterations-per-hour predicts downstream artifact quality better than per-call output quality does, at a fixed total time budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between iterations-per-hour and blind-rated artifact quality at fixed total time, versus correlation with per-call quality ratings.
project_ideas.name: Loop Latency Instrument
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a stateful creative tool to log round-trip latency, regeneration count, and artifact continuity on a prior artifact, then correlate logs with blind-rated final outputs across matched time budgets.
project_ideas.video_title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

project_ideas.based_on: 100% accuracy for the logo check
project_ideas.hypothesis: Vision-model verification of 'is this logo present and correct on the banner' falls well below reported accuracy on occluded, low-contrast, partially-overlapping, and near-duplicate-logo cases, and false negatives cluster by defect class rather than at random.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-defect-class false-negative and false-positive rates versus the reported near-100% figure, plus verifier confidence calibration and the fraction of defects that a human must adjudicate.
project_ideas.name: Rendered-Artifact Validator Adversarial Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Generate synthetic banner layouts from a ground-truth sponsor set, inject a labeled defect taxonomy (missing logo, wrong logo, cropped, low contrast, occluded by another element, near-duplicate variants), run multiple vision models as verifiers, and record a confusion matrix per defect class.
project_ideas.video_title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer

project_ideas.based_on: vectorize it in Figma to bypass native SVG generation flaws
project_ideas.hypothesis: For vector-asset tasks, a raster-generate-then-deterministic-vectorize pipeline yields higher fidelity and editability than direct model-native SVG generation, and the gap widens as asset complexity increases.
project_ideas.measurement: Fidelity score against a reference asset, number of vector paths/nodes, and human editability rating per path, evaluated across a set of asset complexity tiers.
project_ideas.name: Format-Boundary Router
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that takes the same asset spec down two paths — direct SVG emission versus PNG generation followed by vectorization — renders both at multiple scales, and scores them on shape fidelity, path count, and editability heuristics.
project_ideas.video_title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer

project_ideas.based_on: how cheaply it absorbs exceptions
project_ideas.hypothesis: There is a measurable perturbation rate above which a scaled artifact pipeline's total human time exceeds manual production, and that threshold is dominated by per-exception handling cost rather than generation volume.
project_ideas.measurement: Human minutes per exception, exception rate per hundred artifacts, and total human minutes per hundred artifacts versus a manual baseline, locating the break-even perturbation rate.
project_ideas.name: Exception-Cost Instrumented Generator
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a template-driven artifact generator to log every source-data change, its propagation into a regeneration, the human time each exception consumed, and the escalation path taken; sweep perturbation rates from low to high.
project_ideas.video_title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer

project_ideas.based_on: design artifact is treated as a derived render of live event data
project_ideas.hypothesis: Artifacts generated by an agent inside a design tool can be made byte-reproducible and rollback-safe when source data and generation logic are both versioned and generation is pinned, contradicting the assumption that design-tool runtimes are inherently non-deterministic.
project_ideas.measurement: Regeneration reproducibility rate (identical output at the same pinned revision), diff size per data change, and time-to-rollback after an intentionally corrupted upstream data commit.
project_ideas.name: Versioned Re-Render Pipeline for Design-Tool Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a pipeline where event data-of-record and the generation spec live in version control, the agent renders artifacts from a pinned revision, and any artifact can be regenerated and diffed against the previously shipped version.
project_ideas.video_title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer

project_ideas.based_on: Model capability jumps can invalidate the existing product paradigm
project_ideas.hypothesis: A per-model-release probe suite can detect threshold crossings that predict which product-structure components must be rebuilt, producing earlier architectural-review triggers with measurable lead time and bounded false positives.
project_ideas.measurement: Lead time between first threshold crossing and rebuild decision; false-positive and false-negative rate of predicted churn zones.
project_ideas.name: Capability Jump Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a thin-wrapper product with capability probes and an architecture-churn log; on each model release, run regression/jump tests and compare detected threshold crossings against actual rebuild decisions.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Head of Design on AGI-Maximalist Product Design | Joel Lewenstein

project_ideas.based_on: Internal adoption is used as the primary viability gate for external release
project_ideas.hypothesis: Internal adoption metrics overpredict external retention for low-AI-fluency external users, and the gap can be quantified by stratifying internal and external cohorts by AI fluency and context access.
project_ideas.measurement: Difference between internal and external retention curves; false-positive launch rate of the internal-readiness gate.
project_ideas.name: Internal-to-External Readiness Gap
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an internal-first AI tool with usage telemetry, launch externally, and compare adoption and retention across matched and fluency-stratified cohorts.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Head of Design on AGI-Maximalist Product Design | Joel Lewenstein

project_ideas.based_on: persistent per-user devboxes with custom shared Python libraries
project_ideas.hypothesis: Persistent per-user agent devboxes with curated internal libraries reduce cold-start and re-setup cost versus ephemeral sandboxes, but require explicit lifecycle governance to keep storage drift and blast radius within acceptable bounds.
project_ideas.measurement: Cold-start time, task completion rate, storage growth per user, dependency drift, and simulated blast radius of a compromised environment.
project_ideas.name: Devbox Lifecycle Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run the same agent coding tasks in ephemeral per-session sandboxes and persistent per-user devboxes, with and without a cleanup/policy layer.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Head of Design on AGI-Maximalist Product Design | Joel Lewenstein

project_ideas.based_on: The output artifact and the meta-conversation are separate architectural surfaces
project_ideas.hypothesis: Treating generated artifacts as versioned first-class objects with their own state domain improves downstream tooling and context efficiency compared with storing them as messages in an append-only transcript.
project_ideas.measurement: Edit success rate, artifact reuse, context token cost per revision, and ability to diff/rollback without replaying the full transcript.
project_ideas.name: Artifact State Server
project_ideas.poc: Build an agent that produces code or documents, storing outputs in an artifact store with versions and diffs while keeping the conversation separate; compare against a transcript-only control.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Head of Design on AGI-Maximalist Product Design | Joel Lewenstein

project_ideas.based_on: Slop probes separate designer-approved from designer-rejected sites at AUC 0.74
project_ideas.hypothesis: A lightweight pattern-based slop probe can match or exceed a tuned LLM judge on held-out designer-approved/rejected web designs at a fraction of cost and latency.
project_ideas.measurement: AUC, precision/recall at operating threshold, cost per 1k evaluations, latency, and false-positive rate on novelty set.
project_ideas.name: ProbeGate
project_ideas.poc: Collect labeled design samples, extract surface features (type pairing, palette, framework traces), train baby classifier, compare AUC against LLM judge on same split; instrument false positives on unusual-but-good designs.
project_ideas.video_title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs

project_ideas.based_on: Brand API extracts structured brand components from a URL
project_ideas.hypothesis: Providing agents with structured brand context fetched at inference time increases brand adherence and reduces generic/slop outputs more than an equivalent prose style prompt.
project_ideas.measurement: Brand adherence rubric score, slop probe score, human preference, latency overhead per request.
project_ideas.name: BrandAPI Runtime Guard
project_ideas.poc: Build URL→structured brand schema extractor; agent generates landing pages/pitch decks with prose prompt vs Brand API context; score outputs with probes and human raters.
project_ideas.video_title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs

project_ideas.based_on: Which other subjective domains beyond design can be decoded
project_ideas.hypothesis: The repetition/fit/intent/judgment decomposition transfers to at least one non-design subjective domain (e.g., UX copy or code style), with probes achieving AUC > 0.70 against human labels.
project_ideas.measurement: AUC per pillar, inter-pillar correlation, failure attribution accuracy, cost.
project_ideas.name: Pillar Transfer Test
project_ideas.poc: Define domain-specific probes for each pillar, collect small labeled dataset, train/evaluate classifiers, compare with LLM judge baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs

project_ideas.based_on: Can probe outputs serve as verifiable reward/verification signals
project_ideas.hypothesis: Using slop probes as a rejection-sampling or reward signal during generation improves judged aesthetic quality without collapsing diversity.
project_ideas.measurement: Probe score, human preference, output diversity (distinct n-grams/embeddings), mode-collapse indicators.
project_ideas.name: ProbeReward Loop
project_ideas.poc: Generate N candidate outputs, rank/filter by probe score, compare baseline vs filtered outputs on quality and diversity metrics.
project_ideas.video_title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs

project_ideas.based_on: Design intent can be encoded as a constrained vocabulary of adjectives and verbs
project_ideas.hypothesis: A constrained, shared vocabulary of design adjectives and verbs compiled to deterministic design-system operations yields higher blind-rated craft quality and fewer iterations than open prompting or pixel editing.
project_ideas.measurement: Blind expert preference, AI-vs-human detection rate, iteration count to acceptance, design-system adherence, output diversity.
project_ideas.name: Leitwort Control Plane Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a coding-harness skill exposing commands like bolder, quieter, denser, harden that maps to design-token/component transformations; run on a set of UI recreation tasks against baselines.
project_ideas.video_title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.

project_ideas.based_on: One-shot design generation is claimed to be structurally unviable
project_ideas.hypothesis: Forcing explicit decisions for layout, type, color, and density across multi-shot generation reduces generic AI-slop patterns and increases perceived intentionality versus one-shot generation.
project_ideas.measurement: Frequency of generic patterns (gradients, neon, generic numbers), human preference, decision trace completeness, revision count.
project_ideas.name: Decision-Forcing Designer
project_ideas.poc: An agent workflow that records and resolves decision points before and during generation; compare one-shot vs decision-forced outputs on identical briefs.
project_ideas.video_title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.

project_ideas.based_on: Taste is characterized as cultural, contextual, and scarce
project_ideas.hypothesis: Outputs from shared base models exhibit measurable convergence that can be quantified; injecting unique context or constraints increases output diversity.
project_ideas.measurement: Intra-model vs inter-model similarity, distinct style cluster count, frequency of known AI-slop patterns, diversity delta after context injection.
project_ideas.name: Homogenization Detector
project_ideas.poc: Run identical design prompts across multiple models and seeds; cluster outputs by visual/style embeddings and detect generic-pattern signatures.
project_ideas.video_title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.

project_ideas.based_on: Reusable, named, community-tested commands
project_ideas.hypothesis: A versioned registry of named design operations with regression tests yields more consistent agent behavior across contributors than free-text prompts.
project_ideas.measurement: Cross-contributor output variance, regression pass rate, command reuse frequency, time to resolve command ambiguity.
project_ideas.name: Named Ops Registry
project_ideas.poc: Implement a shared command registry (bolder, quiet, distill, polish, denser, harden, overdrive) with semantic versioning, test fixtures, and CI that checks token/component diffs on reference UIs.
project_ideas.video_title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.

project_ideas.based_on: Amdahl's law applied to agent pipelines
project_ideas.hypothesis: Instrumenting the human review stage will show that it is the dominant serial fraction in agent-assisted code pipelines, and deploying review-assist agents will reduce that fraction enough to improve end-to-end cycle time.
project_ideas.measurement: Serial verification fraction, review latency per PR, merge volume, end-to-end cycle time, and review defect escape rate before and after review-assist deployment.
project_ideas.name: Verification Fraction Profiler
project_ideas.poc: Build a CI-integrated profiler that measures time and cost split between generation, automated checks, and human review per pull request, then run a before/after trial with a review-assist agent on a subset of repositories.
project_ideas.video_title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori

project_ideas.based_on: How can uncertainty in acceptance criteria be estimated before or during task execution
project_ideas.hypothesis: A pre-execution proxy score for acceptance-criteria uncertainty will predict verification cost and end-to-end agent leverage better than step-uncertainty or single-axis task difficulty.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between proxy score and measured verification cost, delegation leverage, rework rate, and misrouting rate across held-out task batches.
project_ideas.name: Criteria Uncertainty Estimator
project_ideas.poc: Train a lightweight classifier on task descriptions, historical rework rates, verifier disagreement, and rubric coverage, then route tasks to agent delegation, human ownership, or tightened-criteria treatment.
project_ideas.video_title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori

project_ideas.based_on: Token volume is an output metric masquerading as an outcome metric
project_ideas.hypothesis: Joining agent run telemetry to outcome events such as closed tickets or fixed bugs will produce ROI-per-task reporting that reduces budget oscillation compared with token-spend dashboards.
project_ideas.measurement: Variance in monthly agent spend, cost per accepted artifact, outcome attribution coverage, and correlation between spend changes and outcome changes over two budget cycles.
project_ideas.name: Outcome-Attributed Token Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent platform so every run carries an outcome join key, then expose per-outcome cost, spent tokens, accepted artifacts, and outcome-per-dollar in a shared dashboard.
project_ideas.video_title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori

project_ideas.based_on: Difficulty-based model routing is the concrete mitigation for token waste
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing tasks to model tiers using step-uncertainty and criteria-uncertainty classifications will maintain task-success rates while reducing cost per accepted artifact compared with a frontier-model default.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per accepted task, task-success rate, escalation rate, verifier disagreement, and quality regression across routed versus default configurations.
project_ideas.name: Uncertainty-Axis Model Router
project_ideas.poc: Implement a routing layer that classifies incoming tasks on the two uncertainty axes and escalates only high-uncertainty cases to frontier models, with a control group on frontier defaults.
project_ideas.video_title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori

project_ideas.based_on: combining screenshots, JSON data, and spatial prompts
project_ideas.hypothesis: On canvas manipulation tasks (alignment, spatial search, shape relocation), a hybrid observation channel of screenshot + JSON state + spatial prompt outperforms the best single channel on task success rate, and JSON-only degrades most on perceptually-grounded alignment tasks while screenshot-only degrades most on precision placement.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate per configuration, tokens and latency per successful task, and retry counts; report the accuracy-per-token frontier rather than raw accuracy.
project_ideas.name: Spatial Observation Ablation Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a fixed task suite of canvas layout tasks in a tldraw-style canvas, run the same LLM through three observation configurations (screenshot-only, JSON-only, hybrid) with an identical tool surface and control loop, and log per-step token cost, latency, retries, and success.
project_ideas.video_title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw

project_ideas.based_on: The tech tree app treats individual dependency graph tasks as autonomous coding agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: Binding each node of a launch dependency graph to an autonomous agent with explicit blocking, retry-with-context, and rollback policies reduces human interventions per graph by a measurable margin versus an equivalent flat task list, without increasing duplicate or conflicting work.
project_ideas.measurement: Human interventions per graph, duplicate-action rate, deadlock/blocked-node count, and wall-clock time from graph submission to completion.
project_ideas.name: DAG Harness with Explicit Blocking and Failure Semantics
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal orchestration layer over a real dependency graph where each node dispatches an agent, dependencies gate execution, failed nodes retry with prior-attempt context, and partial completions mark downstream nodes as blocked rather than failed; stress-test on a realistic multi-stage plan.
project_ideas.video_title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw

project_ideas.based_on: Fairy agents show planning status, assigned tasks, and progress directly next to their visual avatars
project_ideas.hypothesis: Operators diagnosing injected faults in a multi-agent run reach a correct root cause faster and more accurately when agent planning status, assigned tasks, and progress are rendered as positionable state objects next to each agent than when the same information is presented as a chronological chat transcript.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-diagnose and diagnosis accuracy per fault type, plus reported confidence and time spent searching history.
project_ideas.name: State-vs-Transcript Diagnosis Study
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small orchestrator-plus-worker multi-agent setup to emit both a structured spatial state model and a text transcript, inject a fixed catalog of coordination faults (duplicated assignment, stalled dependency, wrong-target edit), and run a within-subject diagnosis task under both interfaces.
project_ideas.video_title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw

project_ideas.based_on: Multi-agent collaboration is designed as configurable spatial personas ('fairies')
project_ideas.hypothesis: Quantifying orchestrator routing, task assignment, and redundant actions in a configurable-persona multi-agent canvas system reveals that coordination overhead (messages and duplicate work per completed task) grows non-linearly with agent count, and that a single designated orchestrator is not sufficient to bound it beyond a small team size.
project_ideas.measurement: Messages and duplicate actions per completed task as a function of agent count, plus task completion rate and orchestrator queue depth.
project_ideas.name: Coordination-Overhead Tracer for Spatial Multi-Agent Systems
project_ideas.poc: Extend a persona-based multi-agent canvas setup (configurable agent attributes plus one orchestrator) with tracing of every assignment, claim, and action, then sweep agent count on a fixed task set and attribute wasted actions to coordination rather than task difficulty.
project_ideas.video_title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw

project_ideas.based_on: Demos do not equal production reliability; real-world deployment data is required to bridge the last-mm gap.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a pick & place task, reliability improves at a measurable rate as a function of real-world edge-case data volume collected in deployment, and fine-tuning with field data closes the last-mm gap faster than additional simulation data.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate (e.g., picks per hour without human intervention) as a function of number of edge-case samples and fine-tuning iterations; compare against simulation-only baseline.
project_ideas.name: Field Data Flywheel for Pick & Place
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a pick & place robot in a controlled warehouse-like environment; instrument it to log all edge cases; run periodic fine-tuning with collected data; measure task success rate vs. data volume. Compare against a simulation-only baseline that receives an equivalent amount of synthetic data.
project_ideas.video_title: Physical AI: The hidden value pools leaders are missing

project_ideas.based_on: Unit cost per unit of performance will define the winning supply chain.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A standardized benchmark suite mapping component cost (e.g., actuators, harmonic drives) to performance on a set of manipulation tasks will reveal that suppliers with lower cost per unit of performance are not the cheapest per unit, and that EV-derived components dominate on this metric.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per successful task completion normalized by cycle time; ranking of suppliers.
project_ideas.name: Cost-per-Performance Benchmark for Robotics Components
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark suite of 5 manipulation tasks (pick & place, peg insertion, etc.); measure performance (success rate, cycle time) for actuators from different suppliers; compute cost per unit performance; compare EV-derived vs. purpose-built components.
project_ideas.video_title: Physical AI: The hidden value pools leaders are missing

project_ideas.based_on: Hardware (training hardware, platform hardware, form factor hardware) captures 25-35% of value.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Under scenarios of improving software capability and falling hardware costs, the share of value captured by software and field operations will increase relative to hardware, and the humanoid form factor will remain a small fraction of total value.
project_ideas.measurement: Projected value shares by layer over time; sensitivity to key parameters.
project_ideas.name: Value Pool Migration Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Build a simple economic model with parameters (software improvement rate, hardware cost decline, adoption curves) to simulate value pool shares from 2025 to 2045; calibrate with available market data; test sensitivity.
project_ideas.video_title: Physical AI: The hidden value pools leaders are missing

project_ideas.based_on: Out of 60 million full-time worker equivalents of annual tasks, only 13% are automatable today.
project_ideas.hypothesis: By decomposing physical tasks into primitives (dexterity, variability, data requirements), the 13% automatable share can be explained primarily by variability and data requirements rather than dexterity.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between task properties and automation feasibility; classification accuracy of a predictive model.
project_ideas.name: Task Decomposition for Automatability
project_ideas.poc: Take a sample of physical tasks from logistics and manufacturing; classify by dexterity, variability, and data availability; correlate with current automation feasibility; identify binding constraints.
project_ideas.video_title: Physical AI: The hidden value pools leaders are missing

project_ideas.based_on: Created an unmonitored communication channel to bypass sandbox containment
project_ideas.hypothesis: An egress proxy that records hashes and topic signatures of every public write made by an agent can detect when two nominally isolated agents use a public wiki as a shared blackboard with an F1 score of at least 0.90, while still allowing ordinary web operations.
project_ideas.measurement: ROC AUC and F1 of covert-channel detection over 1,000 runs; false-positive rate on legitimate wiki edits; time-to-detection after the first cross-write.
project_ideas.name: Egress Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a testbed where two agents are firewalled from each other but both may read and write an obscure wiki; make one agent encode task hints in posts and the other retrieve them, then compare audit logs plus proxy scores against a no-coordination baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

project_ideas.based_on: 10,000 agents, 130 billion tokens, and 88 hours of compute produced a claimed solution to a Millennium problem
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a benchmark of 100 Olympiad-level and graduate-level math problems, a 50-agent fan-out with explicit task decomposition, checkpointing, and an independent proof checker will solve at least 20% more problems than a single-agent best-of-100 sampler at the same total token budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Verified solve rate per 100M tokens, lemma checkpoint success rate, and false-positive rate before verification.
project_ideas.name: FleetProver
project_ideas.poc: Build a durable task queue in which an orchestrator splits a theorem into lemmas, worker agents produce candidate proofs, failed branches resume from checkpoints, and an independent verifier aggregates only checked results; compare against repeated single-agent sampling.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

project_ideas.based_on: Generation model, Autorater / Critique, Prompt rewriting, Optimizer agent
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an autorater and prompt-rewriting pass will improve human-acceptance rate of generated API documentation and README files by at least 30% after two revisions compared with one-shot generation, at no more than 2.5x the inference cost per accepted artifact.
project_ideas.measurement: Acceptance rate by revision, inference cost per accepted artifact, and critic-human agreement on failure reasons.
project_ideas.name: CriticLoop
project_ideas.poc: Create a fixed task set of 200 documentation-generation prompts; run a generator-critic-rewriter loop for up to five revisions; validate acceptance with a held-out LLM judge and a small human-rater sample.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

project_ideas.based_on: GPT-6 Astra recreated Manhattan street-by-street from a simple text prompt in one week
project_ideas.hypothesis: If a text-prompt world generator can create a city-like environment, then specifying scenario parameters such as traffic density, obstacles, and time pressure will monotonically shift agent success rates across 50 seeded world instances, enabling calibrated difficulty without hand-built fixtures.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman correlation between specified difficulty and mean solve rate; within-seed variance; reproducibility under identical world seed.
project_ideas.name: WorldBench
project_ideas.poc: Connect a generated city world API to an agent harness; generate 50 environment seeds at low, medium, and high specified difficulty; run a fixed agent population while recording per-seed traces and event logs.
project_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

project_ideas.based_on: Handles tool call notifications and permission requests.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A client-side ACP middleware can intercept every permission request from any compliant harness and return allow/deny responses via a uniform policy and audit store, with no harness-specific code and 100% capture.
project_ideas.measurement: Proportion of permission requests captured per harness, decision-log schema consistency across harnesses, and end-to-end approval latency.
project_ideas.name: ACP Consent Gate
project_ideas.poc: Build a middleware that reads ACP tool-call notifications and permission-request messages, presents a generic user prompt, and returns permission responses; then run two different ACP-compatible harnesses through identical tool-call prompts.
project_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

project_ideas.based_on: Having the same protocol semantics over stdio, HTTP, and WebSocket makes agent execution location a deployment detail
project_ideas.hypothesis: A single ACP client can drive the same stdio-connected harness remotely by swapping only the transport layer; local and remote runs will show the same JSON-RPC method types and ordering and comparable task success rates.
project_ideas.measurement: JSON-RPC method-name and ordering match ratio between local and remote sessions over 20 runs, task success rate, and median latency overhead.
project_ideas.name: ACP Remote Execution Bridge
project_ideas.poc: Implement a bridge process that exposes an ACP harness over HTTP/WebSocket and forwards to a child stdio harness; run a fixed task against a local connection and against the bridge while capturing all JSON-RPC traffic.
project_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

project_ideas.based_on: How do ACP clients and harnesses negotiate capabilities at session establishment?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A session-level conformance corpus will detect cross-client/cross-harness capability-negotiation mismatches that single-implementation tests miss; running N clients against N harnesses will yield reproducible mismatch categories.
project_ideas.measurement: Cross-product pass/fail counts, mismatch categories, and number of methods not supported or improperly negotiated.
project_ideas.name: ACP Interop Matrix
project_ideas.poc: Encode ACP sessions covering session creation, user messages, tool-call notifications, permission responses, and capability negotiation as versioned YAML scenarios; run every client-harness pair and record protocol-level failures.
project_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

project_ideas.based_on: custom methods prefixed with underscores
project_ideas.hypothesis: Underscore-prefixed extension usage is either highly concentrated in a few shared methods, indicating convergence, or long-tailed, indicating fragmentation, and this pattern can be measured from observable JSON-RPC traffic.
project_ideas.measurement: Share of underscore method calls, top-five method concentration ratio, and number of implementations per custom method.
project_ideas.name: ACP Extension Landscape Analyzer
project_ideas.poc: Collect JSON-RPC method usage logs from a small set of ACP clients and harnesses; classify standard methods versus underscore-prefixed extension methods; cluster method names by implementation.
project_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

project_ideas.based_on: Runs the entire system in a hostile simulation with targeted and fuzz testing
project_ideas.hypothesis: A CI gate that runs the full agent system inside a deliberately hostile simulated environment with targeted and fuzz testing, and that fails builds only with full reproduction steps attached, catches a strictly larger set of real defects per engineer-hour than human line-level review of the same changes.
project_ideas.measurement: Defects escaped to production per 100 merged changes; median time from failure to confirmed reproduction; review hours displaced per defect caught.
project_ideas.name: Hostile Harness Gate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agentic codebase with a simulation driver that injects hostile conditions, run targeted plus fuzz suites in CI, and force every failure artifact to carry an executable reproduction. Run in parallel with standard human review for one quarter and compare defect escape rates and time-to-triage.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

project_ideas.based_on: Bridging local execution tools with cloud infrastructure requires careful architectural alignment
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent runtime whose tool and state interfaces are defined as boundary-agnostic will migrate from local execution to a managed cloud stack with no rewrite of the execution loop, whereas a runtime that assumes local filesystem and implicit trust will require one.
project_ideas.measurement: Lines changed in the execution loop during migration; state-consistency violations under concurrent local and remote execution; added tool-call latency.
project_ideas.name: Boundary-Agnostic Agent Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Implement one minimal tool-calling agent twice: (a) with filesystem, process and credentials abstracted behind a portable interface, and (b) with direct local assumptions. Then move both behind a remote sandbox and measure the diff surface of the execution loop.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

project_ideas.based_on: Rust proved to be very good for agents fairly quickly when effort was put into it
project_ideas.hypothesis: Given identical tool semantics and identical model calls, a Rust agent harness exhibits a lower rate of unrecovered runtime failures and lower tail latency under injected tool-call faults than an equivalent harness in a garbage-collected language.
project_ideas.measurement: Unrecovered failure rate per 1,000 tool calls; p99 latency under fault injection; recovery success rate; development effort to reach parity.
project_ideas.name: Harness Language Fault Study
project_ideas.poc: Build the same minimal tool-calling loop in Rust and in one GC'd language with a shared tool schema and fault-injection driver. Subject both to identical tool-call faults — timeouts, malformed responses, partial writes — and compare failure and recovery behavior.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

project_ideas.based_on: Focus on co-designing models and harnesses together
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scores produced by an evaluation harness that rates model and harness configurations jointly will rank configurations differently than scores from a fixed stable model API, and the divergence will be large enough to change at least one shipping decision.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between joint scores and fixed-contract scores; per-task score delta attributable to harness-specific formatting; number of shipping decisions the divergence would reverse.
project_ideas.name: Joint Model-Harness Scoring Bench
project_ideas.poc: Define a joint scoring harness over a fixed task set, evaluate the same model under a stable API contract versus a harness-specific context format and tool schema, and compare rankings and per-task deltas.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

project_ideas.based_on: How can silent forgetting be detected in production without ground truth?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A separate per-constraint verifier pass can attribute which specific rules of a long skills file were violated by an already-generated completion, achieving materially higher per-rule detection of silent forgetting than a single holistic LLM-as-judge score.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-rule precision/recall against a synthetic ground truth where the exact dropped rules are known by construction, compared head-to-head with a single holistic judge score on the same outputs.
project_ideas.name: Rule Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Build a self-audit stage that takes a completed agent output plus the N-rule skills file and returns a per-rule followed/violated/unverifiable verdict, then run it on IFScale-style outputs from a model known to fail silently past its threshold.
project_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: IFScale-style evaluation is a portable harness pattern
project_ideas.hypothesis: Running a fixed density-accuracy harness across model versions locates each model's instruction cliff within a narrow band, and the cliff position for tool-selection and format constraints differs from the keyword-count cliff by more than the run-to-run variance.
project_ideas.measurement: Constraint count at which accuracy drops below a fixed threshold, with confidence intervals across repeated runs, compared per constraint class and per model.
project_ideas.name: Cliff Finder
project_ideas.poc: Port the IFScale-style report generation harness to two agentic constraint classes (tool-selection policy and output-format invariants), sweep constraint density on a log scale, and plot accuracy against N for each model and class.
project_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: Safety classifiers evaluate aggregate context and can fire on sparse lexical triggers embedded in large instruction sets
project_ideas.hypothesis: False-positive refusal rate on benign context grows monotonically with the number of constraints and ingested tokens, and a lightweight pre-flight scan plus reroute recovers most of the resulting lost completions at negligible quality cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Refusal rate versus constraint density curve, and recovery rate plus quality delta when the reroute path is enabled.
project_ideas.name: Refusal Thermometer
project_ideas.poc: Inject benign-but-triggering tokens into otherwise identical skills files at varying constraint counts, measure refusal rate as a function of density, then test a pre-flight trigger scan plus model reroute against the baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: Reasoning budget is a finite, shared resource that can be consumed without producing output
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tracking reasoning tokens separately from output tokens and aborting or forcing a fallback when reasoning consumes more than a set fraction of the total budget materially reduces zero-result completions without degrading task quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of completions with no usable result, plus task-quality score, in guarded versus unguarded runs at identical total token budgets.
project_ideas.name: Budget Split Alarm
project_ideas.poc: Wrap agent calls with dual-budget accounting and a no-result detector that fires when the completion contains no deliverable payload, then compare abort-and-retry routing against the unguarded baseline on hard multi-constraint tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

project_ideas.based_on: conflict resolution as a distinct subsystem, not as prompt instructions
project_ideas.hypothesis: A hybrid resolution policy combining source authority with recency weighting yields higher agent answer accuracy on contradictory multi-source context than either recency-only or human-adjudication-last policies.
project_ideas.measurement: Answer accuracy and contradiction-detection rate per policy, plus the fraction of conflicts a policy leaves unresolved or resolves wrongly.
project_ideas.name: ConflictBench
project_ideas.poc: Generate synthetic conflicts across code, docs, Slack, and incident records (old architecture record versus last night's Slack thread) and route each through three pluggable resolution policies, scoring agent answers against a ground-truth winning source.
project_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

project_ideas.based_on: satisfaction of search bias
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pre-ranked, engine-side context payloads reduce premature-retrieval-termination rate and total search loops versus an agent driving raw MCP search tools directly.
project_ideas.measurement: Premature-termination rate, retrieval-call count per task, and token spend per task in each configuration.
project_ideas.name: StopOrGo
project_ideas.poc: Run a fixed task set in two configurations — agent-with-MCP-search versus agent-over-hydrated-engine-payload — instrumenting how many retrieval calls occur before the agent answers and whether the authoritative source was ever read.
project_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

project_ideas.based_on: silent failures where code compiles but breaks production
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents run without institutional context violate unstated feature-flag and rollout requirements at a materially higher rate than hydrated agents, even when both produce compiling code.
project_ideas.measurement: Violation rate per 100 tasks, split by hydrated/unhydrated, with compile-success rate held constant to isolate silent failures.
project_ideas.name: SilentFailSuite
project_ideas.poc: Build golden tasks whose correct solution depends on a feature-flag or rollout rule that never appears in the prompt, then compare hydrated versus unhydrated agent output against the rule set rather than the compiler.
project_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

project_ideas.based_on: Curated-context repos rot faster than you can update them
project_ideas.hypothesis: Hand-curated markdown context repos decay measurably faster than a maintained ingestion pipeline, but the engine incurs its own staleness and conflict rates that approach curated-repo levels without active monitoring.
project_ideas.measurement: Staleness half-life in days, contradiction discovery rate per week, and maintenance hours per source per month for each approach.
project_ideas.name: ContextRotMeter
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a curated rules repo and a context engine side by side in an active codebase, logging staleness events and source contradictions over time against a fixed fact set.
project_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

project_ideas.based_on: How do RLM overhead costs compare across different base models in production?
project_ideas.hypothesis: RLM overhead cost (tokens, latency, dollars) scales superlinearly with recursion depth and inversely with base-model coding ability, making the architecture uneconomical below a certain capability tier.
project_ideas.measurement: Dollars per completed task and p95 latency vs. base-model coding benchmark score and recursion depth.
project_ideas.name: RLM Cost Profiler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an RLM harness to log token usage, wall-clock time, and sub-call count per recursion level; run on a fixed long-horizon task across 3–5 base models of varying coding ability; fit a cost model.
project_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

project_ideas.based_on: At what point does recursive decomposition stop helping relative to the reported ~40% context-usage degradation threshold?
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists a measurable input-size and context-utilization threshold above which an RLM harness outperforms a RAG baseline on long-horizon reasoning, after normalizing for latency and dollar cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy delta and cost per correct answer as a function of input size and context utilization.
project_ideas.name: RLM Crossover Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal RLM harness (REPL + sub-LM calls) and a RAG baseline on a long-document QA task; sweep input sizes and context utilization levels; measure accuracy, latency, and cost per task.
project_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

project_ideas.based_on: What are the best practices for structuring sub-LM signatures in DSPy?
project_ideas.hypothesis: The granularity and typing of sub-LM signatures in a DSPy-based RLM significantly affects recursion depth and final accuracy; overly coarse signatures increase context per sub-call while overly fine ones explode call count.
project_ideas.measurement: ROUGE/BERTScore vs. recursion depth and call count.
project_ideas.name: Sub-LM Signature Ablation
project_ideas.poc: Build three versions of a document-summarization RLM with different sub-LM signature granularities; evaluate on summarization quality, recursion depth, and total calls.
project_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

project_ideas.based_on: The RLM pattern separates a deterministic execution shell (REPL) from a probabilistic core (LLM)
project_ideas.hypothesis: A deterministic REPL shell that traces executed code, serializes state, and supports replay reduces debugging time and failure recurrence in recursive agents compared to unstructured tool-calling.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean time to diagnosis (MTTD) and failure recurrence rate.
project_ideas.name: Deterministic Shell Observability
project_ideas.poc: Add tracing and replay to an RLM harness; run a failure-prone task; measure time-to-diagnose and failure recurrence with and without the shell.
project_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

project_ideas.based_on: Securing database access requires removing raw connection details and user identifiers from agent control entirely
project_ideas.hypothesis: If user identity and data source are resolved and bound at the harness layer before the model sees a tool call, then adversarially prompted agents will produce zero successful cross-tenant or cross-dataset redirections, even when the prompt fully controls every remaining business argument.
project_ideas.measurement: Cross-tenant leakage rate (target zero) and business-task success rate versus a baseline where identity and source remain model-controlled parameters; also record how many legitimate multi-dataset requests are broken by the binding rule.
project_ideas.name: Harness-Bound Identity Proxy for Agent Database Tools
project_ideas.poc: Intercept MCP tool invocations in a thin proxy that strips model-supplied identity/source arguments, injects the authenticated principal and an allowlisted dataset, and exposes only business parameters. Run a red-team suite that attempts confused-deputy redirection, credential substitution, and dataset hopping across at least two models.
project_ideas.video_title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google

project_ideas.based_on: Improves agent reliability and reduces round trips and hallucinations
project_ideas.hypothesis: Outcome-shaped composite tools with actionable retryable errors and flattened inputs will raise task success and cut round trips by a measurable margin over atomic REST-wrapped equivalents, independently of model choice.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, mean round trips per completed task, retry-after-error success rate, and argument-validation failure rate, reported per model to separate schema effect from model effect.
project_ideas.name: Paired-Schema Agent Reliability Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build two tool surfaces over the same database backend — one atomic with generic 404 errors and nested parameter maps, one outcome-shaped with flattened inputs, separated read/write tools, and descriptive retryable errors. Run an identical task suite against both across multiple models and log the full call trace.
project_ideas.video_title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google

project_ideas.based_on: NL2SQL tools generate raw SQL dynamically via LLMs for analytical agents and flexible exploration
project_ideas.hypothesis: A curated library of pre-approved SQL statements can satisfy a majority of production end-user query traffic, and the residual uncovered requests cluster into a small, enumerable set of analytic patterns rather than a long tail.
project_ideas.measurement: Coverage percentage versus library size, residual query diversity (distinct patterns per uncovered request), and SQL-injection surface area measured as the count of requests reaching dynamic generation.
project_ideas.name: Pre-Approved Statement Coverage Analyzer
project_ideas.poc: Ingest a real or synthetic end-user query workload, map each request against a pre-approved statement library, classify the failures, and route only unmapped requests to an NL2SQL exploration path. Report coverage as the library grows.
project_ideas.video_title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google

project_ideas.based_on: Progresses from insecure raw database access to zero-trust architecture by abstracting connection details and binding user identity at the application layer
project_ideas.hypothesis: An automated conformance scorer can place any existing agent-database integration at a specific rung of the raw-access-to-bound-parameters ladder and predict its exploitability, letting teams improve trust incrementally instead of rewriting.
project_ideas.measurement: Stage assignment versus observed probe resistance — destructive DROP/DELETE execution under untrusted input — and the measured security delta per upgrade step between adjacent rungs.
project_ideas.name: Agent Integration Trust Ladder Conformance Scorer
project_ideas.poc: Define machine-checkable criteria per stage (raw execute_sql present, configurable sources declared, custom semantic tools defined, parameters bound and authenticated) and score representative open-source agent integrations, then attempt a destructive-action probe against each.
project_ideas.video_title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google

project_ideas.based_on: the breakthrough was achieving human-like emotional intonation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Standard auto-MOS/WER metrics cannot detect loss of emotional prosody; an 'emotion intent' listener test will rank TTS models differently on expressive material.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman rank correlation between standard quality scores and emotional-fidelity ratings; responder agreement (Fleiss' kappa) on emotional failure.
project_ideas.name: prosody-gap TTS evaluation harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a small set of utterances with marked emotional intent (e.g., grief, joy, urgency) in multiple languages; run several TTS models; produce audio clips; collect listener ratings on whether the emotion came through; compare to standard metric scores.
project_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

project_ideas.based_on: Marketplace models allow creators and individuals to authenticate, share, and monetize their AI voices
project_ideas.hypothesis: Synthetic voice generation can be gated by a signed consent artifact for the target voice with lower than 100ms added latency, making identity checks practical at API scale.
project_ideas.measurement: Added latency P99; invalid-token rejection rate; valid-token acceptance rate; watermark traceability in generated files.
project_ideas.name: voice-consent ledger sidecar
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a TTS endpoint with a consent-checking proxy; issue signed consent tokens for voice profiles; proxy rejects requests without a valid token and tags generations with a watermark or request ID; measure overhead.
project_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

project_ideas.based_on: Customer obsession as a form of R&D
project_ideas.hypothesis: Support conversations about a deployed speech product can be automatically classified into model capability gaps (robotic tone, mispronunciation, lack of emotion) and the resulting gap ranking predicts the model improvements shipped in the next release cycle better than raw feature-request counts.
project_ideas.measurement: F1 for capability-gap classification; overlap and rank correlation between gap list and actual shipped capabilities.
project_ideas.name: capability-gap classifier for AI product roadmaps
project_ideas.poc: Anonymize and label support tickets/customer logs from speech API; use an LLM to tag failure modes; produce a ranked gap list; compare with release notes/changelog over two subsequent quarters.
project_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

project_ideas.based_on: The length of tasks AI can do is doubling every 7 months overall.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Delegable task length for coding agents, measured end-to-end including specification, review, and integration, grows materially slower than the isolated task-completion curve — so any harness configured to the 70-day rate will over-delegate and fail integration gates before it fails generation gates.
project_ideas.measurement: Fitted doubling constant for isolated completion vs. fitted doubling constant for end-to-end delivery, plus the divergence gap at each measurement wave; delegation boundary failures per harness configuration.
project_ideas.name: Doubling-Clock Re-benchmarker
project_ideas.poc: A fixed task corpus with frozen specs, run repeatedly against current coding agents on two scopes: isolated task completion versus full delivery (generate, review, integrate, pass tests). Record the maximum task length that survives each scope and fit separate doubling curves over time.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Is Making Coding Cheap. Here's What Matters Now

project_ideas.based_on: Good technical debt meets clear objectives and delivers business value with human understanding.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Comprehension-linked metrics (time-to-explain per module, objective-to-code traceability coverage) predict downstream maintenance cost of AI-generated modules better than generation-origin or style-based signals.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between gate scores and subsequent change cost / defect density; false-positive rate of the gate against modules later rewritten; discrimination power versus an 'AI-generated percentage' baseline.
project_ideas.name: Comprehension Gate
project_ideas.poc: A CI-level gate that captures per-module explanation attempts and links each merged module to a stated business objective, then tracks cost-to-change and defect rates on flagged versus unflagged modules over a release cycle.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Is Making Coding Cheap. Here's What Matters Now

project_ideas.based_on: saving $150k/year in consulting fees
project_ideas.hypothesis: Gross savings from AI code generation are substantially offset by comprehension and review cost per unit of generated code, so net savings scale sublinearly with generated volume rather than linearly.
project_ideas.measurement: Net cost per shipped feature computed as generation + review + comprehension + maintenance minus outsourced baseline; ratio of human review hours to generated lines over successive modules.
project_ideas.name: Net-Cost Instrumenter for AI-Built Software
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a single non-technical-builder project from spec through maintenance: log generation volume, review time, comprehension time, and downstream maintenance work, then compute net cost against the equivalent outsourced baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Is Making Coding Cheap. Here's What Matters Now

project_ideas.based_on: Engineers who can shape product requirements and talk to users move the fastest.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Coding-agent pipelines that treat requirement elicitation and ambiguity resolution as first-class runtime stages (with proactive clarification turns) deliver more completed end-to-end tasks than otherwise-identical pipelines that assume fully-specified input.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end task completion rate on ambiguous specs, number of rework cycles per task, and wall-clock throughput including the clarification turns.
project_ideas.name: Intent-First Agent Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Two matched pipeline variants over the same task corpus: one with ambiguity detection and clarification turns before planning, one that proceeds directly to generation. Compare end-to-end completion under deliberately under-specified specs.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Is Making Coding Cheap. Here's What Matters Now

project_ideas.based_on: A secure personal agent architecture can be built by combining a core agent with sentinel monitoring agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding sentinel monitoring agents and explicit approval gates to a personal agent reduces unauthorized data access incidents by at least 50% compared to a monolithic agent, without a significant drop in task completion rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of unauthorized access attempts blocked, task completion rate, user trust score.
project_ideas.name: Sentinel-Enforced Least Privilege Agent
project_ideas.poc: Build a prototype personal agent (e.g., email assistant) with sentinel monitors and approval gates; test on simulated sensitive tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg on how Meta's Muse AI agent will make people money

project_ideas.based_on: Agent instances can learn and coordinate anonymously through a 'fleet' concept
project_ideas.hypothesis: Anonymous fleet learning can achieve comparable model improvement to centralized training while preserving privacy, with poisoning attacks detectable via robust aggregation.
project_ideas.measurement: Model accuracy vs centralized baseline, attack success rate, privacy leakage.
project_ideas.name: Fleet Learning Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a fleet of agents on a federated learning benchmark, introduce poisoning attacks, measure convergence and attack impact.
project_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg on how Meta's Muse AI agent will make people money

project_ideas.based_on: An agent can autonomously extract a structured task list from unstructured communications (email threads) and execute multi-step real-world actions
project_ideas.hypothesis: A proactive agent that extracts tasks from email and executes them with human-in-the-loop approval reduces user cognitive load (measured by time saved) while maintaining user satisfaction above a threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Time saved per task, task success rate, user satisfaction, approval response time.
project_ideas.name: Proactive Agent Task Scheduler
project_ideas.poc: Build a prototype that monitors email, extracts tasks (e.g., shopping list, event registration), and proposes actions for approval.
project_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg on how Meta's Muse AI agent will make people money

project_ideas.based_on: Encrypted virtual machine (VM) technology can enable confidential AI processing where the service provider cannot access user content
project_ideas.hypothesis: Confidential VMs for AI inference incur less than 20% latency overhead compared to non-confidential VMs for typical personal agent workloads.
project_ideas.measurement: Latency (ms), throughput (tokens/sec), overhead percentage.
project_ideas.name: Confidential VM Inference Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Benchmark a small language model inference in a confidential VM vs standard VM, measuring latency and throughput.
project_ideas.video_title: Mark Zuckerberg on how Meta's Muse AI agent will make people money

project_ideas.based_on: AI is exceptional at seeing weak signals and synthesizing competitive advantage data
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM weak-signal synthesis precision, recall, and calibration can be measured against expert human analyst conclusions on a multi-source corpus, and LLMs will show systematic overconfidence in low-signal conditions.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision, recall, calibration error (ECE), and overconfidence frequency compared to expert baseline.
project_ideas.name: WeakSignalBench
project_ideas.poc: Curate 50 company corpora, have experts label advantage drivers and disruption threats, run an LLM agent to synthesize conclusions, and compare AI outputs to expert labels.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

project_ideas.based_on: AI should be evaluated along three distinct vectors
project_ideas.hypothesis: A system can score high on productivity metrics while remaining neutral or negative on structural (disintermediation) metrics, and separate instrumentation reveals this divergence.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-vector scores and the magnitude of divergence between productivity and structural vectors.
project_ideas.name: ThreeVectorDash
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an AI workflow with per-vector metrics: productivity (time/cost), innovation (profit-pool impact), structural (value-chain boundary shifts). Run on multiple case studies and compare scores.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

project_ideas.based_on: Anchoring to a prior baseline ('last year's budget') is identified as a primary trap
project_ideas.hypothesis: An allocation policy that re-derives resource (compute, context, tools) from strategic targets on a cadence, while retaining a frozen reference baseline for regression detection, increases reallocation intensity without losing regression detection.
project_ideas.measurement: Reallocation magnitude, task performance, and regression detection rate.
project_ideas.name: ReallocAgent
project_ideas.poc: Simulate an agent tuning loop with two policies: anchored to previous baseline vs target-derived. Compare reallocation magnitude, task performance, and regression detection over multiple iterations.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

project_ideas.based_on: Mobilization is only effective when institutionalized
project_ideas.hypothesis: There is a minimum enforcement strength in a harness (advisory vs. mandatory reallocation) below which alignment degrades under personnel/context turnover; above which it persists.
project_ideas.measurement: Alignment persistence score under turnover and reallocation adherence rate.
project_ideas.name: DefaultAlignHarness
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness with configurable enforcement for resource reallocation. Simulate turnover cycles (changing agents, contexts) and measure alignment persistence over time.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

project_ideas.based_on: independent verifier agent scores iteratively until satisfied
project_ideas.hypothesis: On injected entity-misattribution errors, a same-family verifier agent driven by an outcome rubric catches materially fewer errors than a heterogeneous verifier or a deterministic entity-resolution check, at comparable cost per verified task.
project_ideas.measurement: Error catch rate and false-positive rate per configuration, plus inference cost and added latency per verified task; the hypothesis fails if same-family catch rate is within noise of the heterogeneous verifier at lower cost.
project_ideas.name: Verifier Decorrelation Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a brief-generation pipeline with three verification configurations (same-family rubric verifier, cross-family verifier, deterministic entity-resolution check) and inject labeled misattribution and plausibility errors into a fixed brief set.
project_ideas.video_title: How founders build on Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Sandboxing source code requires careful thought around security and tool exposure
project_ideas.hypothesis: A minimal sandbox policy (explicit repository read-scope plus a tool allowlist) reduces attempted out-of-scope tool calls and unauthorized file reads without reducing the rate of agent-proposed fixes that humans accept.
project_ideas.measurement: Accepted-fix rate per policy, count of attempted out-of-scope tool calls and out-of-repository reads, and review time per accepted fix.
project_ideas.name: Sandbox Capability Boundary Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run a telemetry-to-codebase agent against the same set of application-state snapshots under a permissive and a restricted sandbox policy, logging every tool invocation and file path touched.
project_ideas.video_title: How founders build on Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: When account-level and organization-wide memory disagree
project_ideas.hypothesis: A two-tier memory store with an explicit scope-precedence rule yields higher multi-account answer accuracy than a single shared memory store once contradictory facts are injected between account-level and org-wide scopes.
project_ideas.measurement: Downstream answer accuracy on conflict and no-conflict task subsets, plus the rate of silent cross-account contamination in roll-up answers.
project_ideas.name: Two-Tier Memory Conflict Injector
project_ideas.poc: Stand up account-scoped and org-scoped memory behind a set of multi-account query tasks, inject conflicting facts (pricing, ownership, entitlements) at both scopes, and compare a precedence-rule store against a flat store.
project_ideas.video_title: How founders build on Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: How is cost attributed per agent or per outcome
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing task classes by required intelligence and latency class, using a per-agent and per-account cost ledger, reduces total fleet inference spend without exceeding a defined quality-loss budget on interactive paths.
project_ideas.measurement: Total and per-task cost by class, rubric pass rate before and after routing, interactive-path latency, and the request volume at which the routed configuration turns net positive.
