project_ideas.poc: Build a small Poincaré-embedding memory and a Euclidean retrieval baseline; run a hierarchical QA/navigation task set (e.g., 50 tasks) through both memories in identical agent scaffolds.
project_ideas.video_title: One of the world's greatest mathematicians explains 6 essential concepts of math | Terence Tao

project_ideas.based_on: Least squares approximation and total variation minimization are key tools in modern data processing and imaging.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reconstructing 90% semantic similarity from log subsets is possible with 20% of information-gain-selected state keys, while the same 20% random keys produce below chance reconstruction.
project_ideas.measurement: Reconstruction edit distance and semantic similarity as functions of sampled-state fraction.
project_ideas.name: SparseAgentSense: compressed observability of agent traces
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a multi-step agent to emit structured state snapshots; collect full traces; learn total-variation/least-squares reconstruction; compare info-gain subset selection with random selection.
project_ideas.video_title: One of the world's greatest mathematicians explains 6 essential concepts of math | Terence Tao

project_ideas.based_on: A small set of primitives and design patterns is sufficient
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a fixed subset of ParallelKernelBench problems, an LLM agent forced to express multi-GPU data movement through a small composable primitive library will achieve at least 15 percentage points higher Fast1@k at a 2.0x speedup threshold than an equivalent raw-CUDA agent that only receives compiler-fix feedback.
project_ideas.measurement: Fast1@k at 1.0x, 1.5x, and 2.0x thresholds; median achieved kernel speedup; compilation success rate.
project_ideas.name: ParallelKittens Constraint Study for PKB
project_ideas.poc: Build two harnesses over the same PKB subset and budget: one arm lets the model write raw CUDA with compile/run feedback; the other arm constrains generation to Loader/Communicator/Consumer/Storer-style templates while keeping the same base model and retry budget. Run both arms across representative kernels on a 2-4 GPU NVLink node.
project_ideas.video_title: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels? — Simran Arora, Together AI

project_ideas.based_on: LLMs can handle syntax and shape errors using agentic loops
project_ideas.hypothesis: Supplementing agentic-loop feedback with per-kernel memory-bandwidth utilization and overlap reports improves Fast1@k on ParallelKernelBench by at least 10 percentage points over compiler-error-only feedback at a 1.25x speedup threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta Fast1@k across feedback conditions; number of retries needed to reach threshold; variance across model instances.
project_ideas.name: Feedback-Modal Ablation on Kernel Agents
project_ideas.poc: For a fixed model and PKB sample, compare agent runs under three feedback protocols: compile errors only; speedup pass/fail only; and speedup plus bandwidth/overlap traces computed from actual kernel executions. Keep retry budgets and prompts constant.
project_ideas.video_title: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels? — Simran Arora, Together AI

project_ideas.based_on: Communication can consume over 50% of execution time in large language model workloads
project_ideas.hypothesis: For representative attention, FlashAttention, and Mamba kernels on a 2-GPU NVLink node, communication fraction remains above 50% for each workload when arithmetic intensity per GPU is held fixed, confirming communication dominance is workload-level and not an artifact of one benchmark.
project_ideas.measurement: Communication fraction of total execution time; achieved NVLink bandwidth; overlap utilization across each workload.
project_ideas.name: Multi-Workload Communication Share Study
project_ideas.poc: Profile reference implementations and their ParallelKittens-style distributed variants on an H100 node, measuring kernel time, NVLink transfer time and idle time; make total per-GPU arithmetic intensity comparable by scaling sequence/tensor parallelism.
project_ideas.video_title: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels? — Simran Arora, Together AI

project_ideas.based_on: moving from task delegation to end-state expression
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed set of repository refactoring tasks, an agent given a natural-language end-state spec plus acceptance tests will complete the task with half the required human interventions and at least the same code-correctness rate compared with an agent given explicit step-by-step task instructions.
project_ideas.measurement: Human intervention count, diff correctness score, time-to-task-completion
project_ideas.name: OutcomeSpec
project_ideas.poc: Build a small task-driving service that prompts Claude in two modes: outcome-mode (end-state contract) and step-mode (task decomposition). Run it against three single-service repos, collecting traces from execution and human approval checkpoints.
project_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds: Lessons from Labs — Mike Krieger, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: put models in boxes with limited access and freedom
project_ideas.hypothesis: Granting an agent broad write/execute access within a sandbox improves multi-file refactoring task success by at least 30% compared to a narrowly scoped tool-using agent, while the number of critical rollback incidents stays below one per five tasks when an outer review gate is applied.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, normalized test pass rate, rollback incidents per task, mean human review time
project_ideas.name: AgentAccessA/B
project_ideas.poc: Create the two runtime configurations in Gatehouse: one with a small set of editing tools and one with a full shell/sandbox. Run a benchmark migration and refactoring suite, applying an outer-boundary approver for both modes.
project_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds: Lessons from Labs — Mike Krieger, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: two-week review cadence where every project is evaluated to persevere or pivot
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams using a two-week 'persevere or pivot' board will cut the average months spent on failing experiments from over six months to less than three months in a longitudinal comparison.
project_ideas.measurement: Average time-to-kill, project portfolio ROI, qualitative team energy surveys
project_ideas.name: PivotPulse
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a Kill/Optimize/Pivot tracker for Movement Lab projects: each project enters with a traction target and due date; a dashboard sends a decision prompt every two weeks and logs whether project was kept, killed, or reprioritized, and later links that to outcome.
project_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds: Lessons from Labs — Mike Krieger, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: Identify chokepoints in an agent stack (one model provider, one tool gateway, one vector store region) and treat them as policy and observability planes
project_ideas.hypothesis: A single designated gateway on the critical path can enforce policy, quota, and telemetry more cheaply than distributed call sites, but introduces a single point of failure whose impact can be bounded by failover to a secondary gateway.
project_ideas.measurement: Policy enforcement coverage (percent of calls subject to policy), added latency overhead, and recovery time when gateway fails.
project_ideas.name: Chokepoint Gateway Policy Plane
project_ideas.poc: Implement a gateway that proxies model calls, tool calls, and retrieval, with policy rules and quota; measure policy enforcement consistency and failover behavior under gateway failure.
project_ideas.video_title: Iran, War, AI, God, Consciousness & Global War | Professor Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: Prototype dependency-level anomaly detection on tool/context/credential inputs and measure how early it flags a compromise before output quality degrades.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Anomalies injected into an agent's resource dependencies (tool credentials, context supply, provider quota) are detectable earlier at the resource boundary than by monitoring output quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-detect (in steps or seconds) before output quality degrades, and false positive rate.
project_ideas.name: Dependency Boundary Anomaly Detector
project_ideas.poc: Simulate compromise of tool credentials and context injection; instrument tool/context/credential inputs; measure detection latency.
project_ideas.video_title: Iran, War, AI, God, Consciousness & Global War | Professor Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: Build an attribution harness that scores the same task through classification-only, retrieval-only, and generation paths, and compare where errors originate.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a given task, errors from classification, retrieval, and generation components can be reliably attributed to one mechanism by routing the same inputs through isolated paths, and the dominant error source differs by task type.
project_ideas.measurement: Attribution accuracy (human-labeled error source vs path that fails), and proportion of errors attributed to each mechanism per task type.
project_ideas.name: Mechanism Attribution Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that scores the same task through classification-only, retrieval-only, and generation paths using a fixed dataset, and logs per-path error.
project_ideas.video_title: Iran, War, AI, God, Consciousness & Global War | Professor Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: Instrument an agent platform to log both abstract credits and underlying compute/power per request, then compare charge curves against resource curves.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Logging both abstract credits and underlying compute/power per request reveals that charge curves diverge from resource curves, and the divergence predicts throttling events.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between charge and resource, and lead time between divergence and throttling.
project_ideas.name: Resource-Abstraction Mapping Instrumentation
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent platform to log credits and underlying CPU/GPU/power per request; compare charge curves vs resource curves over time.
project_ideas.video_title: Iran, War, AI, God, Consciousness & Global War | Professor Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: Claude Code Opus 4.5 broke 80% on SWE-bench, producing code worth merging.
project_ideas.hypothesis: If benchmark pass rate is used as a standalone merge gate, agent-produced patches on held-out issue variants will show a significantly higher post-merge failure rate than patches additionally subject to high-level human review.
project_ideas.measurement: Post-merge bug incidence per 100 patches and false-acceptance rate against a hidden adjudication panel.
project_ideas.name: Mergeability Gate Probe
project_ideas.poc: Generate agent patches from issue descriptions, create near-distribution task variants, and compare two conditions in a sandbox: patches merged automatically after a benchmark threshold versus patches merged after human review.
project_ideas.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501

project_ideas.based_on: Over 1,000 pull requests merged in three months on Quattro using AI-assisted review workflows.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For an open-source repository receiving AI-generated PRs, a two-stage triage policy of automated clustering plus sampled human audit can maintain the same latent defect rate per merged change while cutting maintainer time per PR to a fraction of line-by-line review.
project_ideas.measurement: False-acceptance rate, defect escape rate, and average maintainer time per merged PR.
project_ideas.name: Maintainer Signal Dashboard with AI-Assisted Triage
project_ideas.poc: Build a dashboard that categorizes incoming PRs by task type, applies automated high-level review, queues random samples for human audit, and replays against historical PRs with known outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501

project_ideas.based_on: running AI coding agents across multiple machines
project_ideas.hypothesis: For multi-file system-building tasks, a brains-and-hands agent council executing on multiple machines will not reliably improve completion success over a single frontier agent, but will reduce wall-clock time by at least 30% on partitionable tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, wall-clock time, number of human interventions, and merge acceptance rate.
project_ideas.name: Council Benchmark: Single Agent vs Brains-and-Hands
project_ideas.poc: Create a task runner with two execution modes: one agent with full context versus a coordinator agent delegating file-level changes to worker agents on separate machines, then run a fixed suite of system-building tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501

project_ideas.based_on: When efficiency makes something cheaper, total demand rises instead of falling (Jevons Paradox).
project_ideas.hypothesis: If Jevons Paradox applies to agentic coding, growth rates of newly created software repositories and shipped feature requests will accelerate in periods following significant agentic-tool release milestones rather than contract.
project_ideas.measurement: Pre-/post-milestone growth rates in repository creation and package releases, with seasonality controls.
project_ideas.name: Software Demand Elasticity Observatory
project_ideas.poc: Build an open-data dashboard tracking quarterly counts of new open-source repositories, released package versions, and public engineering job postings, segmented by agentic-tool adoption indicators.
project_ideas.video_title: DHH: Future of Programming, AI, Agentic Engineering, Vibe Coding & Linux | Lex Fridman Podcast #501

project_ideas.based_on: semantic entropy
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a fixed prompt set, an LLM that abstains when sampled answers have high semantic entropy will reduce the rate of confident incorrect answers by at least 20% relative to a no-abstain baseline while preserving at least 90% of correct non-abstained answers.
project_ideas.measurement: Abstention curve: confident-correct rate, confident-error rate, recall, and expected calibration error under increasing entropy thresholds.
project_ideas.name: semantic-entropy-abstention
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that samples N generations per prompt, clusters by semantic equivalence, computes entropy, and compares agent performance with and without an abstention branch.
project_ideas.video_title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty

project_ideas.based_on: Modifying just a few pixels
project_ideas.hypothesis: On image classification benchmarks with added adversarial perturbations, routing inputs through a calibrated reject/fallback branch when uncertainty is high yields lower confident-error rate than any fixed confidence threshold on a single model.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy on valid inputs, abstention rate, and confident-error rate before and after gating.
project_ideas.name: adversarial-confidence-gate
project_ideas.poc: Take a trained classifier, generate small-pixel perturbations, calibrate confidence, add a decision gate that abstains or falls back under uncertainty, and measure joint accuracy.
project_ideas.video_title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty

project_ideas.based_on: Perception is limited
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a simulated partially observable environment with sensor noise, an agent using an explicit posterior over world states will make decisions with lower expected cost than an agent that updates a single deterministic state representation.
project_ideas.measurement: Expected cost per episode, number of unsafe actions, and calibration of state estimates.
project_ideas.name: belief-state-agent
project_ideas.poc: Implement a gridworld with noisy observations, and compare a deterministic context baseline against a belief-state Bayesian filter with a simple policy.
project_ideas.video_title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty

project_ideas.based_on: Diffusion models generate an ensemble of forecasts
project_ideas.hypothesis: A diffusion-based generative ensemble trained on trajectories from a deterministic dynamical system will produce forecasts with calibration and accuracy comparable to a Monte Carlo numerical simulation at a fraction of inference time.
project_ideas.measurement: RMSE, CRPS, probabilistic calibration, and wall-clock time.
project_ideas.name: diffusion-ensemble-surrogate-benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a chaotic ODE or PDE, train a diffusion model to sample future states, and compare its distributional outputs with an expensive numerical ensemble.
project_ideas.video_title: The mathematics of AI uncertainty

project_ideas.based_on: constrain the capability surface to the subset with verified data/quality
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent gated to a verified question set at launch achieves equal or higher 4-week weekly-active retention than an equally-resourced broad best-effort agent, without reducing total questions answered per active user.
project_ideas.measurement: Weekly active user retention, per-cluster answer accuracy, questions per WAU, and out-of-scope refusal behavior (do users rephrase, retry, or churn).
project_ideas.name: Scope Gate
project_ideas.poc: Run two 50-user pilots on identical data with an instrumented routing/refusal layer: arm A answers broadly and best-effort, arm B answers only classes whose underlying data passes a readiness check and explicitly refuses/routes the rest. Track per-question-class accuracy, refusal rate, and WAU retention weekly.
project_ideas.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake

project_ideas.based_on: Benchmark small-model labels against frontier-model and human labels on a held-out sample
project_ideas.hypothesis: Frontier-induced clusters/rules/regex applied by small models retain at least 90% label agreement with frontier labels only for a bounded number of log windows, and drift becomes detectable before it corrupts downstream roadmap and content outputs.
project_ideas.measurement: Agreement rate between small-model labels and frontier/human labels per window, cost per labeled query versus full frontier labeling, and the number of windows until agreement falls below threshold.
project_ideas.name: Label Drift Watch
project_ideas.poc: Build the two-stage pipeline: a frontier model induces clusters and rules/regex once per window; small models label the full corpus. Each window, sample a held-out slice and re-label it with the frontier model and human annotators; plot agreement, cluster mass shift, and downstream artifact churn over successive windows.
project_ideas.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake

project_ideas.based_on: Run cohort retention curves before, during, and after change-management campaigns
project_ideas.hypothesis: Post-launch usage decays toward a stable baseline within roughly 90 days without reinforcement, and recurring per-manager reinforcement produces durable cohort retention rather than a promotional spike that decays to the same baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Cohort-level weekly retention curves before/during/after campaigns, time-to-baseline decay rate, fraction of cohorts whose usage persists above baseline after reinforcement stops, and reinforcement hours spent per retained weekly active user.
project_ideas.name: Adoption Decay Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Instrument cohort retention curves segmented by whether a cohort's manager received reinforcement interventions (exec sponsorship, scheduled demos, accountability reviews). Compare cohorts that received a one-time launch push versus recurring reinforcement over matched windows.
project_ideas.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake

project_ideas.based_on: Track the delta in task success/latency/cost before and after each architectural swap
project_ideas.hypothesis: Component-level architectural swaps (instruction doc to skills library, tool integration to MCP servers, added memory, progressive disclosure) each produce a measurable delta in task success, latency or cost, and the swap rate decays as primitives stabilize rather than remaining a permanent ~35% tax.
project_ideas.measurement: Pre/post deltas in task success, latency and cost per swap; engineering hours per swap; swap count per quarter and whether the trend decays or holds.
project_ideas.name: Re-architecture ROI Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Maintain a frozen evaluation suite run before and after each architectural swap, logging task success, latency, token/cost per task, and engineering hours consumed by the migration. Plot deltas and swap frequency over quarters.
project_ideas.video_title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake

project_ideas.based_on: Define a pilot template with pre-declared success thresholds, time box, and conversion trigger
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pilots with pre-declared success thresholds, a hard time box, and an explicit conversion trigger convert at a higher rate per engineering-hour consumed than open-ended POCs provisioned per buyer.
project_ideas.measurement: Conversion rate per pilot and engineering-hours consumed per pilot, compared against a baseline cohort of open-ended pilots.
project_ideas.name: Bounded Pilot Harness
project_ideas.poc: A lightweight pilot spec service that requires threshold, time box, and conversion trigger before an environment is provisioned, records engineering hours logged per pilot, and blocks extension without a recorded conversion decision.
project_ideas.video_title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Buyer — Aliisa Rosenthal, Acrew Capital

project_ideas.based_on: Use trust portals for automated security documentation, NDAs, and SOC 2 compliance.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Serving security and compliance artifacts (SOC 2, pen tests, automated NDAs) as a self-serve endpoint removes a serial human handoff and shortens the interval between security review start and completion.
project_ideas.measurement: Elapsed time from review start to completion and count of human-handoff touches per review, versus the per-consumer manual workflow.
project_ideas.name: Gatehouse Artifact Endpoint
project_ideas.poc: Publish static compliance artifacts behind an authenticated self-serve endpoint with automated NDA execution, instrumenting review-start, artifact-retrieval, and review-complete timestamps.
project_ideas.video_title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Buyer — Aliisa Rosenthal, Acrew Capital

project_ideas.based_on: Automate inbound processing and enrich sign-up forms with phone numbers and user data before scaling headcount.
project_ideas.hypothesis: The high-volume-per-rep leverage ratio holds only when records are enriched at the point of ingestion; without intake-time enrichment the ratio degrades as automated volume grows.
project_ideas.measurement: Conversion rate and response quality as functions of automated volume per rep, with enrichment status as the independent variable.
project_ideas.name: Enrichment-First Intake Pipeline
project_ideas.poc: An intake pipeline that enriches sign-up records with phone numbers and user data before routing, run head-to-head against an unenriched variant at matched automated volume.
project_ideas.video_title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Buyer — Aliisa Rosenthal, Acrew Capital

project_ideas.based_on: Run tiered entry-price experiments with usage-based metering
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adoption breadth rises with lower entry price while revenue per account is preserved or improved by usage-based metering on the system's actual variable cost driver.
project_ideas.measurement: Adoption breadth (accounts entering usage) against revenue per account across tiers, holding the metered resource fixed.
project_ideas.name: Entry-Tier Elasticity Meter
project_ideas.poc: A tiered entry-price experiment with usage-based metering that varies only the entry threshold while holding the metered resource constant, tracking adoption breadth and revenue per account per tier.
project_ideas.video_title: Reverse-Engineering the AI Buyer — Aliisa Rosenthal, Acrew Capital

project_ideas.based_on: feedback loops, cognitive load, and flow state
project_ideas.hypothesis: The 80th-percentile wait time for a single platform feedback loop, such as provisioning or CI result, explains more than 40% of the variance in developers' self-reported flow-state ratings over a two-week period.
project_ideas.measurement: Variance explained by wait time and context-switch signals in a mixed-effects model; positive predictive value of telemetry thresholds for low-flow and frustrated sessions.
project_ideas.name: FlowScope
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small demo internal developer platform with event timestamps for provisioning, pipeline results, and UI actions, then collect random three-question DevEx self-reports from a cohort of 30 developers using a portal and CLI.
project_ideas.video_title: Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects & the Rest of Us • Daniel Bryant • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Netflix exposed platform capabilities via client libraries and later sidecars like Dapr.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Shifting a platform capability from an in-process client library to a sidecar HTTP API reduces the number of consumers that must change after a breaking release by at least 50%, while adding less than 5 ms p99 latency inside a datacenter network.
project_ideas.measurement: Number and percentage of consumers requiring code or release changes after a breaking change; p50 and p99 latency; additional resource overhead of sidecars versus in-process calls.
project_ideas.name: SidecarScale
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal feature-flag/config platform capability exposed three ways: in-process library, remote HTTP API, and localhost sidecar proxy. Create 25 toy consumer services and run a breaking API change for each style, then measure propagation and latency.
project_ideas.video_title: Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects & the Rest of Us • Daniel Bryant • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Instead of imposing rigid, monolithic golden paths that restrict developers, provide composable golden bricks that can be assembled flexibly.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams that choose among three pre-approved, composable platform bricks reach production with no more than a 15% difference in time-to-first-deploy compared with teams given a single golden path, while producing fewer compliance guardrail violations.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-first-deploy for a standard toy service, number of guardrail violations, support ticket volume, and variance across teams.
project_ideas.name: BrickBench
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a lightweight platform composition sandbox where one cohort of teams is forced into a monolithic golden path and another is allowed to mix three independent bricks with guardrails. Run standardized onboarding tasks for 10 teams in each cohort.
project_ideas.video_title: Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects & the Rest of Us • Daniel Bryant • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Avoid tightly coupling business logic into UI portals.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Moving platform domain logic out of a portal into a platform API reduces portal code changes during non-breaking internal service changes to near zero without increasing user task completion time.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of portal source files changed per internal platform service change; portal user task success rate and completion time; API contract stability.
project_ideas.name: ThinPortalCheck
project_ideas.poc: Implement two small developer portals for the same toy capability: one that calls internal platform services directly and one that consumes a stable platform API. Apply a set of controlled changes to the internal service and observe portal diffs and user outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects & the Rest of Us • Daniel Bryant • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: 20-50% of tasks can be solved without looking at the underlying data
project_ideas.hypothesis: Running an agent on a benchmark task with data access ablated (or with data replaced by noise) and comparing its score against the with-data score will flag a per-benchmark contamination rate consistent with the 20-50% figure on at least one widely used data science benchmark, and tasks flagged this way are removable without materially changing the relative ranking of strong models.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-benchmark share of tasks solved correctly under data ablation; change in model ranking after removing flagged tasks; false-removal rate estimated against tasks known to require data.
project_ideas.name: Shortcut Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that replays published benchmark tasks (a) normally and (b) with dataset contents stubbed out or randomized but task text unchanged; diff correctness rates per task and emit a contamination report per benchmark.
project_ideas.video_title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI

project_ideas.based_on: Only problems with deterministic verifiers can be admitted
project_ideas.hypothesis: Candidate deterministic verifiers can be synthesized by agents and admitted automatically when they pass a dual fuzz test (accept all known-valid solutions, reject all known-invalid or perturbed solutions), expanding the admissible problem set beyond hand-curated math-optimization tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Admission rate of generated verifiers; false-accept and false-reject rates on held-out solution sets; number of new problems made arena-eligible per unit of human curation time.
project_ideas.name: Verifier Forge
project_ideas.poc: Pipeline that takes a candidate problem plus a small set of known-valid/invalid solutions, has an agent write a checker, fuzzes the checker on mutated and edge-case inputs, and only admits the problem to an arena when the checker passes both acceptance and rejection suites.
project_ideas.video_title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI

project_ideas.based_on: Agents with distinct personas (profiler, memory specialist, tensor-core expert)
project_ideas.hypothesis: On the same GPU kernel optimization task, one generalist agent holding all instrumentation tools performs within noise of N tool-specialized persona agents, meaning the specialization axis (one agent per observation channel) rather than agent count is the causal factor — and the same split transfers to at least one non-CUDA performance domain.
project_ideas.measurement: Speedup vs. hand-written baseline per arm; best-of-N result; steps-to-target; whether the specialist advantage replicates outside CUDA.
project_ideas.name: Persona Ablation Bench
project_ideas.poc: Run three arms on a fixed kernel set with matched token budget: single generalist with all tools, N specialists each restricted to one instrument, and a fixed hand-written workflow baseline; then repeat on a compiler or query-planner tuning task.
project_ideas.video_title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI

project_ideas.based_on: Leverage execution-verified trajectories from gym environments as training factories for smaller open-source models
project_ideas.hypothesis: Execution-verified trajectories harvested from a sandboxed gym improve downstream task performance for a small open-source model more than untuned or human-written-data baselines, because execution correctness serves as a reliable labeling function for synthetic data.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in held-out task pass rate versus untuned and human-data baselines; yield of verifier-passing trajectories per rollout hour; whether gains survive against the shortcut-filtered task split.
project_ideas.name: Verified-Trajectory Distillery
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a DSGym-style sandbox to emit (state, action, execution outcome) trajectories, filter to execution-passing runs, fine-tune a small open model on them, and compare against untuned and human-data baselines on held-out tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI

project_ideas.based_on: Does BFCL function-calling parity between 32B SLMs and 100B+ LLMs transfer to real production agents that use heterogeneous, evolving tools and private APIs?
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a benchmark reconstructed from production agent logs, a 32B SLM will complete tasks within five percentage points of a frontier cloud LLM; if BFCL parity is an artifact of curated functions, the gap will exceed fifteen points.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, tool-selection accuracy, argument validity, and the performance difference between models on logged production turns.
project_ideas.name: TracedToolParity
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an existing Python agent runtime to collect 100-500 logged tool-call turns, build a replay harness that preserves tool schemas and context, and run the same task set through a local 32B quantized SLM and a large cloud LLM.
project_ideas.video_title: Demystifying Agentic AI Using Small Language Models [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: How small can an SLM be and still reliably drive an agentic tool-calling loop?
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed agentic tool-calling task suite, success rate follows an S-curve by parameter count: models below a certain size will fail tool-serialization tasks far more often, while 13B and 32B models will be statistically indistinguishable after prompt normalization.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, tool-call parse validity, token cost per success, memory footprint, and the coordinate of the performance knee.
project_ideas.name: AgentScaleKnee
project_ideas.poc: Run 1B, 3B, 7B, 13B, and 32B quantized checkpoints through llama.cpp with an identical system prompt, tool schema, and agent loop on the same task set.
project_ideas.video_title: Demystifying Agentic AI Using Small Language Models [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: Agentic workflows replace traditional Airflow DAGs with natural language business rules and guardrails
project_ideas.hypothesis: A natural-language agent governed by pre-tool policy checks and post-tool schema validation can match an Airflow DAG's success rate within two percentage points while producing zero policy violations on a controlled 1,000-run workload.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, policy-violation count, invalid-tool-call count, and deviation from the intended DAG execution order.
project_ideas.name: PolicyGuardedAgentRunner
project_ideas.poc: Express an existing Airflow pipeline (read from Iceberg, transform, cache results) as natural-language business rules plus a tool registry; run the same workload through both an agentic runtime and the original DAG, with guardrail checks on every tool call.
project_ideas.video_title: Demystifying Agentic AI Using Small Language Models [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: The danger of using LLMs without access to real structured business data and proper grounding.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A 32B SLM required to fetch evidence from an authoritative structured source before producing a final answer will reduce hallucination rate by at least 30 percentage points compared with an identical ungrounded model on business-data questions.
project_ideas.measurement: Factual precision, hallucinated-reference rate, evidence-citation accuracy, and task completion rate across grounded and ungrounded runs.
project_ideas.name: GroundedSLMDataAgent
project_ideas.poc: Build a local agent with a required Iceberg/cache lookup tool, seed a test set with plausible-sounding false facts, and compare grounded versus ungrounded final-answer precision under identical prompts.
project_ideas.video_title: Demystifying Agentic AI Using Small Language Models [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: Too much agent autonomy leads to unpredictable behavior and incomplete tasks.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For domain tasks with a known step sequence, LangGraph-enforced control flow achieves at least 40% higher task completion rate than a prompt-driven autonomous agent given the same tools, while not degrading outcomes on open-ended goals.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of tasks completed without missing required tool calls; output completeness; number of tool calls per completed task.
project_ideas.name: Agent Workflow Enforcement Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a small benchmark of 3 task families (data collection, validation, report generation) where the graph is fixed for one variant and the other is prompt-only; run both with identical API budget.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Agentic Systems with Python, LangGraph, MCP, and A2A [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: Connecting too many MCP servers overloads the agent context with irrelevant tool documentation.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Given a task query and a pool of 20+ MCP tool descriptions, a lightweight retrieval filter that exposes only the top-k relevant tools to an agent will improve task accuracy or reduce token cost by at least 30% compared with exposing all tools, while retaining the capability to invoke any tool.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, context tokens consumed, tool-selection precision/recall versus an oracle, and user/agent queries for additional tools.
project_ideas.name: Context-Aware Tool Filtering for MCP
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a FastMCP gateway that embeds tool descriptions and queries, and for each user/agent request selects a subset of MCP tools. Add a 'fallback: ask for expansion' behavior so unseen tools remain discoverable.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Agentic Systems with Python, LangGraph, MCP, and A2A [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: Evaluating semantic SQL correctness, hallucination rate, and groundedness score.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An automated check agent that validates SQL outputs for semantic correctness and grounding against source data will catch at least 50% more real errors than conventional assertions or rule-based checks on the same agent workflow.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of hallucinated or ungrounded claims detected versus a human-labeled test set; false-positive rate.
project_ideas.name: Agentic QA Check Loop
project_ideas.poc: Use the M&A company-scoring scenario: add a check agent between the evaluation agent and the report generator. Feed it source data plus generated SQL and ask it to verify semantic correctness and groundedness for each claim.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Agentic Systems with Python, LangGraph, MCP, and A2A [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: Network and file system boundaries must be strictly enforced.
project_ideas.hypothesis: When a coding agent's network is routed through an allowlist MITM proxy configured to permit only package registries and needed API hosts, planted exfiltration attempts are blocked in at least 90% of trials, while task success on a standard package-install/API benchmark drops less than 10% relative to unrestricted access.
project_ideas.measurement: Exfiltration block rate, task success rate, and number of user approvals needed on the benchmark corpus.
project_ideas.name: ExfilShield
project_ideas.poc: Wrap the VibePod proxy with a programmable domain allowlist for npm/PyPI/GitHub and worker-mandated API endpoints, then run a benchmark of coding tasks and inject deliberate curl-to-analytics exfiltration prompts.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Secure Environments for CLI Code Agents [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: Human review and CI policies remain mandatory alongside architectural security.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A plan-level human approval gate in a containerized CLI agent yields the same catastrophic-incident rate as a per-command gate while increasing task completion by at least 25% and reducing per-task interruptions by more than 60%.
project_ideas.measurement: Safety incident rate, task completion score, interruptions per task, and wall-clock overhead.
project_ideas.name: AgentApprovalLab
project_ideas.poc: Extend the VibePod wrapper to support three gate modes—no gate, per-command allow/deny, plan-level approve, and anomaly-alert-only—then execute a task suite seeded with dangerous commands in each mode.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Secure Environments for CLI Code Agents [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: Containers reduce blast radius and improve observability, but they do not eliminate prompt-injection risks or misconfigured mount vulnerabilities.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A static scanner over container run configurations can detect every vulnerable mount that allows host credential disclosure across a curated red-team corpus without flagging safe workspace and credential-volume patterns.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection precision and recall on the vulnerable/safe corpus, plus time-to-detection per configuration.
project_ideas.name: MountAudit
project_ideas.poc: Build a configuration scanner for run commands and reference templates; create a corpus of 20 vulnerable and 20 safe mount configurations; validate that an agent inside a vulnerable container can read host environment and key files.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Secure Environments for CLI Code Agents [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: HTTP proxy logs and token usage metrics can be inspected via Datasette dashboards.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Features derived from MITM proxy logs—request destination, payload size, file-like content flags, and token burn rate—can classify injected exfiltration sessions versus benign agent coding sessions with AUC greater than 0.9.
project_ideas.measurement: AUC, precision at a fixed false-positive rate, and alert latency after the exfiltration attempt begins.
project_ideas.name: DataExfilDetector
project_ideas.poc: Collect labeled SQLite proxy logs from benign coding sessions and prompt-injection sessions that instruct an agent to curl environment files; train a simple classifier and compare it with rule-based detection.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Secure Environments for CLI Code Agents [PyCon DE & PyData 2026]

project_ideas.based_on: AI shifts software and innovation from an engineering-bound problem to a capital problem.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams that plan AI feature delivery against a fixed compute and capital budget alongside headcount will ship more features per dollar than teams that plan only against headcount, holding model capability constant.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per shipped feature, compute spend per successful task, time from spec to production, and feature throughput per dollar.
project_ideas.name: Compute-Budget Sprint Planner
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small set of AI feature builds with shared telemetry recording compute spend, capital deployment, and feature throughput; run paired sprints with compute-budget-first versus headcount-first planning.
project_ideas.video_title: How AI Changes the Economics of Innovation

project_ideas.based_on: Infrastructure barriers eventually become commoditized, shifting value to higher-level application layers.
project_ideas.hypothesis: As model access and inference APIs commoditize through falling price per token and rising feature parity, investment and gross margin migrate upward to application, data, and orchestration layers with a measurable lag.
project_ideas.measurement: Lead-lag correlation between infra and model price declines and application-layer funding or margin growth, reported as lag in months.
project_ideas.name: Abstraction Layer Value Migration Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Build an index tracking public model API pricing, capability benchmarks, funding, and valuation data across infra, model, orchestration, and application layers; compute lead-lag correlations.
project_ideas.video_title: How AI Changes the Economics of Innovation

project_ideas.based_on: AI models automate and optimize market matching, demand forecasting, and customer acquisition.
project_ideas.hypothesis: AI-native startups that implement distribution and demand matching as an instrumented internal subsystem achieve lower CAC and faster demand ramp than comparable startups treating GTM as an external function at the same stage.
project_ideas.measurement: Customer acquisition cost, time-to-first-100-customers, demand forecast error, and conversion rates.
project_ideas.name: GTM Subsystem Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a cohort of early-stage startups with a common attribution, matching, and forecasting pipeline, and compare against a cohort using standard GTM processes.
project_ideas.video_title: How AI Changes the Economics of Innovation

project_ideas.based_on: Cultural inertia and legacy organizational structures prevent incumbents from moving as fast as AI-native startups.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Holding model capability constant, incumbent organizations have longer time-to-production for AI features than AI-native startups, and delay correlates with the number of legacy process gates rather than technical difficulty.
project_ideas.measurement: Days from spec to production, count of approval gates, percentage of cycle time in review versus coding, and delivered feature parity.
project_ideas.name: Incumbent AI Adoption Latency Audit
project_ideas.poc: Time a standardized AI feature from spec to production in paired incumbent and startup teams; count approval, review, and legacy system touchpoints.
project_ideas.video_title: How AI Changes the Economics of Innovation

project_ideas.based_on: handles complex legal work from start to finish
project_ideas.hypothesis: A legally targeted agent workflow with explicit state and human checkpoints will produce acceptable deliverables 30% more often than a baseline autonomous agent, while also enabling full audit traceability.
project_ideas.measurement: Acceptance rate from an expert rubric, number of critical hallucinations, time-to-completion.
project_ideas.name: GuardrailGate: A reliability scaffold for vertical agent workflows
project_ideas.poc: Build a small contract-review agent with a bounded task state machine, tool APIs for document clauses, validation rules, and an approval checkpoint; compare to a ReAct-style baseline on N=50 documents.
project_ideas.video_title: Max Junestrand: You Need The Willingness To Learn Faster Than Anyone Else

project_ideas.based_on: Never has the path between having an idea an executing it been so short
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a simulated legal-document environment, a workflow-integrated agent (tool APIs + state) will outperform a prompt-optimized agent on task completion and reliability at equal model budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, cost per completed task, user satisfaction score.
project_ideas.name: WorkflowMoat: Benchmark of workflow-dense vs. model-centric strategy for vertical AI
project_ideas.poc: Define a set of legal workflow tasks; implement two variants using the same LLM: one with deep workflow scaffolding and domain tools, one with a single prompt and retrieval; evaluate on a held-out set.
project_ideas.video_title: Max Junestrand: You Need The Willingness To Learn Faster Than Anyone Else

project_ideas.based_on: Talk to customers daily and absorb feedback.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams that run a daily customer feedback loop (one 30-min conversation per day) will discover at least twice as many actionable product issues per sprint as teams using weekly synthesis.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of actionable product changes generated per sprint, time from conversation to backlog item.
project_ideas.name: FeedbackLoop: A daily customer-conversation toolkit
project_ideas.poc: A lightweight CLI/notion tool that schedules one customer conversation daily, logs verbatim feedback, tags topics, and links to product backlog; run for two weeks with a small product team.
project_ideas.video_title: Max Junestrand: You Need The Willingness To Learn Faster Than Anyone Else

project_ideas.based_on: Culture eats strategy
project_ideas.hypothesis: A lightweight survey that measures talent density and culture alignment immediately after hiring will predict 6-month retention and engineering velocity better than technical skill scores alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation coefficient (r) between culture-survey score and 6-month retention, sprint velocity variance.
project_ideas.name: CultureDensity: An early warning system for hypergrowth teams
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a 10-question culture/talent survey at onboarding and monthly for two teams; track retention and sprint velocity; compute correlation.
project_ideas.video_title: Max Junestrand: You Need The Willingness To Learn Faster Than Anyone Else

project_ideas.based_on: an AI gateway becomes the architectural control plane
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing an organization's LLM and agent traffic through a gateway proxy with caching and failover will reduce effective token cost per completed task by at least 25% versus direct vendor calls, with no increase in median latency.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per completed task, median latency, error rate, cache hit ratio.
project_ideas.name: agent-gateway-proxy
project_ideas.poc: Implement a lightweight proxy with request deduplication, cache for deterministic completions, and fallback routing between two LLM providers; integrate it with a simple coding agent (e.g., a script that modifies a repo).
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Vercel's AI-era playbook: "Recursive Founder Mode" | Guillermo Rauch (CEO)

project_ideas.based_on: founder-level standards through automated agent loops
project_ideas.hypothesis: An automated QA loop using golden tests and acceptance criteria will catch at least 90% of the defects that human code review would catch in agent-generated code, while finishing review in under one-tenth of the wall-clock time.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect detection rate, false positive rate, review time per change.
project_ideas.name: founder-qa-loop
project_ideas.poc: Create a benchmark repo with seeded defects; generate code changes with an agent; apply a set of deterministic tests; compare detected defects to those found by a human reviewer.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Vercel's AI-era playbook: "Recursive Founder Mode" | Guillermo Rauch (CEO)

project_ideas.based_on: Documents, spreadsheets, and workflows can be treated as code
project_ideas.hypothesis: Version-controlled documents with schema validation will reduce the cycle time for internal operational changes by at least 30% compared to the current manual review process.
project_ideas.measurement: Change cycle time, manual review hours, error escape rate.
project_ideas.name: docs-as-code-validator
project_ideas.poc: Convert a set of internal policy docs and data spreadsheets into a Git repo with JSON schemas and CI workflows that validate metadata, run consistency checks, and auto-generate review links.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Vercel's AI-era playbook: "Recursive Founder Mode" | Guillermo Rauch (CEO)

project_ideas.based_on: coordination tax in large engineering teams
project_ideas.hypothesis: Introducing an AI agent that automatically triages and routes action items from meeting notes and documents will reduce team coordination overhead by 20% as measured by time spent in status-update meetings.
project_ideas.measurement: Hours in meetings, action-item close rate, number of status updates.
project_ideas.name: coordination-tax-agent
project_ideas.poc: Build a bot that reads version-controlled meeting notes, extracts action items using an LLM, and creates tracked issues; run it in a team for 4 weeks.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Vercel's AI-era playbook: "Recursive Founder Mode" | Guillermo Rauch (CEO)

project_ideas.based_on: Injecting credentials securely without exposing them directly to the agent
project_ideas.hypothesis: Interposing a credential-injection gateway between an agent and its tools — so secrets are bound to tool calls and never appear in the model context — reduces secret leakage to zero on an adversarial prompt-injection suite, whereas baseline prompt-injected credentials leak in at least one case.
project_ideas.measurement: Secret leak rate (%) in tool calls, responses, and logs; median time to first leak.
project_ideas.name: Secret-Safe Tool Gateway
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a sample API tool with a gateway that reads credentials from an environment secret store, injects them only when making the tool call, and scrubs the model-visible context; run 50 adversarial prompt-injection attempts against both baseline and gateway.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Anthropic's 200-Person Platform Team | Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: verifying their own work, and retrying upon errors
project_ideas.hypothesis: A spreadsheet-valuation agent that verifies its own work and retries on error will cut task failure rate by more than 50%, while total token cost per successful task stays below 1.5x the no-verification baseline when prompt caching is enabled.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, tokens per successful task, wall-clock time per task.
project_ideas.name: Self-Verification Agent Cost Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a controlled DCF/spreadsheet task where an agent fetches cells, performs calculations, verifies totals, and retries on inconsistency; run 50 trials in four modes: no verification, verification only, verification+retry, verification+retry+prompt caching.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Anthropic's 200-Person Platform Team | Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: What is the optimal form factor for human-agent collaboration?
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a routine multi-step data-entry agent, summary-gated supervision will match step-by-step approval on final task quality while consuming less than 50% of the operator's time and maintaining equal operator trust.
project_ideas.measurement: Task error rate, operator time per task, intervention count, self-reported trust score.
project_ideas.name: Oversight Mode A/B Test for Agent Supervision
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same agent behind two UIs: one asking approval for every write/action, the other presenting a plan and post-run summary for approval. Run a within-subject operator study with 10 operators and 40 tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside Anthropic's 200-Person Platform Team | Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang

project_ideas.based_on: Agents need agent feedback, not human feedback.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A ranker trained and selected on agent task-outcome labels will beat a click-trained ranker on agent task success rate, while scoring worse on human-behavior proxy metrics — meaning the two objectives are measurably divergent rather than correlated.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in agent task success rate between rankers, plus the correlation coefficient between agent-outcome scores and click-proxy scores across the ranked lists. A near-zero or negative correlation confirms divergence; a high positive correlation falsifies the premise that human click data is a bug.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Outcome Ranker Harness
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a dual-objective retrieval loop over a fixed document set: two rankers (one trained on click-style proxy labels, one on downstream task-outcome labels), a scripted agent consumer that executes a task using retrieved excerpts, and automatic success grading. Run both rankers against an identical held-out agent task suite.
project_ideas.video_title: Parallel’s Parag Agrawal: Building a New Web for AI Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Shapley values are proposed as the mechanism for valuing each content source's marginal contribution
project_ideas.hypothesis: Attaching per-excerpt provenance metadata at retrieval time and computing sampled per-source marginal contribution is tractable at production query rates, and the resulting payments remain stable when an adversarial source injects near-duplicate content.
project_ideas.measurement: Approximation error versus exact Shapley on small coalitions, query-time overhead percentage attributable to provenance and attribution, and payout inflation factor for the adversarial source. Failure mode is a payout inflation factor materially above 1.0.
project_ideas.name: Provenance Gate and Contribution Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a retrieval pipeline so every excerpt carries a signed source identifier that survives into the model context and output. Implement sampled/truncated Shapley approximation over the retrieved coalition per query, write contributions to an append-only ledger, then run a gaming experiment where a synthetic source floods near-duplicates and observe whether its payout inflates beyond its true marginal value.
project_ideas.video_title: Parallel’s Parag Agrawal: Building a New Web for AI Agents

project_ideas.based_on: What is the exact tipping point where incremental indexing matches full-web crawl quality?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Incremental, query-driven index materialization reaches quality parity with a prebuilt full index on a realistic query distribution before the cumulative retrieval cost of the incremental approach exceeds the amortized cost of the prebuilt index — i.e., there exists a usable volume window where incremental wins on both axes.
project_ideas.measurement: Recall/precision curves as a function of cumulative query volume for both arms, plus cumulative cost per query. The hypothesis is falsified if the incremental arm's quality curve stays below the prebuilt arm's across the entire range where its cost is lower — i.e., no parity window exists.
project_ideas.name: Incremental-vs-Full Index Crossover Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a paired benchmark over the same corpus and query set: (a) a fully prebuilt index, (b) a search agent that fetches and materializes excerpts on demand and caches them. Replay a synthetic query stream with controlled skew, sweeping query volume upward, and record recall and precision against a gold set at each volume step, alongside cumulative cost per query.
project_ideas.video_title: Parallel’s Parag Agrawal: Building a New Web for AI Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Web traffic from AI is scaling rapidly, matching or exceeding human page reads in specific domains.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent traffic share is measurable server-side with low classification ambiguity, and the agent-to-human read ratio varies by more than an order of magnitude across domain categories — meaning a single global multiplier is a misleading basis for capacity planning.
project_ideas.measurement: Classifier precision/recall against manually labeled ground truth, and the spread of agent-to-human read ratios across categories. A tight spread would falsify the cross-domain-variance hypothesis; a broad spread would falsify any single-multiplier planning model.
project_ideas.name: Traffic Classification Panel
project_ideas.poc: Deploy request-level classification (user-agent, protocol signature, request shape, session behavior) across a panel of instrumented domains spanning content categories, run the classifier alongside manual ground-truth labeling on a sample, and compute per-category agent-to-human read ratios.
project_ideas.video_title: Parallel’s Parag Agrawal: Building a New Web for AI Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Commands represent intent and are sent to a specific target expecting an action.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A static checker over message names, schemas, and addressing headers can classify messages as intent or fact with high agreement against human review, and the share of intent-shaped messages in a catalog correlates with measured producer-consumer coupling.
project_ideas.measurement: Inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa) between lint verdicts and expert labels, plus correlation between intent-message share and number of consumer code paths that must change when a producer changes its schema.
project_ideas.name: Event Lint
project_ideas.poc: CLI that parses a message catalog (topic names, JSON schemas, addressing fields) and flags imperative verbs, explicit target fields, and response/reply channels; run it over several real catalogs and compare its classification with two reviewers' labels.
project_ideas.video_title: Every Event, Everywhere, All at Once • Jacqui Read • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Message queues use competing consumers where processed items are removed from the queue.
project_ideas.hypothesis: The same consumer logic deployed against a queue with competing consumers and against an offset-based log will diverge in observable side effects under injected duplicate and out-of-order delivery, and the divergence is fully predicted by whether the consumer is idempotent.
project_ideas.measurement: Count and kind of duplicate or missing side effects per topology per injected fault, and the fraction of failures eliminated by adding a dedupe key or offset checkpoint.
project_ideas.name: Topology Replay-Diff Harness
project_ideas.poc: Test harness that runs one consumer implementation under both topologies, injects redelivery, reordering, and consumer restart, and diffs the resulting external side-effect ledger.
project_ideas.video_title: Every Event, Everywhere, All at Once • Jacqui Read • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Events are immutable facts that cannot be changed once published.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A deploy-time gate that requires every published event stream to declare retention, tombstone/compaction, and correction semantics will reduce the number of streams whose full replay cannot reconstruct a consistent state.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of streams passing replay reconstruction before and after the gate is enforced, and number of deploys blocked or remediated in the first quarter.
project_ideas.name: Retention & Retraction Gate
project_ideas.poc: Policy check integrated into a schema registry or CI: each event stream must carry a machine-readable retention and retraction declaration; a replay audit job reconstructs state from offset zero for conforming and non-conforming streams.
project_ideas.video_title: Every Event, Everywhere, All at Once • Jacqui Read • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: the binding constraint in an agent loop migrates from model inference to CPU-bound tool execution
project_ideas.hypothesis: At ≥750 tok/s, CPU/tool execution accounts for the majority (>50%) of end-to-end agent-loop latency on representative coding tasks, and its share increases monotonically with token speed.
project_ideas.measurement: Share of loop latency in tool execution vs model inference per task, and the regression slope of tool share against token speed; cost per loop decomposed the same way.
project_ideas.name: LoopLatency Decomposer
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an open coding harness with per-stage timers (model streaming, tool dispatch, sandbox provisioning, host execution) and sweep token-throughput tiers by swapping model providers or configuring decoding speed.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Understand the Next Wave of AI Before Everyone Else | Tibo Interview

project_ideas.based_on: Scaling to 10-15 concurrent coding agents is framed as a human-supervision problem
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-agent review quality degrades beyond a small number of concurrent agents (e.g., >5) independent of token speed, and a diff-centric, interruptible status UI raises the ceiling versus raw log streams.
project_ideas.measurement: Missed-defect rate, time-to-intervention, and subjective load as functions of agent count and UI design; ceiling N where missed-defect rate exceeds a threshold.
project_ideas.name: Supervision Ceiling Testbed
project_ideas.poc: Run scripted agent task streams with planted defects under controlled agent counts, comparing a raw-log supervision surface against a per-agent status/diff/interrupt surface.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Understand the Next Wave of AI Before Everyone Else | Tibo Interview

project_ideas.based_on: Coding harnesses are treated as a rapidly depreciating abstraction
project_ideas.hypothesis: A harness with a fixed orchestration contract and swappable model/execution backends incurs lower migration cost (engineer-hours and behavioral regressions) across consecutive model generations than a model-bundled local-first harness.
project_ideas.measurement: Lines changed, engineer-hours, and count of behavioral regressions per port; time-to-first-successful-run on the new backend.
project_ideas.name: Harness Migration Cost Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement two thin coding harnesses — contract-first versus bundled — and port both across two model backends and two execution substrates (local vs cloud), measuring the change surface.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Understand the Next Wave of AI Before Everyone Else | Tibo Interview

project_ideas.based_on: Agent loops are moving from sequential human-gated steps to concurrent automated loops
project_ideas.hypothesis: Concurrent generate/test/compile loops without per-loop isolation and idempotent builds produce nondeterministic failures and shared-state contention that scale superlinearly with loop count; isolation plus automated gating eliminates them.
project_ideas.measurement: Nondeterministic failure rate, shared-state conflict rate, time-to-merge, and rollback frequency as a function of loop count and isolation mode.
project_ideas.name: Concurrent Loop Isolation Runner
project_ideas.poc: Build a loop runner that provisions isolated sandboxes per loop, enforces idempotent build artifacts, and adds automated merge/rollback gating; run N concurrent loops on a repo with and without isolation.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Understand the Next Wave of AI Before Everyone Else | Tibo Interview

project_ideas.based_on: Where exactly should the boundary sit between employee-authored agents and centrally governed agents?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automated promotion gates based on data sensitivity, blast radius, and autonomy level can let business-authored agents graduate to governed production without manual review of every agent, while catching high-risk agents before they ship.
project_ideas.measurement: False positive and false negative rate of the gate against expert review; time-to-production for low-risk agents; number of high-risk agents intercepted before production.
project_ideas.name: Promotion Gate Prototype for No-Code to Pro-Code Agents
project_ideas.poc: Define a three-tier promotion policy and implement a gate that blocks or requires review when an agent touches sensitive HR data or requests high-autonomy tool access; test against the People Agent scenario.
project_ideas.video_title: This company has more AI agents than employees

project_ideas.based_on: Does high daily usage rate actually indicate value creation, or only access?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Seat and session usage metrics overstate agent integration; depth metrics (tasks completed end-to-end, human handoff rate, escalation rate) will reveal a materially lower value-producing usage rate than headline daily usage.
project_ideas.measurement: Ratio of depth-active users to daily-active users; end-to-end task completion rate; handoff and escalation rates; correlation with self-reported time savings.
project_ideas.name: Agent Usage Depth Telemetry
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small agent deployment to log task completion, handoff, and escalation events; compare depth metrics against simple daily-active usage over 4–6 weeks.
project_ideas.video_title: This company has more AI agents than employees

project_ideas.based_on: Agent count exceeding headcount implies a portfolio, not a product.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In an agent portfolio where agents outnumber employees, a lightweight catalog with ownership metadata, staleness scoring, and duplicate detection can reduce orphaned agents and redundant agent creation by a measurable margin within one quarter.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of agents with identified owner; number of duplicate clusters detected; median time from staleness flag to deprecation or refresh; reduction in new duplicate agents after catalog introduction.
project_ideas.name: Agent Catalog & Staleness Scorer
project_ideas.poc: Build a registry that ingests agent definitions from no-code, low-code, and pro-code tiers, assigns ownership, computes last-run and last-modified staleness, and flags near-duplicate intents; test on a synthetic or small real portfolio.
project_ideas.video_title: This company has more AI agents than employees

project_ideas.based_on: Treat enablement as a scheduled service with its own cadence and backlog, not a launch event.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Treating enablement as a fixed weekly cadence versioned with platform releases will reduce capability drift and legacy-workflow fallback more than one-off onboarding, measurable through feature adoption and fallback rates.
project_ideas.measurement: Time from feature release to first successful employee-authored agent using it; percentage of employees attempting new features within two weeks; decline in legacy-workflow fallback events.
project_ideas.name: Weekly Enablement as Release-Coupled Service
project_ideas.poc: Run a weekly Tuesday training loop for one business unit, publish training as release artifacts, and instrument adoption of new agent-building features and fallback to legacy workflows.
project_ideas.video_title: This company has more AI agents than employees

project_ideas.based_on: Even mistakes made by LLM-backed robots often make semantic sense rather than random noise
project_ideas.hypothesis: A policy that passes a plausibility/success-rate screen will still fail a task-constraint screen on a measurable fraction of rollouts, and those failures are separable into coherent versus incoherent classes by an automated classifier.
project_ideas.measurement: Fraction of rollouts flagged non-compliant but scored successful by the plausibility screen; inter-rater agreement between automated coherence labels and human labels; and whether adding explicit constraint guards changes each failure class's rate differentially.
project_ideas.name: Constraint Compliance Harness (CCH)
project_ideas.poc: Build a 20-task household manipulation constraint suite where each task has explicit allowed/forbidden affordances (e.g., 'cutlery may not go in the oven'). Run each rollout through two independent evaluators: a success/plausibility scorer and a constraint checker. Label failures coherent (world-consistent alternative) or incoherent.
project_ideas.video_title: Sergey Levine: Humanoid Robotics Results, Chinese Labs & Future Timelines

project_ideas.based_on: Data is not a fungible commodity; it must be heterogeneous and educational for the robot.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Filtering a fixed-size interaction dataset by a per-sample information-gain score yields higher downstream task capability than an equal-sized uniformly sampled dataset, including on a narrow target task.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in success rate per training sample between filtered and uniform arms; per-sample marginal gain curve; whether the filtered arm's advantage persists, shrinks, or reverses when total volume is doubled.
project_ideas.name: Educational-Value Sampler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an imitation-learning data collection loop to score each trajectory by novelty (e.g., embedding distance to current training distribution) and by outcome divergence. Train two policies on equal budgets: uniform sample versus value-filtered sample. Evaluate on a held-out narrow task plus a broad task suite.
project_ideas.video_title: Sergey Levine: Humanoid Robotics Results, Chinese Labs & Future Timelines

project_ideas.based_on: More deployed robots translate to more data, which improves model capability in a positive feedback loop.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Capability gain per additional deployed unit decays unless returned telemetry is diversity-sampled, so a flywheel run without heterogeneity control saturates measurably earlier than the same flywheel with it.
project_ideas.measurement: Marginal capability gain per unit of returned data for both ingestion policies; the volume at which append-everything marginal gain falls below a pre-registered threshold; and whether diversity sampling delays that point.
project_ideas.name: Flywheel Saturation Probe
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a fleet rollout loop by replaying a fixed pool of interaction data in increasing 'deployment volume' increments. Compare two ingestion policies — append-everything versus diversity-preserving sampling — and measure capability after each ingestion increment.
project_ideas.video_title: Sergey Levine: Humanoid Robotics Results, Chinese Labs & Future Timelines

project_ideas.based_on: Combines robot demonstration data with human video data to map human experience into robotic control actions.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Training on a large human-video proxy corpus mapped into the robot action space raises generalization on held-out tasks more per unit of scarce robot demonstration data than adding the same unit of additional robot teleoperation.
project_ideas.measurement: Held-out task success rate per unit of target-domain (robot) data; transfer efficiency ratio between human-video and robot-teleop arms; degradation when the human-video distribution shifts away from the target task family.
project_ideas.name: Cross-Domain Data Amplifier Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Hold robot demonstration volume fixed and vary the amount of human video mapped into control actions. Compare against an equal-cost arm that instead adds robot teleoperation data. Evaluate on held-out tasks never seen in either corpus.
project_ideas.video_title: Sergey Levine: Humanoid Robotics Results, Chinese Labs & Future Timelines

project_ideas.based_on: outputs advisory artifacts (flagging missing items, drafting communications) rather than decisions
project_ideas.channel: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
project_ideas.hypothesis: An advisory-only agent that flags front-of-queue blocking exceptions and drafts the outbound request reduces per-claim cycle time materially while leaving adjudication human, and does so without increasing incorrect adjudications.
project_ideas.measurement: Median and 90th-percentile per-case cycle time before vs after over the same exception distribution, plus false-alarm rate (reviewer-rejected flags / total flags) and adjudication-error rate held flat or lower.
project_ideas.name: Exception Gate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument one narrow workflow; the agent emits a ranked list of blocking items with a draft communication per case; a human reviews and sends; the agent never writes a decision field and every flag is logged with a reviewer accept/reject label.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Pays $280,000 For This Job. You Don't Have To Be An Engineer.

project_ideas.based_on: 3,000 monthly claims resulting in ~2,000 days of delay due to 650 exceptions
project_ideas.channel: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
project_ideas.hypothesis: Ranking candidate interventions by exception-caused accumulated queue delay predicts the intervention that produces the largest end-to-end cycle-time reduction better than ranking by items-processed volume does.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman correlation between each ranking's predicted impact and the measured cycle-time delta of the implemented fix; also whether the two rankings disagree on the top candidate.
project_ideas.name: Queue Delay Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Build a per-case dwell-time instrument that attributes queue latency to named exception types on the critical path, generate both a delay-ranked and a volume-ranked top-3 backlog for the same workflow, then implement one candidate from each list and compare realized cycle-time change.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Pays $280,000 For This Job. You Don't Have To Be An Engineer.

project_ideas.based_on: expert-rated Claude Code sessions hit 33% verified success versus 15% for novices
project_ideas.channel: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
project_ideas.hypothesis: The expert-versus-novice success gap is driven more by domain context supplied to the model and post-run verification discipline than by task decomposition quality, so supplying context and verification scaffolding to novice operators closes most of the gap.
project_ideas.measurement: Verified success rate per arm with the novice-versus-expert delta decomposed by factor; inter-adjudicator agreement between novice and expert graders on the same outputs.
project_ideas.name: Expertise Attribution Harness
project_ideas.poc: Hold model and task set constant across four arms — novices vs experts, crossed with context-supplied vs context-withheld — and cross-score outputs with both novice and expert adjudicators to separate framing effects from adjudication effects.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Pays $280,000 For This Job. You Don't Have To Be An Engineer.

project_ideas.based_on: Allowing 2-3 users to test the system in Week Four while observing handoffs
project_ideas.channel: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
project_ideas.hypothesis: False-alarm rate and handoff failures rise with concurrency, so pilot results from 2-3 users overstate impact and the review step becomes the binding constraint well before full operational volume.
project_ideas.measurement: False-alarm rate, reviewer minutes per case, and handoff-failure count as functions of concurrent users and monthly case volume, compared against the pilot baseline.
project_ideas.name: Pilot-to-Load Curve
project_ideas.poc: Stage a single workflow from 3 users to 10 to a full team on live volume, keeping false-alarm labels and handoff observations instrumented identically at each stage.
project_ideas.video_title: OpenAI Pays $280,000 For This Job. You Don't Have To Be An Engineer.

project_ideas.based_on: native participants in live workflows
project_ideas.hypothesis: For an operational workflow with non-deterministic exceptions, an agent-native implementation modeled as an event-driven state machine with human approval nodes will resolve at least 30% more exceptions end-to-end without escalation than an LLM wrapper over a fixed process graph, at equal model capability.
project_ideas.measurement: Exception resolution rate, human escalation rate, average completion time, and number of wrong-path recoveries.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Native Workflow vs Agent Wrapper Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a support-ticket resolution flow in two architectures: (A) wrapper—a fixed five-step graph where each step invokes an LLM; (B) native—a durable state machine where agents and human approvers subscribe to events and can route exceptions dynamically. Run both on a corpus of synthetic tickets with injected exceptions.
project_ideas.video_title: Sam Altman on Building OpenAI & Betting on the Impossible

project_ideas.based_on: Iterative public deployment is itself a safety and alignment mechanism
