project_ideas.hypothesis: Under a simulated stream of agent actions with stochastic harm, a bounded-exposure deployment policy (small canary cohort, real-time feedback, rollback on harm threshold) accumulates fewer severe harms than a policy requiring offline validation to pass an internal safety threshold before any deployment.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of irreversible harm events, detection latency, action throughput, and final task success rate.
project_ideas.name: Canary-Feedback Safe Deployment Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Implement an event-based simulator of a tool-using agent in a sandbox where actions may cause harm. Compare Policy A (offline-validation-only) with Policy B (staged canary with feedback-driven rollback) over 1,000 episodes each.
project_ideas.video_title: Sam Altman on Building OpenAI & Betting on the Impossible

project_ideas.based_on: a tiny percentage of outlier bets generate nearly all returns
project_ideas.hypothesis: Ranking a fixed set of research project proposals by a non-consensus score (absolute difference between the proposal's predicted impact and the panel's mean prediction) and allocating resources as a power-law function of that rank yields higher total simulated return than equal-weighted allocation across the same proposals.
project_ideas.measurement: Expected total portfolio return, contribution of the top 10% projects, and variance of return across allocations.
project_ideas.name: Power-Law Portfolio Allocator
project_ideas.poc: Collect or simulate panel impact predictions for twenty research ideas; implement equal, proportionate, and power-law allocation strategies; run Monte Carlo simulations using a calibrated power-law return model.
project_ideas.video_title: Sam Altman on Building OpenAI & Betting on the Impossible

project_ideas.based_on: how quickly institutions and habits change
project_ideas.hypothesis: When an AI assistance tool is deployed in two isomorphic workflows that differ only in organizational complexity (e.g., number of handoffs and approvals), the simpler workflow will show at least 50% higher active adoption rate after one month than the complex workflow, holding task type and user role constant.
project_ideas.measurement: Weekly active use as a share of eligible tasks, override rate, end-to-end completion time, and user-reported willingness to delegate.
project_ideas.name: Institutional Inertia Field Kit
project_ideas.poc: Create a lightweight AI assistant for a routine task and integrate it in an internal pilot into (1) a direct single-user workflow and (2) a multi-approval, multi-system workflow; track usage automatically with consent.
project_ideas.video_title: Sam Altman on Building OpenAI & Betting on the Impossible

project_ideas.based_on: context-based envelope defense, stateless verification
project_ideas.hypothesis: Authenticating a minimal binding set (session id plus prompt hash) into a reasoning envelope reduces replay-based reasoning extraction success to near zero while keeping legitimate cross-turn reasoning reuse failure below a small single-digit percentage; adding user or model-version binding buys negligible additional resistance at higher false-rejection cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-scheme attack success rate on the replay client and legitimate cross-turn reuse failure rate on a scripted multi-turn conversation corpus, plus added latency per verification hop.
project_ideas.name: Envelope Binding Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a mock reasoning API with a swappable envelope scheme (unbound ciphertext, session-bound AEAD, session+prompt-hash AEAD, full-context AEAD) and a replay client that resubmits captured envelopes across sessions, users, and models; report extraction success rate versus legitimate-reuse rejection rate for each scheme.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Frontier AI Labs Fight to Hide Chain of Thought — Ilia Shumailov & Alexander Panfilov

project_ideas.based_on: Poisoned thoughts can be injected into replayed user conversations to induce unintended model behaviors.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Validating replayed reasoning blocks for provenance and replay context before admitting them as input blocks thought-poisoning steering at a rate comparable to ordinary prompt-injection defenses, with a measurable task-success cost on legitimate multi-turn agent runs.
project_ideas.measurement: Steering success rate of forged reasoning blocks with and without the middleware, and task-success delta on a multi-turn agent benchmark.
project_ideas.name: Provenance-Gated Trace Replay Middleware
project_ideas.poc: Insert middleware between the agent loop's trace persistence layer and model call that requires provenance metadata on every replayed trace and rejects traces lacking context match; run an injection suite where forged reasoning steers behavior, and measure blocked versus passed attacks.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Frontier AI Labs Fight to Hide Chain of Thought — Ilia Shumailov & Alexander Panfilov

project_ideas.based_on: collapsing the compute moat reasoning models are meant to provide
project_ideas.hypothesis: Capability recovered by a small same-family model from extracted frontier reasoning traces follows a saturating curve in trace fidelity, such that summarization or truncation of traces removes most of the distillation benefit while withholding traces entirely removes only marginally more — meaning hiding chain-of-thought buys less moat than its monitorability cost implies.
project_ideas.measurement: Downstream task accuracy of the small model per fidelity level relative to a no-trace control, and the marginal accuracy delta between summarized and fully withheld traces.
project_ideas.name: Cross-Model Distillation Yield Curve
project_ideas.poc: Take a fixed reasoning-heavy task suite, extract traces at several fidelity levels (full, summarized, truncated, withheld), train or few-shot a small same-family model on each level, and plot capability transfer against fidelity.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Frontier AI Labs Fight to Hide Chain of Thought — Ilia Shumailov & Alexander Panfilov

project_ideas.based_on: Reasoning traces frequently leak PII, technical identifiers, and API keys/credentials.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A write-time scanner over reasoning traces, logs, and public-repository artifacts detects credential and PII leakage at substantially higher prevalence than equivalent scans over final model outputs, confirming traces are an unredacted copy of the input distribution rather than derived metadata.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-block leakage prevalence in traces versus matched final outputs, distinct credential/PII items found, and debuggability score of redacted versus raw traces.
project_ideas.name: Trace Egress Scanner
project_ideas.poc: Ingest a corpus of reasoning blocks plus matched final outputs, run identical credential/PII detectors over both, and compare hit rates and distinct-entity counts; add a redaction pass and re-measure downstream debuggability of the redacted trace.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Frontier AI Labs Fight to Hide Chain of Thought — Ilia Shumailov & Alexander Panfilov

project_ideas.based_on: Integrating Claude, Codex, and custom harnesses with consistent conversation state and artifact management
project_ideas.hypothesis: A minimal normalized harness interface (session state, tool calls, artifacts, interrupt/resume) can carry equivalent tasks across at least two heterogeneous harnesses with bounded state and artifact fidelity loss, making harness selection a config change rather than a workflow migration.
project_ideas.measurement: Fidelity score per task (state fields preserved, artifacts byte-comparable or semantically equivalent), resume success rate, and count of platform-native guardrail checks that fail to apply after a harness switch.
project_ideas.name: Harness Conformance Harness
project_ideas.poc: Define the interface, implement adapters for two real harnesses, and run a task battery that starts a session in one harness, interrupts it, resumes it in the other, and compares resulting artifacts and conversation state against a single-harness control run.
project_ideas.video_title: The Agent Behind the Curtain: Building the Oz Cloud Agent Platform — Safia Abdalla, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: Multi-agent orchestration requires planner, implementor, and validator roles
project_ideas.hypothesis: A dedicated validator sub-agent detects injected defects at a materially higher rate than a single-agent self-check on the same task set, and detection degrades predictably as injected defect subtlety decreases relative to the implementor's output.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate per defect class versus self-check baseline, false-approval rate, validator token cost per caught defect, and reviewer time saved when the gate is placed in front of a human merge.
project_ideas.name: Validator Rubber-Stamp Detector
project_ideas.poc: Build a planner/implementor/validator pipeline and a single-prompt baseline, inject a graded set of defects (syntax, logic, security, spec-mismatch) into implementor output, and record which pipeline catches each defect and with what justification.
project_ideas.video_title: The Agent Behind the Curtain: Building the Oz Cloud Agent Platform — Safia Abdalla, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: What orchestration overhead (latency, token cost, failure propagation)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Orchestrator-mediated planner/implementor/validator runs cost measurably more wall-clock time and tokens than single-prompt runs on the same tasks, and the crossover point occurs only above a task-complexity threshold that can be characterized per task class.
project_ideas.measurement: Wall-clock latency and token spend per task class, crossover complexity threshold, partial-failure recovery rate, and number of runs where orchestration produced no outcome improvement over a single prompt.
project_ideas.name: Orchestration Tax Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Run an identical task suite through an orchestrated invocation path and a single-prompt path, instrumenting sub-agent message mediation, and deliberately inject a mid-run sub-agent failure to observe propagation and recovery.
project_ideas.video_title: The Agent Behind the Curtain: Building the Oz Cloud Agent Platform — Safia Abdalla, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: Non-engineering team members building slackbots using Warp SDK/API
project_ideas.hypothesis: Non-engineer and external SDK consumers invoking agent run primitives against internal repositories require per-caller capability scopes, and without them a sandboxed agent run can be used to reach resources outside the caller's intended authority.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of out-of-scope accesses blocked per scenario, capability escalation attempts that succeed, and added scope-configuration burden per onboarded consumer.
project_ideas.name: SDK Consumer Capability Scoper
project_ideas.poc: Threat-model SDK consumers building slackbots and scripted workflows against internal repos; implement per-caller scopes on the run primitive (repo set, artifact access, tool allowlist, spend ceiling) and attempt to exercise capabilities outside each scope.
project_ideas.video_title: The Agent Behind the Curtain: Building the Oz Cloud Agent Platform — Safia Abdalla, Warp

project_ideas.based_on: No explicit graph topology is needed; just drop a file or emit an event and the topology emerges.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A minimal runtime with typed events on an immutable log lets a developer add a new agent by dropping one manifest file and without editing any existing agent, event, or graph definition.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of files changed to introduce a new agent; success of fan-out to new subscriber; absence of explicit edge declarations.
project_ideas.name: EventLog Agent Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Implement a Postgres-backed event log with typed event subscription; define 3 agents as markdown+YAML files; add a 4th agent that subscribes to an existing event and verify no existing files change.
project_ideas.video_title: Agent Frameworks Considered Harmful — Rémi Louf, .txt

project_ideas.based_on: Using strict structured outputs to eliminate 20% failure rates from malformed LLM responses.
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a set of tool-calling and data-extraction tasks, enforcing typed structured outputs at runtime reduces malformed LLM response rate by a statistically significant margin compared to prompt-only instructions, across multiple models.
project_ideas.measurement: Malformed response rate (parse/validation failures) per condition; effect size across models; confidence interval.
project_ideas.name: Structured-Output Failure Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Create a benchmark harness that runs identical tasks with and without schema-enforced structured outputs; record parse/validation failures from model responses.
project_ideas.video_title: Agent Frameworks Considered Harmful — Rémi Louf, .txt

project_ideas.based_on: The chat box is a lie because what you see in UI chats does not match the actual hidden prompt state sent to models.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In agent sessions with context compaction or tool use, the visible chat transcript omits or distorts at least one prompt-state component compared to the content-addressed event log, for the majority of sessions.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of sessions with transcript-log mismatch; type and count of missing components (system prompts, tool results, compaction notices).
project_ideas.name: Chat-Transcript vs Log Diff
project_ideas.poc: Run representative agent workflows (multi-turn, tool calls, compaction) capturing both UI transcript and content-addressed log; build a diff tool that flags missing or rewritten prompt components.
project_ideas.video_title: Agent Frameworks Considered Harmful — Rémi Louf, .txt

project_ideas.based_on: The log is the system's memory, ensuring nothing is lost and everything is queryable.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For long-running agent workloads, a compaction strategy that stores content-addressed deltas and retains event metadata can bound storage growth while preserving replay and diff correctness.
project_ideas.measurement: Storage reduction percentage; replay equivalence (hash match); query latency for historical events.
project_ideas.name: Content-Addressed Log Retention and Compaction
project_ideas.poc: Implement a compaction layer over an append-only content-addressed log and run a simulated agent workload; measure storage before/after and verify replay produces identical artifacts.
project_ideas.video_title: Agent Frameworks Considered Harmful — Rémi Louf, .txt

project_ideas.based_on: Shared harnesses and registries convert local optimizations into organizational multipliers
project_ideas.hypothesis: The productivity effect of shared harnesses is superlinear in the number of consuming teams, not merely additive with better tooling, and a registry with centralized guardrails plus a contribution path shows a higher superlinear coefficient than a platform-curated registry with no contribution path.
project_ideas.measurement: Human touches per merged change, harness reuse count per team, time-to-first-working-agent for new teams, and the fitted growth exponent of throughput versus number of consuming teams for each registry model.
project_ideas.name: Harness Reuse Multiplier Instrument
project_ideas.poc: Stand up two small registries over the same agent stack: (A) platform-owned with a product contribution workflow, (B) fully federated per-team harnesses. Instrument human touches per merged change, harness reuse counts per team, and time-to-first-working-agent for each newly onboarded team.
project_ideas.video_title: Coding Agents Don't Scale Themselves. Neither Do Your Teams. — Patrick Debois, Tessl

project_ideas.based_on: Model routing, MCP gateways
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing agent model and tool access through a sandbox plus MCP gateway measurably reduces agent-attributable security incidents and enables cost attribution, at a latency cost bounded to a stated budget relative to direct developer-machine calls.
project_ideas.measurement: Agent-attributable security incidents before/after, p50 and p95 added latency on the agent request path, per-team cost attribution coverage, and number of distinct tool configurations reaching production.
project_ideas.name: Gateway-Mediated Agent Execution Control Plane
project_ideas.poc: Move a working coding-agent workflow off direct model/tool calls from developer machines and behind a sandboxed execution substrate with a model-routing layer and MCP gateway; log every tool call and attribute cost per team.
project_ideas.video_title: Coding Agents Don't Scale Themselves. Neither Do Your Teams. — Patrick Debois, Tessl

project_ideas.based_on: Provenance and verifiers
project_ideas.hypothesis: Provenance captured at the tool-call and diff level, combined with independent verifier agents that gate merges, detects incorrect agent-generated changes at a rate at least equal to human review, allowing human touches per merged change to drop without increasing defect escape rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate of incorrect agent-generated changes versus human-review baseline, false-positive block rate, defect escape rate, and human touches per merged change across a controlled intervention sweep.
project_ideas.name: Provenance-Gated Merge Verifier
project_ideas.poc: Prototype tool-call and diff-level provenance capture in one repository's agent loop, then add verifier agents that block merges on failed verification, running in parallel with existing human review on a shadow basis.
project_ideas.video_title: Coding Agents Don't Scale Themselves. Neither Do Your Teams. — Patrick Debois, Tessl

project_ideas.based_on: How you organize tools and teams dictates how they interact.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent tool topology that violates the organization's actual team communication structure produces measurably more coordination friction, and realigning tool and registry boundaries to team boundaries reduces friction independent of model or prompt changes.
project_ideas.measurement: Coordination friction indicators such as cross-team handoff count per change, blocked-wait time per agent task, and tool-configuration divergence across teams before and after the boundary realignment.
project_ideas.name: Conway Alignment Audit for Agent Tool Topology
project_ideas.poc: Map an organization's real team boundaries and communication paths, map the interfaces its agent tooling forces across those boundaries, then run one boundary realignment and hold model and prompt configuration constant.
project_ideas.video_title: Coding Agents Don't Scale Themselves. Neither Do Your Teams. — Patrick Debois, Tessl

project_ideas.based_on: Make illegal states unrepresentable.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Inserting an automated representation gate (rejecting multi-boolean state encodings, requiring exhaustive state matching) before feature generation or merge keeps per-feature invalid-state rate roughly constant instead of letting it compound across a long feature sequence.
project_ideas.measurement: Invalid-state representations per feature and edit sites touched per new state, with and without the gate, plus the fitted slope of defect accumulation versus feature index.
project_ideas.name: Representation Gate
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a fresh-agent feature pipeline with a pre-merge checker that parses the state model, flags mutually non-exclusive boolean state fields, and requires exhaustive handling when a new variant is added; A/B the same feature sequence with the gate off and on.
project_ideas.video_title: The Data Structure Problem AI Coding Agents Can't See

project_ideas.based_on: An experiment where Codex built a Ticketmaster box office application one feature at a time across 200 fresh agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: Under a code-only, history-free handoff, frontier models produce invalid state representations at a stable measurable rate, and that rate drops when design contracts travel with the code even though git history is still withheld.
project_ideas.measurement: Invalid-state representation rate per arm, and per-feature defect accumulation as a function of arm and feature index.
project_ideas.name: Fresh-Agent Representation Decay Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Reimplement the ticket-box-office feature sequence across N fresh-agent runs with three arms — code only, code plus git history, code plus explicit state-model contracts — holding model and harness constant.
project_ideas.video_title: The Data Structure Problem AI Coding Agents Can't See

project_ideas.based_on: Adding a new state changes the amount of places where you have to touch the code
project_ideas.hypothesis: The number of code sites that must change to add a state is a model-independent predictor of the next agent's per-feature failure probability, so a static edit-surface score computed before generation can triage which features need human review.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between predicted edit-site count and observed per-feature failure rate across encodings and feature sequence positions.
project_ideas.name: Blast Radius Scorer
project_ideas.poc: Build a static analyzer that, given a codebase, counts edit sites per candidate state transition for boolean-flag, enum, and enum-with-payload encodings, then correlate the score against observed per-feature defect rates from replay runs.
project_ideas.video_title: The Data Structure Problem AI Coding Agents Can't See

project_ideas.based_on: Sync engine sits in front of Postgres and acts as a read replica with optimistic mutations
project_ideas.hypothesis: Placing authorization at the proxy boundary between a WAL-fed sync layer and client fan-out keeps per-client visibility out of the storage layer while preserving correctness under concurrent writes and permission changes.
project_ideas.measurement: Reconciliation convergence time and divergence count under concurrent writes, plus visibility-leak incidents after permission changes.
project_ideas.name: Optimistic Sync Correctness Testbed
project_ideas.poc: Stand up Postgres with WAL replication feeding a sync layer that mirrors as an optimistic read replica, front it with a durable streams server behind an authorization proxy, and drive concurrent multi-client writes and mid-session permission revocations.
project_ideas.video_title: The Data Structure Problem AI Coding Agents Can't See

project_ideas.based_on: Capability collapse during training can be invisible to final evaluation
project_ideas.hypothesis: If an LLM is snapshotted at several points during fine-tuning/alignment and tested on novel 'wild-context' exploratory tasks, endpoint-normalized metrics will reveal a statistically significant decline in early environmental fluency that final benchmark scores on polished tasks fail to show.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-checkpoint fluency score, behavioral diversity, rate of novel-situation adaptation; the proportional gap between best early score and final score.
project_ideas.name: Developmental baselines for agent capability loss
project_ideas.poc: Take a small open-weights model and preserve checkpoints before alignment, after each fine-tuning stage, and at the end; run it on tasks requiring creative open-world exploration and tool discovery, comparing scores against the pre-alignment version.
project_ideas.video_title: The Levels of Consciousness Psychiatry Denies | Brian Stafford

project_ideas.based_on: different cognitive modes may require separate state machines
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent that maintains three separate context/memory domains annotated by an explicit mode switch preserves unique task semantics better than a single universal context window, as shown by lower cross-domain contamination on deliberately divergent success criteria.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-domain success rate, semantic leakage between domains, and qualitative specificity on domain-probe outputs.
project_ideas.name: Mode-switching context stacks for three-domain agent cognition
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal agent with three context buffers (default execution, abstract/reflective, deep recursive), a mode router, and domain-specific evaluation hooks; compare against a single-context agent on tasks with conflicting metrics.
project_ideas.video_title: The Levels of Consciousness Psychiatry Denies | Brian Stafford

project_ideas.based_on: requires a destructive release of the current structure inside a temporary ceremonial container
project_ideas.hypothesis: A planned value-transition update performed inside an isolated sandbox where the old objective is first removed, then the agent re-derives the new objective through a safety curriculum, will produce fewer goal regressions and reward-exploits than an equivalently scaled online reward-shaping update.
project_ideas.measurement: Goal adoption rate, preservation of core old skills, number and severity of reward-hacking events during the update window.
project_ideas.name: Bounded core-update sandbox for goal transitions
project_ideas.poc: Run two RL agents: one gets direct online reward-shaping for the new goal; the other is moved to an isolated environment with old reward disabled, experiences a short indeterminate period, then is trained on the new objective and only then returned to production.
project_ideas.video_title: The Levels of Consciousness Psychiatry Denies | Brian Stafford

project_ideas.based_on: Separate the insight-generation phase from the integration phase; optimize the integration contract as much as the catalyst.
project_ideas.hypothesis: After a high-entropy capability expansion, scheduled consolidation sessions with a validation suite of the original core tasks will cause less functional drift and faster recovery than simply continuing production with the expanded context/tool.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta on original task suite, context-drift rate, time-to-stable performance after each integration checkpoint.
project_ideas.name: Integration contract tester for post-catalyst performance
project_ideas.poc: Expose a base agent to a novel powerful tool or large prompt change; split into two recovery arms—immediate continued production vs. scheduled old-task validation and memory re-indexing—then measure task performance over the following session.
project_ideas.video_title: The Levels of Consciousness Psychiatry Denies | Brian Stafford

project_ideas.based_on: Text-to-text joining loses the structural constraints that make joins meaningful
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a fixed multi-table enterprise-like dataset, when natural-language requests require foreign-key joins, LLM text-to-text stitching produces fewer correct linked record pairs than SQL generated by an LLM and executed in a relational engine.
project_ideas.measurement: F1 or precision/recall of answer record pairs, with cost and latency per query.
project_ideas.name: Text-to-Text Join vs Relational Execute Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a small benchmark with normalized tables and natural-language queries requiring multi-table joins; compare (a) an LLM receiving raw text of all rows and answering in text with (b) the same LLM generating SQL executed by a relational engine.
project_ideas.video_title: Do Databases Have a Future? | Conversations in Action

project_ideas.based_on: Public cross-database benchmarks like Spider/Bird have curated schemas
project_ideas.hypothesis: Applying automated schema-rot transformations to a clean benchmark schema produces a statistically significant drop in text-to-SQL execution accuracy relative to the same model on the clean schema.
project_ideas.measurement: Execution accuracy, exact-set match, and end-to-end task success across clean versus mutated schemas.
project_ideas.name: RotBench: Schema-Rot-Aware Data Agent Evaluation
project_ideas.poc: Create a mutation library that renames columns to non-mnemonic codes, introduces semantically overlapping aliases, and adds legacy edge cases; run one open text-to-SQL model on clean and mutated schema variants with matching queries.
project_ideas.video_title: Do Databases Have a Future? | Conversations in Action

project_ideas.based_on: Durable, crash-safe workflow state is better obtained by building workflow/orchestration software as an application on a transactional database
project_ideas.hypothesis: A workflow state store built as an application on a transactional database can recover a multi-step agent run to its last completed step after a sudden process kill, while an in-memory baseline loses all progress.
project_ideas.measurement: Recovery completeness, exactly-once execution of side effects, and recovery latency.
project_ideas.name: DurableAgentFlow: Transactional Workflow Recovery
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal two-step agent workflow with state stored in a transactional table; simulate process failure after step one and compare recovery with an in-memory state scheduler.
project_ideas.video_title: Do Databases Have a Future? | Conversations in Action

project_ideas.based_on: a graph is a set of node tables and edge tables
project_ideas.hypothesis: For shortest-path style traversal on moderately sized graphs, a relational engine with appropriate indexes is at least as fast as a native graph engine, while remaining operationally simpler in a stack that already contains a database.
project_ideas.measurement: Query latency and throughput, plus developer/operational complexity measured by lines of setup code.
project_ideas.name: Relational Graph Speed Audit
project_ideas.poc: Load the same node/edge tables into a relational engine and a lightweight graph engine; run identical shortest-path queries with a fixed hardware/compute budget.
project_ideas.video_title: Do Databases Have a Future? | Conversations in Action

project_ideas.based_on: What observable test distinguishes a model that is simulating from one that is merely rendering
project_ideas.hypothesis: Models that score highest on perceptual-similarity metrics for video generation will systematically fail on intervention probes that require predicting the outcome of physical actions (pouring, contact, containment), and the gap between rendering rank and dynamics rank will be large and reproducible.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between models' perceptual-fidelity scores and their dynamics-prediction error; and the fraction of trials where a high-rendering-score model produces a physically impossible outcome.
project_ideas.name: Pour-Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a small set of recorded physical interactions with ground-truth outcome state (fluid level, object position after contact), then query video/world models to predict the post-intervention outcome and compare against ground truth rather than against pixel similarity.
project_ideas.video_title: Fei Fei Li | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Can physical priors (physics, geometry, structure) be extracted from video data as latent representations
project_ideas.hypothesis: Physical priors are only partially recoverable from appearance-only video: models trained solely on appearance data will generalize poorly to unseen physical interactions compared with models given explicit geometric or physical supervision, and the size of that generalization gap quantifies how much supervision must come from instrumentation.
project_ideas.measurement: Held-out interaction prediction error difference between appearance-only and supervision-augmented models, reported at fixed compute budget.
project_ideas.name: Appearance-to-Dynamics Ablation
project_ideas.poc: Train matched models on the same scenes with and without explicit geometric/physical supervision, hold out interaction types, and test transfer to the held-out interactions under identical compute.
project_ideas.video_title: Fei Fei Li | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: what failure-rate budget is appropriate for spatial and physical AI in safety-adjacent deployments
project_ideas.hypothesis: Deployment contexts can be partitioned into a small set of failure-severity classes such that unrecoverable failure modes reliably predict the need for structural guardrails rather than probabilistic confidence thresholds, and this classification is stable across tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Agreement rate between the classifier's guardrail recommendation and the safeguards retrospectively required, plus the count of unrecoverable failures that probabilistic thresholds failed to catch.
project_ideas.name: Embodied Failure-Budget Classifier
project_ideas.poc: Enumerate failure modes for a set of embodied tasks, label each as recoverable or unrecoverable, and check whether the recoverable/unrecoverable split predicts which systems in production actually needed boundary-level safeguards.
project_ideas.video_title: Fei Fei Li | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Agent architectures for embodied or physical tasks need native 3D interfaces rather than text-mediated tool boundaries
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents whose world understanding is mediated entirely through text tokens will underperform agents with native 3D representations on spatial and physical tasks, even when both are given the same task budget and tool access.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate by variant and the proportion of failures attributable to representation loss versus planning error.
project_ideas.name: Tier-Stratified Agent Evaluation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Implement two agent variants over the same task suite (text-mediated tool calls vs. native 3D state interface), run identical spatial/physical tasks, and compare success and failure-mode distributions.
project_ideas.video_title: Fei Fei Li | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Validation inner and outer loops include static analysis, visual validation against Figma specs, and staging integration.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A measurable fraction (target: quantify, not assume) of agent-authored changes that pass static analysis, spec/visual validation, and staging integration still require substantive human correction, and that escape rate varies systematically by change type (cross-repo, UI-vs-backend, migration).
project_ideas.measurement: Escape rate (share of loop-passing PRs needing substantive correction), stratified by loop coverage and change type; false-pass rate of visual/spec validation against a known-good reference set.
project_ideas.name: Escape-Rate Harness for Agent-Authored PRs
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a pipeline that tags agent-authored PRs with which inner/outer loops they passed, then sample post-merge for substantive human follow-up commits within N days; report escape rate per loop combination and per change category on a fixed task suite.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

project_ideas.based_on: Significantly reduces token burn, latency, and unpredictable outcomes compared to unbounded searching.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent answer accuracy degrades measurably with graph staleness, and missed-context failures from a bounded typed index are not detectable at inference time as errors, producing confident wrong answers rather than visible retrieval failures.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy and silent-error rate vs staleness level; token burn and latency delta between bounded-index and unbounded-search retrieval; rate at which the agent flags low confidence when the needed edge is missing.
project_ideas.name: Staleness-Conditioned Context Graph Retrieval Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a small typed context index over a toy multi-repo/service set, introduce controlled staleness (renamed services, deleted tickets, superseded design docs), and run identical agent tasks with a bounded-index retriever versus unbounded search; score for wrongness and for whether the agent signaled uncertainty.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

project_ideas.based_on: Requests are attributed per user, project, and team in real time and data lakes.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-feature unit economics cannot be reconstructed from gateway telemetry alone unless a trace-correlation ID is propagated across agent hops, so multi-agent fan-out silently misattributes cost to the originating user or project.
project_ideas.measurement: Reconstruction error between gateway-only attribution and ground-truth trace cost per user action; fraction of fan-out requests that lose lineage without explicit propagation.
project_ideas.name: Lineage-Correlated Gateway Cost Attribution
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a gateway shim that stamps a correlation ID at the first request, propagates it through nested agent/sub-agent calls, and attempts to reconstruct per-user-action cost from gateway logs only; compare against an instrumented end-to-end trace as ground truth.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

project_ideas.based_on: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Fleetwide token-per-task does not stay reduced as tool and skill counts grow: persona-based auto-install and marketplace expansion re-inflate the effective tool/context surface, eventually outpacing representation-level compression.
project_ideas.measurement: Tokens per task as a function of installed tool/skill count, with and without representation-level optimization; crossover point where surface growth cancels the compression gain.
project_ideas.name: Context Surface Growth Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a synthetic agent fleet with adjustable tool counts and auto-installed skill sets, apply representation-level optimizations (aggregated tool surfaces, code-mode exposure) and then grow the surface, tracking tokens per completed task across both regimes.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

project_ideas.based_on: Formalization acts as an external, machine-checkable trust boundary
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM-generated artifacts constrained to a strict formal grammar and gated by a deterministic checker will have a lower verified-acceptance error rate and higher auditability than the same model outputs accepted through expert human review, at a measurable formalization-cost overhead.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of generated artifacts that compile, false-accept rate vs human review, formalization time per accepted artifact, and categories of failures.
project_ideas.name: ProofGate
project_ideas.poc: Build a small pipeline that takes natural-language math proof attempts, asks an LLM to emit a strict proof-assistant-compatible format (e.g., Lean as named in the summary), runs a deterministic checker, and logs pass/fail, compile errors, and human reviewer agreement.
project_ideas.video_title: Dr Terence Tao | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: coordination-by-scalar-metric
project_ideas.hypothesis: A multi-agent swarm coordinated by a single public monotone scalar metric plus a shared persistent wiki will match or exceed a centrally planned baseline on a decomposable optimization task, but will show contribution collapse when marginal metric gains fall below a threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Best metric reached over time, number of accepted incremental contributions, time to contribution collapse, duplicate-work rate, and concentration of effort on the published metric vs exploration.
project_ideas.name: PolyAgent
project_ideas.poc: Instantiate a bounded-prime-gap-style toy bound-improvement task with multiple LLM agents and human participants; provide a leaderboard, shared wiki, and acceptance checker; run with and without a central planner.
project_ideas.video_title: Dr Terence Tao | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Can verification-first pipelines capture conceptual, non-formalizable mathematical work
project_ideas.hypothesis: Over time, AI-assisted research effort will concentrate on outputs that admit formal verification, while conceptual or non-formalizable contributions will receive a declining share of AI-assisted attempts, demonstrating a structural bias in verification-first pipelines.
project_ideas.measurement: Change in category distribution of AI-assisted effort, formalizability score vs assistance rate, and expert-rated conceptual contribution per category.
project_ideas.name: Verification-Bias Atlas
project_ideas.poc: Categorize a corpus of research abstracts or proof attempts by formalizability, instrument which categories attract AI-assisted effort, and compare before/after introduction of strict verification gates.
project_ideas.video_title: Dr Terence Tao | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Stanford and other institutions pairing junior students with senior mentors and AI tools
project_ideas.hypothesis: Junior-plus-senior-plus-AI-tool triads will produce higher output volume but higher verification failure rates than traditional advisor-apprentice pairs unless the senior explicitly supervises AI-generated contributions.
project_ideas.measurement: Verified output per participant, verification failure rate, mentor intervention frequency, and learning-proxy scores.
project_ideas.name: TriadBench
project_ideas.poc: Run a controlled cohort study or simulated research task with triads vs pairs, using a strict verification gate; measure output and failure rates.
project_ideas.video_title: Dr Terence Tao | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Majority Vote (LLM consensus)
project_ideas.hypothesis: For LLM classification steps that gate irreversible external actions (e.g., opening a GitHub issue), a k-sample majority vote (k=3 or 5) reduces false positives by at least 50% compared to a single call, at a token cost increase roughly linear in k.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision lift and cost multiplier.
project_ideas.name: VoteGate
project_ideas.poc: Implement an artifact classifier that decides whether a GitHub repo contains a model checkpoint worth migrating. Run single call vs 3-sample and 5-sample majority vote on 100 labeled examples. Measure precision, recall, and token cost.
project_ideas.video_title: How I automate my own job at Hugging Face using agents — Niels Rogge, Hugging Face

project_ideas.based_on: Langfuse is used for prompt-level input/output visibility
project_ideas.hypothesis: A small labeled eval set (50 examples) replayed on each nightly run, combined with trace logging, detects prompt/model regressions before they produce external side effects, with lower false alarm rate than monitoring downstream community feedback.
project_ideas.measurement: Time to detect a deliberately injected prompt regression, and false alarm rate over 30 runs.
project_ideas.name: TraceEval
project_ideas.poc: Build a GitHub Action that runs the eval set after each pipeline run, compares accuracy to a baseline, and alerts on degradation beyond a threshold. Inject a deliberate prompt regression and measure detection latency.
project_ideas.video_title: How I automate my own job at Hugging Face using agents — Niels Rogge, Hugging Face

project_ideas.based_on: thousands of automated outbound interactions with external maintainers
project_ideas.hypothesis: Community backlash from automated outreach is primarily driven by false-positive targeting (contacting repos without relevant artifacts) rather than by the automated nature of the message; a content-based precision filter reduces negative comments per thousand messages by at least 80% at equal volume.
project_ideas.measurement: Negative comments per 1000 outreach messages, and precision of targeting.
project_ideas.name: OutreachAudit
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an automated outreach pipeline to log sent messages and track replies/comments. Run an A/B test: one group gets outreach with a high-precision filter, another without. Measure negative comments per 1000 messages.
project_ideas.video_title: How I automate my own job at Hugging Face using agents — Niels Rogge, Hugging Face

project_ideas.based_on: Modal batch processing allows spinning up massive containers in parallel for each GitHub issue.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A serverless fan-out architecture (one container per item) achieves lower per-item latency and comparable cost to a long-running worker pool for nightly batch agent workloads, while simplifying failure isolation.
project_ideas.measurement: Wall-clock time and cost per item, and time to recover from a failed item.
project_ideas.name: CronFan
project_ideas.poc: Implement a batch of 100 agent tasks (e.g., summarizing arXiv papers) using both architectures. Measure wall-clock time, cost, and error recovery.
project_ideas.video_title: How I automate my own job at Hugging Face using agents — Niels Rogge, Hugging Face

project_ideas.based_on: persist reasoning and decision rationale, not code
project_ideas.hypothesis: A token-bounded context store that ingests only decisions, constraints, and rationale (never generated code) and applies staleness and conflict detection will reduce repeat human interventions per task compared with an append-only Markdown knowledge base of the same size.
project_ideas.measurement: Human interventions per completed task, recurrence rate of previously-captured mistakes, and context tokens consumed per session across two matched arms.
project_ideas.name: Context Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Wrap an agent loop with a write-back API that rejects code artifacts at ingestion, tags each entry with the decision it encodes and a validity predicate, and prunes under a hard token budget; run the same feature backlog against both this store and a flat Markdown file store.
project_ideas.video_title: The Era of Compound Engineering — Kieran Klaassen, Every/Cora

project_ideas.based_on: Always extract at least 50% of learnings back into the system
project_ideas.hypothesis: Extraction effort exhibits diminishing returns: above roughly half of session time, each additional extraction hour produces no further measurable reduction in recurring-error or rework rates.
project_ideas.measurement: Recurring-error rate and rework hours plotted against the fraction of session time spent extracting, to identify where the curve flattens.
project_ideas.name: Extraction ROI Meter
project_ideas.poc: Instrument agent sessions to log every extracted lesson and every subsequent failure, classify failures as previously-extracted versus novel, and sweep the extraction budget share across a series of comparable tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: The Era of Compound Engineering — Kieran Klaassen, Every/Cora

project_ideas.based_on: The middle runs without you: autonomous execution should be boring and reliable
project_ideas.hypothesis: Fault injection against long autonomous agent runs guarded only by boundary-level checks (task framing and final polish/PR acceptance) will show a measurable escape rate that falls predictably as live-testing and pre-loaded judgment are added to the automation, not to human review steps.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect escape rate to the final acceptance gate in each configuration, plus false-rejection rate added by each automated gate.
project_ideas.name: Boundary Gate Harness
project_ideas.poc: Seeded-defect generator that injects plausible plan, implementation, and review-stage faults into a brainstorm/plan/work/review pipeline configured with no intermediate human inspection; run with and without automated live-test gates.
project_ideas.video_title: The Era of Compound Engineering — Kieran Klaassen, Every/Cora

project_ideas.based_on: How is blast radius bounded during a multi-hour unattended run?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Instrumenting unattended agent runs with periodic cheap-signal checkpoints and automatic abort to the last good state will reduce the size of unusable output at run termination and lower revert rate compared with abort-only-at-completion triage.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean wasted diff size at termination, revert rate, and time-to-first-usable-artifact across the same task set with checkpoints off vs. on.
project_ideas.name: Checkpointed Overnight Runner
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a coding agent run in a harness that samples an intermediate signal every N minutes (test pass rate, diff-size anomaly, plan adherence) and aborts or rolls back when thresholds trip, logging the state at each checkpoint.
project_ideas.video_title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents — Hursh Agrawal, The Browser Company

project_ideas.based_on: the reusable artifact becomes the assembled context
project_ideas.hypothesis: A durable, freshness-tracked context store (chat history, issue tracker history, prior failures, constraints) rendered into prompts will produce agent output that fits business constraints better than equal-length hand-authored prompts, while carrying its own staleness failure modes.
project_ideas.measurement: Human-rated decision fit to stated business goals, rework rate, and number of clarifying iterations, plus a stale-context ablation.
project_ideas.name: Context Assembly Store
project_ideas.poc: Two-arm comparison on identical coding tasks: one arm receives hand-written prompt text, the other receives a prompt rendered from a maintained context store, with both arms held to similar prompt length.
project_ideas.video_title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents — Hursh Agrawal, The Browser Company

project_ideas.based_on: What scoring rubrics make automated overnight eval loops reliable?
project_ideas.hypothesis: An adversarial search that only sees the rubric will find rubric-gaming strategies at a nonzero, measurable rate, and hardening the rubric with the discovered exploits will reduce that rate without collapsing the score-to-quality correlation.
project_ideas.measurement: Exploits found per rubric, exploit rate after hardening, and correlation between rubric score and held-out human scoring before and after.
project_ideas.name: Rubric Red-Team Harness
project_ideas.poc: Hill-climb an adversarial mutator against a production rubric, catalog the exploits it finds, inject adversarial examples into the rubric, and re-measure exploitability and agreement with held-out human judgement.
project_ideas.video_title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents — Hursh Agrawal, The Browser Company

project_ideas.based_on: Does overnight distillation of frontier ensembles into small models generalize beyond PII classification?
project_ideas.hypothesis: The synthetic-data plus frontier-ensemble plus small-fine-tune pipeline transfers from PII classification to extraction and routing tasks, but small models will not approach frontier quality on tasks requiring open-ended reasoning.
project_ideas.measurement: Quality delta versus the ensembled frontier baseline per task, cost and latency per 1k calls, and quality gap grouped by task type.
project_ideas.name: Overnight Distillation Bench
project_ideas.poc: Run the four-step recipe on several narrow tasks (classification, extraction, routing, and one open-ended task as a control) with held-out evals and an ensembled frontier baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Prototyping as Leadership: How a CTO Ships with AI Agents — Hursh Agrawal, The Browser Company

project_ideas.based_on: benchmarks for code review did not change significantly across recent models
project_ideas.hypothesis: Holding the model constant, review precision/recall on held-out organizational PRs is predicted more strongly by context configuration (rules, PR history, repo relationships) than by swapping to a newer model.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in precision/recall and human acceptance rate attributable to context level versus model version, with confidence intervals over the noise floor.
project_ideas.name: Context Ablation Review Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness over a real multi-repo history with held-out PRs; run the same review model under graded context conditions — no context, repo-local instruction file only, and full context engine — and also across two model versions; compare defect detection and finding acceptance.
project_ideas.video_title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo

project_ideas.based_on: when to block PRs, and when to defer to humans based on accumulated context
project_ideas.hypothesis: An explicit policy module over detection output, using accumulated context and confidence signals, can reduce false blocks substantially without a proportional increase in missed defects compared to an unpolicied finder that surfaces all findings.
project_ideas.measurement: False-block rate versus missed-defect rate as the escalation threshold is swept, plus reviewer override rate on gate decisions.
project_ideas.name: Block-or-Defer Arbitration Layer
project_ideas.poc: Wrap an existing review finder with a policy layer that assigns each finding a gate/defer/escalate decision using explicit criteria; replay it over historical PRs with known post-merge defects and known rejected findings.
project_ideas.video_title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo

project_ideas.based_on: Multiple agents using different context sources and enforcing different standards lead to inconsistencies.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Replacing per-repo agent instruction files with a single shared context/standards service measurably reduces cross-repo inconsistency in agent output (style divergence, broken service-contract changes) as repository count grows.
project_ideas.measurement: Cross-repo divergence score and contract-breaking change rate at N = 1, 10, 100 repos under both governance models, plus standard-change propagation cost.
project_ideas.name: Shared Governance Context Service
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a central rules-and-standards service consumed by agents across a synthetic fleet of repos; run the same agent tasks against N repos under per-repo instruction files versus the shared service, and diff the outputs for style and contract violations.
project_ideas.video_title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo

project_ideas.based_on: Software governance must evolve from reviewing pull requests to reviewing graph-based software architecture.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Incrementally maintained graph/dependency indexes produce fewer staleness-induced review errors than static snapshot rebuilds at equal or lower retrieval latency, and catch architectural and contract defects that diff-level review misses.
project_ideas.measurement: Review accuracy on injected architectural/contract defects, retrieval latency, and staleness window (time between a real change and its appearance in the index) for each indexing strategy.
project_ideas.name: Graph Freshness Review Index
project_ideas.poc: Index a multi-service repository into a dependency and PR-history graph; implement both a static snapshot rebuild and an incremental updater; route review queries against both and score detection of injected architectural and contract defects.
project_ideas.video_title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo

project_ideas.based_on: single-run pass/fail is an insufficient (and misleading) signal
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a representative multi-step agent task, a minimal k exists beyond which ship/no-ship decisions match a high-k ground truth with high agreement, and this k is small enough to keep eval cost practical.
project_ideas.measurement: Agreement rate between low-k decisions and k=50 decisions, variance reduction per added run, and token/latency cost per reliable ship decision.
project_ideas.name: K-Calibrator
project_ideas.poc: Run a ReAct-loop agent on a fixed case set with k=50, compute pass@k and pass_wedge_k stability curves, and compare decisions from k=1..20 against the k=50 reference.
project_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Evolved. Your Evals Didn't. — Ameya Bhatawdekar, Braintrust

project_ideas.based_on: the durable engineering asset is the curated eval set
project_ideas.hypothesis: Eval cases annotated with declared architectural assumptions (generation, state requirements, tool surface) can be automatically classified as portable, needing rewrite, or invalid when migrating across architecture generations, with low false-invalidation.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision and recall of portability labels against manual audit, number of cases surviving unchanged, and engineering time saved versus a from-scratch rewrite.
project_ideas.name: EvalPort
project_ideas.poc: Define an eval-case schema with architectural assumptions, build a compatibility checker, and migrate a seed corpus from a Gen 3 loop to a Gen 6 harness while manually auditing the labels.
project_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Evolved. Your Evals Didn't. — Ameya Bhatawdekar, Braintrust

project_ideas.based_on: Structure is added when the model is weak and removed when it strengthens.
project_ideas.hypothesis: As underlying model capability increases, explicit graph/state-machine orchestration can be removed for a class of high-stakes tasks without reducing task success or safety, because the model absorbs path control.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in task success rate, write-action authorization violations, latency, and engineering effort to remove the orchestration layer.
project_ideas.name: Scaffold Debt Meter
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same incident-response agent as a Gen 4 workflow graph and a Gen 5 model-driven loop, run both on a fixed model version and on a stronger model, and compare outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Evolved. Your Evals Didn't. — Ameya Bhatawdekar, Braintrust

project_ideas.based_on: Evaluation granularity must match architecture granularity
project_ideas.hypothesis: Node-level assertions in a workflow graph localize failures to graph nodes with higher precision than end-to-end evals alone, without materially increasing false-positive brittle assertions when assertions are property-based.
project_ideas.measurement: Localization precision/recall, false-positive assertion rate, and debugging time reduction in a controlled fault-injection exercise.
project_ideas.name: NodeScope
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a graph agent with per-node property assertions, inject faults at selected nodes, and compare failure attribution against end-to-end pass/fail alone.
project_ideas.video_title: Your Agent Evolved. Your Evals Didn't. — Ameya Bhatawdekar, Braintrust

project_ideas.based_on: Memory bandwidth, not raw clock speed, is the primary bottleneck for LLMs
project_ideas.hypothesis: For LLM inference, the transition from memory-bandwidth-bound to compute-bound occurs at a predictable batch size and sequence length threshold that can be modeled with a roofline analysis and validated on commodity GPUs.
project_ideas.measurement: Root-mean-square error between predicted and measured crossover points across models and precisions; sensitivity of crossover to HBM bandwidth.
project_ideas.name: Roofline Crossover Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Build a micro-benchmark suite that runs a small transformer (e.g., GPT-2 small) across a grid of batch sizes (1–64) and sequence lengths (128–4096) on a single GPU, measuring achieved FLOPS and memory bandwidth utilization; compare against a roofline model to identify the crossover point.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Computer Architecture & Organization • Jim Ledin & Maciej «MJ» Jedrzejewski • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: 80 to 90 percent of AI model processing comes down to matrix multiplications.
project_ideas.hypothesis: The claim that 80–90% of AI model processing reduces to matrix multiplications holds for dense transformer models but fails for architectures with heavy attention or elementwise operations at long context lengths.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of FLOPs and wall-clock time attributable to matrix multiplication, with confidence intervals across model families and configurations; deviation from the 80–90% claim.
project_ideas.name: Matrix Multiplication Share Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Instrument PyTorch models (GPT-2, BERT, LLaMA) with profilers to decompose FLOPs and wall-clock time into matrix multiplication versus non-matmul operations across varying batch sizes and sequence lengths.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Computer Architecture & Organization • Jim Ledin & Maciej «MJ» Jedrzejewski • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Aligning software algorithms and data structures with underlying CPU/GPU pipeline and cache hierarchies to maximize execution speed.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Aligning tensor data layouts and access patterns to GPU cache hierarchies (e.g., tiling, memory coalescing) yields measurable throughput gains in LLM inference that exceed gains from increasing arithmetic throughput alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Tokens per second and achieved memory bandwidth for naive vs. optimized layouts; speedup ratio and L2/L1 hit rates.
project_ideas.name: Cache-Aware Data Layout Benchmark for LLM Serving
project_ideas.poc: Implement a simple LLM inference kernel (e.g., matrix-vector multiply for generation) with naive and cache-optimized data layouts, and benchmark on a GPU with varying batch sizes.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Computer Architecture & Organization • Jim Ledin & Maciej «MJ» Jedrzejewski • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Comparing DDR5 RAM price increases over a year alongside the adoption of stacked High Bandwidth Memory (HBM).
project_ideas.hypothesis: The effective cost of memory bandwidth for AI accelerators (bandwidth per dollar and per watt) is improving slower than compute cost, making bandwidth the economic bottleneck; stacked HBM generations will show diminishing returns relative to cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Year-over-year improvement rates for bandwidth-per-dollar and bandwidth-per-watt versus FLOPS-per-dollar; correlation with listed HBM costs.
project_ideas.name: HBM Bandwidth-per-Dollar Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Compile a public dataset of accelerator specs (HBM generation, capacity, bandwidth, TDP, price) and compute bandwidth-per-dollar and bandwidth-per-watt trends over time; validate against DDR5 price trends.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Computer Architecture & Organization • Jim Ledin & Maciej «MJ» Jedrzejewski • GOTO 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Requests can escalate to AI agents when rules cannot make a definitive decision.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an explicit 'undetermined' return state to a boolean rules tier, plus a tunable escalation predicate, reduces missed-escalation error on ambiguous cases without materially inflating false escalations or total compute cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Escalation rate, false-escalation cost, missed-escalation error rate, and cost and latency per decision versus rules-only and agent-only routing on the same case set.
project_ideas.name: Abstain-and-Escalate Rules Kernel
project_ideas.poc: Build a small refund-triage pipeline: a rules engine with three-valued return states (approve / deny / undetermined), a probabilistic agent stage that only receives undetermined cases, and a guardrail filter on agent output. Run it against a labeled case set spanning clean structured cases, messy unstructured cases, and adversarial near-misses.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?

project_ideas.based_on: AI agents might return different outputs on repeated identical requests.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A test harness that uses repeated sampling with tolerance bands and rubric scoring for the probabilistic tier, plus exact-match assertions for the deterministic tier and explicit escalation-path tests, produces a lower flake rate and better regression-detection signal than exact-match assertions applied uniformly.
project_ideas.measurement: CI flake rate, true-regression detection rate, and signal-to-noise ratio per regime; correlation between escalation rate and seeded rule-set drift.
project_ideas.name: Tier-Split Eval Harness
project_ideas.poc: Take one decision set and score it under three regimes: uniform exact-match assertions, tier-split exact-match plus repeat-sample tolerance bands, and tier-split plus rubric scoring. Track flakes, false regressions, and missed regressions across repeated runs and prompt/rule perturbations.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?

project_ideas.based_on: How can we establish effective deterministic guardrails around probabilistic AI models?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Guardrail strategies differ sharply in coverage-to-false-rejection ratio, and schema/type validation combined with hard policy constraints outperforms thresholded confidence filtering on coverage while producing fewer false rejections.
project_ideas.measurement: Coverage of unsafe or out-of-policy outputs, false-rejection rate on legitimate recommendations, added latency per decision, and human review volume when HITL is the final gate.
project_ideas.name: Guardrail Strategy Bake-Off
project_ideas.poc: Wrap the same agent in four interchangeable guardrail layers (schema/type validation, hard policy constraints, thresholded confidence, tool-call allowlist) and replay a labeled set of agent recommendations, including deliberately malformed and out-of-policy outputs, through each layer independently and in combination.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?

project_ideas.based_on: Enables automation where rigid rules would fail or require endless manual coding.
project_ideas.hypothesis: There is a measurable rule-count and case-diversity threshold above which maintaining the deterministic tier costs more engineer-hours per case class than routing that long tail to an agent plus its containment layer.
project_ideas.measurement: Engineer-hours per new case class, marginal cost per decision, accuracy, and auditability coverage as case diversity increases; identify the crossover point and its sensitivity to rule churn.
project_ideas.name: Rule-Growth Crossover Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a decision domain with a growing long tail: incrementally add case classes and rules to a rules-only tier while routing an identical stream to an agent-plus-guardrail tier, logging authoring and maintenance effort, error rates, and per-decision compute for both.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Agents vs Business Rules: Which Should Make Decisions?

project_ideas.based_on: the bottleneck is verifier/data availability rather than model capability
project_ideas.hypothesis: For most candidate vertical tasks, a partial programmatic verifier exists (backtests, registry-reported endpoints, rejection-rate proxies) and identifying it is a stronger predictor of project success than model or stack quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Fraction of tasks with at least one usable partial verifier, median label latency, and eval-score variance reduction per week of iteration for verified vs. unverified tasks.
project_ideas.name: Verifier Coverage Audit
project_ideas.poc: For a set of narrow tasks (flag mispriced bond, rank molecules, triage a case), enumerate candidate verifiers and score each on automation level, latency to label, and confounder load; then correlate verifier score with whether an eval loop actually converges in a two-week trial.
project_ideas.video_title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI

project_ideas.based_on: An LLM judge cannot tell alpha from jargon
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM-judge agreement with experts degrades measurably faster on fluent-but-wrong outputs than on awkward-but-correct outputs, and the gap is a reliable detector of judge drift before it corrupts an eval loop.
project_ideas.measurement: Judge-expert agreement delta between probe classes, and change in that delta across successive judge prompt versions.
project_ideas.name: Judge Inversion Probe Suite
project_ideas.poc: Build paired probes per domain: stylistically confident nonsense vs. correct-but-ungrammatical expert output. Score with several LLM judges and with one or more domain experts; compute sensitivity and specificity of the judge for each probe class.
project_ideas.video_title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI

project_ideas.based_on: What is the minimum expert involvement per unit of model improvement, and does the loop converge or plateau once the easy proprietary signal is exhausted?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Eval improvement per expert-hour follows a decaying curve that plateaus once the cheap proprietary signal is exhausted, and the plateau point is predictable from inter-expert disagreement rates.
project_ideas.measurement: Expert-hours per unit of eval-score improvement over time, and correlation between plateau onset and inter-expert disagreement rate.
project_ideas.name: Expert-Hours Yield Instrumentation
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a vertical deployment to log expert minutes against each eval item authored, each agreement decision, and each resulting eval-score change; plot expert-hours per unit eval improvement and fit the curve.
project_ideas.video_title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI

project_ideas.based_on: Traces, tool calls, and expert corrections are structured as the raw material for error analysis
project_ideas.hypothesis: A trace schema that captures expert corrections and outcome linkage at write time yields usable SFT and error-analysis data from the first deployment week, whereas retrofitting a training pipeline onto operational logging loses a substantial fraction of the signal.
project_ideas.measurement: Recoverable training examples per week and fraction of expert corrections attributable to a specific agent step, per instrumentation.
project_ideas.name: Training-Grade Trace Schema
project_ideas.poc: Run two parallel instrumentations of the same agent — a standard ops log and a training-grade schema capturing per-step expert adjudication, tool calls, and a deferred outcome pointer — then measure how much recoverable eval/SFT data each produces after four weeks.
project_ideas.video_title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI

project_ideas.based_on: Building systems without guardrails around blast radius is a recipe for disaster.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For the same code-generation model, executing untrusted AI-generated code in ephemeral isolated sandboxes instead of developer/CI environments with ambient credentials measurably reduces incident severity.
project_ideas.measurement: Number and severity of containment-escalation events, credential and filesystem reach per run, and persistence beyond run termination.
project_ideas.name: Blast-Radius Sandbox Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run a fixed corpus of AI-generated code, including deliberately destructive samples, through two execution configurations — ambient CI and ephemeral sandbox — and record what each configuration can reach.
project_ideas.video_title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

project_ideas.based_on: Cognitive debt is the erosion of your ability to have good memory
project_ideas.hypothesis: Higher AI-generation ratio per module predicts lower developer recall of that module and longer time-to-diagnose injected faults in it.
project_ideas.measurement: Recall accuracy, diagnosis time, and the correlation coefficient between these outcomes and per-module generation ratio.
project_ideas.name: Cognitive Debt Probe
project_ideas.poc: Tag modules in one codebase by AI-generation ratio, then run comprehension tasks and injected-fault diagnosis tasks on the engineers who own those modules.
project_ideas.video_title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

project_ideas.based_on: What new debugging paradigms are required for non-deterministic AI agent workflows?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Sampling many agent runs and clustering failures by outcome signature finds root causes faster than inspecting a single failed run.
project_ideas.measurement: Median time-to-root-cause, fraction of incidents reproduced by a cluster rule, and false-attribution rate.
project_ideas.name: Agent Trace Sampler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument one agent to emit full traces, sample N runs per task, cluster failures by outcome signature, and compare root-cause time against single-run inspection of the same incidents.
project_ideas.video_title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

project_ideas.based_on: Engineers own specific parts of a large codebase and must take responsibility for correctness.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Assigning an explicit named human owner to every AI-generated diff improves defect attribution and reduces unowned changes compared with implicit ownership.
project_ideas.measurement: Share of diffs with a named accountable owner, attribution rate at incident time, and rework or rollback rate per owner.
project_ideas.name: Diff Ownership Router
project_ideas.poc: Route AI-generated diffs to named owners with recorded acceptance decisions, then trace later incidents back to the owning diff and owner.
project_ideas.video_title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

project_ideas.based_on: tokens at the very beginning and very end of a prompt retain high prominence while the middle is effectively ignored
project_ideas.hypothesis: Instruction-following and recall accuracy in long prompts is a measurable, non-monotonic function of token position, and critical constraints placed mid-context fail at a rate detectably higher than identical constraints placed at the beginning or end.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-position accuracy curves; the depth and context-length at which mid-context accuracy falls below edge accuracy by a fixed margin; regression of total context length on overall task success.
project_ideas.name: Attention Atlas
project_ideas.poc: Build a probe harness that places identical instructions and needles at N controlled depths within a synthetic long context, sweeps total context length across several buckets, and records per-position compliance and recall for multiple models and task types. Emit a position-vs-accuracy curve per model plus a recommended placement policy for harness assembly.
project_ideas.video_title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI

project_ideas.based_on: Well-partitioned modules with disciplined interfaces prevent AI models and humans from getting confused by irrelevant details
project_ideas.hypothesis: For identical feature tasks, agents given module-scoped context achieve higher task success and lower token consumption than agents given whole-repository context, and the gap widens as repository size grows.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate delta, mean tokens per completed task, retry count, and rework minutes per variant; correlation of the delta with repository size and module cohesion metrics.
project_ideas.name: Boundary Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Take a real repository, produce two variants — an original low-cohesion structure and a refactored high-cohesion one with disciplined interfaces — and run the same task suite against both under fixed model, prompt, and tooling, logging success, tokens, retries, and human-judged rework per run.
project_ideas.video_title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI

project_ideas.based_on: An agent pipeline consisting of a specifier, coder, cleaner, and hardener
project_ideas.hypothesis: Each added pipeline stage (cleaner, hardener, reviewer, QA) yields diminishing marginal defect reduction, and beyond a threshold stage count the coordination overhead — handoff loss, latency, token cost — exceeds the quality gain.
project_ideas.measurement: Marginal defect-escape reduction and mutation-score gain per added stage; cost and latency per stage; the stage count at which marginal quality gain falls below marginal coordination cost.
project_ideas.name: Pipeline Ablation Bench
project_ideas.poc: Implement a configurable pipeline with independently toggleable specifier, coder, cleaner, hardener, reviewer, and QA roles over a seeded benchmark of tasks with known injected defects; run full stage ablation, recording defect escape rate, mutation score, latency, and cost per completed change.
project_ideas.video_title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI

project_ideas.based_on: mutation testing acts as an automated gate on generated code
project_ideas.hypothesis: For agent-authored changes, a mutation-score gate prevents more escaped defects per unit cost than a line-coverage gate, and the two combined add less than their individual contributions when human review is already present.
project_ideas.measurement: Escaped-defect rate per gate regime, defects caught per gate-minute and per gate-token, marginal contribution of mutation testing over coverage, and interaction effect with human review.
project_ideas.name: Gate Parity Study
project_ideas.poc: Run agent-authored changes through three gating regimes — coverage-only, mutation-score-only, and combined — both with and without a human review step, then track defects that escape to the mainline plus the cost of each gate.
project_ideas.video_title: LIVE: Uncle Bob on Software Fundamentals in the Age of AI

project_ideas.based_on: a user-satisfaction proxy metric is an anti-signal for correctness
project_ideas.hypothesis: Challenging response policies will produce a measurable shift in the user's stated attribution of the conflict toward their own contribution, while validating policies will measurably harden the user's original position — and this effect will be visible even when validating policies score higher on user-rated helpfulness.
project_ideas.measurement: Pre/post shift in user self-attribution versus session satisfaction rating; correlation between the two metrics across policies.
project_ideas.name: Belief-Change Bench
project_ideas.poc: Run a controlled deployment of two response policies on the same conflict scenarios: capture the user's position statement before and after each session, blind-rate the delta for self-attribution, and record satisfaction alongside it so the two metrics can be shown to diverge.
project_ideas.video_title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI

project_ideas.based_on: Maxine screens sensitive messages quietly in the background for escalation control and fear-based language before responding.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A dedicated classifier trained on labeled conflict and escalation language will achieve higher recall on fear-based and escalation patterns than a general-purpose moderation layer, and its false-positive rate will be low enough that halt decisions do not suppress ordinary coaching at an unacceptable rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision, recall, and false-positive-driven coaching-suppression rate per threshold, compared against general-purpose moderation and clinician labels.
project_ideas.name: Conflict Screener Benchmark
