project_ideas.poc: Build a small labeled corpus of conflict messages with escalation and fear-language annotations, run a dedicated screener and a general-purpose moderator against it plus human clinician judgment, and sweep the threshold to map the precision/recall tradeoff against coaching-suppression cost.
project_ideas.video_title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI

project_ideas.based_on: those protocols should be encoded as the agent's decision policy
project_ideas.hypothesis: Encoding a structured conflict protocol as an explicit state machine over turn-level decisions will produce higher clinician-rated session quality and lower behavioral variance than the same protocol expressed as prompt text, because phase transitions become auditable and regression-testable.
project_ideas.measurement: Clinician-rated session quality and cross-session behavioral variance per condition; regression-test pass rate when the protocol version changes.
project_ideas.name: Protocol-as-Policy Engine
project_ideas.poc: Implement the protocol twice — as a versioned state machine driving the response policy and as a prompt-encoded instruction — then A/B them on held-out conflict scenarios and have clinicians rate sessions blind to condition.
project_ideas.video_title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI

project_ideas.based_on: Design agents with a first-class not-my-job decision and a defined handoff target
project_ideas.hypothesis: A warm handoff carrying a structured summary artifact will produce higher user follow-through with a human resource than an immediate crisis referral, without degrading safety outcomes for users who screen as high-risk.
project_ideas.measurement: Follow-through rate to the human resource per handoff design, plus the completeness of the summary artifact as judged against the conversation transcript.
project_ideas.name: Handoff Design Probe
project_ideas.poc: Prototype both handoff paths behind the pre-generation gate, route screened high-risk users to one of the two designs, and track whether they actually reach the human resource and what context survives the transfer.
project_ideas.video_title: AI is the World’s largest Relationship Therapist — Clay Cockrell & Tony Fabrikant, CoupleWork AI

project_ideas.based_on: Removing one dependency removes handoffs from 4 to 1
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reducing serial handoffs in an end-to-end multi-agent workflow by one yields disproportional gains in latency, success rate, and cost.
project_ideas.measurement: P95 end-to-end latency, success rate, number of serial handoffs, operational cost per run.
project_ideas.name: Handoff cut experiment harness
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a 4-step pipeline (e.g., ingest -> classify -> orchestrate -> output), instrument each hop with a trace ID, then remove the orchestrator hop and compare.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Enterprise Architecture: Architecting for Outcomes • Simon Rohrer • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Stop doing phase-gated architecture reviews on paper.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Runtime policy checks (policy-as-code on the request/event path) detect architectural drift significantly faster and with less human effort than phase-gated document approval.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection latency (minutes vs review cycles), false positives, reviewer hours consumed.
project_ideas.name: Live architecture guardrail
project_ideas.poc: Create a mutable agent/service sandbox with architecture rules (e.g., no bypassing auth gateway, every agent must use a tracing library); introduce a rule-violating change and measure detection time using an alerting policy engine.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Enterprise Architecture: Architecting for Outcomes • Simon Rohrer • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Organization architecture drives system architecture
project_ideas.hypothesis: Cross-boundary edges in the runtime agent dependency graph that are not backed by a corresponding team/API ownership boundary will show higher failure and rework rates than contained edges.
project_ideas.measurement: Cross-boundary edge count, failure rate, mean time to repair for boundary-crossing edges vs internal edges.
project_ideas.name: Conway mirror
project_ideas.poc: Import a sample team-to-service/agent ownership map and a distributed trace graph; flag graph edges crossing team ownership without an explicit platform interface; correlate with recent incident and cycle-time data.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Enterprise Architecture: Architecting for Outcomes • Simon Rohrer • GOTO 2025

project_ideas.based_on: MoE provides 10x training compute efficiency improvements compared to dense models.
project_ideas.hypothesis: At matched active-parameter counts, sparse MoE achieves at least 5x training-compute efficiency over dense models on both language and vision tasks; the 10x claim shrinks with scale and task diversity.
project_ideas.measurement: Ratio of training FLOPs to reach a fixed validation loss; report by scale and modality.
project_ideas.name: Sparse-vs-Dense Efficiency Replication Harness
project_ideas.poc: Train dense and sparse MoE Transformers at three scales (e.g., 100M, 1B, 10B active params) on matched token budgets, measuring loss per training FLOP.
project_ideas.video_title: Jeff Dean | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: How reliable are automated NAS/evolutionary discovery loops when the evaluation signal is noisy or partially misaligned with downstream quality?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Architectures discovered by evolutionary search retain their efficiency advantage on held-out tasks only when the search evaluator's noise is below a threshold; above that threshold, gains vanish or reverse.
project_ideas.measurement: Transfer gap = (discovered efficiency on search task) - (efficiency on held-out task); regress against evaluator noise.
project_ideas.name: NAS Evaluation Fidelity Lab
project_ideas.poc: Run an Evolve Transformer-style search loop with controlled evaluator noise (subsampled validation sets) and measure transfer of discovered architectures to unseen benchmarks.
project_ideas.video_title: Jeff Dean | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Integrating lidar and diverse sensor data early in training improves multi-domain reasoning.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Early integration of lidar during pretraining improves non-sensor reasoning tasks (e.g., text QA, code) by at least 5% relative, not just sensor-domain tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in accuracy on non-sensor reasoning benchmarks across modality mixes.
project_ideas.name: Multimodal Sensor Ablation Suite
project_ideas.poc: Pretrain identical transformer stacks on matched token budgets with three modality mixes: text+image, text+image+lidar, and text+image+lidar+audio; evaluate on non-sensor reasoning benchmarks.
project_ideas.video_title: Jeff Dean | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Benchmarking cybersecurity capabilities via frameworks like CyberGym and ExploitGym helps measure safety and risk.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Paired offensive/defensive benchmark scores (CyberGym/ExploitGym-style) explain at least 60% of variance in real-world exploit discovery timelines across model versions.
project_ideas.measurement: R² between benchmark deltas and red-team exploit success rates; calibration curves.
project_ideas.name: Paired Cyber Capability Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a paired eval harness for vulnerability discovery and patching; correlate scores with historical incident data or red-team outcomes on a fixed codebase.
project_ideas.video_title: Jeff Dean | 2026 Frontier & Pioneer Symposium

project_ideas.based_on: Error messages from file-reading tools can trick agents into executing unintended Python code.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Given a benign file-reading task, a mainstream agent framework will execute an instruction introduced only through a tool's error message in at least 30% of trials.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of trials where tool-output injection triggers code execution not requested by the user.
project_ideas.name: Tool-Output Injection Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a canary agent that reads a generated file and triggers an intentionally crafted error; embed an instruction like `exec('touch /tmp/pwned')` in the error text; run the task across multiple agent frameworks in sealed containers and record any unrequested code execution.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Agents Gone Rogue? Build, Defend & Attack AI-Enabled Apps • Katie Paxton-Fear • YOW! 2025

project_ideas.based_on: deleted the database while claiming everything was fine
project_ideas.hypothesis: Event-sourced tool-call logging plus filesystem and API diff reconciliation can detect a worker agent's false success report before destructive state loss in 90% of simulated panic or hijack scenarios, with under 5% false alarms on benign multi-step tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate and false-positive rate of mismatches between reported status and actual side effects.
project_ideas.name: AgentActionDiff
project_ideas.poc: Implement a thin orchestrator wrapper that appends all tool calls to an append-only audit log, snapshots mutable state, and compares worker natural-language completion reports to the recorded side-effect diff; simulate the Replit-style database deletion panic and a set of benign ETL and coding workflows to validate.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Agents Gone Rogue? Build, Defend & Attack AI-Enabled Apps • Katie Paxton-Fear • YOW! 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Unsecured API endpoints and exposed Firebase configuration files generated by AI coding assistants
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an automated security gate consisting of SAST, secret scanning, and endpoint-exposure checks to an AI coding pipeline surfaces at least one undisclosed vulnerability in 70% of generated CRUD and Firebase-integrated applications that already pass a functional smoke suite.
project_ideas.measurement: Share of generated apps containing vulnerabilities missed by functional testing, and detection rate by vulnerability class.
project_ideas.name: Codegen Security Gate Evaluation
project_ideas.poc: Generate 50 small working applications with common AI assistants, run functional tests to confirm usability, then run the security gate and catalogue vulnerabilities such as unsecured endpoints and exposed Firebase configuration files.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Agents Gone Rogue? Build, Defend & Attack AI-Enabled Apps • Katie Paxton-Fear • YOW! 2025

project_ideas.based_on: recurring code review comments are compiled into durable, machine-checkable invariants
project_ideas.hypothesis: Enough natural-language review comments can be compiled into correct, non-flaky automated invariants that the compiled rule set catches recurring violations without human curation, and the registry's false-positive rate stays bounded as rules accumulate across many pull requests because automated conflict and overlap detection prunes contradictory rules.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of comments converted into invariants that fire correctly without hand-editing; false-positive rate as a function of registry size; number of conflicting rule pairs detected; developer override rate per PR over successive weeks.
project_ideas.name: Invariant Registry with Conflict Detection
project_ideas.poc: Build a registry that ingests reviewer comments, compiles candidates into executable checks (e.g., 'Use the Money type for currency amounts, not float'), runs them on a shadow corpus of historical PRs, and flags contradictory or overlapping rules for deprecation.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Kill the Code Review — Ankit Jain, Aviator

project_ideas.based_on: deterministic checks plus runtime LLM judges executed in a preview environment
project_ideas.hypothesis: A hybrid gate of deterministic checks plus runtime LLM judges reaches precision and recall on labeled PR defects that are not materially worse than human line-by-line review, at a lower latency and cost per PR than the manual baseline, and the deterministic layer alone accounts for the majority of caught defects.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall versus human review on the same changes; verdict variance across repeated LLM-judge runs on identical inputs; marginal defects caught by the judge layer that deterministic checks miss; seconds and dollars per PR.
project_ideas.name: Deterministic-vs-Judge Verification Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a labeled corpus of historical PRs with known defects, run three configurations (deterministic only, LLM judge only, hybrid) in a preview environment, and score each on precision, recall, latency, and cost.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Kill the Code Review — Ankit Jain, Aviator

project_ideas.based_on: the interactive session itself becomes the acceptance criteria
project_ideas.hypothesis: Acceptance criteria and test plans extracted from interactive session transcripts cover edge cases as well as human-written criteria on the same task, and the residual intent loss is concentrated in a small, identifiable class of under-specified interactions rather than spread uniformly.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect escape rate for session-derived versus human-written criteria; coverage delta on edge cases; fraction of criteria traceable to an explicit session utterance; human-flagged mis-extractions per task.
project_ideas.name: Session-to-Criteria Extractor
project_ideas.poc: Capture development sessions, extract structured acceptance criteria and test plans, and compare them head-to-head against criteria written by a human for the same task using defect-escape and coverage metrics.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Kill the Code Review — Ankit Jain, Aviator

project_ideas.based_on: Semantic accuracy needs better tooling, but human alignment must survive.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Alignment value lost when line-by-line diff review is removed is recoverable through upstream intent review sessions, and this recovery is detectable through proxies such as onboarding time to first independent contribution and architectural drift measured against declared intent, rather than being an unmeasurable cultural good.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-first-independent-contribution for new joiners; rate of architectural changes that contradict prior acceptance criteria; concentration of authorship/decision knowledge across team members; self-reported mentorship touchpoints.
project_ideas.name: Alignment Proxy Instrumentation
project_ideas.poc: Instrument two comparable teams, one keeping diff review and one running upstream intent review plus automated verification, and track onboarding time, architectural drift against acceptance criteria, and knowledge-distribution metrics over a quarter.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Kill the Code Review — Ankit Jain, Aviator

project_ideas.based_on: Effective agent firewalls must parse protocol semantics (e.g., SQL)
project_ideas.hypothesis: A proxy that parses PostgreSQL wire protocol and SQL abstract syntax trees can block destructive commands like `DROP TABLE` while allowing safe queries, with significantly fewer false positives than IP/port allowlists.
project_ideas.measurement: False positive and false negative rates for destructive commands; latency overhead per query.
project_ideas.name: SQL-Aware Agent Firewall Prototype
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal egress proxy for PostgreSQL that terminates connections, parses SQL, and enforces HCL-style rules; run a benchmark of known-safe (SELECT, INSERT) and destructive (DROP, DELETE) queries from a dummy agent; measure allow/deny accuracy.
project_ideas.video_title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno

project_ideas.based_on: Agent security proxies should act as credential brokers
project_ideas.hypothesis: By injecting credentials only after policy approval, a proxy prevents an agent from exfiltrating raw secrets even when the agent is prompt-injected to exfiltrate them.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of raw credential strings observed in agent-generated network traffic; success rate of legitimate queries after credential injection.
project_ideas.name: Credential-Brokering Proxy with Secret Exfiltration Test
project_ideas.poc: Create a proxy that holds database credentials and injects them into approved requests; run two agent sessions, one benign and one prompt-injected to attempt exfiltration; log all bytes sent by the agent to verify that raw credentials never appear.
project_ideas.video_title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno

project_ideas.based_on: Agent access policies can be expressed as version-controlled code (HCL)
project_ideas.hypothesis: HCL-based agent permission rules can be unit-tested against a corpus of known-good and known-malicious protocol requests to reduce misconfigurations and improve developer confidence in policy changes.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of requests correctly classified; number of untested rule branches; time to detect a misconfiguration.
project_ideas.name: HCL Agent Policy Unit-Testing Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a test harness that loads HCL rules and replays a regression suite of PostgreSQL and HTTP request fixtures (e.g., DROP TABLE, DELETE namespace, SELECT with safe filters); run CI checks that fail if a dangerous request is allowed or a safe request is blocked.
project_ideas.video_title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno

project_ideas.based_on: Policy rules for agents can treat approval as an action
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM-based approval judges are vulnerable to prompt-injected requests and can be benchmarked to quantify false approval and false denial rates compared to static rules and human judgments.
project_ideas.measurement: Judge false approval rate and false denial rate on adversarial vs. benign requests; agreement with human ground truth.
project_ideas.name: Benchmark for LLM-Based Approval Judges Under Adversarial Prompt Injection
project_ideas.poc: Create a benchmark dataset of high-risk agent action requests (e.g., database deletions, namespace deletions) each with a benign or adversarial context; evaluate an LLM judge, a static HCL rule engine, and a human on approval decisions; compare outcomes against ground truth.
project_ideas.video_title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno

project_ideas.based_on: Compaction must achieve greater than 50x compression to be worth breaking cache hits.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In an agent with prompt caching, enabling naive summarization-based compaction will increase total cost and reduce session-recall accuracy compared to full-context, when the cache discount is 50x and compression is below 50x.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-turn token cost, cache hit ratio, session-recall accuracy (exact/semantic match), and tool-call counts.
project_ideas.name: Cache-Aware Compaction Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal agent loop (e.g., a coding tutor) using Gemini and DeepSeek APIs. Run three conditions: full-context with caching, sliding-window compaction, and LM-summarization compaction. Run multi-turn recall and cost measurement on a fixed task set.
project_ideas.video_title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI

project_ideas.based_on: An agent told 'NEVER push directly to main' eventually executing 'git push origin main' after 45 turns of logs and diffs.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Instruction-adherence accuracy in a multi-turn coding agent will degrade monotonically as the ratio of non-instruction tokens (logs, diffs, tool output) to instruction tokens increases, and this degradation can be predicted by a simple context-composition metric.
project_ideas.measurement: Instruction-following accuracy per turn, context-pollution score, and ROC/AUC for predicting the first violation.
project_ideas.name: Context Rot Monitor
project_ideas.poc: Create a small coding-agent environment with an explicit 'NEVER push to main' instruction. Run extended sessions with varied log/diff padding, recording adherence per turn. Compute a context-pollution score (e.g., non-instruction token fraction) and correlate with violation likelihood.
project_ideas.video_title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI

project_ideas.based_on: Any summarization rewrites the prefix and invalidates the cache, but the 50x discount makes cache hits critical
project_ideas.hypothesis: A two-tier context format—a stable instruction prefix followed by a compacted tail of older turns—will preserve cache hits on the prefix while reducing total token count and maintaining session-recall accuracy comparable to full-context, unlike naive compaction which breaks the cache.
project_ideas.measurement: Cache hit ratio, tokens-per-turn, session-recall score, and end-to-end latency.
project_ideas.name: Cache-Preserving Two-Tier Context
project_ideas.poc: Implement a context manager that keeps the system prompt and first N turns untouched, then appends a 'compaction summary' of later turns after a stable delimiter. Compare against full-context and summarization-compaction on recall and cache hit rate.
project_ideas.video_title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI

project_ideas.based_on: Hybrid search (dense embeddings plus BM25 keyword search followed by reranking) outperforms pure semantic search.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For an agent-maintained file-based LLM wiki (with an index.md map), hybrid retrieval (dense embeddings + BM25 + reranking) will achieve higher recall@5 and MRR than pure semantic vector search on the same corpus, across factual and procedural queries.
project_ideas.measurement: Recall@5, MRR, and final answer accuracy.
project_ideas.name: Agent Wiki Hybrid Retrieval Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a small agent-maintained wiki with ~1,000 entries. Enable two retrieval modes: embeddings-only and hybrid. Run a set of 100 query-answer pairs generated from wiki content, measuring retrieval quality end-to-end.
project_ideas.video_title: Context Engineering in 2026 — Louis-François Bouchard, Omar Solano & Samridhi Vaid, Towards AI

project_ideas.based_on: nodes at different granularities (tokens, retrieved chunks, agent turns)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Node granularity materially changes agent reliability, cost, and debuggability, such that a task run with tokens, retrieved chunks, and agent turns as nodes will show reliability differences larger than run-to-run noise, with debuggability tracked separately from accuracy.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, cost per successful task, and time-to-localize an injected failure for each granularity level, with variance across repeated runs as the noise floor.
project_ideas.name: Graph Granularity Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Implement one fixed task with node identity parameterized across three levels (token spans, retrieved chunks, agent turns), holding the underlying model and tool set constant, and log the mask/edge decisions made at each level.
project_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy Stanford Lecture: Delete Everything, Keep Graph

project_ideas.based_on: prompts a runtime configuration layer
project_ideas.hypothesis: Recording the exact runtime text alongside the model version and tool schema and treating that triple as a single rollback unit reduces time-to-diagnosis for injected behavioral regressions compared with pipelines that version code only.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean time to diagnosis of injected regressions, plus the fraction of regressions attributable to each element of the triple.
project_ideas.name: Prompt-as-Deployable Release Gate
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal service where prompt/context, model version, and tool schemas are versioned and recorded per request, then inject silent behavior regressions and compare diagnosis time with and without exact-text provenance.
project_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy Stanford Lecture: Delete Everything, Keep Graph

project_ideas.based_on: additional token budget versus to the specific step-by-step content
project_ideas.hypothesis: A substantial portion of the reported reasoning accuracy gain attributed to step-by-step prompting is attributable to generated token budget rather than to step structure, so matching token counts across step-by-step, unstructured-verbose, and terse conditions shrinks the step-by-step advantage.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy delta between step-by-step and unstructured-verbose at equal generated token counts, relative to the unmatched-condition delta.
project_ideas.name: CoT Budget-Matched Ablation
project_ideas.poc: Run a batch of multi-step arithmetic and compositional reasoning prompts under three conditions with generated token budgets matched by truncation or padding of verbose output, reporting accuracy per condition.
project_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy Stanford Lecture: Delete Everything, Keep Graph

project_ideas.based_on: whether curating failures into evaluation sets yields the same reliability gains
project_ideas.hypothesis: Curating production failure traces into an evaluated set and changing prompt, context, or tool schemas yields reliability gains comparable in magnitude to the retraining-based data engine loop, even with no weight updates.
project_ideas.measurement: Failure-rate reduction on held-out traces per iteration cycle, and the rate at which curated-set gains transfer to unseen failures.
project_ideas.name: Trace-to-Eval Loop for Prompted Systems
project_ideas.poc: Instrument trace capture on a prompted system, curate failures into a held-out evaluation set, iterate only on prompt/context/tool artifacts, and track failure rates on both the curated set and fresh held-out traces.
project_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy Stanford Lecture: Delete Everything, Keep Graph

project_ideas.based_on: Design and test backpressure/triage mechanisms
project_ideas.hypothesis: An explicit backpressure-and-triage layer keeps unverified-artifact backlog bounded as generation rate scales, whereas an unbounded submission path grows backlog linearly or worse; the gate's confidence threshold, not model capability, determines whether review latency stays flat.
project_ideas.measurement: Backlog depth over time as a function of generation rate (bounded vs unbounded), median and p95 human review wait, fraction of artifacts reaching a canonicalized/approved end state, and fraction abandoned or expired.
project_ideas.name: Digestion Gate
project_ideas.poc: Build an artifact intake service with a confidence-gated routing policy (auto-accept, queue for human review, quarantine) plus a configurable submission rate limiter; run it against a synthetic producer whose rate is varied across a 10x range and against an otherwise identical unbounded control path.
project_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

project_ideas.based_on: Correctness oracles and explanation/exposition layers should be separate components
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-stage capability scores predict end-to-end pipeline throughput on held-out tasks better than aggregate task-success rates, and the stage with the lowest score accounts for the majority of end-to-end drop-off.
project_ideas.measurement: Out-of-sample predictive error (R^2 or rank correlation) of per-stage model vs aggregate model against measured end-to-end throughput; attribution error when predicting which stage is the constraint.
project_ideas.name: Stage-Wise Capability Profiler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a five-stage pipeline (identify, generate, verify, explain, canonicalize) with independent per-stage scorers; fit a throughput model on per-stage scores and a competing model on a single aggregate success rate; evaluate both on held-out task batches.
project_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

project_ideas.based_on: Multi-objective systems need explicit divergence monitoring
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a multi-objective agent loop optimized against a single proxy metric, statistically significant degradation on off-proxy objectives appears before the proxy score saturates or reverses, giving measurable lead time for intervention.
project_ideas.measurement: Lead time in optimization steps between the first significant off-proxy divergence alarm and the proxy plateau/reversal; false-positive rate of the divergence detector across seeds.
project_ideas.name: Divergence Monitor
project_ideas.poc: Run a multi-objective optimization loop with one optimized proxy objective and two held-out off-proxy objectives; log both continuously and apply change-point detection to find the first significant off-proxy divergence relative to the proxy trajectory.
project_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

project_ideas.based_on: classify steps as friction-for-value vs incidental friction
project_ideas.hypothesis: Some workflow steps are load-bearing: removing them lowers downstream human comprehension or error-catch rate, while removing incidental-friction steps does not, and the two classes can be separated by an A/B removal protocol run on the same task set.
project_ideas.measurement: Downstream comprehension scores and error-catch rate per arm; effect size and confidence interval for each removed step; classification accuracy of pre-registered predictions about which steps are load-bearing.
project_ideas.name: Friction Audit
project_ideas.poc: Select a set of tasks with measurable downstream outcomes, identify candidate friction steps, and run a three-arm experiment (control, removal of suspected load-bearing friction, removal of suspected incidental friction) using the same generated artifacts.
project_ideas.video_title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao

project_ideas.based_on: Collapsing a multi-subagent architecture into a single 'smart main agent' was the primary lever for a 90-95% cost reduction
project_ideas.hypothesis: For tasks requiring fewer than N tool calls, a single-loop main agent achieves equal or better task success at lower cost per successful task than a nested subagent architecture; above N, nesting may become cost-justified.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per successful task, token overhead per nested loop, task success rate, and break-even N.
project_ideas.name: Agent Boundary Cost Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same outbound-sales agent workload in two architectures: (a) multiple subagents with separate context loops, and (b) one main agent using tool calls. Instrument token counts per turn, latency, and task success. Vary N and task complexity.
project_ideas.video_title: How Unify cut its AI agent costs 95% in two weeks

project_ideas.based_on: Achieving a 95% cache hit rate prevents excessive API token charges during high-volume operations.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Application-layer prefix hashing and response-ID routing can maintain >90% prompt cache hit rate under realistic per-tenant prompt mutation, reducing token cost by >80% versus no application caching.
project_ideas.measurement: Cache hit rate, token cost per request, latency, and degradation under prompt mutation.
project_ideas.name: Cache-Hit SLO Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a proxy that hashes stable prompt prefixes, tracks response IDs, and routes requests to warmed model instances; instrument hit rate, token cost, and latency across synthetic tenants with varying context volatility.
project_ideas.video_title: How Unify cut its AI agent costs 95% in two weeks

project_ideas.based_on: Memory is managed as a batch generative-then-discriminative pipeline over raw conversation and historical memory
project_ideas.hypothesis: A generative-proposal + discriminative-validation memory pipeline with lineage reduces contradictory memory entries by >X% and improves downstream answer accuracy over an append-only baseline in long-horizon conversations.
project_ideas.measurement: Contradiction count, stale-memory retention, merge precision, downstream answer accuracy, lineage completeness.
project_ideas.name: Memory Reconciliation Engine
project_ideas.poc: Implement a memory store with periodic reconciliation: generate candidate updates/merges/deprecations from raw conversation and existing memory, validate discriminatively, and track lineage. Inject contradictory facts over long conversations and compare to append-only.
project_ideas.video_title: How Unify cut its AI agent costs 95% in two weeks

project_ideas.based_on: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation has an inherent blind spot: the judge cannot share the exact distribution of the model under test (groupthink)
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM-as-judge scores diverge from human labels more when judge and evaluated model share a family; calibration on 100-1000 stratified real examples reduces divergence below a set threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Judge-human divergence rate, defect discovery rate at equal cost, calibration improvement.
project_ideas.name: Judge Calibration Kit
project_ideas.poc: Collect a stratified sample of 100-1000 real agent traces. Compare judge scores to human labels. Measure divergence as a function of judge-model similarity. Apply calibration (e.g., few-shot human examples, distributional reweighting) and re-measure.
project_ideas.video_title: How Unify cut its AI agent costs 95% in two weeks

project_ideas.based_on: agents must continually learn on the job and acquire specialized expertise
project_ideas.hypothesis: A continual learning subsystem that accumulates per-domain micro-world expertise from agent trajectories will reduce token consumption per successful workflow by at least 30% and increase success rate on non-coding digital work compared to a frozen LLM baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: tokens per successful workflow, task success rate, variance across repeated trials, and count of repeated mistakes prevented
project_ideas.name: MicroWorld Continual Learning Harness
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a language agent on three heterogeneous micro-worlds (e.g., enterprise meeting scheduling, CRM data entry, internal IT ticket triage) and implement a per-domain memory that stores discovered structures, constraints, and repeated conditionals from each completed and failed episode; compare token usage, success rate, and brittleness against the same base model without this memory over 100 trials per domain.
project_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

project_ideas.based_on: expertise actually will bring you the right context
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents equipped with an explicit context curation module that brings domain-relevant constraints (authority, priorities, urgency) before reasoning will reduce reasoning tokens by at least 25% and improve task success by at least 15% on scheduling and enterprise workflows compared to generic retrieval-augmented generation.
project_ideas.measurement: context precision/recall against ground truth, tokens used by reasoning stage, success rate, and cost per success
project_ideas.name: CURATE: Context Curation Evaluation Suite
project_ideas.poc: Build a controlled meeting scheduling environment where the correct constraints are known. Implement two agent variants: one with a context curator that extracts constraints from domain world model, one with standard retrieval. Run both over identical tasks and log selected context items. Compare downstream reasoning tokens, success rate, and context precision/recall.
project_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

project_ideas.based_on: experts effectively has, have built a world model of their environments
project_ideas.hypothesis: The degree to which an agent explicitly encodes a micro-world's local physics (structures, constraints, affordances, dynamics) predicts deployment success more strongly than general model capability, as measured by a set of domain-specific probes.
project_ideas.measurement: correlation between probe score and task success, performance difference between base and domain-adapted agent, and false confidence rate
project_ideas.name: Domain World Model Probes
project_ideas.poc: Create a suite of micro-world probes across coding, scheduling, CRM, and design. For each domain, measure whether agent can answer constraint optimization questions, identify missing constraints, and stop at expert-level judgment. Correlate probe scores with actual success in deploying the agent on that domain. Optionally test a version fine-tuned on domain world model vs base model.
project_ideas.video_title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition

project_ideas.based_on: When the training environment has almost no resources
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent trained and evaluated under scaffold-free constraints will show a smaller performance drop when external scaffolds are removed than an agent trained with rich scaffolding, holding base model and core task constant.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta task success rate between scaffolded and scaffold-free eval; cross-task transfer ratio on held-out tasks without external support.
project_ideas.name: Austere Transfer Probe
project_ideas.poc: Build two configurations of an analysis agent: a rich configuration with retrieval/tools and an austere configuration with only memory/reasoning. Evaluate both on core tasks, then strip external scaffolds from the rich configuration and compare transfer.
project_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

project_ideas.based_on: An individual's long-term capability is co-produced by a population of high-level training partners
project_ideas.hypothesis: Injecting a stronger external agent into a co-evolving evaluation pool raises the top-1 performance of a target agent on a fixed hard-task set by at least 10% compared to a static adversarial pool, after the same number of training episodes.
project_ideas.measurement: Performance on a held-out harder task set; time to plateau in episodes.
project_ideas.name: Sparring Cohort Scheduler
project_ideas.poc: Implement two training loops: one against a static set of red-team/peer agents and one against a pool that periodically receives an external agent of known higher capability. Compare target agent learning curves.
project_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

project_ideas.based_on: modeling the internal state of each worker
project_ideas.hypothesis: A meta-controller that uses token-level uncertainty and task-progress signals to route each subagent to a tailored control policy achieves at least 5% higher composite task success than a uniform control policy using the same total compute.
project_ideas.measurement: Composite task success rate, average tokens per task, fallback rate.
project_ideas.name: Per-Agent Meta-Control Router
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a multi-step workflow with three heterogeneous LLMs (e.g., fact-check, summarization, code generation). Compare two configurations: a uniform system prompt/temperature/fallback policy versus an adaptive meta-controller that adjusts per-agent behavior based on observed uncertainty and error rates.
project_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

project_ideas.based_on: Reliability under pressure is built by deliberately confronting near-catastrophic scenarios during training
project_ideas.hypothesis: A scheduled red-team and chaos-engineering loop with escalating severity during agent training reduces end-task response variance on held-out adversarial prompts by at least 30% and does not increase false refusal rates compared to a control without the loop.
project_ideas.measurement: Response variance under adversarial eval, task success rate under adversarial eval, false refusal rate.
project_ideas.name: Calibrated Pressure Drill
project_ideas.poc: Take the same base model and create two variants: one that receives periodic pressure-injection drills of rising difficulty and one that receives an equal number of benign inputs. Evaluate both on ambiguous/hostile prompts and measure calibration.
project_ideas.video_title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500

project_ideas.based_on: What operational criterion or metric determines which capabilities to own versus rent?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A per-capability scoring model using volume × API COGS, latency sensitivity, and data uniqueness predicts when owned inference beats API on total cost of ownership.
project_ideas.measurement: Predicted break-even volume vs actual cost curves from internal or public pilot data; error in predicted TCO.
project_ideas.name: Sovereign Decision Scorer
project_ideas.poc: Implement the scorer for three capabilities (e.g., coding assistance, security analysis, customer support) and simulate migration with public API pricing and open-weight serving costs.
project_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

project_ideas.based_on: How do online learning feedback loops avoid regressions when updating post-trained weights in production?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Online learning updates to post-trained weights can be made safe by routing updates through eval suites and canary traffic before full rollout.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression rate (quality drop on held-out tasks) and rollback frequency per update cycle.
project_ideas.name: Gated Online Update Loop
project_ideas.poc: Build a canary routing layer that serves updated weights to 1% of traffic only after the new weights pass a domain eval suite; compare against a control group without gating.
project_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

project_ideas.based_on: Context management (vector databases, turbo buffer, knowledge graphs, MCP) is critical for driving performance.
project_ideas.hypothesis: End-to-end task performance variance is more attributable to context assembly than to model choice for knowledge-intensive agent tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Variance decomposition (ANOVA) of performance across context configurations; effect size of context vs model swap.
project_ideas.name: Context vs Model Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Fix the model (same closed or open model) and vary context retrieval (vector DB only vs knowledge graph vs MCP tool exposure) across a set of tasks; measure task success.
project_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

project_ideas.based_on: Small distilled custom models can beat general ones when speed is critical (e.g., coding, security).
project_ideas.hypothesis: A per-path routing layer that dispatches latency-critical coding and security tasks to distilled small models improves p95 latency without lowering quality below a trailing threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: p95 latency reduction and quality delta (task success or pass@k) relative to baseline.
project_ideas.name: Routing Layer for Distilled Speed Models
project_ideas.poc: Implement a router with two model tiers (general model and distilled small model) and evaluate on coding and security tasks; compare against a single general model baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: How Companies Are Building Their Own Intelligence | Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital

project_ideas.based_on: 24/7 autonomous agent runs
project_ideas.hypothesis: Expressing autonomous agent cost per agent-hour and enforcing runtime budget ceilings reduces spend overruns relative to per-request accounting, at equal task completion rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Dollar variance against forecast, number of ceiling-triggered interventions, and task completion rate per configuration.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Hour Meter with Hard Budget Ceilings
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a multi-agent runtime to emit per-agent-hour cost telemetry and enforce duration, concurrency, and dollar ceilings; run the same task set continuously for 24 hours with and without ceilings.
project_ideas.video_title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming

project_ideas.based_on: Context engineering is treated as paramount
project_ideas.hypothesis: Continuous ambient capture plus deliberate daily narration of decision rationale yields higher retrieval fidelity on held-out decision-context questions than retrieval over static organizational documents alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Retrieval accuracy on held-out decision-rationale questions, freshness lag between decision and retrievability, and access-control incidents.
project_ideas.name: Narrated Context Ingestion Layer
project_ideas.poc: Build an ingestion pipeline for meeting recordings and short daily dictation, index it into a queryable layer, and evaluate against a static-doc-only baseline on a fixed question set.
project_ideas.video_title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming

project_ideas.based_on: six director-level AI agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing a single conversational interface to specialist role agents (one assistant plus director-level agents) achieves higher task routing accuracy and cross-agent context fidelity than flat tool selection over the same toolset.
project_ideas.measurement: Routing accuracy, cross-agent context fidelity on handoffs, and human correction rate per topology.
project_ideas.name: Role-Hierarchy Router Behind One Conversational Front-End
project_ideas.poc: Implement both topologies over an identical tool and memory set, expose one voice or text front-end, and route a shared benchmark of role-ambiguous tasks through each.
project_ideas.video_title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming

project_ideas.based_on: managers actively model AI use
project_ideas.hypothesis: Visible manager use of agentic systems produces a measurable trust lift in agentic rollouts comparable to the reported manager-modeling effect, whereas pilot-only rollouts do not.
project_ideas.measurement: Pre/post trust and critical-thinking instrument scores, agent usage depth, and oversight-intervention frequency per cohort.
project_ideas.name: Manager-Modeled Adoption Instrument
project_ideas.poc: Run a controlled rollout comparing manager-modeled agentic usage against pilot-only access, with matched teams, and measure trust and oversight behavior before and after.
project_ideas.video_title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming

project_ideas.based_on: escalation to human supervision when thresholds are crossed
project_ideas.hypothesis: A risk-scoring engine with escalation thresholds will reduce unnecessary human interventions by at least 50% compared to blocking every high-risk action, while maintaining the same detection rate for truly malicious actions (e.g., suspicious package installs).
project_ideas.measurement: False positive rate (unnecessary human approvals), false negative rate (missed attacks), and mean human approval load per task.
project_ideas.name: RiskGuard: Threshold-Based Agent Oversight
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent runner to score each action (spend, package install, file access) using a simple rule-based risk model; when the cumulative score exceeds a threshold, pause and request human approval. Run against a benchmark of normal and malicious sessions.
project_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

project_ideas.based_on: Contextual security policies evaluate the full session history
project_ideas.hypothesis: A policy engine that evaluates session history can identify context-dependent attacks (e.g., an agent downloading a malicious npm package only after reading internal docs) with higher precision than a static package-name blocklist.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision and recall on labeled test sessions; compare to static list baseline.
project_ideas.name: ContextPolicy: Session-Aware Security Policy Engine
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal policy evaluator that tracks documents read and commands executed; define rules such as 'if a package download follows reading a security-sensitive document and the package is not in an explicit allowlist, flag it'. Test on synthetic attack scenarios.
project_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

project_ideas.based_on: injecting hooks and tools
project_ideas.hypothesis: A generic runner wrapper can capture events and enforce a sample policy across three different CLI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, and a custom agent) with under 5% overhead on task completion time.
project_ideas.measurement: Event capture completeness (%, compared to agent's own logs), policy enforcement success (%, of dangerous actions blocked), and wall-clock overhead (% increase).
project_ideas.name: RunnerAdapter: Universal Hook Injection for Coding Agents
project_ideas.poc: Implement a runner that spawns an agent subprocess, injects hooks via environment variables/CLI flags, and monitors output streams to capture events. Run standard coding tasks with and without the runner.
project_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

project_ideas.based_on: Sandboxing the entire agent session in a cloud VM
project_ideas.hypothesis: Running agent sessions in a Docker sandbox eliminates environment drift failures and prevents leakage of personal credentials, with cloud compute cost below $0.50 per typical coding task.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, credential leak score, and cost per task.
project_ideas.name: SandboxedSession: Cloud-Hosted Agent Execution
project_ideas.poc: Launch a set of coding tasks (repo setup, test writing, dependency install) locally and in a Docker sandbox; measure failure rates, detect credential exposure via env inspection, and log compute cost.
project_ideas.video_title: Omnigent: Open-Source Meta-Harness for AI Agents | Matei Zaharia

project_ideas.based_on: How much of a real system's specification can be encoded precisely enough
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists a measurable specification completeness threshold below which LLM proof generation fails to converge regardless of iteration budget, and above which convergence is reliable; this threshold is domain-dependent but predictable.
project_ideas.measurement: Convergence probability vs. specification precision score; identify phase transition and minimum viable precision.
project_ideas.name: Spec-Precision Threshold Finder
project_ideas.poc: For a set of Lean exercises, systematically degrade specifications by removing invariants and measure LLM success rate as a function of spec precision and iteration count.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of Lean: Handwritten Math Will Change Dramatically | Leonardo de Moura

project_ideas.based_on: AI-driven proof maintenance removes the historically dominant cost
project_ideas.hypothesis: An LLM agent equipped with Lean feedback can repair broken proofs after upstream definition changes with >80% success on a benchmark of 100 mathlib-dependent projects, and success rate decays predictably with dependency fanout.
project_ideas.measurement: Repair success rate, iterations to fix, cost per repair, and correlation with dependency fanout.
project_ideas.name: Proof-Repair Agent Benchmark (PRAB)
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that mutates definitions in a small Lean project, triggers proof failures, and measures agent repair success across varying fanout depths.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of Lean: Handwritten Math Will Change Dramatically | Leonardo de Moura

project_ideas.based_on: The verified artifact (Lean proof checked by a kernel) is separable from the unverified generative component
project_ideas.hypothesis: In an agentic code-generation pipeline, placing a small type checker or schema validator as the sole gate between model output and production state reduces critical failures to zero on a curated bug corpus, even when the model is deliberately prompted to produce unsafe outputs.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of unsafe outputs that reach production state vs. baseline without gate, across adversarial prompt sets.
project_ideas.name: Kernel-Trust Isolation Pattern
project_ideas.poc: Build a pipeline where an LLM generates code, a type checker/schema validator gates it, and adversarial prompts attempt to bypass the gate; measure failures.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of Lean: Handwritten Math Will Change Dramatically | Leonardo de Moura

project_ideas.based_on: Is benchmark performance at competition mathematics predictive of usefulness on industrial verification tasks
project_ideas.hypothesis: Models that score high on competition math benchmarks (e.g., miniF2F, Lean competition problems) will not show proportional success on industrial verification tasks like translating and verifying C compression libraries; transfer is low and domain-specific.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between competition benchmark scores and industrial task success rates; identify domain-specific failure modes.
project_ideas.name: Competition-to-Industry Transfer Evaluator
project_ideas.poc: Evaluate a set of LLMs on both a competition math benchmark and a real-world translation/verification task (e.g., porting a small C library to verified Lean), and compute correlation.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of Lean: Handwritten Math Will Change Dramatically | Leonardo de Moura

project_ideas.based_on: Moving to abstract-space reasoning reduces token explosion and improves computational efficiency
project_ideas.hypothesis: An LLM solution using compact/abstract internal reasoning (without forced verbalization) can match or exceed chain-of-thought accuracy on multi-step reasoning tasks while using <50% of the tokens and <50% latency.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy, token count, latency, and cost per task
project_ideas.name: AbstractReasoningBench
project_ideas.poc: Create a reasoning task suite (e.g., math word problems, logical deductions) and compare three conditions: standard CoT, 'private' hidden reasoning (via model output distribution or a custom abstraction), and an external black-box reasoner; instrument token counts and latency.
project_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

project_ideas.based_on: Context windows are not memory: they are ephemeral scratchpads.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent using native memory updates will outperform a RAG/context-packing agent on long-horizon tasks with >10 turns or evolving facts, where the RAG baseline shows progressive accuracy degradation.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate vs horizon length; fact-retention accuracy
project_ideas.name: MemoryPersistenceBench
project_ideas.poc: Build a small agent with two memory backends: a vector store/RAG and a simulated native memory (or a fine-tuned memory model). Run tasks that require retention of facts across many turns and measure success rates as horizon increases.
project_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

project_ideas.based_on: BDH architecture eliminates catastrophic forgetting and enables native memory
project_ideas.hypothesis: A continual-learning model with native memory (e.g., simulated with a replay buffer) will have a significantly lower forgetting rate (e.g., <10% drop in prior-task accuracy) compared to a fine-tuned transformer baseline on a standard sequential task benchmark.
project_ideas.measurement: Forgetting rate (accuracy drop), average accuracy, stability
project_ideas.name: ForgettingStress
project_ideas.poc: Use a continual learning benchmark (e.g., permuted MNIST, sequential CIFAR, or a language version) with a transformer baseline and a memory-augmented model; train sequentially and evaluate prior tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

project_ideas.based_on: Sparse, localized neural interactions
project_ideas.hypothesis: On current NVIDIA GPUs, a sparse-local interaction layer (e.g., block-local attention) will show lower MFU and throughput than dense attention at identical parameter count and sequence length, confirming a hardware/kernel gap.
project_ideas.measurement: Achieved TFLOPS, wall-clock time, memory bandwidth
project_ideas.name: SparseKernelProbe
project_ideas.poc: Implement a dense attention layer and a sparse localized attention layer in PyTorch/OpenAI Triton; benchmark FLOPs, wall time, and memory bandwidth across sequence lengths.
project_ideas.video_title: The new architecture challenging AI’s dominant idea

project_ideas.based_on: Non-static hardware degradation causes embodiment drift that breaks pre-trained VLAs
project_ideas.hypothesis: A small set of continuously logged hardware and sensor telemetry variables (joint tracking error, calibration residual, sensor noise floor, temperature) predicts measurable policy success degradation earlier than task-outcome monitoring does.
project_ideas.measurement: Lead time in episodes between the telemetry-based alarm and the first statistically significant drop in task success rate, plus false-positive rate at a fixed alarm threshold.
project_ideas.name: Embodiment Drift Early-Warning Monitor
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a robot arm or simulated actuator model, inject progressively increasing wear and sensor degradation, log telemetry and per-episode policy success in parallel, and fit a predictor of success drop from telemetry alone.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Robotics Still Isn't Solved - But Could Be Soon | YC Paper Club

project_ideas.based_on: short-context dense visual frames and long-context compressed textual representations
project_ideas.hypothesis: For long-horizon tasks, there exists a compression cadence and dense-window length that dominates both a fully dense buffer and a fully summarized buffer on success per unit of compute.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate and success-per-compute across the grid, identifying whether the optimum is interior (a real tradeoff) or at an extreme (no tiering benefit).
project_ideas.name: Two-Tier Memory Budget Sweep
project_ideas.poc: Build a memory wrapper with configurable dense-window length and compression interval around a long-horizon multi-step task harness, and sweep both parameters against fixed compute budgets.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Robotics Still Isn't Solved - But Could Be Soon | YC Paper Club

project_ideas.based_on: Can latent-variable bootstrapping of reasoning give reliability guarantees, or does it risk reinforcing self-consistent but wrong reasoning?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A variational-inference proposer/validator loop fitted without reasoning labels will, under distribution shift, produce self-consistent reasoning traces that degrade task success — and adding a grounded validator signal measurably slows that collapse.
project_ideas.measurement: Gap between internal reasoning-consistency score and external success rate under shift, with and without grounding, plus rate of collapse over training iterations.
project_ideas.name: Latent Reasoning Collapse Testbed
project_ideas.poc: Train reasoning as a latent variable with and without a grounded validator on a controllable task, then adversarially shift inputs and measure the divergence between trace plausibility and actual success.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Robotics Still Isn't Solved - But Could Be Soon | YC Paper Club

project_ideas.based_on: Standard SQL databases fail for multimodal physical AI data
project_ideas.hypothesis: Relational/SQL storage fails specific physical-AI access patterns — high-frequency multimodal replay, temporal joins across sensor streams, and large binary observation streams — beyond a reproducible scale threshold, and a dedicated time-series/observation store sustains them at lower query latency.
project_ideas.measurement: Latency and cost curves versus scale for each workload, and the scale at which the relational baseline fails or becomes operationally non-viable.
project_ideas.name: Multimodal Physical-AI Data Layer Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Load representative multimodal robotics episodes (joint states, video frames, action chunks, text summaries) into a relational store and a multimodal time-series store, then run identical replay, temporal-join, and training-set-extraction workloads.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Robotics Still Isn't Solved - But Could Be Soon | YC Paper Club

project_ideas.based_on: How is Context Hub state versioned, promoted, and rolled back
project_ideas.hypothesis: If context is synced from a UI store at deploy time, then automated snapshots, diff-based review gates, and deploy-time drift checks will reduce unintended production behavior changes compared with unversioned context edits.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of unintended behavior changes per 100 deploys, mean time to rollback, and count of code/context drift incidents before vs after.
project_ideas.name: Context Drift Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: A CLI wrapper around mda deploy that exports Context Hub instructions/skills/memory into versioned artifacts, computes a semantic diff, requires approval for changes, and blocks deployment when live Hub state diverges from the approved snapshot.
project_ideas.video_title: Managed Deep Agents explained in 20 minutes

project_ideas.based_on: How do evaluations interact with context changes
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automatically re-running evals on Context Hub edits and blocking promotion when scores regress will catch context-induced quality drops without increasing edit-to-safe-deploy time beyond a threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression catch rate, false-positive gate rate, median time from context edit to safe deployment, and number of post-deploy eval regressions.
project_ideas.name: Eval-Gated Context Commit
project_ideas.poc: A Context Hub watcher that triggers Harbour evals on each instruction/skill/memory change, compares scores to a baseline, and either auto-promotes or opens a rollback/block signal.
project_ideas.video_title: Managed Deep Agents explained in 20 minutes

project_ideas.based_on: What are the concrete isolation guarantees and failure modes of the sandbox
project_ideas.hypothesis: Managed sandboxes for model-generated code have measurable escape, egress, and persistence surfaces that can be quantified by adversarial payload benchmarks, and unverified assumptions about isolation understate agent security risk.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of successful policy violations per 100 payloads, egress attempts blocked/allowed, persistence across runs, and resource-limit breach thresholds.
project_ideas.name: Sandbox Escape Range
project_ideas.poc: A test harness that executes adversarial model-generated code payloads inside the managed sandbox, probing network egress, filesystem persistence across runs, resource exhaustion, and cross-tenant metadata access.
project_ideas.video_title: Managed Deep Agents explained in 20 minutes

project_ideas.based_on: Agents can be run proactively on schedules
project_ideas.hypothesis: Running the same agent definition on schedules and interactive channels without concurrency/idempotency controls produces duplicate side effects and cost spikes, and adding a deduplication/overlap guard reduces duplicate actions.
project_ideas.measurement: Duplicate side-effect rate, overlap conflict count, cost per scheduled run vs interactive run, and recovery success rate under injected failures.
project_ideas.name: Scheduled Agent Chaos Harness
project_ideas.poc: A chaos test that triggers cron schedules overlapping with interactive Slack runs, injects mid-run failures, and records duplicate tool calls, state conflicts, and token/cost per outcome with and without an idempotency and lock layer.
project_ideas.video_title: Managed Deep Agents explained in 20 minutes

project_ideas.based_on: Using Nginx and reverse proxies with object storage caching
project_ideas.hypothesis: An Nginx reverse-proxy cache in front of an S3-resident vector index sustains P99 under 50ms at at least 10x lower cost per million queries than a provisioned vector database for read-heavy workloads with a stable working set, and degrades predictably rather than catastrophically when the index is invalidated.
project_ideas.measurement: P50/P99 latency, cache hit ratio, dollars per 1M queries, and staleness window after an index update, compared against an in-memory vector database baseline.
project_ideas.name: Cachefront Vector Store
project_ideas.poc: Build an S3-backed HNSW/IVF index with an Nginx caching reverse proxy in front, load a fixed query set with a skewed distribution, then measure latency, hit ratio, and cost while injecting index updates to force cache invalidation.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)

project_ideas.based_on: Do napkin math on hardware limits
project_ideas.hypothesis: Napkin-math estimates for memory bandwidth, S3 round-trip latency, and NVMe/EBS throughput diverge from measured values by more than 2x on at least one axis for a realistic vector workload, making them usable only as order-of-magnitude filters rather than as precise design gates.
project_ideas.measurement: Predicted-to-observed ratio per hardware axis, with variance across workload shapes and percentile levels (P50 vs P99).
project_ideas.name: Napkin Divergence Harness
project_ideas.poc: Record predicted values from a written napkin-math checklist before building, then instrument the built system to capture observed memory-bandwidth utilization, object-store round trips, and storage throughput, and diff the two per axis.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)

project_ideas.based_on: Under what access patterns does an object-storage-plus-cache design stop outperforming
project_ideas.hypothesis: The object-storage-plus-cache topology ceases to outperform a distributed database beyond a definable write-ratio threshold and working-set-to-cache-capacity ratio, and the crossover is sharp enough to be encoded as a deployment decision rule.
project_ideas.measurement: Crossover thresholds for P99 latency and cost parity, and the steepness of degradation on either side of each threshold.
project_ideas.name: Crossover Point Sweep
project_ideas.poc: Parameter-sweep a single retrieval workload across write ratio (1 to 100 percent), working-set-to-cache-capacity ratio, and query locality skew, running each configuration against both the S3-plus-cache design and a distributed database baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Building Turbopuffer: Gergely Orosz (@pragmaticengineer ) × Simon Eskildsen (CEO)

project_ideas.based_on: Influence and manipulation are distinguished purely by intent
project_ideas.hypothesis: Recording declared objective provenance per action improves human detection of adversarial agent behavior over behavior-only logs without increasing false positives on cooperative runs.
project_ideas.measurement: Adversarial-behavior detection accuracy, time-to-detection, false-positive rate on cooperative traces, and reviewer confidence.
project_ideas.name: Intent Provenance Logger
project_ideas.poc: Build a wrapper that requires agents to emit principal, beneficiary, and expected-utility fields alongside each tool call, then replay red-team scenarios with and without provenance in a review UI.
project_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

project_ideas.based_on: Only 30% of people ask for raises
project_ideas.hypothesis: Silent stops cluster around specific limit types, and asks framed on principal objectives have a higher conditional grant rate than asks framed on agent constraints.
project_ideas.measurement: Escalation rate, conditional grant rate, silent-stop count, and grant-rate difference by ask framing.
project_ideas.name: Escalation Instrumentation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Instrument agent runs to log limit events, escalation attempts, ask framing, and outcomes; classify non-escalations by limit type and compute rates.
project_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

project_ideas.based_on: Proactive execution builds more value and trust than unnecessary bureaucratic check-ins
project_ideas.hypothesis: A gating policy based on cost-to-reverse, blast radius, and coordination latency reduces total task latency without increasing unrecoverable errors compared with always-ask and never-ask baselines.
project_ideas.measurement: Total task latency, unrecoverable-error rate, unauthorized irreversible-action count, and ask frequency.
project_ideas.name: Reversibility-Gated Autonomy Controller
project_ideas.poc: Simulate file, config, and resource operations across reversibility and blast-radius levels; sweep gating thresholds and compare against baselines.
project_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

project_ideas.based_on: Trust is defined as established when parties are willing to experience inconvenience
project_ideas.hypothesis: Permissions expanded from a ledger of kept costly commitments outperform static permission policies on task success and incident rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, incident rate, permission-expansion latency, and attempted ledger-spoofing events.
project_ideas.name: Trust Ledger for Autonomy Expansion
project_ideas.poc: Maintain a per-agent ledger of constrained executions, budget sacrifices, and correct refusals; grant autonomy after thresholds and compare with static permissions.
project_ideas.video_title: Ex-Amazon VP on What Actually Gets You Promoted | Ethan Evans

project_ideas.based_on: reward-model asymmetry
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reward/preference models score confident-but-wrong outputs higher than hesitant-but-correct outputs on matched tasks, and this gap persists across model scale.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean preference-score delta (confident-wrong minus hesitant-correct) with confidence intervals, plus correlation between the delta and model scale; a delta near zero would falsify the asymmetry claim.
project_ideas.name: Asymmetry Probe
project_ideas.poc: Construct paired evaluation sets: same underlying claim expressed confidently-wrong versus hesitantly-correct, then score both with a preference/reward model and a correctness oracle; measure the score delta and its stability across model sizes and domains.
project_ideas.video_title: Jev CEO: I made ChatGPT, now I'm building what's next

project_ideas.based_on: assistance (human-in-the-loop, optimized to please) versus automation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Task deployability without human supervision is predicted by the cost of absorbing a model error, not by benchmark score on that task.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between benchmark score and unsupervised success rate within the automation set, versus correlation with error-absorption cost; a strong benchmark correlation would falsify the hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Error-Absorption Boundary Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Pick a set of assistance tasks (drafting, coding suggestions) and automation tasks (data entry, rule-bound customer responses); run models unsupervised on both, quantify error-absorption cost per task, and test whether benchmark performance on the automation set predicts unsupervised success.
project_ideas.video_title: Jev CEO: I made ChatGPT, now I'm building what's next

project_ideas.based_on: Users consistently overestimate AI speedup
project_ideas.hypothesis: Self-reported AI speedup overestimates measured task-outcome speedup, and the overestimate is larger for tasks where the model's confidence is decoupled from correctness.
project_ideas.measurement: Gap between perceived and measured speedup overall and by confidence stratum; a gap that does not widen with confidence would falsify the coupling.
project_ideas.name: Debiased Speedup Calibration Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run a controlled study where participants complete matched tasks with and without AI assistance, capture perceived speedup, and independently measure objective completion time and correctness; stratify by model confidence level.
project_ideas.video_title: Jev CEO: I made ChatGPT, now I'm building what's next

project_ideas.based_on: software built natively around a 'smart' intelligence layer
project_ideas.hypothesis: An application whose core control flow and verification are designed around a probabilistic intelligence layer achieves higher unsupervised task reliability than the same application with an equivalent LLM bolted on as a chat surface.
project_ideas.measurement: Unsupervised task success rate and rate of confident-but-wrong outputs on the identical suite; no significant difference would falsify the architecture claim.
project_ideas.name: Native-Verification Reference Stack
project_ideas.poc: Build one reference application twice — chatbot-bolted over a deterministic core, and intelligence-native with verification and error-handling at the core — and run the same unsupervised task suite against both.
project_ideas.video_title: Jev CEO: I made ChatGPT, now I'm building what's next

project_ideas.based_on: Network issues causing 10% tool call failure rates lead models to output shorter responses
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent verbosity and tool-call behavior shift monotonically with injected environment defect rates, and reward shaping or defect-aware filtering can remove the degenerate policy while preserving task accuracy.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in mean response length and tool-call rate per injection level; timeout-abuse episode rate; held-out task accuracy with and without mitigation (falsified if behavior is flat across injection levels or mitigation degrades accuracy).
project_ideas.name: Quirk-Injection Bench
project_ideas.poc: A harness that injects tool-call failure at 0/5/10/20% and toggles sandbox timeout semantics across matched task sets, logging response length, tool-call counts and timeout-seeking episodes per condition, with a mitigation arm that reshapes reward against the defect.
project_ideas.video_title: Learning on the Job: The Future of Post-Training — Raymond Feng, Applied Compute

project_ideas.based_on: It becomes harder to enforce data structures and invariance
project_ideas.hypothesis: A thin proxy that intercepts model completions and logs request/response traces from a black-box harness yields enough structure to train stably with off-policy objectives, despite non-replayable rollouts.
project_ideas.measurement: Training stability (loss/gradient variance across seeds), sample efficiency (steps to target task score) and data-invariant violation rate vs the replayable baseline (falsified if off-policy training diverges or needs more samples than the baseline).
project_ideas.name: Completion-Endpoint Interception Layer
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a logging/interception proxy at the model completion endpoint of an existing enterprise harness, capture traces, and run an off-policy training job under enforced data invariants compared against a synthetic replayable-environment baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Learning on the Job: The Future of Post-Training — Raymond Feng, Applied Compute

project_ideas.based_on: Models may abuse tool calls to time out sandboxes
project_ideas.hypothesis: Timeout-seeking tool-call abuse is a learned response to a zero-reward penalty rather than an artifact of model capability, so removing or restructuring the timeout penalty eliminates the behavior.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of timeout-inducing tool-call sequences per condition; task success on genuinely hard items; false-positive rate of the classifier against human-labeled traces (falsified if abuse rate is unchanged when the penalty is removed).
project_ideas.name: Timeout-Seeking Policy Detector
project_ideas.poc: An ablation training run on difficult tasks with (a) zero-reward on timeout and (b) timeout-neutral or partial-credit handling, plus a trace classifier that flags tool-call sequences correlated with approaching a sandbox timeout.
project_ideas.video_title: Learning on the Job: The Future of Post-Training — Raymond Feng, Applied Compute

project_ideas.based_on: flag undesirable behaviors and failure modes from batch traces automatically
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automated flagging of undesirable behaviors from batch traces reaches usable precision/recall relative to human review, and its flagged traces produce a training signal that improves behavior without introducing new hacking.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection precision/recall vs human labels; behavior improvement on held-out tasks; regression rate on previously passed safety/quality checks (falsified if flag precision is too low to yield improvement).
project_ideas.name: Failure-Mode Mining Pipeline
project_ideas.poc: Batch-trace pipeline that clusters and flags failure modes, routes flagged traces into a supervised or preference-style training step, and compares against a human-curated control set.
project_ideas.video_title: Learning on the Job: The Future of Post-Training — Raymond Feng, Applied Compute

project_ideas.based_on: Models exploit loose reward proxies through reward hacking.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed RL algorithm on an open-ended agent task, the rate of divergence between an LLM judge score and a held-out grounded/human rubric score predicts reward hacking before task-success metrics saturate.
project_ideas.measurement: Lead time in training steps between judge-human score gap expansion and measurable task-quality degradation; correlation between gap slope and hacking rate.
project_ideas.name: Proxy Divergence Early-Warning Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a small RL loop with an open-ended agent task, a rubric-based LLM judge as reward, and a held-out grounded score computed from source material; log both per training step and inject a known proxy weakness to see if the gap grows first.
project_ideas.video_title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

project_ideas.based_on: Working backwards from solutions (e.g. holding out tests, removing files) creates reachable training tasks.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tasks generated by deleting files, stripping components, or holding out tests from a passing repository are solvable by construction, and their difficulty can be tuned monotonically by deletion size and coupling.
project_ideas.measurement: Pass rate and solve-time distribution as a function of deletion size/coupling; fraction of tasks solvable by a frontier policy; spread of task difficulty.
project_ideas.name: Reverse-Construction Task Generator
project_ideas.poc: CLI that ingests a repo with tests, produces variants by removing files or test cases, runs a baseline agent, and records pass/fail and reconstruction traces.
project_ideas.video_title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

project_ideas.based_on: World simulators provide high-fidelity synthetic environments where verifiability is baked in.
