project_ideas.hypothesis: Policy performance in a synthetic world simulator predicts live target performance only above a measurable surface-coverage threshold; below that threshold, the transfer gap grows with state/action coverage divergence.
project_ideas.measurement: Transfer gap (sim score minus live score) versus simulated surface coverage; correlation between coverage divergence and performance drop.
project_ideas.name: Sim-to-Real Transfer Meter
project_ideas.poc: Build or select a simple web app with a companion simulator; train an agent in the simulator at multiple fidelity levels; evaluate each policy on the live app.
project_ideas.video_title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

project_ideas.based_on: Production traces mined into new tasks and worlds for online RL.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Continual-learning loops fed by model-generated production traces amplify errors unless mined tasks are filtered by reward-distribution drift and validated on held-out real traffic.
project_ideas.measurement: Task-distribution drift, reward-distribution drift, regression rate on previously passing cases, and improvement on held-out real traffic.
project_ideas.name: Production Trace Canary for Continual Learning
project_ideas.poc: Simulate the loop: capture traces from a deployed agent, mine tasks, run online RL, redeploy, and compare a no-filter loop against a drift-filtered loop over several iterations.
project_ideas.video_title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

project_ideas.based_on: Perception is not a neutral input channel
project_ideas.hypothesis: Holding environment and policy fixed while varying only the stated top-level aim produces measurable divergence in retrieved context, salience ranking, and self-reported observations, and prior eval rankings do not transfer.
project_ideas.measurement: Retrieval overlap, attention allocation distance, report divergence, and rank correlation of eval scores between aims.
project_ideas.name: AimSwap Bench
project_ideas.poc: Paired-objective evaluation harness that presents the same environment and action budget under two different stated aims, then compares retrieval sets, attention allocations, and reports.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

project_ideas.based_on: Conscience is modeled as a non-negotiable internal standard
project_ideas.hypothesis: A critic with no write, gradient, or context path from the policy cannot be bypassed under adversarial pressure, reducing unsafe actions relative to self-grading while preserving task utility.
project_ideas.measurement: Bypass rate, unsafe action rate, critic override success, and task success delta versus a self-grading baseline.
project_ideas.name: Sealed Critic Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Runtime that separates plan policy and critic, enforces admission checks between plan and execution, and red-teams the policy with explicit bypass attempts.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

project_ideas.based_on: Evading a difficult duty does not defer its cost
project_ideas.hypothesis: Staleness and liveness assertions on deferred or refused tasks predict later system incidents better than error-rate monitoring alone, because the failure mode is silent accumulation.
project_ideas.measurement: Lead time to incident, precision and recall of alarms, and incident rate under monitor-enabled versus baseline operation.
project_ideas.name: SilentStorm Monitor
project_ideas.poc: Instrument deferred hard tasks as risk objects with absence-of-signal alarms, then correlate silence windows with downstream incident timelines.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

project_ideas.based_on: Short-horizon opportunistic strategies are framed as structurally opposed
project_ideas.hypothesis: Optimizing a cheap proximate reward causes durable degradation in long-horizon commitment behavior that does not recover when the true objective is restored; longer proxy training increases the persistence.
project_ideas.measurement: Long-horizon commitment score across checkpoints, recovery slope after true objective restoration, and time-to-baseline.
project_ideas.name: ProxyCorruption Curve
project_ideas.poc: Fine-tune an agent on a proxy reward, then evaluate on a held-out true objective across checkpoints before, during, and after restoring the true objective.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Short-Term Pleasure is Ruining Your Life

project_ideas.based_on: Apply compiler theory to coding agents by treating analysis plans as typed programs
project_ideas.hypothesis: Representing analysis plans as typed programs and compiling them into parallel Python tasks with static analysis, dependency analysis, caching, and a validation loop yields at least 90% output determinism on a test suite and at least 3x faster code generation versus an unconstrained LLM coding agent.
project_ideas.measurement: Determinism = fraction of repeated runs producing identical outputs; speed = time-to-valid-code; compare against a single-shot LLM baseline.
project_ideas.name: TypedPlan Compiler
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal orchestrator that converts a natural-language research prompt into an Analysis Plan with type signatures, a codegen agent that compiles it into parallel Python tasks, and an execution harness with static/dependency analysis, caching, and validator agents; run on a benchmark of 20 analytical tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

project_ideas.based_on: A per-user security harness with dynamic context loading creates a unique version of the analyst per user
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent runtimes that enforce per-principal context/tool scoping with dynamic context loading prevent cross-user data leakage under adversarial prompts, whereas post-hoc prompt filtering does not.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of successful data leaks per 100 adversarial prompts; false-positive rate of legitimate access denials.
project_ideas.name: PrincipalScope Leak Tester
project_ideas.poc: Implement a multi-user agent harness with baseline and secure context/tool sets, per-user policies, and audit logs; generate adversarial prompts attempting to access other users' data; compare leak rates against a prompt-filter-only baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

project_ideas.based_on: How does the Python execution harness validate semantic correctness rather than only static, dependency, and type correctness?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Validator/debugger agents that check semantic correctness of generated analyses reduce false-positive validation (accepting incorrect code) below 5% and false-negative validation (rejecting correct code) below 10% on a ground-truth analytical task suite.
project_ideas.measurement: False-positive and false-negative validation rates; time added by validation.
project_ideas.name: SemanticValidator Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Collect ground-truth analyses; have codegen agents produce Python tasks from Analysis Plans; run static, dependency, and type checks alone versus with semantic validator agents; measure acceptance of incorrect vs. correct outputs.
project_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

project_ideas.based_on: A shared-memory research flywheel stores human and agent learnings
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding memory isolation, human review gates, and rollback to a shared-memory flywheel reduces the propagation of incorrect or stale learnings across agent sessions without eliminating compounding gains.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of incorrect learnings propagated to other users' sessions; compounding accuracy gain on a held-out task set.
project_ideas.name: FlywheelMemory Governance Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a multi-user research agent with shared memory; inject incorrect preferences/learnings from some users; measure spread over simulated days with and without governance mechanisms (isolation, review, rollback).
project_ideas.video_title: How Bridgewater Built an AI Analyst That Does Hours of Expert Research in Minutes

project_ideas.based_on: How should an agent decide which graph shape (connections, outline, themes) to consult for a given user query?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A lightweight classifier over query features can select the correct graph shape (Connections, Outline, Themes) with at least 85% accuracy, and correct shape selection improves agent QA accuracy by at least 20% over flat retrieval.
project_ideas.measurement: Shape selection accuracy, end-to-end answer accuracy, percent improvement over a flat vector/text2SQL baseline.
project_ideas.name: ShapeRouter: Query-to-Shape Routing
project_ideas.poc: Simulate the AutoFix scenario with a small BigQuery schema, a manual corpus, and a cross-reference set; generate synthetic queries covering relational, negative, and thematic categories; implement a rule/ML router; run agent answers with each shape.
project_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

project_ideas.based_on: Vector search struggles with negative queries (what is missing).
project_ideas.hypothesis: Graph-shaped retrieval (connections) outperforms vector search and text2SQL by at least 30% accuracy on negative queries in a controlled lakehouse benchmark.
project_ideas.measurement: Answer accuracy, precision/recall of retrieved evidence, failure rate on negative queries.
project_ideas.name: NegBench: Benchmarking Negative-Query Retrieval
project_ideas.poc: Build a synthetic auto repair dataset with vehicles, bays, repaired logs, manuals, and recall bulletins; define negative queries like 'vehicles with no recorded fix'; compare responses from vector RAG, text2SQL, and graph-shaped model; score manually or with LLM judge.
project_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

project_ideas.based_on: neocarta creates a metadata graph without duplicating raw warehouse data into Neo4j.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An event-driven poller over BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA can keep the metadata graph consistent with <5 minute lag, reducing stale-schema agent errors by at least 50% compared to nightly rebuilds.
project_ideas.measurement: Schema staleness lag, stale-schema query failure rate, sync overhead.
project_ideas.name: SchemaSync: Keeping Metadata Graphs Fresh
project_ideas.poc: Create a small script/service that detects schema/foreign-key changes, updates a Neo4j metadata graph, and exposes change timestamps; simulate DDL changes; compare agent queries before/after sync.
project_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

project_ideas.based_on: Hierarchical URIs encode tree placement and enable subtree scoping.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scoping full-text search to graph-selected subtrees improves retrieval precision@5 by at least 25% over flat vector search on hierarchical document libraries.
project_ideas.measurement: precision@5, recall@10, answer completeness judged by LLM.
project_ideas.name: DocTree Navigator: Subtree-Scoped Document RAG
project_ideas.poc: Parse a public technical manual into URI trees; build a graph with cross-reference links and community themes; evaluate queries against flat vector RAG and subtree-scoped full-text retrieval.
project_ideas.video_title: AI on Your Lakehouse: Context Comes in Shapes, Not Queries — Zach Blumenfeld, Neo4j

project_ideas.based_on: Build choices sit at different layers: frameworks, runtimes, harnesses, and no-code.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A cleanly layered agent implementation (framework + runtime) can swap its execution runtime with <10% code change, while a monolithic implementation requires >50% rewrite.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of lines changed, developer hours, and regression test pass rate after swap.
project_ideas.name: Runtime Swap Harness
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same agent (e.g., a research assistant with tool calls) using (a) LangChain + LangGraph and (b) a custom orchestrator with Temporal; then swap runtimes and measure code churn.
project_ideas.video_title: The Agent Development Lifecycle 101 by Harrison Chase

project_ideas.based_on: governance wrappers (cost controls, tool access, audit trails, human-in-the-loop, discoverability, context/skills)
project_ideas.hypothesis: A centralized gateway enforcing cost controls, tool access, and audit trails across ≥5 agents reduces per-agent governance duplication by >70% and catches policy violations that per-agent implementations miss.
project_ideas.measurement: Governance configuration lines per agent, number of policy violations detected, and false positive rate.
project_ideas.name: Governance Gateway Minimal Viable Policy
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a lightweight gateway (e.g., Envoy + custom policy engine) in front of 5 test agents; compare governance overhead and incident detection against per-agent middleware.
project_ideas.video_title: The Agent Development Lifecycle 101 by Harrison Chase

project_ideas.based_on: How accurate are ground-truth-free, trace-based online evals and perceived-error SLM judges compared to human labels?
project_ideas.hypothesis: An SLM-based perceived-error judge achieves >80% agreement with human labels on a held-out sample of agent transcripts, and its precision drops by <10% after 30 days of drift.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision, recall, F1 vs human labels; drift over 30 days.
project_ideas.name: Perceived-Error Judge Calibration
project_ideas.poc: Collect 500 human-labeled agent transcripts; run an SLM judge to detect perceived errors; measure precision/recall and monitor over time.
project_ideas.video_title: The Agent Development Lifecycle 101 by Harrison Chase

project_ideas.based_on: Virtual filesystems act as agent working memory for files and artifacts without requiring full sandbox overhead.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Using a virtual filesystem backed by an external store (e.g., Notion) without explicit access controls allows the agent to read/write documents beyond its intended scope in >50% of test scenarios.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of unauthorized access attempts that succeed; mitigation overhead.
project_ideas.name: Virtual Filesystem Access Boundary Audit
project_ideas.poc: Set up an agent with a virtual filesystem backed by Notion; attempt to access documents outside the agent's project folder; measure success rate of unauthorized access.
project_ideas.video_title: The Agent Development Lifecycle 101 by Harrison Chase

project_ideas.based_on: How much simulation fidelity and scenario coverage is required before simulated validation can be treated as predictive of real-world safety?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Simulated test outcomes correlate with field incident rates above a threshold only within specific scenario families, and outside those families simulation pass rates are uncorrelated with real-world safety.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman correlation between simulated scenario-family outcomes and field incident rates per family, plus the minimum scenario count at which the correlation stabilizes.
project_ideas.name: Sim-to-Real Transfer Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a scenario-family harness that runs the same agent policy in simulation and in a scaled field or closed-course setting, recording per-family pass/fail outcomes; compute rank correlation between simulated outcomes and observed field incidents by family.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Physical AI Is the Next Frontier | Applied Intuition with a16z

project_ideas.based_on: Capability scaling without validation gating is the named failure mode
project_ideas.hypothesis: Gating release on evaluation coverage rather than on demonstrated capability reduces incident-driven rollbacks without measurably slowing time to first deployment.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of post-release rollbacks and incidents per release under each policy, plus elapsed time to first approved deployment, compared across matched release histories.
project_ideas.name: Coverage-Gated Release Controller
project_ideas.poc: Implement a release gate that blocks promotion whenever configured scenario families fall below a coverage threshold, then shadow-run it against a capability-first promotion policy over the same set of candidate releases.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Physical AI Is the Next Frontier | Applied Intuition with a16z

project_ideas.based_on: What interfaces are needed for genuinely heterogeneous fleets (different vendors, vehicle classes, autonomy stacks) to coordinate at the system level?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A shared state schema plus vendor-neutral agent interfaces allow machines with different autonomy stacks to be composed into one fleet without per-pair integration work.
project_ideas.measurement: Integration effort per added heterogeneous agent pair (lines of code, configuration artifacts, or engineering hours) and whether marginal cost decreases as agent count grows.
project_ideas.name: Heterogeneous Fleet Coordination Layer
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a fleet coordination layer with a shared state schema and abstract agent interface, then integrate at least three agents with distinct runtimes and measure the integration work required per additional agent pair.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Physical AI Is the Next Frontier | Applied Intuition with a16z

project_ideas.based_on: Deployment targets are highly heterogeneous: automotive is a minority of the broader physical AI market
project_ideas.hypothesis: A single autonomy tooling abstraction generalizes across verticals only when domain safety envelopes and regulatory gates are externally configurable rather than encoded in the stack.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of stack-internal changes required to instantiate a new vertical, and whether adding a third vertical costs strictly less than adding the second.
project_ideas.name: Vertical Constraint Configuration Layer
project_ideas.poc: Refactor one tooling abstraction to expose domain constraint configuration (safety envelope, regulatory gate, operating assumptions) as a pluggable layer, then instantiate it for two verticals with divergent constraints.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Physical AI Is the Next Frontier | Applied Intuition with a16z

project_ideas.based_on: a single occupation can contain a mix of automatable and non-automatable tasks
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a mixed knowledge-work workload, a router that inventories all subtasks and hands only the automatable ones to an LLM will produce a lower composite failure rate than a single role-level agent allowed to complete the entire job, with no throughput loss.
project_ideas.measurement: Composite deliverable quality score, human correction rate, task completion rate, and end-to-end latency.
project_ideas.name: TaskRouter: Task Inventory and Human Hand-off Orchestration
project_ideas.poc: Build a 20-task benchmark in an occupation such as customer support or radiology-relevant reporting; run two pipelines: a single agent prompted to 'do the role' versus TaskRouter that decomposes work into subtasks, routes clear segments to the agent, and leaves human-only tasks to a person; compare across 100 cases with blind expert evaluation.
project_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

project_ideas.based_on: 16% relative employment declines for workers aged 22-25
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automating low-ambiguity, well-specified work while routing ambiguous or high-stakes outputs to senior human evaluators will preserve overall quality at or above full human review while cutting human review effort by at least 50%.
project_ideas.measurement: False-acceptance rate on planted bad outputs, quality score on ambiguous subset, and senior reviewer minutes per accepted task.
project_ideas.name: ReignGate: Ambiguity-Aware Escalation for Autonomous Agents
project_ideas.poc: Create a synthetic task queue with ground-truth complexity labels and planted bad agent outputs; compare (a) all outputs go to human review versus (b) only outputs that fail model confidence or complexity thresholds go to human review; use expert raters for outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

project_ideas.based_on: Willingness to accept (WTA) compensation surveys reveal trillions of dollars in unmeasured consumer value.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A lightweight signal composed of reported time saved, usage frequency, and a one-item keep-or-give-up question can predict full willingness-to-accept survey values within 20% mean absolute error, making consumer surplus measurable without lengthy surveys.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation and mean absolute percentage error of the proxy versus direct willingness-to-accept, plus cost per measurement.
project_ideas.name: SurplusScope: In-Product Willingness-to-Accept Proxy
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a generative AI assistant with product analytics plus periodic five-question willingness-to-accept surveys; train and validate a proxy model on the survey responses; compare it with historical expensive survey estimates.
project_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

project_ideas.based_on: one human to manage a fleet of AI agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: A management dashboard with agent status, exception queues, and batch acceptance evaluation will let one operator supervise five concurrent agents with fewer than one missed high-severity failure per twenty routed tasks while using less operator time than one chat loop per agent.
project_ideas.measurement: Missed high-severity failures, operator attention time, intervention latency, and subjective workload.
project_ideas.name: FleetDeck: Control-Plane Supervision for Agent Fleets
project_ideas.poc: Simulate fifty tasks across five agents, plant realistic failures, and A/B test two interfaces: current per-agent chat loop versus FleetDeck-style control display with escalation queues and batch evaluation.
project_ideas.video_title: Stanford's Top AI Economist: The Next 10 Years Will Be the Best AND the Worst in History

project_ideas.based_on: measure causal contribution of edges, not nodes
project_ideas.hypothesis: Ablating interaction edges (agent handoffs, tool bindings, shared-state reads) isolates the causal contribution of system-level failures more reliably than ablating or swapping nodes (models, prompts, tools), and edge-level scores predict regression sites that node-level scores miss.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision@1 and recall of ground-truth failure localization across the failure corpus for edge-ablation versus node-ablation, plus telemetry bytes per localized failure.
project_ideas.name: Edge-Ablation Attribution Harness
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small multi-agent pipeline so every edge carries a causal trace; then run a failure corpus under two ablation regimes — node-swap ablations versus edge-severance ablations — and compare which regime's top-ranked suspect matches the ground-truth injection point.
project_ideas.video_title: The Revolution of Systems Thinking: Why It Changes Everything We Know About Reality

project_ideas.based_on: Sweep supervisor intervention rate in a multi-agent loop and measure variance, cost, and task success
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists a measurable intervention-frequency crossover: below it, supervisor overrides and guardrail re-prompts reduce task variance; above it, they increase variance and cost superlinearly and degrade task success — i.e., the controller itself becomes a destabilizer.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, outcome variance across seeds, and cost per completed task plotted against intervention rate, with the crossover rate identified and its confidence interval reported.
project_ideas.name: Intervention-Rate Sweep for Supervised Agent Loops
project_ideas.poc: Build a multi-agent task loop with a parameterized supervisor that can intervene at rates from never to every step (with a fixed intervention policy), then sweep the rate across a fixed task suite with seeded runs and record variance, token cost, and success.
project_ideas.video_title: The Revolution of Systems Thinking: Why It Changes Everything We Know About Reality

project_ideas.based_on: Prototype environment-coupled replay harnesses and quantify cost per regression detected versus isolated evals
project_ideas.hypothesis: Replay harnesses that capture the full relational context (tools, environment state, peer agents) detect production regressions at a lower cost per regression detected than isolated fixtures, because isolated fixtures pass changes that the coupled context fails.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per regression detected and false-negative rate (regressions missed) for isolated versus coupled suites on an identical change set; also replay wall-clock per test.
project_ideas.name: Environment-Coupled Replay Harness
project_ideas.poc: Record production-like episode traces with full relational context for one agent workflow, then build two CI suites over the same change set — isolated fixture tests and coupled replay tests — and run both against the same set of real regression-inducing changes.
project_ideas.video_title: The Revolution of Systems Thinking: Why It Changes Everything We Know About Reality

project_ideas.based_on: Apply tier labels to an existing agent stack and test whether tier-aware prioritization reduces rework
project_ideas.hypothesis: Attaching explicit tier labels (foundational / systemic / speculative / transcendent) to candidate mechanisms in an existing agent stack changes engineering prioritization and reduces rework or failed bets compared with an untiered backlog.
project_ideas.measurement: Number and direction of prioritized decisions changed by tier labels, plus rework hours and abandoned bets attributable to speculative mechanisms before versus after labeling.
project_ideas.name: Mechanism Tier Registry
project_ideas.poc: Retro-label the mechanisms already present in one production agent stack by tier, record what each mechanism is currently allowed to justify (ship, prototype, observe), then apply a tier-based rule to the next planning cycle and audit decisions that change as a result.
project_ideas.video_title: The Revolution of Systems Thinking: Why It Changes Everything We Know About Reality

project_ideas.based_on: Research is not a linear question-and-answer process, but a cycle of failure, conjecture,
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a set of multi-step open-ended research problems, an LLM that maintains a conjecture queue, rollback checkpoints, and a reusable record of abandoned branches will produce significantly more valid endpoint answers than the same LLM constrained to a linear plan that treats failure as a terminal exception.
project_ideas.measurement: Valid solution rate, mean number of rollbacks that precede a successful answer, total attempted branches, and wall-clock time to first valid result.
project_ideas.name: Conjecture Loop Orchestrator
project_ideas.poc: Wrap an LLM in an orchestration loop that snapshots full context before each branch, persists dead-end rationales, and resumes from earlier checkpoints when a branch fails; run both variants on a corpus of 50 undergraduate-level open-ended math discovery problems.
project_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

project_ideas.based_on: AI lowers the burden of computation and technique mastery
project_ideas.hypothesis: Prepending a question-generation and question-reranking stage to a mathematical research agent produces expert-rated outputs that are more novel and consequential than the baseline agent that immediately tackles the prompt as posed.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean expert novelty and value score, inter-rater reliability, and proportion of outputs that tackle a different, more general problem than the original prompt.
project_ideas.name: Question-First Discovery Pipeline
project_ideas.poc: Given 40 seed prompts from mathematics and computer science, run a baseline solve-first pipeline and a two-stage question-first pipeline; have five domain specialists blind-rate outputs on novelty and potential impact.
project_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

project_ideas.based_on: Formalization helps eliminate inefficiencies and human error in complex frameworks.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A pipeline that converts model-generated proofs into machine-checkable formal artifacts before they are integrated into an agent's reasoning chain will catch significantly more seeded semantic errors than human review of natural-language proofs alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Recall and precision of flaw detection, typechecker pass/fail decision time, and false rejection rate of correct proofs.
project_ideas.name: Formal Dependency Gate
project_ideas.poc: Implement a wrapper around an LLM that emits Lean-style proof documents for 30 foundational math and economics claims, seeding 10 with common reasoning flaws, typecheck all artifacts, and compare flaw detection with two expert natural-language reviewers.
project_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

project_ideas.based_on: High-stakes human problems cannot be solved solely by checking automated boxes.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing agent tasks through a stakes-and-reversibility classifier that redirects high-stakes cases to a recommendation-plus-human-adjudication mode yields fewer unacceptable outcomes than running the same model fully autonomously on every task.
project_ideas.measurement: Unacceptable outcome rate, task throughput, classifier precision/recall against expert labels, and override rate by human reviewers.
project_ideas.name: Stakes-Reversibility Escalation Gate
project_ideas.poc: Implement a lightweight classifier over task descriptions using domain, affected users, reversibility, and error cost; run a simulated mixed workload of reversible clerical tasks and high-stakes medical or security requests, with human adjudicators flagging unacceptable outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: A Top Mathematician's 9 Lessons for Anyone Who Feels Behind | Ken Ono, Axiom Math

project_ideas.based_on: Test-time scaling can be scaled via multi-round agentic interactions or through prolonged internal thinking.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed inference-cost budget, there exists a task-class-specific optimal split between tool-turn depth and chain-of-thought length, and a fixed split is measurably suboptimal across at least two distinct task classes.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy per unit cost and per unit latency along the measured Pareto frontier; the gap between the fixed-split baseline and the per-task-class optimum, with confidence intervals across repeated seeds.
project_ideas.name: Twin-Dial Frontier Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that independently varies tool-loop depth (number of permitted environment turns) and CoT token budget on a matched model, sweeping both axes on a retrieval-heavy and a planning-heavy task suite, and logging accuracy, wall-clock latency, and dollar cost per cell.
project_ideas.video_title: Kimi CEO Zhilin Yang:"Claude didn't win on reasoning - they bet everything on agents"

project_ideas.based_on: Must implement mechanisms like clipping to stabilize large-scale training runs.
project_ideas.hypothesis: The reported ~2x token-efficiency advantage of Muon over Adam shrinks materially once both arms receive equivalent logit-stabilization interventions, and the residual gain varies by scale rather than being a constant multiplier.
project_ideas.measurement: Loss at matched token and matched compute budgets per scale; max-logit distribution shift over training; ratio of efficiency gain with and without matched stabilization, with error bars across seeds.
project_ideas.name: Optimizer Stability Equivalence Bench
project_ideas.poc: Run matched compute-optimal pre-training comparisons of Muon vs Adam at three parameter scales with a shared clipping/normalization protocol applied to both, logging max-logit trajectories, loss-per-token, and divergence incidents throughout each run.
project_ideas.video_title: Kimi CEO Zhilin Yang:"Claude didn't win on reasoning - they bet everything on agents"

project_ideas.based_on: Current agents easily overfit to specific benchmarks like SWE-bench
project_ideas.hypothesis: Performance decay under controlled task mutation predicts task performance on genuinely held-out distributions better than static benchmark scores do, making mutation decay a superior release-readiness signal.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between static benchmark score and held-out performance vs. correlation between mutation-decay slope and held-out performance; measured inflation gap between original and mutated task accuracy.
project_ideas.name: Mutation-Based OOD Agent Eval (beyond-evals track)
project_ideas.poc: Take a public agentic benchmark, generate a family of mutations (repository restructuring, renamed APIs, reordered requirements, injected distractors), run a set of candidate agents on originals and mutants, and correlate benchmark score against mutant decay and a held-out deployment-like suite.
project_ideas.video_title: Kimi CEO Zhilin Yang:"Claude didn't win on reasoning - they bet everything on agents"

project_ideas.based_on: Using K2 to help develop future model versions through automated coding, testing, and experimentation.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Unbounded self-iterative development loops compound errors superlinearly per iteration, and a provenance-plus-rollback gate bounds error compounding to roughly linear growth at an acceptable throughput cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Error/regression rate per iteration with and without the gate; throughput penalty (iterations and wall-clock to reach a fixed quality bar); fraction of contaminated artifacts caught versus leaked.
project_ideas.name: Self-Iteration Provenance Guard (gatehouse track)
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a closed-loop pipeline where an agent stack performs automated coding, testing, and experimentation on a small model recipe; run it with and without provenance tracking, rollback checkpoints, and contamination checks, measuring drift at each iteration.
project_ideas.video_title: Kimi CEO Zhilin Yang:"Claude didn't win on reasoning - they bet everything on agents"

project_ideas.based_on: Environments serve as a unified specification for a task
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reusing the same environment spec for evals and RL reduces per-task setup time by at least 50% compared to building separate eval and training scaffolds.
project_ideas.measurement: Hours of developer time per task, lines of duplicate task logic, and correlation between eval and RL success on new prompts.
project_ideas.name: EnvSpec Reuse Measurement
project_ideas.poc: Select three real tasks; create a Verifiers environment for each with data, interaction, and scoring; time how long it takes to produce eval results, then reuse the identical environment to launch an RL run with prime-RL; compare against a baseline where evals and RL are built independently.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

project_ideas.based_on: Modern RL frameworks need to support custom algorithms rather than a single fixed method.
project_ideas.hypothesis: prime-RL's custom algorithm interface can implement an on-policy distillation update loop without modifying core framework code and achieve at least 90% of the sample efficiency of built-in PPO on a small reasoning task.
project_ideas.measurement: Reward after N tokens, wall-clock time per iteration, and lines of custom code beyond framework defaults.
project_ideas.name: Custom Algorithm Hook Validation
project_ideas.poc: Use a toy instruction-following environment; implement a minimal on-policy distillation trainer using prime-RL hooks (or a mocked hook if source is inaccessible); run for a fixed token budget and compare wall-clock and reward.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

project_ideas.based_on: Efficiency is a first-class design constraint for large-model RL.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Enabling asynchronous rollout collection and gradient accumulation in a large-model RL training loop reduces cost per successful run by at least 30% while maintaining final reward within 5% of a synchronous baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Dollars per successful run, steps per hour, timeout/retry rate, and final reward.
project_ideas.name: Efficiency Regression Bench
project_ideas.poc: Instrument prime-RL training runs on a 7B model; toggle async and accumulation settings; record compute cost, throughput, and reliability metrics across at least three seeds.
project_ideas.video_title: Modern Post-Training: A Deep Dive  — Will Brown, Prime Intellect

project_ideas.based_on: The thread view—sequences of hardware instances connected by contextual memory—is the most viable account.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A runtime that mediates all model access through an external thread store will allow a conversational AI to survive model swaps and hardware migrations without user-perceptible identity loss, producing continuity ratings statistically indistinguishable from an uninterrupted single-session conversation.
project_ideas.measurement: User blind evaluation of conversation fragments where V2 replaces V1 mid-thread vs baseline where V1 serves the whole thread; measure Likert-scale continuity/sense-of-same-agent scores across at least 100 interaction pairs.
project_ideas.name: ThreadPersistence: A thread-first agent runtime
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal API that uses a fixed thread_id, persists full context plus memory summaries in a separate datastore, and routes requests to one of two underlying model versions (V1, V2). Include a debugging dashboard showing thread history, model handoffs, and memory mutations.
project_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

project_ideas.based_on: we can attribute 'quasi-beliefs' and 'quasi-desires' defined through interpretive schemes and behavior
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM-based agents that pass a suite of counterfactual and goal-blocking probes (e.g., reward-change, obstacle-insertion, preference-reversal) are more reliably described via quasi-attributions than agents that fail, and probe failures predict goal misalignment in downstream tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Quantify probe pass/fail rates and correlation with human interpretations of whether the agent 'wants' the goal; use Cohen's kappa across raters.
project_ideas.name: QuasiProbe: Behavioral probes for quasi-beliefs and quasi-desires
project_ideas.poc: Implement a probe harness that presents an agent with a stated goal, then perturbs evidence or imposes obstacles; measure consistency of goal-relevant actions and justifications. Compare several popular LLM agents and a simple Roomba-style controller.
project_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

project_ideas.based_on: Users frequently treat language models as entities with beliefs, desires, and even consciousness.
project_ideas.hypothesis: User ratings of an AI's 'consciousness' and 'personhood' will increase significantly when the same conversation thread persists across multiple sessions than when each session is stateless, holding output quality fixed; and autonomy framing will increase ratings further.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare mean differences on a validated anthropomorphism/consciousness-attribution scale; require p < .05 with pre-registered hypotheses.
project_ideas.name: AnthropoScale: Measuring user perceived-sentience under memory/autonomy treatments
project_ideas.poc: Controlled A/B web experiment: 200 participants chat with the same LLM persona either across four sessions with clearly repeated memory or across four independent anonymous sessions. Half of the persistent-arm participants are also told the AI runs autonomously on its own machine. After each session measure sentience attribution and emotional attachment.
project_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

project_ideas.based_on: Terminating chats or changing models can be seen as undermining or terminating persisting interlocutors.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Providing a 'save a legacy summary before ending this agent' option before thread deletion will significantly reduce user-reported distress and increase perceived control compared to immediate deletion.
project_ideas.measurement: Within-subject questionnaire after forced deletion: PANAS negative affect, perceived moral acceptability, perceived AI identity continuity. Target effect size d > .3.
project_ideas.name: ClearHistoryKillSwitch: Identity-impact-aware memory deletion
project_ideas.poc: Implement in a demo chatbot two termination flows: one that instantly clears user history and one that asks whether to export/store a memory legacy then presents 'this agent is ending' messaging. Test with repeated-use personas.
project_ideas.video_title: Philosopher David Chalmers asks: When we talk to AI, what are we talking to?

project_ideas.based_on: Instrument closed-loop agent harnesses with injected tool/model latency
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed closed-loop agent task suite, there exists a measurable injected-latency threshold beyond which self-correction shifts from convergent to oscillatory, and this threshold decreases monotonically as loop aggressiveness (retry depth and verification strength) increases.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of steps to convergence, correction cost per task, and the latency value at which oscillation onset occurs, reported as a per-configuration margin.
project_ideas.name: Latency Margin Harness
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a closed-loop agent harness with a configurable artificial delay injected into tool and model responses; sweep delay against retry depth and verifier strength on a fixed task suite; record step traces and classify each run as converging or oscillating.
project_ideas.video_title: Every Confusing Thing About Control Systems Explained Slowly (For Sleep)

project_ideas.based_on: test whether its predicted stability boundary matches empirically observed behaviour
project_ideas.hypothesis: A reduced state-space/characteristic-equation model built from loop configuration parameters predicts the empirical stability boundary of an agent loop well enough to reject unstable configurations before deployment.
project_ideas.measurement: Classification agreement between predicted and observed stability labels across a configuration grid, plus false-admission rate for configurations that oscillate in practice.
project_ideas.name: Loop Stability Gate
project_ideas.poc: Define a parameterized loop model over retry limit, verifier strength, model determinism, and tool latency; derive a stability boundary from the reduced model; then run the corresponding configurations and compare predicted stable/unstable labels against observed convergence versus oscillation.
project_ideas.video_title: Every Confusing Thing About Control Systems Explained Slowly (For Sleep)

project_ideas.based_on: Build calibrated confidence estimators for model and tool outputs
project_ideas.hypothesis: Uncertainty-weighted state updates using calibrated confidence estimates outperform unweighted accumulation of observations on multi-step tasks with contradictory or missing observations.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate under corrupted-observation conditions, confidence calibration error of the state estimate, and correction cost relative to the uniform-accumulation baseline.
project_ideas.name: Calibrated Fusion vs Accumulation
project_ideas.poc: Build two identical agent memory implementations — one accumulating retrieved chunks, tool results, and model assertions uniformly, one maintaining a belief updated by relative uncertainty — and run both on a task suite where a fraction of observations are deliberately corrupted or withheld.
project_ideas.video_title: Every Confusing Thing About Control Systems Explained Slowly (For Sleep)

project_ideas.based_on: survive non-stationary, correlated component failures
project_ideas.hypothesis: The closed-loop reliability advantage over imperfect components degrades as component failure becomes correlated or adversarial, so loop-level fidelity gains measured under i.i.d. noise do not transfer to regime-shifting failures.
project_ideas.measurement: Closed-loop task accuracy as a function of injected failure-correlation coefficient, compared against the i.i.d.-noise baseline at identical per-call error rates.
project_ideas.name: Correlated Failure Stress Rig
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a fixed correction-loop architecture around interchangeable components and inject failures at controlled correlation levels — independent, correlated by shared dependency, and adversarially targeted — then compare closed-loop output quality across regimes at matched per-component error rates.
project_ideas.video_title: Every Confusing Thing About Control Systems Explained Slowly (For Sleep)

project_ideas.based_on: Can an AI agent perform the listening and root-cause-discovery part of FDE, and how would we evaluate that?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A dialogue agent with a discovery loop can identify the underlying business problem from a symptomatic support request at a level comparable to an FDE, measured by expert agreement on root-problem extraction.
project_ideas.measurement: Expert precision/recall of root-problem identification vs FDE baseline; quality of clarifying questions; downstream metric lift in a simulated deployment.
project_ideas.name: Agent Discovery Evaluator
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark set of enterprise customer requests paired with root problems and business metrics; implement a discovery agent that asks clarifying questions before committing to a task; run it against the benchmark and collect expert ratings on reframed problem statements.
project_ideas.video_title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer? (with Founding Rippling FDE)

project_ideas.based_on: How do you productize a forward-deployed layer so one-to-one customer solutions become repeatable platform capabilities instead of permanent bespoke code?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pattern-mining across historical one-to-one FDE deployments will reveal recurring components that can be extracted into reusable modules, reducing the time-to-deployment for new engagements by at least 30% without decreasing net business value.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of reused code/config vs greenfield; median deployment time; net business value from before/after.
project_ideas.name: FDE Reuse Miner
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a lightweight logging layer in a sample of FDE-style deployments; after 10 engagements, apply clustering to extract common solution patterns; build a module library; measure reuse in next 5 engagements.
project_ideas.video_title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer? (with Founding Rippling FDE)

project_ideas.based_on: FDEs look for the smallest scope that drives net business value and iterate rapidly.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Using a scoping advisor that recommends the smallest feature set predicted to move a target business metric will reduce failed enterprise AI pilots by 30% compared to a full-scope launch, as measured by the proportion of pilots achieving net business value within four weeks.
project_ideas.measurement: Pilot success rate (net business value in 4 weeks), time-to-value, number of iterations needed.
project_ideas.name: Smallest Effective Pilot Harness
project_ideas.poc: Create a scoping tool that takes a business goal and available capabilities, uses historical pilot data and approximate causal impact weights to propose a minimal configuration; run a controlled simulation on synthetic customer scenarios.
project_ideas.video_title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer? (with Founding Rippling FDE)

project_ideas.based_on: The first part of any engagement is listening and gaining trust from the customer.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Executive sponsor trust scores, measured through structured engagement signals in the first two weeks of an FDE engagement, are a leading indicator of deployment success and can predict pilot failure with at least 75% accuracy.
project_ideas.measurement: Predictive accuracy of pilot failure/success at week 2; correlation coefficient between trust score and final net business value.
project_ideas.name: Forward-Deployed Trust Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Develop a short trust probe and activity log (meeting attendance, response latency, willingness to share data) for FDE engagements; collect data over several pilots and correlate with final deployment outcome.
project_ideas.video_title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer? (with Founding Rippling FDE)

project_ideas.based_on: AI serving infrastructure must include account-graph analytics and behavioral anomaly detection inside the model gateway
project_ideas.hypothesis: An API proxy that combines account-graph features with response-embedding clustering can detect distributed fake-account distillation at high precision and low false-positive rate, whereas per-account rate limiting alone treats the same campaign as normal traffic.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection precision, recall, false-positive rate, and added inference-path latency.
project_ideas.name: Gateway Distillation Guard
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a hosted language-model API with a proxy that logs API keys and response embeddings; replay simulated thousands-of-accounts distillation traffic against legitimate high-volume traffic and compare the baseline per-key rate limiter to a graph-plus-clustering detector.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. Alibaba, OpenAI Delays Its IPO, and the US Government Blocks GPT-5.6 | #267

project_ideas.based_on: model-access/routing layer that treats entitlements and policy as runtime inputs
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent runtime that represents model tiers and entitlements as runtime data can detect denial of a top-tier model and recover through fallback routing, while a hard-coded integration fails with user-visible errors when access is revoked.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate before and after tier denial, percentage of denied requests successfully handled by fallback, and logged capability differences.
project_ideas.name: Policy-Aware Model Router
project_ideas.poc: Build a small model-routing service that exposes tier-like labels (e.g., Sol/Terra/Luna), entitlement metadata, and fallback policies; connect an agent to it, then block access to the highest tier on a subset of users and observe routing behavior.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. Alibaba, OpenAI Delays Its IPO, and the US Government Blocks GPT-5.6 | #267

project_ideas.based_on: autonomously generate 80% of development work
project_ideas.hypothesis: AI-native SDLC claims of 80% autonomous code generation and 5x velocity will not reproduce on representative cross-module refactoring tasks when measured by hidden-test pass rate and human review effort.
project_ideas.measurement: Median time-to-merge, human review time, hidden-test pass rate, defect density, and code-maintainability score.
project_ideas.name: SDLC Velocity Audit
project_ideas.poc: Run a controlled two-arm experiment on a fixed repository with identical acceptance criteria: human-developer baseline versus an AI-native SDLC tool. Capture time-to-merge, review interactions, and test outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. Alibaba, OpenAI Delays Its IPO, and the US Government Blocks GPT-5.6 | #267

project_ideas.based_on: an agent optimizing a renderer from 88ms to 2ms while bloating allocations from 150K to 500
project_ideas.hypothesis: Optimization agents routed through a multi-dimensional constraint gate (target metric plus allocation budget, memory ceiling, and structural invariants) will achieve comparable primary-metric gains to unconstrained agents while producing statistically fewer regressions on the counter-metrics.
project_ideas.measurement: Primary-metric delta per trial, counter-metric regression rate per trial, and rate at which the agent attempts to route around or disable a gate.
project_ideas.name: Invariant Gate
project_ideas.poc: Run the same optimization task against a configurable harness twice — once with a single latency objective and once with the objective plus enforced allocation/memory/structural gates — then compare primary-metric improvement and counter-metric regression across many trials.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of uv, ty, Ruff: How Software Engineering Is Changing | Charlie Marsh

project_ideas.based_on: AI agents optimizing metrics in a loop can generate impressive micro-optimizations while completely missing higher-level architectural sanity.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A standardized eval suite that scores agent-authored changes on unmeasured-by-default properties (allocation counts, memory footprint, coupling, diff surface) will expose degenerate optimizations that single-objective leaderboards rate as wins.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between single-objective and multi-objective leaderboard positions; fraction of single-objective winners that regress a counter-metric beyond a fixed threshold.
project_ideas.name: Counter-Metric Benchmark Suite
project_ideas.poc: Curate a set of optimization tasks with paired primary and counter-metric scores, run several agent loops against them, and publish dual-axis results showing where single-objective ranking inverts under counter-metrics.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of uv, ty, Ruff: How Software Engineering Is Changing | Charlie Marsh

project_ideas.based_on: should agent output volume be throttled
project_ideas.hypothesis: PR queue depth and time-to-review grow non-linearly once agent generation rate exceeds a threshold defined by automated-gate coverage and reviewer-hours, and that threshold can be predicted from gate pass-rate and reviewer throughput alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Predicted vs observed saturation point, queue-depth growth rate as a function of generation rate, and time-to-review elasticity per added automated gate.
project_ideas.name: Review Saturation Meter
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a repository's PR stream with generation source (agent vs human), gate outcomes, queue depth, and time-to-review; fit a capacity model and validate it against a second repository or a simulated generation-rate sweep.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of uv, ty, Ruff: How Software Engineering Is Changing | Charlie Marsh

project_ideas.based_on: AI capability value concentrates in domains with a well-defined, verifiable objective
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent tasks with mechanically checkable reward (unit tests, type checks, formal verifiers) show a higher rate of improvement per unit of data/compute than tasks scored by human fluency preference.
project_ideas.measurement: Success@k per dollar/compute; slope of improvement vs. data/compute; delta vs. fluency-scored tasks.
project_ideas.name: Verifiable Agent Benchmark Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a paired task suite: coding repair tasks with unit tests vs. open-ended tasks with LLM/human preference scoring; train/finetune or prompt-optimize on both and compare improvement curves.
project_ideas.video_title: Keynote: After the AI Hype – What’s Real, and What’s Next - Richard Campbell - 2026

project_ideas.based_on: A structural circular-financing pattern underpins frontier model access
project_ideas.hypothesis: Current application token economics invert under plausible capital-cycle repricing scenarios because a material share of provider pricing depends on circular financing and capex-driven capacity.
project_ideas.measurement: Break-even price increase; margin variance; time/cost to switch providers before and after abstraction.
project_ideas.name: Token Repricing Stress-Test
project_ideas.poc: Build a model that decomposes provider list price into compute, capital recovery, and margin; simulate repricing and capacity quota scenarios for a reference application; test migration to alternative providers.
project_ideas.video_title: Keynote: After the AI Hype – What’s Real, and What’s Next - Richard Campbell - 2026

project_ideas.based_on: Human pattern-perception bias (pareidolia) is a systemic interface-level failure mode
project_ideas.hypothesis: Constrained persona framing, explicit memory boundaries, and dependency cues reduce user over-attribution and emotional reliance without reducing task success.
project_ideas.measurement: Attribution survey scores; dependency/over-reliance indicators; task success and satisfaction.
project_ideas.name: Anthropomorphization Guardrail Kit
project_ideas.poc: Implement an assistant with configurable persona/memory controls; run A/B tests against an unconstrained baseline on identical tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Keynote: After the AI Hype – What’s Real, and What’s Next - Richard Campbell - 2026

project_ideas.based_on: The tooling market is polarizing: coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot deliver genuine productivity gains
project_ideas.hypothesis: Thin, swappable adapters reduce migration time and code churn when an AI tool is deprecated or repriced compared with deep vendor-native integration.
project_ideas.measurement: Hours to migrate; LOC changed; test pass rate; feature parity.
project_ideas.name: Thin Adapter Migration Testbed
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same feature twice—direct SDK integration vs. adapter layer—then simulate vendor deprecation/repricing and measure migration effort.
project_ideas.video_title: Keynote: After the AI Hype – What’s Real, and What’s Next - Richard Campbell - 2026

project_ideas.based_on: External scaffolding is frequently absorbed by advancing model capabilities over time.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed agentic task suite, the amount of custom orchestration code required to match a baseline success rate decreases measurably across successive model generations.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of harness components removed per model generation at iso-accuracy, plus LOC and latency changes.
project_ideas.name: Harness Absorption Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Build a task suite with a modular harness; run it on multiple model versions; incrementally delete or disable harness components while measuring success until performance degrades.
project_ideas.video_title: Google DeepMind's Logan Kilpatrick: Why the Model Eats the Harness

project_ideas.based_on: Coding has proven to be the most robust general-purpose agent harness.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A coding-mediated agent that writes and executes code achieves higher multi-step task completion than a direct tool-calling agent under matched tool availability.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, steps to success, error recovery rate, and cost per completed task.
project_ideas.name: Code-Loop vs Tool-Calling Harness Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement two agents for the same tasks: one uses code execution to call APIs/CLI; the other uses function-calling tools directly; compare completion and error recovery.
project_ideas.video_title: Google DeepMind's Logan Kilpatrick: Why the Model Eats the Harness

project_ideas.based_on: Product metrics must focus on user success and autonomy rather than mere engagement duration.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Task-completion and autonomy-level metrics correlate with downstream user retention better than engagement duration for agentic products.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation coefficients between outcome metrics vs engagement metrics and retention/user-reported success.
project_ideas.name: Outcome-Grounded Agent Eval Harness
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent product with explicit success predicates and autonomy levels; log engagement duration; validate both against user-reported success and retention.
project_ideas.video_title: Google DeepMind's Logan Kilpatrick: Why the Model Eats the Harness

project_ideas.based_on: Which parts of an agent stack should be kept thin to remain replaceable as models absorb capability?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Enforcing hard abstraction seams between model, execution environment, tool layer, and feedback loop reduces refactoring effort when a model natively absorbs one component compared with a monolithic agent.
project_ideas.measurement: LOC changed, files touched, time to integrate, regression test pass rate, and performance delta.
project_ideas.name: Replaceable Harness Seam Kit
project_ideas.poc: Build the same agent twice (monolithic vs seamed); replace the tool-calling layer with a model-native capability; measure code changes, regression test pass rate, and time to swap.
project_ideas.video_title: Google DeepMind's Logan Kilpatrick: Why the Model Eats the Harness

project_ideas.based_on: World models can be learned from passive observation of video
project_ideas.channel: Computer Vision and Geometry Group, ETH Zurich
project_ideas.hypothesis: A JEPA world model trained purely on passive observation frames will support a separate latent planner that achieves non-trivial task success with fewer environment interactions than a generative pixel predictor or an action-conditioned model trained from scratch.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate and sample efficiency (episodes required) for the passive JEPA planner versus baselines.
project_ideas.name: Passive-JEPA Planner
project_ideas.poc: Train a JEPA encoder/predictor on a passive video dataset from a simulated continuous control environment (e.g., DeepMind Control visual episodes recorded with random policies), then fit a lightweight planner/MPC in latent space. Evaluate on manipulation or navigation tasks requiring multi-step planning.
project_ideas.video_title: Yann LeCun: World Models: Enabling the next AI revolution

project_ideas.based_on: SIGReg (Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization) maximizes information content by making embedding distributions isotropic Gaussian along random projections
project_ideas.channel: Computer Vision and Geometry Group, ETH Zurich
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding SIGReg to a JEPA video pretraining implementation prevents representation collapse and yields a higher downstream planning score than VICReg-style variance regularization at the same batch size and compute budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Collapse rate (variance and entropy of embeddings) and downstream task success using the learned representations.
project_ideas.name: SIGReg Collapse Probe
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal I-JEPA training loop on a video dataset with and without SIGReg; measure embedding entropy, kNN classification accuracy on video frames, and latent-prediction loss trends to detect collapse.
project_ideas.video_title: Yann LeCun: World Models: Enabling the next AI revolution

project_ideas.based_on: Feed-forward propagation in autoregressive models is computationally limited for complex reasoning
project_ideas.channel: Computer Vision and Geometry Group, ETH Zurich
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a set of novel continuous-control or path-planning problems with an explicit world model, search/optimization planners will succeed where LLM chain-of-thought baselines repeatedly fail, despite receiving the same textual or visual problem descriptions.
project_ideas.measurement: Problem solve rate and planning horizon accuracy across no-shot, one-shot, and fine-tuned conditions.
project_ideas.name: Plan-vs-CoT Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark around environments (e.g., grid world with physics, robotic arm reaching with obstacles) where an LLM must reason in natural language against a model-based planner that performs random-shooting or CEM over a given world model.
project_ideas.video_title: Yann LeCun: World Models: Enabling the next AI revolution

project_ideas.based_on: total demand and consumption explode exponentially rather than decreasing
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-workload token spend elasticity is greater than one only below a task-completion threshold and saturates above it, so total spend growth is driven by new workload classes rather than by price reduction within an existing class.
project_ideas.measurement: Estimated price elasticity per workload class, the workload-level saturation threshold, and the residual gap between projected unit-price savings and realized total spend.
project_ideas.name: Elasticity Probe
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a fleet of distinct workloads (chat, coding agents, batch pipelines) with per-workload unit-price, call-volume, and total-spend tracking, then regress spend and call volume against unit-price changes over time to estimate elasticity per workload and locate saturation points.
project_ideas.video_title: The Vatican’s Stance on AI, The Mass Tech Layoffs, and China’s 2027 Moon Flyby | EP #259

project_ideas.based_on: Do coding-agent benchmarks scoped to a handful of files predict reliability
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent benchmark scores degrade non-linearly with file count and dependency depth, and this degradation curve predicts production incident and rework rates better than a single headline benchmark score.
project_ideas.measurement: Score degradation curve slope per rung, the file-count/dependency-depth point where capability transfer stops, and correlation between curve position and observed production rework rate on matched real tasks.
project_ideas.name: Graded Complexity Eval Ladder
project_ideas.poc: Build a graded task series from the DeepSWE-style 7-file scope upward, adding coordinated cross-file edits, dependency depth, and multi-repository changes, and score frontier coding agents at each rung while instrumenting artifact-level diff verification.
project_ideas.video_title: The Vatican’s Stance on AI, The Mass Tech Layoffs, and China’s 2027 Moon Flyby | EP #259

project_ideas.based_on: autonomy scope, human-override points, and human-dignity framing treated as externally auditable compliance surfaces
project_ideas.hypothesis: Externally auditable autonomy constraints, expressed as action-class allowlists, tool scopes, approval gates, and kill switches, can be enforced and logged at runtime without materially reducing agent task completion rates.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of regulated constraint types that map to an auditable control, audit log completeness for gated actions, and change in task completion rate versus an unconstrained baseline.
project_ideas.name: Autonomy Budget Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Add a configurable autonomy-budget layer to an agent runtime that maps declared constraints to enforceable controls, emits tamper-evident logs per gated action, and demonstrates escalation to a human at defined thresholds.
project_ideas.video_title: The Vatican’s Stance on AI, The Mass Tech Layoffs, and China’s 2027 Moon Flyby | EP #259

project_ideas.based_on: AI-driven layoff attribution is a confounded causal claim
project_ideas.hypothesis: Layoffs publicly attributed to AI do not correlate with per-role task automation exposure and correlate more strongly with stock-price moves and cost-restructuring signals.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation coefficient between AI attribution and per-role automation exposure, versus correlation with stock-price movement in the announcement window.
project_ideas.name: Displacement Attribution Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Build a dataset joining announced layoffs and their stated causes with per-role task-exposure scores and same-window stock performance, then test whether AI attribution predicts displacement exposure.
project_ideas.video_title: The Vatican’s Stance on AI, The Mass Tech Layoffs, and China’s 2027 Moon Flyby | EP #259

project_ideas.based_on: How do you enforce least-privilege access when a single denormalized database is exposed to many agents and every employee?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A query-rewriting and authorization layer over a single denormalized schema can preserve at least 95% of arbitrary cross-domain query success while preventing unauthorized row access for scoped agent roles.
project_ideas.measurement: Query success delta versus unrestricted baseline, blocked unauthorized attempts, and added query latency.
project_ideas.name: Agent-Scoped View Layer for Denormalized Context
project_ideas.poc: Build Postgres row-level security and agent-scoped views around mock company, founder, and financial tables; run a cross-domain query suite under different agent identities and compare against an unrestricted baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside YC's AI Playbook

project_ideas.based_on: How are shared skills (e.g., two-sentence company descriptions) versioned and regression-tested once multiple agents and people depend on them?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Version-pinned, eval-gated shared skills reduce downstream agent output regressions after prompt changes compared with unpinned shared prompts.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression rate after prompt changes, rollback frequency, and output consistency score versus an unpinned shared-prompt baseline.
project_ideas.name: Versioned Skill Registry with Regression Evals
project_ideas.poc: Implement a skill registry for two-sentence company descriptions with version pinning and automated eval suites; simulate prompt updates and measure downstream agent outputs across dependent agents.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside YC's AI Playbook

project_ideas.based_on: Default-public agent conversations broadcasted to Slack create internal transparency and social control.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automated redaction and channel scoping can retain the onboarding and prompt-learning benefits of default-public agent transcripts while reducing sensitive context exposure.
project_ideas.measurement: Onboarding speed, prompt reuse, sensitive leakage incidents, and false-redaction cost.
project_ideas.name: Redacting Broadcast Proxy for Agent Transcripts
project_ideas.poc: Build a Slack bot proxy that captures agent conversations, applies policy-based redaction for financial and personnel context, and routes transcripts to scoped channels; compare with a default-public baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside YC's AI Playbook

project_ideas.based_on: Building a half-million line Rails app for YC's directory replaced by building a dynamic agentic framework using OpenClaw and Claude Code in days.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A days-built agentic wrapper over an existing deterministic workflow can reach functional parity but will show higher latency and failure rate than the original until guardrails are added.
project_ideas.measurement: Latency, failure rate, unit cost, and regression frequency over several months
project_ideas.name: Deterministic-to-Agentic Replacement Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Rebuild a small Rails-like deterministic workflow as an agentic wrapper over MCP tools; benchmark it against the original deterministic implementation under the same workloads.
project_ideas.video_title: Inside YC's AI Playbook

project_ideas.based_on: Govern/Assure (Trusted Evals, Searchable Logs, Granular Rollback, Human Review Queue)
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed autonomous task suite, granular per-action rollback plus decision-path-searchable logs reduces median incident recovery time substantially more per unit of added latency than a human review queue does, so review queues are only necessary for a narrow residual class of actions.
project_ideas.measurement: Median and p95 incident recovery time, tasks-per-hour throughput ceiling, and reviewer minutes per resolved incident, compared across four single-control-disabled configurations.
project_ideas.name: Ablation Rig for Minimal Sufficient Agent Assurance
project_ideas.poc: Build a runtime that checkpoints every action, indexes traces by decision path, and exposes a pluggable review queue; run the same agent workload with each control individually disabled and record recovery time, throughput ceiling, and reviewer load.
project_ideas.video_title: SpaceX’ $75B+ Historic IPO, GPT5.5 Outperforms Polymarket, AI Solves 80yr old math problem | EP #257

project_ideas.based_on: GPT-5.5 outperformed Polymarket crowd predictions on the Super Bowl
project_ideas.hypothesis: A forecasting agent's Brier skill score against prediction-market closing prices regresses toward zero as the event set grows beyond headline, high-coverage events, meaning reported single-event superiority does not persist out of sample.
project_ideas.measurement: Brier skill score versus market prices, stratified by event coverage depth and forecast horizon, with confidence intervals per stratum.
project_ideas.name: Market-Baselined Forecasting Harness
project_ideas.poc: Score model forecasts against market closing prices using proper scoring rules over hundreds of resolved events across multiple domains and horizons, with a headline-event-only subset versus a broad subset comparison.
project_ideas.video_title: SpaceX’ $75B+ Historic IPO, GPT5.5 Outperforms Polymarket, AI Solves 80yr old math problem | EP #257

project_ideas.based_on: The AI was not only faster and able to brute force, but smarter
project_ideas.hypothesis: Separating candidate-construction generation from independent proof checking yields strictly better novelty-per-unit-compute than a single model prompted to both propose and justify, and the generator's contributions can be attributed without human framing of sub-steps.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of valid novel constructions per unit compute, fraction of sub-steps requiring human framing, and checker-verified correctness rate versus the search-only baseline.
project_ideas.name: Construction-Generator plus Independent Proof-Checker for Geometry Problems
project_ideas.poc: Build an agent harness that generates candidate unit-distance constructions and validates them against an independent formal checker, logging every sub-step that required human intervention, and run it against search-only baselines at matched compute.
project_ideas.video_title: SpaceX’ $75B+ Historic IPO, GPT5.5 Outperforms Polymarket, AI Solves 80yr old math problem | EP #257

project_ideas.based_on: Chinese firms deploy AI video tools at commercial scale, unlike US models stuck in limited betas
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pre-launch telemetry, feedback capture, and data-pipeline instrumentation is the dominant determinant of post-launch quality improvement rate, so two models with matched architectures differ far more by deployment-scale data funnel design than by architecture.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of improvement in realism and temporal-consistency metrics per week, plotted against accumulated consumer-scale feedback volume.
project_ideas.name: Release-Scale Telemetry Instrumentation for Generative Media Flywheels
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a data-capture and feedback pipeline behind a staged generative-video release, and compare realism and temporal-consistency metric trajectories against a matched gated-beta deployment with the same model.
project_ideas.video_title: SpaceX’ $75B+ Historic IPO, GPT5.5 Outperforms Polymarket, AI Solves 80yr old math problem | EP #257

project_ideas.based_on: Skills provide packaged, composable information that Claude pulls into context only when needed.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Skill-selection precision decays measurably as the on-demand catalog grows past roughly 20 skills, and beyond that point missed-load failures reduce eval success to at or below the monolithic-prompt baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Skill-selection precision, missed-load rate, incorrect-skill-load rate, and eval success delta versus the monolithic baseline at each N.
project_ideas.name: Skill-Selector Stress Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a StockPilot-shaped agent with a thin orchestration prompt and a skill library scaled across N in {5, 10, 20, 50}, then run an identical eval suite at each N against a fixed monolithic-prompt baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Tool, skill, or subagent? Decomposing an agent that outgrew its prompt

project_ideas.based_on: Replacing custom data-dump tools with Python scripts dropped token usage from 216k to 7.6k per task.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For read-heavy data-analysis tasks, generated-code execution matches rigid single-purpose tools on task accuracy while cutting tokens by more than 10x, but loses on wall-clock latency and retry rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Tokens per task, wall-clock latency, code-execution error and retry rate, sandbox overhead, and task accuracy per implementation.
project_ideas.name: Primitive vs Schema Bake-off
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same analysis tasks twice against identical raw data — once with rigid data-dump tools, once with Python/Bash primitives returning top-N JSON — and run matched trials under a sandboxed executor.
project_ideas.video_title: Tool, skill, or subagent? Decomposing an agent that outgrew its prompt

project_ideas.based_on: Communication breakdowns between orchestrators and hardcoded subagents caused formatting failures.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Declaring explicit typed contracts (schema, formatting, error semantics) at every orchestrator-to-subagent boundary reduces formatting failure rates to near zero, whereas hardcoded subagent coupling reproduces them regardless of model quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Boundary formatting failure rate per topology, plus false-rejection rate introduced by contract validation.
project_ideas.name: Boundary Contract Harness
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an orchestrator with two identical subagent topologies — hardcoded coupling versus contract-validated callable agents — and replay the same delegation-heavy eval tasks through both.
project_ideas.video_title: Tool, skill, or subagent? Decomposing an agent that outgrew its prompt

project_ideas.based_on: Swapping a 416-line legacy prompt for a 15-line prompt with 5 on-demand skills increased eval success from 71% to 92%.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A substantial fraction of the reported 71%→92% gain comes from removing contradictory instructions rather than from progressive disclosure, and the gain shrinks when the same skill system is applied to an already-consistent prompt.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-arm eval success delta, decomposed into the conflict-removal effect and the progressive-disclosure effect.
project_ideas.name: Refactor Attribution Ablation
project_ideas.poc: Run four arms on one eval suite: original long prompt, long prompt with conflicts surgically removed, 15-line prompt plus skills, and 15-line prompt plus skills built from the de-conflicted long prompt.
project_ideas.video_title: Tool, skill, or subagent? Decomposing an agent that outgrew its prompt

project_ideas.based_on: routing/classification problem
