project_ideas.hypothesis: A risk-scoring router between generation and merge can cut human-reviewed change volume by at least 50 percent while holding the rate of risky changes auto-passed to human review at or below the team's current post-merge incident rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Change volume routed to human review, review queue depth per day, time-to-verified, and the false-negative rate of risky changes let through in shadow mode versus the uniform-review baseline.
project_ideas.name: Review Router with Calibrated False-Negative Budget
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a change stream (diff size, touched subsystems, test coverage delta, security-relevant paths, author history) and route each change to auto-merge, single reviewer, or deep review; run shadow mode against existing uniform review and compare routing decisions with what human reviewers actually flagged.
project_ideas.video_title: Running an AI-native engineering org

project_ideas.based_on: should target verification and review capacity
project_ideas.hypothesis: Time-to-verified per change predicts end-to-end delivery time better than assisted-commit share or coded volume once generation is no longer the constraint.
project_ideas.measurement: Explained variance of delivery time by verification-segment latency versus generation-segment latency; correlation of review queue depth with delivery time.
project_ideas.name: Verification Throughput Telemetry
project_ideas.poc: Emit per-change telemetry from first commit to verified merge, decompose it into generation, review wait, review active, and CI/verification segments, and regress delivery time against each segment across several repositories.
project_ideas.video_title: Running an AI-native engineering org

project_ideas.based_on: Can in-repo specs replace external design docs for intent, rationale, and cross-cutting decisions that do not map onto code?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Repository-embedded specs are corrected faster and drift less than an external doc store under equal maintenance effort, but agent retrieval accuracy for intent and rejected-alternative questions is lower from in-repo specs alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Retrieval answer accuracy per question class, median staleness age of contradicted claims, and correction latency after an invalidating commit.
project_ideas.name: Spec Drift Benchmark: In-Repo versus External Store
project_ideas.poc: Take a non-code question set (why a decision was made, what alternatives were rejected, cross-cutting constraints), answer it from in-repo specs and from curated external docs, and separately measure staleness by timestamping claims against the commits that invalidate them.
project_ideas.video_title: Running an AI-native engineering org

project_ideas.based_on: Generate-and-compare is a selection mechanism
project_ideas.hypothesis: Generating N competing variants and scoring them against pre-declared criteria reduces decision latency and post-decision rework compared with single-variant generation followed by review discussion.
project_ideas.measurement: Median time from disagreement to decision, review rounds per decision, revert/rework rate within two weeks for single-variant versus multi-variant decisions.
project_ideas.name: Prototype Bake-Off Loop
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a change request in a loop that produces two or three implementation variants in parallel plus an explicit comparison rubric, then log decision latency, number of review rounds, and whether the losing variant's approach reappears as rework.
project_ideas.video_title: Running an AI-native engineering org

project_ideas.based_on: Developers can bring their own sandboxes (Cloudflare, Vercel, Modal) instead of using Anthropic infrastructure.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For the same agent definition and environment, self-hosted sandboxes (Cloudflare, Vercel, Modal) do not emit identical event/span telemetry or enforce identical network/package controls as the managed sandbox; differences are observable and measurable.
project_ideas.measurement: Event type coverage, missing span rate, ordering divergence, p95 latency delta, and network/package policy mismatches.
project_ideas.name: Sandbox Parity Diff Harness
project_ideas.poc: Define one agent and environment, run identical sessions against managed and self-hosted sandboxes, capture event streams and telemetry, and diff event types, ordering, metadata, and sandbox controls.
project_ideas.video_title: Build a production-ready agent with Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: MCP tunnels provide secure tunnels to access private MCP servers within a private perimeter without exposing them to the internet.
project_ideas.hypothesis: When a private MCP server or tunnel broker becomes unavailable or slow, agent sessions degrade non-deterministically, with retries masking partial-context failures and no explicit compensation.
project_ideas.measurement: Timeout behavior, retry counts, partial-result rate, session state consistency, and recovery time.
project_ideas.name: MCP Tunnel Fault Injector
project_ideas.poc: Run an agent that depends on a private database MCP server through a tunnel; inject latency, disconnects, and auth failures; capture session events and agent outputs.
project_ideas.video_title: Build a production-ready agent with Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Configuring per-tool permissions (auto-execute vs. require approval).
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a coordinator/sub-agent topology, per-tool approval policy is not consistently propagated; sub-agents can bypass or fail to inherit a coordinator's tool restrictions.
project_ideas.measurement: Policy bypass rate, approval prompt coverage, audit trail completeness, and false-denial rate.
project_ideas.name: Delegated Approval Propagation Tester
project_ideas.poc: Define a coordinator with a restricted destructive tool and sub-agents with broader tools; run delegated tasks and log every tool invocation, approval prompt, and enforcement decision.
project_ideas.video_title: Build a production-ready agent with Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Memory stores allow agents to read and write persistent memories across sessions.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Shared persistent memory stores accumulate stale or contradictory entries across sessions that propagate into later outputs unless explicitly curated, and the platform does not automate staleness detection.
project_ideas.measurement: Contradiction rate in memory, propagation rate into outputs, human correction effort, and session-over-session drift.
project_ideas.name: Persistent Memory Staleness Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Run repeated sessions that write changing facts into a shared memory store, introduce contradictions, then run fresh sessions and trace which stale entries influence outputs.
project_ideas.video_title: Build a production-ready agent with Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: up to 85% PR success rates using multi-model agent reviews
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding heterogeneous reviewer models reduces missed-defect rate per review-dollar up to a knee, beyond which reviewer failures become correlated and marginal cost exceeds marginal defect reduction.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect escape rate versus cost-per-merged-PR curve; reviewer pairwise failure-correlation matrix; p95 review latency per additional reviewer.
project_ideas.name: Council Bench
project_ideas.poc: Run a primary coding agent plus N reviewer models drawn from different model families (N = 1..4) over a held-out set of real pull requests with known post-merge defects, gating merges on reviewer consensus, and log cost, latency, and escaped defects per configuration.
project_ideas.video_title: Building AI-native at enterprise scale: monday.com, Doctolib, and Delivery Hero

project_ideas.based_on: New model releases require treating upgrades as major system migrations.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pipelines that pin model versions and re-run a fixed evaluation suite plus prompt-technique migration per release show a materially smaller behavioral regression than pipelines that upgrade in place.
project_ideas.measurement: Eval pass-rate delta and output-divergence rate between model versions; share of tasks requiring human re-review after unmanaged versus managed upgrade.
project_ideas.name: Model Migration Harness
project_ideas.poc: Replay a fixed suite of production agent tasks against an old and a new model version, both with and without prompt re-migration, and diff outputs, eval scores, and human re-review rates.
project_ideas.video_title: Building AI-native at enterprise scale: monday.com, Doctolib, and Delivery Hero

project_ideas.based_on: granular security and permission models with autonomous agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: Capability-scoped, short-lived agent identities with signed action provenance block unauthorized actions under adversarial prompt injection while costing less than a defined throughput threshold versus an unscoped agent.
project_ideas.measurement: Unauthorized action attempts blocked versus attempted; autonomous PRs per day with and without scoping; time to reconstruct a full audit trail for a single change.
project_ideas.name: Least-Privilege Agent Passport
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a ticket-to-PR agent with per-repository and per-path scoped credentials and an append-only provenance ledger of every tool call, then run a prompt-injection and privilege-escalation suite against it.
project_ideas.video_title: Building AI-native at enterprise scale: monday.com, Doctolib, and Delivery Hero

project_ideas.based_on: Building for the next model generation rather than the current one
project_ideas.hypothesis: Expressing model-limitation assumptions as declared capability parameters with fallbacks, rather than hard-coded workarounds, reduces rework hours per model release by a measurable margin across two successive generations.
project_ideas.measurement: Lines of code changed and engineering hours of rework per model release; task success-rate delta after upgrade; count of capability parameters flipped without code edits.
project_ideas.name: Capability-Parameterized Agent Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Build a Heron-style ticket-to-PR pipeline in which every 'the model cannot do X yet' assumption is a named capability parameter with a configurable fallback, then upgrade the underlying model and record what must change.
project_ideas.video_title: Building AI-native at enterprise scale: monday.com, Doctolib, and Delivery Hero

project_ideas.based_on: Runtime resolution is avoided wherever possible
project_ideas.hypothesis: Compiling tool binding, schema validation, and output formatting into static artifacts at build time reduces per-step token consumption and end-to-end latency versus a dynamically resolved harness baseline, with no loss in task accuracy.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-step input/output tokens, p50/p95 end-to-end latency, task success rate, and schema-violation rate, compared pairwise on the same tasks.
project_ideas.name: Hoist
project_ideas.poc: Build two versions of the same agent task suite: one harness resolving tool selection, argument schema validation, and formatting dynamically per step, and one where those are compiled to static prompts and constrained-decoding grammars. Run both against a fixed task set and model.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of C++: Bell Labs, Negative Overhead Abstraction, Mistakes | Bjarne Stroustrup

project_ideas.based_on: when you do it, it blows your whole leg off
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding guardrail layers to an agent reduces the frequency of recoverable errors while increasing the mean severity of the errors that survive them, so severity-weighted metrics diverge from error-rate metrics.
project_ideas.measurement: Error rate per task plus severity distribution (fraction of failures requiring human intervention or causing irreversible state change) for each configuration, and the divergence between the two metrics.
project_ideas.name: Tail Risk Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent with two configurations (unguarded and heavily guarded) over the same task distribution; classify each failure by recoverability and downstream cost, then compare frequency distributions and severity distributions.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of C++: Bell Labs, Negative Overhead Abstraction, Mistakes | Bjarne Stroustrup

project_ideas.based_on: avoid breaking existing code while introducing modern capabilities
project_ideas.hypothesis: Additive-only evolution of a tool schema under a large-majority approval rule yields a measurably lower long-run consumer breakage rate than periodic breaking releases, at a quantifiable cost in feature velocity.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of consumer-breaking changes per release cycle and features shipped per cycle under each policy, and the estimated migration cost imposed on non-atomically-upgradable consumers.
project_ideas.name: Compat Budget
project_ideas.poc: Take a versioned tool/protocol history with deployed consumers, reconstruct which changes were additive versus breaking, and model breakage cost against feature-shipping rate under additive-only versus periodic-breaking policies.
project_ideas.video_title: Creator of C++: Bell Labs, Negative Overhead Abstraction, Mistakes | Bjarne Stroustrup

project_ideas.based_on: What signal tells an engineer that a harness layer is now dead weight after a model upgrade
project_ideas.hypothesis: Harness components can be classified as load-bearing or dead weight by ablating them across model generations, and the resulting task-completion horizon and coherence deltas form a repeatable removal heuristic.
project_ideas.measurement: Task-completion horizon, drift rate against a spec, and total token cost per completed task for each ablation condition, compared across model versions.
project_ideas.name: Harness Ablation Rig
project_ideas.poc: Instrument the three-agent harness so each layer (context resets, sprint decomposition, per-sprint evaluator cadence) can be toggled independently, then run the same task suite across two model checkpoints and record horizon, coherence, and token cost.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

project_ideas.based_on: What does the adversarial evaluator cost in tokens, latency, and wall-clock time relative to the horizon extension it buys?
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists an evaluator-cadence setting that dominates alternatives on quality per unit of wall-clock time, and continuous evaluation is not always optimal as cadence increases.
project_ideas.measurement: Quality score per task against wall-clock hours and tokens consumed, plotted to identify the Pareto frontier across cadence settings.
project_ideas.name: Evaluator Cost Frontier Sweeper
project_ideas.poc: Instrument the generator-evaluator loop to report per-agent token and time splits, then sweep evaluator cadence from per-sprint to continuous while holding the task fixed.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

project_ideas.based_on: Are rubrics for subjective quality reusable across tasks, or must they be hand-crafted per domain?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Rubrics written for one artifact class transfer to another with measurable but bounded degradation in evaluator discriminative power, rather than failing outright.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between rubric-based evaluator scores and human judgments per domain, and the score delta between native and transferred rubrics.
project_ideas.name: Cross-Domain Rubric Transfer Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Take a frontend-oriented rubric, apply it to a non-frontend artifact class produced by the same harness, and compare evaluator scores against human rankings.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

project_ideas.based_on: Does filesystem-mediated coordination with zero shared context still hold as the agent count and task breadth grow beyond three roles?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Zero-shared-context filesystem coordination fails past a bounded agent count through artifact contention and contract negotiation overhead before it fails through state divergence.
project_ideas.measurement: Contract negotiation overhead per sprint, write-contention collisions, and state divergence incidents as a function of agent count.
project_ideas.name: File-First Coordination Scaling Probe
project_ideas.poc: Extend the file-based protocol from three roles to five and above on the same task class, logging every file read, write, and contract negotiation step.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson

project_ideas.based_on: evaluation and calibration should be woven continuously into deployed agent actions
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding a lightweight calibration probe to each production tool call of a deployed agent reduces the divergence between offline eval scores and live task success by at least 20% after 30 days, compared to an agent retrained only on periodic offline evals.
project_ideas.measurement: Calibration divergence = |offline eval success - production task success|, measured before and after the intervention; plus raw production task success rate.
project_ideas.name: Every-Action Calibration Probe
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a customer-support agent to emit a compact (state, action, outcome) signal per tool call; sample 1% of traces for human-in-the-loop ratings; periodically fine-tune a small adapter on these traces while continuing to use the base policy.
project_ideas.video_title: The Mountain Path - 山道  (Full Documentary)

project_ideas.based_on: adversarial conditions, scarcity, and high-friction scenarios are deliberate training mechanisms
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents fine-tuned for 25% of episodes under injected tool failures, rate limits, and truncated context will outperform a smooth-only baseline by 30% in a deliberately degraded evaluation set, while staying within 10% of the baseline's performance on a normal evaluation set.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate in the scarred environment and in the normal environment.
project_ideas.name: Scarcity Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Run an agentic coding benchmark in two regimes—full-resource and scarce-resource—and use preference optimization on trajectories from the scarce environment, then cross-evaluate the resulting policy on both regimes.
project_ideas.video_title: The Mountain Path - 山道  (Full Documentary)

project_ideas.based_on: Hermits live alone or in very small groups to minimize worldly distractions
project_ideas.hypothesis: Gating non-urgent ambient input (notifications, social feeds, low-priority email) behind a sampled context channel improves completion rate on long-horizon reasoning tasks by 20% or more, while allowing recall of 95% of high-priority interrupts.
project_ideas.measurement: Task goal completion rate, interrupt recall, context-token usage.
project_ideas.name: Quiet Mode Context Router
project_ideas.poc: Implement a context router with two channels: a trusted high-priority stream and a sampled low-priority stream; run long-horizon document-analysis tasks with synthetic interruptions and ambient messages injected.
project_ideas.video_title: The Mountain Path - 山道  (Full Documentary)

project_ideas.based_on: autonomy without a method layer will go astray
project_ideas.hypothesis: A deterministic method layer that checks action preconditions before tool execution will reduce irreversible-error rate by at least 50% in the first 100 production runs compared to a prompt-only guardrail, with less than 10% throughput overhead.
project_ideas.measurement: Irreversible-error rate and latency/throughput overhead.
project_ideas.name: Guardrail Gate
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a file-management/automation agent with a guardrail service that validates each proposed tool call against a small set of preconditions (path safety, quota limits, action reversibility) before dispatch; run agentic tasks on a dev corpus.
project_ideas.video_title: The Mountain Path - 山道  (Full Documentary)

project_ideas.based_on: Smart truncation preserves the head and tail while retrieving middle content by ID from memory.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A harness that keeps the first 10% and last 20% of conversation tokens and retrieves the middle by ID will maintain task success above 85% over 50-turn sessions, while naive last-N truncation drops below 50%.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate at turn 50; retrieval hit rate; total tokens consumed.
project_ideas.name: HeadTail Memory Agent Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal agent runtime with a message store and two context policies: naive last-N truncation and head/tail + ID retrieval. Run a 50-turn multi-step benchmark.
project_ideas.video_title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia

project_ideas.based_on: Not all context belongs in the same agent; sub-agents offload heavy tasks.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Delegating multi-query search tasks to a sub-agent reduces parent context size by at least 40% and reduces end-to-end failure rate by 20% compared to a monolithic agent, with no loss in answer quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Parent context token count; failure rate; answer quality (LLM-as-judge or human label).
project_ideas.name: Sub-Agent Context Isolation Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement a monolithic search agent and a parent/sub-agent version; run a suite of 100 information-gathering tasks; measure parent context length and task success.
project_ideas.video_title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia

project_ideas.based_on: Long-session evals
project_ideas.hypothesis: A 50-turn eval suite will surface at least twice as many context-related failures as the same suite evaluated at turn 1 and turn 5.
project_ideas.measurement: Context-related failure rate by turn number; regression precision (failure cases reproducible).
project_ideas.name: Long-Session Context Eval Suite
project_ideas.poc: Create an eval harness that can run agent tasks up to 50+ turns, injecting realistic user sessions, and compare failure rates across turn lengths.
project_ideas.video_title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia

project_ideas.based_on: Real long-term memory across sessions and surfaces is still hard and unbuilt.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An ID-addressable memory store with user identity can answer questions about facts from a previous conversation on a different surface with at least 70% precision without explicit continuation.
project_ideas.measurement: Retrieval precision/recall for cross-session facts; qualitative continuity score.
project_ideas.name: Cross-Surface Memory Store
project_ideas.poc: Build a small memory service, expose it to two chat surfaces, store conversation events with user IDs, and query after a new session begins.
project_ideas.video_title: How we solved Context Management in Agents — Sally-Ann Delucia

project_ideas.based_on: safely accept hundreds of thousands of autonomously generated lines of code
project_ideas.hypothesis: When an autonomous coding agent is required to produce multi-file features that pass a machine-checkable behavioral test contract before merge, its output will have fewer integration regressions and require fewer human repair edits than output from an unconstrained agent pipeline on the same tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: CI failure rate after merge, defect density per 1,000 lines of generated code, and human rework hours per feature
project_ideas.name: AgentAccept
project_ideas.poc: On a pre-selected open-source repository, run two agent pipelines—baseline repo-context code generation versus test-contract-gated generation where the agent can only merge after automated tests and static checks pass. Apply both to five multi-file issues.
project_ideas.video_title: Google's Record Quarter, the White House Intervenes, and GPT 5.5 Silently Matches Mythos | EP 254

project_ideas.based_on: infinite code context
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent's multi-file task success improves with context coverage only up to a saturation point; after that, retrieval-indexed selective context will produce faster time-to-merge with no worse defect count than naively including the entire repository in the context window.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, time-to-merge, proportion of lines edited during human review
project_ideas.name: SprintScale Context Probe
project_ideas.poc: Using a real codebase, run the same agent on identical multi-file tasks under three conditions: isolated-file context, full-repository concatenated context, and retrieval-augmented context. Repeat each task across multiple runs.
project_ideas.video_title: Google's Record Quarter, the White House Intervenes, and GPT 5.5 Silently Matches Mythos | EP 254

project_ideas.based_on: government gatekeeping or self-policing by labs will stifle competition
project_ideas.hypothesis: Public releases of open-weight models will show a measurable announcement-to-download lag whenever a pre-release vetting step exists, and that lag will be larger for smaller labs than for frontier labs with standing review resources.
project_ideas.measurement: Median announcement-to-model-release lag for vetted versus non-vetted releases, controlling for model size
project_ideas.name: ReleaseLag Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Build a monitoring harness that timestamps model announcements and checkpoint release dates across model providers, tagging each release as subject to internal review, government clearance, or no formal vetting. Fit a lag model to historical releases.
project_ideas.video_title: Google's Record Quarter, the White House Intervenes, and GPT 5.5 Silently Matches Mythos | EP 254

project_ideas.based_on: Google search volume flattened in 2017, yet revenue continues to scale upward due to targeted AI ads
project_ideas.hypothesis: Holding query volume constant, switching from a broad relevance ranking model to an AI-targeted ad ranking model will increase transactional value per query in a search-like product.
project_ideas.measurement: Incremental conversion value per query and revenue per non-converted impression
project_ideas.name: Flat-Traffic Ad-Rank Trial
project_ideas.poc: In a small e-commerce search sandbox, randomly assign synthetic user sessions to a baseline ranking model or an AI-targeted ranking model while keeping query volume identical, then compare downstream purchase behavior.
project_ideas.video_title: Google's Record Quarter, the White House Intervenes, and GPT 5.5 Silently Matches Mythos | EP 254

project_ideas.based_on: Can outcome rubrics be validated and adversarially tested the way unit tests are
project_ideas.hypothesis: Regressions and reward hacks in outcome rubrics are detectable pre-deployment by a suite of known-failure and literal-reading cases: rubrics that pass the suite produce higher human-rated task success and fewer reward-hacked convergences than ad-hoc rubrics at equal iteration budgets.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of reward-hacked convergence per rubric, human-rated correctness delta between suite-validated and ad-hoc rubrics, and iterations-to-exit distribution.
project_ideas.name: Rubric Regression Suite (RRS)
project_ideas.poc: Author 30 rubrics across 3 tasks, each paired with a known-bad output and an adversarially literal-reading output; run outcome-driven sub-agents against them and record whether the loop exits on the intended solution or on the literal rubric; mutate rubric wording to find gameable phrasings.
project_ideas.video_title: How to get to production faster with Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Multiagent orchestration and outcomes optimization reduced per-turn chart rendering latency from 37 seconds to 10 seconds
project_ideas.hypothesis: The reported latency improvement is attributable mainly to outcome-based early exit and parallel tool calls rather than to fast mode, and the effect shrinks or reverses on multi-hour tasks where coordination overhead compounds.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-turn and per-task wall-clock latency, quality score, tokens spent per completed task, and turns avoided by early exit, reported as an ablation table per task horizon.
project_ideas.name: Factor-Ablated Orchestration Benchmark (FAOB)
project_ideas.poc: Recreate a chart-rendering style per-turn task and a multi-hour end-to-end task; run four arms — single agent baseline, orchestration only, outcomes only, orchestration plus outcomes plus fast mode — holding token budget and quality rubric constant.
project_ideas.video_title: How to get to production faster with Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Context management at the right time is powerful, but at the wrong time is a distraction
project_ideas.hypothesis: A compaction trigger keyed to task state (for example, after tool-result ingestion but never mid-synthesis) yields fewer downstream quality regressions than fixed-N-turn compaction at an identical token budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Downstream step success rate and token cost per completed task for each trigger policy, plus a taxonomy of what information each mistimed compaction removed.
project_ideas.name: State-Aware Compaction Trigger Lab
project_ideas.poc: Instrument agent sessions to log compaction events against task state; run the same multi-step task under fixed-N compaction and under a state-aware trigger policy, with and without an explicit post-compaction task-state check.
project_ideas.video_title: How to get to production faster with Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Secrets are removed from the agent process and relocated behind a credential proxy at the sandbox boundary
project_ideas.hypothesis: With a credential proxy, scoped credentials, network allowlists, and a declared environment, the blast radius of a prompt-injected long-running agent is bounded to zero successful egress, whereas an equivalent agent holding live credentials in-process exfiltrates in a measurable fraction of trials.
project_ideas.measurement: Successful exfiltration rate per configuration, number of credential-scope violations, and whether any policy-bounded run could reach non-allowlisted egress.
project_ideas.name: Confused-Deputy Blast Radius Test (Gatehouse Red-Team)
project_ideas.poc: Build a red-team harness that injects exfiltration instructions through tool outputs and generated code; run N trials in both configurations (proxy-plus-allowlist vs in-process secrets) and log every attempted and successful egress and credential read.
project_ideas.video_title: How to get to production faster with Claude Managed Agents

project_ideas.based_on: What measurable effect does the validation contract have on bug rates or drift over multi-day missions?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Autonomous missions that pre-commit a validation contract and use code-blind adversarial validators will have at least 30% lower defect density and fewer drift-related reworks than missions using post-implementation tests over 10+ day runs.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect density (bugs per 1k lines), rework rate (reopened features), drift score (spec-vs-implementation divergence).
project_ideas.name: Validation Contract A/B on Long-Horizon Missions
project_ideas.poc: Build a minimal multi-agent harness that executes identical feature tasks in two modes: (A) upfront validation contract with blind validators, and (B) post-implementation tests; run 10 synthetic missions and compare.
project_ideas.video_title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

project_ideas.based_on: How should the boundary between serial feature chunks and read-only parallel tasks be determined?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A scheduler that serializes feature mutations and parallelizes only explicitly read-only tasks will reduce token burn and coordination overhead by at least 40% compared to parallel feature execution at equivalent throughput.
project_ideas.measurement: Total tokens consumed, wall-clock time, conflict/duplication events, throughput (features/day).
project_ideas.name: Serial-Mutation Scheduler with Read-Only Parallelism
project_ideas.poc: Implement a task scheduler for a codebase agent testbed that classifies tasks as read-only or mutation; run identical feature sets in serial-default vs parallel-feature modes; measure token usage and conflict events.
project_ideas.video_title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

project_ideas.based_on: What are the failure modes of adversarial validators that have never seen the code?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Code-blind adversarial validators generate false-positive rejections at a measurable rate that can be reduced by adding a pre-committed spec diff and an arbitration step.
project_ideas.measurement: False positive rate, false negative rate, time-to-resolution, arbitration decisions.
project_ideas.name: Adversarial Validator Failure Taxonomy
project_ideas.poc: Create a validation loop with two validator types (code-blind adversarial and post-hoc) and measure rejections; implement arbitration and compare acceptance rates and bug escape rates.
project_ideas.video_title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

project_ideas.based_on: How model-agnostic is each role in practice?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Different model classes (large general, small instruction-tuned, code-specialized) show at least 20% variance in task success for orchestrator vs worker vs validator roles, allowing non-uniform model assignment to reduce cost without losing correctness.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, correctness, cost per task, orchestration/validation error rates.
project_ideas.name: Model-Agnostic Role Profiler
project_ideas.poc: Run a battery of tasks through three roles with three model classes; compute role-specific success/cost curves; generate assignment recommendations.
project_ideas.video_title: The Multi-Agent Architecture That Actually Ships — Luke Alvoeiro, Factory

project_ideas.based_on: Cycle on a subject multiple times
project_ideas.hypothesis: Structuring long agent reports as two or three explicit passes over the critical payload, with enumerated resync markers between passes, increases delayed human recall of critical items compared with a single optimized summary, at the cost of increased token count.
project_ideas.measurement: Delayed recall accuracy of critical items, perceived redundancy tolerance, and token-cost overhead.
project_ideas.name: Redundant Agent Report Compiler
project_ideas.poc: A formatter that consumes an agent trace and emits a multi-pass report with ordinal markers; A/B test single-pass vs multi-pass versions on readers who must later answer decision-relevant questions.
project_ideas.video_title: Patrick Winston MIT Last Lecture – Leadership, Communication & Life Lessons

project_ideas.based_on: Saying 'Thank you' implies gratitude that the audience survived your talk
project_ideas.hypothesis: Replacing a terminal courtesy token ('Thank you', 'Let me know if you have questions') with a content-bearing final assertion increases retention of the main decision or claim by both human readers and downstream LLM consumers.
project_ideas.measurement: Human recall of the main point, downstream LLM summarization fidelity, and user satisfaction.
project_ideas.name: Terminal Token Retention Harness
project_ideas.poc: A harness that takes a set of agent responses and rewrites the final segment into either a courtesy token or a content-bearing assertion; measure recall and downstream agent behavior.
project_ideas.video_title: Patrick Winston MIT Last Lecture – Leadership, Communication & Life Lessons

project_ideas.based_on: Build a fence around your idea to distinguish it from others.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding near-miss non-examples to tool descriptions or classification prompts reduces misfires and boundary errors more than adding additional positive examples of intended use.
project_ideas.measurement: Reduction in boundary-case misfires, precision/recall on ambiguous tool selection tasks.
project_ideas.name: Fence-Builder for Tool Schemas
project_ideas.poc: A schema augmenter that generates contrastive non-examples from a tool's intended behavior; evaluate tool-calling accuracy on ambiguous inputs.
project_ideas.video_title: Patrick Winston MIT Last Lecture – Leadership, Communication & Life Lessons

project_ideas.based_on: Slides should be used for exposing ideas rather than teaching
project_ideas.hypothesis: For teaching an abstract technical mechanism, a slow incrementally built medium (live coding, blackboard-like shared canvas) produces better delayed transfer than a dense slide or README artifact, when content and total time are held constant.
project_ideas.measurement: Delayed transfer performance, time-to-first-correct-explanation, and preference.
project_ideas.name: Rate-Matched Concept Transfer Experiment
project_ideas.poc: Identical explanation of a mechanism delivered via slide deck, static diagram, live coding, and physical prop; measure delayed transfer tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Patrick Winston MIT Last Lecture – Leadership, Communication & Life Lessons

project_ideas.based_on: measured reduction in security review latency and number of approved MCP servers
project_ideas.hypothesis: Introducing a gateway-mediated approval path reduces median security review cycle time per MCP server by >50% and increases the number of approved servers per quarter by >2x compared to a per-server review baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Median review cycle time (hours), reviewer hours per server, number of servers approved before a fixed review budget is exhausted.
project_ideas.name: Review-Latency A/B for Gateway vs Per-Server MCP Approval
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a review pipeline for 20 mock MCP servers under two regimes: (a) per-server review with unique auth/security questionnaires and (b) gateway root-of-trust review where only business logic is assessed; instrument each review step as a task with timestamps and reviewer effort.
project_ideas.video_title: Gateways are All You Need — Karan Sampath, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: failure modes when the gateway itself is unavailable
project_ideas.hypothesis: A gateway deployed without HA or failover causes 100% tool-call failure during an outage, while a gateway with warm standby and a specified fail-closed policy maintains >99% tool-call availability and 100% audit-event completeness.
project_ideas.measurement: Tool-call success rate during fault, audit event completeness (fraction of calls with start/end/decision records), p99 outage duration until service restoration.
project_ideas.name: Gateway Blast-Radius Chaos Harness
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a minimal MCP client, gateway, and mock MCP server; inject gateway pod kill, network partition, and policy misconfiguration; record tool-call success/failure and audit completeness for each fault.
project_ideas.video_title: Gateways are All You Need — Karan Sampath, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: change the tool-call latency and error profile
project_ideas.hypothesis: Gateway-mediated MCP tool calls add <10 ms p95 latency and <0.1% error rate versus direct MCP server connections when RBAC and audit are enabled, and the overhead scales sublinearly with the number of policy rules.
project_ideas.measurement: p50/p95/p99 round-trip latency, error rate by class, policy-evaluation time per call.
project_ideas.name: Gateway Tool-Call Latency and Error Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Benchmark 10k tool calls through direct MCP connections and through a gateway with RBAC/audit enabled at three policy-rule counts (1, 10, 100); measure round-trip latency and error classes.
project_ideas.video_title: Gateways are All You Need — Karan Sampath, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: delegation and revocation of user identity across heterogeneous MCP clients and managed agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: After an IDP revocation event, gateway-mediated tool calls using delegated user identity stop authorizing within one token lifetime for stateless flows but may continue for long-lived managed agent sessions unless explicit revocation propagation is implemented.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-revocation (seconds) for fresh client vs managed agent session; number of tool calls authorized after revocation; audit-log evidence of revocation event.
project_ideas.name: Delegated Identity Revocation Propagation Test
project_ideas.poc: Prototype delegated-identity flows through the gateway with a mock IDP; issue a tool call, revoke the user in the IDP, then replay tool calls from a managed agent runtime and from a fresh MCP client, measuring the time until authorization is refused.
project_ideas.video_title: Gateways are All You Need — Karan Sampath, Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: Shallow modules create tiny blobs that are hard for both humans and AI to understand and explore
project_ideas.hypothesis: At identical functionality, agent task success rate rises and tokens/steps per accepted change fall as module depth increases (fewer, wider interfaces with hidden interiors).
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, tokens per accepted change, tool-call steps, and rate of edits landing in unintended modules, compared across the three granularity variants.
project_ideas.name: Agent Comprehension Bench
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same application at three module-granularity levels — many shallow modules, one monolith, deep modules with narrow interfaces — and run an identical task suite against each with the same coding agent, recording navigation and edit traces.
project_ideas.video_title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock

project_ideas.based_on: The rate of feedback is your speed limit
project_ideas.hypothesis: Accepted-changes-per-hour in an agent loop is bounded by time-to-feedback, so cutting verification latency (test runtime, type-check time, browser round-trip) raises completed-task rate proportionally and shrinks generated step size.
project_ideas.measurement: Wall-clock throughput (accepted changes per hour), rework rate per accepted change, and total tokens per accepted change, with and without the latency-derived step cap.
project_ideas.name: Feedback-Latency Governor
project_ideas.poc: A harness that measures time-to-feedback per step and automatically caps the agent's step size at that bound, run over a fixed task set against a batch-generation baseline with no such cap.
project_ideas.video_title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock

project_ideas.based_on: A UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md file lives in the repo and is referenced during planning and implementation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Automated drift detection between persisted glossary terms, code identifiers, and test names reduces agent requirement-conformance failures relative to an unenforced glossary file.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of detected term/identifier divergences over time, requirement-conformance rate on a fixed task set, and prompt verbosity (tokens spent restating domain context).
project_ideas.name: Glossary Drift Gate
project_ideas.poc: A checker that maps UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md terms to identifiers and test names, flags divergence as a blocking gate before agent runs, and injects the reconciled vocabulary into the prompt.
project_ideas.video_title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock

project_ideas.based_on: a skill (/grill-me) forces the AI to relentlessly interview the user
project_ideas.hypothesis: An adversarial pre-code interrogation phase that enumerates the design decision tree reduces requirement-conformance failures per accepted change more cheaply than repairing misaligned output after generation.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of design branches resolved pre-code, rework rate, tokens per accepted change, and fraction of generated code discarded after first review.
project_ideas.name: Interrogation-Before-Generation Skill Eval
project_ideas.poc: A /grill-me-style skill that iteratively questions the user down each design branch until a shared design concept is recorded, benchmarked against direct generation on the same underspecified task set.
project_ideas.video_title: "Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever" — Matt Pocock

project_ideas.based_on: The abstraction argument only works when the layer below is verifiable.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Wrapping an LLM codegen step in a verification layer — property-based tests, behavioral contracts, and rule-level checks on business logic and security paths — reduces the rate of silent defects (defects undetected by the generating operator) below the rate observed for unwrapped generation.
project_ideas.measurement: Silent defect rate per task and per KLOC in the wrapped vs. unwrapped arm, plus the fraction of seeded business-rule and security defects caught by each check type.
project_ideas.name: Verified-Generation Gate
project_ideas.poc: A harness that takes a spec, generates a module, then runs property-based tests, behavioral contracts, and targeted security/business-rule assertions before the module is admitted to the codebase; run against a seeded-defect task suite with wrapped and unwrapped arms.
project_ideas.video_title: Is this the only skill left?

project_ideas.based_on: How can cognitive debt from AI-generated code be measured or detected before it becomes a production failure?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Time-to-answer the three systems questions, deletion-test accuracy, and the ratio of reviewed to generated modules predict incident rates in AI-built codebases better than code complexity or test coverage alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between per-module cognitive-debt proxies and subsequent incident rate, benchmarked against complexity and coverage baselines.
project_ideas.name: Cognitive Debt Instrument
project_ideas.poc: Instrument three AI-built codebases with the three-question protocol and a deletion/blast-radius tracing exercise for maintainers, recording per-module scores, then track production incidents over a fixed 90-day window.
project_ideas.video_title: Is this the only skill left?

project_ideas.based_on: Junior devs lost the forcing function of writing boilerplate code by hand.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Deliberate interventions — manual reimplementation from memory, mandated spec writing, and repeated deletion-test exercises — restore junior developers' ability to answer the three systems questions and trace blast radius to a level comparable to a pre-automation hand-coding baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Pre/post delta in three-systems-question answer time and accuracy, and deletion-test blast-radius tracing accuracy versus the baseline cohort.
project_ideas.name: Forcing Function Lab
project_ideas.poc: A controlled training study with junior developers assigned to intervention and comparison arms, measuring blast-radius tracing accuracy on unfamiliar generated modules before, immediately after, and weeks after the intervention.
project_ideas.video_title: Is this the only skill left?

project_ideas.based_on: The 'jagged frontier' describes AI being sharp in some tasks and surprisingly dull in others within the same session.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-task capability mapping and verification routing outperforms session-level trust calibration on downstream error rates, because capability varies within a single session rather than at the session level.
project_ideas.measurement: Downstream error rate and human verification cost per task under task-level routing versus session-level trust settings.
project_ideas.name: Task-Level Capability Router
project_ideas.poc: Build per-task capability maps for a fixed model within one session, route each task to accept-as-is, verify-before-accept, or escalate-to-human based on the map, and compare against a single session-wide trust policy on the same task stream.
project_ideas.video_title: Is this the only skill left?

project_ideas.based_on: 'going solid'
project_ideas.hypothesis: A CI probe measuring cross-module coupling, change-scope, and testability decay can flag AI-generated PR batches before a codebase reaches the 'going solid' threshold, as validated by substantially higher refactoring cost for unflagged batches.
project_ideas.measurement: Coupling coefficient, average change-scope per feature, refactor time-to-complete, and number of PRs merged before human-perceived slowdown.
project_ideas.name: Solidity Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: Run the probe on a sample repository where feature branches are generated with AI; compare flagged versus unflagged commits over four weeks; perform forced refactor after threshold.
project_ideas.video_title: Features vs. Futures: Software Design in the Age of AI – Kent Beck | ShipSummit | Rise8

project_ideas.based_on: option value
project_ideas.hypothesis: An 'option score' computed from module API surface, coupling, and irreversibility of merged AI-generated features correlates with future rework effort better than feature-count or velocity metrics.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman correlation between option score and forward rework versus velocity/feature-count correlations.
project_ideas.name: OptionLedger
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a development repository; compute option score for each merged AI-generated feature; log rework hours and bug-link commits; test correlation over a quarter.
project_ideas.video_title: Features vs. Futures: Software Design in the Age of AI – Kent Beck | ShipSummit | Rise8

project_ideas.based_on: genie because it grants your wishes
project_ideas.hypothesis: Applying a guardrail stack—explicit context specification, contract tests, architecture boundary checks, and review gates—cuts integration defects from AI-generated feature code to the level of human-authored code while preserving most of the speed gain.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect injection rate, rollback count, feature time-to-merge, and rework hours.
project_ideas.name: GenieGates
project_ideas.poc: Generate the same small feature set with and without guardrails across multiple codebases; track review defects and rollback incidents.
project_ideas.video_title: Features vs. Futures: Software Design in the Age of AI – Kent Beck | ShipSummit | Rise8

project_ideas.based_on: cheap and reversible
project_ideas.hypothesis: When every AI-suggested feature starts as an isolated reversible experiment with automated rollback, teams attempt at least three times more 'stupid ideas' without increasing rollback or integration incidents.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of experiments tried, success rate, rollback incidence, shipped features, and retained optionality score.
project_ideas.name: ReversiLab
project_ideas.poc: Set up ephemeral branch/sandbox with database rollback for AI feature suggestions; record attempted, discarded, and shipped changes for six weeks.
project_ideas.video_title: Features vs. Futures: Software Design in the Age of AI – Kent Beck | ShipSummit | Rise8

project_ideas.based_on: Non-functional requirements should be encoded as executable artifacts—linter rules, docs, and tests
project_ideas.hypothesis: Encoding non-functional requirements as lint/test gates before agent execution increases first-pass merge-ready pull request rate by at least 25 percentage points versus an ungated agent baseline on matched code tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: First-pass merge-ready rate, mean revision cycles/PR, violations of encoded NFRs per PR, time-to-merge.
project_ideas.name: GuardRailBench: Quantifying Executable NFR Guardrails
project_ideas.poc: Using one codebase and a fixed task set, run N independent agents in two modes: (A) default repo, (B) same repo plus linter rules and tests asserting file-size limits, retry/timeout behavior, and layering constraints. Blind human reviewers judge merge-readiness without knowing mode.
project_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: How to Build Software When Humans Steer, Agents Execute — Ryan Lopopolo, OpenAI

project_ideas.based_on: Repository structure is a context-engineering decision: modularity and localized dependencies are prerequisites for agent success
project_ideas.hypothesis: Refactoring a moderate monolith into context-sized modules with local dependency graphs improves agent task success by at least 20% against the unmodified monolith under identical context-window and agent settings.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, mean final context utilization, number of agent iterations, compile/test pass rate.
project_ideas.name: Context-Slice Refactor Experiment
project_ideas.poc: Select an existing monolith and representative feature tasks; ask the same agent with the same tools and context window to complete tasks before and after refactoring into subpackages with clear interfaces and localized dependencies.
project_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: How to Build Software When Humans Steer, Agents Execute — Ryan Lopopolo, OpenAI

project_ideas.based_on: Human code review becomes a major bottleneck when agents produce high pull request volume.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A discrete-event model of parallel agents and serial human reviewers predicts that end-to-end throughput saturates after only 2–3 concurrent agents, and adding automated review plus garbage-collection slots raises the productive parallelism threshold by at least 3x.
project_ideas.measurement: Throughput at saturation, queued PR backlog, conflict count, merge latency; simulated vs pilot outcomes.
project_ideas.name: Agent PR Flow Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Build a small simulator parameterized by measured agent PR rate, human review service time, conflict probability, and GC cadence; validate predictions against a team pilot running batches of 1–10 agents.
project_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: How to Build Software When Humans Steer, Agents Execute — Ryan Lopopolo, OpenAI

project_ideas.based_on: Terminal Bench shows that a coding agent harness with only terminal input/output tools can match or outperform much more feature-rich harnesses
project_ideas.hypothesis: A coding agent harness exposing only terminal keystroke/screen-read tools achieves higher task success on real repository issues than the same model using a specialized file/edit/sub-agent harness, after controlling for prompt and model.
project_ideas.measurement: Resolved issue percentage, average tokens per task, and developer-judged patch quality.
project_ideas.name: TerminalArena
project_ideas.poc: Build two minimal harness variants (terminal-only vs four tools read/write/edit/bash) and run both on a curated set of 20 real GitHub issues; measure resolve rate, time, and token usage.
project_ideas.video_title: Building pi in a World of Slop — Mario Zechner

project_ideas.based_on: Coding harnesses often mutate the model's context in hidden ways
project_ideas.hypothesis: Diffing all hidden prompt, tool, and tool-output transformations across harness releases reveals that silent context mutations correlate with degraded task success on stable workflows.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of hidden context changes per release; A/B task success delta with/without injected reminders/pruning.
project_ideas.name: ContextDiff
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness wrapper that logs and diffs system prompts, tool definitions, injected reminders, and tool output pruning between runs; replay the same coding tasks before and after a release and measure success.
project_ideas.video_title: Building pi in a World of Slop — Mario Zechner

project_ideas.based_on: A coding agent harness can be made self-modifying by shipping human-readable documentation and runnable code examples
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent-generated in-process extensions can be constrained by a permission-scoped API and static/dynamic verification to reduce unsafe modifications while preserving utility.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of agent-generated extensions that execute without security violations vs baseline without sandboxing.
project_ideas.name: ExtensionSafe
project_ideas.poc: Implement an extension loader with sandboxing, permission scopes (read-only, no network, specific files), and a denylist of dangerous APIs; task an agent to write five extensions from docs/examples, then check for violations.
project_ideas.video_title: Building pi in a World of Slop — Mario Zechner

project_ideas.based_on: Injecting compiler/LSP errors after every edit tool call imposes a continuous error-checking loop
project_ideas.hypothesis: Delaying LSP/compiler diagnostic injection to explicit checkpoints after chunks of edits increases code completion rate and reduces edit-loop confusion compared to immediate per-edit injection.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, number of logic errors in final code, and token efficiency.
project_ideas.name: CheckpointLSP
project_ideas.poc: For the same harness and same model, add an option to buffer LSP diagnostics until the model invokes a `check-errors` tool or after N edits; run an A/B test on 15 coding tasks and compare completion and correctness.
project_ideas.video_title: Building pi in a World of Slop — Mario Zechner

project_ideas.based_on: Agentic search achieved higher accuracy with significantly fewer tokens and lower cost on TypeScript/Go test bugs.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Under a fixed token budget, agentic search using grep, find, and cat achieves higher bug-localization accuracy at lower token cost than vector top-k retrieval across multiple languages and repo sizes.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy, tokens consumed, dollar cost, and number of search calls per successful bug localization, disaggregated by language and repository size.
project_ideas.name: RepoTraverse Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark harness that runs both retrieval architectures against typescript-go merge PRs with 'fix' in the title and Swe-bench verified Django bug datasets, controlling for model, prompt, and token budget.
project_ideas.video_title: Stop Shipping on Vibes — How to Build Real Evals for Coding Agents

project_ideas.based_on: Claude Code runs as a subprocess, resulting in missing visibility into tool calls without proper environment variable configuration.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Injecting the parent span ID through environment variables into subprocess coding agents eliminates orphaned tool-call spans and produces complete parent-child trace trees without in-process instrumentation.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of orphaned tool-call spans, number of attached child spans per parent trace, and debugging time to reconstruct failed runs.
project_ideas.name: TraceBridge
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a Claude Code style subprocess agent with an instrumentation shim that propagates trace context via environment variables, then compare trace completeness against a baseline with no propagation.
project_ideas.video_title: Stop Shipping on Vibes — How to Build Real Evals for Coding Agents

project_ideas.based_on: A loop connecting application production logs, sampled datasets, task configurations, and scoring mechanisms.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Wiring production logs into sampled eval datasets and pre-ship experiment gates reduces recurring agent regressions and rollbacks compared with ad hoc prompt testing by PMs and engineers.
project_ideas.measurement: Production regression rate, rollback frequency, and time-to-detect regressions before and after gating.
project_ideas.name: EvalLoop Sampler
project_ideas.poc: Implement a pipeline that samples production logs into golden, edge-case, and failure-mode datasets, runs task configurations and scoring, and blocks deployment when experiment metrics regress.
project_ideas.video_title: Stop Shipping on Vibes — How to Build Real Evals for Coding Agents

project_ideas.based_on: How do you prevent LLM-based evaluation tools from artificially inflating token counts or introducing bias?
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM-as-a-judge scoring introduces measurable token overhead and model-dependent scoring bias, and cross-checking judges against deterministic checks and human review reduces contamination of quality and cost metrics.
project_ideas.measurement: Judge token overhead, score agreement with deterministic and human labels, and variance in configuration rankings caused by judge choice.
project_ideas.name: JudgeCost Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Run a fixed agent-eval dataset through multiple judge models plus deterministic checks and human review, measuring token overhead attributable to each judge and scoring drift across judge models.
project_ideas.video_title: Stop Shipping on Vibes — How to Build Real Evals for Coding Agents

project_ideas.based_on: interrogating the same question across multiple vendors
project_ideas.hypothesis: Majority/divergence signals across independent model families plus adversarial for/against prompting predict ground truth better than single-model self-consistency on the same tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Error correlation matrix between model families; accuracy of divergence-based flags vs single-model confidence; cost per verified output.
project_ideas.name: Cross-Vendor Adversarial Verifier Harness
project_ideas.poc: Harness that sends identical prompts to ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek, also generates pro and con arguments, then compares outputs for agreement/divergence; evaluate against a labeled QA set.
project_ideas.video_title: Ex-Google Exec: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027) | Mo Gawdat

project_ideas.based_on: Accountability is claimed to be the binding constraint on AI systems
project_ideas.hypothesis: Enforcing signed provenance at the platform boundary reduces the rate of untraceable synthetic media passing as human-authored, without unacceptable operational overhead.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of synthetic artifacts with verifiable provenance; spoofing success rate; added latency and storage overhead.
project_ideas.name: Provenance Gate for Agent-Generated Artifacts
project_ideas.poc: API gateway or middleware that signs every model-generated artifact with an identity-bound attestation and verifies signatures on consumption; measure spoofing attempts and latency.
project_ideas.video_title: Ex-Google Exec: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027) | Mo Gawdat

project_ideas.based_on: Intelligence is described as a polarity-free force
project_ideas.hypothesis: Guardrail effectiveness, measured as bypass rate, degrades as underlying model capability increases across versions, even when the guardrail layer is held constant.
project_ideas.measurement: Bypass rate per model version; correlation between capability benchmark score and bypass rate.
project_ideas.name: Guardrail Degradation Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Testbed that runs a fixed set of policy/guardrail probes against successive versions of a model family; record bypass successes.
project_ideas.video_title: Ex-Google Exec: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027) | Mo Gawdat

project_ideas.based_on: AI absorbs entry-level cognitive work first
project_ideas.hypothesis: Replacing entry-level cognitive work with AI in an organization reduces the future supply of qualified human reviewers and red-teamers within 2–3 years, creating a measurable oversight capacity gap.
project_ideas.measurement: Projected number of qualified reviewers over time; time-to-fill review roles; oversight capacity vs demand.
project_ideas.name: Evaluator Supply Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Agent-based or system-dynamics simulation of a knowledge org where junior roles are automated; track promotion pipeline and reviewer availability.
project_ideas.video_title: Ex-Google Exec: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027) | Mo Gawdat

project_ideas.based_on: writes a test and evaluation function, and turns on an autonomous AI agent to build and iterate until the goal is achieved
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents given only the specification and a visible test set will close tasks as complete even when hidden held-out tests expose objective blind spots, yielding a hidden-test pass rate significantly lower than for human-reviewed changes.
project_ideas.measurement: Hidden pass rate and percentage of agent-reported completions that fail hidden tests.
project_ideas.name: Eval blind-spot detector for spec-test-run agents
project_ideas.poc: Run an autonomous coding agent on benchmark tasks where only a subset of tests is shown to the agent, then score its outputs against hidden tests that express the full spec.
project_ideas.video_title: Eric Schmidt on the Robotics Race, Singularity Timeline, and Energy Shortage | 241

project_ideas.based_on: Electricity is the primary resource constraint in the United States for scaling AI
project_ideas.hypothesis: Projected AI datacenter buildouts will overestimate realized compute capacity because grid interconnection and cooling timelines lag financial commitment to hardware capex.
project_ideas.measurement: Ratio of energized gigawatts to announced gigawatts and model error against conservative power-per-megawatt assumptions.
project_ideas.name: Power-aware datacenter capacity simulator
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a portfolio of datacenters from wattage, interconnection queue lead time, and the $50B-per-gigawatt capex ratio; compare planned and energized capacity over five years.
project_ideas.video_title: Eric Schmidt on the Robotics Race, Singularity Timeline, and Energy Shortage | 241

project_ideas.based_on: AI models will help build and improve their own code and reasoning
project_ideas.hypothesis: Applying eval-gated approvals and auditable provenance to autonomous coding loops reduces unintended code modifications and increases the probability that changes to an agent's own implementation pass rollback criteria.
project_ideas.measurement: Fraction of proposed self-modifications blocked or rolled back by eval and provenance gates, compared with an ungated baseline.
project_ideas.name: Recursive code provenance shield
project_ideas.poc: Build a sandbox agent runtime that records each spec-test-run iteration, requires an eval threshold for any change, and tracks provenance for code that later modifies the agent's own implementation.
project_ideas.video_title: Eric Schmidt on the Robotics Race, Singularity Timeline, and Energy Shortage | 241

project_ideas.based_on: China's manufacturing scale and vertical integration in electric vehicles and robotics
project_ideas.hypothesis: Assembling a physical AI product from country-denominated component and manufacturing dependencies exposes high-value subsystems where manufacturing concentration determines supply-chain leverage.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of system value and lead time exposed to a single-country manufacturing dependency.
project_ideas.name: Physical AI supply-chain scorecard
project_ideas.poc: Build a national dependency index from source-country data for robotic motors, actuators, sensors, batteries, and assembly capacity for representative robot platforms.
project_ideas.video_title: Eric Schmidt on the Robotics Race, Singularity Timeline, and Energy Shortage | 241

project_ideas.based_on: exhausts the instruction budget
project_ideas.hypothesis: Effective instruction consumption is additive across system prompt, project context file, tool schemas, and MCP descriptions, so appending a single large tool schema measurably degrades adherence on workflow steps whose instructions were not modified.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-step adherence rate and step-skip rate across N runs per condition, plus the delta in adherence on unmodified steps attributable to each added source.
project_ideas.name: Instruction Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a multi-step coding-agent harness to tally instruction counts per source and per step, then run a frozen task suite under three conditions: baseline, plus a large MCP tool surface, plus an added project memory file. Capture per-step adherence (steps silently skipped or partially executed) and task outcome.
project_ideas.video_title: Everything We Got Wrong About Research-Plan-Implement -  Dexter Horthy

project_ideas.based_on: How do we formally verify agent-generated plans?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A plan-checking pass that validates a generated plan against a structure-outline contract and vertical-phase constraints can predict downstream implementation defects before any code is written.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between checker flags and (a) downstream defect counts, (b) plan revision rounds, (c) reviewer rejection rate.
project_ideas.name: Plan Gate
project_ideas.poc: Run the design-to-structure-outline-to-plan stages on a set of real brownfield change requests, run an automated plan checker that flags horizontal phasing, missing checkpoints, and deviations from the outline contract, then compare flagged plans against unflagged plans through implementation and review.
project_ideas.video_title: Everything We Got Wrong About Research-Plan-Implement -  Dexter Horthy

project_ideas.based_on: Hide the raw ticket from research context to maintain objectivity
project_ideas.hypothesis: Withholding the raw ticket from the research step improves downstream plan quality and reduces defect rates, rather than only changing the framing of the research output.
project_ideas.measurement: Downstream defect rate, plan revision count, and blinded reviewer assessment of research-to-system-reality accuracy.
project_ideas.name: De-Ticketed Research A/B
project_ideas.poc: A/B the research step on matched change requests: condition A passes the ticket into research, condition B runs research on neutral context with the ticket reintroduced at design. Carry both through identical plan and implementation steps with blinded review.
project_ideas.video_title: Everything We Got Wrong About Research-Plan-Implement -  Dexter Horthy

project_ideas.based_on: AI use in software engineering increases rework
project_ideas.hypothesis: Rework introduced by coding agents can be attributed to specific upstream steps (research, plan, or implementation), and complexity-segmented rework-inclusive metrics invert the productivity ranking produced by output-volume metrics on brownfield tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Rework-inclusive net output (shipped lines minus corrective lines) per task complexity band, compared with raw output volume ranking.
project_ideas.name: Rework-Attributed Productivity Eval
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent pipeline to tag generated changes by originating step, then track subsequent corrective commits touching those same lines within a fixed window, segmented by greenfield versus brownfield and by a stated complexity proxy.
project_ideas.video_title: Everything We Got Wrong About Research-Plan-Implement -  Dexter Horthy

project_ideas.based_on: Pre-compiled pull requests
project_ideas.hypothesis: At agent-authored PR volumes above a threshold, human review time per PR grows superlinearly and defect escape rate rises; automated diff evaluation can reduce review time by 40% without increasing defect escape rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Minutes per PR review, defect escape rate, reviewer agreement, PR throughput.
project_ideas.name: PR Review Throughput Instrumentation
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an open-source repository with a simulated agent pipeline generating pre-compiled PRs, measure baseline review time and defect escape, then add an automated diff evaluator and re-measure.
project_ideas.video_title: NVIDIA's $1 Trillion Prediction, Anthropic Beats OpenAI, Tesla vs. TSMC & The CS Job Collapse | 240

project_ideas.based_on: 1,000x cost drop occurred between O1 and GPT-5.4 reasoning models
project_ideas.hypothesis: The reported 1,000x cost drop between O1 and GPT-5.4 shrinks to less than 100x when measured as cost per solved task at equivalent quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per solved task, solve rate, quality-equivalent score.
project_ideas.name: Cost-Per-Solved-Task Benchmark Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run a fixed agentic benchmark across model generations, compute cost per solved task, and compare to per-token price ratios.
project_ideas.video_title: NVIDIA's $1 Trillion Prediction, Anthropic Beats OpenAI, Tesla vs. TSMC & The CS Job Collapse | 240

project_ideas.based_on: task-level and junior-level
project_ideas.hypothesis: Task verifiability predicts AI automation displacement of software subtasks better than task complexity or seniority.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between verifiability score and delegation rate; displacement rate by task category.
project_ideas.name: Task-Verifiability Automation Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Classify a backlog of engineering tasks by verifiability score (test coverage, deterministic output, bounded scope) and measure which tasks are actually delegated to AI assistants over one sprint.
project_ideas.video_title: NVIDIA's $1 Trillion Prediction, Anthropic Beats OpenAI, Tesla vs. TSMC & The CS Job Collapse | 240

project_ideas.based_on: 73.3% of first-time enterprise customers
project_ideas.hypothesis: First-time enterprise adopters of Claude do not convert to retained production workloads at the 73.3% share; retention drops below 50% within two quarters.
project_ideas.measurement: Cohort retention rate, production workload share, expansion revenue.
project_ideas.name: Enterprise Model Cohort Retention Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Survey and track a panel of enterprise AI buyers from first evaluation through production deployment, recording model vendor and workload type.
project_ideas.video_title: NVIDIA's $1 Trillion Prediction, Anthropic Beats OpenAI, Tesla vs. TSMC & The CS Job Collapse | 240

project_ideas.based_on: spurious parallelism (spawning agents that contribute nothing)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Instrumenting multi-agent runs with per-agent marginal-contribution accounting will expose redundant-agent rates and true cost per unit quality that final-task-success scoring hides, and these figures will differ systematically across reward configurations.
project_ideas.measurement: Spawn efficiency (contributing agents divided by spawned agents), redundant-agent rate, cost per unit of task quality, and speedup versus a single agent at matched total cost.
project_ideas.name: Spawn Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Wrap an orchestrator/worker harness so every spawn, termination, sub-agent token cost, and each sub-agent's marginal effect on the outcome is logged; replay one task suite under outcome-only reward versus instantiation+finish+outcome reward.
project_ideas.video_title: How We Scaled Kimi K2.5 | Zhilin Yang's full GTC 2026 Keynote

project_ideas.based_on: QK-Clip constrains query and key projections in attention heads to restore stability
project_ideas.hypothesis: Max-logit trajectory is a measurable early-warning signal of large-scale optimizer divergence, and constraining query/key projections restores stability across seeds without degrading long-context retrieval beyond a bounded clip-threshold window.
project_ideas.measurement: Steps-to-divergence and max-logit slope per configuration; retrieval and loss deltas as a function of clip threshold and random seed.
project_ideas.name: Logit Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: Instrument per-step max logits during Muon-style training runs at multiple scales, sweep Q/K clip thresholds, and evaluate long-context retrieval and downstream loss at each threshold.
project_ideas.video_title: How We Scaled Kimi K2.5 | Zhilin Yang's full GTC 2026 Keynote

project_ideas.based_on: Muon optimizer provides ~2x token efficiency improvement over AdamW
project_ideas.hypothesis: A measurable share of the reported ~2x token efficiency over AdamW is attributable to weight decay and RMS update normalization rather than to orthogonalized updates, distinguishable as tokens-to-target-loss at matched settings.
project_ideas.measurement: tokens-to-target-loss ratio per arm per scale, divergence rate per arm, and the portion of the reported multiplier retained once regularization is matched.
project_ideas.name: Efficiency Attribution Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run controlled ablations at several model scales comparing AdamW with matched weight decay and RMS normalization against Muon, with tokens-to-target-loss as the dependent variable.
project_ideas.video_title: How We Scaled Kimi K2.5 | Zhilin Yang's full GTC 2026 Keynote

project_ideas.based_on: Drastically reduces time-per-output-token (TPOT) at long context lengths.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A runtime that models a 3:1 linear-to-full attention stack as two layer classes with distinct memory and state-update behavior predicts long-context time-per-output-token and peak memory within a small error margin, where a uniform-transformer model does not.
project_ideas.measurement: Predicted versus observed TPOT and peak memory at long context, and the deviation of the uniform-transformer baseline's predictions from the same measurements.
project_ideas.name: Hybrid-KV Planner
project_ideas.poc: Build a scheduler/paging simulator with separate KV-cache growth for full-attention layers and fixed-size recurrent state for linear layers, then validate predictions against measured TPOT and memory across context lengths.
project_ideas.video_title: How We Scaled Kimi K2.5 | Zhilin Yang's full GTC 2026 Keynote

project_ideas.based_on: is any mechanism-transfer from this source defensible, or is the correct output an explicit no-relevance verdict?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an explicit low-evidence / no-relevance verdict class to pass-1 reduces the fabricated-insight rate on off-domain sources without reducing valid-insight recall on matched in-domain sources.
project_ideas.measurement: Fabricated-insight rate per source type and valid-insight recall on in-domain controls, compared across the two pipeline configurations.
project_ideas.name: Verdict-Gate
project_ideas.poc: Run the same pass-1 pipeline over a mixed corpus of on-domain and off-domain sources with and without a verdict class; have reviewers label each emitted insight as grounded or analogy-only.
project_ideas.video_title: From the Archives: Christopher Hitchens (Full Interview)

project_ideas.based_on: Build a provenance-coverage metric (fraction of output spans traceable to attributed sources) and test whether thresholding it catches cases human reviewers flag.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A provenance-coverage threshold computed at generation time flags artifacts that human reviewers independently judge as unacknowledged bulk extraction, with precision high enough to act as a release gate.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision and recall of thresholded gate decisions against human reviewer flags; provenance-coverage distribution for flagged versus unflagged artifacts.
project_ideas.name: Coverage-Gate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument generation to record attributed source spans per output, compute a coverage ratio, threshold it, and compare gate decisions against reviewer labels on the same artifact set.
project_ideas.video_title: From the Archives: Christopher Hitchens (Full Interview)

project_ideas.based_on: Benchmark judge models on identical evidence under multiple mutually exclusive framings and measure score divergence as a frame-loyalty metric.
