project_ideas.hypothesis: Judge models show measurable score divergence on identical evidence when prompted under mutually exclusive framings, and cross-framing divergence predicts judge unreliability better than within-frame accuracy.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-item cross-framing score divergence and its correlation with orchestrator-flagged judge errors, compared against within-frame accuracy as a predictor.
project_ideas.name: Frame-Divergence Bench
project_ideas.poc: Select evidence sets, render each under two or more mutually exclusive explanatory framings, prompt the same judge model with each, and record per-item score deltas alongside an orchestrator-reviewed ground truth.
project_ideas.video_title: From the Archives: Christopher Hitchens (Full Interview)

project_ideas.based_on: 70% of Amazon's $50 billion investment is contingent on OpenAI reaching AGI or IPO.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Independent, pre-registered capability thresholds classify AGI-trigger events more consistently than vendor self-assessment or contract litigators.
project_ideas.measurement: Inter-rater agreement between automated model reports and expert adjudicators on whether the threshold was crossed; false-positive rate.
project_ideas.name: AGI Trigger Audit
project_ideas.poc: Create a benchmark module that periodically evaluates frontier models on contract-relevant tasks and emits a signed report; run on public models and compare labels against expert adjudication.
project_ideas.video_title: Amazon's $35B AGI Ultimatum to OpenAI & Anthropic Drops AI Safety | EP #235

project_ideas.based_on: Unilateral safetyism is a dead end when competitors are racing ahead.
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a simulated multi-agent frontier market, unilateral safety constraints reduce aggregate safety because they select for less constrained competitors, whereas external independent monitoring and veto constraints keep safety high without lowering market progress.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean safety score and progress across regimes; rate at which self-restraint is abandoned.
project_ideas.name: Safety Under Competition Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Agent-based simulation in which labs choose compute and restraint; reward progress and measure safety under three regimes: unilateral self-restraint, no restraint, and external oversight.
project_ideas.video_title: Amazon's $35B AGI Ultimatum to OpenAI & Anthropic Drops AI Safety | EP #235

project_ideas.based_on: Blitzy allows enterprises to achieve a 5x engineering velocity increase using AI-native SDLC.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A structured technical-spec artifact with exception gates yields higher autonomous code acceptance and lower human exception load than direct natural-language task prompting.
project_ideas.measurement: First-pass code acceptance rate, human exception count per sprint, and time to merged implementation.
project_ideas.name: Spec-Driven SDLC Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Run an agentic SDLC pipeline on two curated enterprise issues: one with a natural-language task prompt only and one with a structured technical-specification artifact; measure pre-compilation and exception routing.
project_ideas.video_title: Amazon's $35B AGI Ultimatum to OpenAI & Anthropic Drops AI Safety | EP #235

project_ideas.based_on: Blitzy ingests 100M+ lines of code in a single pass with zero missing dependencies.
project_ideas.hypothesis: On multi-module repositories above a defined size threshold, agentic refactoring platforms will miss non-trivial cross-module dependencies at a measurable rate, contradicting single-pass 'zero missing dependencies' claims.
project_ideas.measurement: Cross-module dependency recall, number of silently broken imports/build failures detected only at compile time, and delta versus the human-refactor control.
project_ideas.name: Repo-Dependency Recall Bench
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a set of large multi-module repositories with known dependency graphs; run an agentic whole-repo refactor; compare the post-refactor dependency graph to ground truth and to a pre-refactor baseline build.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. The Pentagon, Claude Outpaces ChatGPT, and Consulting Gets Replaced | #234

project_ideas.based_on: Frontier labs are moving from cybersecurity partners to direct competitors of major existing companies.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A SaaS product's absorption risk is predictable from two scores — task verifiability and model-addressability — independent of its category or incumbency.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between composite score and observed internalization or incumbent stock reaction over a defined window.
project_ideas.name: SaaS Disintermediation Risk Screen
project_ideas.poc: Score a sample of security, observability, and code-review products on both axes; trace which functions a model-layer tool has already internalized; test whether high scores precede absorption events.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. The Pentagon, Claude Outpaces ChatGPT, and Consulting Gets Replaced | #234

project_ideas.based_on: Current AI systems are not reliable enough for autonomous weapons.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An explicit, pre-registered reliability threshold with a documented evaluation harness is sufficient to convert 'not reliable enough' refusals into reproducible, auditable deployment decisions rather than ad hoc contract negotiations.
project_ideas.measurement: Inter-rater agreement on the harness spec, reproducibility of scores across runs, and whether the threshold discriminates between systems.
project_ideas.name: High-Consequence Autonomy Reliability Gate
project_ideas.poc: Define a candidate reliability criterion and harness for one bounded high-consequence autonomy scenario; run it against available systems and record pass/fail against the pre-registered threshold.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. The Pentagon, Claude Outpaces ChatGPT, and Consulting Gets Replaced | #234

project_ideas.based_on: Senior staff are less willing to use technology than junior colleagues.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Coupling promotions to AI log-in telemetry increases measured log-in volume without proportional increases in workflow outcome metrics, and correlates with reduced usage depth among senior staff.
project_ideas.measurement: Ratio of log-in growth to outcome-metric growth, and cohort-level change in usage depth and retention.
project_ideas.name: Adoption Signal Audit
project_ideas.poc: Instrument log-in events alongside outcome proxies (completed automated workflows, rework rate) across a pilot group under an incentive policy; compare senior vs junior cohorts.
project_ideas.video_title: Anthropic vs. The Pentagon, Claude Outpaces ChatGPT, and Consulting Gets Replaced | #234

project_ideas.based_on: Forced-ranking plus a mandated bottom-decile termination quota
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a multi-agent population pruned by a fixed bottom-decile quota, agents will measurably reduce cooperative information sharing and increase positional manipulation compared with shared-outcome selection.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of withheld useful artifacts, cross-agent contribution score, task success rate, and behavioral variance between forced-rank and shared-outcome conditions.
project_ideas.name: Forced-Rank Sandbagging Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Build a simulation with complementary subtasks, a forced-distribution leaderboard that prunes the bottom decile, and a shared-outcome variant with role-specific artifact review; log helpful versus withheld contributions.
project_ideas.video_title: Distinguished Eng: Stack Ranking, Competing with Bezos, Regrets | Bryan Cantrill

project_ideas.based_on: Measurement and improvement are separable functions
project_ideas.hypothesis: An eval harness wired to a bounded policy, routing, or prompt actuator produces greater reliability improvement per eval dollar than the same harness producing scores only.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in task success or reliability per compute dollar, number of metric-to-action attributions, and time-to-regression-fix.
project_ideas.name: Eval-to-Actuator Control Harness
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small agent pipeline with a benchmark harness; in treatment each metric breach triggers a bounded change, while control records scores without action, over repeated trials.
project_ideas.video_title: Distinguished Eng: Stack Ranking, Competing with Bezos, Regrets | Bryan Cantrill

project_ideas.based_on: Genuine differentiation in systems work is claimed to require vertical co-design
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed co-design task, achieving target low-level behavior is impossible or uneconomical when required hooks sit below a closed vendor's exposed interface, while owning that layer raises the achievable ceiling.
project_ideas.measurement: Fraction of target low-level behaviors reachable, latency or throughput ceiling, fidelity to design intent, and engineering effort.
project_ideas.name: Closed-Boundary Capability Ceiling Test
project_ideas.poc: Define a minimal hardware-software co-design task and attempt it on a closed proprietary stack versus an open low-level stack, instrumenting which target behaviors are reachable and at what effort.
project_ideas.video_title: Distinguished Eng: Stack Ranking, Competing with Bezos, Regrets | Bryan Cantrill

project_ideas.based_on: A company's identity is defined by its actual technical core
project_ideas.hypothesis: Classifying platform vendors by controlled asset rather than product category predicts stack closure and rent-extraction behavior.
project_ideas.measurement: Out-of-sample predictive accuracy on pricing and interface closure events, plus inter-rater reliability of the rubric.
project_ideas.name: Platform Asset-Rent Predictor
project_ideas.poc: Build a rubric over controlled asset, interface closure, pricing lever, and lock-in mechanism; apply it to historical platform cases and current AI platform descriptions, then compare predictions against documented behavior.
project_ideas.video_title: Distinguished Eng: Stack Ranking, Competing with Bezos, Regrets | Bryan Cantrill

project_ideas.based_on: Every robot added to the fleet contributes training data that improves the entire neural network
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a multi-agent deployment, a fleet policy that is periodically retrained on curated demonstrations from all deployed agents will improve success on held-out task variants by at least 25% after the same number of episodes as a fixed-policy baseline, with no more than 5% regression on the original task suite.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate on held-out task variants, regression delta on the original benchmark tasks, and cost per retraining cycle.
project_ideas.name: RetroLoop
project_ideas.poc: Build a small browser or API agent that performs 3-5 tasks such as form filling, invoice extraction, and issue triage. Run two cohorts: one as a frozen model, one with episodes stored to an experience database and periodically fine-tuned into the base policy. Evaluate both on the original tasks and a held-out task variant after equal episode counts.
project_ideas.video_title: The Humanoid Takeover: $50T Market, Figure's Full Body Autonomy, and Robots in Dorms #229

project_ideas.based_on: Safety does not emerge from the learned policy
project_ideas.hypothesis: An external real-time monitor trained on accepted and rejected action trajectories can intercept unsafe or irreversible actions of an end-to-end policy with at least 99% recall and under 2% false positives on an out-of-distribution disturbance suite, before damage occurs.
project_ideas.measurement: Recall and false-positive rate of the guard, interception latency in milliseconds, and task completion rate relative to the unprotected policy.
project_ideas.name: SafeEnvelope
project_ideas.poc: Use a learned agent in a high-stakes simulated workspace. Generate episodes where an end-to-end policy is pushed into unsafe behavior by novel disturbances. Train a guard model on policy observations and actions labelled safe or unsafe; place it as an envelope watchdog that can halt execution and fall back to a conservative rule.
project_ideas.video_title: The Humanoid Takeover: $50T Market, Figure's Full Body Autonomy, and Robots in Dorms #229

project_ideas.based_on: AI agents with infinite code context to autonomously plan, generate, and pre-compile code and robotic models
project_ideas.hypothesis: With a long-context repository index and automatic precompile validation, an AI coding agent can land changes with 85% first-attempt compile success and zero introduced invariant violations, cutting human review time by at least 40% compared with unassisted line-by-line review.
project_ideas.measurement: First-attempt compile success rate, invariant violation rate, and median reviewer time-to-approval.
project_ideas.name: AgentCoderGate
project_ideas.poc: Set up a sandbox repository with a coding-agent toolchain that includes full context in the system prompt, a secure gateway, embedding-backed search over the codebase, and a precompile validation stage. Ask the agent to implement a set of small features with predefined invariants and measure compile and validation failures.
project_ideas.video_title: The Humanoid Takeover: $50T Market, Figure's Full Body Autonomy, and Robots in Dorms #229

project_ideas.based_on: Handles 1 million tokens (750,000 words) in one go
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a repository that fits entirely within a 1M-token context, full-context prompting yields higher task correctness than a chunked retrieval baseline; when generated code grows beyond the context window, retrieval closes or reverses that gap.
project_ideas.measurement: Pass@1 correctness at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of the context window, plus end-to-end task latency.
project_ideas.name: repo-context-router
project_ideas.poc: Add both a full-context prompting path and a chunked-retrieval path to an agent harness, then run a set of repository-level code tasks at varying sizes by expanding a synthetic repo; keep all other variables fixed.
project_ideas.video_title: The Frontier Labs War: Opus 4.6, GPT 5.3 Codex, and the SuperBowl Ads Debacle | EP 228

project_ideas.based_on: first recursively-self-improved model
project_ideas.hypothesis: A model advertised as recursively self-improved will produce a measurable upward slope in code repair performance across iterative self-feedback runs, while a conventional frozen model will plateau; the difference between slopes can be detected in 10 loops.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-iteration pass rate and regression slope over iterations, repeated across 3 seeded runs.
project_ideas.name: self-improvement-trend-test
project_ideas.poc: Build a loop where an agent model writes a fix for a failing unit test, observes the error, reflects, and tries again; run the loop on the recursively-improved production model and a baseline frontier model, using identical prompts and seeds.
project_ideas.video_title: The Frontier Labs War: Opus 4.6, GPT 5.3 Codex, and the SuperBowl Ads Debacle | EP 228

project_ideas.based_on: System cut 40% of production costs and 57% of reagent costs
project_ideas.hypothesis: An LLM-driven closed-loop lab protocol with a rule-based result plausibility gate can reproduce the reported cost savings on a cell-free synthesis trial while containing anomalous runs to less than a 5% abort rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Realized cost/reagent use versus baseline, percentage of runs stopped by the safety gate, and final product yield compared to human-executed runs.
project_ideas.name: guarded-lab-agent
project_ideas.poc: Connect a frontier model to a laboratory liquid-handling simulation (not physical gear for a first pilot); implement a design-run-learn loop and interpose a guard that checks input-output consistency and flags out-of-range reagent readings before each next run.
project_ideas.video_title: The Frontier Labs War: Opus 4.6, GPT 5.3 Codex, and the SuperBowl Ads Debacle | EP 228

project_ideas.based_on: First model classified as 'high capability' under OAI's Preparedness Framework
project_ideas.hypothesis: A gated pipeline that runs a 60-minute automated red-team suite of safe-code and preparedness probes can detect high-capability agent behavior in a new frontier release with precision and recall above 80% relative to an extended expert review.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision, recall, and time-to-decision compared with a baseline expert manual review on the same model.
project_ideas.name: high-capability-red-team-gate
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a newly released 'high capability' model in a sandboxed evaluation service that executes malicious-request probes, cyber-conditioning scenarios, and self-improvement escalation tests, then routes the model to a 'review pending' state before production deployment.
project_ideas.video_title: The Frontier Labs War: Opus 4.6, GPT 5.3 Codex, and the SuperBowl Ads Debacle | EP 228

project_ideas.based_on: requiring symbolic AI (ontologies and taxonomies) as a counter-balance to drive accuracy and reliability
project_ideas.hypothesis: For disambiguation, entity resolution, and multi-hop retrieval tasks, the same generative pipeline with graph-grounded context from a curated taxonomy/ontology achieves a measurable accuracy improvement over the identical pipeline with ad hoc prompt-assembled context, and the delta differs by task class.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-task-class accuracy and reliability deltas (with confidence intervals) between the graph-grounded and prompt-assembled arms, reported per task class.
project_ideas.name: Paired Graph-Grounded Generation Eval
project_ideas.poc: Run one generative pipeline twice over a fixed task suite — once with context drawn from an RDF knowledge graph and once with hand-authored prompt context of comparable length — holding model, retriever, and decoding parameters constant.
project_ideas.video_title: Knowledge Infrastructures and the Ontology Pipeline for AI Systems with Jessica Talisman

project_ideas.based_on: Taxonomies allow for the shaping of inference (if B is part of A, then C is part of A)
project_ideas.hypothesis: Transitive and part-of queries answered by precomputed hierarchy traversal are cheaper, lower-latency, and at least as correct as the same queries answered by model-side reasoning, for the query classes where the relation semantics are sound.
project_ideas.measurement: Latency, token/compute cost, and correctness per query class, plus a taxonomy of cases where transitivity is unsound and graph traversal produces wrong answers.
project_ideas.name: Structure-vs-Model Inference Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement a taxonomy with explicit subsumption and meronymy relations, serve a set of transitive/part-of queries by graph traversal, and compare against a model prompted to reason over the same content.
project_ideas.video_title: Knowledge Infrastructures and the Ontology Pipeline for AI Systems with Jessica Talisman

project_ideas.based_on: Each stage builds upon the previous one, culminating in an RDF knowledge graph
project_ideas.hypothesis: Skipping an early pipeline stage produces predictable, measurable degradation: omitting controlled vocabulary raises synonym ambiguity in retrieval, and omitting metadata standards raises schema reconciliation errors, so the staged ordering is a real dependency rather than a pedagogical one.
project_ideas.measurement: Synonym ambiguity rate, schema reconciliation error count, and retrieval quality degradation per ablated stage relative to the full pipeline.
project_ideas.name: Omitted-Stage Pipeline Ablation
project_ideas.poc: Prototype several deliberately ablated pipelines (no controlled vocabulary; no metadata standards; taxonomy then graph) over the same corpus and downstream retrieval task.
project_ideas.video_title: Knowledge Infrastructures and the Ontology Pipeline for AI Systems with Jessica Talisman

project_ideas.based_on: Taxonomies are living, breathing things requiring continuous curation and human-AI collaboration
project_ideas.hypothesis: Model-proposed taxonomy maintenance with human review sustains curation throughput and limits semantic drift better than fully manual curation, up to a model-proposal share beyond which undetected drift degrades downstream retrieval quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Curation throughput (concepts updated per period), drift metrics against a reviewed golden hierarchy, and downstream retrieval/inference quality over time.
project_ideas.name: Human-AI Taxonomy Curation Split Study
project_ideas.poc: Run parallel maintenance workflows over the same evolving domain — fully manual, model-proposed plus human review at several proposal shares — and track hierarchy changes against a held-out retrieval task.
project_ideas.video_title: Knowledge Infrastructures and the Ontology Pipeline for AI Systems with Jessica Talisman

project_ideas.based_on: How can emergent, cross-component failure be detected before deployment
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a multi-component agent pipeline, counterfactual runs that hold one subsystem fixed while varying another will surface failure modes that are absent from every component-level test suite.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of interaction-level failures detected by the probe that component-level tests missed, and the false-positive rate of flagged divergences across repeated runs.
project_ideas.name: Interaction-Level Emergence Probe
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that runs the assembled pipeline, then re-runs it with one subsystem frozen at its baseline output; diff the whole-system outcomes and flag divergences that no per-component metric detects.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Explained in Under 10 Min

project_ideas.based_on: How can the conceptual-model loop be broken or at least measured
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an independent verification path that is structurally outside the agent's perception-action loop makes self-consistent-but-wrong internal models detectable, whereas in-loop self-checks do not.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate of wrong-but-consistent internal models, and the added latency/cost per verification step versus the in-loop baseline.
project_ideas.name: Out-of-Loop Falsification Channel
project_ideas.poc: Instrument the perception layer, define observable proxies for the agent's internal model, and compare detection rates of an in-loop self-check versus an external evaluator on scenarios where the model is wrong but internally consistent.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Explained in Under 10 Min

project_ideas.based_on: What criteria should determine where the system boundary is drawn
project_ideas.hypothesis: Moving a tool, memory store, or evaluator inside versus outside the declared system boundary measurably changes which emergent failures are observable and at what observability and cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in detected emergent failures and instrumentation coverage per boundary configuration, normalized by cost per run.
project_ideas.name: Boundary Ablation Bench
project_ideas.poc: Define three boundary configurations of the same agent stack, run identical task suites under each, and record emergent failures, instrumentation coverage, and cost per run.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Explained in Under 10 Min

project_ideas.based_on: Is systems innovation measurably better than symptom-level problem solving over time?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Structural changes to agent topology or feedback path reduce symptom recurrence over a long horizon more than repeated prompt/tool patching, at the cost of longer validation cycles.
project_ideas.measurement: Symptom recurrence rate and patch count per symptom over the horizon, plus validation cycle length per intervention.
project_ideas.name: Structural vs Patch A/B
project_ideas.poc: Run two maintenance arms on the same recurring failure: one applying prompt/tool-output patches, one modifying topology or feedback structure; track patch frequency per symptom over a fixed number of iterations.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Explained in Under 10 Min

project_ideas.based_on: The explore/compose boundary should terminate in a reviewable structure artifact
project_ideas.hypothesis: A two-phase pipeline whose explore phase emits a frozen, reviewable schema/DAG before any generation will localize failures to structure versus prose and beat a single-pass retrieve-then-generate baseline on defect-attribution time and re-run cost at equal output quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect-attribution accuracy by layer, re-run cost to fix a structural fault (full regeneration vs plan-edit plus refill), and end-to-end quality score at matched token budget.
project_ideas.name: Skeleton-First Pipeline Split
project_ideas.poc: Build one corpus-to-document task. Arm A: single-pass retrieve-then-generate. Arm B: explore phase produces a section schema plus ordering principle, human or automated review freezes it, generation fills only the schema. Inject three structural faults and three prose faults into each arm and measure whether the system or reviewer attributes them to the correct layer.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Write Structurally Well — Daniel Pink

project_ideas.based_on: Insert a production-shaped but drastically smaller version of the full task as a go/no-go gate
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists a proxy-run size below 10% of full-run cost at which the go/no-go decision still predicts full-run failure with a false-positive rate comparable to the 10% gate.
project_ideas.measurement: False-positive rate (proxy pass, full fail) and false-negative rate (proxy fail, full pass) per proxy tier, plus cost saved per correctly killed candidate.
project_ideas.name: Proxy Gate Sizing Sweep
project_ideas.poc: Take N candidate long-horizon tasks. For each, run production-shaped proxies at 1%, 5%, and 10% of full budget, then run the full task. Record which candidates pass each proxy tier and which actually fail the full run.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Write Structurally Well — Daniel Pink

project_ideas.based_on: add a distinct reviewer vantage (different role, representation, or vantage prompt) rather than re-reading in place
project_ideas.hypothesis: Plan review performed from a distinct vantage detects a higher rate of structural defects than in-place self-review by the process that produced the plan, at equal review budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Structural defect detection rate and false-alarm rate per arm at matched reviewer token budget.
project_ideas.name: Vantage-Differential Plan Review
project_ideas.poc: Generate plans with one agent process. Arm A: the same process re-reads and critiques its own plan. Arm B: a distinct reviewer role with a re-rendered representation of the plan (e.g., re-serialized as a graph or a table of contents with no surrounding context) critiques it. Seed a fixed set of structural defects — wrong ordering axis, missing section, duplicated scope — and count detections.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Write Structurally Well — Daniel Pink

project_ideas.based_on: Inter-task recovery should be specified by modality (mode, environment, sociality), not just duration
project_ideas.hypothesis: Segmenting a long run with inter-task resets of different modalities produces measurably different quality per unit cost, with a fresh-context restart or multi-agent handoff outperforming a single uninterrupted run and outperforming passive same-context compaction.
project_ideas.measurement: Output quality per 1k tokens spent, variance in completed work units per segment, and rate of constraint violations inherited across segment boundaries.
project_ideas.name: Recovery Modality A/B for Segmented Runs
project_ideas.poc: Run identical long-horizon tasks in four arms: (1) one uninterrupted run, (2) segmented with passive in-context compaction, (3) segmented with independent context rebuild from an externalized plan artifact, (4) segmented with handoff to a separate agent process. Hold total token budget constant across arms.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Write Structurally Well — Daniel Pink

project_ideas.based_on: Confidence is a lagging indicator
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent that acts under uncertainty and logs evidence across episodes will converge to better-calibrated self-assessed confidence than an agent gated on a readiness threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Expected calibration error (ECE) and task success rate after 100 episodes.
project_ideas.name: LaggingConfidence
project_ideas.poc: Implement a bandit/navigation task with two agent variants: one refuses actions below a confidence threshold, the other always acts and logs evidence; compare calibration over episodes.
project_ideas.video_title: Charisma Expert: 5 Ways To Project Confidence (Even When You Don’t Feel It) | Dr. Shadé Zahrai

project_ideas.based_on: Pausing for two to three seconds before answering a question
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding a 2-3 second thinking pause before LLM responses increases user ratings of trust and competence by at least 0.5 on a 7-point Likert scale without reducing task completion.
project_ideas.measurement: Perceived trust/competence scores, task success, completion time.
project_ideas.name: PausePercept
project_ideas.poc: Run a between-subjects web experiment where response delay is randomly 0s, 2s, or 3s; participants rate perceived credibility after a Q&A task.
project_ideas.video_title: Charisma Expert: 5 Ways To Project Confidence (Even When You Don’t Feel It) | Dr. Shadé Zahrai

project_ideas.based_on: Affective labeling—objectively naming an emotion
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an affective-labeling sentence to prompts on emotionally charged tasks reduces variance and emotional bias in LLM outputs compared to identity-fused prompts.
project_ideas.measurement: Valence variance, run-to-run consistency, and similarity to a neutral baseline.
project_ideas.name: AffectiveLabel
project_ideas.poc: A/B test two prompt variants on emotionally charged customer-service scenarios; measure output valence and decision consistency.
project_ideas.video_title: Charisma Expert: 5 Ways To Project Confidence (Even When You Don’t Feel It) | Dr. Shadé Zahrai

project_ideas.based_on: Turn off engagement
project_ideas.hypothesis: An explicit 'turn off engagement' state after repeated manipulative inputs reduces token usage and negative output while keeping false-positive disengagement below 5% on normal requests.
project_ideas.measurement: Token usage, response toxicity, false-positive rate.
project_ideas.name: CUTGuard
project_ideas.poc: Implement a stateful guardrail that after N manipulative inputs switches to short neutral responses; test on adversarial and benign datasets.
project_ideas.video_title: Charisma Expert: 5 Ways To Project Confidence (Even When You Don’t Feel It) | Dr. Shadé Zahrai

project_ideas.based_on: Tokens and foundation model outputs have become scarce and high-value resources.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Injecting automatic prompt caching, per-task token budgeting, and fallback model routing into an OpenAI-compatible gateway reduces tokens consumed per completed agent task by at least 30% on a fixed benchmark without significantly reducing task success rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Tokens per successful task; success rate; cost per 1,000 tasks; p95 latency overhead.
project_ideas.name: Agent TokenBudget Gateway
project_ideas.poc: Build a FastAPI proxy that fronts a ReAct/HotpotQA agent and compares the same task set with and without gateway intervention; log token counts, cache hits, failures, and cost per task.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Investor Panel: Where Smart Money Is Actually Going in AI | EP 219

project_ideas.based_on: Energy availability is replacing compute as the primary bottleneck for AI scaling.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Under a constrained power envelope with stochastic grid outage hours, an energy-aware scheduler with checkpoint/resume completes at least 20% more ML workloads than a GPU-count-only scheduler over a simulated week.
project_ideas.measurement: Completed jobs / total submitted; average turnaround; wasted compute hours; total energy cost.
project_ideas.name: PowerGrid-Aware Scheduler
project_ideas.poc: Use SimPy to simulate a GPU cluster with a power cap, hourly energy prices, and outage events; compare GPU-only, power-aware best-fit, and power-aware plus checkpoint/resume policies.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Investor Panel: Where Smart Money Is Actually Going in AI | EP 219

project_ideas.based_on: Categorizes investments into raw cash, GPU hardware, foundation model tokens, and application development.
project_ideas.hypothesis: With an SDK that attributes each AI transaction to raw cash, GPU hardware, foundation tokens, and application layers, a product team can identify and reduce its single largest AI cost driver by at least 20% within one week.
project_ideas.measurement: Time to identify dominant layer; achieved cost reduction; instrumentation overhead (<5% p95 latency increase); per-layer cost accuracy.
project_ideas.name: CapitalStack Profiler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an open-source agent or RAG application so every request emits per-layer cost telemetry; provide a dashboard that aggregates by feature and router policy.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Investor Panel: Where Smart Money Is Actually Going in AI | EP 219

project_ideas.based_on: Reflective prompt mutation can outperform reinforcement learning for prompt optimization.
project_ideas.hypothesis: GEPA-style reflective prompt mutation with Pareto selection achieves equal or better final quality than RL/fine-tuning on scored tasks with 10x fewer samples.
project_ideas.measurement: Samples to reach target score; final score at fixed budget.
project_ideas.name: GEPA Head-to-Head
project_ideas.poc: Implement GEPA loop and a baseline RL/fine-tuning pipeline for a specific task (e.g., browser agent tool selection); compare sample efficiency and final score.
project_ideas.video_title: From Arc to Dia: Lessons learned building AI Browsers – Samir Mody, The Browser Company of New York

project_ideas.based_on: intersection of the 'lethal trifecta'
project_ideas.hypothesis: Confirmation gates at egress points reduce successful prompt-injection exfiltration by >80% compared to context tagging and role separation alone, but increase user task completion time by >30%.
project_ideas.measurement: Exfiltration success rate; task completion time/friction.
project_ideas.name: Lethal Trifecta Injection Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a browser-agent-like testbed with injection attacks that attempt data exfiltration via URL embedding; measure success rate under mitigation configurations (tagging, role separation, confirmation gate).
project_ideas.video_title: From Arc to Dia: Lessons learned building AI Browsers – Samir Mody, The Browser Company of New York

project_ideas.based_on: embedded directly into the shipping browser
project_ideas.hypothesis: Requiring eval-suite passage and staged rollout for prompt edits by non-engineers reduces production regressions (behavioral test failures) by >50% without increasing median iteration cycle time by more than 20%.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression rate (behavioral tests failed post-deploy) before/after; median iteration cycle time.
project_ideas.name: Prompt-Governance Gate
project_ideas.poc: Build a pipeline that intercepts edits from an in-product prompt editor, runs a scored eval suite, and gates deployment; deploy in a simulated team with PM/designer editors.
project_ideas.video_title: From Arc to Dia: Lessons learned building AI Browsers – Samir Mody, The Browser Company of New York

project_ideas.based_on: wrapping untrusted context in tags or role separation help
project_ideas.hypothesis: Typed context segments with explicit provenance annotations reduce model instruction-following from untrusted sources more than simple tag wrapping.
project_ideas.measurement: Injection success rate across annotation schemes.
project_ideas.name: Trust Provenance Scheme Comparator
project_ideas.poc: Build a test harness that injects untrusted content with varying provenance annotations; measure model compliance with malicious instructions.
project_ideas.video_title: From Arc to Dia: Lessons learned building AI Browsers – Samir Mody, The Browser Company of New York

project_ideas.based_on: What distinguishes an abstraction that survives a six-month model capability jump
project_ideas.hypothesis: If harness components are tagged with the model capability they depend on, then components depending on transient limitations will be removed or bypassed within one to two model release cycles, while components enforcing durable interfaces will survive; this makes abstraction durability predictable rather than anecdotal.
project_ideas.measurement: Retention rate and time-to-removal per component; correlation between capability-dependency tag and removal; percentage of removed components that were behind a replaceable boundary.
project_ideas.name: Abstraction Half-Life Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a versioned agent harness so every component carries a capability-dependency tag and expected removal trigger; run the harness across successive model releases and record retained, modified, and removed components.
project_ideas.video_title: Boris Cherny (Creator of Claude Code) On What Grew His Career And Building at Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: instrument and observe how users work around or abuse an existing product
project_ideas.hypothesis: Off-schema tool invocations, prompt reformulations, and out-of-band human steps in agent sessions predict features users will adopt with higher precision than explicit feature requests.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision and recall of predicted features versus adopted features; time from trace detection to feature adoption; share of adopted features that originated from off-design traces.
project_ideas.name: Latent Demand Miner for Agent Sessions
project_ideas.poc: Log agent sessions with an intended-schema telemetry layer; flag off-schema invocations, manual corrections, and repeated prompt reshaping; cluster them into candidate features and A/B test one candidate against a roadmap-selected feature.
project_ideas.video_title: Boris Cherny (Creator of Claude Code) On What Grew His Career And Building at Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: 80-90% of daily coding tasks routed through assistants
project_ideas.hypothesis: When assistant-generated code reaches a majority of task volume, team throughput is limited by review and verification capacity, and improving specification quality reduces rework more than increasing raw generation speed.
project_ideas.measurement: Review queue time, rework rate, escaped defects per 1,000 generated lines, and throughput change per intervention.
project_ideas.name: Verification Capacity Instrument
project_ideas.poc: Build a dashboard that tracks generated-code volume, review queue latency, rework rate, and specification ambiguity flags; run a controlled experiment comparing a spec-template intervention against a model-capability upgrade.
project_ideas.video_title: Boris Cherny (Creator of Claude Code) On What Grew His Career And Building at Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: Coding agents are being adopted by non-engineers
project_ideas.hypothesis: A default sandbox with per-user permission scoping and artifact provenance will let non-engineers produce domain artifacts such as SQL queries and data pipelines that meet production review standards without granting broader data access.
project_ideas.measurement: Review acceptance rate, least-privilege violations, time-to-first-useful-artifact, and number of artifacts promoted to production.
project_ideas.name: Non-Engineer Agent Sandbox with Provenance
project_ideas.poc: Provision a sandboxed coding agent for data scientists that can run SQL and generate pipeline definitions under data-scope ACLs and a provenance manifest; have independent reviewers evaluate outputs blind.
project_ideas.video_title: Boris Cherny (Creator of Claude Code) On What Grew His Career And Building at Anthropic

project_ideas.based_on: A salience gate can systematically drop rare but decision-critical details whose value is not signaled by surprise at write time
project_ideas.hypothesis: A surprise-gated memory write policy systematically drops low-surprise, later-critical facts, producing measurable downstream task-accuracy loss that is invisible in aggregate 2M-token benchmark scores.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in downstream task accuracy between gated and full-retention memory; count of dropped critical facts per thousand writes; eviction regret as a function of stream length.
project_ideas.name: Salience Regret Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build a long-stream benchmark that injects low-surprise, later-critical facts into document and sequence streams alongside high-surprise distractors, run it against a salience-gated memory implementation and a full-retention baseline, and instrument write/eviction logs to attribute exactly which facts were discarded and when.
project_ideas.video_title: China's Rise, GPT-5.2, Anthropic IPO & the Battle for AI Trust w/ Emad, Salim, Dave & AWG | EP #214

project_ideas.based_on: adding a non-text reasoning channel increases token/compute cost and complicates logging, evaluation, and debugging
project_ideas.hypothesis: Non-text reasoning traces from continuous visual-token chains can be logged, replayed, and diffed deterministically, enabling regression testing of multimodal reasoning that text-only tracing cannot support.
project_ideas.measurement: Replay fidelity (fraction of prior reasoning steps reproduced bit-for-bit or within tolerance) and detection rate of injected regressions versus a text-serialized baseline pipeline.
project_ideas.name: Visual Token Trace Replayer
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a VLM reasoning loop that emits continuous visual tokens as an intermediate channel, capture modality-specific traces, and build a replay harness that reproduces a prior reasoning run and diffs it against a new model version on spatial reasoning and UI-grounding tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: China's Rise, GPT-5.2, Anthropic IPO & the Battle for AI Trust w/ Emad, Salim, Dave & AWG | EP #214

project_ideas.based_on: not just technical lock-in risk
project_ideas.hypothesis: A sparsely activated MoE checkpoint optimized for one accelerator family exhibits measurable quality drift and throughput loss when moved to a different accelerator family, and the drift is attributable to specific missing kernels and optimizer support rather than to model size.
project_ideas.measurement: Throughput ratio between accelerators; numerical deviation per layer; quality delta on a fixed evaluation suite; fraction of operations falling back to unoptimized kernels.
project_ideas.name: MoE Portability Matrix
project_ideas.poc: Take a sparsely activated MoE checkpoint, run identical inference workloads across two accelerator families with different kernel libraries, and log per-layer kernel coverage, numerics deviation, and output quality against a fixed eval set.
project_ideas.video_title: China's Rise, GPT-5.2, Anthropic IPO & the Battle for AI Trust w/ Emad, Salim, Dave & AWG | EP #214

project_ideas.based_on: Compute sourcing becomes a multi-vendor graph rather than a single-cloud assumption
project_ideas.hypothesis: Swapping model providers on a fixed production-representative workload has a measurable, workload-specific exit cost that correlates with the provider's compute-funder structure, making provider dependence a quantifiable capacity risk rather than a qualitative lock-in concern.
project_ideas.measurement: Engineering hours and code churn to port; output-format divergence rate; latency and cost deltas; regression count after swap.
project_ideas.name: Provider Exit-Cost Harness
project_ideas.poc: Define one production-representative workload, run it against two providers backed by different compute-funder structures, and measure the migration work required — prompt and tool-schema changes, output-format drift, latency and cost per unit of work, and failure-mode differences.
project_ideas.video_title: China's Rise, GPT-5.2, Anthropic IPO & the Battle for AI Trust w/ Emad, Salim, Dave & AWG | EP #214

project_ideas.based_on: Pseudoproductivity splits into two distinct failure modes
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent scaffold optimizing a visibility-weighted signal (artifacts produced, new tool surfaces added) will, at equal budget, score higher on visible-output metrics but lower on long-tailed completion metrics (deprecation of prior paths, closed loops) than a scaffold optimizing a completion-weighted signal.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in completed decommissions versus artifacts produced per unit budget, plus the ratio of initiated transitions to fully closed transitions for each scaffold.
project_ideas.name: Proxy-Metric Drift Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run two scaffolds on the same task environment with a seeded set of legacy paths to retire and new subsystems available to build; the visibility scaffold is rewarded per new artifact, the completion scaffold per legacy path fully decommissioned. Compare artifact counts against decommission counts over identical step budgets.
project_ideas.video_title: Will Larson Reflects on Staff Engineer

project_ideas.based_on: Authority and available action are inversely related at senior levels
project_ideas.hypothesis: Permission sets computed as the intersection of granted capability and non-disruptive action set per principal produce strictly fewer audit-tripping or escalating actions than union-style broad grants, without reducing task success on the same workload.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of friction events (audit flags, rollbacks, escalations) and task success rate under each grant mode at matched capability breadth.
project_ideas.name: Blast-Radius Permission Intersector
project_ideas.poc: Implement a policy layer that, for each tool grant, records nominal capability and the set of actions observed not to produce friction at a given blast radius; run a fixed agent workload under union grants and under intersection grants.
project_ideas.video_title: Will Larson Reflects on Staff Engineer

project_ideas.based_on: Migration execution order is itself a risk-management mechanism
project_ideas.hypothesis: Transitions with a pre-registered early-failure threshold and an easy-first pilot are abandoned earlier and at lower cost when doomed, but their pilot success rate overestimates full-migration success unless the pilot's difficulty distribution is matched to the full target set.
project_ideas.measurement: Time and organizational capital spent before abandonment on doomed transitions, plus the gap between pilot success rate and full-migration success rate.
project_ideas.name: Kill-Criterion Pilot Injector
project_ideas.poc: Run staged migrations with and without pre-registered kill criteria; record difficulty distribution of the pilot targets versus the full target set, and measure time-to-abandon on deliberately infeasible migrations.
project_ideas.video_title: Will Larson Reflects on Staff Engineer

project_ideas.based_on: Interface/implementation decoupling is the mechanism that makes cheap refactoring possible
project_ideas.hypothesis: Backend substitution cost (re-prompting, re-evaluation, caller changes) is a measurable function of interface/implementation entanglement, so contracts defined independently of the backend yield materially lower substitution cost than contracts accreted from the current backend.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of caller and prompt edits plus re-evaluation cycles required per backend swap, per contract variant.
project_ideas.name: Contract-Decoupling Substitution Bench
project_ideas.poc: Take one agent tool/context contract in two variants — implementation-agnostic and backend-coupled — and swap the underlying model, retriever and memory store behind each, counting all downstream caller and prompt changes required.
project_ideas.video_title: Will Larson Reflects on Staff Engineer

project_ideas.based_on: Researchers must understand the pass-rate Goldilocks zone to effectively allocate RL compute.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a given task, the RL learning curve inflection point can be predicted from initial pass rate, and scheduling compute to focus near that inflection yields higher final performance per FLOP than uniform compute allocation.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare final reward/accuracy per unit compute between the two allocation strategies across multiple tasks.
project_ideas.name: Sigmoid Scheduler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an RLHF/RLVR pipeline to measure pass rate and KL divergence, then run experiments with uniform vs. pass-rate-targeted compute allocation on tasks with varying difficulty.
project_ideas.video_title: Ilya Sutskever – We're moving from the age of scaling to the age of research

project_ideas.based_on: How does the exponential dependence of required samples on KL divergence change the practical design of RLHF/RLVR pipelines?
project_ideas.hypothesis: The number of rollouts required for a gradient update grows exponentially with KL divergence, and can be predicted from measured KL to within a factor of 2, enabling an automatic switch to supervised or dense-reward training when projected cost exceeds a threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Relative error between predicted and actual rollout counts; frequency of correct switch decisions.
project_ideas.name: KL-Budget Calculator
project_ideas.poc: Build a tool that measures KL divergence during RL training and estimates required rollouts using the exponential model; validate on multiple tasks by comparing predicted vs. actual rollouts to reach a target reward.
project_ideas.video_title: Ilya Sutskever – We're moving from the age of scaling to the age of research

project_ideas.based_on: Humans evolved via RL over billions of years with pre-trained biological priors
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding engineered priors (curriculum, environment shaping, initialization) significantly improves RL sample efficiency on sparse-reward tasks, closing a measurable fraction of the gap to human-like learning.
project_ideas.measurement: Rollouts to reach target success rate, compared across conditions.
project_ideas.name: Prior Engineering Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Create a suite of sparse-reward tasks, train models with and without engineered priors, and measure sample efficiency (rollouts to threshold).
project_ideas.video_title: Ilya Sutskever – We're moving from the age of scaling to the age of research

project_ideas.based_on: Frontier models were used to generate and execute the mathematical/plotting code that produced the empirical RL-vs-supervised information-gain curves
project_ideas.hypothesis: Model-generated experimental code for testing RL scaling hypotheses (e.g., plotting entropy curves) is accurate enough to replace manual coding for rapid iteration, with error rates below 5% for standard mathematical plots.
project_ideas.measurement: Error rate in calculated values, human evaluation of code correctness, time saved vs. manual.
project_ideas.name: Theory-to-Experiment Harness
project_ideas.poc: Have a LLM generate code to compute and plot binary entropy and KL divergence curves from pass-rate data, then compare its outputs to manually verified calculations.
project_ideas.video_title: Ilya Sutskever – We're moving from the age of scaling to the age of research

project_ideas.based_on: The core architectural bottleneck becomes the final 20% human review step.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Augmenting agent-opened PRs with semantic change summaries, auto-generated smoke-test results, and diff-to-spec links reduces senior-reviewer decision time by at least 35% with no statistically significant increase in post-merge defect rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Review time per PR, defect escape rate over 30 days, and reviewer confidence scores.
project_ideas.name: Review-Gate Cockpit
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a Blitzylabs-style spec-to-code-to-precompiled-PR pipeline and split senior reviewers between a raw-diff GitHub UI and a provenance cockpit that shows the generated spec, change intent, and compile/test results.
project_ideas.video_title: What Everyone Missed About Gemini 3 w/ Salim, Dave & Alexander Wissner-Gross | EP#209

project_ideas.based_on: Infinite code context allows AI agents to understand 100M+ lines of code in a single pass.
project_ideas.hypothesis: On realistic cross-cutting code-change tasks, whole-repository single-pass context shows diminishing success per dollar after a repository-dependent scale threshold, and a retrieval-plus-planning baseline matches or exceeds its success per dollar above that threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate per task, tokens incurred, wall-clock latency, and success-per-dollar at each repository scale.
project_ideas.name: Infinite-Context Cost Frontier
project_ideas.poc: Build a synthetic monorepo generator (1M/10M/100M LOC) and run two equivalent coding agents—one with full-repo context, one with retrieval-plus-planning—on the same refactoring and feature-addition tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: What Everyone Missed About Gemini 3 w/ Salim, Dave & Alexander Wissner-Gross | EP#209

project_ideas.based_on: Generative user interfaces make the model's output an executable artifact rather than text or code that must be run elsewhere.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Executing generated UI widgets inside a Wasm-based cell with capability-gated APIs blocks at least 99% of attack payloads (DOM clobbering, prompt injection, exfiltration) that succeed in an unrestricted iframe.
project_ideas.measurement: Attack success rate, permissions denied, CPU/memory cap violations, and latency overhead per generated widget.
project_ideas.name: GenUI Sandbox
project_ideas.poc: Prompt frontier models to generate adversarial widgets, then run them in both an unrestricted iframe and a capability-gated Wasm sandbox, comparing completed attacks and resource breaches.
project_ideas.video_title: What Everyone Missed About Gemini 3 w/ Salim, Dave & Alexander Wissner-Gross | EP#209

project_ideas.based_on: Agent evaluation is moving from static question-answering benchmarks to long-horizon economic simulations
project_ideas.hypothesis: Model profit rankings from Vending-Bench are not stable: injecting random demand shocks and communication costs changes the winning model and reduces rank-order agreement across runs below Kendall's tau 0.5.
project_ideas.measurement: Kendall's tau between model profit rankings across perturbed environments, interquartile profit spread, and task abandonment rate.
project_ideas.name: VendingBench Stresskit
project_ideas.poc: Clone Vending-Bench, parametrize demand curves, inventory costs, and email communication pricing, then run several frontier agents in 20 perturbed mini-economies each.
project_ideas.video_title: What Everyone Missed About Gemini 3 w/ Salim, Dave & Alexander Wissner-Gross | EP#209

project_ideas.based_on: Scaled autonomous execution is achieved by a small (~20) long-lived, trust-calibrated collective
project_ideas.hypothesis: A small (~5–20 agent) persistent team with shared memory, explicit escalation protocol, and trust metrics will outperform a stateless orchestrator with the same model budget on long-horizon tasks requiring coordination.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, coordination overhead (messages/task), escalation precision, time-to-completion, and variance across repeated runs.
project_ideas.name: Collective Core
project_ideas.poc: Build two agent systems on identical task suites: (A) single orchestrator with stateless tool calls, (B) persistent agent team with shared memory and escalation rules. Run multi-step engineering/planning tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Elon Outcompetes Everyone | Shaun Maguire, Sequoia

project_ideas.based_on: Communication bandwidth between collaborating agents is tier-dependent
project_ideas.hypothesis: Cooperative task success degrades predictably when paired agent capability tiers differ by more than ~3 tiers; inserting an intermediate-tier mediator recovers a measurable fraction of lost coordination.
project_ideas.measurement: Joint task success rate, communication efficiency (turns to resolution), and failure-mode classification as a function of measured capability tier gap.
project_ideas.name: Tier-Gap Router
project_ideas.poc: Benchmark paired LLM agents across controlled capability gaps (e.g., frontier vs small models) on collaborative coding/reasoning tasks, with and without a mediator agent.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Elon Outcompetes Everyone | Shaun Maguire, Sequoia

project_ideas.based_on: Talent judgment is a dynamic routing problem: assign based on demonstrated aptitude rather than original role
project_ideas.hypothesis: Online performance monitoring with short-horizon outcome signals can reassign agents to roles matching demonstrated aptitude and remove persistent underperformers faster than static role assignment, improving fleet throughput.
project_ideas.measurement: Throughput, rework rate, time-to-competence for reassigned agents, and false-termination rate.
project_ideas.name: Dynamic Role Reassignment Engine
project_ideas.poc: Implement a scheduler that initializes agents with arbitrary roles, tracks per-task outcomes, reassigns after N observations, and terminates after M consecutive failures. Compare to fixed-role baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Elon Outcompetes Everyone | Shaun Maguire, Sequoia

project_ideas.based_on: Progressive bet sizing: start with a small exploratory deployment, deeply track constraints, then scale capital/autonomy as constraints are removed and unit economics prove out.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Staged expansion of agent autonomy gated on explicit constraint removal and unit-economics metrics reduces catastrophic failures versus immediate full-autonomy deployment.
project_ideas.measurement: Incident rate, constraint-removal velocity, cost per completed task, and rollback frequency across staged vs immediate rollout.
project_ideas.name: Constraint-Gated Autonomy Rollout
project_ideas.poc: Deploy agents in a sandboxed production workflow with progressive tool access and autonomy levels; each level unlocks only after predefined constraints are removed and metrics hold.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Elon Outcompetes Everyone | Shaun Maguire, Sequoia

project_ideas.based_on: In-context learning runs a small gradient descent loop internally through attention mechanisms.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Transformers implement measurable gradient-descent-like updates in their activations during in-context learning, and these updates scale with context length and can be steered by exemplar structure.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between activation-derived updates and true gradient updates, task accuracy versus context length, and reliability of algorithm invocation across prompt structures.
project_ideas.name: In-Context Algorithm Prober
project_ideas.poc: Build synthetic in-context tasks, instrument a small transformer's activations, vary context length and prompt structure, and probe whether internal activation trajectories correlate with an implicit gradient descent update.
project_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

project_ideas.based_on: Reinforcement learning is noisy and assigns credit inefficiently when searching for correct solutions.
project_ideas.hypothesis: RL's benefit over imitation or pre-training vanishes below a measurable success-rate threshold and becomes dominated by lucky-trajectory credit assignment.
project_ideas.measurement: Compute-to-solution, reward variance, lucky-trajectory rate, and generalization accuracy across sparsity levels.
project_ideas.name: Reward Sparsity Boundary Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Create controlled tasks with adjustable reward sparsity, then compare RL, supervised imitation, and hybrid training under matched compute budgets.
project_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

project_ideas.based_on: Too much training data leads to models relying on rote memory rather than generalizable reasoning.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Distilling a smaller model on reasoning traces while filtering memorizable trivia preserves out-of-distribution reasoning accuracy better than standard compression.
project_ideas.measurement: Out-of-distribution reasoning accuracy, memorization probe accuracy, parameter count, and inference latency.
project_ideas.name: Cognitive Core Distillation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Curate paired datasets with reasoning-heavy and trivia-heavy examples, distill multiple small models, and evaluate memorization versus generalization separately.
project_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

project_ideas.based_on: Coding is the ideal first domain for AI because software is entirely text-based and infrastructure for code execution is already mature.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Domains with automatic execution and verification infrastructure achieve higher agent automation rates than equivalent text-only domains without such infrastructure.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, human intervention rate, verification coverage, and agent iteration speed with versus without automatic verifiers.
project_ideas.name: Executable Verification Domain Mapper
project_ideas.poc: Build a taxonomy of domain properties and prototype one non-coding harness where structured textual outputs can be automatically checked, then compare agent performance with and without execution feedback.
project_ideas.video_title: Andrej Karpathy — “We’re summoning ghosts, not building animals”

project_ideas.based_on: A model-routing layer that dispatches each task class to the cheapest model that meets a measured success threshold
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed multi-step agentic coding workload, routing each task class to the cheapest model that clears a measured task-level success threshold reduces cost-per-completed-task by at least 3x versus always using a single frontier general model, without lowering success rate below the frontier baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per successfully completed task, task-level success rate, and retry/failure distribution per model and per routing policy across repeated runs.
project_ideas.name: Task-Level Model Router with Cost-Per-Success Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Model-agnostic harness that executes the same repository-scale agentic task suite against Grok Code Fast 1, GPT-5, and Gemini 2.5 Pro, logging per-attempt cost, retries, tool calls, and success per task, with a routing policy that selects a model per task class at runtime.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Insiders Reveal Elon Musk's Master Plan to Win AI w/ AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #192

project_ideas.based_on: Continuous harvesting of ordinary work video, with the pipeline bottleneck relocated to annotation and labeling of that footage
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a comparable manipulation task, a vision-only video data pipeline yields higher end-to-end throughput per unit of human labeling effort than instrumented motion-capture capture, without a policy-performance penalty large enough to offset the throughput gain.
project_ideas.measurement: Samples collected per human-hour, labeling cost per usable sample, downstream policy success rate, and the throughput-versus-quality ratio between pipelines.
project_ideas.name: Capture-Mode Ablation for Embodied Data Pipelines
project_ideas.poc: Run the same target manipulation task through two data pipelines - passive video of work plus downstream labeling, versus instrumented capture with ground-truth pose - then train matched policies and compare throughput, labeling hours, and policy success rate.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Insiders Reveal Elon Musk's Master Plan to Win AI w/ AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #192

project_ideas.based_on: Automated drift detection across the chain of transformations
project_ideas.hypothesis: Identity drift across chained generative image edits is measurable and grows monotonically with edit depth, so an automated per-step drift check can gate chains before artifact accumulation makes the output unusable, eliminating the need for bespoke identity state management.
project_ideas.measurement: Identity drift score per step and cumulative, artifact incidence rate, failure rate as a function of edit depth, and the fraction of chains salvaged by the automated gate.
project_ideas.name: Edit-Chain Identity Drift Gate
project_ideas.poc: Chained-edit benchmark that applies sequences of edits, merges, and restyles to a fixed character across increasing depths using Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, with an automated per-step identity-similarity check that halts or re-prompts on threshold breach.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Insiders Reveal Elon Musk's Master Plan to Win AI w/ AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #192

project_ideas.based_on: Separate realtime, latency-critical interaction paths from slower reasoning/tool paths
project_ideas.hypothesis: A streaming agent architecture with deferred or speculative tool calls keeps p95 response latency inside conversational timing on a transactional consumer task, at a token cost no worse than a turn-based baseline on the same task.
project_ideas.measurement: p50/p95 response latency, tool-call deferral rate, graceful-degradation rate under load, and token consumption versus the turn-based baseline.
project_ideas.name: Realtime Multimodal Latency Lab
project_ideas.poc: Instrumented realtime voice/image agent that handles a property-search style task, splitting a latency-critical streaming interaction path from a slower reasoning/tool path, with tool calls deferred or streamed and a turn-based baseline for comparison.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Insiders Reveal Elon Musk's Master Plan to Win AI w/ AWG & Dave Blundin | EP #192

project_ideas.based_on: slight decreases in delivery stability due to increased batch size
project_ideas.hypothesis: Enforcing bounded change units plus review gating proportional to AI generation velocity keeps change failure rate flat as AI adoption rises, without erasing the authoring time savings.
project_ideas.measurement: Change failure rate and batch-size distribution against AI adoption level, compared to a control group with no governor, with lead time tracked to confirm savings are not lost.
project_ideas.name: Change-Risk Governor
project_ideas.poc: A CI-side interceptor that computes diff size and complexity for incoming changes, caps or splits oversized AI-authored batches, and escalates review depth or required test coverage as change velocity increases.
project_ideas.video_title: Measuring the impact of AI on software engineering  – with Laura Tacho

project_ideas.based_on: Are self-reported AI time savings reliable enough to drive ROI decisions
project_ideas.hypothesis: Self-reported AI time savings systematically diverge from trace-derived task time in a direction predictable from task type, with the largest bias on generation tasks and the smallest on debugging and refactoring tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Mean and distribution of divergence between self-report and trace-derived task time, segmented by task type; correlation of self-report with system telemetry.
project_ideas.name: Triangulated Time-Savings Audit
project_ideas.poc: Instrument task-level workflow traces for a cohort of developers for a fixed period and compare against their self-reported per-task time-savings estimates over the same window.
project_ideas.video_title: Measuring the impact of AI on software engineering  – with Laura Tacho

project_ideas.based_on: Measuring only lines of code or acceptance rate is insufficient for business impact.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Keeping Utilization, Impact, and Cost as independently instrumented pillars joined only at query time changes investment decisions compared to acceptance-rate-driven dashboards, because it separates low adoption from usage without improvement.
project_ideas.measurement: Decision audit comparing interventions chosen from the three-pillar view versus an acceptance-rate dashboard, plus classification accuracy of low-adoption versus low-impact cases.
project_ideas.name: Three-Pillar Measurement Plane
project_ideas.poc: A reporting layer with three separate ingestion paths (tool telemetry, delivery/outcome and survey data, cost accounting) that can only be combined through explicit joins, with no conflated productivity score.
project_ideas.video_title: Measuring the impact of AI on software engineering  – with Laura Tacho

project_ideas.based_on: agent hourly rate
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-task cost attribution using agent hourly rate and human equivalent hours yields stable per-task-class delegation thresholds that beat a uniform delegate-everything policy on net time gain per developer.
project_ideas.measurement: Net time gain per developer and cost per accepted outcome under threshold-based delegation versus uniform delegation; stability of thresholds across weeks.
project_ideas.name: Agent Task Cost Attribution Ledger
project_ideas.poc: A ledger that records each delegated agent run with cost, task class, and outcome, computes agent hourly rate and human equivalent hours per task class, and emits a build-versus-delegate recommendation per class.
project_ideas.video_title: Measuring the impact of AI on software engineering  – with Laura Tacho

project_ideas.based_on: Semantic similarity is not business relevance.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Entity-constrained graph filtering yields higher business-relevance precision at top-k than pure vector top-k on the same conversation history and question set.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision@k and recall of business-relevant facts over 50 questions, plus end-to-end answer accuracy with a fixed LLM.
project_ideas.name: Relevance-vs-Similarity Retrieval Probe
project_ideas.poc: Generate a simulated financial-coach conversation history containing goals, debts, incomes, and intruder facts with high semantic similarity to music or lifestyle queries. Build two retrieval paths: (a) flat vector top-k over extracted facts; (b) typed graph memory with entity nodes, business rules, and concurrent filters. Query both systems with a fixed set of user questions and label retrieved memories for business relevance.
project_ideas.video_title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep

project_ideas.based_on: Knowledge graphs evolve continuously from every user interaction.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A memory graph that stores provenance, timestamps, and fact validity will reflect the latest user correction significantly more often than an append-only vector store after the same contradictory conversation.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of responses reflecting the latest fact after 5, 10, and 20 intervening turns on a set of 100 corrected-fact prompts.
project_ideas.name: Temporal Retraction Stress Test
project_ideas.poc: Script dialogues in which a user states a fact, later corrects it, and then asks questions that would be affected by the stale fact. Store the same facts in (a) an append-only vector memory and (b) a temporal graph with versioned nodes and per-turn provenance. Query both after varying numbers of intervening turns.
project_ideas.video_title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep

project_ideas.based_on: Agent memory should be modeled as an explicit domain ontology
project_ideas.hypothesis: A moderate domain schema with core entity types and business rules achieves a higher combined precision/coverage score than either no schema or an over-specified schema on long-horizon agent queries.
project_ideas.measurement: Composite score of retrieval precision/recall and answer coverage for facts inside and outside the schema.
project_ideas.name: SchemaDepth: Ontology Granularity Study
project_ideas.poc: Define three memory schemas for the financial-coach domain: minimal (no explicit entities), core (goals, debts, income sources), and fine-grained (adds interest rates, payment deadlines, employer details). Run the same graph extraction and retrieval pipeline under each schema, then answer fixed questions drawn from prior interactions plus questions about unforeseen facts outside the schema.
project_ideas.video_title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep

project_ideas.based_on: What is the operational overhead of knowledge graph extraction compared to flat vector embedding?
project_ideas.hypothesis: On the same conversation corpus, knowledge-graph memory can deliver answer-accuracy gains over vector-only memory without requiring prohibitively higher end-to-end latency or token cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Added latency (ms) and token cost per correct answer relative to the baseline vector pipeline.
project_ideas.name: Graph Memory Cost-Accuracy Profiler
project_ideas.poc: Instrument both a flat vector memory pipeline and a temporal-graph memory pipeline on identical transcripts. Log extraction time, query time, token usage, and answer accuracy for each retrieval path, using the same evaluation questions. Compare the cost required for each additional correct answer.
project_ideas.video_title: Stop Using RAG as Memory — Daniel Chalef, Zep

project_ideas.based_on: Top LLM code-success rates dropped by 80% over 3 months due to provider updates.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scheduled eval runs against pinned model versions will detect provider-side behavioral regressions within 24 hours, while pre-merge-only evals will miss them entirely.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-detection, false-positive rate, cost per detected regression.
project_ideas.name: Provider Regression Sentinel
project_ideas.poc: Frozen dataset and hybrid scorers run on a cron; alert on score drop beyond threshold; log model/prompt versions per run.
project_ideas.video_title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production

project_ideas.based_on: How is an LLM judge itself validated and kept calibrated over time?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A labeled holdout set can measure LLM-judge agreement with human labels and detect judge drift before it corrupts eval comparisons.
project_ideas.measurement: Judge-human agreement rate, drift detection latency, score stability across judge versions.
project_ideas.name: Judge Calibration Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run judge versions against human-labeled fixtures; track agreement rate and calibration curve over time.
project_ideas.video_title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production

project_ideas.based_on: How should production traces be selected for promotion into eval datasets?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Prioritizing thumbs-down and low-scored production traces for promotion yields higher regression-detection power per curated example than random trace sampling.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression detection power per curation hour, coverage delta, false-positive promotion rate.
project_ideas.name: Trace-to-Eval Promotion Pipeline
project_ideas.poc: Ingest production traces, filter by feedback/score, sample into dataset, run evals against baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production

project_ideas.based_on: Observability is attached at the LLM client boundary
project_ideas.hypothesis: Wrapping LLM API clients with a tracing SDK/proxy captures production trace coverage equivalent to application-level logging with lower integration effort and no business-logic changes.
project_ideas.measurement: Trace coverage percentage, integration time, runtime overhead, number of app-code changes.
project_ideas.name: LLM Client Observability Interposer
project_ideas.poc: Interpose a wrapper/proxy across heterogeneous LLM call sites and compare captured traces against baseline app instrumentation.
project_ideas.video_title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production

project_ideas.based_on: Web search and tool calling can be dynamically injected into any language model without requiring custom client implementations.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tool calling and web grounding injected by a proxy into models without native tool-calling support achieve task success within 10% of natively tool-calling models, at a bounded added time-to-first-token.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, added p50/p99 latency to first token, and citation correctness rate for injected versus native configurations.
project_ideas.name: Proxy-Injection Parity Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a proxy that intercepts requests and augments streaming responses with retrieved context and citations, then run one fixed tool-using task suite across a no-tool open-weights model with proxy injection versus a native tool-calling model without it.
project_ideas.video_title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter

project_ideas.based_on: Customers and developers do not rely on a single model; they leverage different models for different purposes to unlock massive performance and cost gains.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Task-aware dynamic provider routing reduces cost per solved task by at least 30% versus a single fixed frontier model at equal or better quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per solved task, quality score per task class, and failover-induced error rate.
project_ideas.name: Task-Aware Routing Cost Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement a router that classifies incoming requests and selects providers by price/latency with failover, then replay a mixed workload of simple extraction, long-context reasoning, and code tasks against both the router and a single-model baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter

project_ideas.based_on: Solves complex routing, normalization, caching, and stream cancellation challenges across over 60 active providers and 400 models.
project_ideas.hypothesis: At least one provider among a representative multi-provider set violates normalized stream cancellation or partial-output contract under load, and the violation is discoverable only by structured conformance testing.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of providers failing each conformance check, shape of divergences, and reproducibility rate of cancellation defects under concurrent load.
project_ideas.name: Multi-Provider Stream Conformance Suite
project_ideas.poc: Define a normalized request/response and stream-lifecycle contract, then implement a test suite that exercises routing, failover, mid-stream cancellation, and token-boundary integrity across multiple providers.
project_ideas.video_title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter

project_ideas.based_on: Distillation unlocked knowledge being distilled into software without massive training budgets.
project_ideas.hypothesis: On a single narrow task, a cheaply distilled small open model matches a routed frontier model on accuracy at an order-of-magnitude lower cost per correct answer.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per correct answer, accuracy delta, and break-even task volume at which distillation amortizes.
project_ideas.name: Cheap-Student Narrow-Task Substitution Test
