project_ideas.poc: Distill a small open-weights model on teacher outputs for one narrow task within a sub-$600 compute budget, then compare it head-to-head against a routed frontier model on a held-out evaluation set.
project_ideas.video_title: Fun stories from building OpenRouter and where all this is going - Alex Atallah, OpenRouter

project_ideas.based_on: complement reductionist debugging with holistic systemic synthesis
project_ideas.hypothesis: Across agent systems with known emergent failure modes, interaction-level tracing (handoff sequences, context-loss events, path divergence) will localize failures that component-level eval suites fail to attribute at a statistically higher rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Root-cause localization rate and time-to-attribution for each mode on the injected fault set; count of faults localized by interaction tracing but not by component evals.
project_ideas.name: InteractionTrace: Emergent-Failure Localizer for Multi-Agent Systems
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a small multi-agent pipeline with two analysis modes: a component-level eval harness and a trajectory/interaction tracer. Inject a set of intentionally emergent faults (context degradation across handoffs, subagent ping-pong, contradictory tool contracts) and have both modes attempt root-cause attribution.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Learning Systems Thinking is Essential in Tech - Diana Montalion

project_ideas.based_on: organizations design systems that mirror their communication structures
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed agent capability set, varying only the communication topology (handoff schema, shared-context scope, subagent boundaries) produces larger differences in end-to-end task outcomes than varying prompt or capability quality.
project_ideas.measurement: Variance in task success and in failure-mode distribution attributable to topology versus to capability/prompt changes; regression rate when capability is improved without topology change.
project_ideas.name: Topology First: Handoff-Protocol Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build one task suite and three or more topology variants (centralized orchestrator, peer handoff, shared-blackboard) holding prompts and tools constant; run identical workloads and compare trajectory behavior and task success.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Learning Systems Thinking is Essential in Tech - Diana Montalion

project_ideas.based_on: do not replace human relational and architectural judgment
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tasks classified as language-level transformation can be delegated to models without degrading output coherence, while tasks classified as relationship/coherence judgment degrade measurably when delegated, and the rubric predicts which is which.
project_ideas.measurement: Coherence and judgment scores by task class and condition; rubric classification accuracy versus observed degradation; rate of undetected over-delegation.
project_ideas.name: Delegation Rubric Gate
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a task set spanning both classes; run each with and without model assistance; an independent reviewer scores coherence and relational soundness blind to condition.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Learning Systems Thinking is Essential in Tech - Diana Montalion

project_ideas.based_on: writing down dissenting viewpoints improves collaborative problem-solving
project_ideas.hypothesis: Requiring dissent to be written as an explicit artifact before a decision reduces recurrence of the same debate in multi-agent critique/review workflows relative to immediate-response critique.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of recurring debate cycles per design decision, decision reversal rate, and time-to-stable-decision across the two modes.
project_ideas.name: Dissent Before Decision: Debate-Loop Reducer
project_ideas.poc: Implement two review modes in a design-review agent workflow: immediate critique versus a staged step that captures dissenting positions as a persisted artifact before the decision step. Run repeated review sessions on the same evolving design.
project_ideas.video_title: Why Learning Systems Thinking is Essential in Tech - Diana Montalion

project_ideas.based_on: Human-in-the-loop is a latency constraint, not just a governance choice
project_ideas.hypothesis: If action authorization is moved from inline per-action approval to pre-authorized policy predicates with provenance logging, then a simulated high-tempo defense agent can execute at machine speed with zero unlogged policy violations and >90% lower median action latency than an inline-approval baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Median and tail action latency, policy violation rate, audit completeness score, human intervention frequency.
project_ideas.name: Policy-Bound Autonomy Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Build a runtime that wraps tool calls with declarative policy bounds, logs decision provenance, supports post-hoc replay, and compare against an inline human-approval gate on a drone-swarm engagement simulation.
project_ideas.video_title: Aliens, AI Weapons, China & Global Conflict: Palmer Luckey Sounds the Alarm | EP #169

project_ideas.based_on: A multi-domain data-aggregation layer that fuses heterogeneous sensors
project_ideas.hypothesis: If a fusion and autonomous prioritization layer is inserted upstream of an agent planner, then context token count and mis-prioritization errors will decrease versus raw multi-tool signal ingestion without reducing task success.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, context token count, time-to-decision, mis-prioritization rate.
project_ideas.name: Fusion-Prioritization Agent Layer
project_ideas.poc: Implement an orchestration layer that aggregates heterogeneous tool outputs and logs, deduplicates and ranks by task-relevant threat/priority, then passes only ranked state to a planner; benchmark on a multi-source incident triage task.
project_ideas.video_title: Aliens, AI Weapons, China & Global Conflict: Palmer Luckey Sounds the Alarm | EP #169

project_ideas.based_on: Can a software-defined countermeasure layer adapt faster than an adversary's autonomy iteration cycle
project_ideas.hypothesis: If a countermeasure is deployed as a software policy update, then time from threat observation to effective countermeasure will be lower than a hardware-locked baseline, but only when rollback and evaluation tooling are present.
project_ideas.measurement: Time from threat observation to effective countermeasure, rollback safety, change failure rate.
project_ideas.name: Adaptation-Latency Benchmark for Software-Defined Countermeasures
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a novel adversarial drone behavior, deploy a countermeasure as a software policy update versus a hardware reconfiguration, and measure time-to-field under both conditions.
project_ideas.video_title: Aliens, AI Weapons, China & Global Conflict: Palmer Luckey Sounds the Alarm | EP #169

project_ideas.based_on: The relevant threat model is asymmetric and multi-polar
project_ideas.hypothesis: If agent tool-call authorization is tiered by actor type and attribution confidence, then simulated attack success from non-deterrable rogue actors will decrease without exceeding a 5% false-positive rate on trusted peer actions.
project_ideas.measurement: Attack success rate, false-positive rate, authorization latency.
project_ideas.name: Threat-Tiered Agent Security
project_ideas.poc: Build an agent tool-call authorization layer with tiers (trusted peer, rogue, unknown) and confidence scores; simulate peer and rogue agent attacks against a shared toolset.
project_ideas.video_title: Aliens, AI Weapons, China & Global Conflict: Palmer Luckey Sounds the Alarm | EP #169

project_ideas.based_on: first-party video consent for every avatar
project_ideas.hypothesis: A consent artifact cryptographically bound to a specific trained avatar model, with a revocation path that hard-disables generation, can be implemented without making avatar enrollment unusably slow.
project_ideas.measurement: Enrollment time overhead per avatar (target: within the reported 4-minute avatar creation flow), successful block rate of generation attempts after revocation (target 100%), and audit-trail completeness for every generated asset.
project_ideas.name: Consent-Bound Avatar Registry
project_ideas.poc: Build a small registry service: record consent statement, hash and sign it, bind the hash into the avatar model's metadata, gate every inference call on a live consent check, and expose a revoke endpoint that invalidates future generation while retaining an audit log.
project_ideas.video_title: The Future of AI Avatars and DeepFake Technology w/ Joshua Xu & Steve Brown | EP #161

project_ideas.based_on: Giving an agent agency requires training it on personal history, values, and knowledge bases
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent's agreement with a principal's own answers increases measurably with curated personal corpus coverage up to a saturation point, after which additional raw data yields diminishing or negative returns.
project_ideas.measurement: Agreement rate (exact/partial match, plus rubric score) versus corpus slice size and category; marginal fidelity per data category; point at which additional data stops helping.
project_ideas.name: Principal-Agreement Benchmark for Personal Corpora
project_ideas.poc: Collect a principal's answers to a held-out set of decisions and judgment prompts; build agents grounded in incrementally larger curated corpus slices (history, values, professional knowledge); score agreement against the principal's own answers at each increment.
project_ideas.video_title: The Future of AI Avatars and DeepFake Technology w/ Joshua Xu & Steve Brown | EP #161

project_ideas.based_on: What standards will emerge for verifying the authenticity of real-time AI video calls?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Signed capture-time attestation combined with a challenge-response secret in a separate channel detects real-time avatar impersonation with acceptable user-perceived latency, outperforming shared verification words alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Impersonation detection rate, false-rejection rate on genuine calls, added call-setup latency, and task-completion time versus a password-only baseline.
project_ideas.name: Live-Call Provenance Challenge
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a calling flow where the initiator's device signs a capture attestation and the callee requests a nonce answerable only out-of-band; measure end-to-end added latency and run an adversarial test with a cloned-voice impersonator.
project_ideas.video_title: The Future of AI Avatars and DeepFake Technology w/ Joshua Xu & Steve Brown | EP #161

project_ideas.based_on: AI agents can synthesize fragmented medical data across specialties to provide critical health insights.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent that assembles fragmented records across specialties in a single reasoning pass detects flagged conditions earlier than standard referral pathways, but at a false-positive cost that must be quantified before deployment.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection lead time in days versus standard pathway, false-positive rate per panel, and specialist-confirmed precision on flagged cases.
project_ideas.name: Cross-Silo Diagnostic Lead-Time Harness
project_ideas.poc: Run a retrospective, outcome-blinded review where the agent processes historical lab panels and record fragments, flags candidate conditions, and its flags are compared against the eventual clinical outcome and the documented referral timeline.
project_ideas.video_title: The Future of AI Avatars and DeepFake Technology w/ Joshua Xu & Steve Brown | EP #161

project_ideas.based_on: Transfer learning across tasks
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists a deployment volume V such that a single general agent runtime plus transfer learning achieves lower cost per successful task than N task-specific agents, and that V is lower than the team's realistic 12-month task volume for at least one task family.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per successful task as a function of number of tasks and invocations; crossover volume V; per-task success-rate delta between generalist and specialist.
project_ideas.name: Crossover Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build one shared runtime with a transfer mechanism (retrieval + tool reuse + few-shot adaptation) and N narrow task-tuned baselines over a shared task suite; sweep volume per task and measure cost per successful task, adaptation time per new task, and a failure taxonomy.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Experts Q&A: How Humanoid Robots Will Impact Every Industry | EP #160

project_ideas.based_on: How will cybersecurity for humanoid robots be maintained at scale?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Signed on-device model updates combined with remote attestation and fleet-level anomaly telemetry can detect a defined set of tampering and spoofed-sensor threat classes on untethered edge agents without requiring continuous connectivity.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate and mean time to detect per injected threat class, false-positive rate across the clean fleet, and fraction of detection possible offline.
project_ideas.name: Signed Edge Policy with Fleet Attestation
project_ideas.poc: Prototype signed update delivery, boot-time and periodic attestation, and a fleet anomaly detector; inject tampered model weights, spoofed sensor streams, and rolled-back firmware into a test fleet and measure detection latency and false-positive rate.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Experts Q&A: How Humanoid Robots Will Impact Every Industry | EP #160

project_ideas.based_on: Fusion plants deployed in existing substation locations will eliminate transmission needs.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed capacity target, deployment topology that reuses already-permitted sites reaches operational readiness earlier than the same capacity delivered through new long-haul build-out, and existing sites absorb a measurable share of the load without downstream upgrades.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-capacity delta between topologies; share of target capacity absorbed by existing sites before requiring upgrades; sensitivity of the delta to permitting latency.
project_ideas.name: Brownfield Interconnect Planner
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a milestone timeline model with separate engineering and permitting milestones for two topologies (new build-out vs. co-located at existing handoff points), including residual capacity at existing sites as a variable.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Experts Q&A: How Humanoid Robots Will Impact Every Industry | EP #160

project_ideas.based_on: Humanoid robots will enter the workforce first in vast numbers, followed by homes and space.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Ordering autonomy rollouts by environment observability and blast radius rather than by task value or capability readiness yields a higher reliability record at the point of first entry into an unstructured environment.
project_ideas.measurement: Incident rate per 1,000 task executions by tier; rollback frequency at tier transition; reliability record at first unstructured-environment entry.
project_ideas.name: Observability-First Rollout Ladder
project_ideas.poc: Define an observability and blast-radius score per environment tier, run two rollout orderings against the same capability baseline, and compare incident rates and rollback frequency at each tier transition.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Experts Q&A: How Humanoid Robots Will Impact Every Industry | EP #160

project_ideas.based_on: Lattice OS is positioned as a software layer spanning multiple autonomous platforms
project_ideas.hypothesis: A shared policy/control runtime spanning heterogeneous tool and body simulators reduces per-substrate integration effort and capability propagation latency compared with bespoke per-substrate stacks.
project_ideas.measurement: Integration effort per substrate, latency from capability update to all substrates, task success rate, and code reuse percentage.
project_ideas.name: Substrate-Agnostic Agent Runtime Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal Lattice-style orchestration layer, point it at three simulated execution substrates with different action interfaces, and run an identical task suite against bespoke controllers for each substrate.
project_ideas.video_title: The Billionaire Building America's AI Military | EP #158

project_ideas.based_on: What is the actual cost in latency/throughput of keeping a human accountability step
project_ideas.hypothesis: Inserting a human accountability checkpoint into a high-tempo autonomous pipeline imposes a measurable latency/throughput tax that scales nonlinearly with decision tempo and criticality.
project_ideas.measurement: Decisions per hour, p95 latency, missed opportunities, error rate, and operator workload.
project_ideas.name: Human Accountability Latency Tax
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a high-tempo intercept or triage pipeline with human-in-the-loop placed at different decision points, comparing fully autonomous, human-on-loop, and human-in-loop variants.
project_ideas.video_title: The Billionaire Building America's AI Military | EP #158

project_ideas.based_on: Can general-purpose embodied agents reliably operate existing human interfaces
project_ideas.hypothesis: General-purpose computer-use agents operating legacy human interfaces achieve lower task success and higher brittleness than API-instrumented equivalents, but recover through retry/replan at a predictable overhead.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success, intervention rate, recovery success, time-to-completion, and failure taxonomy.
project_ideas.name: Legacy Interface Agent Reliability Harness
project_ideas.poc: Benchmark the same tasks on a GUI-only legacy application versus an API-instrumented version using the same agent model, with and without retry policies.
project_ideas.video_title: The Billionaire Building America's AI Military | EP #158

project_ideas.based_on: Cost-plus contracting disincentivizes speed and efficiency, rewarding higher costs.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Programs measured by cost-reimbursement versus outcome-linked rewards diverge in delivery speed and cost efficiency even when technical talent and scope are held constant.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-delivery, total cost, rework, scope creep, and milestone slip.
project_ideas.name: Incentive-Outcome Contract Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Run an agent-based or human-subject simulation of two development programs under cost-plus and fixed-outcome payoff rules, tracking delivery milestones and spend.
project_ideas.video_title: The Billionaire Building America's AI Military | EP #158

project_ideas.based_on: choose or constrain the response policy
project_ideas.channel: Front Row Seat with Ken Coleman
project_ideas.hypothesis: Inserting an explicit practical/emotional/social classifier with a per-mode response policy ahead of an otherwise identical generator reduces human-rated register-mismatch failures relative to the unmodified generator, at less than a 15% latency penalty.
project_ideas.measurement: Mismatch rate delta between arms, classifier accuracy against held-out turn labels, and end-to-end latency/cost delta per turn.
project_ideas.name: ModeGate
project_ideas.poc: Build a labeled multi-turn turn-level dataset of mode and mismatch outcomes; run a frozen model with and without an upstream classifier + policy router; blind-rate both arms for mismatch.
project_ideas.video_title: The Key to Mastering Conversations and Being Memorable

project_ideas.based_on: then ask 'Did I get that right?'
project_ideas.channel: Front Row Seat with Ken Coleman
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an explicit confirmation round-trip reduces silent misinterpretation, measured as downstream corrections or rollbacks, by more than an equivalent budget spent improving paraphrase fidelity alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of post-hoc corrections/rollbacks per task, confirmation acceptance rate, and added round trips per completed task.
project_ideas.name: LoopBack
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a task-completion agent with a paraphrase-then-confirm gate; run two treatment arms (better paraphrase vs. confirmation request) against an ungated baseline on the same task suite.
project_ideas.video_title: The Key to Mastering Conversations and Being Memorable

project_ideas.based_on: The goal of communication is connection, not just information transfer.
project_ideas.channel: Front Row Seat with Ken Coleman
project_ideas.hypothesis: Text-only synchronization measures such as lexical alignment, response-latency coupling, and turn-taking symmetry correlate with human-reported connection ratings while remaining largely uncorrelated with task-success scores.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation (and partial correlation controlling for task success) between synchronization metrics and human connection ratings.
project_ideas.name: SyncScore
project_ideas.poc: Collect human connection ratings on a set of human-agent transcripts; compute candidate synchronization metrics on the same transcripts; test correlation structure against task-outcome labels.
project_ideas.video_title: The Key to Mastering Conversations and Being Memorable

project_ideas.based_on: a low-base-rate but high-salience element in the context window disproportionately steers downstream judgment
project_ideas.channel: Front Row Seat with Ken Coleman
project_ideas.hypothesis: A low-frequency, high-salience distractor inserted into context shifts downstream judgment by a measurable margin, and an explicit base-rate restatement in the prompt recovers most of that shift where adding more relevant context does not.
project_ideas.measurement: Judgment-shift magnitude in percentage points across arms, and recovery fraction attributable to base-rate restatement versus added context.
project_ideas.name: BaseRateBench
project_ideas.poc: Construct matched prompts differing only in the presence of one vivid low-base-rate item; run three arms (control, distractor, distractor + base-rate restatement) on a judgment task with objective ground truth.
project_ideas.video_title: The Key to Mastering Conversations and Being Memorable

project_ideas.based_on: Can the value of specific architectural options be quantitatively estimated rather than argued qualitatively?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scoring architectural abstractions by estimated switching cost and probability distribution of future change predicts which abstractions teams actually exercise or extend in practice, and correlates with perceived value.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between predicted option value and observed frequency of abstraction use/extension; qualitative validation via developer interviews.
project_ideas.name: OptionScorer
project_ideas.poc: Build a lightweight tool that takes a set of architectural decisions (e.g., provider-agnostic interface, abstraction layer) and outputs an option value score based on a survey of switching costs and uncertainty estimates; validate against git history or decision logs of actual abstraction usage in open-source projects.
project_ideas.video_title: Thinking Like an Architect - Gregor Hohpe - NDC London 2025

project_ideas.based_on: When does centralizing a decision outperform delegating it to the actor with local context?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Delegating decisions to consequence-bearing actors improves decision quality over centralized expert decisions when context locality is high and coordination costs are low, but centralization wins when coordination costs exceed a threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Decision quality score, latency, coordination overhead as a function of context locality and communication cost; identify crossover point.
project_ideas.name: DecisionDelegationBench
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a multi-agent system with a decision task (e.g., resource allocation) under two conditions: centralized oracle vs. local agents. Vary communication costs and context locality. Measure outcome quality and latency.
project_ideas.video_title: Thinking Like an Architect - Gregor Hohpe - NDC London 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Is there a repeatable procedure for extracting the underlying goal from a stated technical request?
project_ideas.hypothesis: An explicit goal-inference step that maps requested actions to intended outcomes reduces the frequency of building wrong solutions and improves alignment with the requester's actual criterion.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy of inferred goal vs. true hidden goal; reduction in rework in a simulated task; user-rated alignment.
project_ideas.name: GoalBoomerang
project_ideas.poc: Implement a prompt-based module in an agent pipeline that, before executing a technical request (e.g., 'we need cloud-native'), asks clarifying questions to infer underlying goals (e.g., resilience). Evaluate on a set of synthetic requests with known hidden goals.
project_ideas.video_title: Thinking Like an Architect - Gregor Hohpe - NDC London 2025

project_ideas.based_on: Liquid neural networks require minimal compute to package intelligence into devices.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed edge task, a liquid neural network can achieve latency, memory, and energy consumption low enough for battery-powered on-device execution while maintaining accuracy within a small margin of a comparable small transformer, without cloud inference.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-inference latency, peak memory, energy per inference, model size, and accuracy delta between liquid neural network and small transformer.
project_ideas.name: Edge Liquid Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Implement the same edge task with a liquid neural network and a small transformer, deploy both on a phone, laptop, and embedded device, and measure compute, memory, latency, energy, and accuracy.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Leaders Reveal the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs (At FII Miami 2025) | EP #150

project_ideas.based_on: Tensor processors are positioned as simpler and easier to program than GPUs
project_ideas.hypothesis: Porting representative training and inference workloads from CUDA to an open tensor processor software stack requires less developer effort and yields substantially lower total cost of ownership than an equivalent GPU system, without unacceptable throughput loss.
project_ideas.measurement: Developer hours to port, number of compatibility blockers, training and inference throughput, and total cost of ownership ratio.
project_ideas.name: Tensor Portability Index
project_ideas.poc: Port at least two representative AI workloads to a tensor processor stack, compare against a GPU baseline, and track developer hours, compatibility issues, throughput, and cost.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Leaders Reveal the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs (At FII Miami 2025) | EP #150

project_ideas.based_on: Only 11% of enterprise technology use cases reached production over five years
project_ideas.hypothesis: Teams that change organizational architecture through dedicated AI product ownership, literacy programs, and process redesign achieve a higher pilot-to-production conversion rate than teams that only add models or tools.
project_ideas.measurement: Pilot-to-production conversion rate, time from pilot to production, and adoption metrics across programs with and without organizational interventions.
project_ideas.name: Enterprise AI Production Mechanics
project_ideas.poc: Study enterprise AI programs that moved from pilot to production and document the specific organizational, governance, and process interventions compared with stalled programs.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Leaders Reveal the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs (At FII Miami 2025) | EP #150

project_ideas.based_on: An 11-person team using AI and quantum sensors solved GPS-denied navigation
project_ideas.hypothesis: A small team using AI and quantum sensors can match or exceed the navigation accuracy of a larger conventional team in an adjacent GPS-denied or sensor-limited domain under controlled test conditions.
project_ideas.measurement: Position error, team size, time to solve, and cost per successful navigation run.
project_ideas.name: Small Team Sensor Fusion Replication
project_ideas.poc: Replicate a small-team AI-plus-sensor approach in an indoor or urban navigation testbed and compare against a larger conventional team using standard methods.
project_ideas.video_title: AI Leaders Reveal the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs (At FII Miami 2025) | EP #150

project_ideas.based_on: Which benchmark suite or task distribution demonstrates that open models genuinely match GPT-4o at 96% lower cost?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Using a task-level regression suite of structured tool-use and reasoning tasks, a routing layer can maintain the same success rate as a GPT-4o-only agent while achieving a per-successful-task cost reduction of at least 50% on a 500-task sample (not necessarily the advertised 96%).
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate per task, total cost, cost per successful task, and number of router-induced regressions across the 500 tasks.
project_ideas.name: Task-cost parity harness for open vs closed frontier models
project_ideas.poc: Build a model gateway with adapters for DeepSeek-V3/R1 and GPT-4o; instrument each task with success checks and cost meters; replay a recorded workload with single-model and routing strategies.
project_ideas.video_title: DeepSeek vs. Open AI - The State of AI w/ Emad Mostaque & Salim Ismail | EP #146

project_ideas.based_on: Can curriculum learning from broad pretraining to specialized, continuously evaluated fine-tuning be applied to training agent sub-policies without catastrophic forgetting?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Staged fine-tuning (broad general instruction tuning -> task simulation -> tool-call distillation with evaluation gates) produces fewer forgetting episodes and lower total training cost than an equal-budget one-shot mixed-domain fine-tuning run for a small LM.
project_ideas.measurement: Tool-call accuracy, held-out task recall/forgetting rate, total compute hours, and convergence steps required.
project_ideas.name: Layered curriculum fine-tuning for tool-calling agents
project_ideas.poc: Use a 1B-7B open-weight model; split the same final dataset; train two variants (one-shot vs staged gates); evaluate tool-call correctness and held-out task recall.
project_ideas.video_title: DeepSeek vs. Open AI - The State of AI w/ Emad Mostaque & Salim Ismail | EP #146

project_ideas.based_on: Once weights are open, provider-side safety, licensing, and access controls are no longer the enforcement point
project_ideas.hypothesis: If operators were to deploy open-weight agents, the presence of policy artifacts (model cards, logging policy, tool permission boundaries, alerting) can be scored; a measurable governance score will be inversely correlated with expected time-to-remediate a reported safety incident.
project_ideas.measurement: Governance checklist score, simulated detection/response time in minutes.
project_ideas.name: Open-weight responsibility linter
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a static checker that scans deployment configurations and model cards for governance controls, then run tabletop incident simulations to estimate detection and response times.
project_ideas.video_title: DeepSeek vs. Open AI - The State of AI w/ Emad Mostaque & Salim Ismail | EP #146

project_ideas.based_on: treats a single canonical platform and unified data cloud as a prerequisite for reliable agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: For the same policy/model and ticket set, an agent whose tool layer reads from a unified normalized enterprise store will complete at least 15 percentage points more end-to-end support tasks than an identical agent using three separate application APIs.
project_ideas.measurement: Task-completion rate, correct fact retrieval, tool-call efficiency, and number of cases requiring human escalation.
project_ideas.name: Data-Fabric Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark with 200 support tickets and three mocked enterprise APIs (CRM, billing, knowledge); implement two equivalent agents using the same base model and escalation rules—one with fragmented app-specific tools and one with a Data Cloud-style merged read model.
project_ideas.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141

project_ideas.based_on: AI agents autonomously resolve ~95% of routine requests first, human agents remain only for escalation
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent-first support operation with a confidence threshold that routes low-confidence cases to humans will achieve equal or better outcome quality at lower cost than fully autonomous or human-first baselines, and the optimal threshold shifts with ticket complexity.
project_ideas.measurement: Cost per resolved ticket, escalation rate, quality score against held-out labels, and tail latency.
project_ideas.name: Confidence-Gated Support Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Use a labeled customer-support corpus to simulate three policies: fully autonomous, human-first, and confidence-gated triage with thresholds from 70% to 95%; route low-confidence agent cases to simulated human analysts and compare performance on routine versus edge-case tickets.
project_ideas.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141

project_ideas.based_on: agentic developer tools can move from augmenting existing engineers to suppressing headcount growth
project_ideas.hypothesis: When agentic developer tools are introduced into treatment teams, measured engineering productivity improves by at least 20% compared with control teams, and approved net-new engineering headcount for a fixed roadmap shrinks by at least one planned FTE per team in the following planning cycle.
project_ideas.measurement: Merged pull requests per developer per month, cycle time, defect escape rate, and delta in proposed net-new engineering hires.
project_ideas.name: Engineering Hiring Elasticity Probe
project_ideas.poc: In a mid-sized software organization, roll out AI developer tools to 10 treatment teams while keeping 10 comparable teams on the existing toolchain for two quarters; instrument repository metrics and compare staffing-plan proposals per team.
project_ideas.video_title: Salesforce Founder Gives the Truth on AI Agents  w/ Marc Benioff | EP #141

project_ideas.based_on: significance is measured by cost of change
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing agent-assisted decisions to human review by estimated cost of change (low reversibility to humans, high reversibility to the model) dominates uniform human review on total cost and on downstream rework rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Rework rate per decision, total human review minutes, and cost per accepted decision; pass condition is lower or equal rework at materially lower review time for the cost-based policy.
project_ideas.name: Reversal-Cost Router
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent-assisted workflow to log decision type, a reversibility-cost estimate, routing outcome, and whether the decision was later reverted. Build a small taxonomy of agent-system decisions (model/vendor choice, tool schema, memory layout, eval harness, prompt template), assign each a cost band, and A/B the cost-based routing policy against uniform review on a bounded set of real tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Evolution of software architecture with the co-creator of UML (Grady Booch)

project_ideas.based_on: a visual modeling/reasoning language was pushed into being an executable programming language
project_ideas.hypothesis: Layer absorption is detectable before it becomes expensive: artifacts that start as reasoning/notation and begin acquiring execution semantics (code generation, side effects, control flow, state mutation) exhibit measurable structural signals that predict later complexity growth and contributor defection.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of flagged artifacts against a hand-labeled set of 'this became a runtime' cases, plus correlation between rung crossings and subsequent maintenance cost or usage decline in the tracked repos.
project_ideas.name: Abstraction-Creep Linter
project_ideas.poc: Define a minimal ladder of execution-semantics indicators (emits executable artifacts, mutates external state, owns control flow, becomes a required runtime dependency) and run the checker over a set of agent-repo specification artifacts — plan/DSL artifacts, schema definitions, prompt-template layers — tracking which ones cross rungs over time.
project_ideas.video_title: Evolution of software architecture with the co-creator of UML (Grady Booch)

project_ideas.based_on: Old code never dies; you have to kill it.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Requiring an owner, a retirement trigger, and a migration or emulation path at component creation bounds long-lived complexity: components registered with retirement metadata are actually removed or migrated at a higher rate than unregistered components of comparable age.
project_ideas.measurement: Fraction of registered components that reach an explicit retirement or migration event; count of registered components that outlive their stated trigger without action (the failure signal); total line/component count versus the pre-registry baseline.
project_ideas.name: Retirement-Trigger Registry
project_ideas.poc: Add a creation-time manifest for every new component in a bounded repo (prompt chains, adapters, legacy-service wrappers, tool shims) recording owner, retirement trigger condition, and migration path. Run for a fixed period and compare removal/migration events against a matched set of pre-registry components.
project_ideas.video_title: Evolution of software architecture with the co-creator of UML (Grady Booch)

project_ideas.based_on: they lack true reasoning and embodiment
project_ideas.hypothesis: Grounding provenance matters more than grounding presence: agent architectures differing only in grounding signal (static context vs. live execution feedback vs. simulated environment interaction) differ measurably in decision quality on cross-cutting systemic tasks, and execution feedback partially substitutes for embodiment-style grounding.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of systemic-context errors per configuration, plus score stability across repeated runs; refutation condition is no significant difference attributable to grounding signal.
project_ideas.name: Grounding-Signal Comparison Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build three otherwise-identical agent configurations on a task set requiring systemic, cross-cutting decisions (e.g., choosing and justifying a tool-contract or memory-schema design), swap only the grounding signal, and blind-score outputs for systemic consistency and for confidently-stated but contextually wrong claims.
project_ideas.video_title: Evolution of software architecture with the co-creator of UML (Grady Booch)

project_ideas.based_on: domain-neutral LLM-based agents
project_ideas.hypothesis: An LLM-based agent, prompted with a top-level ontology (e.g., BFO) and conflicting domain definitions, can resolve conflicts (e.g., 'virion' vs 'pathogen') without collapsing legitimate distinctions, achieving higher inter-annotator agreement than domain-expert-only resolution.
project_ideas.measurement: Definition convergence rate (% of conflicts resolved), preservation of domain-specific distinctions (expert rating), and time to resolution compared to a human neutral arbiter baseline.
project_ideas.name: Neutral Arbiter Agent
project_ideas.poc: Build a prototype that ingests conflicting definitions from two life-science subdomains, uses BFO constraints to propose unified definitions, and compares outputs to human expert arbitration on a held-out set of conflict cases.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Do Things with Ontologies

project_ideas.based_on: modeling dispositions/roles as first-class realizable entities
project_ideas.hypothesis: Modeling agent capabilities as realizable entities (dispositions/roles) with explicit substrate attachment improves planning correctness on tasks requiring unexercised capabilities compared to boolean state flags, because planners can reason over latent capabilities.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, planning latency, and number of invalid tool attempts across the two registry designs.
project_ideas.name: Disposition-Typed Capability Registry for Agents
project_ideas.poc: Implement two versions of a tool registry for an LLM agent: one with boolean flags, one with typed disposition entities; evaluate on a set of planning tasks that require recognizing unexercised capabilities.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Do Things with Ontologies

project_ideas.based_on: Design an interoperability benchmark comparing silo-based pipelines against ontology-mediated ones
project_ideas.hypothesis: Ontology-mediated data integration pipelines reduce integration latency and mapping effort and lower error rates compared to silo-based point-to-point pipelines when integrating N heterogeneous sources.
project_ideas.measurement: Integration latency, number of mapping rules, query error rate, and cost of adding a new source for each pipeline.
project_ideas.name: Ontology-Mediated Integration Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build two pipelines for a synthetic multi-source dataset (e.g., 5 sources with different schemas); one uses a shared ontology-based semantic layer, the other uses point-to-point mappings. Compare on integration tasks and adding a new source.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Do Things with Ontologies

project_ideas.based_on: Define a versioning/deprecation policy for an upper ontology layer
project_ideas.hypothesis: A versioned upper ontology with explicit deprecation and migration policies reduces downstream migration cost and semantic drift across dependent domain models compared to an unversioned top-level ontology.
project_ideas.measurement: Time to migrate, number of breaking changes, and semantic drift (difference in inferred classifications pre/post migration).
project_ideas.name: Fallibilist Ontology Versioning Protocol
project_ideas.poc: Define a versioning scheme for a small top-level ontology (e.g., BFO subset) and simulate a scientific finding that changes a core class; measure migration effort for 5 dependent domain models.
project_ideas.video_title: How to Do Things with Ontologies

project_ideas.based_on: If response variety < input variety
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed agent harness, the gap between measured input-condition diversity and enumerated response-option diversity predicts task failure rate better than model tier or prompt length on benchmarks with controlled input diversity.
project_ideas.measurement: Spearman correlation between variety gap and per-family failure rate; head-to-head comparison against baselines (model tier, prompt tokens) on the same benchmark split.
project_ideas.name: Variety Gap Meter
project_ideas.poc: Wrap a harness to log a canonical signature for each incoming condition (clustered into condition classes) and each emitted response (tool call plus argument class). Compute cardinality and entropy for both sides per task family, then correlate the gap with failures.
project_ideas.video_title: Demystifying the Viable System Model: A Practical Approach

project_ideas.based_on: A deconfliction layer whose only mandate is preventing operational friction
project_ideas.hypothesis: Separating an anti-oscillation coordination layer from a resource-bargaining and monitoring layer reduces concurrent-load oscillation failures relative to a single orchestrator owning all three, without degrading task success rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Counts of duplicate and contending tool calls, lock-wait time, budget overruns, and task success rate under increasing concurrency, plus attribution of each failure to exactly one of the two layers.
project_ideas.name: Split-Orchestrator Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build two harnesses over the same tool set: (A) one orchestrator owning dedup, ordering, budgets, and monitoring; (B) a deconfliction component whose only mandate is ordering, locking and dedup, plus a management component that negotiates token budgets and reports delivery. Run identical concurrent multi-agent workloads against both.
project_ideas.video_title: Demystifying the Viable System Model: A Practical Approach

project_ideas.based_on: At what depth should recursive self-similar decomposition terminate
project_ideas.hypothesis: Marginal task value per recursion level decays faster than marginal token and latency cost beyond a small depth, and a cost-aware termination heuristic matches fixed-depth-3 quality at lower total cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Quality-versus-cost curves per recursion depth; total tokens and wall-clock time to reach a fixed success threshold, compared against fixed-depth baselines.
project_ideas.name: Recursion Depth Budget Controller
project_ideas.poc: Implement a self-similar harness contract instantiated at every nesting level, instrument marginal value (success delta) and marginal cost per level across task suites, and implement a stopping rule driven by remaining budget and observed marginal value.
project_ideas.video_title: Demystifying the Viable System Model: A Practical Approach

project_ideas.based_on: Organizations need functional 'rooms' for management activities even if they reject traditional hierarchical roles.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Peer agent topologies with no designated orchestrator exhibit measurable emergent management behavior — repeated serialization, informal rate limiting, implicit priority ordering — visible in inter-agent channel traces and correlated with specific failure classes.
project_ideas.measurement: Prevalence of detected emergent-management patterns and their correlation with recurring failures (duplicated work, livelock, starvation) relative to the orchestrated control.
project_ideas.name: Emergent Management Detector
project_ideas.poc: Run a swarm of peer agents on a shared task with no orchestrator. Instrument inter-agent channels for latency, drop rate and staleness, then mine traces for deconfliction-like and budget-like patterns and compare against an orchestrated control run.
project_ideas.video_title: Demystifying the Viable System Model: A Practical Approach

project_ideas.based_on: Do not fight the last war
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents that inject retrieved successful trajectories under a distribution shift will score lower than agents that re-derive per-episode, and adding an online shift detector before memory injection will recover most of the gap.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate before vs. after the shift point, regret relative to an oracle re-derivation policy, rate of confidently applied stale playbooks, and change in success when the shift gate is enabled.
project_ideas.name: Last-War Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build paired environments where episode statistics shift at a known point; run three policies with the same base model — top-k trajectory retrieval, rule extraction, and per-episode re-derivation — with and without a shift-gated injection step. Log every injected exemplar and whether it was subsequently contradicted.
project_ideas.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk

project_ideas.based_on: Tactics alone leads to 'tactical hell'
project_ideas.hypothesis: A two-tier agent with an explicit fast reactive controller plus a slow elevation layer that rewrites objectives will outperform a single-loop agent of equal per-step reasoning budget on long-horizon tasks, and deliberation spend will pay off only above a measurable stakes/latency threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Long-horizon task success, variance of action distribution (thrash proxy), number of goal rewrites per episode, and net payoff of deliberation as a function of stakes and time budget.
project_ideas.name: Tier-Boundary Router
project_ideas.poc: Implement both agents on an identical task suite. Instrument the router and sweep the switching criterion across task stakes and time budgets, counting the number of objective rewrites and the total cost paid at the tier boundary.
project_ideas.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk

project_ideas.based_on: tactical defeat that became a strategic victory
project_ideas.hypothesis: Optimizing a well-chosen operative metric alone will invert outcomes relative to an independently scored governing objective on tasks engineered to contain a Tet-Offensive-style level shift, and this inversion will be detectable only by the higher-level scorer.
project_ideas.measurement: Operative metric vs. governing objective correlation across iterations, fraction of iterations where the two move in opposite directions, and detection latency of the inversion by each scorer.
project_ideas.name: Inverting-Metric Harness
project_ideas.poc: Define per-task metric hierarchies with a separately measured governing objective; train or route one arm on the operative metric and one on the hierarchical objective; check whether the operative-metric arm improves locally while regressing on the governing objective.
project_ideas.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk

project_ideas.based_on: understanding the culture and social environment of the opponent
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents maintaining a persistent, refreshed counterparty/context model (norms, incentives, social environment) will outperform agents treating the environment as a generic interface in multi-agent scenarios, and stale counterparty models will degrade performance in the same way stale playbooks do.
project_ideas.measurement: Negotiation/coordination outcome quality, number of plan revisions attributable to counterparty evidence, and performance decay of the frozen model as opponent behavior drifts.
project_ideas.name: Counterparty Model Injection
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a persistent context artifact that conditions plan selection in agent-vs-agent scenarios; run an ablation with the artifact frozen at t0 versus continuously refreshed, against a no-model baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk

project_ideas.based_on: Can boundary judgments be encoded as an explicit, versioned, machine-checkable artifact
project_ideas.hypothesis: Scope diffs in a versioned scope manifest predict failure-class regressions in an eval suite better than version-number-only or prompt-diff tracking; systems with manifest-gated deployments ship fewer scope-induced regressions.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of scope-diff → degraded-eval-class prediction, and delta in scope-induced regression rate between manifest-gated and ungated deployment paths.
project_ideas.name: Scope Manifest with Scope-Diff Eval Triggering
project_ideas.poc: Define a manifest schema (included data, tools, signals, memory scope, excluded items and rationale), wire it to a fixed eval suite, and replay a series of real or injected scope changes to check whether the diff identifies which eval classes degrade.
project_ideas.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023

project_ideas.based_on: emergent behavior comes from interactions rather than components
project_ideas.hypothesis: Defects in the interaction graph (handoff contract violations, schema mismatches, unbounded retry/return paths, routing cycles) correlate with task failures more strongly than per-component quality scores.
project_ideas.measurement: AUC of interaction-graph features vs. component-score baseline for predicting task failure; time-to-root-cause in a debugging trial with and without graph telemetry.
project_ideas.name: Interaction-Graph Telemetry
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a multi-agent pipeline to emit handoffs, message schemas, and retry/return paths as a graph per task run; label failed runs and compare a graph-defect feature set against a per-component score baseline as predictors of failure.
project_ideas.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023

project_ideas.based_on: positioning monitoring and coordination as distinct first-class functions
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent runtime that implements goal setting, resource allocation, decision making, monitoring, and coordination as separately replaceable components detects its own drift and reconciles conflicting subagents faster than a single-loop runtime with folded control, at an acceptable interface overhead.
project_ideas.measurement: Time-to-drift-detection, successful conflict reconciliation rate, and added latency/message overhead of the separated architecture.
project_ideas.name: Five-Function Control Plane
project_ideas.poc: Build two runtimes over the same task family: a monolithic decision loop and a five-component control plane with its own monitoring and coordination interfaces; inject drift and subagent goal conflicts into both.
project_ideas.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023

project_ideas.based_on: Does deliberately widening a system boundary improve outcomes monotonically, or does it introduce new failure modes past some width?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Outcome quality rises with boundary width only up to an inflection point, after which added context and interacting variables introduce new failure modes and degrade net outcome per unit cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Outcome quality and quality-per-cost as functions of boundary width, with the location and stability of the inflection point across task families.
project_ideas.name: Boundary-Width Sweep
project_ideas.poc: On a fixed task family, run a controlled sweep of boundary width (amount of context, number of tools, scope of signals considered), scoring each width on outcome quality and resource cost.
project_ideas.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023

project_ideas.based_on: Bad design can be detected with concrete, objective red flags
project_ideas.hypothesis: An automated design critic using objective red-flag detectors (long methods, deep nesting, information leakage) achieves >80% recall and <20% false-positive rate against expert design review on a corpus of AI-generated code.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision, recall, and F1 against expert judgment; number of revision iterations to reach zero red flags; change in expert-rated design quality after automated review.
project_ideas.name: RedFlag Reviewer
project_ideas.poc: Curate 200 code snippets (100 expert-flagged bad, 100 good). Implement detectors for long methods, deep nesting, and information leakage. Compare classifications to expert labels. Then integrate into a generate–review–revise loop to measure iteration count to clean.
project_ideas.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL

project_ideas.based_on: interface complexity is the cost and the useful functionality hidden behind it is the benefit
project_ideas.hypothesis: Consolidating agent tools into fewer, more general schemas (deep tools) increases task success rate and reduces selection latency compared to equivalent shallow, specialized tool sets.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, number of tool calls, token usage, and error rate of incorrect tool selection.
project_ideas.name: DeepTool Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build two versions of a tool suite for a multi-step agent task (e.g., file manipulation): one with 10 specialized tools (insertChar, backspace, deleteSelection), one with 3 general tools (insert, delete, replace). Run an LLM agent on the same 100 tasks and compare.
project_ideas.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL

project_ideas.based_on: Which software design principles transfer to non-code artifacts
project_ideas.hypothesis: Software design principles (deep interfaces, general-purpose operations, red flags) predict quality and success of non-code artifacts: agent tool schemas, prompt templates, and multi-agent topologies.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between design metrics and task success, latency, token cost; expert ratings of design quality.
project_ideas.name: Design Transfer Matrix
project_ideas.poc: Define metrics for interface complexity, generality, and red flags on tool schemas and prompts. Correlate with task success across 50 agent tasks using different prompt/tool designs.
project_ideas.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL

project_ideas.based_on: Investing 10-20% extra time today on design pays back significantly in the long run.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A 10–20% upfront design investment in agent tool surfaces and prompts yields net positive cumulative capability over a 3-month horizon compared to tactical shipping.
project_ideas.measurement: Cumulative capability (features delivered minus rework cost) at 1, 2, and 3 months; crossover point where strategic exceeds tactical.
project_ideas.name: Strategic Design Accounting
project_ideas.poc: Simulate two teams building the same agent pipeline: one tactical (ship ASAP), one strategic (spend 15% on design). Measure cumulative features and bug fixes over simulated project timeline with injected complexity costs.
project_ideas.video_title: Can Great Programmers Be Taught? - John Ousterhout - Agile LnL

project_ideas.based_on: Complex systems are defined by interactions between components, not the components themselves
project_ideas.hypothesis: Varying message contracts or feedback rules in a multi-agent task loop produces a larger change in end-to-end failure rate than varying individual agent prompts or models over comparable engineering effort.
project_ideas.measurement: Effect size on task success or failure rate across intervention sweeps, normalised by intervention cost.
project_ideas.name: Interaction-Layer Failure Attribution
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal task-driven multi-agent system with swappable agents and interaction modes. Run sweeps: keep agents fixed and alter interaction topology or shared-context policy; then keep interactions fixed and alter one agent.
project_ideas.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving

project_ideas.based_on: Stable-looking systems can collapse rapidly when positive feedback loops push them to the edge of chaos
project_ideas.hypothesis: A retry/load feedback model of an agent workload shows critical slowing down (rising autocorrelation and variance) before catastrophic failure and outperforms static latency alarms in lead time at equal false-alarm rate.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection lead time, false-positive rate, and AUC compared with static latency or error-rate thresholds.
project_ideas.name: Runaway-Feedback Collapse Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Build a Python or NetLogo simulation where failing agents retry and publish load; increase request rate until collapse. Compute lag-1 autocorrelation and variance on a system-state time series.
project_ideas.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving

project_ideas.based_on: Emergence of full racial segregation from mild individual preferences.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A low-tolerance local 'copy what neighbours use' rule will produce an extremely concentrated tool or prompt distribution above a sharp threshold, whereas below that threshold the same rule leaves high diversity.
project_ideas.measurement: Herfindahl-Hirschman Index and discontinuity slope over threshold sweeps, plus critical threshold width.
project_ideas.name: Agent Monoculture Phase-Transition Probe
project_ideas.poc: Implement an agent-based model of agents choosing among tools where each agent mildly prefers the tool used by a majority of its neighbours; sweep tolerance threshold and graph rewiring; visualise concentration.
project_ideas.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving

project_ideas.based_on: Agent-based modelling provides understanding of emergent behavior without high predictive accuracy.
project_ideas.hypothesis: When an agent workflow is changed by a single interaction rule, ABM-based parameter fitting identifies the changed rule more accurately than black-box LLM or trace explanations, while black-box prediction forecasts the new outcome more accurately than the ABM alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Forecast error for the predictor and top-1 root-cause accuracy for each explanation path.
project_ideas.name: Diagnose-a-Shift: Black-Box vs Mechanistic Root-Cause Harness
project_ideas.poc: Generate logs from an ABM with known interaction rules, train a black-box sequence predictor, then create shifted logs by changing one rule. Ask each diagnostic path to localise the changed rule and forecast outcomes.
project_ideas.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving

project_ideas.based_on: Counting negatives in a loop determines loop polarity
project_ideas.hypothesis: An LLM-based causal graph extractor can classify logged agent loops as reinforcing or balancing with >80% agreement with human coders.
project_ideas.measurement: F1 score / agreement with human labels; predictive accuracy of runaway vs. stable outcomes.
project_ideas.name: LoopPolarity
project_ideas.poc: Collect traces from a multi-agent simulation, use an LLM to build causal graphs from the traces, compute loop polarity by counting negative links, and compare to human annotations.
project_ideas.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World

project_ideas.based_on: stocks accumulate over time and have memory
project_ideas.hypothesis: Explicit outflow policies (summarization/eviction) in a long-horizon agent improve task success and bound context growth compared to append-only logs.
project_ideas.measurement: Task completion rate, context utilization, and redundancy/irrelevant content ratio.
project_ideas.name: StockFlow Memory Manager
project_ideas.poc: Build an agent with a memory manager exposing inflow (add) and outflow (summarize/forget) knobs; benchmark on a long-horizon task with two policies: append-only vs. managed stock.
project_ideas.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World

project_ideas.based_on: Failing to account for delays leads to overshooting and policy resistance
project_ideas.hypothesis: Inserting a configurable observation wait after actions, based on estimated environmental delay, reduces oscillatory behavior and wasted tool calls in interactive environments.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of corrective actions, oscillation amplitude, and task success rate.
project_ideas.name: DelayAware Agent Controller
project_ideas.poc: In a simulated environment with adjustable delay, run an agent with and without delay dampening and compare corrective action counts and stability.
project_ideas.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World

project_ideas.based_on: Decision-makers operate based on mental models that filter information and shape actions
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents that state assumptions before acting and reconcile them with observed outcomes show lower policy resistance and fewer repeated mistakes.
project_ideas.measurement: Prediction calibration, repeated error rate, and decision revision frequency.
project_ideas.name: Mental Model Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent to emit explicit predictions before each tool use; after outcomes, store mismatches and feed them back into subsequent decisions; compare to a baseline agent without this loop.
project_ideas.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World

project_ideas.based_on: Continuous flow approximation works extremely well in queuing applications
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a queuing/agent-throughput scenario, an aggregate continuous approximation yields lower end-to-end decision error than a per-event discrete trace below a definable arrival-rate threshold, where the discrete representation amplifies arrival-measurement noise.
project_ideas.measurement: Decision error versus ground truth as a function of arrival rate and queue length; the arrival-rate value at which the error ordering inverts, with confidence intervals over seeds.
project_ideas.name: Granularity Crossover Bench
project_ideas.poc: Build paired continuous and discrete implementations of the same throughput scenario with seeded noisy arrival measurements, then evaluate both against ground truth across a sweep of arrival rates and queue depths.
project_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski

project_ideas.based_on: Building a model using an outside-in approach helps distinguish exogenous constants from endogenous variables
project_ideas.hypothesis: A tool runtime where each unit/type is declared once and inherited structurally through the derivation graph blocks more integration defects at construction time, and leaks fewer to runtime, than per-call schema validation — but only until the unit vocabulary grows heterogeneous enough to force escape hatches.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of mismatches caught at authoring/construction time versus runtime escape rate, plus blocked-construction events and escape-hatch usage per unit added as the registry scales.
project_ideas.name: Inherited Contract Layer for Tool Orchestration
project_ideas.poc: Implement a minimal orchestration runtime with declared contracts, structural inheritance, and an extensible type registry; run the same task suite against a per-call JSON-schema validation baseline.
project_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski

project_ideas.based_on: Building a model using an outside-in approach helps distinguish exogenous constants from endogenous variables and enforce units
project_ideas.hypothesis: Outside-in authoring (fixed inputs first, derived nodes last) reduces rework and unit-mismatch errors versus unordered authoring when the exogenous/endogenous boundary is known at the start, but its advantage shrinks or inverts when that boundary is initially ambiguous.
project_ideas.measurement: Rework cycles per model, unit/consistency mismatch count, and time-to-first-valid-simulation, compared across cohorts and across boundary-known versus boundary-ambiguous variants.
project_ideas.name: Outside-In Under Boundary Uncertainty
project_ideas.poc: Two authoring cohorts build the same workflow model with a deliberately ambiguous boundary; one uses an outside-in order, the other an unordered order preserving the same final artifact.
project_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski

project_ideas.based_on: Spreadsheets lack clear input/output separation
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent memory substrates without an enforced read/write distinction exhibit a higher rate of stale-read and self-referential-write defects, and those defects are detected less often by standard evaluation than equivalent defects in substrates with enforced separation.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect incidence and defect-detection rate by existing eval suites for each substrate, with detection gap expressed as undetected defects per injected fault.
project_ideas.name: Read/Write Separation Audit for Agent Memory
project_ideas.poc: Implement two memory substrates over identical retrieval logic — one conflating retrieved context with mutated state, one with a hard read/write boundary — then seed equivalent contamination faults in each.
project_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski

project_ideas.based_on: There are nine holistic thinking perspectives analogous to the blind men and the elephant parable.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A rubric that scores explicit coverage of the nine Holistic Thinking Perspectives against a design artifact detects defects that a single-perspective review admits, and artifacts with low perspective coverage fail more often in downstream implementation than artifacts with high coverage.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect detection rate and false-negative rate per review mode, plus correlation between perspective-coverage score and downstream defects; report the number of defects caught only by the multi-perspective mode.
project_ideas.name: Perspective-Coverage Review Gate
project_ideas.poc: Build a scorer that labels each perspective as covered/absent with evidence spans for a corpus of design docs and agent specifications, run paired single-perspective vs. nine-perspective reviews, and track which review flagged defects that later materialized.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering

project_ideas.based_on: Optimizing subsystems independently does not lead to a system optimum
project_ideas.hypothesis: Pipelines whose component metrics are derived from a single system-level objective achieve higher end-to-end task success than otherwise identical pipelines whose components are tuned independently to local metrics.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end task success delta between configurations, plus the gap between summed component scores and measured end-to-end success (local-global divergence).
project_ideas.name: Global-Objective vs. Local-Metric Dial
project_ideas.poc: Take one decomposed agent pipeline, instantiate two configurations (independent per-agent tuning vs. objective-derived component scoring), and run both across a shared task suite with the same components and prompts.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering

project_ideas.based_on: Early stages of problem formulation and conceptualization are missing from standards.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Inserting an explicit, scored intent-formulation stage with misalignment detection before solution work reduces rework and raises intent-alignment scores relative to a process-only workflow that proceeds directly to step execution.
project_ideas.measurement: Rework rate, number of clarification turns, and post-hoc human intent-alignment rating, comparing gate-enabled vs. process-only runs.
project_ideas.name: Intent Formulation Gate
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a front-end stage that restates the user's situation, records open questions, and blocks execution when an alignment threshold is not met; A/B it against a conformance-only workflow on identical tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering

project_ideas.based_on: The human brain can only hold about 7 plus or minus 2 objects at once (Miller's Rule).
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tool schemas and context layouts that expose roughly 6-7 top-level elements per level with hidden internals yield higher model task success than wide flat surfaces exposing many more elements at one level.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate and error-type distribution as a function of top-level element count per level; test whether the curve peaks in the 6-7 band.
project_ideas.name: Interface Fan-Out Sweep
project_ideas.poc: Generate the same capability as tool/interface schemas at varying top-level element counts (3, 7, 12, 20) with equivalent underlying functionality, and run the same task set against each layout.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering

project_ideas.based_on: systemic properties only appear at the system level
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding a whole-session evaluation harness that scores final, emergent, ecosystem-level outcomes will catch a class of cascade failures that component-level metrics miss in multi-agent orchestration.
project_ideas.measurement: Detection rate and precision of whole-session vs component-only metrics; number of failure modes visible only at system level; runtime overhead.
project_ideas.name: Emergence Harness: Whole-Session Agent Evaluation
project_ideas.poc: Build a small multi-agent system with interchangeable subagents; run a suite of end-to-end scenarios with injected perturbations; compare aggregated component scores against whole-system outcome scores and list cases where rankings invert.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

project_ideas.based_on: Identified five necessary functions: System 5 (policy/identity), System 4 (intelligence/environment), System 3 (control/overview), System 2 (stability/coordination), and System 1 (sub-systems/operations).
project_ideas.hypothesis: Mapping an existing agent architecture onto VSM and adding a separate environment-scanning/intelligence loop (System 4) will reduce the frequency of surprise failures when task distributions shift, compared to a monolithic baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Surprise failure rate, recovery time after distribution shifts, system survival rate; audit coverage score.
project_ideas.name: VSM-Check: Agentic Viability Audit
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a deployed agent system to identify VSM functions, add a low-frequency scanning subsystem that watches environment changes, and run long-duration simulations with variable task distributions.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

project_ideas.based_on: How we draw the line between the system and the environment is a matter of judgement.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Making an agent's context and tool scope an explicit, versioned boundary register that stakeholders can review yields fewer harmful exclusions than an implementation-chosen, static scope, while adding acceptable latency.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of relevant stakeholders/sources missing from final output; false inclusion rate; setup/review time.
project_ideas.name: GateHouse: Boundary Board for Agent Scopes
project_ideas.poc: Implement an agent that loads tools and context sources from an auditable scope file; present scenarios where key stakeholders or data sources are outside the default scope; compare explicit review vs static default.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

project_ideas.based_on: PSMs offer a way of representing situations to enable participants to clarify predicaments, converge on actionable issues, and agree on commitments.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For ambiguous, multi-stakeholder task requests, an agent that first elicits and checks a rich picture/causal map will increase participant commitment and reduce plan rework versus an agent that solves from the raw request.
project_ideas.measurement: User-rated shared understanding and commitment score, rework rate, final task success, dialogue overhead.
project_ideas.name: RichPicture Agent: Structure-Before-Solve Planner
project_ideas.poc: Build two variants of a planner for unstructured tasks; one converts the request directly into a plan, the other runs a mapping and elicitation dialogue first; conduct A/B tests with users.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

project_ideas.based_on: four-valued answer schema
project_ideas.hypothesis: Models using a four-valued schema (yes/no/it depends/don't know) will show a lower false-commitment rate on ambiguous inputs than those using binary or probability-threshold schemas, without a significant drop in accuracy on unambiguous inputs.
project_ideas.measurement: False-commitment rate, overall accuracy, and calibration on ambiguous vs unambiguous subsets.
project_ideas.name: Ambiguity-Aware Output Contracts
project_ideas.poc: Build a benchmark of deliberately ambiguous yes/no questions, run the same model under three output contracts (binary, probability-threshold, four-valued), and score false commitments and overall accuracy.
project_ideas.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

project_ideas.based_on: STALL is a pre-action deliberation gate
project_ideas.hypothesis: Inserting a mandatory pre-action stage that restates the situation and asks interrogative prompts reduces premature wrong actions in agent loops, with a quantifiable latency/token cost that is outweighed by success rate gains on complex tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end success rate, number of premature tool calls, latency, token spend.
project_ideas.name: STALL Gate: Pre-Action Deliberation for Agents
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent framework with and without a STALL-inspired pre-action step, then compare on tasks with known failure modes of reactivity.
project_ideas.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

project_ideas.based_on: fixed perspective checklist (HTP-style)
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent context-gathering stage that uses a fixed HTP-style perspective checklist will miss fewer required facts on complex tasks than an unstructured 'be thorough' instruction, measured by missed-fact rate, with moderate token overhead.
project_ideas.measurement: Missed-fact rate, token cost, time.
project_ideas.name: Perspective Enumeration Harness (HTP Ablation)
project_ideas.poc: Create tasks with a known set of required facts, run two context-gathering strategies (checklist vs unstructured), and measure coverage.
project_ideas.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

project_ideas.based_on: unstated premises
project_ideas.hypothesis: An LLM-based reviewer trained to extract unstated premises from generated arguments can achieve precision/recall above 0.7 against human-annotated implicit assumptions, making it a viable automated critical thinking step.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision, recall, F1.
project_ideas.name: Premise Probe: Unstated Assumption Extractor
project_ideas.poc: Build a premise-extraction pipeline, evaluate on a dataset of arguments with annotated hidden assumptions.
project_ideas.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

project_ideas.based_on: 99% of all requirements we see right now in most of our system designs are not verifiable
project_ideas.hypothesis: An authoring-time linter that rejects agent task descriptions and tool contracts lacking an observable predicate, unit, or verification method will reduce the proportion of unverifiable specs by at least 50% compared with human review alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of specs flagged per category; reduction in unverifiable specs after linter feedback; inter-rater agreement between linter and human reviewers on verifiability judgments.
project_ideas.name: Agent Requirement Linter
project_ideas.poc: Build a rule-based and LLM-assisted linter over YAML/JSON agent specs that flags unverifiable phrases, missing units, and absent verification methods; run it on a sample of 100 agent task specs and tool contracts; require authors to address flags before merge.
project_ideas.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019

project_ideas.based_on: Every tier must have direct/allocated and derived requirements
project_ideas.hypothesis: Mapping agent components onto a fixed multi-tier ladder with allocated and derived requirements at each tier will reduce the number of mis-tiered constants and lower change propagation cost compared with an ad-hoc layer assignment.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of mis-tiered constants before and after refactor; number of files changed when swapping a low-tier parameter; traceability coverage of allocated and derived requirements per tier.
project_ideas.name: Tier Ladder Mapper for Agent Pipelines
