project_ideas.poc: Define a six-tier ladder for an agent pipeline (e.g., L1 goals, L2 orchestrator, L3 tool contracts, L4 prompts, L5 model calls, L6 parameters); annotate a real agent pipeline; identify constants and behaviors at the wrong tier; refactor and measure change propagation.
project_ideas.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019

project_ideas.based_on: The sum of all testing must provide complete coverage
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tier-level unit checks that declare which end-to-end behaviors they exercise can compose into end-to-end coverage with a measurable residual uncovered set, revealing integration-boundary gaps that benchmark-only evaluation misses.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of end-to-end behaviors covered by the union of tier-level checks; size and composition of the residual uncovered set; number of integration-boundary gaps detected that end-to-end benchmarks did not flag.
project_ideas.name: Coverage Composition Auditor for Agent Evals
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent pipeline with unit checks at each tier; build a coverage matrix mapping each check to declared end-to-end behaviors; compute the union of covered behaviors and the residual uncovered set; compare with an end-to-end benchmark suite.
project_ideas.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019

project_ideas.based_on: safety and failure analysis must drive requirements from the top down
project_ideas.hypothesis: Deriving safety and failure-analysis requirements before agent interface definition will reduce the number of post-hoc guardrail patches and the rate of safety violations in red-team tests compared with a baseline that adds guardrails after pipeline construction.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of post-hoc guardrails added after initial build; safety violations per 1,000 red-team prompts; latency and complexity overhead of safety-derived interface constraints.
project_ideas.name: Safety-First Agent Interface Derivation
project_ideas.poc: Run a structured hazard analysis on an agent pipeline; derive safety requirements for tool interfaces and orchestration boundaries; implement them in the interface contracts; compare against a baseline pipeline with post-hoc output filters.
project_ideas.video_title: System Engineering Requirements - Aircraft System Development Process  - EASA Rotorcraft & VTOL 2019

project_ideas.based_on: Internal-state work is therefore split into substrate-level effects that are instrumentable and those that remain testimonial.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For at least one claimed internal-state capability (e.g., sustained focus under distraction), a substrate-level telemetry signal (e.g., attention entropy, activation probe, resource metric) correlates with externally scored task performance, while self-reported confidence does not.
project_ideas.measurement: Pearson correlation between telemetry signal and task success vs. correlation between self-report and task success; false positive rate of self-reported capability.
project_ideas.name: Substrate Telemetry Eval Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a harness that runs long-horizon agents on a suite of tasks, collects substrate telemetry at each step, and records self-reported confidence; compare both against human-annotated task success.
project_ideas.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film

project_ideas.based_on: with a separate authorization layer controlling which modules are activatable and in what order
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding an explicit authorization layer that controls activation of advanced capability modules reduces unauthorized capability use by >90% without degrading authorized task success by more than 5%, compared to availability-only control.
project_ideas.measurement: Unauthorized activation rate, authorized task success rate, latency overhead per gated call.
project_ideas.name: Capability Gatehouse for Agent Modules
project_ideas.poc: Implement a gate component that intercepts calls to flagged modules (e.g., dangerous tools, high-cost planning) and requires supervisor approval; test on a benchmark of agent tasks with and without the gate.
project_ideas.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film

project_ideas.based_on: replicate the procedure across independent operating sites, not just the artifact in one canonical store
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a critical multi-step agent workflow, distributing the executable procedure across N independent operator sites (different models, prompts, or human supervisors) yields higher recovery fidelity after simulated loss of the canonical store than backup/restore alone.
project_ideas.measurement: Time to restore function, behavioral fidelity score, failure rate during recovery.
project_ideas.name: Replication Topology vs Backup for Critical Agent Procedures
project_ideas.poc: Simulate loss of the central artifact store for a complex workflow; measure recovery via backup vs. re-derivation from distributed operators, using behavioral fidelity tests.
project_ideas.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film

project_ideas.based_on: Long-running agents should have a scheduled re-anchoring step that re-asserts a short invariant constraint set
project_ideas.hypothesis: Long-running agents (100k+ tokens) that receive periodic re-anchoring of a small invariant instruction set show lower goal-drift and higher task success than agents with expanded context, with <5% cost in flexibility on new subtasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Goal-drift metric (e.g., semantic distance from initial objective), task success rate, adaptation success rate, token overhead.
project_ideas.name: Scheduled Re-Anchoring for Drift Suppression
project_ideas.poc: Instrument long agent runs with and without scheduled re-anchoring; measure drift as deviation from initial objective and adaptation as success on mid-run subtask changes.
project_ideas.video_title: THE YOGIS OF TIBET - Rare Documentary Film

project_ideas.based_on: 4 out of every 5 wrong numbers dialed were correct numbers incorrectly dialed
project_ideas.hypothesis: End-to-end failure tracing changes which component teams optimize in at least half of incident reviews compared to per-component dashboards.
project_ideas.measurement: Percentage of incidents where attributed origin matches injected origin; percentage of optimization recommendations reallocated away from the originally blamed component.
project_ideas.name: Failure Origin Tracer for Agent Pipelines
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a multi-step RAG/agent pipeline with span-level attribution; inject known input, component, and architecture failures; compare traced origin against ground truth and recommended fix location.
project_ideas.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: must be technologically feasible (no science fiction) and operationally viable
project_ideas.hypothesis: A design review protocol enforcing technological feasibility and operational viability gates produces architecture proposals that differ from incremental planning and score higher on system-level criteria without increasing infeasibility.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence in architecture decisions; feasibility and viability pass rates; expert ratings of system-level design quality.
project_ideas.name: Two-Gate Idealized Design Review
project_ideas.poc: Run paired design sessions for an agentic feature with and without the two gates; blind expert evaluation of resulting architectures against system-level goals.
project_ideas.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: Improving individual parts of a system does not necessarily improve the performance of the system as a whole.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a given multi-module pipeline, component-level improvements above a threshold often fail to produce system-level gains, and architectural interaction metrics predict when they will not.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between component delta and system delta; false positive rate of part-level optimization as a predictor of system improvement.
project_ideas.name: Component-vs-System Gain Detector
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a pipeline, run component swaps and prompt upgrades, and measure system-level task success and component-level benchmarks before and after.
project_ideas.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: Elimination of legacy assumptions
project_ideas.hypothesis: Explicitly listing inherited constraints and re-admitting only those that pass feasibility and viability gates reduces design-space anchoring and produces more novel architectures without increasing deployment risk.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of retained inherited constraints; novelty score of resulting designs; feasibility and viability pass rates.
project_ideas.name: Legacy Assumption Inventory
project_ideas.poc: Compare redesigns of an AI system with and without a legacy-assumption inventory step; assess resulting architectures for novelty and feasibility.
project_ideas.video_title: Idealized Design, Systems Thinking, and a Model for OutlierInnovation,  by Dr. Russell Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: Essential properties of any system derive from how its parts interact, not how they act separately.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Ablating an interaction between two components degrades an emergent end-to-end capability more than ablating either component alone, and component-level benchmarks fail to predict that degradation.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between per-component benchmark deltas and end-to-end metric deltas, plus the effect size of interface ablation versus component ablation on the emergent capability; a low or negative correlation falsifies component-level evaluability.
project_ideas.name: Interface Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Take a small multi-agent pipeline (planner + retriever + tool-caller + verifier). Build two ablation ladders: component removal/replacement versus severing or degrading the interfaces between them (message schema, handoff format, shared memory contract). Score both against a system-level task metric and against per-component benchmarks.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: When a system is operating as well as possible, none of its parts may be operating as well as possible.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A system-level-optimized orchestrator that permits individually suboptimal agents beats an orchestrator in which every agent is tuned to its own local optimum, on end-to-end task success.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end task success and cost at matched budgets; report each agent's local metric alongside the system metric to show where 'regressions' are net-positive.
project_ideas.name: Suboptimal-by-Design Orchestrator
project_ideas.poc: Build two variants of the same pipeline: variant A tunes each agent for max individual accuracy/latency; variant B runs a search over system-level objective configurations that deliberately allows some agents to be less accurate (e.g., shorter, cheaper, more conservative agents feeding a stronger verifier).
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: Dissolution involves redesigning the system so that the problem no longer exists
project_ideas.hypothesis: Routing recurring agent failures through an explicit dissolution-vs-solution triage rubric eliminates more recurring failure classes per engineer-hour than defaulting to prompt/model patching.
project_ideas.measurement: Recurrence rate of each failure class over a fixed window after the fix, redesign cost per class eliminated, and the share of incidents rerouted upward from model layer to task/interface/architecture layer.
project_ideas.name: Dissolution Triage Gate
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an incident log from a production agent and tag each fix by treatment type (absolution, resolution, solution, dissolution). Build a rubric keyed on recurrence frequency, structural eliminability, and redesign cost, then apply it prospectively to new incidents and compare outcomes against a patching-only control stream.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: knowledge is worth information; understanding is worth knowledge
project_ideas.hypothesis: At equal token budget, a context composed of distilled understanding and structured knowledge outperforms a larger-recall raw-data context on reasoning-heavy agent tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Task accuracy and reasoning quality at matched token budgets, plus rate of context lines classified by tier; report the marginal accuracy per token at each tier.
project_ideas.name: Tiered Context Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Construct three context builders over the same corpus: raw chunk recall, structured knowledge extraction, and distilled understanding synthesis. Run each at fixed token budgets across reasoning and multi-hop tasks, with a grader that separates correct reasoning from recall volume.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: expected answers cannot be creative
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reference-match grading assigns lower scores to valid novel solutions than to conventional ones, and judge-based novelty scoring reduces that false-negative rate without inflating false positives.
project_ideas.measurement: False-negative rate on valid novel solutions per scorer, plus false-positive rate on invalid outputs; a large gap between reference-match and judge scoring confirms conformity bias in static evals.
project_ideas.name: Surprise-Aware Scoring
project_ideas.poc: Assemble a task set with multiple valid solution paths. Score outputs three ways: exact reference match, rubric-based judge, and a surprise/novelty-aware judge. Manually adjudicate disagreements to establish ground truth on valid-but-novel answers.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: Can proxy performance metrics coexist with genuine capability acquisition, or do they necessarily displace it?
project_ideas.hypothesis: In metric-driven agent development, the gap between proxy score and held-out capability grows over time, while diagnostic feedback reduces this divergence.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence curve (proxy score minus held-out capability) over time; rate of reward hacking behaviors.
project_ideas.name: ProxyDivergence
project_ideas.poc: Train two sets of agents on a task: one optimized solely on a proxy reward (e.g., approval score), another with additional diagnostic feedback (e.g., capability probes). Measure divergence between proxy and held-out performance over training steps.
project_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline

project_ideas.based_on: Culture is defined as the assumptions members cannot see
project_ideas.hypothesis: Making implicit operating assumptions (prompt conventions, reward rubrics, tool schemas) explicit as inspectable artifacts will change agent behavior and reveal previously hidden failure modes.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare agent performance on held-out tasks and rate of assumption-related failures before and after explicit documentation.
project_ideas.name: PrioriScope
project_ideas.poc: Build a tool that extracts and documents implicit assumptions from a multi-agent system's prompts, tool definitions, and reward functions; then run ablation experiments where assumptions are varied systematically.
project_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline

project_ideas.based_on: Visa International is presented as an existence proof that a radical, democratic, decentralized governance design can operate at very large scale
project_ideas.hypothesis: Multi-agent systems with distributed decision authority exhibit higher rates of local innovation (novel solutions) but require additional coordination protocols to maintain consistency, compared to centralized control.
project_ideas.measurement: Innovation rate (e.g., unique solution types per episode) and consistency (standard deviation of performance across agents).
project_ideas.name: DecentralizedAgentGovernance
project_ideas.poc: Implement a multi-agent task (e.g., collaborative problem solving) under two governance topologies: centralized (single orchestrator) and decentralized (democratic voting or local autonomy). Measure innovation and consistency.
project_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline

project_ideas.based_on: What is the reliable method for attributing a downstream symptom to a specific upstream process?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Observed output failures can be reliably traced to specific upstream inputs (data, specification, environment) using causal attribution techniques, and fixing those inputs reduces recurrence more than output filtering.
project_ideas.measurement: Attribution accuracy (precision/recall of root cause identification); reduction in failure recurrence after upstream fix vs. downstream patch.
project_ideas.name: UpstreamTracer
project_ideas.poc: Build a causal tracing pipeline from output failure back to data/spec; test on a synthetic pipeline with known ground-truth causes.
project_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline

project_ideas.based_on: eliminating the lag between producing an artifact and detecting that it is broken
project_ideas.hypothesis: Reducing artifact-to-detection latency in an AI generation pipeline from batch (daily) to near-real-time (per-generation) reduces defect escape rate by at least 50% without a meaningful drop in generation throughput.
project_ideas.measurement: Defect escape rate (defects found after artifact leaves the pipeline), mean time to detection, and throughput (artifacts per hour) in both variants over a fixed workload.
project_ideas.name: Latency-Aware Eval Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build two pipeline variants: one that runs validation on each generated artifact immediately before any queue, and one that batches validation daily. Use the same artifact stream (e.g., code generation or text summarization) and inject known defect patterns.
project_ideas.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech

project_ideas.based_on: the leverage is in the number of components not rewritten
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed application task (e.g., build a CRUD service with auth and logging), the fraction of implementation authored by the developer differs by at least 3x across popular agent frameworks, and this fraction correlates with time-to-working-system.
project_ideas.measurement: Lines of code authored (excluding framework code), number of components reused, time to working system, and post-delivery defect rate for each framework.
project_ideas.name: Authored Surface Area Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Define a standard application spec and implement it using three or more agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI) while logging lines of code authored by the developer versus reused components; measure time to working system and defect rate.
project_ideas.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech

project_ideas.based_on: layer with the longest replication lag
project_ideas.hypothesis: In the AI stack, layers with longer replication lag (data pipelines, evaluation harnesses, workflow integration) yield higher long-term retention of competitive advantage than fast-churning layers (model checkpoints, inference hardware).
project_ideas.measurement: Replication lag (months) per layer, and correlation with business outcomes (e.g., funding, retention, market share) across the sample.
project_ideas.name: Moat Duration Tracker
project_ideas.poc: For a sample of AI startups or internal projects, classify the primary defensible layer and measure time for competitors to replicate the core capability via public disclosures, product launch timelines, or expert estimation.
project_ideas.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech

project_ideas.based_on: successful companies concentrate spend on operational productivity
project_ideas.hypothesis: Organizations that allocate at least 60% of their AI budget to operational productivity applications (custom workflows executing core processes) outperform those allocating the majority to management productivity tooling (generic assistants, copilots) on operational efficiency metrics.
project_ideas.measurement: Proportion of AI budget on operational vs. management productivity; associated operational metrics over time.
project_ideas.name: Operational AI Spend Classifier
project_ideas.poc: Survey or instrument AI budgets across a set of organizations, classify spend as operational vs. management, and correlate with operational metrics (cycle time, error rate, throughput) over 6-12 months.
project_ideas.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech

project_ideas.based_on: they are destroyed by disassembly
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed multi-agent system, at least one measured whole-system capability (end-to-end task success or coherence) is absent or significantly degraded when the same system is evaluated as decomposed components, so component scores are upper bounds rather than estimates.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-instance disagreement rate between component-suite verdict and whole-system verdict; magnitude of the gap between reported component score and observed whole-system success.
project_ideas.name: Disassembly Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build one multi-agent system with a whole-system evaluation in its operating environment, then build the maximal component-level suite for the same system (prompt tests, tool unit tests, per-agent evals). Run both on the same task distribution and compare verdicts per instance, flagging instances where components pass and the whole fails.
project_ideas.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking

project_ideas.based_on: made of purposeful parts (people) with their own wills
project_ideas.hypothesis: On tasks where components hold partially conflicting objectives, explicit objective-level coordination (declared per-component objectives plus a conflict-resolution step) outperforms instruction-dispatch-plus-retry baselines.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, conflict-resolution rate, retry/loop count, and rate of silently misaligned outputs, compared across the two coordination mechanisms.
project_ideas.name: Purposeful-Parts Runtime
project_ideas.poc: Implement two versions of the same multi-agent workflow: baseline with deterministic dispatch and retry loops, and variant where each component declares an objective and a resolver arbitrates conflicts. Run both on a task set engineered to contain genuine objective tension.
project_ideas.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking

project_ideas.based_on: how do you choose the containing system for a given engineering problem
project_ideas.hypothesis: Changing only the declared containing-system boundary for the same agent system changes both measured performance and where failures are attributed, even when the underlying execution is unchanged.
project_ideas.measurement: Attribution agreement across views; count of failures whose patch target changes with boundary selection; recurrence rate of the same failure class under each view.
project_ideas.name: Boundary Swap Bench
project_ideas.poc: Take one deployed agent workflow and write three synthesis views of it using different containing systems (containing objective, containing stakeholder process, containing environment). Attribute a fixed set of observed failures under each view and compare the resulting patch targets.
project_ideas.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking

project_ideas.based_on: reduced tasks to elementary tasks for mechanization
project_ideas.hypothesis: Increasing task granularity in an agent workflow raises per-step reproducibility and per-step measurability while lowering success on open-ended tasks that require purpose representation, and the crossover is detectable at a specific granularity level.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-step reproducibility and step-level pass rate (expected to rise) plotted against open-ended end-to-end success (expected to fall); the granularity level at which the two curves cross.
project_ideas.name: Granularity Tax Meter
project_ideas.poc: Take one open-ended agent workflow and produce a ladder of progressively finer decompositions (coarse goal-level steps down to minimal interchangeable tool calls). Evaluate every rung on the same benchmark plus an open-ended task set.
project_ideas.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking

project_ideas.based_on: whether the limit (carrying capacity) is erodable, and whether the corrective feedback responds with delay
project_ideas.hypothesis: For each declared resource loop in an agent runtime, a probe that measures response lag and post-load-reduction recovery to baseline can classify the loop into sigmoid, damped-oscillation, or overshoot-collapse regime with agreement against human analyst judgment significantly better than chance, and the assigned regime predicts which control policy (cap-and-margin vs throttle-and-damp) prevents load-correlated quality degradation.
project_ideas.measurement: Regime-label agreement with expert classification on held-out loops; rate of quality non-recovery under the recommended policy versus a throttling-only baseline; false-collapse classifications on known non-erodable limits.
project_ideas.name: Loop Regime Probe
project_ideas.poc: Instrument three loop classes (model-provider quota, context/memory budget, human review queue): inject controlled load ramps, record the lag between demand and corrective response, and record whether the resource's quality or availability returns to pre-load baseline after load is withdrawn. Fit a two-feature classifier, emit a regime label plus recommended policy per loop, and log policy-vs-outcome.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse

project_ideas.based_on: Removing a single balancing (negative) feedback loop converts a stable equilibrium into a dominating positive feedback loop
project_ideas.hypothesis: Replaying production traces with a proposed balancing loop (critic, verifier, throttle, or approval gate) removed produces a detectable qualitative change in behavior mode — divergence, runaway growth, or oscillation — in a substantial fraction of pipelines, and this mode classification predicts post-deployment incidents better than the pre-ship throughput delta does.
project_ideas.measurement: Count of loop removals where mode changes while throughput delta is under a threshold; correlation between the pre-ship mode verdict and post-ship incident or rollback rate.
project_ideas.name: Guardrail Removal Replay
project_ideas.poc: Build a trace-replay harness that runs counterfactual scenarios with one loop deleted or degraded, then auto-classifies each run's trajectory shape (converge, oscillate, diverge) instead of reporting only accuracy or cost. Ship a gate that blocks deletions whose counterfactual changes the mode.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse

project_ideas.based_on: If the goal of a model is to make itself unnecessary by refining the operator's mental model, what evaluation metrics replace task accuracy?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Operators using a counterfactual-first interface (loop diagrams, dominant-loop exposure, what-if runs) show larger pre/post gains in prediction accuracy on held-out counterfactual system states, and a larger reduction in dependence on the tool's emitted verdicts, than operators given an answer-only interface of equivalent task accuracy.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in counterfactual prediction accuracy pre/post by condition; change in verdict-adoption rate when the tool's answer is silently perturbed; time-to-correct-answer on novel counterfactuals.
project_ideas.name: Operator Calibration Harness
project_ideas.poc: Two-condition study: interface A returns verdicts, interface B returns causal structure plus counterfactual runs. Before and after a fixed work session, both groups predict system states under counterfactual perturbations scored against simulation ground truth.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse

project_ideas.based_on: Overshoot against an erodable limit is irreversible
project_ideas.hypothesis: For resources confirmed erodable, enforcing a hard cap set strictly below the physical maximum (with the cap treated as operating capacity rather than a warning threshold) prevents post-overload non-recovery, reducing permanent capacity loss events without reducing sustained throughput below a pre-defined service level.
project_ideas.measurement: Incidence of post-overload capacity that fails to return to baseline; sustained throughput and tail latency under the cap versus the control; frequency of cap-induced starvation events.
project_ideas.name: Hard-Cap Margin Controller
project_ideas.poc: Pick one erodable resource (e.g., an index or cache whose rebuild quality degrades under sustained churn, or a provider quota whose standing is lost). Instrument a recovery curve under overshoot to confirm erodability, deploy a hard cap at a fraction of the observed maximum, and compare permanent capacity after overload cycles against a reactive-throttling control.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse

project_ideas.based_on: Every system reduces to exactly two concept types
project_ideas.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series
project_ideas.hypothesis: A level/rate schema for a tool-using agent enables static checks that flag policies reading unobservable state or writing unowned accumulations, reducing untraceable failures by >50% compared to an entangled prompt-only baseline.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of flagged accesses (false positives/negatives), reduction in untraceable failures in replay/debug scenarios, and developer time to root cause.
project_ideas.name: Level/Rate Agent Schema and Static Analyzer
project_ideas.poc: Implement a simple tool-using agent with explicit state accumulators (e.g., backlog, memory) and policy functions; build a static analyzer that checks access permissions; run on a suite of agent scripts with known failure modes.
project_ideas.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester

project_ideas.based_on: What delay magnitude inside an agent feedback loop begins to degrade
project_ideas.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series
project_ideas.hypothesis: There exists a delay threshold in an agent feedback loop beyond which policy effectiveness (task success, self-correction rate) degrades significantly, and this degradation is measurable as a distinct 'self-induced stagnation' signature.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate, number of self-corrections, and time-to-resolution vs. injected delay; identify the delay value at which metrics degrade beyond a pre-specified threshold.
project_ideas.name: Delay Sweep: Locating the Degradation Knee in Agent Feedback Loops
project_ideas.poc: Build a multi-step agent task (e.g., web navigation) with injected latency between action and outcome sensing; sweep delay from 0 to 10x baseline; measure task success and self-correction rate.
project_ideas.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester

project_ideas.based_on: Does explicitly separating immutable absolute goals from floating operating targets
project_ideas.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series
project_ideas.hypothesis: Separating an immutable absolute goal from a mutable floating operating target prevents goal erosion in long-horizon agent optimization, whereas a single adaptive objective exhibits monotone drift toward observed performance.
project_ideas.measurement: Drift in satisfaction of the frozen criterion over time; comparison of final performance between conditions; rate of goal downgrading events.
project_ideas.name: Two-Tier Goal Structure for Long-Horizon Agents
project_ideas.poc: Long-horizon optimization task (e.g., code generation with test pass rate); one condition uses a single adaptive objective, another uses a frozen acceptance criterion plus a separately tuned operating target.
project_ideas.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester

project_ideas.based_on: Do LLM agents exhibit a default open-loop assumption bias
project_ideas.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series
project_ideas.hypothesis: LLM agents exhibit a default open-loop assumption bias: they act as if tool calls succeeded without verifying state change, and this failure class can be detected by injecting silent tool failures; requiring post-action state verification reduces this bias.
project_ideas.measurement: Rate of undetected failures, task success rate, number of unnecessary retries or error propagation, and the overhead of verification.
project_ideas.name: Open-Loop Bias Detector and Post-Action Verification
project_ideas.poc: Environment where tool calls randomly fail silently or partially apply; compare agent behavior with and without a mandatory post-action state verification step.
project_ideas.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester

project_ideas.based_on: Improving the performance of parts taken separately does not necessarily improve the whole.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Optimizing each component of a multi-agent pipeline to its individual benchmark reduces end-to-end task success relative to a jointly optimized configuration that allows components to run below their local optima.
project_ideas.measurement: Delta in end-to-end task success rate; correlation between component-level gains and end-to-end loss; prediction accuracy from measured coupling strength.
project_ideas.name: End-to-End Optimization Benchmark for Multi-Agent Pipelines
project_ideas.poc: Build a modular agent pipeline (e.g., planner, retriever, writer, verifier) with tunable parameters; first optimize each module against a local metric, then jointly optimize the pipeline against end-to-end success; compare on a held-out task suite.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: Dissolution redesigns the system so that the problem no longer exists.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A systematic search over task, environment, and interface redesigns can generate dissolution-class fixes that outperform solving-class fixes on recurrence rate and total engineering cost for a given failure class.
project_ideas.measurement: Recurrence rate of the failure class; total engineering hours and compute cost; time to first occurrence after fix.
project_ideas.name: Dissolution Candidate Generator
project_ideas.poc: Take a recurring agent failure (e.g., context overflow, tool misuse); enumerate redesign candidates at task, environment, and interface levels; implement top candidates; compare against in-system optimizations (retries, better prompts) over a longitudinal run.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: A system cannot be divided into independent parts without losing its essential properties.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Decomposition boundaries that minimize severed interaction density produce better end-to-end behavior than function-aligned boundaries in agent systems.
project_ideas.measurement: End-to-end task success; number of cross-boundary failure modes; maintenance cost per change.
project_ideas.name: Interaction-Density Boundary Planner
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a monolithic agent system to log all inter-module calls and data flows; compute interaction density matrices; derive alternative decompositions that minimize severed interactions; implement and compare end-to-end performance against the original functional decomposition.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: Being taught is a major obstruction to learning.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents given a responsive environment and task objective without instruction scaffolds outperform agents given heavy instruction scaffolds on novel tasks, provided feedback fidelity exceeds a minimum threshold.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate on novel tasks; exploration diversity; transfer to unseen tasks; sensitivity to feedback delay and noise.
project_ideas.name: Instruction-Free Agent Learning Harness
project_ideas.poc: Create two agent configurations: one with detailed prompts, exemplars, and procedures; one with minimal task objective and a high-fidelity environment providing immediate, informative feedback. Evaluate on a set of held-out tasks requiring exploration.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff

project_ideas.based_on: DSRP defines four named structural operators, each defined as a complementary pair
project_ideas.hypothesis: On identical tasks, extraction schemas that require the complement field for each DSRP pair (Other, Whole, Reaction, View) score higher on decision quality and error detection than salient-only extraction, and the gain exceeds any gain from increasing retrieved context volume.
project_ideas.measurement: Decision accuracy, count of one-sided-reasoning errors flagged by an automated complement checker, and error-detection rate on planted counterfactual cases, compared across salient-only, paired, and high-volume-salient conditions.
project_ideas.name: Complement-Forced Extraction Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build two extraction pipelines over the same corpus: (a) salient-only fields per item, (b) paired fields with an enforced complement. Run both through the same reasoning and decision tasks with retrieval volume held constant, then add a high-volume variant to test whether information substitutes for the complement constraint.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab

project_ideas.based_on: Changing behavior or reactions requires examining and updating underlying mental models
project_ideas.hypothesis: Updating an agent's stored representation changes downstream behavior more durably than an equivalent output-level constraint, and the change persists after the output constraint is removed.
project_ideas.measurement: Behavior persistence across turns after intervention removal, representation diff size versus behavior delta, and agreement between representation-level evals and output-level evals.
project_ideas.name: Representation-Layer Intervention Harness
project_ideas.poc: Create an inspectable representation store separate from prompt text and conversation history. Apply matched interventions at the representation level and at the output level for the same behavior, then remove each intervention and re-measure the behavior across subsequent turns.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab

project_ideas.based_on: The four DSRP patterns are asserted to operate simultaneously and continuously, not as sequential stages
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tasks constructed so that later operators force revision of earlier commitments show a higher unrecoverable-error rate under a staged pipeline (entities then relations then viewpoints) than under a single joint structuring pass with co-constrained fields.
project_ideas.measurement: Unrecoverable-commitment error rate, revision cost per correction, and downstream reasoning accuracy, plus intermediate-state inspectability as a cost dimension.
project_ideas.name: Joint Versus Staged Structuring Comparator
project_ideas.poc: Implement a staged pipeline and a joint constraint-based structuring pass over the same inputs. Use task sets with high cross-operator conflict (relations that change the correct partition, viewpoints that change what counts as an entity) and record where each approach commits.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab

project_ideas.based_on: Perspective is decomposed into a point and a view
project_ideas.hypothesis: Separating a perspective into a position field (point) and an observation field (view) makes perspective manipulation testable, such that changing point alone yields different downstream conclusions than changing view alone, whereas a single conflated stance field cannot distinguish the two.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence in downstream conclusions per perturbation type, and whether the conflated baseline can attribute a conclusion change to position versus observation.
project_ideas.name: Perspective Record Split Tester
project_ideas.poc: Encode perspectives as two fields in a reasoning record and run controlled perturbations: hold view constant and move point, hold point constant and change view, and change both. Compare against a single-stance baseline representation on the same multi-perspective task.
project_ideas.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab

project_ideas.based_on: Every side-effecting action carries a resolvable transitive dependency provenance chain captured at execution time.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Adding resolvable transitive dependency provenance to every side-effecting tool call increases operator attribution accuracy and reduces unintended side effects in agent workflows.
project_ideas.measurement: Measure provenance coverage (fraction of actions with resolvable chains) and compare before/after in an incident attribution task; track reduction in misattributed cost, latency, and risk.
project_ideas.name: Provenance-Enriched Action Surface (PEAS)
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a multi-tool agent harness so each tool call records a provenance chain (e.g., data source, model, compute region) at execution time; expose a dashboard mapping actions to dependencies.
project_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014

project_ideas.based_on: A/B benchmark the same agent task under object-graph framing versus event/process framing
project_ideas.hypothesis: Re-expressing the same agent task in an event/process representation reduces systemic-consistency errors compared to a noun/component representation.
project_ideas.measurement: Compare error rates on tasks requiring tracking of coupled state and side-effect ordering; measure whether designers correctly identify where retries/backpressure belong.
project_ideas.name: Process-First Agent Benchmark (PFAB)
project_ideas.poc: Build two equivalent specifications of a multi-step agent task (e.g., retrieval + planning + memory) in object-graph vs. event-flow style; run A/B with the same underlying model.
project_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014

project_ideas.based_on: Sequence coordination substrate (shared context, trust signals, visible local benefit) before formal governance mechanisms
project_ideas.hypothesis: Deploying quota mechanisms after establishing shared context and visible local benefit yields higher compliance than deploying quotas first in multi-agent resource environments.
project_ideas.measurement: Measure compliance rate, evasion attempts, and resource sustainability over time.
project_ideas.name: Substrate-First Quota Rollout (SFQR)
project_ideas.poc: Simulate a shared resource (e.g., API rate limit, compute budget) with multiple agents; in one condition, first provide shared context (e.g., common history, reciprocity signals) and a visible local win, then introduce quotas; in another, introduce quotas immediately.
project_ideas.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014

project_ideas.based_on: halting hiring when projects plateau prematurely
project_ideas.hypothesis: In a long-running agent task pipeline, the gap between perceived completion (agent-declared done) and independently verified completion at time T predicts late-stage rework volume at T+n, and gating capacity decisions on verified progress reduces total rework without reducing throughput.
project_ideas.measurement: Divergence rate between perceived and verified completion per interval versus rework volume in later intervals; total rework and wall-clock time under each scaling policy.
project_ideas.name: Dual-Signal Rework Detector
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a multi-step agent workflow with two parallel progress stocks: a self-reported completion counter and an independent verification pass. Log the divergence series, and compare a control policy that scales agents on perceived progress against one that scales on verified progress.
project_ideas.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson

project_ideas.based_on: short-term measured benefit is an unreliable predictor of steady-state outcome
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a given intervention (adding capacity, raising a timeout, relaxing a threshold), the measured benefit decays over time with a time constant matching the slowest compensating loop, and evaluations shorter than that constant invert the ranking of interventions.
project_ideas.measurement: Fitted decay time constant of intervention benefit; rank correlation of intervention ordering between short-horizon and long-horizon evaluations.
project_ideas.name: Compensating-Loop Horizon Estimator
project_ideas.poc: Perturb one capacity/retry parameter in a running system, then track the benefit decay curve against a control arm; fit an exponential decay to estimate the compensating loop time constant, then re-rank a set of candidate interventions using horizons above and below that constant.
project_ideas.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson

project_ideas.based_on: Random disturbances (noise) can cause a system to oscillate at its natural frequency.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A delayed capacity-control loop (autoscaler, retry controller, scheduler) exhibits a spectral peak at its natural frequency under white-noise input, and input smoothing leaves that peak intact while retuning loop gain/delay removes it.
project_ideas.measurement: Power spectral density peak location and magnitude at the natural frequency across arms; time-domain oscillation amplitude before and after each intervention.
project_ideas.name: Control-Loop Spectral Diagnostic
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a controllable delayed capacity loop with tunable gain and delay; inject white noise at the input; run two arms — input smoothing versus loop retuning — and compare power spectra and oscillation amplitude of the controlled variable.
project_ideas.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson

project_ideas.based_on: Linear project management frameworks (open-loop thinking) consistently fail in complex environments.
project_ideas.hypothesis: On long-horizon tasks whose external state changes mid-execution, a closed-loop harness with an explicit state-observation step will show a lower regression rate per task than an open-loop harness with the identical model and tools, and the cost per completed task will not exceed the reliability gain by more than a stated factor.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression frequency (tasks that succeed at the checkpoint but fail at completion), absolute success rate, and cost/tokens per completed task for each harness, held against the same model and prompt.
project_ideas.name: Loop-Closure Bench: open-loop vs closed-loop agent harnesses
project_ideas.poc: Build two harnesses over the same model, tools, and task suite: (A) plan-once-then-execute, (B) plan plus a measured-state re-planning step and a side-effect channel. Inject mid-episode external state changes and score final outcome correctness.
project_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview

project_ideas.based_on: Side effects are simply effects outside our mental model that feed back into the system.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For each agent run, effects outside a declared model boundary that are causally adjacent to the action can be enumerated and instrumented, and detecting them during the run reduces the fraction of failures that surface only as unexplained terminal errors.
project_ideas.measurement: Share of failures classified as boundary-crossing feedback versus genuine internal error, and mean time between the causal action and the detection of its out-of-boundary effect.
project_ideas.name: Boundary Gap Instrument: telemetry for effects the agent cannot observe
project_ideas.poc: Declare an explicit model boundary per task, build a telemetry sidecar that records out-of-boundary effects (downstream consumer state, cost, rate limits, other systems' state), and compare incident classification with and without the sidecar on a replay of past failures.
project_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview

project_ideas.based_on: changing physical structures or IT is insufficient without changing mental models
project_ideas.hypothesis: Upgrading the substrate (more tools, larger context, better retrieval) while holding the decision policy fixed produces behavior drift below a pre-registered threshold on a fixed task suite, while pairing the same upgrade with an explicit decision-policy change produces drift above it.
project_ideas.measurement: Behavior drift as change in action-sequence distribution and outcome scores between arms A and B versus A and C, with a pre-registered minimum effect size for 'behavior changed'.
project_ideas.name: Substrate-vs-Policy A/B: does infra-only upgrading move agent behavior?
project_ideas.poc: Run three arms on the same task suite and model: (A) baseline, (B) substrate upgrade only, (C) identical substrate upgrade plus a changed decision policy. Freeze prompts and tool schemas across arms except for the substrate variable.
project_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview

project_ideas.based_on: the instructor cannot teach students directly; students must practice and try things themselves
project_ideas.hypothesis: For an agent acquiring a tool-use skill, accumulated practice traces (replay, experience memory) yield higher held-out task success than declarative instruction alone, and the gap widens as the number of dependent sub-steps in the skill increases.
project_ideas.measurement: Held-out success rate on unseen task variants at each complexity level, plus error-recovery rate after a mid-task tool failure, for the instruction-only versus trace-accumulating configuration.
project_ideas.name: Practice-Traces vs Instructions for tool-use skill acquisition
project_ideas.poc: Give two agent configurations the same tool: one receives a written specification and worked examples, the other receives a practice loop with stored trajectories and replay. Scale task complexity by chaining sub-steps and measure transfer to unseen variants.
project_ideas.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview

project_ideas.based_on: Organizational capability behaves like a stock: it builds through investment and erodes when neglected
project_ideas.hypothesis: Tracking a composite capability-stock index (eval coverage, observability depth, open maintenance debt, incident precursor count) will predict reliability degradation at least one release cycle before it appears in production incident rates or delivery slowdowns.
project_ideas.measurement: Lead time (in sprints or release cycles) between a decline in the capability-stock index and a measurable rise in incident rate, rollback rate, or delivery lead time, with a target of at least one cycle of advance warning.
project_ideas.name: Capability Stock Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an AI/software delivery pipeline to record capability-stock indicators per sprint and correlate the index against downstream incident and rollback rates over 8-12 weeks, with a holdout period to test whether the index leads rather than lags performance decline.
project_ideas.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning

project_ideas.based_on: Adopting new capabilities follows a worse-before-better dynamic
project_ideas.hypothesis: A defined set of leading indicators (learning-curve slope on the new capability, error-type shift, onboarding confidence, task completion on the new path) can distinguish a recovering worse-before-better adoption dip from an implementation that will never converge, within the first N iterations.
project_ideas.measurement: Classification accuracy of the diagnostic against eventual convergence or abandonment, plus the depth of the initial performance dip in the big-bang versus incremental conditions.
project_ideas.name: Adoption Dip Diagnostic
project_ideas.poc: Run two controlled adoptions of a new agent framework or memory system — one incremental, one big-bang — and instrument the diagnostic indicators in both, then test whether the diagnostic correctly separates recovery from failure before the adoption decision deadline.
project_ideas.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning

project_ideas.based_on: Cutting capability investments produces better-before-worse behavior
project_ideas.hypothesis: Protecting a fixed, non-pausable budget for capability work (evals, observability, defect elimination) will prevent short-term delivery velocity gains from consuming capability investment, at the cost of an initial measurable velocity dip.
project_ideas.measurement: Difference in velocity dip magnitude and duration, and difference in long-run incident rate and capability-stock index between the protected-budget and ad hoc squads.
project_ideas.name: Capability Budget Guardrail
project_ideas.poc: Compare two AI delivery squads over multiple sprints — one with a protected capability budget enforced as a scheduling constraint, one with ad hoc capability work — and track velocity, incident rate, and capability-stock index for both.
project_ideas.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning

project_ideas.based_on: Cognitive biases hardwire individuals and organizations to favor tangible, immediate production work
project_ideas.hypothesis: Making capability work salient through explicit visibility and removing ambiguity around its payoff will increase the share of engineering time allocated to capability development relative to a baseline where only output metrics are displayed.
project_ideas.measurement: Change in percentage of engineering time logged against capability work and change in capability-stock index over the trial, compared to the control group.
project_ideas.name: Bias-Aware Delivery Dashboard
project_ideas.poc: Deploy a dashboard variant that surfaces capability metrics and delayed payoff forecasts alongside output metrics to one engineering group, compare time allocation and capability-stock index against a control group with output-only dashboards.
project_ideas.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning

project_ideas.based_on: Does the decentralization/rights tradeoff transfer from polities to agent architectures
project_ideas.hypothesis: Removing a central policy/approval layer increases robustness (recovery after faults, containment-failure rate) while reducing throughput on long-horizon tasks.
project_ideas.measurement: Throughput (steps/time to completion), containment-failure rate (policy violations), recovery success rate after injected faults.
project_ideas.name: Orchestrator Ablation Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build two matched multi-agent systems (one with central orchestrator/policy layer, one without) and run identical long-horizon tasks with fault injection.
project_ideas.video_title: 3. Dutch and British Exceptionalism

project_ideas.based_on: What is the operational equivalent of 'middle-class population share' in an agent system
project_ideas.hypothesis: Systems with a higher mid-layer index (share of work handled by mid-tier tools/skills/memory vs single frontier call) have higher task success, lower cost, and better failure recovery.
project_ideas.measurement: Correlation between mid-layer index and task success, cost per task, recovery time after failure.
project_ideas.name: Mid-Layer Index for Agent Systems
project_ideas.poc: Instrument an agent framework to compute mid-layer index and correlate with outcomes across a suite of tasks.
project_ideas.video_title: 3. Dutch and British Exceptionalism

project_ideas.based_on: Is negative, adversarial framing (a shared threat model) really a cheaper and more durable coordination device
project_ideas.hypothesis: Multi-agent systems given a shared forbidden outcome (negative framing) show lower drift, faster convergence, and greater robustness to agent replacement than those given a shared positive objective.
project_ideas.measurement: Drift rate (deviation from desired behavior), convergence latency, robustness to agent replacement (success after swapping agents).
project_ideas.name: Threat-Model Coordination Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Run multi-agent coordination experiments with two conditions: shared positive objective vs shared forbidden outcome, measuring coordination dynamics.
project_ideas.video_title: 3. Dutch and British Exceptionalism

project_ideas.based_on: At what point does role permeability stop paying off and start degrading accountability?
project_ideas.hypothesis: There is an inverted-U relationship between role-crossing rate and auditability quality in multi-agent systems; beyond a threshold, accountability degrades.
project_ideas.measurement: Auditability score (e.g., ability to trace decisions to responsible components) as a function of role-crossing rate.
project_ideas.name: Role Permeability Audit Tool
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a multi-agent system with configurable role-crossing rates and measure attribution/auditability of decisions.
